State layout changes require matching headers/library. Caller owns observer/handler/frame lifetimes; payload capacity/depth failures remain observable without suppressing legacy callbacks. Input origin is UNKNOWN, handlers are pure, and language builders expose no typed observer facade. This does not establish complete family styling, action content, localization or physical accessibility parity.

Optional C progress presentation adds masked localized accessible/visible text, custom decorative children and bounded explicit font/style/color/linebox refinements, preserving legacy zero paint and numeric enabled-position semantics. Native/WASI/deterministic software coverage is scoped; complete family token mapping, root Form role, arbitrary Styled inheritance and language-builder presentation remain unfinished. See docs/QUESTIONNAIRE_PROGRESS.md.

Actual WASM desktop/touch progress tests cover opt-in localized labels, short visible text, decorative children, explicit text metrics, compiled selected usage, numeric semantics and real choice navigation; default presentation remains unchanged. This is scoped browser evidence, not complete family styling/localization/accessibility parity.

Additive C named Title/Description/ChoiceDescription and decorative Error content have independent LEGACY/TOKENS policies, explicit text refinements and scoped native/WASI/software-pixel tests. Source four-size text tiers are opt-in; shared design-size proportional tiers are CUI extensions. Legacy zero text/Error paint and one localized Alert are retained. Named text parts do not gate inactive/disabled schema items themselves. Input refinements and trailing action layout, custom Button action content, arbitrary Styled, Form role and language-builder presentation remain unfinished. Actual WASM desktop/touch checks cover opt-in named text/token/refined/custom Error modes, one Alert identity, mode-change event silence, compiled C11 usage and routed validation/navigation; this remains scoped browser evidence. See docs/QUESTIONNAIRE_PRESENTATION.md.

Bounded C geometry adds root/item/choices/actions/card patches, checked custom numeric formulas, minimum-height composition and default choice text refinements. Independent pre-change zero draw/software/memberwise semantics oracle, native/WASI routing/clipping/preflight and ASan checks are scoped evidence. No geometry browser proof, implicit inheritance or language facade is claimed. Input left-only padding/independent editor style and Button/trailing actions remain required followups. See docs/QUESTIONNAIRE_GEOMETRY.md.
components.state_ownership: Caller retains question definitions, state and all workspace buffers. An attached observer, handler/userdata and disjoint frame arenas remain alive through detach and all in-flight callbacks; rebuild matching headers/library after the state pointer ABI extension.
components.interaction: cui_questionnaire_event_fn emits live legacy model events; cui_questionnaire_validate_fn validates answers. The optional persistent typed observer runs synchronously before each legacy callback with frozen bounded copied payloads; handlers are observational and input metadata is UNKNOWN.
components.usage: Initialize definitions/workspace once; compose current controls each frame and handle answer/submit events. Optional masked slot styles refine boxes; six localized labels override defaults. Rebuild consumers after changing the by-value options ABI. Additive keyboard policies offer OFF/letters/numbers, item-only answer entry and host-selected Control/Meta submission; zero preserves legacy routing. Language builders omit these policies. Pure answer/submission snapshots copy effective values into caller-owned bounded storage without callbacks or model mutation; query_copy reports scalar state. Language builders omit snapshot APIs. Optional typed observation freezes Completed/Submit as one pair, preserves legacy callback replacement and nested mutations, and reports capacity/depth failures without suppressing legacy events. Detach can return BUSY while an outer callback pins resources. Language builders omit observer attachment, typed payloads and arenas. Additive progress presentation supports masked localized accessible/visible labels, borrowed decorative child composition and explicit bounded text size/linebox/style/color; zero preserves legacy paint and enabled-position numeric semantics. No implicit typography cascade or language-builder progress facade is provided. Additive named Title/Description/ChoiceDescription and decorative Error content use independent LEGACY/TOKENS text policies and masked text refinements. Zero extracts legacy text metrics and preserves Error paint; separate text wrappers do not recreate heading gap automatically. Four-size token tiers are source-derived; shared design-size proportional tiers are CUI extensions. Schema parts need an Item container for active/disabled gating; Error keeps one localized Alert. Callbacks are borrowed, pure and C-only; no family style cascade or model events are added. Additive independent geometry exposes five masked container/card patches, checked full numeric metrics and borrowed extended choice renderers. NULL/zero retains the exact legacy path; numeric values never implicitly cascade. Shared design size wins over custom scalar, then explicit masks win. Minimum blank area shares the real card hit/focus/semantic ID; fixed overflow and ancestor clipping remain ordinary Core behavior. Default choice text refinements stay inside the existing reducer. Input asymmetric padding/editor style, Button/trailing actions, Form role, arbitrary Styled and language-builder geometry remain required followups.

option(CUI_BUILD_RESPONSIVE_DASHBOARD "Build the native responsive dashboard example" OFF)

endif()
option(CUI_BUILD_ACCESSIBILITY "Build optional pinned Linux AccessKit bridge (prebuilt cache)" OFF)
option(CUI_FETCH_SDL "Fetch pinned SDL3 when system package absent" OFF)
function(cui_warnings target)
 if(CUI_SANITIZE AND NOT MSVC)
  target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer)
  target_link_options(${target} PUBLIC -fsanitize=address,undefined)
 endif()
 if(target MATCHES "^(test_|dist_)")
  if(MSVC)
   target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE /UNDEBUG)
  else()
   target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE -UNDEBUG)
  endif()
 endif()
 if(MSVC)
  target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE /W4)
 else()
  target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror)
 endif()
endfunction()

 install(FILES ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/${name}.pc DESTINATION lib/pkgconfig)
endfunction()

documents.README.md:
# CUI

An experimental C11 native UI framework: Clay layout, unstyled interaction primitives, themed controls, and independent renderer adapters. Embed it in an existing host or run the SDL3 workbench. No browser engine, JavaScript VM, Rust runtime, or platform types in the public core API.

**Development snapshot; full component parity remains unfinished.** All 78 component families have real C/WASM gallery stories and explicit [feature status](docs/gpui-parity.json). The library includes themed controls, Unicode editing, retained docking and virtual lists, charts, Markdown and composed application examples. Native accessibility, full language services/IME/bidi and exact platform behavior remain in progress; a tested subset does not verify a whole family.

[**Open the browser component gallery**](https://matteo.merola.co/cui/) — all 78 catalog entries, with interactive stories compiled from the same C11 implementation to WebAssembly. The HTML/Canvas browser host is an optional gallery adapter; native applications do not depend on it. See [browser build and validation](docs/WEB_GALLERY.md).

![CUI workspace composed from real components and rendered from C in WebAssembly](docs/screenshots/readme-workspace.png)

The current [composed application](docs/COMPOSED_APPS.md) uses CUI navigation, account menus, cards, forms and pricing actions. This capture shows the real C/WASM draw list rendered by the browser adapter; it is not a mockup.

Build a real window with the [native app starter guide](docs/NATIVE_APP_STARTER.md): dependencies, CMake/Make/linker flags, sidebar pages and a bottom account menu.

For a standalone native source bundle, run `make native-dist`. Unpack
`build/cui-native.tar.gz` outside this checkout, then run `make` and
`./build/native_starter`. The archive includes CUI sources and Inter Regular/Bold;
the consumer needs a C11 compiler, GNU Make, `ar`, pkg-config, SDL3 >= 3.2,
FreeType and HarfBuzz development packages. See the guide for platform limits.

## Build and run

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja
cmake --build build
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
./build/cui_gallery
./build/cui_gpu_demo --font /path/to/font.ttf
```

Core/software need a C11 compiler and CMake; Python3 checks generated headers and the manifest. Native examples optionally discover SDL3 >=3.2, FreeType and HarfBuzz through pkg-config. Set `CUI_FONT` or `--font` for an explicit font. Missing native dependencies leave portable targets available; they do not create a fake native gallery.

```sh
cmake --preset headless && cmake --build --preset headless && ctest --preset headless
cmake --preset sanitize && cmake --build --preset sanitize && ctest --preset sanitize
./build/cui_gallery --headless --section text --dark --screenshot build/text.ppm
./build/cui_gallery --smoke 3 --screenshot build/native.bmp
```

The SDL_Renderer compatibility adapter reports its actual renderer name. It requests high pixel density windows, keeps layout and pointer coordinates in logical window units, and rasterizes text, rounded shapes, images and shadows at the current renderer density. Text shaping and caret positions remain stable when moving between displays; the text library also exposes explicit `*_scaled` paint APIs for other hosts. Rounded fills and borders retain bounded batches of up to 128 scanline strips through SDL_RenderFillRects, with no added antialiasing. The separate SDL_GPU implementation uses a borrowed device/window, SPIR-V/Vulkan shaders, antialiased geometry and a bounded glyph atlas. It has been exercised on Linux Xorg with an Intel Graphics device reported by SDL. Metal/D3D shader formats remain pending; SDL_GPU backend selection alone does not establish hardware acceleration. GPU tests register only with `-DCUI_GPU_TESTS=ON`, requiring an actual device/window. The independent Sokol GLCORE adapter borrows a host OpenGL context and framebuffer and has actual pixel/cache tests on the same Intel/Mesa device; see [its contract](backends/sokol/README.md). It has no SDL dependency.

## A small application

```c
#include "cui/cui_components.h"

void settings_frame(cui_context *ui, bool *notifications) {
    cui_theme theme = cui_theme_light();
    cui_begin_frame(ui, 640, 480, 1.0f / 60);
    cui_begin_box(ui, cui_id_from(ui, "settings"), (cui_box){
        .width = -1, .height = -1, .padding = 24, .gap = 12,
        .background = theme.background
    });
    cui_label(ui, &theme, cui_string("Settings"));
    cui_switch(ui, cui_id_from(ui, "notifications"), &theme,
               cui_string("Notifications"), notifications, false);
    cui_end_box(ui);
    cui_draw_list list = cui_end_frame(ui);
    /* Consume list synchronously using your renderer before the next frame. */
    (void)list;
}
```

Create/destroy the context in the host; queue input before begin. Width/height 0 fit, negative grow, positive fix logical pixels. Stable scoped keys retain identity when lists reorder. Strings are copied to a bounded frame arena; returned draw/semantic pointers expire at the next begin. Read [API ownership](docs/API.md) and [the core contract](docs/CORE.md).

## Header-only distribution

`dist/` covers portable/headless composition, not a complete native window host.
It is reproducibly generated from modular sources and includes pinned Clay. In one C translation unit:

```c
#define CUI_IMPLEMENTATION
#include "cui.h"
#define CUI_BASE_IMPLEMENTATION
#include "cui_base.h"
#define CUI_COMPONENTS_IMPLEMENTATION
#include "cui_components.h"
```

Other translation units include those headers without implementation macros. Base includes the editor implementation; styled components include theme, overlay, virtual and plot implementations. Standalone optional models also have their own implementation macros. The single-TU test starts with the snippet above without a declaration pre-pass; multi-TU executables are also tested. Conventional static library targets use `include/cui/`. C++ and Zig host examples are in [examples/embedding](examples/embedding).

For every portable implementation, including effects and the theme registry, use
this alternative in one dedicated implementation file:

```c
#define CUI_IMPLEMENTATION_ALL
#include "cui_all.h"
```

Other files include `cui_all.h` without the macro. The generated
[implementation inventory](dist/implementations.json) lists individual headers,
macros and source files. This umbrella excludes native adapters and the optional
Rust regex provider, which are separately linked libraries. Component declarations,
including Sidebar, are available through the umbrella.

Compile the implementation file once into a static library and link your app
sources against it. Keep implementation macros out of app headers so ordinary app
edits do not rebuild the amalgamation. Regenerate only when vendored CUI changes;
the modular CMake build already compiles separate source files in parallel.

For a native SDL3 app, use the installed `cui-sdl3` pkg-config package and the
[native starter](docs/NATIVE_APP_STARTER.md). CMake supplies the transitive static
libraries and FreeType/HarfBuzz/SDL3 dependencies. If assembling sources manually,
the adapter also needs `cui_text.h`, `cui_bidi.h`, `cui_sdl3.h`,
`cui_accessibility.h`, `src/text/cui_text.c`, the bidi implementation,
`backends/sdl3/cui_sdl3.c`, and its private software bitmap/shadow/shape headers.
Include the portable effects implementation (`CUI_EFFECTS_IMPLEMENTATION`) for
shadow support; `CUI_IMPLEMENTATION_ALL` includes it. Copying only `dist/` does
not supply those native sources or third-party native libraries.

`python scripts/amalgamate.py` regenerates; `make dist-check` checks exact reproducibility. `python tools/component_vendor/vendor.py /empty/destination --layer components` copies the layer dependency closure and licenses. This currently vendors all implemented controls in that layer; per-component source slicing is pending. No CLI is required to consume the library.

## Validation and scope

`make check lint format-check dist-check`, `make bench`, and `make gallery` are available. Tests cover previous-frame ordered routing, nested capture/clips/focus scopes, Unicode scalar editing and history, randomized keyed virtualization, independent semantics, software pixels, shaped text, SDL cache/clipboard services, actual GPU readback, embedding, and gallery bounds. [Platform matrix](docs/PLATFORM_MATRIX.md) distinguishes runtime evidence from authored CI. Windows/macOS portable CI jobs are configured; results and limitations are recorded in the matrix. Fifteen headless modules also run in a pinned [WASI runner](docs/WASI.md); this is separate from browser support.

Read [the nightly report](docs/NIGHTLY_REPORT.md), [full component reference](docs/COMPONENTS.md), [architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), [component authoring](docs/COMPONENT_AUTHORING.md), and [remaining maintainer actions](docs/MAINTAINER_ACTIONS.md). All performance figures include workload context in [PERFORMANCE.md](docs/PERFORMANCE.md); none compare to other frameworks.

For a compact view of all 78 families, read [component status](docs/COMPONENT_STATUS.md).
Run `python scripts/cui_status.py Input Icon Sidebar` to inspect selected families'
features, evidence and limitations directly from the manifest.

Original CUI source is MIT. Vendored Clay and Sokol are zlib-licensed. GPUI Kit 0.7.1 is a pinned functional reference, not linked or copied into the C runtime; see [upstream baseline](docs/upstream-baseline.md) and [dependency inventory](third_party/dependencies.json).

For macOS development, see [native Mac builds and `.app` packaging](docs/MACOS.md) and [Linux-to-macOS cross compilation](docs/MACOS_CROSS.md). These workflows still require Mac runtime acceptance.

# Optional pinned regex provider

This backend is separate from default C11 CUI builds. It implements the portable `cui_text_match` ABI with source Regex1.13.1 admission and capture-free regex-automata0.4.18 PikeVM matching. See `docs/INPUT_REGEX.md` for Input ordering, lifetimes, limits and proof.

`pin.json` records exact source Cargo.lock crate archives, official Rust1.85.1 manifest/toolchain archives and the private patch SHA. `Cargo.lock` is a separate frozen path-dependency build lock; archive checksums remain authoritative. `cache.patch` only adds bounded fallible capture-free cache preparation; original upstream APIs are unchanged. The patch is not a general fallible capture API. All external sources remain in the caller's private cache, never vendored binaries or global installations.

Use an already verified complete official Rust1.85.1 prefix with matching target std. `scripts/build_regex.py --cache CACHE --toolchain PREFIX [--archive-dir VERIFIED_ARCHIVES] [--target wasm32-wasip1]` verifies every crate archive before extraction and the patch/lock digests, then builds offline/locked with private CARGO_HOME. With archive-dir missing, the script may fetch only pinned checksum-verified crate URLs. The script never installs a toolchain, changes rustup or invokes a default Cargo registry download. Target std must match the exact compiler. The toolchain receipt documents verified official acquisition; the supplied installed prefix is trusted caller-owned tooling and is checked for exact version/commit.

Source/parser compilation and Arc ownership creation may use infallible Rust allocation; OOM can terminate the process. Session creation/rebinding uses seven fallible cache reservations plus one fallible handle allocation. Match performs zero allocation. Native ordinary panics are caught at C entrypoints, but a host's default panic hook may print before catch; the backend neither logs candidates nor replaces a global hook. WASI panic recovery is unsupported. Handles/leases must be valid, externally synchronized, and used on one thread; forged pointers and direct caller writes are not protected.

Native Linux archive link dependencies are taken from Rust1.85.1's `native-static-libs` receipt: gcc_s, util, rt, pthread, m, dl, c. WASI reports libc only. Do not copy the Linux dependency list to another target. `backends/regex/CMakeLists.txt` is a standalone strict consumer harness accepting prebuilt regex/Core archives; it never invokes Rust. Root optional OFF-by-default registration, relocatable install/package targets and platform-specific CI are integrator-owned. No native Windows/macOS binary support is claimed by the Linux receipt.

Distribute the applicable notices under `licenses/` with optional artifacts: MIT chosen for alternate-license crate dependencies, Rust MIT/Apache notices and its complete official COPYRIGHT inventory. Root's dependency registry/install notices remain separate registration work. No source Input-family completeness claim follows from this optional matcher slice.

# SDL3 compatibility adapter

This optional C11 adapter owns an SDL window and an `SDL_Renderer`. It is separate
from the SDL_GPU adapter. `cui_sdl3_driver()` reports the renderer selected by SDL;
the accelerated capability is set only for a selected driver other than
`software`. A detected OpenGL driver does not prove hardware execution rather
than a Mesa software driver.

Call creation, input polling, rendering and destruction on the main thread.
The caller owns the `cui_font` and must keep it alive until adapter destruction.
Primary, secondary and middle mouse buttons, stable touch contacts, keyboard
modifiers, repeated keys, precise wheel input, UTF-8 text and composition events
are translated. Compatibility mouse events generated by touch are suppressed. Window resize/expose invalidates the UI. Quit and
window close cause `cui_sdl3_poll()` to return false.

The clipboard-only `cui_platform` interface supplies `clipboard_set` and
`clipboard_get`; its `poll` and `text_input` callbacks are null. The getter's
storage lasts until the next getter call or adapter destruction. Embedded NUL
bytes are rejected on set. SDL text input is enabled at creation. The adapter forwards composition/preedit
with UTF-8 byte ranges and scopes commits to the original focused control. The
focused painted caret updates the host candidate rectangle. See [IME](../../docs/IME.md)
for the four tested consumers and remaining physical-device/OS validation.

Rendering supports solid fills, rounded rectangles and borders, nested rectangle
clipping, source-alpha blending and HarfBuzz/FreeType glyph coverage. Rounded
geometry uses one horizontal strip per pixel row; it has no multisample edge
antialiasing. Textures persist in an LRU cache with at most 256 entries and 4 MiB
of stored grayscale coverage (up to 16 MiB of RGBA texture data). A cache key uses
dimensions, coverage hash and byte comparison; texture color/alpha modulation
allows reuse across theme changes. Allocation, font and draw failures propagate
as `false`. Glyphs that exceed the cache memory budget fail explicitly.

Analytic triangle meshes use bounded CPU coverage rasters uploaded as ordered
SDL textures. Per frame the adapter permits 256 triangles and 8 million clipped
texels (32 MiB uploaded RGBA), plus one triangle scratch buffer of up to 32 MiB;
SDL/driver allocations are additional. Unsupported transforms, malformed commands
and capacity exhaustion fail explicitly. Mesh preparation occurs before clearing;
later draw failures are not whole-frame atomic. Resources are released on failure
and the next frame can retry. See [the mesh contract](../../docs/design/SDL3_MESH.md)
for clipping, presentation transforms, limits and recovery. Private-Xvfb software
readback tests cover pixels and injected failures; physical GPU and other OS
drivers remain separate validation requirements.

Use `cui_sdl3_render_capture()` to save a BMP before presentation while framebuffer
contents are defined. The lower-level `cui_sdl3_save_bmp()` reads the current
framebuffer; do not rely on its contents after `SDL_RenderPresent`.

Validation on the development machine: SDL3 3.4.16, Linux Xorg with SDL `opengl`
driver, and SDL dummy video with `software` driver. Other platforms and Wayland
require their own runtime validation. The adapter does not provide native
accessibility bridges, pen translation, GPU resource sharing or image commands.
Touch routing and composition have injected SDL service tests; these are separate
from real touchscreen and OS candidate-window acceptance.

Frame scheduling: call `cui_sdl3_frame_delta()` immediately before each submitted
frame to measure monotonic elapsed seconds (first call is zero). Presentation
already requests vsync; an additional fixed sleep reduces the achievable refresh
rate. When Core has no redraw demand, `cui_sdl3_wait_events(backend, timeout_ms)` sleeps
until input or the caller's deadline, retaining the wakeup event for poll. Idle
waits reset the frame clock so a newly triggered animation starts at its first
frame rather than skipping the time spent idle. Run
`cui_sdl3_poll()` after rendering and before an idle wait to apply the latest
text-input focus and caret, then again after waking to dispatch input. Keep
submitting frames while `cui_needs_redraw()` is true, including animation demand.
The examples cap idle waits at 250 ms; applications with external timers should
choose their nearest deadline and explicitly invalidate Core when their model
changes. Threaded producers can arrange an SDL event wakeup on the main thread.

# SDL GPU renderer

The Vulkan/SPIR-V adapter submits mesh commands through a dedicated vertex buffer
and premultiplied triangle pipeline. The fragment shader evaluates quadratic
coverage from interpolated ST derivatives; it never rasterizes a mesh bitmap.
The frame limit is 196608 mesh vertices and 32768 draw records. Invalid meshes
or capacity overflow reject the frame before the render pass changes the target.

The RGBA8 UNORM target retains the existing byte-domain primitive behavior. Linear
premultiplied paint is unpremultiplied, sRGB encoded, and premultiplied by alpha
and analytic coverage before ONE/ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA blending. This conversion
preserves colors alongside byte primitives; it is not linear-light framebuffer
compositing. The native pixel tests require a real Vulkan device and window,
and exercise overlap, transformed placement, DPI clipping and curve coverage.

Coverage follows the frozen lockfile's `gpui-pre-wgpu 0.3.8` shader function
`src/shaders.wgsl::fs_path_rasterization`, including the norm of both S
derivatives in its0.001 solid fast path. Intel Vulkan readback checks numeric
coverage for ordinary and vertical-S triangles, mixed rectangle/mesh ordering,
borrowed vertices, mesh capacity failure and unknown-command rejection.

# Deterministic software renderer

This adapter allocates an owned, straight-alpha RGBA8 image with dimensions up to
16384 by 16384. Resize is transactional: allocation failure preserves the old
image. Pixel pointers remain valid until the next resize or destruction.

Each render clears the image, composites solid and rounded geometry, draws
rounded borders and intersects nested clipping rectangles (maximum depth 64).
Coverage is tested at pixel centers; geometry edges are not antialiased. Alpha
composition preserves straight RGB even when destination alpha is zero.
Malformed clipping stacks and nonfinite geometry return `false`.

With `CUI_HAS_TEXT`, the caller may supply an owned `cui_font` to render shaped
grayscale glyphs. Keep that font alive until renderer destruction. Without a
font or text support, text commands return `false`; the text capability is unset.
Geometry-only compilation requires the C11 standard library and math library,
without SDL, FreeType or HarfBuzz.

PPM capture exports RGB and discards alpha; it is intended for opaque screenshot
frames. No GPU acceleration or native accessibility is claimed.

# Independent Sokol GLCORE renderer

This adapter consumes CUI draw lists directly through pinned `sokol_gfx.h`.
It does not call SDL_Renderer or SDL_GPU, does not include SDL, and does not use
`sokol_app`. The separate example uses SDL3 solely to own a desktop OpenGL host.

Create a desktop OpenGL 3.3 core context and make it current before calling
`cui_sokol_create`. Keep that same context current on the creating thread for
all adapter operations, including destruction. The host owns the window, GL
context, framebuffer and font. An RGBA8, single-sample framebuffer is required;
the pipeline does not use depth or stencil attachments.

```c
cui_sokol *renderer = cui_sokol_create((cui_sokol_config){
    .font = font,
    .target = {.framebuffer = 0, .width = pixel_width, .height = pixel_height}
});
cui_renderer backend = cui_sokol_interface(renderer);
backend.render(backend.user, &draw_list, clear);
/* The host presents its window after rendering. */
```

The target dimensions are physical pixels, while draw-list dimensions are
logical pixels. Update the target after resize or DPI changes. Nested clipping
intersects in logical coordinates and becomes a physical scissor. Command order
is preserved. The adapter clears and owns one complete pass per render; it is
not a function to call inside an already-active Sokol pass.

By default, the adapter initializes Sokol and commits each successful frame.
Only one owner may initialize the process-wide Sokol runtime. Other adapters
may set `borrow_runtime=true` to share an existing GLCORE Sokol runtime; in that
mode the host performs `sg_commit()` after all its rendering. Destroy borrowers
before the owner. Host-owned Sokol must stay alive and provide compatible
resource pool capacity. If the host already compiles Sokol's implementation,
compile this adapter with `CUI_SOKOL_EXTERNAL_RUNTIME` to avoid duplicate symbols.
The adapter changes GL state; host GL code must restore its state afterwards.
It resets Sokol's state cache before its pass to accommodate preceding host GL
calls. It does not own or destroy external framebuffer objects.
Each adapter renders at most once per Sokol frame; rendering it again before
the host commits returns `false`. Borrowing requires the exact pinned Sokol API.

Solid and rounded fills, rounded borders, rectangular clipping, and source-alpha
blending are implemented. Rounded coverage uses a signed-distance fragment
shader with derivative antialiasing. Ordinary sharp rectangles retain full
coverage even when only one pixel wide. RGB blending uses straight source colors
with SRC_ALPHA/ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA, while alpha uses ONE/ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA.
Transparent framebuffer readback follows that GPU blend convention; it is not
the software adapter's straight-alpha image export.

Optional `CUI_HAS_TEXT=1` enables the caller-owned FreeType/HarfBuzz font. Shaped
glyph coverage uses immutable GPU textures and a bounded LRU cache: at most 256
entries, 4 MiB CPU coverage, and 16 MiB RGBA GPU glyph storage, plus bounded
creation scratch. Glyphs already referenced by the current frame cannot be
evicted. A frame exceeding the cache's capacity fails explicitly rather than
destroying a texture still needed by that frame. Warm-cache glyphs allocate no
new textures and tint/alpha changes reuse coverage. Without a usable font, text
commands fail and the text capability is absent.

CPU frame staging and the GPU vertex buffer are bounded by `max_quads` (default
8192, maximum 100000). Malformed draw commands, unbalanced clipping, excessive
geometry or glyph capacity are rejected before a render pass starts. Shader and
resource creation states are checked. Underlying Sokol fatal allocation or GL
assertion failures are not a device-loss recovery path. Bitmap image commands
use the existing bounded RGBA cache. Gradient mesh paint, shadows, general
transforms and non-GL Sokol backends remain unsupported.

The unmodified upstream pin and license are in `third_party/sokol/PIN.md`.
Build this source with `include/`, a SYSTEM include for `third_party/sokol`, and
the platform desktop GL library plus math. Text additionally links `cui_text`.
The adapter library has no SDL dependency. The demo links core/components,
SDL3, GL and optionally shaped text:

```sh
cui_sokol_demo --smoke 3 --screenshot sokol.ppm
```

Verified on Linux Xorg with GL vendor Intel and renderer
`Mesa Intel(R) Graphics (ARL)`. FBO readback tests cover blend/order, nested clip,
logical/physical scaling, rounded fill/border, glyph coverage, persistent-cache
reuse/eviction, bounded frame failure and borrowed-runtime ownership. The same
geometric adapter compiles and runs without FreeType/HarfBuzz. Other operating
systems, Wayland, GLES, Metal, Vulkan, D3D11 and WebGPU are unverified or not
implemented by this adapter. Software OpenGL drivers may run the same GLCORE
API; the API name alone does not prove hardware execution.

Native mesh commands upload borrowed XY/ST triangles to the bounded vertex stream.
A separate premultiplied pipeline computes the pinned quadratic source coverage
from screen-space derivatives; meshes do not use the bitmap cache. The existing
RGBA8 target stores byte-domain sRGB-like values. Mesh linear premultiplied paint
is unpremultiplied, sRGB encoded, then premultiplied by alpha and coverage before
blending. This preserves primitive appearance but does not claim linear-light
framebuffer compositing. Mesh capacity consumes one quad slot per six vertices
(or one final three-vertex slot); overflow rejects the frame before its GPU pass.

The coverage equation follows `gpui-pre-wgpu 0.3.8`, pinned by the frozen GPUI
Kit lockfile: `src/shaders.wgsl::fs_path_rasterization`. The solid fast path tests
the norm of both S derivatives against0.001; this matters for vertical curves.
Real Intel/Mesa GL readback tests check numeric coverage in both orientations,
encoded half-alpha overlaps, mixed primitive/mesh ordering, translated DPI
clips, borrowed vertices, capacity failure and unknown-command rejection.

# CUI bridge v1: C ABI and Python builders

This slice exposes real CUI row, column, label, and Button components through a portable C11 shared-library ABI. Python retains a convenient widget tree; each `step()` submits that tree to Core and renders a frame. The bridge owns copied UTF-8 strings, stable CUI IDs, Button state, and a bounded click queue. Callbacks run during `dispatch()`, after the C frame returns. `step()`/`poll_events()` allow integration with another event loop.

Build privately from the repository root:

```sh
cmake -S bindings/bridge -B build-bridge -G Ninja
cmake --build build-bridge --target cui_bridge test_bridge_core
ctest --test-dir build-bridge -R '^bridge_' --output-on-failure
```

Set `CUI_BRIDGE_LIBRARY` to the built shared library and `PYTHONPATH=bindings/python`; run `bindings/bridge/examples/save_changes.py`. The example uses SDL and requires `CUI_TEST_FONT` to point at an existing TTF. Use `App(backend='none')` for headless operation. An unavailable SDL backend or missing font reports an error; it does not silently run headless.

The public header is `include/cui/cui_bridge.h`. Call `cui_bridge_abi_version()` and `cui_bridge_options_size()` before constructing `cui_bridge_options`; set `struct_size` and `abi_version`. Destroy every app with `cui_bridge_destroy()`. Node handles contain slot and generation and belong to the app that created them. C callers must preserve that provenance; Python rejects cross-app widgets and use after disposal. All calls for one app must occur on one thread. Strings must be NUL-terminated UTF-8, up to 4096 bytes excluding NUL; setters copy them. Width and height must be finite logical pixels in `(0, 32768]`. Nodes and pending events have configurable fixed capacities (defaults 256, maximum 1024 nodes and 4096 events); errors do not overwrite output handles, bounds, or events.

The design size setter maps to CUI's complete `inherit`, `xs`, `sm`, `base`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, `2xl` through `9xl` scale; Button defaults to `base`. Python `.gap(2)` and `.gap_px(2)` mean two logical pixels. `.gap_units(2)` means eight logical pixels (four pixels per unit). `.rounded_md()` selects the theme's medium Button rounding. Custom hover RGBA maps to existing primary, secondary, or outline Button palettes; ghost custom hover is unsupported. Unsupported props are rejected explicitly.

This is a narrow first slice, not a binding of all 78 manifest components. Native SDL requires an explicit font path and its existing renderer; headless metrics are approximate. Events are bounded and must be drained with `poll_events()` or `dispatch()`. Python callback exceptions propagate after the C frame and can be handled by the caller. The current C ABI is not a layout engine or arbitrary CSS API, and the bridge makes no full GPUI parity claim. Windows DLL exports are annotated, but Windows runtime behavior has not been validated here.

"""Actual SDL Button rendered by CUI components; set CUI_TEST_FONT and CUI_BRIDGE_LIBRARY."""
import os
from cui_bridge import App, button, label, row

font = os.environ["CUI_TEST_FONT"]
save = button("save").primary().rounded_md().size("base").label("Save changes")
status = label("Ready", key="status")

def saved(_event):
    status.label("Saved")

save.on_click(saved)
with App(backend="sdl", title="CUI Python bridge", width=480, height=240,
         font_path=font) as app:
    app.mount(row().gap_units(2).children(save, status))
    app.run()

"""Native sidebar workspace; --headless checks real navigation and editing."""
import argparse
import os
from cui_bridge import App, button, checkbox, column, input, item, label, root_view, row, sidebar, tabs

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
parser.add_argument('--headless', action='store_true')
args = parser.parse_args()
status = label('Ready', key='status')
name = input('name', 'Alex Morgan')
email = checkbox('email', 'Email notifications').checked()
save = button('save').label('Save changes').primary().rounded_md().on_click(
    lambda event: status.label('Saved account: ' + name.current_text()))
account = item('account-page', 'Account').children(
    column().gap_units(3).children(label('Account details'), name, save, status))
preferences = item('preferences-page', 'Preferences').children(
    column().gap_units(3).children(label('Notifications'), email))
pages = tabs('pages').children(account, preferences).select(account)
account_action = item('account-action', 'Account').on_click(lambda event: pages.select(account))
preferences_action = item('preferences-action', 'Preferences').on_click(lambda event: pages.select(preferences))
navigation = sidebar('navigation').visual_size(180, 280).children(account_action, preferences_action)
root = root_view().padding(24).children(column().gap_units(4).children(
    label('CUI workspace'), row().gap_units(6).children(navigation, pages)))
options = dict(width=820, height=460, title='CUI sidebar workspace')
if not args.headless:
    options.update(backend='sdl', font_path=os.environ['CUI_TEST_FONT'])
with App(**options) as app:
    app.mount(root)
    if args.headless:
        def press(node):
            x, y, width, height = app.bounds(node)
            assert width > 0 and height > 0
            app.queue_pointer('down', x + width/2, y + height/2)
            app.queue_pointer('up', x + width/2, y + height/2)
            app.step(); app.dispatch(); app.step()
        app.step(); press(preferences_action)

        assert status._text == 'Saved account: ' + name.current_text() and name.current_text().endswith('!')
        print('PASS sidebar workspace: navigation, native input and save callback')
    else:
        app.run()

# SDL3 compatibility adapter

This optional C11 adapter owns an SDL window and an `SDL_Renderer`. It is separate
from the SDL_GPU adapter. `cui_sdl3_driver()` reports the renderer selected by SDL;
the accelerated capability is set only for a selected driver other than
`software`. A detected OpenGL driver does not prove hardware execution rather
than a Mesa software driver.

Call creation, input polling, rendering and destruction on the main thread.
The caller owns the `cui_font` and must keep it alive until adapter destruction.
Primary, secondary and middle mouse buttons, stable touch contacts, keyboard
modifiers, repeated keys, precise wheel input, UTF-8 text and composition events
are translated. Compatibility mouse events generated by touch are suppressed. Window resize/expose invalidates the UI. Quit and
window close cause `cui_sdl3_poll()` to return false.

The clipboard-only `cui_platform` interface supplies `clipboard_set` and
`clipboard_get`; its `poll` and `text_input` callbacks are null. The getter's
storage lasts until the next getter call or adapter destruction. Embedded NUL
bytes are rejected on set. SDL text input is enabled at creation. The adapter forwards composition/preedit
with UTF-8 byte ranges and scopes commits to the original focused control. The
focused painted caret updates the host candidate rectangle. See [IME](../../docs/IME.md)
for the four tested consumers and remaining physical-device/OS validation.

Rendering supports solid fills, rounded rectangles and borders, nested rectangle
clipping, source-alpha blending and HarfBuzz/FreeType glyph coverage. Rounded
geometry uses one horizontal strip per pixel row; it has no multisample edge
antialiasing. Textures persist in an LRU cache with at most 256 entries and 4 MiB
of stored grayscale coverage (up to 16 MiB of RGBA texture data). A cache key uses
dimensions, coverage hash and byte comparison; texture color/alpha modulation
allows reuse across theme changes. Allocation, font and draw failures propagate
as `false`. Glyphs that exceed the cache memory budget fail explicitly.

Analytic triangle meshes use bounded CPU coverage rasters uploaded as ordered
SDL textures. Per frame the adapter permits 256 triangles and 8 million clipped
texels (32 MiB uploaded RGBA), plus one triangle scratch buffer of up to 32 MiB;
SDL/driver allocations are additional. Unsupported transforms, malformed commands
and capacity exhaustion fail explicitly. Mesh preparation occurs before clearing;
later draw failures are not whole-frame atomic. Resources are released on failure
and the next frame can retry. See [the mesh contract](../../docs/design/SDL3_MESH.md)
for clipping, presentation transforms, limits and recovery. Private-Xvfb software
readback tests cover pixels and injected failures; physical GPU and other OS
drivers remain separate validation requirements.

Use `cui_sdl3_render_capture()` to save a BMP before presentation while framebuffer
contents are defined. The lower-level `cui_sdl3_save_bmp()` reads the current
framebuffer; do not rely on its contents after `SDL_RenderPresent`.

Validation on the development machine: SDL3 3.4.16, Linux Xorg with SDL `opengl`
driver, and SDL dummy video with `software` driver. Other platforms and Wayland
require their own runtime validation. The adapter does not provide native
accessibility bridges, pen translation, GPU resource sharing or image commands.
Touch routing and composition have injected SDL service tests; these are separate
from real touchscreen and OS candidate-window acceptance.

Frame scheduling: call `cui_sdl3_frame_delta()` immediately before each submitted
frame to measure monotonic elapsed seconds (first call is zero). Presentation
already requests vsync; an additional fixed sleep reduces the achievable refresh
rate. When Core has no redraw demand, `cui_sdl3_wait_events(backend, timeout_ms)` sleeps
until input or the caller's deadline, retaining the wakeup event for poll. Idle
waits reset the frame clock so a newly triggered animation starts at its first
frame rather than skipping the time spent idle. Run
`cui_sdl3_poll()` after rendering and before an idle wait to apply the latest
text-input focus and caret, then again after waking to dispatch input. Keep
submitting frames while `cui_needs_redraw()` is true, including animation demand.
The examples cap idle waits at 250 ms; applications with external timers should
choose their nearest deadline and explicitly invalidate Core when their model
changes. Threaded producers can arrange an SDL event wakeup on the main thread.

# Deterministic software renderer

This adapter allocates an owned, straight-alpha RGBA8 image with dimensions up to
16384 by 16384. Resize is transactional: allocation failure preserves the old
image. Pixel pointers remain valid until the next resize or destruction.

Each render clears the image, composites solid and rounded geometry, draws
rounded borders and intersects nested clipping rectangles (maximum depth 64).
Coverage is tested at pixel centers; geometry edges are not antialiased. Alpha
composition preserves straight RGB even when destination alpha is zero.
Malformed clipping stacks and nonfinite geometry return `false`.

With `CUI_HAS_TEXT`, the caller may supply an owned `cui_font` to render shaped
grayscale glyphs. Keep that font alive until renderer destruction. Without a
font or text support, text commands return `false`; the text capability is unset.
Geometry-only compilation requires the C11 standard library and math library,
without SDL, FreeType or HarfBuzz.

PPM capture exports RGB and discards alpha; it is intended for opaque screenshot
frames. No GPU acceleration or native accessibility is claimed.

# Native CUI for Node.js and TypeScript

This binding creates a real CUI scene. The N-API addon calls the shared C bridge; CUI computes layout and queues input events. The SDL backend renders an actual native window. JavaScript owns callbacks and updates nodes after `step()` returns from C. The fluent API currently exposes row, column, label, and button. Other manifest components are not exposed by this binding.

## Build and run

Prerequisites: CMake, Ninja, C compiler with C11, Node.js 18+ and its `node_api.h` development header. Native windows require installed SDL3 3.2 or newer, FreeType, and HarfBuzz development packages; CMake does not fetch them by default. From the repository root:

```sh
cmake -S bindings/node -B build-node -G Ninja -DCUI_BUILD_NATIVE=ON
cmake --build build-node --target cui_node_bindings test_bridge_core
ctest --test-dir build-node -R "^(bridge_core|node_binding|node_addon_safety)$" --output-on-failure
node bindings/node/examples/save.cjs --headless
```

The build places `cui.node` in `build-node/`; set `CUI_NODE_ADDON=/absolute/path/to/cui.node` if using another build directory. The private CMake project builds the C bridge and links the addon; there are no npm packages or node-gyp steps. For an actual window, ensure CMake reports that SDL3 and text adapters are enabled, and provide a font file:

```sh
CUI_FONT_PATH=/path/to/font.ttf node bindings/node/examples/save.cjs
```

The SDL backend creates a native window. Headless mode runs CUI scene construction, layout, and input without opening a window. The example exits on Ctrl+C. For a finite native smoke check under a fresh Xvfb display:

```sh
CUI_NODE_ADDON="$PWD/build-node/cui.node" CUI_FONT_PATH=/path/to/font.ttf \
  xvfb-run -a node bindings/node/test/native.test.cjs
```

This checks window creation, a frame, button click, close, and disposal. Do not point it at an active desktop display.

Node 25 can run the TypeScript example directly with type stripping:

```sh
node --experimental-strip-types bindings/typescript/examples/save.ts
```

For older Node versions, compile the TypeScript file with a TypeScript compiler already available in your project. The declarations are in `bindings/typescript/index.d.ts` and exported by the Node package's `types` field.

## API

```js
const {App, row, column, label, button} = require('./bindings/node');
const status = label('Ready');
const save = button('save').primary().rounded_md().label('Save changes')
  .on_click(() => status.label('Saved'));
const app = new App({backend: 'headless', width: 480, height: 240});
app.mount(column().gap_units(2).children(row().children(save, status)));
app.step();
const b = save.bounds();
app.pointer('move', b.x + 2, b.y + 2)
  .pointer('down', b.x + 2, b.y + 2)
  .pointer('up', b.x + 2, b.y + 2);
app.step();
app.dispose();
```

`gap(n)` and `gap_px(n)` specify logical pixels. `gap_units(n)` multiplies by 4, so `gap_units(2)` is 8 logical pixels. Buttons support `primary`, `secondary`, `outline`, `ghost`, a BASE default size, methods `inherit()`, `xs()`, `sm()`, `base()`, `md()`, `lg()`, `xl()` (with `small()`, `medium()`, `large()` aliases), and `size(name)` for the full INHERIT–9XL scale, rounding methods, `disabled`, and `hover_color('#RRGGBB[AA]')`. `rounded_md()` maps to the bridge's large rounding preset; `rounded_px(n)` sets an exact radius. Unsupported style methods are absent.

`App.step(dt)` renders one frame, then drains click events and calls handlers. A handler may update labels and button styles for the next frame. `App.start(fps)` schedules `step` with Node timers, keeping the event loop responsive. `App.stop()` stops the timer; `App.close()` requests CUI closure and stops it; `App.dispose()` releases native resources. Host tests can queue `pointer` and `key` events, then call `step`. Handles belong to one app, and operations after disposal or removal throw.

`App.run()` is the synchronous native callback runner for live window resize.
It dispatches handlers after each completed frame and returns on close. Callback
errors are rethrown after leaving the native runner. Unlike timer-based `start()`,
it blocks JavaScript timers and I/O until closure. Do not mix the two loops or
call `step()`/`run()` recursively from a handler. See
[runner lifecycle](../../docs/BINDING_NATIVE_RUN.md) for ownership and errors.

"""Small retained Python authoring layer over CUI's portable bridge ABI v1.

The widget tree lives in Python. ``step`` submits it through real CUI components;
``dispatch`` invokes Python callbacks only after the C frame has returned.

from __future__ import annotations

import ctypes as C
import datetime
from dataclasses import dataclass
import math
import os
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, ClassVar, Iterator, Literal


def _utf8(value: str, limit: int = 4096) -> bytes:
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise TypeError("expected a string")
    if "\x00" in value:
        raise ValueError("NUL is not allowed in bridge strings")
    encoded = value.encode("utf-8")
    if len(encoded) > limit:
        raise ValueError(f"bridge strings are limited to {limit} UTF-8 bytes")
    return encoded


class BridgeError(RuntimeError):
    """A rejected bridge operation with its C status code."""

    def __init__(self, code: int, message: str):
        super().__init__(f"CUI bridge {code}: {message}")
        self.code = code


class _Handle(C.Structure):
    _fields_ = [("slot", C.c_uint32), ("generation", C.c_uint32)]


class _Rect(C.Structure):
    _fields_ = [("x", C.c_float), ("y", C.c_float),
                ("width", C.c_float), ("height", C.c_float)]

    _fields_ = [("type", C.c_int), ("node", _Handle),
                ("frame_sequence", C.c_uint64)]

    _fields_ = _Event._fields_ + [("checked", C.c_uint32), ("value", C.c_double),

    def font_fallbacks(self, paths: list[str] | tuple[str, ...]) -> "App":

        self._ensure_open()

            raise ValueError("fallbacks must be a list/tuple of at most 32 paths")

    def mount(self, tree: Widget) -> "App":

        def validate(node: Widget, parent: Widget | None, path: str, depth: int) -> None:
            if depth >= 128:
                raise ValueError("widget tree exceeds 128 levels")
            if id(node) in seen:
                raise ValueError("widget tree contains a cycle or shared node")

                raise ValueError("widget belongs to a different App")

                raise ValueError("widget belongs to a disposed App")

                if node.kind == "otp_input": node._change("set_total",node._total)
                if _KIND[node.kind] >= 3:

                if node.kind in _BOOLEAN or (node.kind == "item" and node._checked_set):
                    node._change("set_checked", int(node._checked))
                if node.kind in {"slider", "number_input"}:
                    node._change("set_range", *node._range)
                if node.kind in {"pagination", "rating"}:
                    node._change("set_total", node._total)
                if node.kind in _NUMERIC:
                    node._change("set_value", node._value)
                if node.kind == "attachment": node._change("set_attachment",node._attachment)
                if node.kind == "image" and node._image is not None: node._change("set_image",*node._image)
                if node.kind == "time_field": node._change("set_time",_Time(*node._time))
                if node.kind in {"calendar", "date_picker"}: node._change("set_date",_Date(*node._date))
                if node.kind == "color_picker": node._change("set_color",node._color)
                if node.kind == "chart": node.chart_kind(("line","area","bar","pie")[node._chart_kind]);node.chart_data(node._chart_data)
                if node.kind == "plot": node.plot_points(node._plot_points)
                if node.kind == "data_table": node._change("set_selection_mode",node._selection_mode)
                if node.kind == "sidebar" and node._open_set: node._change("set_open",int(node._open))
                if node.kind == "data_table" and node._matrix is not None: node.table_data(*node._matrix)
                if node.kind == "text_view": node._change("set_text_format",node._text_format)
                if node._question_flags is not None: node._change("question_config",*[int(v) for v in node._question_flags])
                if node._panel_size is not None: node._change("set_value",node._panel_size)
                if node._visual is not None:
                    node._change("set_visual", *node._visual)
                if node._extent is not None:
                    node._change("set_scroll_extent", *node._extent)
                if node._step_status is not None:
                    node._change("set_step_status", node._step_status)
                if node.kind in _DISABLED and (node.kind != "item" or node._disabled):
                    node._change("set_disabled", int(node._disabled))
                if node.kind == "collapsible" or (node.kind == "item" and node._open_set):
                    node._change("set_open", int(node._open))

                if node._avatar_identity is not None:

                if node._avatar_placeholder is not None:
                    enabled, name = node._avatar_placeholder

                    node._change("set_variant", _VARIANT[node._variant])
                    node._change("set_size", _SIZE[node._size])

                    node._change("set_disabled", int(node._disabled))

                if node._anchor is not None:

                    node._change("set_open", 1)

        except Exception:
            if created:
                self._api.node_remove(self._ptr, created[0]._handle)
            for node in created:

    def step(self, dt: float = 1 / 60) -> None:
        if getattr(self, "_running", False):
            raise RuntimeError("step is unavailable during run")

        self._api.check(self._api.step(self._ptr, dt))

    def queue_pointer(self, phase: str, x: float, y: float) -> None:

    def poll_events(self) -> Iterator[Event]:
        self._ensure_open()
        while True:
            if not self._ptr:
                return
            raw = _EventEx()
            buffer = C.create_string_buffer(4097)
            required = C.c_uint32()
            status = self._api.poll_event_ex(self._ptr, C.byref(raw), buffer, 4097,
                                             C.byref(required))
            if status in (1, 2):
                return
            self._api.check(status)
            node = self._by_handle.get((raw.node.slot, raw.node.generation))
            if node is not None:
                yield Event({1:"click", 2:"change", 3:"close"}[raw.type], node, raw.frame_sequence,
                            bool(raw.checked), raw.value, buffer.value.decode("utf-8"),
                            (raw.selected.slot, raw.selected.generation))

    def poll_notifications_v1(self) -> Iterator[NotificationV1]:
        """Consume owning V1 snapshots without callbacks; shares the legacy queue.

        Requires optional V1 symbols, exact native layout and a <=1MiB payload
        including NUL. Capacity failures retain the event for a capable consumer.
        Existing step/dispatch behavior is unchanged.
        """
        self._ensure_open()
        try:
            size = self._api.lib.cui_bridge_notification_v1_size
            versions = self._api.lib.cui_bridge_notification_versions
            poll = self._api.lib.cui_bridge_poll_notification_v1
        except AttributeError as error:
            raise BridgeError(9, "V1 notification symbols unavailable") from error
        size.argtypes = versions.argtypes = []
        size.restype = versions.restype = C.c_uint32
        if not (versions() & 1) or size() != C.sizeof(_NotificationV1):
            raise BridgeError(8, "V1 notification capability/layout mismatch")
        poll.restype = C.c_int
        poll.argtypes = [C.c_void_p, C.c_uint32, C.POINTER(_NotificationV1),
                         C.c_void_p, C.c_uint32, C.POINTER(C.c_uint32)]
        while self._ptr:
            raw = _NotificationV1()
            capacity = 4097
            for attempt in range(2):
                buffer = C.create_string_buffer(capacity)
                required = C.c_uint32()
                status = poll(self._ptr, C.sizeof(raw), C.byref(raw), buffer, capacity,
                              C.byref(required))
                if status != 5:
                    break
                if attempt or required.value <= capacity or required.value > 1024 * 1024:
                    raise BridgeError(5, "V1 notification payload exceeds limit or invalid capacity retry")
                capacity = required.value
            if status in (1, 2):
                return
            self._api.check(status)
            if raw.schema_version != 1 or raw.struct_size != C.sizeof(raw) or raw.text_length >= capacity:
                raise BridgeError(8, "invalid V1 notification output")
            text = bytes(buffer.raw[:raw.text_length]).decode("utf-8")
            handle = (raw.node.slot, raw.node.generation)
            selected = (raw.legacy.selected.slot, raw.legacy.selected.generation)
            legacy = LegacySnapshotV1(raw.legacy.type, raw.legacy.checked, raw.legacy.value,
                                      text, selected)
            common = (handle, self._by_handle.get(handle), raw.frame_sequence,
                      bool(raw.flags & 1), raw.node_kind, legacy)
            if raw.payload_kind == 0:
                yield ActivationNotificationV1(*common)
            elif raw.payload_kind == 1:
                yield BooleanChangeNotificationV1(*common, bool(raw.payload.boolean_value))
            elif raw.payload_kind == 5:
                table = raw.payload.table
                yield TableChangeNotificationV1(*common,
                    "selection" if table.reason == 1 else "sort", table.row, table.column,
                    table.sort_column, table.sort_direction)
            elif raw.payload_kind == 6:
                yield SurfaceCloseNotificationV1(*common, raw.payload.surface_result)
            else:
                yield LegacyNotificationV1(*common, self._by_handle.get(selected))

    def poll_value_notifications_v1(self) -> Iterator[ValueNotificationV1]:
        """Owning opt-in value views on the shared queue; never dispatch callbacks.

        Requires optional value symbols and exact V1 layout. Requests only known
        advertised scalar/text/selection categories. Old libraries fail without
        fallback draining; text retries once up to 1MiB including NUL.
        """
        self._ensure_open()
        try:
            size = self._api.lib.cui_bridge_notification_v1_size
            versions = self._api.lib.cui_bridge_notification_versions
            categories = self._api.lib.cui_bridge_notification_value_payloads_v1
            poll = self._api.lib.cui_bridge_poll_value_notification_v1
        except AttributeError as error:
            raise BridgeError(9, "V1 value notification symbols unavailable") from error
        for query in (size, versions, categories):
            query.argtypes = []
            query.restype = C.c_uint32
        if not (versions() & 1) or size() != C.sizeof(_NotificationV1):
            raise BridgeError(8, "V1 value notification capability/layout mismatch")
        mask = categories() & ((1 << 2) | (1 << 3) | (1 << 4))
        if not mask:
            raise BridgeError(9, "V1 value notification categories unavailable")
        poll.restype = C.c_int
        poll.argtypes = [C.c_void_p, C.c_uint32, C.c_uint32, C.POINTER(_NotificationV1),
                         C.c_void_p, C.c_uint32, C.POINTER(C.c_uint32)]
        while self._ptr:
            raw = _NotificationV1()
            capacity = 4097
            for attempt in range(2):
                buffer = C.create_string_buffer(capacity)
                required = C.c_uint32()
                status = poll(self._ptr, C.sizeof(raw), mask, C.byref(raw), buffer,
                              capacity, C.byref(required))
                if status != 5:
                    break
                if attempt or required.value <= capacity or required.value > 1024 * 1024:
                    raise BridgeError(5, "V1 value payload exceeds limit or invalid capacity retry")
                capacity = required.value
            if status in (1, 2):
                return
            self._api.check(status)
            if (raw.schema_version != 1 or raw.struct_size != C.sizeof(raw) or
                    raw.text_length >= capacity or buffer.raw[raw.text_length] != 0 or
                    raw.flags & ~1 or bool(raw.flags & 1) != bool(raw.frame_sequence) or
                    required.value != raw.text_length + 1 or
                    raw.legacy.text_length != raw.text_length or
                    raw.legacy.frame_sequence != raw.frame_sequence or
                    (raw.node.slot, raw.node.generation) !=
                    (raw.legacy.node.slot, raw.legacy.node.generation) or
                    raw.kind not in (1, 2, 3) or raw.legacy.type != raw.kind):
                raise BridgeError(8, "invalid V1 value notification output")
            try:
                text = bytes(buffer.raw[:raw.text_length]).decode("utf-8")
            except UnicodeDecodeError as error:
                raise BridgeError(8, "invalid V1 value notification UTF-8") from error
            handle = (raw.node.slot, raw.node.generation)
            selected = (raw.legacy.selected.slot, raw.legacy.selected.generation)
            legacy = LegacySnapshotV1(raw.legacy.type, raw.legacy.checked, raw.legacy.value,
                                      text, selected)
            common = (handle, self._by_handle.get(handle), raw.frame_sequence,
                      bool(raw.flags & 1), raw.node_kind, legacy)
            tag = raw.payload_kind
            if ((tag == 0 and raw.kind != 1) or
                    (tag in (1, 2, 3, 4, 5) and raw.kind != 2) or
                    (tag == 6 and raw.kind != 3) or tag not in range(8) or
                    (tag in (2, 3, 4) and not mask & (1 << tag))):
                raise BridgeError(8, "invalid V1 value notification kind/tag")
            if tag == 0:
                yield ActivationNotificationV1(*common)
            elif tag == 1:
                if raw.payload.boolean_value > 1:
                    raise BridgeError(8, "invalid V1 boolean payload")
                yield BooleanChangeNotificationV1(*common, bool(raw.payload.boolean_value))
            elif tag == 2:
                value = raw.payload.scalar_value
                if not math.isfinite(value) or value != raw.legacy.value:
                    raise BridgeError(8, "invalid V1 scalar payload")
                yield ScalarChangeNotificationV1(*common, value)
            elif tag == 3:
                yield TextChangeNotificationV1(*common, text)
            elif tag == 4:
                value = (raw.payload.selected.slot, raw.payload.selected.generation)
                if value != selected or bool(value[0]) != bool(value[1]):
                    raise BridgeError(8, "invalid V1 selection payload")
                yield SelectionChangeNotificationV1(*common, value, self._by_handle.get(value))
            elif tag == 5:
                table = raw.payload.table
                if table.reason not in (1, 2):
                    raise BridgeError(8, "invalid V1 table payload")
                yield TableChangeNotificationV1(*common,
                    "selection" if table.reason == 1 else "sort", table.row, table.column,
                    table.sort_column, table.sort_direction)
            elif tag == 6:
                if raw.payload.surface_result not in (1, 2, 3):
                    raise BridgeError(8, "invalid V1 surface payload")
                yield SurfaceCloseNotificationV1(*common, raw.payload.surface_result)
            else:
                yield LegacyNotificationV1(*common, self._by_handle.get(selected))

    def dispatch(self) -> int:
        """Invoke callbacks after step; Python exceptions propagate outside C frames."""
        count = 0
        for event in self.poll_events():
            callback = (event.node._callback if event.type == "click" else
                        event.node._close_callback if event.type == "close" else event.node._change_callback)
            if callback:
                callback(event)
            count += 1
        return count

    def run(self, dt: float = 1 / 60) -> None:
        """Run the native event loop; dispatch after paint, including live resize.

        dt is retained for source compatibility and validated; native scheduling
        supplies actual frame timing. Older bridges fail clearly without fallback.
        """
        self._ensure_open()
        if not math.isfinite(dt) or dt <= 0:
            raise ValueError("run requires positive finite dt")
        if getattr(self, "_running", False):
            raise RuntimeError("app is already running")
        try:
            runner = self._api.lib.cui_bridge_run
        except AttributeError as exc:
            raise RuntimeError("native callback runner unavailable in this bridge") from exc
        callback_type = C.CFUNCTYPE(C.c_int, C.c_void_p)
        runner.restype = C.c_int
        runner.argtypes = [C.c_void_p, callback_type, C.c_void_p]
        failure = []
        @callback_type
        def after_frame(_user):
            try:
                self.dispatch()
                return 0
            except BaseException as exc:
                failure.append((exc, exc.__traceback__))
                return 3  # Stop C first; foreign exceptions must never cross C.
        self._running = True
        try:
            status = runner(self._ptr, after_frame, None)
        finally:
            self._running = False
        if failure:
            exc, traceback = failure[0]
            raise exc.with_traceback(traceback)
        if status != 2:  # CLOSED is normal runner termination.
            self._api.check(status)

    def request_close(self) -> None:
        self._ensure_open()
        self._api.check(self._api.request_close(self._ptr))

    def close(self) -> None:
        if self._ptr:
            self._api.destroy(self._ptr)
            self._ptr = None
            for node in self._by_handle.values():
                node._app = node._handle = None
                node._disposed = True
            self._by_handle.clear()

    def __enter__(self) -> "App":
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *_exc) -> None:
        self.close()

    def __del__(self):
        if getattr(self, "_ptr", None):
            self.close()

# SDL3 compatibility adapter

This optional C11 adapter owns an SDL window and an `SDL_Renderer`. It is separate
from the SDL_GPU adapter. `cui_sdl3_driver()` reports the renderer selected by SDL;
the accelerated capability is set only for a selected driver other than
`software`. A detected OpenGL driver does not prove hardware execution rather
than a Mesa software driver.

Call creation, input polling, rendering and destruction on the main thread.
The caller owns the `cui_font` and must keep it alive until adapter destruction.
Primary, secondary and middle mouse buttons, stable touch contacts, keyboard
modifiers, repeated keys, precise wheel input, UTF-8 text and composition events
are translated. Compatibility mouse events generated by touch are suppressed. Window resize/expose invalidates the UI. Quit and
window close cause `cui_sdl3_poll()` to return false.

The clipboard-only `cui_platform` interface supplies `clipboard_set` and
`clipboard_get`; its `poll` and `text_input` callbacks are null. The getter's
storage lasts until the next getter call or adapter destruction. Embedded NUL
bytes are rejected on set. SDL text input is enabled at creation. The adapter forwards composition/preedit
with UTF-8 byte ranges and scopes commits to the original focused control. The
focused painted caret updates the host candidate rectangle. See [IME](../../docs/IME.md)
for the four tested consumers and remaining physical-device/OS validation.

Rendering supports solid fills, rounded rectangles and borders, nested rectangle
clipping, source-alpha blending and HarfBuzz/FreeType glyph coverage. Rounded
geometry uses one horizontal strip per pixel row; it has no multisample edge
antialiasing. Textures persist in an LRU cache with at most 256 entries and 4 MiB
of stored grayscale coverage (up to 16 MiB of RGBA texture data). A cache key uses
dimensions, coverage hash and byte comparison; texture color/alpha modulation
allows reuse across theme changes. Allocation, font and draw failures propagate
as `false`. Glyphs that exceed the cache memory budget fail explicitly.

Analytic triangle meshes use bounded CPU coverage rasters uploaded as ordered
SDL textures. Per frame the adapter permits 256 triangles and 8 million clipped
texels (32 MiB uploaded RGBA), plus one triangle scratch buffer of up to 32 MiB;
SDL/driver allocations are additional. Unsupported transforms, malformed commands
and capacity exhaustion fail explicitly. Mesh preparation occurs before clearing;
later draw failures are not whole-frame atomic. Resources are released on failure
and the next frame can retry. See [the mesh contract](../../docs/design/SDL3_MESH.md)
for clipping, presentation transforms, limits and recovery. Private-Xvfb software
readback tests cover pixels and injected failures; physical GPU and other OS
drivers remain separate validation requirements.

Use `cui_sdl3_render_capture()` to save a BMP before presentation while framebuffer
contents are defined. The lower-level `cui_sdl3_save_bmp()` reads the current
framebuffer; do not rely on its contents after `SDL_RenderPresent`.

Validation on the development machine: SDL3 3.4.16, Linux Xorg with SDL `opengl`
driver, and SDL dummy video with `software` driver. Other platforms and Wayland
require their own runtime validation. The adapter does not provide native
accessibility bridges, pen translation, GPU resource sharing or image commands.
Touch routing and composition have injected SDL service tests; these are separate
from real touchscreen and OS candidate-window acceptance.

Frame scheduling: call `cui_sdl3_frame_delta()` immediately before each submitted
frame to measure monotonic elapsed seconds (first call is zero). Presentation
already requests vsync; an additional fixed sleep reduces the achievable refresh
rate. When Core has no redraw demand, `cui_sdl3_wait_events(backend, timeout_ms)` sleeps
until input or the caller's deadline, retaining the wakeup event for poll. Idle
waits reset the frame clock so a newly triggered animation starts at its first
frame rather than skipping the time spent idle. Run
`cui_sdl3_poll()` after rendering and before an idle wait to apply the latest
text-input focus and caret, then again after waking to dispatch input. Keep
submitting frames while `cui_needs_redraw()` is true, including animation demand.
The examples cap idle waits at 250 ms; applications with external timers should
choose their nearest deadline and explicitly invalidate Core when their model
changes. Threaded producers can arrange an SDL event wakeup on the main thread.

# Deterministic software renderer

This adapter allocates an owned, straight-alpha RGBA8 image with dimensions up to
16384 by 16384. Resize is transactional: allocation failure preserves the old
image. Pixel pointers remain valid until the next resize or destruction.

Each render clears the image, composites solid and rounded geometry, draws
rounded borders and intersects nested clipping rectangles (maximum depth 64).
Coverage is tested at pixel centers; geometry edges are not antialiased. Alpha
composition preserves straight RGB even when destination alpha is zero.
Malformed clipping stacks and nonfinite geometry return `false`.

With `CUI_HAS_TEXT`, the caller may supply an owned `cui_font` to render shaped
grayscale glyphs. Keep that font alive until renderer destruction. Without a
font or text support, text commands return `false`; the text capability is unset.
Geometry-only compilation requires the C11 standard library and math library,
without SDL, FreeType or HarfBuzz.

PPM capture exports RGB and discards alpha; it is intended for opaque screenshot
frames. No GPU acceleration or native accessibility is claimed.

# Accessibility

Controls submit an independent semantic snapshot with identity, role, accessible name, bounds, disabled/checked/focused state and scalar value. Compound controls also expose relationships, selection, scroll ranges and modal scopes. Headless tests validate named subsets of these states and keyboard interactions; they do not establish complete family acceptance.

The browser gallery projects these snapshots into DOM controls for focus and assistive technologies. Its hidden native text-input bridge supports composition for Input, Textarea, Editor and Questionnaire, plus Numeric, OTP and Combobox; per-consumer filtering and history differ. Caret/selection painting, pointer positioning and Unicode grapheme/word editing have tests. Bidirectional caret geometry, full browser screen-reader testing and mobile virtual-keyboard acceptance remain unfinished. See [IME](IME.md) and [editing](EDITING.md).

Native Windows UIA, macOS AX, Linux AT-SPI, Android/iOS accessibility bridges and AccessKit integration remain unimplemented. Real screen-reader, contrast, text scaling, reduced-motion and touch-target acceptance is required before v1.0. High contrast is a token theme with tested control colors, not platform certification. See [v1 readiness](V1_READINESS.md) and [platform evidence](PLATFORM_MATRIX.md).
