# Bidirectional text analysis

`cui_bidi_resolve` resolves one UTF-8 paragraph as one unwrapped line using
vendored SheenBidi 3.0.0, commit
`cfe430e7375a7845b679adae9d51dac6deaa8858` (Apache-2.0).
The upstream [release](https://github.com/Tehreer/SheenBidi/releases/tag/v3.0.0)
updates its property tables to Unicode 17.0.0. Vendored files are unmodified;
`third_party/sheenbidi/manifest.json` records their SHA-256 checksums.

The engine applies paragraph detection/base levels, explicit embeddings and
isolates, weak types including numbers, paired brackets, neutrals, implicit
levels, line resets, and visual run ordering. The wrapper returns logical scalar
levels after L1, visual runs, a visual-to-logical scalar permutation, and
mirrored code points where odd-level characters have a Unicode mirror mapping.
It follows [Unicode 17 UAX #9 revision 51](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/tr9-51.html).
Explicit direction overrides P2/P3; auto modes choose the requested fallback
when no outside-isolate strong character determines paragraph direction.

All offsets are Unicode scalar indices, not UTF-8 byte positions. Strict UTF-8
validation rejects overlong, truncated, surrogate, and out-of-range encodings.
Input containing more than one paragraph is rejected atomically. Empty input
succeeds. A final paragraph separator is accepted. Control characters, including
X9-removed characters, remain in the output permutation; consumers must suppress
formatting controls when painting. Odd-level runs are read from their logical
end toward their start. Mirrored output is analysis data; choosing the corresponding
mirrored glyph still belongs to the shaping engine.

Callers provide disjoint output buffers and a scalar decoding workspace. Each
capacity must be at least the UTF-8 byte length, a conservative bound sufficient
for every scalar/run. A capacity error, invalid input, or backend allocation
failure leaves all outputs and the result unchanged; workspace is scratch and
may change. Input and arrays must be valid for their declared sizes. The backend
uses transient heap objects, so the workspace contract does not promise an
allocation-free algorithm. The wrapper never changes SheenBidi's global allocator.
Do not change that global allocator concurrently with processing. Upstream
reference counts and scratch allocation are thread-safe by default; scratch
buffers may be retained in the backend's global pool after a call.

The headless test accepts paths to the pinned Unicode `BidiCharacterTest.txt`
and `BidiTest.txt`. It checks every expected level and visual position after
filtering X9-removed characters. The full suites pass 91,707 character cases
and 770,241 property/direction cases. Property tests use one representative
Unicode scalar per bidi class as permitted by the Unicode test instructions.
They cover isolates, embeddings, numbers, neutral/bracket resolution and deep
nesting. Additional checks cover malformed UTF-8, conservative capacities,
atomic failure, paragraph rejection, empty input and mirroring.

This API does not yet connect to rendering, font fallback, shaping, grapheme
cluster ordering (L3), wrap-position selection, caret navigation, hit testing, or
selection. In particular, reversing scalar indices in a run is not sufficient
to render a cluster correctly: shaping and cluster handling must follow. No
claim of complete international-text rendering parity is made.

CMake builds this as the optional `cui_bidi` static library by default. Disable it
with `-DCUI_BUILD_BIDI=OFF`; Core does not link it implicitly. Installed consumers
can use `pkg-config --cflags --libs cui-bidi`. Its archive contains the private
backend objects, so consumers do not need a separate SheenBidi library.

For manual integration compile `Source/SheenBidi.c` with `SB_CONFIG_UNITY` and private
include paths `third_party/sheenbidi/Headers` and `third_party/sheenbidi/Source`.
Only the CUI header is public. Preserve upstream notices and LICENSE in bundles.

## Reusable paragraph and wrapped-line analysis

`cui_bidi_paragraph_create` analyzes the complete paragraph through I2 once,
copying decoded scalars into an owned immutable object. The caller can reuse both
input and decoding workspace immediately. `cui_bidi_paragraph_destroy` releases
the object and backend references; NULL destruction is accepted. No vendor type
appears in the CUI public API. Creation leaves the output pointer unchanged on
invalid UTF-8, insufficient workspace, multiple paragraphs, or allocation failure.

`cui_bidi_paragraph_levels` returns the paragraph levels before L1, scalar count,
and paragraph base. `cui_bidi_paragraph_line` takes a nonempty scalar range inside
that paragraph and applies L1/L2 to that line using the original paragraph
analysis. The caller chooses ranges after determining wrap positions. A Latin
continuation of a Hebrew paragraph consequently retains the Hebrew base;
resolving the continuation alone with auto direction would change that base.
Explicit embeddings and isolates crossing a wrap retain their paragraph context.
Line-local trailing whitespace resets to the paragraph base under L1.

Line output levels use indices relative to the requested range. Mapping entries
and run logical starts remain absolute paragraph scalar indices. Result scalar
count is the requested line length. Output capacity needs only that scalar
length, and every output and result remains unchanged on any failure. Paragraph
level output capacity needs the paragraph scalar count. Empty paragraphs are
valid objects but have no nonempty line range. Neither function mutates the
paragraph, so independent output buffers can be used concurrently, provided
no thread destroys the object or changes the backend global allocator.

Tests compare paragraph levels and every wrapped-line run, level, mirror and
visual scalar position with the pinned upstream paragraph/line API, across
Hebrew, Arabic, numbers, paired brackets, an isolate spanning wraps and explicit
embeddings. They also verify the L1 trailing-space reset, retained RTL base,
caller-buffer independence, bounds including SIZE_MAX, insufficient capacities,
empty objects and atomic preservation of every output buffer.

This adds wrapped-line bidi analysis, not a complete wrapping or shaping system.
Offsets are scalars, and callers must choose boundaries between whole grapheme
and shaping clusters. The API does not enforce those boundaries or apply L3.
Shaping, font fallback, painting, caret/selection and hit testing remain separate
integration work; no rendering parity is claimed.
documents.docs/BIDI_SHAPING.md:
# Optional bidirectional glyph layout

`cui_font_layout_line` adds an explicit bidirectional shaping path alongside the
existing `cui_font_measure*` and `cui_font_draw*` functions. When enabled, those
ordinary calls also use this shaping path with automatic paragraph direction.
The explicit line API returns an owned `cui_text_layout`, a borrowed view
of visual glyphs and runs, and `cui_text_layout_draw` to rasterize that positioned
layout. Public types contain only portable CUI and C types.

The full UTF-8 paragraph is analyzed by the pinned Unicode 17 bidi module. The
caller then selects a scalar line range (SIZE_MAX length means through the end).
L1/L2 use the full paragraph context, including embeddings and isolates crossing
wraps. Visual directional runs are split into logical script subruns. Script
properties come from the linked HarfBuzz Unicode functions. Common/Inherited/
Unknown characters adopt a preceding strong script in the directional run, or
the next strong script when none precedes them; a wholly weak run remains Common.
This is basic script itemization, not full UAX #24 Script_Extensions resolution.

RTL script subruns are placed in reverse subrun order. Each logical UTF-8 subrun
is shaped with an explicit HarfBuzz direction, script, language (BCP47 or default
`und`) and `MONOTONE_GRAPHEMES` cluster level. HarfBuzz's output glyph order is
preserved, including ligatures and combining glyphs sharing one cluster. There
is no scalar-level reversal of shaped glyphs. The shaping input uses the selected
line as pre/post context; BOT/EOT flags mark the line's actual boundaries. Bidi
paragraph context is retained, but Arabic joining does not cross a line boundary.
Default ignorables, including bidi formatting controls, affect shaping but are
removed from the final glyph stream. HarfBuzz handles direction-dependent glyph
mirroring; the scalar mirror output from the bidi analyzer is not reshaped.

Glyph `cluster_byte` values are absolute byte offsets into the original UTF-8
paragraph, including for a wrapped line starting after byte zero. They may repeat
or skip source bytes; they are not scalar indices or one-to-one caret positions.
Run byte ranges use the same source coordinates. Glyph `x/y` are final origins
relative to the line baseline, with y increasing downward; advances use that same
coordinate convention. Width is the sum of absolute horizontal subrun advances,
not an ink bounding box. Height/ascent come from the primary and used fallback face metrics. View
arrays remain valid until layout destruction.

Creation owns all glyph/run storage and releases transient paragraph/shaper
buffers before return. Input text may be reused immediately. Allocation and
validation failures preserve the caller's layout output pointer. The layout retains its selected and fallback faces independently of caller
references: closing fonts or replacing registrations does not invalidate it.
Borrowed fallback/style registrations still require their source handles to stay
alive for future layout creation until the registration is cleared. Fonts are UI-thread confined, as in the existing text adapter. Draw
coordinates refer to the line top-left; partial raster failure can already have
emitted glyph callbacks. The renderer can instead consume the portable glyph
view. Drawing another glyph size between layout creation and drawing is safe:
the saved layout size is reapplied to the face.

## Integration

When both optional native text and bidi targets exist, define `CUI_TEXT_BIDI` for
`cui_text` and link it privately to `cui_bidi`. Without that definition, the new
creation function returns `CUI_TEXT_LAYOUT_UNAVAILABLE` without modifying its
output; plain text needs no bidi link. No public compile definition is necessary.
The normal native text adapter still requires FreeType and HarfBuzz.

Register `tests/unit/test_text.c` as a new test linked to `cui_text`, `cui_bidi`
and the existing FreeType/HarfBuzz package target, with a private include path
`third_party/sheenbidi/Headers`. Define `CUI_TEXT_BIDI` for the test target when enabled, and keep assertions
active. Without that definition, the same test checks the atomic UNAVAILABLE
contract and needs no bidi/HarfBuzz reference include or link. The test uses
`CUI_TEST_FONT` or a portable Noto/DejaVu/Liberation font search, and
`CUI_TEST_ARABIC_FONT` or Noto Sans Arabic/DejaVu Sans. The Arabic case checks
character coverage and explicitly logs any untested joining/mark raster case.
It compares visual directional coverage/levels directly to pinned SheenBidi,
then glyph IDs, source clusters, offsets and advances directly to HarfBuzz. It
checks mixed Latin/Hebrew/Arabic/numbers/brackets, isolates, nonzero wrapped-line
source offsets, RTL script-subrun ordering, actual Arabic mark clusters and
joining with a supporting face, style face selection, invalid UTF-8 and atomic
failure. Existing ASCII metrics and raster checksums match the plain interface.
Both enabled and disabled builds compile with strict warnings; enabled tests
pass with address and undefined-behavior sanitizers.

The linked HarfBuzz and selected font determine shaping/version coverage. These
headless comparisons demonstrate the tested shaping and bidi behavior, not
complete international-text rendering parity. No system font installation is
performed.

## Limits

The caller chooses line breaks at complete grapheme/shaping-cluster boundaries;
this API accepts scalar ranges and does not enforce cluster-safe boundaries,
compute wrapping widths, or expose unsafe-to-break glyph flags. Script/directional
itemization is basic and is not a full cluster-aware script resolver. Existing
style registration selects the primary face; an explicit caller chain can
supply complete script/directional subruns. There is no OS font discovery or
per-grapheme mixed-face fallback inside a subrun. There is no language detection,
vertical layout, justification, caret mapping, selection or hit testing. Core,
widgets and backend commands using the native text adapter benefit from the
enabled ordinary-call routing. No other Core/widget behavior is changed.

The shaping contracts follow the primary
[HarfBuzz buffer documentation](https://harfbuzz.github.io/harfbuzz-hb-buffer.html)
and [cluster documentation](https://harfbuzz.github.io/working-with-harfbuzz-clusters.html);
paragraph/run rules follow [Unicode 17 UAX #9](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/tr9-51.html).

## Ordinary text and hard lines

With `CUI_TEXT_BIDI` enabled, ordinary styled/unstyled measure and draw calls
analyze each P1 paragraph with auto-LTR fallback, use script/direction shaping,
and paint its visual glyph stream. These calls support every Unicode B paragraph
separator (LF, CR, U+001C/U+001D/U+001E, NEL and U+2029). CRLF is one break.
U+2028 creates a hard line inside the same paragraph, preserving the complete
paragraph direction/isolate/embedding context across that break. Separators
produce no glyphs. Empty and trailing lines still occupy one face line height.

Measurement returns maximum line advance width and the sum of line heights.
Drawing resets horizontal origin to the caller's x for each line and advances
the top/baseline by that face's line height. Empty text occupies one empty line,
as in the existing measurement interface. Every line is fully laid out before
any raster callback: malformed UTF-8 or allocation failure emits nothing and
returns false; measurement returns {0,0}. Raster failures can still be partial.
The explicit glyph-layout API permits an empty scalar range and retains that
paragraph's base and metrics, allowing empty U+2028 continuation lines.

Tests independently reproduce the original FreeType/HarfBuzz ASCII shaping and
raster loop to compare legacy single-line glyph pixels, metrics and baselines,
including ligatures/kerning. Ordinary mixed RTL/multiline rendering is compared
against explicitly selected paragraph-line layouts, whose run/glyph data is
checked against the upstream references. Tests cover all B separators, CRLF,
U+2028 context, empty/trailing lines, baseline progression and invalid input
following a valid line. Real Arabic joining/mark raster checks also call the
ordinary adapter APIs. Disabled builds retain the original adapter path.

This is hard-line processing, not automatic word wrapping or a caret system.
The simple script itemization/fallback limitations above still apply. Each
explicit U+2028 line currently reanalyzes its paragraph; large numbers of such
lines may warrant caching reusable analysis in a future text-layout object.

## Explicit caller-registered font fallback

`cui_font_set_fallbacks` installs an ordered borrowed chain of actual CUI font
handles; `cui_font_register_fallbacks` opens and owns an ordered list of file
paths. Both replace the complete chain transactionally, accept zero entries to
clear, and reject counts above `CUI_FONT_FALLBACK_MAX` (32), NULL entries,
duplicates/self handles for the borrowed setter, and failing paths. A failed
call leaves the old chain working and releases partially opened owned faces.
Current owned entries cannot be reborrowed into the replacing chain.

The chain belongs to the root handle passed to layout/measurement/drawing, not
to a style variant. Existing style-selection rules are applied to the primary
and each direct fallback entry. Chains are not recursively traversed. Borrowed
fallback and style handles must remain alive while registered for future calls.
Owned entries are released on replacement/owner close. Font close releases a
reference, and layouts retain each actual candidate face independently: a layout
can still be painted after chain/style replacement or caller font close. Its
view exposes borrowed retained CUI handles in `faces`; never close those view
handles. `run.face_index` identifies the face whose glyph IDs the run contains.
All font/registration operations remain confined to the UI thread.

Coverage is chosen for each entire script/directional subrun. The first face
that shapes the complete subrun without glyph zero is selected. This keeps
joining Arabic letters and their marks together and never switches faces inside
a HarfBuzz output cluster. HarfBuzz's REMOVE_DEFAULT_IGNORABLES flag lets joining controls, CGJ,
variation selectors and tags affect shaping without requiring standalone cmap
entries. Coverage uses actual shaped output, not nominal cmap checks: valid
normalization/composition can cover combining sequences even when a standalone
mark has no cmap entry. Every visible shaped glyph must be nonzero.
No complete covering face, or any shaped glyph zero, yields explicit
`CUI_TEXT_LAYOUT_MISSING_GLYPH` and preserves the output pointer. Ordinary draw
returns false with no callbacks if layout/coverage fails; ordinary measure returns
{0,0}. Missing-glyph tofu is not reported as a successful fallback layout.

Runs use their selected faces for both HarfBuzz shaping and FreeType rasterization.
All glyph origins share one baseline. If fallback is actually used, ascent and
descent are maxima across the primary and used faces, and line height is the
maximum of all used native line heights and combined ascent/descent. No-fallback
lines preserve the existing primary face height exactly, including rounded metric
conventions. Unused registered fallback faces do not enlarge the line. Hard-line
baseline progression uses each computed line height. `cui_font_get_metrics` remains
the selected primary face's generic metrics, since it has no text argument;
text-specific fallback extents are available from layout/measurement.

Tests verify a Noto Latin primary actually lacks Arabic/Hebrew, then compare
successful fallback glyph IDs, marks, advances and pixels with direct HarfBuzz/
FreeType shaping on the registered script faces. They verify original source
clusters, script run order, mixed baseline maxima, Arabic joiners/marks/VS/CGJ,
missing coverage failures, first-fit selection, invalid/capacity registration,
partial owned-open cleanup, style-face selection, and retained raster stability
after owned/borrowed chain replacement and root/variant font close. ASCII metrics
and raster regressions remain unchanged. Font lookup also accepts portable
DejaVu faces and explicit `CUI_TEST_FONT`, `CUI_TEST_ARABIC_FONT` and
`CUI_TEST_HEBREW_FONT`; cases already covered by the primary are explicitly logged
as untested missing-primary cases rather than inventing missing-glyph evidence.

Without bidi enabled, chain registration/lifetime APIs still work and are tested,
but the existing legacy ordinary shaping path does not consult the chain; explicit
layout creation remains UNAVAILABLE. There is no automatic system font discovery,
color-emoji rendering, per-grapheme mixed-face segmentation, automatic word
wrapping, or caret/selection/hit-test implementation. Whole-run coverage may fail
when separate fonts collectively cover a run but no one font covers it completely.

## Renderer fixture validation

The native software renderer test no longer treats nonempty `.notdef` pixels as
multilingual evidence. Its Arabic and Hebrew samples first create layouts on
explicit optional fixture faces and assert every source glyph ID is nonzero.
Those validated faces are registered in the primary font's fallback chain, and
ordinary drawing is checked against the explicit layout's raster checksum,
coverage and measurement. Existing ASCII/ligature and renderer geometry checks
remain independent. Tests search known portable Noto/DejaVu/Liberation fixture
paths, or honor `CUI_TEST_ARABIC_FONT` and `CUI_TEST_HEBREW_FONT`; missing or
unsupported fixtures explicitly report the script case skipped. With bidi OFF,
the test reports source-glyph proof unavailable and keeps its ordinary ASCII
regressions. Legacy nonempty tofu pixels are never labeled successful RTL proof.
This fixture search is test setup, not production OS font discovery.

The native line layout also exposes a cluster-boundary geometry foundation.
`view.clusters` partitions each shaped directional/script subrun into complete
HarfBuzz monotone grapheme clusters, sorted by visual advance position. Byte
ranges remain offsets into the original paragraph, including caller-selected
wrapped lines. Geometry uses glyph advance pens, not ink extents or glyph offsets;
selection rectangles use the layout's common baseline line height across actual
fallback faces. Layout ownership retains both these arrays and their faces.

`cui_text_layout_carets` reports the preceding logical cluster's end (upstream)
and following logical cluster's start (downstream). At directional transitions
these affinities can have distinct visual positions. Results sort by x, then
upstream before downstream. Empty lines provide both affinities at x=0 and the
original line offset. `cui_text_layout_hit_test` projects finite coordinates onto
this single line and chooses the nearest cluster edge; equal distances prefer
the requested affinity, then the first cluster in visual order. The y coordinate
is validated but does not choose another line. Default-ignorable bytes omitted
by shaping attach to the adjacent logical cluster; a wholly omitted subrun has
one zero-width cluster. Zero-width edges follow the same deterministic tie rule.

`cui_text_layout_selection` normalizes reversed logical endpoints and emits one
rectangle per complete selected cluster, in visual order, including zero-width
rectangles. Callers can merge adjacent rectangles for painting. Caret and
selection endpoints inside a cluster (including interior ligature or combining
mark offsets) are rejected. NULL output with zero capacity queries the count;
INVALID and CAPACITY leave both output and count unchanged. Hit-test invalid
inputs also preserve output. All three APIs return UNAVAILABLE without changing
outputs in BIDI-off builds.

This is not full editing caret parity: there are no GDEF ligature interior
carets, independent stops inside omitted controls, cross-run grapheme analysis,
visual keyboard navigation, multi-line hit-testing, or Core/Edit/Textarea wiring.
Fonts can shape several characters into one cluster, so a valid UTF-8 character
boundary need not be an accepted geometry boundary. Actual automatic word
wrapping and editor selection/caret policies remain caller responsibilities.
The cluster grouping follows [HarfBuzz's cluster model](https://harfbuzz.github.io/working-with-harfbuzz-clusters.html);
interior ligature carets would additionally require the optional
[OpenType GDEF ligature caret list](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/gdef#ligature-caret-list-table).

# Build a native UI in Python, JavaScript or TypeScript

For installable local wheel, npm, Go module and Rust crate artifacts, see the
[packaging guide](PACKAGING.md). Linux alpha packages are tested outside the
checkout; registry publication and other platform packages remain pending.

The component builders let you author a UI tree in your language. CUI performs
layout and input handling in C; the optional SDL adapter draws a native window.
The bridge exposes tested API subsets for all 78 catalog families through native CUI renderers and app services,
plus rows, columns, radio groups and composite items. Python, JavaScript,
TypeScript, [Go](GO_BUILDERS.md) and [Rust](RUST_BUILDERS.md) construct these
components in their own language and receive copied events after C frames.
This is a tested API subset for each family. The
[component coverage and limitations](BRIDGE_COMPONENTS.md) identify unsupported
options; the [machine-readable coverage](binding-coverage.json) keeps all 78 entries.
Clipboard and Theme are app services; the other families have component builders.
This is language authoring coverage, not complete option or feature parity.

## Dependencies and compiler

Build from the repository root with CMake 3.20+, Ninja, a C11 compiler and
Python 3.10+. GCC and Clang work on Linux. Python uses standard-library `ctypes`,
without pip dependencies. Node additionally needs Node 18+ and its development
headers (`node_api.h`); no npm packages or node-gyp are required. The TypeScript
example uses Node's built-in type stripping, tested here with Node 25.

Native windows additionally require installed SDL3 3.2+, FreeType, HarfBuzz,
pkg-config and an existing TrueType/OpenType font. CMake discovers and links
these libraries. Set the font path explicitly. A missing native adapter reports
an error when you request SDL; it does not silently select headless mode.

The portable C bridge and Python have Linux, macOS and Windows CI evidence for
the previously published control subset. Node, Go and Rust runtime validation
uses Linux. The expanded model tests run headlessly on Linux; native Windows
and macOS binding applications have not been validated. Windows DLL exports,
Node import library discovery and macOS Node linker settings are provided. See the [platform matrix](PLATFORM_MATRIX.md).

## Python: build and launch

```sh
cmake -S bindings/bridge -B build-bridge -G Ninja
cmake --build build-bridge --target cui_bridge test_bridge_core test_bridge_components
ctest --test-dir build-bridge -R '^bridge_' --output-on-failure
export CUI_BRIDGE_LIBRARY="$PWD/build-bridge/libcui_bridge.so"
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/bindings/python"
export CUI_TEST_FONT=/path/to/your/font.ttf
python bindings/bridge/examples/save_changes.py
```

The example opens a native window with a Save button and a status label. Clicking
Save updates the label. Its UI is defined in Python:

```python
import os
from cui_bridge import App, button, label, row

status = label("Ready", key="status")
save = (button("save").primary().rounded_md().size("base")
        .label("Save changes").on_click(lambda event: status.label("Saved")))

with App(backend="sdl", title="My CUI app", width=480, height=240,
         font_path=os.environ["CUI_TEST_FONT"]) as app:
    app.mount(row().gap_units(2).children(save, status))
    app.run()
```

For a window-free check, use `App()` without SDL. After mounting, call
`app.step()`, obtain `(x, y, w, h) = app.bounds(save)`, queue pointer down/up
inside that rectangle, call `app.step()` and then `app.dispatch()`. The checked-in
[Python tests](../bindings/python/test_bridge.py) demonstrate this using actual
CUI hit testing. Headless mode computes layout and draw commands; it does not
paint a window or provide native font metrics.

## JavaScript and TypeScript: build and launch

```sh
cmake -S bindings/node -B build-node -G Ninja
cmake --build build-node --target cui_node_bindings test_bridge_core test_bridge_components
ctest --test-dir build-node -R '^(bridge_|node_)' --output-on-failure
node bindings/node/examples/save.cjs --headless
export CUI_FONT_PATH=/path/to/your/font.ttf
node bindings/node/examples/save.cjs
node bindings/typescript/examples/save.ts
```

The shared bridge and Node addon are built together. CMake supplies include paths
and linker flags; the addon remains in the build directory. If you choose another
directory, set `CUI_NODE_ADDON` to its absolute `cui.node` path. On Windows the
Node project also requires `node.lib` and reports an actionable configure error
if it is unavailable.

Maintainers can repeat the Linux native checks without desktop windows by
configuring the Node build with `-DCUI_BRIDGE_NATIVE_TESTS=ON` and
`-DCUI_TEST_FONT=/path/to/font.ttf`, then running
`python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir build-node -- -R '^(bridge_|node_)'`.
These opt-in checks need Xvfb, xwininfo, xwd, xdotool and ImageMagick's convert.
The runner clears inherited desktop sockets and launches a disposable display;
native probes refuse to run without that isolation marker.

```js
const {App, row, label, button} = require('./bindings/node');
const status = label('Ready');
const save = button('save').primary().rounded_md().base()
  .label('Save changes').on_click(() => status.label('Saved'));
const app = new App({backend: 'sdl', width: 480, height: 240,
  title: 'My CUI app', fontPath: process.env.CUI_FONT_PATH});
app.mount(row().gap_units(2).children(save, status));
app.start();
```

`start()` schedules frames with Node timers so other timers and I/O can run.
Closing the native window disposes the app. Use `stop()` to stop scheduling,
`close()` to request closure, and `dispose()` to release resources explicitly.
The [TypeScript example](../bindings/typescript/examples/save.ts) uses the same
builders and [type declarations](../bindings/typescript/index.d.ts). Node type
stripping executes the example; it does not perform static type checking.

## Styling, state and callbacks

Buttons support primary, secondary, outline and ghost variants, disabled state,
theme rounding or an explicit radius, and custom hover colors for primary,
secondary and outline variants. Sizes cover `xs`, `sm`, `base`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`,
`2xl` through `9xl`; `base` is the default. Python uses `.size("sm")`; JS/TS
also offer `.sm()`, `.md()` and `.lg()`. `rounded_md()` maps to the existing
larger rounding preset. Arbitrary CSS properties and per-button padding overrides
are not exposed yet.

`gap_px(8)` means eight logical pixels. `gap_units(2)` also means eight logical
pixels, using four pixels per unit. `gap(8)` retains the explicit-pixel meaning.
Python's `step()` and `dispatch()` are separate; JS `step()` performs both.
Callbacks execute after the C frame has finished, so exceptions remain in your
language. A callback can update labels, disable a button or close the app.

The language layer retains its tree; the bridge owns copied strings, stable IDs
and button state and composes immediate CUI frames. Nodes belong to one app.
Disposed or stale handles are rejected. Keep each app on one thread and serialize **all calls across all apps**: the
core uses a process-global Clay context. Explicitly release each app, and drain its bounded event queue. Most strings must be valid UTF-8 without
embedded NUL, at most 4096 bytes. Clipboard accepts 64 KiB; Settings search accepts
256 bytes; chart labels and table cells accept 128 bytes. Trees support up to 128 levels including their
root; deeper construction is rejected before frame submission.
See the [C ABI guide](../bindings/bridge/docs/README.md)
and [public header](../include/cui/cui_bridge.h) for capacities and status codes.

[Go builders](GO_BUILDERS.md) and [Rust builders](RUST_BUILDERS.md) now construct
real component trees in their own language and dispatch copied native events.
The older [C-host examples](LANGUAGE_BINDINGS.md) remain useful for embedding an
existing C-authored application.

## Form controls and copied change events

`on_change` receives a snapshot captured when the C component changed. Read
`event.checked`, `event.value`, or `event.text`; these remain accurate even when
multiple frames are queued before Python dispatch. JavaScript dispatches after
each `step()`. Programmatic setters update the model without emitting user events.
`radio` is standalone; use `radio_group` with `item` children for exclusive choice.

```python
from cui_bridge import App, column, checkbox, input, label, slider

status = label("Ready")
notifications = checkbox("notifications", "Enable notifications").checked()
name = input("name", "Alex").on_change(lambda event: status.label(event.text))
volume = slider("volume").range(0, 100, 1).value(50)
with App() as app:
    app.mount(column().gap_units(2).children(name, notifications, volume, status))
    app.step()  # Headless layout; choose backend="sdl" and font_path for a native window.
```

```javascript
const cui = require('./bindings/node/index.cjs');
const status = cui.label('Ready');
const name = cui.input('name', 'Alex').on_change(event => status.label(event.text));
const app = new cui.App();
app.mount(cui.column().gap_units(2).children(
  name, cui.checkbox('notifications', 'Enable notifications').checked(),
  cui.slider('volume').range(0, 100, 1).value(50), status
)).step();
app.dispose();
```

The Python and Node `test_components` fixtures exercise real pointer hit testing,
disabled behavior, numeric ranges, UTF-8 edits, grouped selection and panel visibility.
Design sizes, rounding, and custom hover styling currently apply to Button;
other component styling APIs are a separate unfinished bridge capability.

## Dialogs, trees, images and date entry

Surface builders use `open()` and `on_close()`; popovers and hover surfaces
require a live `anchor(node)`. Dialog, Sheet and Popover accept child components.
AlertDialog uses its native confirmation actions. A Tree uses up to 64 flat Item
children in preorder; Item `step_status(depth)` sets depth and `checked(True)`
starts a branch expanded. In JavaScript use `checked(true)`.

`image_rgba(pixels, width, height, stride)` accepts decoded RGBA8 bytes. Both the
builder and C bridge own copies. Dimensions are 1–2048, stride is at least
`width * 4`, and byte count must equal `stride * height`, at most 16 MiB. Decode
PNG/JPEG files in your application. Attachment currently exposes metadata and
progress; its bridge has no file transfer, remove or retry actions.

Calendar and DatePicker accept `date_value(year, month, day)`, including old
dates, and expose `current_date()`. The current bridge uses English single-date
mode. TimeField uses `time_value(hour, minute, second)` and `current_time()`.
ColorPicker uses packed `0xRRGGBBAA` with `color_rgba()` and `current_color()`;
its event copies both the packed number and `#RRGGBBAA` text. OTPInput uses
`total(cells)` and `current_text()`; send one cell per queued text-input event.

The runnable workspace examples compose navigation tabs, account fields,
notification preferences, date entry and a confirmation dialog. They create
actual component trees. Use `--headless` for their deterministic interaction
checks or omit it for a native window:

```sh
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/bindings/python"
export CUI_BRIDGE_LIBRARY="$PWD/build-bridge/libcui_bridge.so"
python bindings/bridge/examples/workspace.py --headless
# Native: set CUI_TEST_FONT to an existing font first.
python bindings/bridge/examples/workspace.py
node bindings/node/examples/workspace.cjs --headless
# Native: set CUI_FONT_PATH to an existing font first.
node bindings/node/examples/workspace.cjs
```

Only Button exposes the bridge's design sizes, rounding and hover-color styling
at this stage. Other families use native defaults and the specific options
listed in the coverage guide; a constructor does not imply all native options
are mapped. Headless tests cover events and lifetime; they do not prove native
pixel rendering on every operating system.

Form accepts Item fields whose children are real controls; Item label/detail
supply field metadata. Disabling Form or a field suppresses its child controls.
InputGroup uses editable text and Item button addons; Item `step_status(0..3)`
chooses the addon alignment and `on_click` receives addon presses.
Notification is an in-app card. It uses title/detail, `open`, `is_open`, click and
close callbacks. Cards share one stack; there is no OS notification delivery,
autohide or action-button API in this bridge subset. The close callback arrives after the close animation completes;
`is_open()` becomes false when dismissal starts. Set the title/detail before opening.

FocusTrap accepts children and `open()`/`is_open()`. Its open modal focus scope
blocks pointer actions outside the subtree; closing restores outside interaction.

## Native fonts and fallback faces

Pass an existing font file that covers your text. Missing glyphs cause a render
error. Python and JavaScript/TypeScript let you replace the SDL font's ordered,
owned fallback chain with `app.font_fallbacks(["/absolute/path/symbols.ttf"])`.
The chain accepts at most 32 paths; `[]` clears it. Configure it before frames.
Go provides `Options.FontFallbacks` and `SetFontFallbacks`; Rust provides
`app.font_fallbacks(&["/absolute/path/symbols.ttf"])`. The bridge opens and owns
the fallback faces and rejects an invalid replacement without discarding the
previous chain. Fallback registration requires SDL; headless mode reports that
the backend is unavailable. It does not scan your machine for fonts.

## Sidebar navigation with editable pages

These examples define their layout and controls in Python or JavaScript. The
Sidebar selects Account or Preferences; Tabs provides the page content. Account
contains a native Input and a Save callback that reads its current text. No
C-authored application is launched behind the language API.

```sh
# Use the bridge and addon builds from the earlier sections.
python bindings/bridge/examples/sidebar_workspace.py --headless
node bindings/node/examples/sidebar-workspace.cjs --headless
# Open native windows when you want to interact with the example.
CUI_TEST_FONT=/absolute/path/font.ttf python bindings/bridge/examples/sidebar_workspace.py
CUI_FONT_PATH=/absolute/path/font.ttf node bindings/node/examples/sidebar-workspace.cjs
```

```python
from cui_bridge import (button, checkbox, column, input, item, label,
                        root_view, row, sidebar, tabs)

status = label('Ready', key='status')
name = input('name', 'Alex Morgan')
email = checkbox('email', 'Email notifications').checked()
save = button('save').label('Save changes').primary().rounded_md().on_click(
    lambda event: status.label('Saved account: ' + name.current_text()))
account = item('account-page', 'Account').children(
    column().gap_units(3).children(label('Account details'), name, save, status))
preferences = item('preferences-page', 'Preferences').children(
    column().gap_units(3).children(label('Notifications'), email))
pages = tabs('pages').children(account, preferences).select(account)
account_action = item('account-action', 'Account').on_click(lambda event: pages.select(account))
preferences_action = item('preferences-action', 'Preferences').on_click(lambda event: pages.select(preferences))
navigation = sidebar('navigation').visual_size(180, 280).children(account_action, preferences_action)
root = root_view().padding(24).children(column().gap_units(4).children(
    label('CUI workspace'), row().gap_units(6).children(navigation, pages)))
```

Mount `root` on the SDL `App` described above and run its event loop. The checked-in
[Python example](../bindings/bridge/examples/sidebar_workspace.py) includes both
the window loop and a deterministic headless interaction check. The
[JavaScript example](../bindings/node/examples/sidebar-workspace.cjs) builds the
same UI; [Go](GO_BUILDERS.md) and [Rust](RUST_BUILDERS.md) each include a composed
workspace with navigation, editing, callbacks and a confirmation dialog.

## Retained models and native interaction

The language builders retain a tree and owned data. CUI renders immediate frames
from that tree and manages native state for editors, scrolling, selection, dock
layouts, questionnaires and Settings. Event callbacks run after each C frame,
using copied snapshots rather than live pointers. With Python, dispatch events
explicitly after stepping; Node dispatches as part of `step()`.

MessageScroller contains Item messages; `detail` is the sender and
`step_status(0/1)` selects incoming/outgoing. It follows the newest message on
its initial frame. Carousel contains Item slides and provides `select` and
`selected`. Resizable contains Item panels with `panel_size(100..4096)` widths;
real divider dragging updates the panel and emits its numeric change event.
VirtualList contains up to 64 keyed Item rows in a fixed-height vertical viewport.
`scroll_to` and `scroll_offset` work on MessageScroller and VirtualList.

Editor owns multiline text and exposes `current_text` and copied change events.
TextView supports `text_format("markdown"|"html"|"plain")`, rendered UTF-8 byte
selection with `select_text`, and copied `selection_text`. Neither currently
exposes completion providers or clipboard shortcuts through the bridge.

Chart copies `chart_data([["Label", value], ...])` and accepts
`chart_kind("line"|"area"|"bar"|"pie")`. Table contains Item rows with Item text
cells; the first row is the header. DataTable copies `table_data(headers, rows)`
and supports `selection_mode("row"|"column"|"cell")`. Its change event text is
JSON containing `reason`, `row`, `column`, `sortColumn` and `sortDirection`.
Indices are one-based, with zero meaning none. Sort events request an order;
replace the matrix yourself to apply it. Plot copies `plot_points([[x,y], ...])`;
its bridge subset draws dots and does not yet expose axes, pan/zoom or hit tests.

Command contains Item actions. `label` changes the native filter query;
`current_text` and `selected` read it back. An Item's `detail` adds a filter
keyword, and its click callback receives native confirmation. Sidebar contains
Item navigation actions and supports `open`, `select`, `selected` and copied
navigation events. RootView can be the sole root and adds `padding(0..256)`.

Questionnaire contains Item questions with Item choices. Before mounting, use
`question(required=True, multiple=False)` in Python or `question(true, false)`
in JavaScript. The first frame freezes the schema. `questionnaire_next`,
`questionnaire_previous`, `questionnaire_submit`, `questionnaire_state` and
`choice_selected` expose progress. Submission enforces native answer rules;
change events contain copied JSON snapshots of answers and navigation.

Dock contains Item panels with child controls. After its first frame,
`dock_activate`, `dock_move_split`, `dock_active` and `dock_panel_bounds` expose
its retained layout. `dock_serialize` returns copied opaque `CUIDOCK 1` text,
not JSON. Panel metadata freezes on the first frame; restoring serialized layouts
and floating OS windows are not exposed yet.

## Settings pages and reset defaults

Settings uses Item pages, nested Item groups, then Switch, Checkbox, Input or
NumberInput fields. Input/NumberInput `detail` supplies the field title;
Input `label` supplies editable text and NumberInput `value` supplies its number. The first successful frame captures reset values
and freezes titles and topology. Only fields support disabled state.

```python
from cui_bridge import App, column, input, item, settings, switch

updates = switch("updates", "Automatic updates").checked()
name = input("name", "Alex").detail("Display name")
general = item("general", "General").children(
    item("account", "Account").children(updates, name))
preferences = settings("preferences").visual_size(760, 400).children(general)
with App(width=900, height=600) as app:
    app.mount(column().children(preferences))
    app.step()  # First frame captures defaults.
    name.label("Changed")
    preferences.settings_reset(general)
    app.dispatch()  # Reset delivers copied field change events.
    assert name.current_text() == "Alex"
```

`settings_query(text)` copies a search string of at most 256 UTF-8 bytes.
`settings_page()` reads the selected Item; `settings_select(page)` navigates and
emits a copied page event. `settings_field_bounds(field)` locates a visible
control for host input. `settings_reset(page)` restores all fields in that page,
including programmatic edits. The same method names work in JavaScript/TypeScript.
Limits are eight pages, 32 total groups and 128 total fields. Persist preferences
in your application; custom setting fields and dropdowns are not mapped yet.

## Theme, clipboard and speech services

`app.theme_presets()` returns native preset names. `app.theme_preset(index)`
changes one app's theme; `app.current_theme_preset()` is empty until an explicit
choice. The bridge does not automatically watch the host's appearance preference.

SDL apps support `clipboard_set(text)` and copied `clipboard_get()` on the owner
thread, outside a frame. Headless mode reports backend unavailable. Clipboard
text is valid UTF-8 without NUL, up to 64 KiB.

Speech exposes `speech_start`, `speech_report(text, final)`, `speech_finish`,
`speech_transcript` and `speech_active`. The host supplies recognition results;
this component does not capture audio or include a speech recognition provider.
Copied lifecycle events distinguish start, transcript and finish.

The [coverage guide](BRIDGE_COMPONENTS.md) documents capacities and unsupported
features for every family. [Validation receipts](validation/component-builders-expanded-78.txt)
record the combined checks and their platform limits.

For native callback loops, live resizing, callback failure containment and the
manual-loop compatibility contract, see [binding native runners](BINDING_NATIVE_RUN.md).

The optional `cui_date_time_picker.h` single civil date/time API is C-only in this revision. Generated source SDKs carry its header/implementation, but Python/JavaScript/TypeScript/Go/Rust builders and bridge records do not expose its typed value/state, assignment, options, helpers or result. Do not pass legacy date-only builder storage to it. See `docs/DATE_TIME_PICKER.md`.

# Native callback runners in language bindings

Python `App.run()`, Go `App.Run(dt)`, Rust `App::run()` / `run_with(...)` and
Node/TypeScript `App.run()` delegate to `cui_bridge_run`. The SDL callback loop
owns event pumping and frame scheduling so native modal resizing can continue
layout and paint. Call from the app's creating UI thread. Mount a tree first.
Python/Go retain and validate the legacy positive finite `dt` argument for source
compatibility; the native host supplies actual frame timing.

Application handlers execute after a completed native frame. They may update
nodes or request close. Nested run and step calls are rejected. Python and Node
retain the original exception, Go recovers a panic, and Rust uses `catch_unwind`;
all stop the C runner before rethrowing/resuming in the language caller. Rust
builds using `panic=abort` retain the toolchain's abort behavior. No language may
unwind through a C callback.

A normal window close returns normally. After the runner exits, its native host
is released and the app is terminal: release the app owner as usual. Python
`close()`, Node `dispose()` and Go `Close()` may also destroy the owner inside a
handler; the bridge defers actual destruction until the runner exits. These
wrappers invalidate their handles immediately and avoid using them afterward.
Rust ownership prevents dropping a mutably borrowed app while `run` is active;
use `run_with(|app| app.close())` for a safe close request/update hook.

Manual APIs remain: Python `step`/`dispatch`, Go `Step`/`Dispatch`, Rust
`step`/`dispatch`/`frame`, and Node `step`. Node `start`/`stop` still use timers and
keep the JavaScript event loop responsive. The synchronous native `run()` blocks
Node timers/I/O until closure; choose it when native modal-resize behavior is
needed. It cannot be combined with `start()` on the same app.

Dynamic wrappers resolve the new optional runner lazily. Older bridges can still
use manual APIs; runner use fails clearly when unavailable. Portable/headless
backends do not support the native runner. Rust's existing dynamic packaging
support is Linux; static Go/Rust builds require refreshed canonical SDK sources
containing the runner. No generated SDK snapshot is changed by this wrapper patch.

Validation lives in Python `test_run_native_virtual.py`, Node
`test/run-native.test.cjs`, Go `TestNativeRunLifecycle`, and Rust
`tests/run_native.rs`. Native tests require the isolated-display marker and font
path and must be launched through `scripts/test_local.py`; never point them at
the desktop display. They cover callback delivery, normal close, foreign failure
containment, terminal lifecycle and reentrancy; Python additionally exercises a
real X11 resize through the native runner. Underlying SDL live-resize behavior

# Controlled boolean Base requests

`cui_boolean_events.h` adds `cui_base_switch_events` and
`cui_base_toggle_events`. These portable C11 Base reducers draw nothing; submit
one inside its same-ID layout box. Switch retains `CUI_ROLE_SWITCH`; Toggle
retains `CUI_ROLE_BUTTON`. Neither is implemented by remapping Check semantics.
The separate shared `cui_control_events.h` provides the result and metadata types.
`cui_components.h` adds Styled `cui_switch_events` and `cui_toggle_events`.
Language bindings and generated build/export registration remain separate work.

```c
#include <cui/cui_boolean_events.h>

typedef struct { bool enabled, allow_change; } model;
static void requested(void *user, const cui_component_boolean_request *request) {
    model *state = user;
    if (state->allow_change)
        state->enabled = request->requested; /* Otherwise reject by leaving it alone. */
}
/* Caller submits the same-ID box during an ordinary frame. */
cui_component_action_result submit_flag(cui_context *ui, cui_id enabled_id, model *state) {
    return cui_base_switch_events(ui, enabled_id, cui_string("Enabled"), state->enabled,
        (cui_boolean_event_options){0},
        (cui_component_boolean_handler){requested, state});
}
```

The bool argument is an immutable entry snapshot. Each supported accepted event
invokes the optional callback synchronously with typed `current` and `requested`
values: `current` is the entry bool and `requested` its inverse. Two accepted
activations produce two identical value proposals, even when the owner accepts
the first. Semantics retain the entry snapshot during that submission; the next
submission observes owner assignments. There is no hidden write, getter, retained
value, acceptance return flag, or synthesized CHANGE notification.

Missing callback means read-only. `activation_count` still reports accepted
attempts; `request_count` counts callbacks actually delivered. Rejecting a request
does not undo Core input consumption or reroute it to the parent. Counts are
per invocation, saturate at `SIZE_MAX`, and set `count_overflow` if an increment
would overflow. Saturation does not stop dispatch. Reading or copying the result
has no event effects.

`valid` reports argument preflight: nonnull context, nonzero ID and readable-name
descriptor (nonempty names require nonnull data). It does not establish that the
frame will finish without layout/capacity/duplicate-ID errors. `submitted` means
ordinary active submission was reached, including disabled controls; it is false
outside an active frame, under inert/layout-only ancestry, and in protected
measurement/prepaint phases. Disabled/inert/omitted submissions dispatch nothing.
No loading state is added.

Options preserve role-default keyboard and pointer focus unless explicitly
modified. `no_pointer_focus` retains pointer activation and explicit/keyboard
focus; `skip_tab` and `tab_index` configure tab navigation. Base disabled Switch
and Toggle preserve their existing parent routing; they do not add Check's
required/focusable/disabled-hit-barrier policy. Existing mutable Base entry points
remain aggregate: several accepted events still produce one legacy bool flip.
Existing Styled aggregate callbacks are unchanged by this slice.

Request metadata comes from genuine accepted activation snapshots in event-index
order, frozen before the callback. It includes pointer/touch contact/device
identity, keyboard evidence or accessibility origin as present; never fabricate
pointer evidence for keyboard/accessibility. Request and metadata structs are
pointer-free and can be copied beyond callback/frame/context lifetime. The
callback pointer, user storage and name bytes remain borrowed for their existing
synchronous submission/frame boundaries.

The loop checks eligibility immediately before each delivery; it does not queue
all future callbacks. A callback consuming a later accessibility event can prevent
its later delivery. Core may already have accepted events during `cui_interact`:
`cui_cancel_event_activation` then returns false rather than undoing acceptance.
Cancellation before reducer submission remains effective. This API does not alter
Core's event-specific consumption rules.

Callbacks may update owner/unrelated state, omit later siblings through ordinary
caller control flow, or mark close/removal pending. **Destroying the active
context, recursively submitting the same component/frame, or freeing active
storage during a callback is unsupported.** Defer teardown until submission/frame
completion. No destruction guard, asynchronous callback registration, global
routing, or bridge-runner destruction guarantee is introduced.

The unit fixture exercises mouse/touch, Enter/Space/repeat filtering,
accessibility multiplicity and later-event consumption, both initial bool values,
owner acceptance/rejection, no-handler read-only behavior, invalid arguments,
protected phases, inert/layout-only/omitted/disabled submissions, exact role/focus
policy, disabled-parent routing, and legacy aggregate compatibility. Build
registration and generated SDK resources must be integrated by the module owner;
this guide does not claim those snapshots already contain the new API.


## Styled Switch and Toggle

The additive Styled facades accept the same bool snapshot and typed handler as
Base, plus existing appearance options and optional presentation state:

```c
/* During an ordinary frame, inside the application's parent layout box: */
cui_component_action_result submit_styled_flag(cui_context *ui, cui_id id,
                                               const cui_theme *theme, model *state,
                                               cui_switch_state *motion) {
    return cui_switch_events(ui, id, theme, cui_string("Enabled"), state->enabled,
        motion, (cui_switch_options){.size = CUI_CONTROL_SMALL},
        (cui_component_boolean_handler){requested, state});
}
```

Switch owns its root, track, thumb and label/content layout. Optional
`cui_switch_state` retains spring and tooltip presentation; it never owns the
boolean model. Toggle uses existing `cui_toggle_paint` and optional
`cui_hover_state` for its tooltip. Accessibility names, size/design metrics,
custom content, focus styling, disabled appearance and tooltip options retain
their existing roles. Do not wrap these Styled calls in another same-ID box;
that same-ID box requirement applies to the headless Base entry points.

Both legacy `on_change` **and** `change_user` option fields must be NULL, even
when the new handler is absent. Any conflict fails preflight with `valid=false`
before semantic submission, content callbacks, spring/tooltip mutation or paint.
Missing new handler remains read-only, rather than selecting legacy mutation.

A handler assignment changes application state immediately, while all requests,
semantics and paint in this invocation keep the original bool. The next
submission reflects the assignment. Passive inert/layout-only composition can
still measure/paint content, but emits no requests and does not mutate caller
spring or tooltip storage. Outside submission/protected phases the new facades
return without invoking content or touching presentation state.

Legacy `cui_switch_ex` and `cui_toggle_ex` remain aggregate. Their callbacks still
run before reading the external bool for semantic/paint updates. Switch's private
paint extraction retains its old dereference sequence: label-left content may
change the external value after spring-target calculation and before track-color
selection. The new facade deliberately supplies a local entry snapshot to that
same paint path; it does not retime legacy behavior.

`test_boolean_styled_events.c` checks controlled accept/reject painting and
semantics, pointer/key/accessibility multiplicity, read-only and disabled behavior,
all frozen size metrics and an explicit design size, custom content geometry,
all callback/user conflict combinations, passive storage preservation, and legacy
callback/content mutation timing. Existing Button/Check and Base boolean fixtures
remain independent regression coverage. Active-context destruction and recursive
submission remain unsupported as documented above; no cross-language event
coverage is implied.

`cui_bridge_poll_event_ex` copies queued CHANGE snapshots, including editable
text. A capacity failure preserves the event for retry. The legacy event poll
returns CLICK events and skips CHANGE events.

The table covers all 78 manifest families plus four bridge-only structural kinds
(Row, Column, RadioGroup, Item). Each row describes the supported subset; this
does not imply full source component parity.

Settings uses Item page and group nodes, with Switch, Checkbox, Input, or
NumberInput leaves. Set page/group and boolean-field titles with `set_text`;
set Input/NumberInput titles with `set_detail_text`. Set Input content with
`set_text` and NumberInput values with `set_value`. The first successful frame
captures reset defaults and freezes
field topology and titles. `settings_set_query` copies up to 256 UTF-8 bytes;
`settings_get_page` and `settings_field_bounds` require an initialized frame.
Page selection CHANGE events copy the selected handle. Field CHANGE events
copy the field's value or text; native reset emits one event for each field in
the page, including fields already at their default. Programmatic input and
number changes remain available after initialization, and reset restores the
captured defaults. Only individual fields accept `set_disabled`.

DataTable CHANGE events include copied JSON text with `reason` (`selection` or `sort`),
`row`, `column`, `sortColumn`, and `sortDirection`. The numeric event value is
the selected one-based row; use the JSON for exact column and sort snapshots
when multiple changes are queued. A caller can replace the matrix after a step
to implement the requested sort order.

The visual families above expose their documented default variants. Avatar is
an initials avatar with no image source. Marker is a single text child; Shimmer
is a single line. The bridge has no arbitrary C content callback entrypoint.
Scrollable currently uses a vertical viewport and caller-supplied extents.
All strings are copied and all event payloads are snapshots; none of these
limited variants implies full source component parity.

SDL applications can call `cui_bridge_set_font_fallbacks` with up to 32 explicit
UTF-8 font paths. The native font loader opens an owned replacement chain
transactionally; an invalid path leaves the old chain intact. A render failure
after backend creation returns `CUI_BRIDGE_CORE_ERROR` rather than reporting
the backend unavailable. The optional native regression test uses
`CUI_TEST_FONT_PATH` for a primary font without ✓ and
`CUI_TEST_FALLBACK_FONT_PATH` for a font with ✓; run it under isolated Xvfb.

# Bridge notification snapshots (V1)

The additive C API `cui_bridge_poll_notification_v1` returns a versioned typed view of the **existing** notification queue. It does not register callbacks, change timing, add input routing, or turn applied bridge mutations into controlled requests. The legacy ABI version, options, event structs and polling APIs remain unchanged. [The design](design/BRIDGE_TYPED_EVENTS_SLICE.md) includes future wrapper work; C, Python and JS/TypeScript manual polling are implemented here.

## Capability and polling

```c
#include <cui/cui_bridge.h>

static cui_bridge_status next_notification(cui_bridge_app *app,
                                           cui_bridge_notification_v1 *event,
                                           char text[4097], uint32_t *required) {
    if (!(cui_bridge_notification_versions() & 1u) ||
        cui_bridge_notification_v1_size() != sizeof(*event))
        return CUI_BRIDGE_INVALID_STATE;
    return cui_bridge_poll_notification_v1(app, sizeof(*event), event,
                                           text, 4097, required);
}
```

V1 capability is bit0. The size query includes native ABI padding; never pack the FFI struct manually. Exact size is required before consumption, and successful output includes `struct_size` and `schema_version=1`. Dynamically loaded consumers must look up the optional new symbols; older libraries lack them and continue supporting their old APIs. Future layouts require a new versioned symbol, not writes beyond V1 storage.

Step/render still produces snapshots before foreign-language dispatch. The V1 manual poll only consumes data; reading returned records never dispatches or changes component values. Poll V1, `poll_event_ex`, or filtered `poll_event` from one consumer: all drain the **same queue**, so mixed calls consume successive events rather than independent copies. The old filtered poll still skips/discards every non-CLICK event.

`kind` is ACTIVATE, CHANGE or LIFECYCLE. `payload_kind` determines the active union member. `node` and `node_kind` describe the origin captured at enqueue time; `legacy` retains the complete old checked/value/text-length/selected-handle snapshot. UTF-8 text is copied separately into caller storage. `frame_sequence` stays uint64; `HAS_FRAME` is present only for nonzero captured sequences. Identity is context-local, not a timestamp or global ordering. No input index, source, pointer/key/accessibility evidence, or Core `cui_id` is fabricated from bridge handles.

## Committed initial allowlist

The table is the complete typed producer allowlist for this slice. Do not enable additional tags solely because a generic numeric/text field looks plausible.

| Enqueue producer | `kind` / `payload_kind` | Typed payload |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Existing CLICK enqueue, including simple click adapters | ACTIVATE / NONE | No inferred input evidence. |
| Checkbox, Switch, Toggle CHANGE | CHANGE / BOOLEAN | `payload.boolean_value`, exactly0/1, already applied bridge state. |
| DataTable selection and sort | CHANGE / TABLE | `payload.table`: reason, row, column, sort_column, sort_direction, copied directly at the original enqueue point. |
| Existing CLOSE enqueue (surfaces and notification close) | LIFECYCLE / SURFACE | `payload.surface_result`, existing ACCEPTED/CANCELLED/CLOSED constants. |
| Every other CHANGE producer | CHANGE / LEGACY | Complete `legacy` fields and copied UTF-8 text; no guessed typed meaning. |

DataTable indices preserve the existing bridge convention: zero means no selected row/column/sort column; selected indices are one-based. The existing bridge supports at most16 columns and32 rows. Column2 and above remain integers in V1 instead of becoming booleans. Old `legacy.checked` still contains the raw column integer and old JSON remains unchanged. Typed table fields are captured beside JSON; no poll-time parsing or latest-state getter reconstructs them. Selection reason is `CUI_BRIDGE_TABLE_SELECTION`; sort reason is `CUI_BRIDGE_TABLE_SORT`.

SCALAR, TEXT and SELECTION tags/union members are reserved and **not emitted** by this slice. Input/Textarea/Editor/OTP, numeric controls, selection composites, date/time/color, questionnaire/speech/dock and other producers stay LEGACY. A selected-item handle in `legacy.selected` is a historical slot/generation snapshot. It may be stale at delivery; do not resolve it to a replacement node reusing that slot. Stale origins are dropped under the same rules as existing extended polling.

## Storage, failures and lifetime

Supply disjoint fixed-output, required-size and text storage, with the declared writable extents. Success copies complete text plus NUL, publishes the fixed result, and consumes exactly once. `text_length` excludes NUL. Empty text still needs capacity1. This poll allocates nothing, truncates nothing and adds no new text limit. Existing producers have their own bounds; common editable snapshots fit4096 bytes, so4097 is a useful starting buffer, not a universal schema limit.

On `CAPACITY`, only `required_capacity` changes. The live event remains queued, fixed output/text bytes remain unchanged, and retrying with that capacity retrieves the same snapshot. Preceding stale origins may already have been cleaned up; failure is not a transaction restoring stale entries. `EMPTY`, invalid size/arguments and other errors leave outputs unchanged. C callers choose allocation/retry policy. The Python and Node wrappers start with4097 bytes and retry once with the requested capacity, up to1MiB including NUL. An oversized, non-increasing or repeated capacity response raises an error without truncation; a capacity failure leaves the live event queued for another capable consumer. Memory allocation failures also propagate.

Queue storage keeps the existing max-event policy (default256, maximum4096). New typed fields add fixed per-slot bytes; no second queue or per-event typed allocation is introduced. Existing queued text allocations and failure handling remain. Queue exhaustion can happen after a component has mutated: a failed step does not roll back bridge state or previously queued events.

The returned struct and caller text copy remain valid after later frames, origin removal or app destruction, provided the caller storage survives. They do not own live nodes. C pointer copying is not ownership transfer, and copying arbitrary `cui_event` does not deep-copy borrowed text.

## Python and JS/TypeScript manual mode

Python already separates stepping from dispatch:

```python
app.step()
for event in app.poll_notifications_v1():
    if isinstance(event, BooleanChangeNotificationV1):
        print(event.value, event.frame_sequence)
```

Import `BooleanChangeNotificationV1` from `cui_bridge`. Python returns frozen dataclasses: `ActivationNotificationV1`, `BooleanChangeNotificationV1`, `TableChangeNotificationV1`, `SurfaceCloseNotificationV1`, or `LegacyNotificationV1`. Common fields include `handle` (slot/generation tuple), optional `node`, `frame_sequence` (exact Python integer), `has_frame`, `node_kind`, and frozen `legacy`. Table `reason` is `"selection"` or `"sort"`; indices remain one-based. `legacy.checked_raw` preserves the integer, `legacy.text` owns its string, and `legacy.selected_handle` preserves historical identity. Only `LegacyNotificationV1` adds optional `selected_node`.

```js
app.step_only(); // submit a frame; do not dispatch callbacks
let event;
while ((event = app.poll_notification_v1()) !== undefined) {
  if (event.kind === 'table-change') console.log(event.column, event.frame);
}
```

JS `step()` and `run()` retain automatic legacy callback dispatch. Choose `step_only()` and own the drain for manual mode; it has the same alive/running guards and default `dt=1/60` as `step`. Mixing default dispatch with manual polling consumes successive records from one queue; it never fans out copies. Python `dispatch()` likewise drains the same queue.

JS returns frozen records with discriminants `activation`, `boolean-change`, `table-change`, `surface-close`, or `legacy`. Shared fields are `schemaVersion:1`, frozen `handle`, optional `node`, exact uint64 `frame:bigint`, `hasFrame`, `nodeKind`, and frozen `legacy` (`type`, `checkedRaw`, `value`, `text`, frozen `selectedHandle`). Boolean records add `value`; table records add `reason`, `row`, `column`, `sortColumn`, `sortDirection`; surface records add numeric `result`; legacy records add optional `selectedNode`. TypeScript exports the discriminated `NotificationV1` union and requires BigInt-capable compilation/runtime (for example ES2020/Node18). Convert BigInt explicitly when serializing JSON; converting to Number can lose precision.

Text and raw handle copies survive later frames, removal and app destruction. Optional node references are resolved by exact slot **and generation** at delivery, never by slot alone; they are live wrapper objects, not independent node ownership, and may later become invalid. Returned record immutability does not freeze the referenced node. Python lazily checks optional C symbols, V1 capability and exact native struct size; older libraries remain usable through existing APIs and manual V1 polling raises an explicit unavailable/mismatch error. Node checks both addon availability and optional native symbols/layout. Neither wrapper registers listeners, auto-dispatches new views, or interprets reserved payload tags as scalar/text/selection values.

## Supported boundary and proof

Python and JS/TypeScript provide owning manual views; Go/Rust availability is independent of this slice. Existing callbacks retain their after-frame timing and old payload conversions, including legacy boolean column loss and JS Number frame precision limits. There are no new dispatch/fanout hooks, listener lifetimes, promises, synchronous rejection or request bindings. The [binding audit](design/COMPONENT_EVENTS_BINDINGS.md) remains authoritative for those existing limitations. No full family uniformity or parity is claimed.

`tests/unit/test_bridge_notifications.c` uses the real headless bridge to verify old ABI layouts, shared-queue old/new interleaving, FIFO boolean snapshots versus later mutation, queue exhaustion without false rollback, stale origin cleanup/generation reuse, stale selected-handle retention, size/capacity failures and exact retries, UTF-8/4096-byte copies, all16 DataTable columns plus sort fields, legacy raw fields/JSON and surface close outcomes. Legacy bridge C and Python regression suites remain required. Native CTest runs use the invisible wrapper:

```sh
python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir build -- -R 'bridge_notifications|bridge_core|bridge_components|bridge_python'
```

`bindings/python/test_notifications_v1.py` and `bindings/node/test/notifications-v1.test.cjs` exercise real queued boolean/table/activation records, manual versus legacy consumption and owning copies. Python additionally injects optional-symbol/layout/capacity protocol failures. The Node test-only uint64 conversion fixture checks values beyond2^53 through UINT64_MAX using the polling conversion helper; these are conversion checks, not fabricated input/frame evidence. `bindings/node/test/notifications-v1-protocol.test.cjs` reuses the test-only C provider in `bindings/tests/notification_v1_fixture.c` in fresh Linux processes (preloaded via `LD_PRELOAD`, with `CUI_NOTIFICATION_FIXTURE=edges|capacity|limit|zero|repeat|size|unavailable`). It verifies full native-to-JS uint64 conversion, large copied payload retries, explicit protocol errors, and continued legacy dispatch. These injected records are separate from the real queued tests. `bindings/node/test/notifications-v1.types.ts` checks union narrowing/read-only fields when compiled with `tsc --noEmit --strict --target ES2020 --module Node16 --moduleResolution Node16`.

Build/test registration, exports/generated SDKs, and human/LLM guide indexing are integrator-owned. This guide documents implemented source behavior; wrapper availability must be checked separately.

# Manual queued notifications in Go and Rust

`App.PollNotificationV1()` in Go and `App::poll_notification_v1()` in Rust drain
one notification from the same native FIFO used by legacy polling and dispatch.
They invoke no handlers. `Step`/`step` already leave that queue alone; no alternate
step method is needed. Existing dispatch, frame and run behavior is unchanged.
Choose one queue owner: mixing dispatch and manual polls consumes each entry once,
in call order. These are asynchronous committed snapshots, not synchronous
controlled-component requests or binding callback subscriptions.

Go returns `(NotificationV1, bool, error)`; false with nil error means empty.
`Kind` selects activation, Boolean change, table change, surface close or Legacy;
only its applicable Boolean/Table/Surface pointer is populated. Rust returns
`Result<Option<NotificationV1>>`, with an owning enum for the same variants.
Metadata contains captured raw slot/generation identity, node kind, exact `uint64`
/ `u64` frame, `HasFrame` / `has_frame`, and the complete owning legacy snapshot.
Frames are context-local, not global timestamps or native activation identities.
Go resolves an originating Node only by its complete registered handle. Rust's
Node embeds its app identity and captured generation. Native polling skips stale
origins. A legacy selected handle stays raw: no slot-only lookup or inference that
it is still live. All protocol integers retain their unsigned widths.

Only the native initial allowlist is typed: activation, Checkbox/Switch/Toggle
committed Boolean changes, DataTable changes, and surface close. Input text,
sliders and grouped selection remain Legacy. Reserved scalar/text/selection tags
are not advertised as supported. Table columns preserve the native 1-based value
(including values greater than one); zero retains its native sentinel meaning.
The legacy snapshot includes the original textual table representation too.

```go
notification, ok, err := app.PollNotificationV1()
if err != nil { return err }
if ok && notification.Kind == cui.NotificationBooleanChangeV1 {
    checked := notification.Boolean.Value
    _ = checked
}
```

```rust
if let Some(cui_builders::NotificationV1::BooleanChange(meta, checked)) =
    app.poll_notification_v1()?
{
    let _snapshot = (meta.frame, checked);
}
```

Both wrappers verify the optional V1 symbols, advertised version bit and exact C
structure size before polling. Older shared libraries still support the old APIs;
new polling reports unavailable (Rust `Error(9)`) without draining legacy events.
Go statically linked older libraries use weak optional references on supported
GCC/Clang toolchains; Rust source builds compile the current schema. Shared-library
resolution is implemented for Unix and Windows; only Linux execution was checked
for this slice, not cross-platform runtime parity.

Text is copied into owned strings before returning. The first buffer holds 4097
bytes, followed by at most one capacity retry, capped at 1 MiB including NUL.
Oversized required capacity returns Go `ErrNotificationPayloadLimit` or Rust
`NOTIFICATION_PAYLOAD_LIMIT`; that live event remains queued. Inconsistent capacity
reports and malformed schema/tag/UTF-8 responses fail explicitly. Validation after
a successful native read cannot undo that read; no promise of retaining malformed
third-party library responses is made. No silent Legacy fallback is performed.

## Verification

`bindings/go/cui/notifications_v1_test.go` and Rust `tests/notifications_v1.rs`
exercise the real C queue: Boolean entry snapshots, FIFO/manual ownership, stale
origin removal, copied UTF-8 text and multi-column table payloads. Go also
interleaves legacy polling and verifies no automatic callbacks.
`bindings/tests/notification_v1_fixture.c` is a separate test-only shared shim:
its `CUI_NOTIFICATION_FIXTURE` modes `edges`, `capacity`, `limit`, `zero`, `repeat`,
`size`, and `unavailable` inject protocol responses. These are not evidence that
real UI producers emit oversized text or maximal frame values. Use a fresh
process per mode. It exports only V1 entry points and links the real bridge for
ordinary App APIs. On Linux Rust shared-library tests preload this shim; Go loads
it explicitly. Production libraries contain no fixture hooks.

A local external CTest harness invokes these suites through `scripts/test_local.py`
with private Xvfb. The shim compiles as C11 with `-Wall -Wextra -Werror -pedantic`.
The wrappers also compile against source-built static SDKs. Generated SDK copies
are validation inputs only; their regeneration belongs to the integrator.

Run the reproducible offline Linux matrix from a fresh, regenerated SDK checkout:

```sh
python scripts/test_notification_bindings.py \
  --build-dir /absolute/external/notification-checks \
  --library /absolute/native-build/libcui_bridge.so
```

Requires an existing Git checkout, Go (cgo/C11), Cargo, CMake, `cc`, and `xvfb-run`; the supplied
shared bridge must already implement V1. No dependency installation or network
resolution is performed (`GOTOOLCHAIN=local`, Go proxy/checksum lookup disabled,
Cargo offline). Use an external build directory. The script stages the binding
sources without modifying SDKs, checks bridge header/source freshness, builds the
existing test-only fixture with strict warnings, and runs CTest through the
private display wrapper. Full Go/Rust portable static and dynamic suites cover
real V1 queues and legacy compatibility; fourteen further cases cover the seven
injected protocol modes in both languages. Native window lifecycle tests are
explicitly excluded from this font-free notification matrix; the separate native
runner suite owns those checks.

Optionally pass `--older-library /absolute/pre-v1-build/libcui_bridge.so` to add
two genuine missing-symbol compatibility cases (twenty total). Synthetic
`unavailable` mode otherwise checks version negotiation, not missing symbols.
Every compiler/test failure exits nonzero. Staged inputs, language build caches,
CTest configuration and `ctest/Testing/Temporary/LastTest.log` remain under the
build directory for diagnosis. Repeated runs preserve prior staged inputs; save
CTest logs separately when retaining historical run evidence.
