# Bridge value notification views (V1)

The C-only `cui_bridge_poll_value_notification_v1` opts into scalar, plain-text and selected-handle views on the **existing shared notification queue**. It preserves the shipped V1 layout, ABI version, size/version queries, old polling functions and dispatch timing. [Initial V1 notifications](BRIDGE_NOTIFICATIONS.md) still define ownership and queue behavior. This API reports existing applied bridge mutations; it is not a direct-C facade, controlled request, callback registration or synchronous foreign veto.

```c
#include <cui/cui_bridge.h>

static cui_bridge_status next_scalar(cui_bridge_app *app,
                                     cui_bridge_notification_v1 *out,
                                     char *text, uint32_t capacity,
                                     uint32_t *required) {
    if (!(cui_bridge_notification_versions() & 1u) ||
        cui_bridge_notification_v1_size() != sizeof(*out) ||
        !(cui_bridge_notification_value_payloads_v1() & CUI_BRIDGE_VALUE_SCALAR_V1))
        return CUI_BRIDGE_INVALID_STATE;
    return cui_bridge_poll_value_notification_v1(app, sizeof(*out),
        CUI_BRIDGE_VALUE_SCALAR_V1, out, text, capacity, required);
}
```

Dynamic consumers must resolve the two new optional symbols before calling them. Older libraries lack these symbols; retain old APIs or report unavailable without draining through another poll. The category query returns `CUI_BRIDGE_VALUE_SCALAR_V1 | CUI_BRIDGE_VALUE_TEXT_V1 | CUI_BRIDGE_VALUE_SELECTION_V1`; each bit is `1u << payload_tag`. Request only categories understood by your decoder. [Python](BRIDGE_VALUE_NOTIFICATIONS_PYTHON.md) and [JavaScript/TypeScript](BRIDGE_VALUE_NOTIFICATIONS_JS.md) and [Go](BRIDGE_VALUE_NOTIFICATIONS_GO.md) and [Rust](BRIDGE_VALUE_NOTIFICATIONS_RUST.md) owning value polling are implemented separately. Rust static builds require the paired SDK; dynamic exports are negotiated. Existing V1 manual methods retain their initial typed allowlist. Bundled Go/Rust SDK source snapshots include the C API.

## Complete scalar producer allowlist

| Existing bridge producer | New opt-in payload | Precision and event boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Slider | CHANGE / SCALAR | Existing local float is promoted to stored double; no precision beyond the actual float interaction is invented. |
| NumberInput | CHANGE / SCALAR | Stored double copied directly after existing aggregate `result.changed`; numeric draft text is not a text event. |
| Rating | CHANGE / SCALAR | Existing float value promoted to double. |
| Pagination | CHANGE / SCALAR | Existing page stored as model double; not an arbitrary integer/ID transport. |

Read `payload.scalar_value` only for SCALAR. The full `legacy` snapshot is retained, including the same double in `legacy.value`, checked/raw fields, historical selected handle, frame and text length. Typed values are captured beside those fields at enqueue, before later model mutation. Poll does not parse JSON or query current node state. Existing component aggregate counts, input ordering and render traversal stay unchanged; this does not add per-edit/per-input multiplicity or COMMIT/SUBMIT notifications. Programmatic setters and render-only Progress do not acquire notification producers.

All other producers retain their existing classification: initial CLICK/BOOLEAN/TABLE/SURFACE tags are unchanged, and remaining CHANGE producers stay LEGACY. Combobox, unaudited selection composites, date/time/color and Menu/Dropdown commands remain LEGACY. No family parity claim is made.

## Complete plain-text producer allowlist

Input, Textarea, Editor and InputGroup emit CHANGE / TEXT only when their existing aggregate changed result enqueues a record. Read the complete UTF-8 bytes from the separate caller buffer and `text_length`; there is no text pointer in the union. `legacy.text_length` describes the same owned queued copy. Existing input buffers hold4096 bytes plus NUL; lengths are UTF-8 bytes, not characters. Multiple edits in one frame remain a single final aggregate snapshot. No before/after selection, individual edit, submit, commit or reason is invented. InputGroup addon CLICK events retain their separate origin/order.

Text classification occurs only after the existing enqueue copy succeeds; allocation/queue failure behavior is unchanged. A later setter changes the model without rewriting queued bytes or producing an event of its own. Old V1 and unrequested TEXT masks still return the complete LEGACY text. Textarea/Editor do not gain secure masking. The bridge currently exposes no masked/password configuration and copies underlying plain model bytes; direct C Input facade redaction does not carry over. OTP, Speech and TextView remain LEGACY. Future secure support must address both typed and legacy queued copies before exposing a security option; this API makes no secure-text promise.

The public bridge key enum lacks Backspace/Delete/select-all keys, so the portable fixture cannot prove deletion-to-empty through that input surface. It tests initial empty model/setter silence instead of fabricating an empty edit event. The general V1 empty-text capacity contract remains one byte for NUL.

## Complete selection producer allowlist

RadioGroup, Tabs, Select, List and Stepper emit CHANGE / SELECTION at their existing aggregate enqueue sites. `payload.selected` is the full uint32 slot/generation handle captured at enqueue; `legacy.selected` retains the same historical identity and `legacy.value` retains its old numeric slot snapshot. This is a bridge Item handle, not a Core uint64 ID, numeric index, previous-selection record or direct-C selection callback. No reason/input index/activation evidence is invented.

Existing validation captures a nonzero selection only for a live direct child. A nonzero model value that fails that validation remains LEGACY rather than being mislabeled a clear. An explicit model0, if an existing producer enqueues it, represents an empty handle `{0,0}`. The public clear setter itself is silent; tests do not invent an empty selection input event to exercise that representation. Normal public selected setters reject stale/wrong-parent handles before mutation.

The enqueue count and final-state aggregation remain unchanged. List can enqueue the same selected Item again on activation. Select's existing final comparison can suppress a complete frame that returns to its initial item; direct C's newer per-transition observer does not cause bridge records to appear. Delayed delivery preserves the captured generation after selected-item removal/reuse; it never resolves a historical slot to a replacement. Origin-staleness cleanup remains the existing poll policy.

Menu and DropdownButton commands remain LEGACY even when their old selected field contains an Item handle. Combobox query and selection enqueue sites also remain LEGACY, including their text, because they share a mixed snapshot model with different reasons. Tree/Carousel/Command/Sidebar/Dock/Settings are not classified merely because their value looks like a child slot. No additional manifest family or synchronous foreign callback is introduced.

## Backward compatibility and failures

Existing Go/Rust V1 decoders reject unknown/reserved tags after consuming a record. Therefore `cui_bridge_poll_notification_v1` continues returning newly captured value producers as LEGACY, with complete unchanged legacy fields/text and an inactive zeroed union. The new poll with mask0 does the same. The new poll returns SCALAR/TEXT/SELECTION only for the requested category and its explicit allowlist. Legacy `poll_event_ex` retains its original scalar snapshot; filtered `poll_event` still skips/discards CHANGE while looking for CLICK. Every path drains the **same FIFO**; it never broadcasts duplicate events.

Unsupported mask bits (including bits for NONE/BOOLEAN/TABLE/SURFACE/LEGACY), wrong struct size, null fixed-output or null required-capacity pointer fail INVALID_ARGUMENT before stale cleanup or queue consumption, with outputs intact. This check does not modify the legacy poll contract. Existing stale origin/generation cleanup still happens during a valid poll. CAPACITY changes only `required_capacity`, preserving fixed/text output and the live record; preceding stale cleanup is not rolled back. Empty text requires capacity1 for NUL. Exact-capacity retry retrieves the same captured scalar. EMPTY and other failures preserve outputs. Caller storage extents must be valid and disjoint as required by V1.

The poll allocates nothing, adds no text cap, truncates nothing and introduces no queue or per-event typed allocation. Existing queue-full behavior is unchanged: a control may already have mutated before enqueue fails, and prior records remain queued. No rollback is implied. Copied scalar/metadata records survive later frames, origin removal and app destruction while caller storage survives; handles do not own live nodes.

`node` remains uint32 slot/generation identity; frame sequence remains exact uint64 and only HAS_FRAME is available. No input index, source, pointer/key/accessibility snapshot or Core `cui_id` is inferred. Do not convert uint64 frame identities to a lossy JS Number in future wrappers; the scalar's double representation is unrelated to frame/handle precision.

## Proof and validation

[test_bridge_value_notifications.c](../tests/unit/test_bridge_value_notifications.c) drives real headless bridge input for all four producers, including NumberInput key mutation above float precision, pointer Slider/Rating/Pagination changes, delayed capture after a later setter, disabled controls and closed Collapsible child suppression. There is no new public bridge inert/layout-only switch; the fixture exercises existing closed-content suppression rather than injecting Core routing. It freezes V1 size/offsets, verifies category negotiation, invalid mask/size/output atomicity, exact capacity retry, mask0/old-V1 downgrade, old extended/filtered poll interleaving, unchanged boolean/text classifications and queue exhaustion without false rollback. Existing initial-V1 and bridge core/component tests remain required.

```sh
python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir build -- -R '^(bridge_selection_notifications|bridge_text_notifications|bridge_value_notifications|bridge_notifications_v1|bridge_core|bridge_components)$'
```

[test_bridge_text_notifications.c](../tests/unit/test_bridge_text_notifications.c) additionally drives all four text producers with real UTF-8 input, one aggregate for two queued edits,4096-byte boundary/exact retry, delayed copies, old/masked-out/extended-poll interleaving, unchanged disabled behavior and queue-full mutation without rollback. It does not inject a secure bridge configuration or allocation-failure hook.

[test_bridge_selection_notifications.c](../tests/unit/test_bridge_selection_notifications.c) additionally drives all five selection producers, old/masked-out/extended polling, delayed selected handles, stale selected generations and slot reuse, List repeat, Select return-to-initial suppression, clear-setter silence, disabled controls, exact capacity/error atomicity and overflow without rollback. Real Menu/Dropdown commands and Combobox query/selection remain LEGACY even when value masks are requested.

Native automated tests use the invisible wrapper; no desktop display is required. Build registration, generated SDK source snapshots and human/LLM indexes include this C API. Python, JS/TypeScript, Go and Rust have owning value wrappers. The [design checkpoint](design/BRIDGE_VALUE_NOTIFICATIONS_SLICE.md) describes deferred categories and compatibility decisions; it is not evidence those categories ship.

# Go owning value notifications

`(*App).PollValueNotificationV1() (ValueNotificationV1, bool, error)` is an additive,
manual owning view over the existing FIFO. `PollNotificationV1`, its struct and enum,
legacy `PollEvent`, `Dispatch`, `Step` and `Run` keep their contracts. Nothing here
registers callbacks, broadcasts events or makes foreign synchronous requests.

```go
field := cui.Input("name")
app, err := cui.New(cui.Options{})
if err != nil { panic(err) }
defer app.Close()
if err := app.Mount(cui.Column("root").Children(field)); err != nil { panic(err) }
if err := app.Step(1.0 / 60); err != nil { panic(err) }
for {
    event, ok, err := app.PollValueNotificationV1()
    if err != nil { panic(err) }
    if !ok { break }
    switch event.Kind {
    case cui.ValueNotificationScalarChangeV1:
        fmt.Println(event.Scalar.Value)
    case cui.ValueNotificationTextChangeV1:
        fmt.Println(event.Text.Text)
    case cui.ValueNotificationSelectionChangeV1:
        fmt.Println(event.Selection.Handle)
    }
}
```

The example assumes imports `fmt` and `github.com/mattmezza/cui/bindings/go/cui`.
Call `Step` after host input as appropriate; it does not automatically dispatch Go
handlers. Do not also drain through `Dispatch`/`Run` when manual ownership is intended.
All consumers divide the same queue rather than receiving independent copies.

`ValueNotificationKindV1` is a separate enum, with activation, boolean, table,
surface-close and legacy alternatives plus scalar/text/selection. Exactly the
kind-selected payload pointer is nonnil; activation/legacy have no typed pointer.
The new payloads are `ScalarChangeV1{Value float64}`, `TextChangeV1{Text string}` and
`SelectionChangeV1{Handle Handle, Node *Node}`. The common fields mirror the existing
view, including complete owning `LegacySnapshotV1`. Existing enum values/types do
not acquire extra alternatives.

Frames remain exact `uint64`, handles/indices exact `uint32`, scalar values binary64.
NumberInput retains its double precision; Slider/Rating cannot recover precision
already lost in float models. See [the C allowlist](BRIDGE_VALUE_NOTIFICATIONS.md)
for the four scalar, four plain-text and five selection producers. Combobox/menu
and unsupported producers remain LEGACY, with no JSON parsing or invented evidence.
The bridge has no secure-text configuration or inferred redaction. This API is not
a forwarding layer for all direct-C event facades.

Values, strings and identities are copied and survive later model mutation/removal
and app disposal. Go records are caller-mutable, not frozen objects. Payload pointers
point to owned Go allocations, not C storage. Optional `Node` references are live
objects resolved by exact slot **and generation**, not immutable model snapshots.
A removed historical selection retains its identity but resolves to nil.

Both dynamic symbol lookup and the portable static weak-symbol path independently
resolve size/version/category/poll capabilities. Only advertised known category
bits are requested; unknown capability bits are ignored. Missing optional symbols,
wrong layout/version or no known category fails before polling, without fallback
to a legacy drain. Older libraries remain usable through existing polling APIs.

The existing allocation policy starts at 4097 bytes, permits one strictly growing
retry and caps capacity at 1 MiB including NUL. `ErrNotificationPayloadLimit` and
inconsistent retries leave the live record queued. Successful native polling
consumes before decoding; malformed kind/tag/metadata/UTF-8/payload errors cannot
roll the record back. Decode checks include genuine frame presence, legacy identity
consistency, finite scalar values, full selection identity and negotiated tags.
No source/input-index/activation metadata is fabricated.

## Evidence and reproduction

`bindings/go/cui/value_notifications_v1_test.go` exercises real queued NumberInput,
Input and RadioGroup events in both static and dynamic builds, binary64 precision,
old/new FIFO interleaving, setter/disabled silence, copied UTF-8 and actual removal of a historical selection.
Go's public mounted-tree API cannot append/recreate a replacement in this fixture.
A separate **synthetic registry entry** checks same-slot/different-generation lookup;
this is not Go allocator-reuse proof. Actual C allocator reuse is covered separately
by C/Python/JS tests. An actual older initial-V1 library proves unavailable value
polling leaves queued text available to the old poll.

Build test executables offline, without regenerating SDK copies:

```sh
cd bindings/go
GOTOOLCHAIN=local GOPROXY=off go test -tags cui_dynamic -c ./cui -o "$build_dir/go-dynamic.test"
GOTOOLCHAIN=local GOPROXY=off go test -c ./cui -o "$build_dir/go-static.test"
```

Use `CGO_CFLAGS=-I/absolute/canonical/include` when testing against a newer canonical
header before SDK regeneration. Register executables in an external CTest harness.
Set `CUI_VALUE_REAL=1` for real producers; dynamic mode also needs an absolute
`CUI_BRIDGE_LIBRARY`. For an actual older library set `CUI_VALUE_OLD=1` and run only
`-test.run=^TestValueNotificationV1TextFIFO$`. Static portable checks exclude
`-test.skip=^TestNativeRunLifecycle$`; SDL runner tests need their native build/font
and are outside this portable slice. Existing V1 and other portable Go tests remain
included. Run CTest only through `python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir "$build_dir"`.

The isolated Linux provider in `cui/testdata/value_notifications_provider.c` is
synthetic protocol evidence, not input evidence. Compile it with strict C11 warnings,
`-fPIC -shared`, canonical `-Iinclude`, and `-Wl,--no-as-needed -L"$old_bridge_dir"
-lcui_bridge -Wl,-rpath,"$old_bridge_dir"`. It depends on the actual older bridge for
normal App functions; do not substitute it for production. The no-known-category and missing-query modes also retain actual queued text for the old poll. A second build with
`-DCUI_VALUE_FIXTURE_MISSING` omits the category query. Point dynamic library selection
to the provider and run only `TestValueNotificationV1Protocol`, fresh process per
`CUI_VALUE_FIXTURE` mode: `edges`, `capacity`, `size`, `unavailable`, `missing`, `limit`,
`zero`, `repeat`, `tag`, `kind`, `utf8`, `nul`, `flags`. These check exact uint64 extremes,
unknown capability filtering, optional exports, malformed output and bounded copies.

Rust value wrappers and generated SDK publication remain separate integration work.

The repository integrator runner also stages current SDK sources and registers
static, dynamic, legacy, protocol and actual older-library cases offline:

```sh
python scripts/test_notification_bindings.py --build-dir /absolute/validation-dir \
  --library /absolute/current/libcui_bridge.so \
  --value-older-library /absolute/initial-v1/libcui_bridge.so
```

The older value library must expose initial V1 but lack the new value symbols.
Without it, missing-export/older-library no-drain cases are explicitly deferred.
The independent `--older-library` option tests a genuinely pre-V1 library instead.

# JavaScript and TypeScript owning value notifications

`App.poll_value_notification_v1(): ValueNotificationV1 | undefined` is an explicit,
manual drain of the **same queue** used by `poll_notification_v1()`, legacy dispatch,
`step()` and `run()`. It adds no listeners or synchronous requests. Existing V1
API/types and automatic dispatch stay unchanged. Use `step_only()` when the caller
owns draining; mixing consumers divides events rather than broadcasting them.

```js
const c = require('@cui/native');
const app = new c.App();
try {
  app.mount(c.column().children(c.input('name', '')));
  app.step_only(); // call after each host input/frame as appropriate
  let event;
  while ((event = app.poll_value_notification_v1()) !== undefined) {
    if (event.kind === 'text-change') console.log(event.text);
    if (event.kind === 'scalar-change') console.log(event.value);
    if (event.kind === 'selection-change') console.log(event.selectedHandle);
  }
} finally { app.dispose(); }
```

The new union extends the existing notification alternatives with:

| Kind | Owning payload |
| --- | --- |
| `scalar-change` | `value: number`, the captured C binary64 value |
| `text-change` | `text: string`, copied UTF-8 |
| `selection-change` | frozen `selectedHandle: {slot, generation}`, optional `selectedNode` |

See [the C allowlist](BRIDGE_VALUE_NOTIFICATIONS.md) for the exact four scalar,
four plain text and five selection producers. Combobox, menu and other unsupported
producers retain complete `legacy` snapshots; no JSON is parsed. NumberInput retains
its double precision; Slider/Rating cannot recover precision already lost in their
float models. There is no secure-text configuration or inferred redaction in this
bridge API. This is not uniform component-event-facade coverage.

Records, legacy snapshots and handle objects are frozen. Strings/numeric values and
handles survive later mutation, queue reuse and app disposal. `node`/`selectedNode`
are optional live JS object references resolved by the complete slot/generation;
these references are not immutable model snapshots. Removed historical selections
retain their copied handles without resolving a replacement generation. Handles and
indices are exact uint32 Numbers; every frame is an exact uint64 **BigInt**, including
values above 2^53. JSON serialization requires an explicit BigInt conversion policy.

The production addon resolves the new C exports optionally, verifies V1 size/version,
and requests only advertised known bits SCALAR/TEXT/SELECTION. Unknown capability bits
are ignored. Missing addon method, missing native exports, or no known categories
throw without falling back to another drain. Older native libraries remain usable
through existing APIs. A missing/mismatched capability is checked before polling.

Storage starts at 4097 bytes, with one strictly growing retry capped at 1 MiB including
NUL. Invalid/non-growing/repeated/over-limit capacity responses throw; capacity failure
does not consume the live record. A successful native poll consumes before validation:
malformed tags/kinds, frame/legacy mismatches, flags, scalar values, selection handles,
UTF-8 or termination cause a protocol error and cannot roll that record back. No
unavailable source, activation or input-index evidence is fabricated.

## Validation and reproduction

`bindings/node/test/value-notifications-v1.test.cjs` uses actual queued input for
NumberInput, Input and RadioGroup, old/new FIFO, setter silence, payload copies and
removed/reused selection generations. Run it again with `CUI_EXPECT_OLD=1` and an
addon linked to an actual initial-V1 library to prove unavailable value polling does
not drain its queued text. Legacy notification/binding/component tests also pass.

The separate Linux interposition fixture is **synthetic protocol evidence**, not UI
input. It checks unknown capability filtering, partial exports, layout failure,
malformed kind/tag/flags/UTF-8/NUL, retry limits, an 8192-byte copy and uint64 extremes.
The Node CMake project registers the real-queue and Linux protocol cases:

```sh
cmake -S bindings/node -B build-node -DCUI_BUILD_NATIVE=OFF
cmake --build build-node --target cui_node_bindings cui_value_notification_fixture
python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir build-node -R '^node_value_notifications'
```

To include actual old-library and missing-symbol cases, configure with
`-DCUI_NODE_VALUE_OLD_LIBRARY=/absolute/path/to/older/libcui_bridge.so` and also
build `cui_node_old_value_bindings` and `cui_value_notification_missing_fixture`.
These cases are not registered without an explicitly supplied old library.
The synthetic provider is test-only and never adds hooks to the production addon.

For an external compatibility harness, compile the addon and fixture manually:

```sh
# Set bridge_dir to the directory containing the desired libcui_bridge.so.
cc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -fPIC -shared \
  -Iinclude -I/usr/include/node bindings/node/addon.c \
  -L"$bridge_dir" -lcui_bridge -Wl,-rpath,"$bridge_dir" -o "$build_dir/cui.node"
cc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -fPIC -shared -Iinclude \
  bindings/node/test/value-notifications-provider.c -o "$build_dir/provider.so"
# Compile again with -DCUI_VALUE_FIXTURE_MISSING for the partial-export case.
```

Register Node invocations in an external CTest harness with `CUI_NODE_ADDON` selecting
the addon. For each protocol mode set `LD_PRELOAD` to the fixture and
`CUI_VALUE_FIXTURE` to `edges`, `capacity`, `size`, `unavailable`, `missing`, `limit`,
`zero`, `repeat`, `tag`, `kind`, `utf8`, `nul` or `flags`; run
`value-notifications-protocol.test.cjs` in a fresh process. The `missing` fixture must
use the missing-export build and an actual older bridge library, so the real library
cannot supply the omitted symbol. Run native CTest only through
`python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir "$build_dir"` (private Xvfb).

Both old and new type fixtures compile with pinned TypeScript 5.8.3:

```sh
npm exec --yes --package typescript@5.8.3 -- tsc --noEmit --strict \
  --target ES2022 --module NodeNext --moduleResolution NodeNext \
  bindings/node/test/notifications-v1.types.ts \
  bindings/node/test/value-notifications-v1.types.ts
```

Go/Rust value wrappers and generated package/SDK publication are separate integration
work. Generated `index.d.cts` continues to re-export the canonical TypeScript file.

# Python owning bridge value notifications

`App.poll_value_notifications_v1()` is an explicit manual drain of the [C value notification queue](BRIDGE_VALUE_NOTIFICATIONS.md). It yields frozen owning values without invoking callbacks. Existing `poll_notifications_v1()`, `poll_events()`, `step()`, `run()` and `dispatch()` retain their behavior. All poll/dispatch paths consume successive records from the **same queue**; they do not broadcast copies.

```python
from cui_bridge import (
    App, column, input, TextChangeNotificationV1,
    ScalarChangeNotificationV1, SelectionChangeNotificationV1,
)

with App() as app:
    field = input("message", "")
    app.mount(column().children(field))
    app.step()  # submit; Python dispatch remains explicit
    # After later input/steps, own the queue drain:
    for event in app.poll_value_notifications_v1():
        if isinstance(event, TextChangeNotificationV1):
            print(event.text)
        elif isinstance(event, ScalarChangeNotificationV1):
            print(event.value)
        elif isinstance(event, SelectionChangeNotificationV1):
            print(event.selected_handle)
```

The additive `ValueNotificationV1` type includes the existing notification classes and three new frozen dataclasses. Shared fields remain `handle`, optional origin `node`, exact integer `frame_sequence`, `has_frame`, `node_kind` and frozen complete `legacy` snapshot.

| New class / `kind` | Owning fields | C allowlist |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ScalarChangeNotificationV1` / `scalar-change` | `value: float`, copied binary64 | Slider, NumberInput, Rating, Pagination. Float-based controls retain their actual float precision; NumberInput retains stored double. |
| `TextChangeNotificationV1` / `text-change` | `text: str`, copied and decoded UTF-8 | Plain Input, Textarea, Editor, InputGroup only. |
| `SelectionChangeNotificationV1` / `selection-change` | `selected_handle: tuple[int,int]`, optional `selected_node` | RadioGroup, Tabs, Select, List, Stepper only. |

Selection handles retain full uint32 slot/generation identity, including a stale historical selection. `selected_node` is resolved only by that exact pair from the current Python registry; slot reuse cannot resolve to another generation. It is a live Widget reference, not independent node ownership, and can later become disposed. The handle, scalar, text and complete legacy snapshot remain usable after later frames and app destruction. Frozen records do not freeze referenced Widgets. Python currently has no public per-node remove API; the stale-generation test explicitly uses the C fixture boundary and updates the test registry.

Existing activation, boolean, table, surface-close and Legacy classes are also returned by the new method. Combobox query/selection, Menu/Dropdown commands and unaudited families retain Legacy records. Typed values reflect existing aggregate enqueue behavior, not direct C's per-event facade semantics or new submit/commit events. The C allowlist and its secure-text limitations remain authoritative: the bridge exposes plain edit text and does not inherit direct C Input facade password redaction. No new secure input, synchronous foreign requests, registration hooks or family parity is claimed.

## Negotiation, errors and lifetime

The generator resolves optional V1 size/version and value-category/poll symbols before reading any queue record. It requests only the intersection of compiled-known SCALAR/TEXT/SELECTION bits and the library's advertised bits; unknown advertised bits are never enabled. An older library lacking symbols, or a library advertising no known value category, raises an explicit `BridgeError` without draining through an old poll. Existing old APIs remain usable. A native V1 layout/version mismatch likewise fails before polling. Existing `poll_notifications_v1()` continues receiving newly captured values as complete Legacy snapshots from the old C symbol.

Text starts with4097 bytes including NUL and retries once for a strictly larger requested capacity, at most1MiB including NUL. Oversized, zero/non-increasing or repeated capacity responses raise `BridgeError`; no truncation occurs. C CAPACITY leaves the live record queued; allocation failures propagate. Invalid size/version/flags/frame presence, inconsistent legacy metadata, missing NUL/invalid UTF-8, unsupported tag/kind/category or malformed typed values raise protocol errors. A decode error follows a successful consuming C poll and does not restore that record. No fallback or replay is attempted.

Payloads are notifications of applied bridge behavior. Reading a record does not invoke its Widget callback; calling `dispatch()` separately drains later records through the existing legacy path. No callback fanout or ownership change is added. The borrowed C text is copied into Python strings before yielding; result reads do not reference a mutable C text buffer.

## Tests and compatibility

[The new Python fixture](../bindings/python/test_value_notifications_v1.py) covers real NumberInput key mutation beyond float precision, copied UTF-8, selection/live and historical generations, old/new shared draining, existing boolean/table views, immutable fields and snapshots surviving app close. Its synthetic Python protocol provider separately checks exact UINT64_MAX frames/uint32 handles, compiled-known capability masking, wrong layout, malformed typed output, large retry and capacity limits. These are conversion/protocol tests, not fabricated UI input evidence. Existing initial V1 and legacy Python suites remain required.

The real old-library case requires `CUI_BRIDGE_OLD_LIBRARY` pointing to an actual initial-V1 library without value symbols. It queues text there, proves the new method reports unavailable, and then retrieves the same bytes through old V1 polling. Without this explicit library the old-library case skips; it must not be counted as proved merely by the synthetic provider.

Adjacent NumberInput and Input composition is also exercised through real input.
A renderer identity collision exposed during this work is fixed; regression tests
cover both ordinary and focused fields without changing public viewport IDs.

Native validation uses `python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir build`; the Python bridge backend is `none` for these fixtures. CTest registers the fixture as `bridge_python_value_notifications`; set the explicit old-library environment variable to include its compatibility case. No other language value wrapper is implemented by this change.

# Rust owning value notifications

`App::poll_value_notification_v1(&mut self) -> Result<Option<ValueNotificationV1>>`
is a separate opt-in owning view over the existing queue. The original
`NotificationV1` enum and `poll_notification_v1` method remain unchanged, including
exhaustive matches. This adds no listeners, foreign synchronous requests or dispatch
hooks. Polling and `dispatch`/`run` divide the same FIFO; they do not broadcast copies.

```rust
use cui_builders::{App, Kind, ValueNotificationV1};
fn main() -> Result<(), cui_builders::Error> {
let mut app = App::headless(640., 480.)?;
let root = app.root(Kind::Column, "root")?;
app.child(root, Kind::Input, "name")?;
app.step(1. / 60.)?;
while let Some(event) = app.poll_value_notification_v1()? {
    match event {
        ValueNotificationV1::ScalarChange(_, value) => println!("{value}"),
        ValueNotificationV1::TextChange(_, text) => println!("{text}"),
        ValueNotificationV1::SelectionChange(_, selected) => println!("{:?}", selected.handle),
        _ => {}
    }
}
Ok(())
}
```

Call `step` after host input as needed.
`step` does not dispatch Rust callbacks. Choose manual draining or the existing
callback dispatch loop deliberately.

The separate enum retains activation, boolean, table, surface-close and legacy
alternatives, and adds `ScalarChange(MetadataV1, f64)`,
`TextChange(MetadataV1, String)` and
`SelectionChange(MetadataV1, SelectionChangeV1)`. The latter contains
`handle: RawHandle` and `node: Option<Node>`. Full legacy snapshots remain available
in common metadata. Strings/numeric values/identities are owned Rust data and survive
later mutation, removal, queue reuse and app drop. Rust callers can mutate their own
returned values; this is not an immutable model snapshot.

Frames are exact `u64`, slots/generations/indices exact `u32`, scalar values binary64.
NumberInput keeps its double precision; Slider/Rating cannot recover precision
already lost in float models. Optional Node capabilities are checked against the
current full C slot/generation using a read-only getter before being returned; a
removed identity does not resolve to a replacement generation. Node values remain
live capabilities, not retained C objects; later operations still validate them.

See [the C allowlist](BRIDGE_VALUE_NOTIFICATIONS.md) for the four scalar, four plain
text and five selection producers. Combobox/menu and unsupported producers remain
LEGACY. Nothing parses their JSON or invents input source, activation or index
metadata. No bridge secure-text configuration or inferred redaction is provided.
This does not establish uniform direct-C component-event-facade coverage.

Dynamic builds resolve optional size/version/category/poll exports, verify layout,
and request only advertised known category bits. Unknown capability bits are ignored.
Missing exports, unsupported version or no known categories return `Error(9)` before
polling, without fallback to another drain. A layout mismatch returns
`NOTIFICATION_PROTOCOL_ERROR`. Older dynamic libraries remain usable through their
existing APIs. **Static builds link strong symbols from the paired bundled SDK**, as
the existing Rust V1 implementation does; rebuild the crate with its matching bundled
bridge. Compatibility with mismatched older static archives is not promised. Rust
stable provides no portable weak-symbol mechanism here.

The shared allocation policy starts at 4097 bytes and permits one strictly growing
retry capped at 1 MiB including NUL. `NOTIFICATION_PAYLOAD_LIMIT` and inconsistent
capacity responses leave a live record queued. Successful native polling consumes
before decode; malformed output cannot be rolled back. Validation covers schema,
flags, kind/tag, legacy/frame/identity consistency, negotiated tags, finite scalar
values, selected identities, UTF-8 and NUL termination. Invalid UTF-8 returns `Error(7)`;
other malformed output returns `NOTIFICATION_PROTOCOL_ERROR`.

## Evidence and reproduction

`tests/value_notifications_v1.rs` uses actual NumberInput/Input/RadioGroup input in
both static and dynamic builds: precision, setter/disabled silence, old/new FIFO, existing Checkbox/DataTable typed alternatives,
owned copies after app drop, and actual selection removal plus same-slot/new-generation
replacement through Rust's public `child` API. Old and new selected identities remain
distinct and the historical event has no live Node. The old enum's exhaustive-match
fixture compiles unchanged.

Build offline using existing pinned dependencies (this crate adds none):

```sh
CUI_BRIDGE_LIB_DIR="$bridge_dir" CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$dynamic_target" \
  cargo test --offline --manifest-path bindings/rust/Cargo.toml --no-run
CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$static_target" \
  cargo test --offline --manifest-path bindings/rust/Cargo.toml --no-run
```

Register the resulting unit, builders, callback-panic, notification and value test
executables in an external CTest harness, with `CUI_VALUE_REAL=1` and
`--test-threads=1`. Serialized tests respect the process-global layout runtime.
Exclude `run_native` explicitly from these portable checks; SDL runner proof requires
its separate native build and font. Execute native CTest only through
`python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir "$build_dir"` (private Xvfb).

For older-library proof, run the dynamic value executable with an actual initial-V1
library selected through `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `CUI_VALUE_OLD=1`, and test filter
`real_text_fifo_or_older_library_no_drain`. It queues real UTF-8 input, checks value
polling is unavailable, then retrieves the unchanged text with old polling.

`tests/fixtures/value_notifications_provider.c` is separate Linux **synthetic protocol
proof**, not UI input evidence. Compile it with strict C11 warnings, `-fPIC -shared`,
canonical `-Iinclude`, and link normal App exports from an actual older bridge with
`-Wl,--no-as-needed -L"$old_bridge_dir" -lcui_bridge -Wl,-rpath,"$old_bridge_dir"`.
Compile another with `-DCUI_VALUE_FIXTURE_MISSING` to omit its category query.
Use `LD_PRELOAD` for the provider and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` for the old bridge; run only
`synthetic_protocol` in a fresh dynamic test process per `CUI_VALUE_FIXTURE` mode:
`edges`, `capacity`, `size`, `unavailable`, `missing`, `limit`, `zero`, `repeat`, `tag`,
`kind`, `utf8`, `nul`, `flags`. This covers uint64 extremes, unknown-bit filtering,
partial exports, malformed output and bounded 8192-byte copies. The no-known-category
and missing-query modes also run the real text test to verify no drain.

Generated SDK/package publication is separate integrator work; no SDK copies change
in this wrapper slice.

# Buttons

`cui_button` keeps the default primary style and controlled disabled flag.
`cui_button_ex` adds primary, secondary, outline, ghost, destructive and link
variants; XSmall/Small/Medium/Large sizes; loading and selected presentation; explicit
or growing width; leading/trailing text; and a presentation-content callback.
Every variant uses `cui_base_button` for capture, keyboard activation and focus.
The content callback should draw presentation without nested interactive controls.

At the default 16px theme font, XS/S/M/L heights are 20/24/32/32px,
with 12/14/14/16px labels and horizontal padding of 4/8/10/12px.
Medium and Large intentionally share a height in the frozen upstream source.
These metrics scale with `theme.font_size / 16`; the legacy generic
`theme.control_height` and `theme.padding` do not override button size metrics.
Text uses a 1.25 line height and the content row is centered vertically without
vertical padding reducing the available label space.

Set `.icon = cui_string("close")` to add a real SVG icon. With `.icon_only = true`,
the button is square and hides the visible label while retaining `name` for
accessibility. For example, a Small close button uses a 24px target and a 14px
icon. Dialog and sheet close controls use this path. The theme's `icon_loader`
can replace that artwork; custom content callbacks remain available for other
compositions.

```c
if (cui_button_ex(ui, save_id, &theme, cui_string("Save changes"),
    (cui_button_options){.variant = CUI_BUTTON_OUTLINE,
        .size = CUI_CONTROL_SMALL, .loading = saving})) {
    begin_save();
}
```

Loading suppresses activation and focus, draws an animated SVG loader, and exposes
an accessible description. Disabled text/background preserve theme contrast;
hover/pressed states tint enabled surfaces and keyboard focus has a distinct border.
Selected is application-owned presentation; it does not imply a semantic pressed state. For value toggling use `cui_toggle` or the controlled toggle group.

With `custom_colors`, `pressed || selected || open` selects `colors.active`
(or `outline_active`); otherwise hover selects `hover`, then `normal` is the
fallback. A selected/open button therefore keeps its active background while
hovered or pressed. Disabled painting takes precedence over those states. Use a
custom interactive row when selected, hovered and pressed need independent
colors; see [Interaction](INTERACTION.md#custom-clickable-rows).

Component variants and theme palettes are different enums. Primary maps to
`CUI_THEME_BUTTON_PRIMARY`; secondary/danger/warning/success/info map to their
namesakes; default/outline map to `CUI_THEME_BUTTON_DEFAULT`. Ghost uses
secondary active, accent hover and a transparent normal background; its pressed
background comes from default active. Link uses `link`, `link_hover` and
`link_active`. There is no `CUI_THEME_BUTTON_GHOST` palette. Set `custom_colors`
on a component for a local override instead of copying the theme.

Headless tests exercise all nine variants, four sizes and four themes, measured
bounds, adornments, content callbacks, semantic names and ordinary push-button state and keyboard
suppression while loading. SVG icons, custom palettes and animation are separate
pending capabilities; a text adornment does not implement the Icon catalog family.

Buttons additionally support warning, success, and info intent variants and
extra-small density (`CUI_CONTROL_XSMALL`). The `outline` flag combines with an
intent to use its theme color for the border and label on the surface background.
The original standalone `CUI_BUTTON_OUTLINE` remains available. Semantic intent
foreground tokens are used for filled labels, including `on_danger`.

`selected` controls presentation only, matching the frozen reference. It no
longer mislabels an ordinary push button as checked; use the separate toggle
control for toggle semantics. Full upstream button parity, including independent
explicit toggle metadata and richer icon/tooltip/animation options, is still
under audit. Tests exercise all variants/densities across four themes plus
colored-outline painting, pointer activation and disabled keyboard suppression.

## Bounded paint handlers

Use [Button styles](BUTTON_STYLES.md) for additive instance, hover, active, selected, disabled and focus paint refinements. Explicit masks preserve zero values; callbacks are borrowed pure calculations and cannot change geometry or dispatch input. Legacy submission remains available.

# Button pointer activation barriers

Disabled and loading Buttons now prevent a pointer press on their visible area
from activating an underlying parent. This applies to `cui_base_button` when
disabled and to styled `cui_button` when disabled or loading. Existing callback,
keyboard and controlled state contracts are unchanged.

`cui_semantic_details.blocks_pointer_activation` is an append-only, opt-in Core
flag. Zero preserves the previous behavior of other controls. The previous-frame
hit graph considers a flagged element even when it is disabled, using the same
clip, modal, layer and submission-order rules as other pointer targets. A topmost
barrier consumes primary DOWN without moving focus or assigning capture. Primary
UP over a barrier cannot create an activation, including an activation of a
previously captured ancestor. Existing capture still receives motion and UP for
cleanup; CANCEL still clears capture. A later unobstructed press works normally.

This flag blocks pointer activation and pointer focus only. It does not disable
Tab, programmatic focus or keyboard activation on an otherwise enabled element.
It does not consume wheel events or prevent touch panning an actual scroll owner.
It also does not clear an existing text composition when the blocked press occurs.
Hover, cursor and current-frame prepaint occlusion are independent: callers that
need a passive hover occluder must use the existing hover/prepaint participation
contract. The flag alone is not a general visual or hover occlusion policy.

The focused regressions are `test_pointer_activation_blocker.c` (Core-only) and
`test_button_activation_blocker.c` (real Base and styled Buttons and Scrollable).
They cover legacy zero behavior, disabled/loading mouse and touch, focus retention,
release activation counts, capture cleanup, cancellation, subsequent clicks,
keyboard activation, clipping, later siblings, elevated layers, modal eligibility,
composition retention, hover independence and ancestor wheel/touch scrolling.

`tests/web/test_button_activation_blocker.py` independently builds its real CUI
WASM fixture and drives Chromium mouse, keyboard, wheel and CDP touch contacts.
The unfixed frozen source failed both disabled mouse and touch assertions with
parent count 1 and parent focus; the corrected source preserves the textbox focus
and leaves both callback counts at zero. The browser fixture also checks enabled
clicks, retained capture, cancellation and scrolling without page fallback. Run it
with pinned Playwright 1.58.0 and Chromium 1208; its `--source-root` option permits
the same regression against an earlier source checkout.

This is a scoped correctness fix, not certification of the complete upstream
Button family, every host, accessibility platform or physical touch device. The
separate Button completion audit still records remaining API and evidence gaps.

Worker validation on the frozen `6e36b5a` base: warning-enabled native build had
no warnings; existing CTest passed 121/122, with only the expected generated
distribution mismatch pending integrator regeneration. Both new standalone tests
passed `-std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror`, and passed ASan/UBSan with
leak detection. The existing Button behavior test also passed the sanitizer run.
The independent strict WASM build and full Chromium 1208 suite passed after the
fix. These results do not substitute for the integrator's generated distribution
and platform CI checks.

# Typed Button artwork

Button can borrow an Icon, Spinner or ProgressCircle descriptor through
`leading_artwork`. `loading_artwork` accepts an Icon descriptor. Existing string
icons and zero-initialized options retain their behavior. `leading_content`
takes priority over both typed slots.

The rules come from pinned v0.7.1 `button/button_icon.rs` (`ButtonIconVariant`,
`ButtonIcon::render`): loading replaces an ordinary Icon with a Spinner, using
its custom loading Icon when provided. An explicit Spinner or ProgressCircle
remains that artwork while loading, and ignores the loading replacement. A
custom loading Icon rotates with the existing 800ms quadratic Spinner cycle;
reduced motion leaves it static. This API does not add menus, progress ownership,
or a complete Button source parity claim.

```c
static bool save_button(cui_context *ui, cui_id id, const cui_theme *theme,
                        cui_icon_state *mark) {
    cui_button_artwork leading = {
        .kind = CUI_BUTTON_ARTWORK_ICON,
        .icon = mark,
        .icon_options = {.custom_color = true, .color = {25, 160, 80, 255}}
    };
    return cui_button_ex(ui, id, theme, cui_string("Save"),
                         (cui_button_options){.leading_artwork = &leading});
}
```

Initialize the caller-owned `mark` with `cui_icon_state_init`, then check
`cui_icon_set_name(mark, cui_string("check"), NULL, NULL)` before composition.
Destroy it with `cui_icon_state_destroy` only after all rendering has completed.
The caller owns Icon state and its bounded retained masks. Use
`cui_icon_set_limits` to constrain memory, and `cui_icon_state_collect` only
when prior draw lists have finished rendering. Button does not collect or
release caller resources. ProgressCircle borrows caller-provided RGBA storage,
its state, and any optional motion state. No Button artwork heap allocation is
introduced. Underlying Icon preparation can allocate within its configured
limits; the default Spinner uses the existing bounded context resource cache.

Button's resolved artwork size wins over descriptor dimensions: legacy/design
size, numeric `pixel_size`, and then explicit `icon_size` determine the slot.
Custom Icon color, opacity and nonloading transform are retained. Spinner
rotation replaces the transform while animated. ProgressCircle diameter is
resolved by Button; its fraction, color, clock, motion and raster scale remain
caller-controlled. A Spinner's default Loader is selected when its `icon` is
null. An ordinary Icon requires an initialized caller-owned Icon state.

A standalone Button copies descriptor values before accepted click callbacks.
Group copies its child option structures but borrows artwork descriptors:
callbacks must not mutate those descriptors until `cui_button_group_ex` returns.
Referenced render-resource states remain mutable for painting and must live
through renderer completion. Descriptor/result/resource objects must not alias;
known overlapping result ranges are rejected. Contained pointer targets are
not copied. Neither API freezes arbitrary caller mutations to resource storage.

Optional result outputs report local Icon preparation failures (including the
exact `cui_icon_error`) or ProgressCircle raster/argument/capacity failure. The
failed slot remains the resolved size and paints no stale image. Invalid
structural descriptors reject the Button without callbacks or result writes.
A zero-progress fraction is valid. Only the selected artwork descriptor receives
a result; ignored descriptors retain their previous output. Result outputs do not certify Core command,
layout, frame-arena, renderer, or GPU success; check those APIs separately.

Inert composition still paints and can update visible artwork resources or
request animation redraws, while preserving Button interaction state and
suppressing callbacks, hover notifications and tooltips. Layout-only composition
reserves the same slot but does not prepare artwork, change resource/result
state, or request redraw. Measurement and prepaint callbacks cannot compose
Buttons. Loading still disables activation independently of artwork kind.

The focused fixtures cover all 14 design sizes plus four legacy sizes, both
densities and both joined axes, custom color, computed/explicit size, replacement
and retained artwork, passive state/resource invariants, and bounded resource
failures. Native Noto and Chromium WASM fixtures exercise actual font/layout and
Canvas pixels; injected CDP touch is not physical-device validation.

Failure fixtures exercise configured Icon limits, ProgressCircle storage capacity,
and a full context resource table. They do not force a physical allocator failure.

# Button behavior

This change audits the Button at pinned GPUI component v0.7.1 commit
`87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34` (`button/button.rs`,
`button/button_icon.rs`, `base/button.rs`). It covers the features below;
custom shadows, ordered tab indexes, action-keybinding tooltip registries,
and arbitrary tooltip builders remain outside this API. It does not certify
whole-family parity or physical-device accessibility.

`cui_button_ex` retains the original primary variant, four legacy sizes,
zero-initialized options, boolean activation result, and replacement `content`
callback. Design sizes continue to derive all fourteen metrics from the theme.
Default, Text and Custom append to the existing variants. Outline remains
orthogonal. Link and Text use a hand cursor and no horizontal padding; Link
keeps its legacy control height, while Text fits its natural content. Default
uses the theme's default button palette. Custom uses an explicitly resolved
palette; it does not reproduce the source's Oklab color mixing or shadow.

Positive finite `height`, `font_size`, and `icon_size` override derived metrics
(up to 4096 logical pixels). Rounding selects theme, none, half-theme,
double-theme, or a caller's nonnegative finite radius. Compact reduces padding
and keeps known text/icon content at least as wide as the control height.
Arbitrary callback content must supply a suitable `width` when it needs a
minimum width. Positive width is an intentional clipping constraint; negative
width retains Core's grow convention. Callers must allow enough height for
arbitrary content.

Named `icon`, `trailing_icon`, `loading_icon` and `dropdown_caret` use the real
SVG icon renderer. The catalog always lists all names, but default builds
embed 126 SVG assets; choose bundled names (such as `check`, `arrow-right`,
`chevron-down`, `loader`) or supply a theme loader / `CUI_ICON_ALL_ASSETS`
for other catalog assets. Loading suppresses activation, exposes busy metadata, and
fades the normal/selected palette to 80% rather than using disabled colors.
A named loading glyph rotates using frame time; reduced motion keeps it still.
A `leading_content` callback takes precedence over generated loading/leading
artwork, allowing a caller-owned Progress or Spinner composition.
`trailing_content` replaces trailing artwork. `children` appends content after
the label or existing replacement callback. Slot callbacks own their borrowed
user data, geometry, colors, and nested semantics.

`on_click` runs once per accepted activation. The boolean return still reports
that same activation: use one action path, rather than handling both as separate
actions. `on_hover` reports interactive hover edges when a caller-owned state
is supplied. Disabled/loading controls ignore activation and hover callbacks.
`selected` remains presentation-only, with stable semantic value zero;
`toggle_semantics` plus `toggled` explicitly supplies checked/value metadata.
Browser or accessibility adapters must map that metadata appropriately; this
change does not add a generic browser `aria-pressed` mapping.

Pointer focus defaults remain compatible. `prevent_pointer_focus` opts into
pointer activation/capture without replacing current keyboard focus, using
Core's `no_pointer_focus` policy. Tab, Enter, Space, programmatic focus and
cancellation continue through Core. `skip_tab` removes the tab stop;
`hide_focus_ring` affects paint only. Focus rings otherwise show only for
focus-visible interaction. `custom_cursor` uses the cursor-only setter and
preserves the control's other semantics.

Optional state stores only hover lifecycle, tooltip state, an ellipsis buffer,
and an absolute next-wake deadline. Zero-initialize it, keep one state per
stable ID, and keep it alive across frames; an ID change resets it. No state
heap allocation or cleanup is required. Existing icon resources remain owned
by the context. Tooltips use the shared hover implementation and require a
viewport in `tooltip_options`; Escape, disabled state and targeted cancellation
close/suppress them. Hosts should honor invalidation and
`state.next_wake_seconds` in the Core frame-time clock (zero means idle).

A positive `label_width` makes the plain label unwrapped and clipped. With
state, it also ellipsizes at a grapheme boundary while preserving the complete
original accessible name (or explicit `accessibility_label`). The scratch
buffer is 256 bytes: a truncated prefix is capped at 252 bytes plus U+2026 and
NUL. A fully fitting label remains borrowed and has no 256-byte cap. If the
ellipsis itself cannot fit, the visible label is empty. This is plain-label
truncation, not a rich-text filter, shaping replacement, or callback-content
truncation.

```c
#include "cui/cui_components.h"
static cui_button_state save_state;
static void save(void *user) { ++*(unsigned *)user; }
void save_control(cui_context *ui, const cui_theme *theme, unsigned *saves) {
    (void)cui_button_ex(ui, cui_id_from(ui, "save"), theme, cui_string("Save changes"),
        (cui_button_options){.icon = cui_string("check"), .on_click = save,
            .action_user = saves, .state = &save_state,
            .prevent_pointer_focus = true, .custom_cursor = true,
            .cursor = CUI_CURSOR_POINTER});
}
```

Validation is scoped to `test_button_behavior.c` and
`test_button_behavior.py`: controlled activation/cancellation and pointer focus,
keyboard activation, inert loading/disabled state, stable toggle metadata,
432 variant/size/density paint-containment cases, real SVG slot geometry,
custom content, Unicode/buffer-boundary ellipsis and tooltip lifecycle. The browser slot test also requires the host preview height to include the
expanded variant and custom-content rows, and fails if those drawings are
clipped by the canvas. The
browser uses Chromium CDP touch contacts and actual mouse/keyboard input,
not direct reducer calls. Native headless tests do not constitute SDL window
or physical touchscreen coverage.

Constrained labels now use the current frame's laid-out label bounds. A positive
Button width, a grow width, or a positive `label_width` produces one clipped,
no-wrap label with a grapheme-boundary prefix and an ellipsis when it fits.
The original full label remains the semantic name. Leading/trailing artwork,
text, custom slots and the caret retain their own layout allocation; custom
content callbacks remain responsible for their internal layout. The content
clip also contains their paint. FIT buttons retain intrinsic sizing.

For fixed/grow Buttons, `content` children receive the current frame's inner width,
including space reserved for padding and leading/trailing slots. Ordinary wrapped
text and `cui_text_paragraph_colored(..., wrap=true)` wrap there just as they do
inside a normal box. A custom mail row can use a grow-width row containing a
fixed-width avatar and a grow-width column for the sender, subject and preview.
The callback runs once during submission; resizing needs no previous-frame bounds
or callback replay. Explicit fixed-width children and unwrapped text still obey
those choices, and the Button clips overflowing paint. Nested scroll/clipping
boxes retain their ordinary Core layout behavior.

`test_button_content_layout.c` compares wrapped line counts with normal boxes for
plain and paragraph text, fixed/grow widths, first-frame layout and resizing,
avatar/text columns and leading/trailing slots. It also checks text bounds, avatar
allocation and one callback invocation per submission. `test_button_content_font.c`
repeats these cases with a caller-opened native font.

`allow_content_overflow` is an explicit compatibility opt-out for the former
wrapping/overflow behavior.

Automatic label paint copies the full original bytes into the context's bounded
frame arena, using `cui_set_prepaint_parts`; it introduces no heap allocation or
new label-length limit. Borrowed slot resources retain their existing lifetime.
The optional caller-owned `cui_button_state.label` remains a 256-byte diagnostic
and compatibility buffer, so its truncated prefix keeps the previous bound.
Without that state, prefixes are limited by available width and frame capacity.
Prefixes preserve graphemes, while ellipsis fitting uses separately measured
prefix and ellipsis widths; this does not claim contextual shaping across the
join. Font shaping and glyph fallback remain adapter responsibilities.

Arena, command and registration capacity errors remain observable through Core's
error API and empty failed frame. Accepted callbacks occur during submission,
before later paint allocation failures; paint failure does not roll back an
already accepted action. Layout-only ancestry emits no label paint. Inert ancestry
paints and clips the same content without changing the optional state buffer.

`test_button_label_layout.c` covers fixed/grow current-frame resizing, all 18
legacy/design sizes in both densities, full semantics, leading/trailing slots,
caret, caller byte mutation, grapheme prefixes, malformed shapes, bounded arena
failure/recovery, inert/layout-only behavior and the opt-out. The independent
`test_button_label_font.c` repeats the matrix with a real caller-opened native
FreeType/HarfBuzz font; the portable ZWJ case is separate from the native font's
supported combining-mark case. `test_button_label_layout.py` compiles actual WASM,
checks Canvas pixels, current-frame widths and ellipsis commands, and dispatches
real Chromium mouse and CDP touch contacts. These tests close this label-layout
slice; they do not certify the entire Button family or physical device behavior.

Standalone Button composition under inherited inert or layout-only ancestry now
uses a passive path selected by Core's ordinary-submission phase queries. Inert
scopes retain content layout, artwork, clipping and presentation; layout-only
scopes retain layout without paint. Neither path registers Button metadata,
reduces tooltip state, invokes action/hover notifications, schedules a tooltip wake, or
changes any bytes of the caller-owned Button state. Content callbacks still run
to compose the visual children; they remain application code.

The original state pointer remains borrowed through deferred label paint, so its
existing 256-byte diagnostic-prefix cap stays consistent without a temporary
stack-state lifetime. The synchronous legacy overflow/explicit-ellipsis branch
uses a temporary paint copy whose visible bytes Core copies immediately; no
temporary state pointer reaches deferred paint. Passive ID reuse preserves state; a later ordinary frame
performs normal ID reconciliation. Explicit disabled/loading options in an
ordinary frame retain their existing blockers, hover/tooltip cleanup and loading
presentation. Calls outside ordinary submission, including font measurement and
prepaint callbacks, perform no standalone Button work. This is a CUI passive
composition correctness rule, not an upstream GPUI inert-scope parity claim.

The focused passive lifecycle fixture compares complete preloaded caller-state
bytes across fixed/grow labels, same/changed IDs, direct/inherited ancestry,
tooltip open/pending/suppressed states and zero/nonzero frame deltas. It retains
strict no-draw assertions for layout-only composition and checks ordinary touch
reuse, cancellation, disabled/loading behavior and guarded phases. The native
font fixture and independent Chromium WASM fixture extend that evidence to real
font measurement and actual hover-opened tooltips, Canvas paint and mouse/CDP
touch/keyboard reuse; they do not claim physical touchscreen coverage.

Visible inert loading artwork keeps its animation redraw requests. Layout-only
loading composes the same-sized icon slot without calling the artwork painter or
requesting invisible animation redraw. The existing Core paint-enabled query
distinguishes these policies; caller state/deadlines remain unchanged in both.
The fixture separately checks Core redraw state after each begin-frame reset and
verifies normal loading resumes, rather than inferring wake behavior from pixels.

### Numeric sizing, open presentation, and caret

`pixel_size` is an optional finite logical-pixel size in `(0, 4096]`; zero retains
legacy/design sizing. Negative, nonfinite, or larger values reject the Button
before layout, semantic registration, or callbacks. Numeric sizing follows the
pinned source's numeric `Size` branch: horizontal padding is 20% of the size,
leading/trailing artwork is 75%, normal text uses the theme's base font, and the
content gap uses the medium gap. A normal button has intrinsic content height;
an icon-only button defaults to a square of `pixel_size` except Link/Text. Compact mode does not
change numeric padding. Link and Text still have no horizontal padding.

Numeric sizing takes precedence over legacy/design metrics. Explicit `height`,
`font_size`, and `icon_size` then override their respective metrics; `width`
retains its existing FIT/grow/fixed behavior. Numeric dimensions are literal
logical pixels, independent of density, while base text, medium gap, and medium
caret follow theme density. Raster artwork reserves its rounded-up pixel extent;
the existing Icon resource capacity and validity rules still apply. This bounded
API does not promise successful artwork allocation for every large valid size.
Joined ButtonGroup children retain their own numeric sizing and `open` options
when group legacy/design/style inheritance is applied.

`open` selects active presentation without changing checked/value semantics,
selection, callbacks, focus, or managing a menu. It is independent of `selected`
and `toggled`. The dropdown caret uses normal foreground at 75% alpha even when
hover, press, open, disabled, or selected changes the label palette. Outline and
custom normal foregrounds are respected; loading and ancestor opacity still
compose over the whole control. Numeric sizing uses the medium caret size,
independent of numeric or explicitly overridden leading artwork size.

This slice implements those three documented contracts, not complete Button
family or platform parity. Its focused tests cover numeric precedence and geometry
across all 18 legacy/design sizes and two densities, normal/compact/icon-only
layout, explicit dimensions, custom/outline caret tint, disabled/loading paint,
and invalid numeric domains. A real Noto font fixture and Chromium WASM fixture
exercise the same implementation; Chromium input evidence is not physical device
validation. Existing constrained-label and passive lifecycle fixtures remain
separate regression gates.

The numeric formulas come from pinned `button/button.rs` lines 615–619 and
662–670, `sizing.rs` lines 337–343, and `select.rs` lines 59–67 at upstream
commit `87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`. Numeric Link/Text normal and icon-only buttons use intrinsic height and width,
matching the source no-padding branch; explicit caller dimensions still win.
The zero numeric default preserves CUI's established legacy icon-only sizing.

### Event-aware click callbacks

`on_click_event` receives one `cui_button_click_event` for every accepted
activation, in frame input order. The legacy `on_click` runs first for each event
when both are present, using the same `action_user`. Either callback can be used
alone. `cui_button_ex` continues to return one boolean indicating that at least
one activation was accepted; the callbacks preserve each individual event.

The payload contains the stable target ID, successful frame sequence, event
index and event type. Pointer activations include release coordinates in Core
logical pixels, pointer type/button/contact/device, release modifiers, and click
count (an unspecified zero normalizes to one). Keyboard activations carry the
accepted key and modifier bits, without a fabricated pointer position.
Accessibility activations have a distinct origin. Modifier bits for keyboard or
touch are a CUI extension: the pinned source ClickEvent helper reports no such
modifiers. This is an accepted-event snapshot, not a full source MouseClickEvent
with down and up samples, keyboard hitbox, first-mouse or touch long-press data.

The callback pointer is borrowed only until that callback returns. The structure
contains no borrowed pointers, so copying the value retains it safely across
frames or context destruction. `event_index` identifies that dispatched frame,
not a future queue entry; `frame_sequence` is scoped to context lifetime and its
existing wrap boundary. The callback must not end/reenter a frame or overwrite
an active Group workspace. Callback registration and descriptor fields are
snapshots; controlled model changes retain their existing semantics.

Disabled, loading, cancelled and passive inert/layout-only submissions produce
no callback. Repeated key events rejected by Core produce no callback. In a
styled ButtonGroup, child legacy and event callbacks both dispatch when the
group has no `on_change`. When `on_change` is present it overrides both child
callbacks, including the existing pointer-only/default or ALL_ACTIVATIONS policy.
The Base optional child event-index hook runs at that same dispatch point, after
legacy, and `result.callbacks` counts each actual callback invocation.

Cooperative `cui_consume_event` during the legacy notification cannot erase the
new notification for the already accepted event. The event-aware callback returns
`void`; it does not promise GPUI capture/bubble propagation or restore a consumed
event. The separate capture/propagation proposal records the remaining source
contracts in `validation/button-click-capture-next33.md`.

```c
struct button_model {
    unsigned clicks;
    cui_button_click_event last_click;
};
static void button_clicked(void *user, const cui_button_click_event *event) {
    struct button_model *model = user;
    model->last_click = *event;
    model->clicks++;
}
bool draw_event_button(cui_context *ui, const cui_theme *theme,
                       struct button_model *model) {
    return cui_button_ex(ui, 100, theme, cui_string("Open"),
        (cui_button_options){.on_click_event = button_clicked, .action_user = model});
}
```

The focused unit fixture verifies same-frame multiplicity and order, release
metadata, repeat/cancel/current-disabled rejection, cross-frame touch identity,
copy lifetime, accessibility, Group override and legacy-then-event order.
The real Noto native fixture uses that same implementation. Chromium WASM uses
actual mouse/keyboard/CDP touch input, modifiers, cancellation, passive rejection
and joined Group behavior; it is not evidence of physical OS/device input.

# Button activation evidence

`cui_button_click_event` now appends `has_evidence` and `evidence`, a copied
`cui_activation_snapshot`. The existing release-derived fields retain their
behavior. In particular, legacy `click_count` normalizes a pointer count of zero
to one, while `evidence.press.click_count` and `evidence.release.click_count`
preserve the raw host counts, including zero.

```c
static cui_button_click_event last_click;
static void remember_click(void *user, const cui_button_click_event *event) {
    (void)user;
    last_click = *event; /* No contained pointers; usable after the callback/frame. */
}
static bool compose_button(cui_context *ui, cui_id id, const cui_theme *theme) {
    return cui_button_ex(ui, id, theme, cui_string("Save"),
        (cui_button_options){.on_click_event = remember_click});
}
```

For each accepted event, standalone Button copies the evidence before invoking
legacy `on_click`, then invokes `on_click_event` once with the frozen payload.
Legacy callback consumption of that accessibility event cannot erase the
already accepted notification. Multiple accepted events retain input order and
separate evidence; repeated keys and cancelled activations remain rejected.
Callback-driven changes to later events still follow existing cooperative
consumption and current-semantic validation rules. This is not capture/bubble
propagation and does not restore consumed events.

Styled ButtonGroup prepares each child's payload before its legacy callback,
then forwards it through the existing post-legacy event-index hook. Its bounded
transient forwarding records require no heap allocation or public workspace
extension. Existing child callback counts remain unchanged. Group `on_change`
continues to override both child notifications and their preparation hook,
including the existing source-pointer-only versus explicit all-activations
policy. This does not change borrowed artwork descriptor lifetimes.

Base Group appends an optional `prepare_click_event` hook. It receives a
borrowed, const copied Core snapshot before legacy/post-legacy callbacks. Copy
it during the hook if it must be retained. Preparation is excluded from
`cui_button_group_result.callbacks`, which counts action notifications. The old
`on_click_event(user, ui, event_index)` remains compatible and still runs after
legacy notification even if legacy consumption makes a later Core query fail.

The evidence is forwarded unchanged from Core. A matching retained capture can
provide press and release samples across frames, including mouse, pen or touch.
An accepted unmatched release has release evidence without a fabricated press.
Keyboard bounds describe the previous rendered clipped routing rectangle,
which can differ from this frame's relaid-out Button. Accessibility evidence
contains no fabricated pointer samples or key bounds. `has_evidence` reports
successful copying; callers should inspect the individual `has_*` flags.

The payload can survive later frames or context destruction. Target/frame/index
identity remains local to the originating context and cannot identify recreated
contexts or a complete frame-sequence wrap. The callback pointer itself is
borrowed only until that callback returns. Refer to `ACTIVATION_SNAPSHOTS.md`
for Core rejection and capture lifetime details.

Pinned v0.7.1 uses `Button` click listeners (`button/button.rs`) and the
`gpui-pre=0.3.8` MouseClickEvent/KeyboardClickEvent contracts audited in
`validation/button-event-contract-next33.md`. First-focusing-click and
long-press metadata, source key-up focus-generation policy, signed tab paths
and event-local capture/bubble propagation remain separate gaps. This slice
forwards supported evidence and does not certify whole Button-family parity.

The focused headless fixture also reruns the existing callback contract suite.
It covers repeated clicks, cross-frame contacts, leave/re-entry, mismatched
release, cancellation, raw versus normalized counts, modifiers, old keyboard
bounds after relayout, accessibility consumption by legacy callbacks, retained
copies, Group multiplicity/override and the old Base index hook. Noto and actual
WASM/Chromium fixtures exercise font layout and genuine mouse/keyboard/CDP touch
input. Injected CDP contacts are not physical-device or OS adapter validation.

# Button built-in state painting

This slice corrects built-in Button painting against GPUI Kit 0.7.1 commit
`87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`. It adds no public API.
The broader [state refinement audit](design/BUTTON_STATE_REFINEMENT_AUDIT.md)
still describes proposed work, including callbacks, focus rendering, shadows,
compound hover and theme fidelity. This slice does not complete that parity row.

For Ghost, pointer hover uses the accent foreground and accent fill; dark
mode halves the fill alpha. Pressed uses the default active fill and normal
Ghost foreground. Selected/open uses the secondary active fill and normal
Ghost foreground, suppressing pointer hover and pressed changes. Outlined
selected Ghost uses the default active fill instead. These are distinct source
states, even when a theme happens to give them the same colors.

Outlined selected Link and Text retain their normal foreground. Filled
selected Link uses active link ink; filled selected Text uses foreground alpha
0.7. Outlined Ghost/Link/Text retain outline border geometry with transparent
built-in borders, matching the source's orthogonal outline construction.
Explicit custom palettes keep their own background, border and foreground
values; selected remains the custom active background.

Disabled wins over selected/open and loading. Filled intent/custom borders use
alpha multiplied by 0.15; Secondary uses 1.5, clamped to 255. Outlines use
0.5. The existing built-in Default rule remains half-alpha input background
and input border. Ghost/Link/Text keep transparent disabled backgrounds and
muted foreground at half alpha. Loading keeps its normal or selected/open
colors, suppresses pointer styling, and fades the whole control to 0.8 unless
also disabled. Returning to an interactive state restores normal hover paint.

Source evidence:
[Button render and variant resolvers](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-kit/blob/87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34/crates/component/src/button/button.rs),
particularly render lines 703–733, outline selected lines 1274–1283, and
variant disabled lines 1316–1376. CUI resolves these formulas using its existing
solid-color palette. CUI theme defaults, RGB token derivation and source
OkLab/non-solid backgrounds remain separate limitations. Focus-ring behavior
is unchanged. Activation reduction, callbacks, aggregate bools and sizing are
unchanged; selected/open still do not implicitly set toggled semantics.

`tests/unit/test_button_state_refinement.c` checks both themes, all variants,
custom translucent colors, outlined/filled disabled borders, Ghost hover and
pressed/selected/open combinations, disabled plus selected/loading, loading
fade and recovery. It asserts semantic inertness/busy/presentation separation,
text and border draw colors, and actual software-rendered blank interior
pixels. Text commands are checked directly and omitted from software pixel
rendering because the portable test has no font backend. Loading icons remain
in the rendered list; pixel samples avoid their slot.

Validation used strict portable C11 warnings (`-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic
-Werror`) and a private CMake build rooted in the isolated worktree. The new
fixture was registered only in that private build's CTest file. Seven tests
passed through `python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir
/tmp/cui-button-state-build`: the new fixture, Button behavior, passive
lifecycle, activation blocker, callback events, click event and click snapshot.
Root integration must register the new fixture in canonical CMake and refresh
owned consumer guidance/generated resources. No native windows were opened.
