# Float-HSLA inline color entry

`cui_color_hsla.h` supplies reusable normalized float HSL/encoded-RGBA conversions
and source-format hex operations. It depends only on Core declarations, and the
primitive implementation can link independently with the math library. This is
HSL lightness, not HSV brightness; encoded RGB is unpremultiplied and receives no
sRGB transfer-function conversion. It is separate from Plot's linear shader seam.

`cui_color_hsla_entry.h` adds a caller-owned float selection/preview/draft model
and a real Input field. Existing byte `cui_color_entry`, HSV `cui_color_picker`,
theme parsing, Plot and their event contracts remain unchanged. Handwritten
Python, Node/TypeScript, Go and Rust builders do not expose this new model.

Use normalized finite components in inclusive 0..1. Checked operations reject
NaN, infinity or out-of-range values atomically; they do not wrap hue, clamp,
snap to steps or discard latent hue on achromatic colors. Hue 1 is retained as
owner state, although it renders like hue 0. Optional absence differs from a
present transparent color. C float preserves source-scale precision, without
promising bit-identical arithmetic on every C platform.

Initialize a zeroed `cui_color_hsla_entry_state` once and retain its address. The
editor borrows its ten-byte owned draft; the state cannot be copied/moved, and its
members are read-only to callers. Destroy after the final draw list has been
consumed. Repeated destroy is safe. Init/sync/preview/restore/direct-value commit
format locally and allocate a fresh editor before publishing new float fields.
Allocation failure restores the old buffer/editor/history/model; success resets
Input state and undo history. Do not call these operations during field submission
or while prior draw data remains borrowed.

`cui_color_hsla_entry_sync` silently copies optional owner committed/preview values
and derives display text. Dirty draft conflicts unless replacement is explicit,
even for an equal owner. Preview replaces only preview/display; restore returns
to committed display. Both respect dirty replacement and leave committed unchanged.
Set-draft admits empty text or hash followed by up to eight ASCII hex digits;
complete text previews, incomplete text retains the last valid preview. Empty
text cannot commit or clear selection; silent owner sync to absent clears it.

The crucial precision distinction is explicit commit versus derived display:

- Sync, direct HSLA preview/commit, ordinary frames and theme changes retain the
  supplied float components. Formatting is never fed back through the hex parser.
- Hex parsing accepts optional hash and 3/4/6/8 digits, expands nibbles, divides
  bytes by 255, then converts float RGB to HSL. No CSS names/functions/decimal
  channel grammar is included. The UI additionally requires hash (or empty draft).
- Source-style formatting truncates channels and omits alpha only when opaque:
  float alpha `.5` displays `7F`. Explicit hex commit reparses even an unchanged
  formatted draft, so Enter on that display commits `127/255`, not `.5`.
  Direct `commit_value` retains `.5`. This deliberate distinction matches the
  frozen source's suppression of programmatic display feedback.

Conversions write output only on success. Hex parse writes only on COMPLETE;
NULL output validates. The formatter reports required payload bytes (7 or 9),
capacity includes NUL, and insufficient capacity leaves destination untouched.
NULL/0 probes length and returns CAPACITY; NULL/nonzero is invalid. Invalid
arguments report required zero. Inputs/outputs must be disjoint. No universal
byte-exact float hex round-trip or cross-platform GPU arithmetic claim is made.

Commit results distinguish SELECT (close requested) and UPDATE (no close request).
Both succeed for same-value commits. The inline field owns no popup, so a close
request is not a completed dismissal. The actual Input field handles focused,
accepted nonrepeated Enter as SELECT in queue order; consumed, IME-owned,
disabled, readonly, inert or layout-only paths do not commit. Invalid admission
is `input.rejected`; submitting admitted incomplete text increments the separate
rejected-commit count. Counts do not depend on installing an observer.

The outer observer receives one copied summary after Base semantics or styled
paint if at least one commit completed. Previous is the entry selection at the
start of submission; final committed may differ from preview if text follows
Enter in the same frame. Metadata is UNKNOWN with actual eligible frame only,
without invented source/index/activation facts. The payload is pointer-free and
can be copied beyond callback/context lifetime. Handler/user/options are entry
snapshots; borrowed label/user must survive return. Do not mutate/free live entry,
context or borrowed resources, or recursively submit UI, inside the callback.
Update a separate owner and sync before the next submission.

The executable owner example is
[`tests/unit/test_color_hsla_entry_owner.c`](../tests/unit/test_color_hsla_entry_owner.c).
It submits the real styled field, enters shorthand text and commits with Enter,
then applies a separately copied owner value on the next submission. The focused
fixture compiles and runs it, with C++ header compatibility and existing byte
ColorEntry/Picker/Picker Events/Input regressions. `test_color_hsla_model.c` uses
linker-wrapped real editor allocation failures to verify rollback at every editor
allocation budget; no public allocator test hook is introduced. The primitive
test links without CUI implementations to prove independent reuse.

Configure `tests/fixtures/color_hsla` with a matching `-DCUI_LIBRARY=/path/libcui.a`
and a private Release build directory. The failure fixture uses GNU/ELF linker
wrapping and is not a claim of Windows/macOS allocator-injection coverage. Build
with strict warnings, then run `python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir <dir>`
with a private home-cache TMPDIR. Assertions remain enabled in Release. The
semantic tests prove textbox naming/readonly/disabled facts and theme backgrounds,
not native AT announcements or hardware rendering.

This slice has no popup/open owner, palette/HSLA tabs, slider UI, native screen
sampler or foreign builders. The next popup coordinator must apply SELECT close
requests before its own outer notification, preserving source close-before-Change
timing; it cannot simply forward an early inner callback. Future sliders must
use direct float updates and avoid rewriting an active drag from formatted hex.
These remain separately reviewed work; full ColorPicker parity is not claimed.

Integrator guidance: register new Base sources `cui_color_hsla.c` and
`cui_color_hsla_entry.c`, and styled `src/components/cui_color_hsla_entry.c`.
Keep primitive tests linked only to the primitive implementation and `m`; field
tests and owner example link CUI. The failure-injection test additionally needs
`--wrap=malloc`, `--wrap=calloc`, `--wrap=realloc`. Embed guarded private
`src/base/cui_color_hsla_entry_internal.h` before both entry sources when generating
standalone headers; no private declarations belong in public headers. Canonical
source metadata, SDK/dist/skill generation and standalone/CUI_ALL verification
remain the integrator's next gate.

# Command

Command is an inline command palette, composed from the real persistent Input,
virtual rows and Scroll control. The scroll area spans the panel width; rows reserve space for its scrollbar and horizontal insets. An application can host it in the existing
Dialog/Overlay. This module follows the pinned GPUI 0.7.1
`component/src/command/{command,item,state}.rs` contracts; it does not supply a
native application Action registry or automatically create a modal dialog.

```c
char query_buffer[256] = {0};
cui_edit *query = cui_edit_create((cui_edit_config){
    .buffer = query_buffer, .capacity = sizeof(query_buffer)});
cui_command_row workspace[64];
cui_command_state state;
cui_command_init(&state, workspace, 64, query);

cui_command_item settings[] = {
    {.label = cui_string("Profile"), .icon = cui_string("user")},
    {.label = cui_string("Billing"), .disabled = true},
};
cui_command_entry entries[] = {
    {.kind = CUI_COMMAND_ITEM,
     .item = {.label = cui_string("Calendar")}},
    {.kind = CUI_COMMAND_SEPARATOR},
    {.kind = CUI_COMMAND_GROUP, .heading = cui_string("Settings"),
     .items = settings, .item_count = 2},
};
cui_command_options options = cui_command_default();
options.label = cui_string("Commands");
cui_command(ui, id, &theme, &state, entries, 3, options);
```

Initialize once, submit each frame, and destroy the editor after the state is no
longer rendered. Workspace and editor remain application-owned. Model-only use
can initialize with a null editor. The base source links without Core, Theme or
Edit implementations, and allocates nothing.

Entries, strings, keyword arrays and callback users are borrowed until the next
rebuild. Keep them alive through rendering and any direct model operation such
as `cui_command_confirm`. Rebuilding validates the worst-case unfiltered row
capacity before writing; include headings and every supplied separator in that
capacity. The module limits workspace and supplied items to 4096. Bad model or
capacity leaves the existing model unchanged. Measurement must produce finite,
positive outer row heights no greater than one million logical pixels.

Filtering trims whitespace, then matches a case-insensitive substring in the
label or any keyword. Default folding handles ASCII; supply `options.matches`
for Unicode case folding or another host search policy. Turning off filterable
keeps all rows but still reports searchable query changes. Turning off
searchable hides the Input, retains all rows and suppresses query callbacks,
including for a programmatically modified hidden editor.

Original indices survive filtering: all ungrouped items use section zero in
input order. Groups use their group ordinal, offset by one when any ungrouped
item exists. Empty groups hide their headings. Leading, trailing and repeated
separators are omitted. Disabled items remain visible and count as matches,
but cannot be selected or confirmed.

Up/Down wrap through enabled items. Enter invokes the selected action first,
then the confirmation callback, including for items with no action. Pointer
entry changes the highlight without scrolling; a click confirms. Row pointer
capture is exercised across separate press, movement and release frames.
Keyboard changes request nearest scrolling; a model reinstall preserves an
eligible original path and does not move the viewport. Explicitly cleared
selection remains cleared until navigation or a query change. A changed query
resets to the first enabled result and calls selection before query. Callbacks
run synchronously after the model update; callers may inspect state, but must
not destroy the UI/editor/state or invalidate borrowed model storage while a
render call is in progress. Unlike GPUI deferred callbacks, CUI has no window
lease or liveness object: application dispatch owns that lifecycle boundary.

`action` and `binding` share an `action_user`; the host resolves a live binding
for the same executable action. The default row draws its resolved hint using
Kbd. A binding takes precedence over a checked mark. Custom content owns its
keybinding presentation, and checked custom items still receive the source's
trailing check. Application scope/keymap registration and platform-specific
Action dispatch remain host responsibilities.

Default list maximum is 300 logical pixels. Frame uses popover colors, a
one-pixel border and radius_lg; bordered=false removes that frame. List inset is
4, default rows use horizontal8/vertical6 padding and font14/line20; headings
use font12/line16, and separators occupy9. Theme density scales those metrics.
The 380-pixel default width is a portable convenience; negative width grows.
Growing palettes use retained width for measurement with an initial380 estimate.
Default labels use a clipped single-line box; automatic arbitrary intrinsic
wrapping/measurement is not implemented. A row's `measure` callback receives
available outer content width and font size, returns its complete outer height,
and can implement wrapping/custom variable heights. It must agree with its
content callback. Every flattened row is measured each submission; only visible
rows invoke content and submit semantic/paint nodes. This has bounded O(n)
measurement and avoids drawing all offscreen children, but does not reproduce
GPUI's typography/action-binding row measurement cache.

Header/footer/empty callbacks receive current state and render arbitrary CUI
content. Loading shows the actual Icon spinner beside Input and suppresses the
empty slot. Placeholder, empty message and accessible label can be supplied by
the application for localization. ListBox/Option semantics expose selection,
disabled state and busy status. Quick-action mode focuses the Command frame;
searchable mode focuses the actual Input. Row options have no Tab stop, while
application-provided child controls retain their own semantics.

For Dialog composition set `cui_surface_options.no_escape_dismiss=true`.
Command consumes the first Escape when a searchable query is nonempty. Empty
query Escape calls `on_cancel` and remains unconsumed; let that callback request
`cui_surface_request_close(ui, surface, CUI_SURFACE_CANCELLED)`. The next surface
submission applies the decision policy, removes the modal and restores trigger
focus. Do not immediately destroy/close the host from an action callback. The
headless suite exercises this actual Surface composition, including the two
Escape presses and focus restoration.

Link the base and component sources into normal CUI. Styled implementation
uses Components/Input, Edit, Scroll, Icon and Content/Kbd. Tests additionally
use Surface/Overlay for modal composition. A base-only test defines
`CUI_COMMAND_BASE_ONLY` and links `src/base/cui_command.c` plus math only.

# Command observers

Include `cui/cui_command_events.h`. The additive `cui_command_rebuild_events`,
`cui_command_select_events`, `cui_command_move_events` and
`cui_command_confirm_events` accept the existing arguments, an explicit nonzero
metadata target after state, and a `cui_command_event_handler`. Existing functions
and public layouts remain unchanged. Base and Styled submission are available; foreign bindings remain separate work.

```c
static void confirmed(void *user, const cui_command_activation *event) {
    cui_command_index *saved = user;
    *saved = event->value; /* Copy the confirmed path, not later selected state. */
}
/* state/options/selected_path are application-owned. */
/* cui_command_confirm_events(state, 90, options,
 *     (cui_command_event_handler){.on_activate=confirmed,.user=&selected_path}); */
```

`result.control` is the exact legacy bool result: false can mean no change or
invalid input, and does not imply rollback. Zero target rejects before any reducer
work. Counts record actual synchronous observer calls, saturating with
`count_overflow`; absent callbacks ignore user and preserve reducer behavior.
Base metadata is PROGRAMMATIC with the supplied target, without invented context,
frame, index or activation evidence, even when the application calls it in a UI
frame. Section/row indices are operation-time paths, not stable item IDs.

Selection CHANGE follows each successful select/move transition or changed-query
rebuild that installs a different eligible path. `has_previous` establishes whether
`previous` exists. Rebuilds with `query_changed=false` remain silent even if model
replacement removes/changes selection. Selection loss emits no new event.
Explicit Base `query_changed=true` can notify on initialization, unlike Styled's
initial false flag; it need not mean different query bytes. Direct select/move
retain the legacy policy of ignoring options.disabled/loading. Confirm respects
options/item disabled, but loading and missing action/hooks do not suppress it.

Rebuild installs state and freezes all selected-path snapshots, then invokes the
new query observer **before either legacy hook**. When all are eligible the order
is new query → old select → new selection → old query. The old hooks retain their
relative order and timing. Query observation requires changed && searchable and
borrows the original untrimmed raw query view only during callback. This explicit
ordering exception lets old select/query hooks replace/reallocate query storage
without adding a dangling-view read afterward. The old select hook retains only
its pre-existing obligation to preserve the view for old on_query when installed.
No allocation, workspace or hidden query snapshot is added. To retain text use
`cui_component_event_copy_utf8` with explicit bound/storage and check its status;
a struct copy does not own text.

Other new observers follow the old hook. Select freezes paths before legacy code
can redirect state. Confirm snapshots actual selected row and legacy confirm/user,
then runs action → captured old confirm → new activation. Action-induced selection
changes do not rewrite the confirmed path. Same-item/repeated confirmations remain
separate ACTIVATE calls. No callback rejects an operation, changes consumption or
introduces commit/submit semantics.

Handlers/user borrow through the outer call. Selection/activation payloads are
pointer-free copies, safe to retain beyond resource teardown. New handlers may
copy facts or set unrelated application flags; they must not mutate/rebind active
state/editor/model/resources, recurse into the same operation, destroy resources
or unwind across C. Legacy mutations retain their existing timing. Defer removal
and teardown until the outer operation and any renderer consumption complete.
Missing callbacks do not make controls read-only. Clearing selection remains the
existing silent helper. Styled behavior is specified below; Base always remains contextless.

## Styled submission and causes

`cui_command_events(ui, id, theme, state, entries, count, options, handler)`
returns the same typed result with the legacy Styled bool in `control` and counts
across all operations actually observed during that call. No final-state replay,
extra model interaction or allocation is added. A later false return retains
successful earlier query/selection notifications, including before invalid custom
geometry. The same early-query exception and callback lifetime rules apply.

The leading rebuild detects an externally edited query by the existing hash. It
is PROGRAMMATIC with no invented frame/input evidence, including under disabled,
inert/layout-only ancestry or loading. Initial/unchanged rebuild remains silent.
An aggregate query-input change reports UNKNOWN with the proven active frame,
without picking a text event/index; Escape query-clear has its actual keyboard
frame/index/source. Hover selection is aggregate and may be stationary: it reports
UNKNOWN/frame-only, not a fabricated pointer event. No per-edit query claim.

A row's activation evidence is captured after its current semantic interaction,
before hover-selection or custom content/binding/old callbacks can consume input
or redirect state. One genuine accepted activation supplies its exact snapshot;
multiple/missing evidence reports frame-only UNKNOWN. Shared event target is the
Command root; the snapshot keeps its actual row target. Confirm snapshots the
actual selected path at confirm entry, including legacy redirects. If it differs
from the clicked row, the copied clicked-row activation snapshot is omitted;
known causal input index/source remains. Action changes after confirm entry do
not rewrite that identity. Keyboard loop observations have actual frame/index/
KEYBOARD evidence, without inventing accepted activation for a query-editor target.

`on_cancel(user, const cui_command_cancel_request *)` reports REQUEST to dismiss
the host, not completed dismissal. It runs after legacy on_cancel, or independently
when only the new observer is installed, on the same eligible empty-query Escape
branch. `cancel_request_count` counts actual observer calls. No additional consume,
invalidation, overlay close or veto is introduced. Nonempty searchable Escape
still clears/rebuilds query rather than requesting cancellation.

UI observations require a nonzero ordinary active frame; inert/layout-only,
measurement and out-of-frame work emit no new UI callbacks. Legacy callback and
mutation rules remain unchanged. Disabled suppresses UI interaction; loading is
busy presentation and does not suppress existing nonempty-row confirmation.
No submission emits nothing and registers no callback. Command rows retain OPTION with the existing pointer_activatable detail; actual
accessibility FOCUS and ACTIVATE are supported without a role remap. This does not
claim broader foreign/platform accessibility parity. Custom content, matching and binding
callbacks remain separate APIs. Native synchronous observers do not add bridge or
Python/Node/Go/Rust event categories.

# Shared component event metadata

The additive `cui_component_events.h` utility supplies common metadata and a bounded text-copy helper. It does **not** change any existing component callback, result, state owner or dispatch timing. The [78-family coverage](design/COMPONENT_EVENTS_COVERAGE.md), [binding audit](design/COMPONENT_EVENTS_BINDINGS.md) and [design contract](design/COMPONENT_EVENTS_CONTRACT.md) describe the wider work. The first [Button and Check facades](CONTROL_EVENTS.md) are implemented; [Switch/Toggle facades](BOOLEAN_EVENTS.md) are also implemented; implemented family guides below describe their precise scope. The [current coverage audit](design/COMPONENT_EVENTS_REMAINING.md) records remaining gaps and justified exceptions. This utility is not full component parity.

## Names and meanings

`cui_component_event_metadata` is a pointer-free value containing a kind, nonzero stable target ID, presence flags, optional context-local frame/index, source, and an optional copied `cui_activation_snapshot`. Component values and reasons stay in separate typed payloads: a requested boolean, tri-state, date, double or selection is not a `void *value`.

| Kind | Meaning supplied by the component that uses it |
| --- | --- |
| `CUI_COMPONENT_EVENT_ACTIVATE` | Accepted attempt to invoke an action; no implied value change. |
| `CUI_COMPONENT_EVENT_REQUEST` | Proposed typed value; the owner may reject it. |
| `CUI_COMPONENT_EVENT_CHANGE` | A transition that actually applied. |
| `CUI_COMPONENT_EVENT_COMMIT` | Gesture/transaction completion, possibly with no net change. |
| `CUI_COMPONENT_EVENT_SUBMIT` | Explicit submission, distinct from typing or blur. |
| `CUI_COMPONENT_EVENT_LIFECYCLE` | Component-specific open/close/begin/end reason, kept separately. |

`cui_component_event_init(&metadata, kind, target, source)` validates the enums and target and clears unavailable fields. `SOURCE_UNKNOWN` omits `HAS_SOURCE`; `SOURCE_PROGRAMMATIC` explicitly records a known application origin without inventing an input event. Pointer, keyboard and accessibility sources may also be explicitly supplied when known. Source alone does not imply activation evidence. An all-zero struct is not a valid target-bearing event.

Presence flags are authoritative. `HAS_FRAME`, `HAS_INDEX`, `HAS_SOURCE` and `HAS_ACTIVATION` describe optional information; index zero is a valid first event, not an absence sentinel. `cui_component_event_set_frame_index(&metadata, frame_sequence, event_index)` records a known pair and rejects frame zero, index `SIZE_MAX`, or replacement of copied activation identity. The utility does not infer a position for programmatic work. Frame/index identities are local to the originating context and cannot be compared across recreated contexts. No timestamp, global ordering, physical device or pointer position is manufactured.

## Copy accepted evidence before mutable callbacks

This complete helper can be used by a component adapter at its existing accepted-activation point. Calling it does not route, consume, accept or redispatch an input event:

```c
#include <cui/cui_component_events.h>

static bool activation_metadata(cui_context *ui, size_t event_index,
                                cui_component_event_metadata *out) {
    cui_activation_snapshot snapshot;
    if (!cui_event_activation_snapshot(ui, event_index, &snapshot))
        return false;
    return cui_component_event_from_activation(out, CUI_COMPONENT_EVENT_ACTIVATE,
                                                &snapshot);
}
```

Use a real snapshot or its unchanged copy. `from_activation` checks nonzero identity and supported accepted event types, derives the source, and copies existing evidence; it cannot authenticate a fabricated struct. Pointer release, key down/up and accessibility activation are supported. The utility preserves the snapshot exactly, including optional press/release/key-bounds flags. Key and accessibility events gain no fake pointer sample. Snapshot acquisition must precede mutable callbacks that could consume input. Failed helpers leave outputs unchanged.

The resulting metadata may be copied by value and kept after callback, later frames or context destruction. This guarantee covers this pointer-free metadata and Core's snapshot, not arbitrary typed component payloads. In particular, copying `cui_event` does **not** deep-copy its borrowed text pointer.

## Copy borrowed text into caller storage

`cui_component_event_copy_utf8(source, maximum_bytes, storage, capacity, &copied)` returns a `cui_component_event_copy_status`. Argument order deliberately places the source and payload byte limit before destination storage and its capacity. The source length and maximum are UTF-8 **bytes**, not glyphs. Capacity includes the trailing NUL; the returned `cui_str.length` excludes it.

```c
static cui_component_event_copy_status keep_text(cui_str borrowed,
                                                 char storage[257], cui_str *saved) {
    return cui_component_event_copy_utf8(borrowed, 256, storage, 257, saved);
}
```

The caller owns both storage and descriptor. Keep storage alive for every use of the copied view. The helper allocates nothing, truncates nothing and never retains a handler or pointer. It checks the maximum and capacity before reading bytes, reuses Base's existing UTF-8 validation, rejects embedded NUL, and uses `memmove` so source and destination text may overlap. The output descriptor itself must be disjoint from both text regions. `{NULL,0}` is valid empty input but still requires one writable destination byte for NUL. Callers must provide the declared readable/writable extents; no C function can discover arbitrary allocation sizes from a pointer.

`COPY_INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `COPY_LIMIT`, `COPY_CAPACITY` and `COPY_INVALID_UTF8` leave **both destination bytes and output descriptor unchanged**. A source length of `SIZE_MAX` fails as a limit error before adding NUL or reading bytes. No partial output or required-size side channel is published on failure. Caller-selected limits make the memory/time budget explicit; this utility does not choose a hidden global payload limit.

## Integration and lifetime boundary

These are portable C11 header-only helpers. Include `cui/cui_component_events.h`; the text-copy helper calls existing `cui_edit_valid_utf8` and therefore requires the existing portable `cui` library. Metadata-only use needs no extra runtime or allocation. No platform/Clay types, callback registration, scheduler or networking are introduced.

Direct C components still retain their existing behavior: Button legacy callback precedes its typed callback; controlled requests are distinct from owner acceptance; frame-result reads do not replay callbacks. Speech explicit pump, bridge queued language delivery, retained Surface/Notification/Dock registrations and current-frame Plot/Chart deferred callbacks keep their own documented timing and lifetimes. This utility neither permits recursive frame/component submission nor context destruction during callbacks.

No binding event facade or automatic callback export is supplied by this slice. Future facades and bindings require their own typed-value, lifetime, multiplicity, reentrancy and compatibility tests. Applications must choose one side-effect path per action rather than performing it from both callback and frame result.

The focused `tests/unit/test_component_events.c` exercises actual accepted pointer, keyboard and accessibility snapshots, evidence retention after consumption/context destruction, absent/programmatic metadata, identity overwrite rejection, atomic UTF-8 failure, exact byte/capacity limits, empty text, malformed encodings, overflow-sized input and overlapping copies. Native test runs use the invisible wrapper:

```sh
python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir build -- -R component_events
```

The helper is registered in native and WASI tests and included in generated distributions, the Go/Rust source SDKs and the agent resource index. Inclusion of a C header in a source SDK does not expose a language wrapper. Binding event facades remain documented omissions.

## Nonblocking application work

The separate [async HTTPS fetch example](../examples/async_fetch/README.md) builds an actual native UI using the existing synchronous Button callback. It copies requests to a worker, shows loading, prevents duplicate requests, delivers completions through a bounded mailbox and wakes the idle UI. Its guide covers failure, retry, stale responses, cancellation and joined shutdown, with deterministic offline tests. Networking and worker code belong to the optional Linux host example; they are not Core APIs or a replacement event-dispatch architecture.

The bridge separately supports [versioned typed manual notification polling](BRIDGE_NOTIFICATIONS.md). These queued post-mutation views preserve legacy dispatch timing and do not provide synchronous value rejection through language bindings.

The controlled [Slider phase facade](SLIDER_EVENTS.md) preserves double values and distinguishes BEGIN/UPDATE/COMMIT/CANCEL, including cancellation without fabricated input evidence. The [Styled Slider facade](STYLED_SLIDER_EVENTS.md) adds themed rendering with the same controlled double phases. Foreign-language request facades remain unsupported.

The [Base Input observer](TEXT_INPUT_EVENTS.md) and [Styled Input facade](TEXT_INPUT_STYLED_EVENTS.md) report committed text changes and eligible submissions synchronously. These input facades do not add rejectable edit requests; [multiline observers](MULTILINE_EVENTS.md) are available separately. [Go and Rust manual notification views](BRIDGE_NOTIFICATIONS_GO_RUST.md) preserve typed queue values with owning payloads; their callbacks retain existing timing.

[RadioGroup observers](SELECTION_EVENTS.md) report actual owner selection transitions after the existing request callback. Select/Combobox and general selection requests remain outside that slice; RadioGroup activation snapshots are unavailable at its preserved reducer step.

[Textarea observers](MULTILINE_EVENTS.md) deliberately aggregate committed revision changes into at most one notification per submission. They do not claim a single input cause, per-event delivery or submission intent; Editor observers use the same aggregation, after its entire completion/multicursor/painting pass.

[Select observers](SELECT_EVENTS.md) report each actual selection transition, preserving the full list pass and popup-close timing. [Combobox observers](COMBOBOX_EVENTS.md) preserve Base/query and popup-list phase ordering; option accessibility limitations are explicit in both guides.

[Surface completed-close observers](SURFACE_EVENTS.md) use caller-owned retained registration, unlike render-call-only handlers. Existing close decisions and result consumption stay separate from lifecycle notification.

[MenuTree observers](MENU_EVENTS.md) report each applied command synchronously,
including repeated commands. ContextMenu and Simple Menu forwarding are implemented separately; Dropdown forwarding is also implemented separately; this is not complete menu-family coverage.

[NumberInput observers](NUMBER_EVENTS.md) report an aggregate committed double
change after the legacy reducer, independently of draft revisions or submission.
They preserve step-policy callbacks and do not provide rejectable numeric requests.

Additional implemented observers cover [Tabs selection](TABS_EVENTS.md),
[ContextMenu commands](CONTEXT_MENU_EVENTS.md), [Pagination, Stepper and Rating](NUMERIC_SELECTION_EVENTS.md),
and [Calendar/DatePicker selected dates and ColorPicker RGBA](PICKER_EVENTS.md).
[Simple Menu commands](SIMPLE_MENU_EVENTS.md) preserve repeated activations.
Their guides specify aggregation and timing. These additions do not automatically extend binding allowlists.

[DropdownButton](DROPDOWN_EVENTS.md) exposes separate action and menu handlers
while preserving their phase order. [OTP](OTP_EVENTS.md) provides aggregate
accepted-operation and completion counts on CHANGE; completion is not submission.
These C additions do not extend the foreign notification allowlist automatically.

[Collapsible transitions](DISCLOSURE_EVENTS.md) report every applied expanded
bool write before final semantics and paint. [Single List selection](LIST_EVENTS.md)
reuses the ordered selection seam after legacy activation/confirmation callbacks.
Accordion, multi-list and ToggleGroup also report each applied transition; see
[disclosure events](DISCLOSURE_EVENTS.md) and [List events](LIST_EVENTS.md).
The [opt-in bridge value API](BRIDGE_VALUE_NOTIFICATIONS.md) currently supports
scalar, plain-text and selection notifications; existing polling retains its contract, and Python, JS/TypeScript, Go and Rust expose separate owning value polls.

[Tree events](TREE_EVENTS.md) observe each applied selection and expansion transition and every row invocation without replaying reduction; callbacks precede later semantics and paint.

[DataTable events](TABLE_EVENTS.md) cover sort, single selection, exact multi-selection sets and column width/move transitions;
[Settings events](SETTINGS_EVENTS.md) cover navigation and built-in boolean,
number and choice fields plus committed text revisions. Explicit programmatic and UI resets report RESET separately from normal EDIT changes.


[TimeField events](TIME_FIELD_EVENTS.md) report zero or one final typed time
change after the complete Base/Styled operation; draft/focus changes are separate.
[Sidebar events](SIDEBAR_EVENTS.md) report each row invocation and distinguish
controlled expansion REQUEST from actual uncontrolled CHANGE after legacy callbacks.
Collapse and header/footer actions remain separate slices; no generic TREEITEM accessibility activation support is implied.


[Attachment actions](ATTACHMENT_EVENTS.md) observe OPEN/REMOVE/RETRY at the
original category callback seams, with aggregate zero/one counts per category.
They report requested host actions, not completed deletion/upload work.

[Scrollable final-offset observers](SCROLL_EVENTS.md) pair Base reduction or Styled composition with one final notification after children. They preserve legacy input consumption and report aggregate offsets, including normalization, without inventing an input cause. VirtualList and MessageScroller retain their separate typed result contracts.

[HoverCard and Tooltip model observers](HOVER_EVENTS.md) distinguish the applied open-state transition from composition admission and actual visibility. Pure Base policy has no invented input evidence; Styled aggregation carries only a genuine frame. Pending timers and omitted components retain no handler.

# Component composition, state and interaction

CUI composes visible UI each frame between `cui_begin_frame` and `cui_end_frame`. The context retains focus, prior hit regions, resources and transient routing. Application-owned values and explicit models persist between frames. A persistent model is not a retained application widget tree. Model-only families require application composition; this guide does not claim complete upstream parity. See the [implementation manifest](gpui-parity.json) for per-family limitations.

This guide mirrors [component-usage.json](component-usage.json), the website metadata. “Immediate frame submission” means values/descriptors suffice; “application model + frame composition” highlights explicit persistent model, behavior or resource storage. Both use the same frame engine.

Keep stable IDs for the same logical controls. Retain borrowed strings, arrays, buffers and callback user data for the lifetime documented by each header, including through `cui_end_frame` when deferred layout/painting uses them. Model-bound arrays may need to survive until the next successful bind/rebuild; notification and host registrations outlive a submission. Never retain callback-borrowed URLs without copying. See [frames and callbacks](IMMEDIATE_AND_STATE.md) and [core lifecycle](CORE.md).

Component action/change callbacks run synchronously at the API's event-reduction point; model operations may also emit events. Speech recognizer/input callbacks may originate outside frame submission; queue reports and pump on the owning thread. User pointers must be valid for that call and for any longer registered-model lifetime. Rendering another frame alone must not replay application side effects. Content/render/paint/measure callbacks are for composition and may run during measurement; never put saving, network requests, deletion or other application actions in paint-only callbacks.

For example, inside an active frame, save only on activation:

```c
if (cui_button(ui, save_id, theme, cui_string("Save"), false))
    save_document(app);
if (cui_checkbox(ui, notify_id, theme, cui_string("Notifications"),
                 &app->notifications, false))
    persist_preferences(app);
```

The checkbox updates the application's bool. Controlled Switch/Toggle `on_change` receives the requested bool; accept by updating the authoritative value or reject by leaving it unchanged. See the complete [controlled callback example](IMMEDIATE_AND_STATE.md#use-a-controlled-callback). Initialize models once, retain them across frames, and destroy/dispose allocated models explicitly. External model changes should invalidate the context; honor animation deadlines and reduced motion.

## Accordion

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains bool expansion values and optional per-panel cui_disclosure_motion arrays.

**Interaction:** Returns whether expansion changed; cui_disclosure_panel_fn composes panel children and cui_disclosure_header_fn custom headers.

**Usage:** Submit stable item IDs and current expansion each frame; keep motion and style arrays alive through end_frame.

API: `cui_accordion`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_disclosure.h); [guide](DISCLOSURE.md).

Additional event includes: `cui/cui_disclosure_events.h`.

## AlertDialog

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains cui_surface_state and child form/application data.

**Interaction:** cui_surface_decision_fn may veto close; cui_surface_closed_fn observes close; take_result consumes the decision.

**Usage:** Initialize the appropriate surface kind, open from an action, and pair end only when begin succeeds. Consume result once.

API: `cui_surface_init`, `cui_alert_dialog`, `cui_surface_take_result`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_surface.h); [guide](SURFACES.md).

Additional event includes: `cui/cui_surface_events.h`.

## Alert

**Composition:** immediate frame submission. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller optionally retains a bool visible flag referenced by cui_alert_options.visible.

**Interaction:** Returns dismissal; writes supplied visibility.

**Usage:** Submit the current title/message and visibility; handle dismissal in the returned event branch.

API: `cui_alert`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_content.h); [guide](CONTENT.md).

Direct C `cui_alert_events` and `cui_alert_dismiss_fn` observe the completed built-in dismissal after the legacy visibility write. See [dismissal timing and ownership](ALERT_EVENTS.md).

## Attachment

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains cui_attachment_state and owns attachment model, metadata and resource lifetime.

**Interaction:** cui_attachment_result reports actions; cui_attachment_action_fn receives remove/retry activation.

**Usage:** Submit transfer status and progress; perform removal/retry in action callbacks, not render callbacks.

API: `cui_attachment`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_media.h); [guide](MEDIA.md).

Additional event includes: `cui/cui_media_events.h`.

## Avatar

**Composition:** immediate frame submission. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains name, borrowed RGBA pixels, bounded circular cache and destination storage through rendering. Optional typed placeholder state and mask versions also survive draw completion; named SVG uses the context cache. Metrics and palettes are copied values.

**Interaction:** Interactive avatars return activation; interactive stacks return the selected index or SIZE_MAX. Application opens the selected profile.

**Usage:** Initialize a circular image cache once; submit borrowed image pixels with a revision. Missing/invalid images fall back to initials; stacks use stable application keys. Opt into shared design sizes, deterministic identity palettes or anonymous SVG placeholders without changing legacy defaults.

API: `cui_avatar`, `cui_avatar_ex`, `cui_avatar_stack`, `cui_avatar_image_init`, `cui_avatar_image_prepare`, `cui_avatar_measure`, `cui_avatar_identity`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_content.h); [content guide](CONTENT.md); [profile images and conversations](AVATAR_MESSAGE_EXAMPLES.md); [Avatar styling from Python, JS/TS, Go and Rust](AVATAR_STYLE_BINDINGS.md). Direct C observers: `cui_avatar_events`, `cui_avatar_stack_events`; callbacks `cui_component_activation_fn`, `cui_avatar_stack_activation_fn`. See [activation guide](AVATAR_EVENTS.md).

## Badge

**Composition:** immediate frame submission. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller owns counts, badge options and child state; callbacks compose arbitrary child content synchronously.

**Interaction:** Child controls return their own actions; corner indicators provide nonfocusable status semantics.

**Usage:** Initialize options with cui_badge_defaults, select count/dot/icon and call cui_badge_ex with a content callback every frame.

API: `cui_badge_defaults`, `cui_badge_ex`, `cui_badge`. Callback: `cui_button_content_fn`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_components.h); [guide](BADGE.md), [guide](COMPONENTS.md).

## Bubble

**Composition:** immediate frame submission. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller owns child data; no separate bubble model.

**Interaction:** Child controls handle their own events.

**Usage:** Begin the surface, compose child controls, then end it in the same frame.

API: `cui_begin_bubble`, `cui_end_bubble`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_content.h); [guide](CONTENT.md).

## Button

**Composition:** immediate frame submission. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller owns application data; cui_button_options controls presentation.

**Interaction:** Returns true on activation; invoke the application action in that branch.

**Usage:** For Save, call save_document only when cui_button returns true. content is a composition callback, not an action handler.

API: `cui_button`, `cui_button_ex`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_components.h); [guide](BUTTON.md).

## Checkbox

**Composition:** immediate frame submission. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains bool or cui_check_state value; context owns focus.

**Interaction:** Returns true when the caller-owned value changes.

**Usage:** Pass the current value by pointer and persist preferences in the change branch.

API: `cui_checkbox`, `cui_checkbox_ex`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_components.h); [guide](CONTROLS.md).

## Clipboard

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** host adapter facility; no standalone styled clipboard widget.

**State:** Host retains backend and application owns clipboard buffers; cui_platform carries portable callbacks.

**Interaction:** Clipboard reads/writes are host interface calls, not a rendered widget action callback.

**Usage:** Obtain the host clipboard interface and supply it to editing/copy controls; compose a Copy button to trigger application copying.

API: `cui_sdl3_clipboard_interface`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_sdl3.h); [guide](INTERFACES.md).

## Collapsible

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains bool expansion values and optional per-panel cui_disclosure_motion arrays.

**Interaction:** Returns whether expansion changed; cui_disclosure_panel_fn composes panel children and cui_disclosure_header_fn custom headers.

**Usage:** Submit stable item IDs and current expansion each frame; keep motion and style arrays alive through end_frame.

API: `cui_collapsible`, `cui_collapsible_ex`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_disclosure.h); [guide](DISCLOSURE.md).

Additional event includes: `cui/cui_disclosure_events.h`.

## DropdownButton

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**Usage:** Initialize line storage once and submit the multiline editor each frame.

API: `cui_textarea`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_textarea.h); [guide](TEXTAREA.md).

Additional event includes: `cui/cui_multiline_events.h`.

## TimeField

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains cui_time_state and cui_time value.

**Interaction:** Returns true when the time value changes.

**Usage:** Submit segment state and time by pointer; persist accepted time in the change branch.

API: `cui_time_field`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_picker.h); [guide](PICKERS.md).

Additional event includes: `cui/cui_picker_events.h`.

## Carousel

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains state, geometry workspace and slide data.

**Interaction:** cui_carousel_change_fn observes selection; cui_carousel_render_fn composes slides.

**Usage:** Initialize capacity once, submit slides each frame and handle selected-index changes separately from slide rendering.

API: `cui_carousel_state_init`, `cui_carousel`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_carousel.h); [guide](CAROUSEL.md).

## DescriptionList

**Composition:** immediate frame submission. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller owns item descriptors/content; no separate list model.

**Interaction:** cui_description_render_fn composes custom values; child controls provide actions.

**Usage:** Submit label/value descriptors each frame; respect the resolved layout width in custom content.

API: `cui_description_list`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_description.h); [guide](DESCRIPTION_LIST.md).

## Dialog

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains cui_surface_state and child form/application data.

**Interaction:** cui_surface_decision_fn may veto close; cui_surface_closed_fn observes close; take_result consumes the decision.

**Usage:** Initialize the appropriate surface kind, open from an action, and pair end only when begin succeeds. Consume result once.

API: `cui_surface_init`, `cui_surface_begin`, `cui_surface_end`, `cui_surface_take_result`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_surface.h); [guide](SURFACES.md).

Additional event includes: `cui/cui_surface_events.h`.

## Dock

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame adapter + retained base model.

**State:** Application retains cui_dock, cui_dock_view and the panel registry; keep callback data alive through renderer completion.

**Interaction:** Panel render callbacks compose active content; on_event reports select, close, reorder, move, split and resize; allow_operation may veto structural actions.

**Usage:** Create the model and view once, register stable panel keys, submit cui_dock_view_render each frame and serialize the model between frames.

API: `cui_dock_view_create`, `cui_dock_view_render`, `cui_dock_view_destroy`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_dock.h); [guide](DOCK.md), [guide](DOCK_MODEL.md).

## List

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains cui_list_state, selected cui_id and item array.

**Interaction:** Returns changes; cui_choice_activation_fn / cui_choice_confirm_fn / cui_choice_cancel_fn handle list interaction.

**Usage:** Keep keys stable; submit current items and selection, then handle activation/confirmation callbacks synchronously.

API: `cui_list`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_choice.h); [guide](CHOICE.md).

Additional event includes: `cui/cui_list_events.h`.

## Menu

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains menu entries and popup/menu-tree state.

**Interaction:** Returns activation and writes the activated cui_id through the action pointer; check/radio entries update caller values. cui_menu_render_fn composes custom content.

**Usage:** Initialize menu-tree state once and submit stable entry IDs each frame; invoke application actions from the returned activation and action key.

API: `cui_menu_tree`, `cui_menu`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_choice.h); [guide](CHOICE.md).

## Popover

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains cui_surface_state and child form/application data.

**Interaction:** cui_surface_decision_fn may veto close; cui_surface_closed_fn observes close; take_result consumes the decision.

**Usage:** Initialize the appropriate surface kind, open from an action, and pair end only when begin succeeds. Consume result once. Use cui_popover_begin for explicit anchor/offset/arrow positioning, paired with surface_end; legacy surface_begin keeps its original placement. Arrow rendering requires a mesh-capable adapter; SDL3 and browser adapters support bounded analytic meshes with documented limits. The gallery starts in legacy mode; explicitly select source anchors to explore all eight popup anchors, signed custom gap, arrow toggle, app/host reference rem and edge clamping. Open the card before the inert/modal demonstrations. The copyable complete C11 snippet follows the current mode.

API: `cui_surface_init`, `cui_surface_begin`, `cui_surface_end`, `cui_surface_take_result`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_surface.h); [guide](SURFACES.md).

Additional event includes: `cui/cui_surface_events.h`.

## Resizable

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains state, slots and panel descriptors.

**Interaction:** cui_resizable_resize_fn observes size changes; panel content composes controls.

**Usage:** Initialize slot storage, submit panel descriptors each frame and save sizes after resize events.

API: `cui_resizable_state_init`, `cui_resizable`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_resizable.h); [guide](RESIZABLE.md).

## Root View

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains cui_root, plugin instance storage, registry and bound surface/notification storage.

**Interaction:** cui_root_content_fn composes application content; cui_root_copy_fn handles copy; plugins have explicit lifecycle hooks.

**Usage:** Initialize root/plugin storage, render content and facilities each frame, then dispose after use.

API: `cui_root_init`, `cui_root_render`, `cui_root_dispose`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_root.h); [guide](ROOT.md).

## Scrollable

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains cui_scroll_state offsets and supplies content/viewport dimensions.

**Interaction:** Legacy begin/end reduce scroll input. Optional paired observers report one applied final offset after children and finish; normalization is not evidence of user input.

**Usage:** Preserve caller offsets. Base observer begin may return false for a valid no-change pair and must still be finished. Styled observer begin returns admission: end only after true. Handlers are borrowed by finish/end; do not mix pairing layers.

API: `cui_scrollable_begin`, `cui_scrollable_end_ex`, `cui_base_scrollable_events`, `cui_base_scrollable_finish_events`, `cui_scrollable_begin_events`, `cui_scrollable_end_events`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_scroll.h); [event header](../include/cui/cui_scroll_events.h); [guide](SCROLL.md); [event guide](SCROLL_EVENTS.md).

## Settings

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains page state/workspace, descriptors and actual setting values.

**Interaction:** cui_setting_render_fn composes controls; cui_setting_dirty_fn and cui_setting_reset_fn implement application dirty/reset behavior.

**Usage:** Initialize page/query storage; submit descriptors and implement each setting through its render/dirty/reset functions.

API: `cui_settings_state_init`, `cui_settings`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_settings.h); [guide](SETTINGS.md).

Additional event includes: `cui/cui_settings_events.h`.

## Sheet

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains cui_surface_state and child form/application data.

**Interaction:** cui_surface_decision_fn may veto close; cui_surface_closed_fn observes close; take_result consumes the decision.

**Usage:** Initialize the appropriate surface kind, open from an action, and pair end only when begin succeeds. Consume result once.

API: `cui_surface_init`, `cui_surface_begin`, `cui_surface_end`, `cui_surface_take_result`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_surface.h); [guide](SURFACES.md).

Additional event includes: `cui/cui_surface_events.h`.

## Sidebar

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains sidebar state/cache, entry descriptors and selected application route.

**Interaction:** cui_sidebar_content_fn composes regions; menu-item results expose selection/activation.

**Usage:** Initialize measurement cache, submit current entries, and update routing from menu-item events.

API: `cui_sidebar_state_init`, `cui_sidebar`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_sidebar.h); [guide](SIDEBAR.md).

## StatusBar

**Composition:** immediate frame submission. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller owns left/center/right descriptors and displayed data.

**Interaction:** cui_chrome_render_fn composes regions; child controls handle actions.

**Usage:** Submit region content each frame; preserve application data outside the bar.

API: `cui_status_bar`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_chrome.h); [guide](CHROME.md).

## Tabs

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains selected cui_id, item array and optional motion/scroll state.

**Interaction:** Returns selection changes; cui_tab_panel_fn composes selected panel content.

**Usage:** Submit tab descriptors and current selected key; keep optional animation state across frames.

API: `cui_tabs`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_choice.h); [guide](CHOICE.md).

Event API includes: `cui/cui_tabs_events.h`.

## Theme

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** application style data; passed during frame submission.

**State:** Caller retains cui_theme value and any icon-loader user/backing storage.

**Interaction:** cui_theme_icon_loader_fn resolves icon SVG; theme selection is an application event.

**Usage:** Choose/copy a preset and pass its address to styled controls; invalidate after changing it.

API: `cui_theme_light`, `cui_theme_preset_get`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_theme.h); [guide](THEME_GUIDE.md).

## TitleBar

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains cui_title_bar_state and window interface binding.

**Interaction:** on_close callback handles application close; window host functions implement native window behavior.

**Usage:** Submit current window information each frame; keep host/user pointers valid during calls.

API: `cui_title_bar`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_chrome.h); [guide](CHROME.md).

## Toolbar

**Composition:** immediate frame submission. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller owns item/command descriptors and command user data.

**Interaction:** cui_toolbar_render_fn composes items; cui_toolbar_command.on_activate handles command activation.

**Usage:** Submit command descriptors each frame and perform application actions in on_activate.

API: `cui_toolbar`, `cui_toolbar_command_render`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_toolbar.h); [guide](TOOLBAR.md).

Additional event includes: `cui/cui_toolbar_events.h`.

## Tree

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains model/state, selected cui_id and borrowed node/expansion arrays until next successful rebuild.

**Interaction:** cui_tree_result separates selection_changed, expansion_changed and activated key.

**Usage:** Rebuild preorder data when it changes; submit visible rows each frame and open the activated application item from the result.

API: `cui_tree_create`, `cui_tree_rebuild`, `cui_tree`, `cui_tree_destroy`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_tree.h); [guide](TREE.md).

Event API includes: `cui/cui_tree_events.h`.

## VirtualList

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame adapter + retained base model.

**State:** Application retains cui_virtual_list and cui_virtual_widget_state; keyed extents live in the model and row controls remain application-owned.

**Interaction:** cui_virtual_render_item_fn composes the visible window; cui_virtual_measure_item_fn supplies intrinsic measurement; optional cui_scroll_handler observes aggregate final offsets after composition, with UNKNOWN source.

**Usage:** Rebuild keyed extents between frames and keep keys stable during row callbacks. Use cui_virtual_list_draw_events for final-offset observation; inspect changed separately from delivered change_count and the unchanged deferred control_result.

API: `cui_virtual_list_draw`, `cui_base_virtual_list`, `cui_virtual_list_draw_events`, `cui_base_virtual_list_events`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_virtual_scroll.h); [guide](VIRTUAL_LIST.md), [guide](VIRTUALIZATION.md), [guide](VIRTUAL_EVENTS.md).

Additional event includes: `cui/cui_virtual_events.h`.

## Chart

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains cui_chart_state, its RGBA pixel buffer/byte capacity, data arrays and resources used by options.

**Interaction:** Hit testing identifies data; tooltip/format/paint callbacks customize output and are not application action callbacks.

**Usage:** Submit data/options each frame; route application actions from explicit hit testing or child controls.

API: `cui_chart`, `cui_chart_hit_test`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_chart.h); [guide](CHART.md).

The gallery custom tooltip toggle uses `cui_chart_tooltip_build_fn` with copied row strings. See [the callback example](CHART_TYPED_TOOLTIP.md), [point-axis layout](CHART_SOURCE_POINT_AXIS.md), [Radar title policy](CHART_RADAR_TOOLTIP_TITLE.md) and [current-frame painting](PLOT_CHART_CURRENT_FRAME.md).

## Command

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains command state, row workspace, cui_edit query and command descriptors.

**Interaction:** on_select/on_query/on_confirm/on_cancel observe synchronous interaction; command item action invokes application work.

**Usage:** Initialize bounded query/row storage, submit entries each frame, and execute actions only from confirmation/action events.

API: `cui_command_init`, `cui_command`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_command.h); [guide](COMMAND.md).

Event API includes: `cui/cui_command_events.h`.

## DataTable

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains allocated model/state, data rows/columns and any borrowed label storage.

**Interaction:** cui_table_result reports interaction; cui_table_label_fn provides accessibility text and cui_table_cell_fn composes visible cells.

**Usage:** Bind data when changed, submit virtual cells each frame, and handle selection/sort actions from the result.

API: `cui_table_create`, `cui_data_table`, `cui_table_destroy`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_table.h); [guide](TABLE.md).

Additional event includes: `cui/cui_table_events.h`.

## Plot

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame adapter + standalone numeric model; bounded software rasterizer.

**State:** Caller retains scales, samples, path commands, RGBA pixels, tick labels and callback state; no retained widget tree.

**Interaction:** cui_plot_activate_fn receives validated pointer positions; pure numeric operations return cui_plot_result and the application routes pan/zoom.

**Usage:** Build paths and render into caller-owned pixels, then submit a themed bitmap and axes each frame; keep labels and pixels alive through renderer completion.

API: `cui_plot_view`, `cui_plot_axis`, `cui_plot_raster`, `cui_plot_path`, `cui_plot_map`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_plot_view.h); [guide](PLOT.md); [numeric model](PLOT_MODEL.md).

## Table

**Composition:** immediate frame submission. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller owns row/cell hierarchy and data; no retained table model is required.

**Interaction:** Composition only; child controls handle actions.

**Usage:** Submit sections, rows and cells using balanced begin/end nesting each frame.

API: `cui_table_begin`, `cui_table_begin_row`, `cui_table_begin_cell`, `cui_table_end`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_table.h); [guide](TABLE.md).

## TextView

**Composition:** application model + frame composition. **Scope:** styled frame component.

**State:** Caller retains state and all source/rendered/layout workspace buffers.

**Interaction:** on_link/open_url handle link interaction; image resolves resources; other content/measurement hooks compose or paint.

**Usage:** Initialize bounded workspace, set text on changes, then submit each frame. Decoded link URLs are borrowed only during callbacks: copy for deferred use.

API: `cui_text_view_init`, `cui_text_view_set_text`, `cui_text_view`. [Public header](../include/cui/cui_text_view.h); [guide](TEXT_VIEW.md).
documents.docs/COMPOSED_APPS.md:
# Northstar: a composed native CUI application

Northstar is a complete, editable workspace demo assembled from real CUI
controls. Its overview, pricing and settings pages share a responsive navigation
shell and an account menu. It demonstrates application composition rather than
individual controls in isolation.

![Northstar desktop overview](../examples/composed_apps/screenshots/overview-desktop.png)

## Build and run

From the repository root:

```sh
cmake -S examples/composed_apps -B examples/composed_apps/build -G Ninja
cmake --build examples/composed_apps/build
ctest --test-dir examples/composed_apps/build --output-on-failure
```

The standalone project includes the checkout's CUI library, native adapters and
full repository test suite, then builds the `northstar` host and the additional
`composed_app_interactions` test. C11 sources compile with the repository's
warnings-as-errors settings. Requirements are CMake 3.20+, Ninja and a C/C++
compiler; the existing optional adapters use installed SDL3 3.2+, FreeType and
HarfBuzz. No new dependencies or downloads are introduced. The repository's
pinned optional SDL3 fetch remains available via `-DCUI_FETCH_SDL=ON`.

Choose an existing font file and launch the native application:

```sh
FONT=/usr/share/fonts/noto/NotoSans-Regular.ttf
examples/composed_apps/build/northstar --font "$FONT"
examples/composed_apps/build/northstar --font "$FONT" --page pricing
examples/composed_apps/build/northstar --font "$FONT" --page settings --width 390 --height 844
```

The font shown above was available on the Linux validation machine. Substitute
a real TrueType/OpenType file on your system. Native mode returns an error if
the adapter or font is unavailable; it does not silently become a headless demo.

For the portable core without native dependencies:

```sh
cmake -S examples/composed_apps -B examples/composed_apps/build-headless -G Ninja -DCUI_BUILD_NATIVE=OFF
cmake --build examples/composed_apps/build-headless --target northstar test_composed_app
examples/composed_apps/build-headless/test_composed_app
examples/composed_apps/build-headless/northstar --headless --page overview
examples/composed_apps/build-headless/northstar --headless --page pricing --width 390 --height 844
```

Headless mode builds actual CUI layout/render commands. The separate interaction
test drives actual pointer, keyboard, text and scroll events and asserts
application state. Headless execution does not open or validate a native window.

## What works

- **Navigation:** a real CUI sidebar menu switches Overview, Plans & billing and
  Settings. The hamburger hides/restores the desktop sidebar. Below 760 logical
  pixels, navigation starts hidden and the hamburger reveals it below the header;
  selecting a page closes it. It is an inline panel, not an overlay drawer.
- **Account:** the real account popup offers workspace settings and a local demo
  sign-in/sign-out command. Its desktop label reflects the saved display name; narrow layouts use a compact Account label. Popup
  dismissal and keyboard navigation come from CUI.
- **Overview:** a hero CTA opens pricing, metric cards stack on narrow content,
  and Personalize workspace opens settings. Metrics are explicitly sample data.
- **Pricing:** three cards show Starter, Team and Studio. Selecting a plan changes
  state, updates the selected CTA, displays confirmation and dispatches a callback.
  Re-selecting the current plan does not dispatch another change. Cards stack
  when content width is below 720 logical pixels.
- **Settings:** a CUI form associates the required name with a real text editor;
  checkbox and switch retain preferences. Save rejects an empty or ASCII
  whitespace-only name, stores the accepted name in session state and dispatches
  a save callback. Invalid saves leave the previous saved name intact.
- **Scrolling:** CUI scrollable content keeps stacked cards and forms reachable.
  Tracks hide when the authored page extent fits the current viewport.

![Northstar desktop pricing](../examples/composed_apps/screenshots/pricing-desktop.png)

## Copy the scene into your own host

The [scene header](../examples/composed_apps/app.h) contains only public CUI and
standard C types. SDL and font adapters live in [main.c](../examples/composed_apps/main.c).
[app.c](../examples/composed_apps/app.c) owns the application state and composition:

```c
#include "app.h"

static void changed(void *user, app_event event, app_snapshot state) {
    (void)user;
    if (event == APP_PLAN_CHANGED) {
        /* Dispatch your application's plan workflow using state.plan. */
    }
    if (event == APP_SETTINGS_SAVED) {
        /* Persist state.saved_name, state.notifications and state.sync. */
    }
}

composed_app *app = composed_app_create(changed, NULL);
/* Check app and your cui_context allocation before continuing. */
cui_begin_frame(ui, width, height, dt);
composed_app_scene(ui, app, width, height);
cui_draw_list commands = cui_end_frame(ui);
/* Render commands now, before another frame or app destruction. */
```

`composed_app_frame` combines begin, scene submission and end for a standalone
host. Use `composed_app_scene` when embedding into your own frame or gallery.
It builds a full-window shell using the width/height supplied by the host;
provide a context viewport matching that shell. Stable `APP_*` control IDs in
the header support testing and automation. Use one instance per context: the
IDs are intentionally fixed rather than namespaced for multiple side-by-side
instances in the same context.

Callbacks run synchronously during control submission on the UI thread. They
receive a read-only snapshot; its strings borrow application storage and can
change on the next interaction. Copy strings before retaining them. Do not
recursively submit a frame or destroy the app/context from a callback. Destroy
the app with `composed_app_destroy` after the renderer has consumed its last
draw list. The host owns CUI context, font and backend destruction separately.

To follow a host application's selected theme, copy its theme into the scene
before submitting the frame:

```c
cui_theme selected = cui_theme_dark();
composed_app_set_theme(app, &selected);
/* selected may now go out of scope: color/metric values were copied. */
composed_app_scene(ui, app, width, height);
```

Call the setter between frames on the UI thread. Calling it every frame is
supported; it preserves the selected plan, editor/preferences, session and
keyboard focus. `composed_app_set_theme(app, NULL)` restores Northstar's default
native palette. Pointer-valued icon hooks and their user storage remain owned by
the host and must retain the lifetimes required by CUI; copying the theme does
not copy data behind those pointers.

Cards and the header use `theme.surface`, the document uses `theme.background`,
and scene ink, borders and controls follow the supplied theme. The hero and
feedback panels derive subtle tints from its palette. The navy navigation rail
intentionally keeps its own readable light ink across themes. Light, dark,
high-contrast and terminal themes run through the complete interaction test;
representative header/hero/card ink contrast, keyboard focus paint, copied-theme
storage and live theme switching are also checked. These are targeted checks,
not a claim of a comprehensive accessibility audit.

![Northstar with a dark host theme](../examples/composed_apps/screenshots/overview-dark.png)

To restyle the demo further, edit the `sidebar` composition and page render
functions. To connect it to production data, replace the sample metrics and
implement authentication, billing and persistence in your application layer.
The sample callback is the integration boundary.

## Native captures and interaction validation

Linux/X11 native captures were inspected for all three pages at 1200×900 and
390×844. The screenshots in this folder were produced by the actual SDL3 host,
not a browser recreation. A bounded native capture is reproducible:

```sh
FONT=/usr/share/fonts/noto/NotoSans-Regular.ttf
TMPDIR=/your/writable/cache timeout 15 xvfb-run -a -s '-screen 0 1600x1200x24' \
  examples/composed_apps/build/northstar --font "$FONT" --page pricing \
  --frames 3 --capture examples/composed_apps/build/pricing.bmp
```

Set `TMPDIR` to an existing writable directory when `/tmp` space is constrained.
Omit `TMPDIR=...` when your default temporary directory has sufficient space.
Capture requires a positive `--frames` count and a native backend. It writes the
last bounded frame to BMP; zero frames runs interactively until window close.

The native interaction check uses xdotool to choose Team, sign in through the
account menu, navigate to Settings, type Grace Hopper, change both preferences,
save and sign out. It asserts the resulting callback log and saves the final
native frame:

```sh
TMPDIR=/your/writable/cache timeout 20 xvfb-run -a -s '-screen 0 1600x1200x24' \
  examples/composed_apps/native-check.sh "$FONT"
```

The explicit Xvfb screen size matters: the default 1024×768 display would clamp
pointer coordinates for a 1200×900 application window. The check rejects a
display smaller than the window. Its fixed coordinates are specific to this
scene and the validated font; adapt them if changing layout/font metrics.
Artifacts appear in `build/native-interactions.log` and
`build/native-interactions.bmp`.

![Native settings after editing and saving](../examples/composed_apps/screenshots/settings-saved-desktop.png)

### Scrolling in an embedding or browser host

Narrow pricing cards stack vertically. Team (`APP_PLAN_TEAM`, 131) and Studio
(132) may start below the viewport; this is expected. CUI retains their raw
semantic bounds, but hit geometry is clipped to the document viewport. A host
that exports only visible controls may omit those IDs until you scroll. Do not
click stale offscreen centers or assume all three CTAs are immediately visible.

Route scroll input to a point inside `APP_CONTENT` (150), rather than the header,
sidebar or an open account menu. For a pixel-based host such as DOM wheel input:

```c
cui_rect content = cui_bounds(ui, APP_CONTENT);
cui_queue_event(ui, (cui_event){
    .type = CUI_EVENT_SCROLL,
    .x = content.x + content.w / 2,
    .y = content.y + content.h / 2,
    .dy = -192,              /* Negative moves the document downward. */
    .scroll_precise = true /* Logical pixels, not wheel ticks. */
});
composed_app_frame(ui, app, width, height);
/* Re-read current bounds/visible semantics; repeat until the CTA is visible. */
```

For DOM `deltaMode == DOM_DELTA_PIXEL`, map positive `deltaY` to negative CUI
`dy` and account for CSS-to-logical-pixel scaling in coordinates/deltas. With
`scroll_precise == false`, deltas are wheel units: `dy = -1` moves this scene
48 logical pixels downward. Feeding pixel deltas as nonprecise units multiplies
them by 48 and usually jumps straight to the end. Re-read bounds after rendering
the scrolled frame before dispatching pointer down/up.

The real vertical scrollbar is `cui_scrollbar_id(APP_CONTENT, true)` from
`cui/cui_scroll.h`. It exposes current value/minimum/maximum in its semantic
record, supports pointer dragging, and supports Home/End/PageUp/PageDown when
focused. Its End key reveals the last Studio CTA. Tests exercise precise wheel
reveal/click of Team, scrollbar-keyboard reveal/click of Studio, reverse pixel
scroll and exact wheel-unit movement for all four themes at both 390×844 and
360×420. No scene-specific browser scrolling API is required.

### Reproduce native host-theme validation

The optional native audit driver lives in `test_app.c` behind
`APP_THEME_NATIVE`; ordinary CTest stays portable. Build it explicitly after the
native example build above:

```sh
EXAMPLES=examples/composed_apps
cc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -DAPP_THEME_NATIVE \
  -Iinclude -I"$EXAMPLES" "$EXAMPLES/app.c" "$EXAMPLES/test_app.c" \
  "$EXAMPLES/build/cui-build/libcui_sdl3.a" \
  "$EXAMPLES/build/cui-build/libcui_text.a" "$EXAMPLES/build/cui-build/libcui.a" \
  $(pkg-config --cflags --libs sdl3 freetype2 harfbuzz) -lm \
  -o "$EXAMPLES/build/test_theme_native"
```

The driver accepts `--native FONT light|dark|contrast|terminal OUTPUT_DIRECTORY`.
It runs a bounded 1200-frame window that closes after the verified workflow
settles, captures each visited page and its final
frame, prints measured control centers for automation, and returns success only
if the native interactions produced Team selection, sign-in/out and one saved
Grace Hopper profile with notifications off and sync on. The following helper
uses the measured centers rather than fixed per-theme coordinates:

```sh
cat > "$EXAMPLES/build/theme-check.sh" <<'SH'
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
font=$1
theme=$2
example_dir=$(pwd)/examples/composed_apps
"$example_dir/build/test_theme_native" --native "$font" "$theme" "$example_dir/build" \
  >"$example_dir/build/$theme-theme.log" 2>&1 &
client=$!
sleep 0.8
window=$(xdotool search --name '^Northstar / theme audit$')
xdotool windowfocus "$window"
click() {
  line=$(rg "^bound id=$1 " "$example_dir/build/$theme-theme.log" | tail -1)
  x=$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | awk '{sub("x=","",$3); print $3}')
  y=$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | awk '{sub("y=","",$4); print $4}')
  xdotool mousemove --window "$window" "$x" "$y" click 1
  sleep 0.6
}
click 120 # Overview CTA opens pricing.
click 131 # Choose Team.
click 101
xdotool key --window "$window" End Return # Sign in.
sleep 0.6
click 112 # Settings navigation.
click 140
xdotool key --window "$window" ctrl+a
xdotool type --window "$window" --clearmodifiers --delay 5 'Grace Hopper'
sleep 0.6
click 141
click 142
click 143
click 101
xdotool key --window "$window" End Return # Sign out.
wait "$client"
rg '^native event=' "$example_dir/build/$theme-theme.log"
SH
for theme in light dark contrast terminal; do
  timeout 30 xvfb-run -a -s '-screen 0 1600x1200x24' \
    sh "$EXAMPLES/build/theme-check.sh" "$FONT" "$theme" || break
done
```

Run from the repository root and set `TMPDIR` if needed as described above.
The helper assumes the validated font and Linux tools. It waits briefly for
window creation and bounded frame progress; slower machines may need longer
waits/timeouts. Each theme writes `<theme>-overview.bmp`, `<theme>-pricing.bmp`,
`<theme>-settings.bmp`, `<theme>-settings-saved.bmp` and `<theme>-theme.log` in the
build directory. Actual native workflows passed for all four themes; committed
light/dark PNGs show the captured SDL frames.

## Scope and limits

The scene's state is local and in memory. Demo sign-in does not authenticate,
plan selection creates no subscription or payment, and save does not write a
file or server. Notification/sync toggles record preferences without performing
those services. Closing the app resets its state. Prices and activity metrics
are illustrative, not an external product offer or telemetry feed.

Native operation and actual interaction were validated on Linux with SDL3
3.4.18, FreeType/HarfBuzz and Noto Sans under Xvfb. Physical displays, Wayland,
Windows and macOS have not been validated by this example. It uses CUI controls
painted into an SDL desktop window, not operating-system-native widgets.
Regular font shaping works; additional bold/italic font faces can be registered
by an embedding host for stronger typography. No claim of complete component
or platform parity is implied.

Page scroll extents are explicit scene estimates, chosen for this sample's
content and responsive breakpoints. Update those estimates alongside page
content or font changes; they are not an automatic document measurement system.
Name validation only rejects empty/ASCII-whitespace-only names and the editor
limits storage to 79 UTF-8 bytes; it is not a full identity validation policy.
