# Content components

`cui_content.h` adds controlled alert dismissal; named avatar initials; composable bubble and group surfaces; empty states; keyboard hints; loading indicators; dividers; and a shared delayed hover lifecycle. These portable C11 APIs use the existing theme and draw list. They do not imply complete GPUI Kit family parity.

Alerts carry text naming their severity, an optional title, custom textual icon, banner style, width, and size multiplier. A dismiss button reports activation and updates optional application-owned visibility. Passing false visibility omits the entire subtree next frame. Success and warning currently use the theme primary color with distinct text because the theme has no separate success/warning tokens. Rich content can instead be composed with boxes; the convenience alert renders plain text.

Avatar fallback takes the first scalar of the first and last ASCII-whitespace-separated words, uppercases ASCII letters, and preserves valid non-ASCII UTF-8. Empty/invalid input produces `?`. Its semantic name retains the person's name. The circular surface has an explicit pixel size. Image loading, generated hue palettes, exact typographic centering, custom icons, and overlapping groups remain pending.

Bubble and GroupBox begin/end pairs accept arbitrary child controls or text. Bubble offers filled, secondary, muted, tinted, outline, ghost, and destructive surfaces. The caller supplies child text colors and owns horizontal placement, maximum width, wrapping, reactions, and footer content. Empty provides title and description; a custom actionable empty state can use a GroupBox instead. Empty custom-image/icon slots and GPUI's exact typography remain pending.

Keyboard formatting takes modifier bits, the display key label, and an explicit platform convention. It supports Ctrl/Alt/Shift/Win labels and macOS symbols in stable order, reports required bytes, and bounds/NUL-terminates the output. The caller supplies special-key labels; action/keybinding lookup is application-owned. `cui_kbd` styles any resulting string.

The legacy `cui_spinner` is an eight-dot phase ring with Loading status semantics and moving-frame invalidation. Use `cui_spinner_ex` for the source-style decorative Loader SVG, custom color/icon/easing/size and caller-owned bounded wake scheduling; see [Spinner](SPINNER.md). Skeleton supports arbitrary size, radius, a secondary opacity, and a legacy cosine pulse; `cui_skeleton_ex` adds source-style caller-clocked motion. Reduced motion freezes both APIs. Divider accepts horizontal/vertical orientation and length.

`cui_hover_update` is the reusable Tooltip/HoverCard timing reducer. Trigger hover and keyboard focus open after a configured delay. Once open, hovering content keeps it open; leaving starts a cancellable close delay. Escape or disabled closes immediately. Invalid time steps do not advance timers. `cui_tooltip` and the composable HoverCard begin/end pair now render viewport portals above their clipping ancestors. They observe previous-frame clipped trigger/card regions, support keyboard-focus opening, and flip/clamp popup placement to the provided viewport. Escape suppresses reopening until hover and focus leave the trigger. Cards keep open while their contents are hovered or a child retains focus; tooltips never own a focus stop. Trigger descriptions preserve existing semantic details. Applications supply viewport and popup dimensions and frame time; text/layout is clipped to those bounds. Automatic text sizing/wrapping, tooltip animation, collision avoidance among unrelated overlays, native accessibility announcements, and all upstream appearance options remain pending. HoverCard is nonmodal and does not trap or take keyboard focus.

Headless tests verify UTF-8 validation, formatting truncation, lifecycle transitions, reduced motion and animated redraw, measured geometry, named semantic snapshots, controlled pointer dismissal, actual portal clipping escape, edge flipping, keyboard opening, hover-card retention, Escape suppression, trigger-description preservation, and omission of dismissed content across all four themes. The worker compiles the new files with C11 strict warnings, runs `test_content` linked to the core library, and runs the existing CTest suite. Build/distribution registration belongs to the integrator.

Avatar initials in `cui_avatar_ex` support independent `custom_background` and
`custom_foreground` flags with `background` and `foreground` colors. Zero options
retain the theme primary/on-primary defaults; explicit colors apply only when the
image is missing or invalid, including transparent colors. Photo ring colors
continue to use `custom_ring`/`ring`.

## Explicit HoverCard tap mode and relationships

[HoverCard extended policy](HOVER_CARD_EXTENDED.md) adds caller-accepted trigger toggles, a bounded outside-tap workspace and optional current-trigger controls/expanded snapshots. The legacy hover helper is unchanged. Strict outside taps differ from arbitrary mouse-up-out; collapsed native accessibility state and foreign wrappers remain separate work.

Typed single-stroke hints and ordinary grouped composition are documented in [Keyboard shortcut hints](KBD.md). For decorative Skeletons with an application-owned busy region and completion status, see the [loading-region example](../examples/loading_region/README.md). These examples distinguish Core/DOM/native event evidence from unverified screen-reader speech.

# Contextual native text

Core text commands retain the original paragraph and a half-open UTF-8 byte
range for the selected visual line. Native software, SDL3, SDL GPU and Sokol
renderers use that context for bidi analysis. A wrapped line beginning with
numbers or punctuation therefore keeps the direction of its original paragraph.
This change preserves Clay's existing wrap choices; it does not implement UAX14
line breaking or visual arrow navigation.

## Portable interfaces

`cui_text_line_source` contains `paragraph`, `byte_start` and `byte_end`.
Endpoints are paragraph-relative UTF-8 scalar boundaries. Hard paragraph
separators are excluded. U+2028 remains inside the paragraph: native drawing
splits its physical lines while retaining the shared bidi context. A geometry
factory request selects one physical line and cannot include U+2028 in its range.

`cui_text_context_line` copies a paragraph and submits a selected line.
`cui_text_context_line_colored` additionally copies sorted, nonoverlapping color
spans, also in paragraph-relative bytes. Colored submission selects one physical
line and rejects a range containing U+2028. There are at most
`CUI_TEXT_COLOR_SPAN_MAX` (4096) spans. A shaped cluster takes the color at its
first original byte; a color boundary inside a ligature or combining cluster
does not split shaping. Both submission functions return false on invalid input
or capacity failure. Capacity reports `CUI_ERROR_CAPACITY`; failure does not
consume frame bytes or submit an element.

Ordinary `cui_text` wrapping also retains provenance. Core records submissions
in an array bounded by `max_elements`, resolves Clay's exact `baseChars` pointers,
and copies text into `frame_bytes`. It does not search for matching substrings.
Contextual lines share paragraph storage but have unique slice storage, so
repeated text and equal-start/different-end ranges remain distinct. CRLF suffixes
retained by Clay are removed from the visible line without changing the original
paragraph boundaries. Draw descriptors and color spans have the same lifetime
as the draw list: consume them before the next frame or context destruction.
Any renderer retaining commands must deep-copy their paragraphs and spans.

## Native host setup

Add the range factory to a native font configuration:

```c
cui_config config = {
    .measure_user = font,
    .measure = cui_font_measure,
    .measure_styled = cui_font_measure_styled,
    .font_metrics = cui_font_get_metrics,
    .text_geometry = cui_font_text_geometry,
    .text_geometry_line = cui_font_text_geometry_line,
};
```

A measurement wrapper needs matching geometry wrappers sharing `measure_user`.
`cui_get_text_geometry_line` preserves output on failure, checks the session
metadata, and releases a partial failed session. Successful sessions are owned
and immutable; release them once with `cui_release_text_geometry`. `byte_length`
is the full paragraph length. Caret, hit and selection offsets are original
paragraph-relative bytes, including when the selected line starts later.
The native adapter translates validated byte endpoints to the existing scalar
line-layout API. It retains shaped arrays and font faces, not the source buffer.

The old factory contract is unchanged. When a range selects the entire
paragraph, the helper can use the old `text_geometry` factory. Other ranges
require `text_geometry_line`; unavailable geometry uses the legacy measured
editing path. BIDI-off native factories return UNAVAILABLE. Ordinary contextual
drawing retains legacy BIDI-off drawing; colored contextual drawing requires
the optional native bidi implementation. Editor selects its established
fragment path when visual geometry is unavailable. Browser renderers do not
consume these native contextual/color descriptors in this batch.

## Multiline consumers and ownership

Textarea row records include original paragraph boundaries and hard-line
indices. Textarea and Editor share visual geometry for hits, caret x, preferred
vertical columns, reveal, selection spans and composition underlines. Primary
pointer-selected bidi affinity survives idle frames. The final IME rectangle
comes from the actual painted caret child's bounds after layout, including when
its blink is invisible. Logical editing offsets and keyboard motion keep their
existing policies; secondary Editor cursors do not gain persistent dual bidi
affinity or visual navigation.

One context resource caches at most 64 requested line sessions and 1 MiB of
unique paragraph bytes per frame. Visible rows and requested navigation rows
are created lazily; identical paragraph/range/style requests share a session.
Queries outside a frame use a temporary owned session. Beginning a new frame
releases cached sessions/source copies, observing host font registrations and
metrics changes. Source changes within a frame create a new immutable session.
Capacity, allocation, unavailable and unsupported-boundary failures retain the
measured fallback. Styled `cui_textarea_result.visual_error` reports the first
visible-line factory failure separately from edit/layout errors.

For a configured visual host, an active composition also retains one exact
preedit snapshot per state in a context resource, bounded to 65,535 bytes.
Unchanged composition reuses row layout across idle frames. Its resource owns
and frees the snapshot; caller state receives no allocation handle or cleanup
duty. Omitted resources and context destruction clean up ownership. Model
identity is compared without dereferencing a previous model. Rebinding to a
different model invalidates cached rows. Reinitialize state before destroying
and replacing a model at the same address; Editor's borrowed model must outlive
its state. Caller row arrays must remain alive and must not be shared by widgets.

Editor shapes each highlighted contextual line once, then supplies at most 64
color spans. Excessive spans report `CUI_TEXTAREA_CAPACITY` and paint a plain
contextual line. Gutter line indices are cached during row layout; gutter paint
visits visible rows, and digit-width counting refreshes on model revision.
Long individual paragraphs still require paragraph analysis for each selected
native line; this is not an incremental native paragraph-analysis cache.

Host measurement, geometry and raster calls are UI-thread confined. Keep host
font/style registrations consistent through draw-list consumption. After an
external metrics change, call `cui_text_metrics_changed` before the next frame.
No GDEF interior-ligature caret, cross-run grapheme, OS font discovery, bidi visual
arrow, or complete international editing parity is claimed. Prefix fallback is
not claimed visually correct for unsupported interior-cluster boundaries.

## Validation and integration

`tests/unit/test_contextual_text.c` exercises malformed UTF-8/ranges, duplicates,
CRLF provenance, frame ownership, copied colors, atomic capacity failures,
immutable cached sessions, exact cleanup and the 64-session bound with a 200 KB
paragraph. `tests/integration/test_contextual_text.c` uses actual Noto Sans plus
explicit Hebrew/Arabic fallbacks. It checks RTL caret/hit/selection geometry,
rendered selection pixels, wrapped punctuation raster hashes, U+2028 context,
Editor cluster colors and software-rendered pixels, pointer affinity through
idle frames, IME update/cancel/commit/Undo, retained sessions after source/font
changes, and a document over 200 KB with bounded idle viewport/composition work.
Missing font/bidi fixtures return 77; missing-glyph raster never counts as success.

The portable unit target links `cui`. The native integration target links
`cui`, `cui_text`, and `cui_software` (with native text enabled), and should use
CTest's skip-return-code 77. Root CMake registration and distribution regeneration
are integrator-owned. The older audit's standalone `cui_font_draw_styled` call
intentionally bypasses descriptors; use the new contextual test for the actual
renderer path rather than treating that legacy call as contextual rendering.

# ContextMenu command notifications

`cui_base_context_menu_events` and `cui_context_menu_events` add synchronous per-command observation to the existing Base and Styled ContextMenu. They use the unchanged `cui_menu_command_handler`, payload and result from [MenuTree events](MENU_EVENTS.md). Legacy ContextMenu entry points retain their behavior. Simple Menu and DropdownButton forwarding are separate, pending slices; this does not establish uniform component or binding coverage.

```c
static void selected(void *user, const cui_menu_command *event) {
    cui_id *last_command = user;
    *last_command = event->command;
}
/* During the existing frame, after submitting the receiving target: */
cui_menu_command_result result = cui_context_menu_events(
    ui, receiving_target, &theme, cui_string("Actions"), entries, entry_count,
    &action, &menu, options, (cui_menu_command_handler){selected, &last_command});
```

The Base form takes the legacy Base arguments followed by the handler: `ui, target, entries, count, action, state, disabled, dt, keep_open_checks, handler`. It reduces without drawing; Styled retains the existing popup layout and painting. Call either facade once for a given submission, rather than calling the legacy reducer as well.

Right-click opening, reanchoring and programmatic `cui_context_menu_open` emit no command notification. The original receiving bounds, popup-scope checks, anchor, focus restoration and opening order remain intact. `event.target` is the public receiving target, even if `state.overlay.trigger` restores focus to another control. `command` is the activated leaf ID, including nested leaves.

Each actual MenuTree command forwards exactly once at its existing commit seam, after action output, check/radio writes and close policy. Repeated keep-open commands remain separate notifications, including a return to the initial checked value. Closing-command exit policy is frozen before observation. `legacy_activated` preserves the aggregate bool; `command_count` counts actual handler invocations, so a missing handler yields zero while normal mutations still occur. `valid`, `submitted` and overflow semantics are those of MenuTree, including inert/layout-only suppression.

Metadata kind is ACTIVATE. Genuine pointer/touch, keyboard and supported menu accessibility events retain their source/frame/index evidence. MenuTree's reducer precedes current semantic registration, so the normal path has no copied activation snapshot; no opening event, focused target or programmatic action is converted into invented activation evidence. Copied pointer-free payloads survive the callback, frame and context lifetime.

Handlers may update caller-owned values or consume later input under the existing reducer rules. Payload/handler arguments are borrowed synchronously; active descriptors, child arrays, state, values and user storage must remain alive through submission. Direct mutation of in-flight menu navigation, freeing active storage, recursive submission and context destruction inside dispatch remain unsupported. Schedule removal or shutdown after submission/frame completion. Notifications cannot veto applied mutations and do not introduce open/close callbacks, queues or callback retiming.

[test_context_menu_events.c](../tests/unit/test_context_menu_events.c) exercises Base and Styled with distinct receiver/restore-focus identities, real right-click opening/reanchoring, repeated accessibility check commands, nested keyboard activation, mouse/touch, missing observers, owner updates, later-input consumption, disabled/inert/omitted calls, modal rejection and copied lifetimes. Existing `test_choice` remains the legacy behavior regression suite. Native tests run only through the invisible-display wrapper:

```sh
python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir build -- -R '^(context_menu_events|choice)$'
```

The integrator registers the new fixture in CMake and distribution/documentation exports. No binding facade or parity promotion is included.
documents.docs/CONTROLLED_SIBLING_AUDIT.md:
# Controlled sibling audit

This audit began at base `513883e` (integration/next17). It exercises real
frame/event routing, caller-owned values, completed-frame semantics, and actual
draw commands. The follow-up fixes ListMulti callback forwarding in the base
reducer. The default audit now passes; `--radio` separately preserves the known
Radio regression. CMake registration remains the integrator's responsibility.

## Confirmed defects

1. **Fixed: ListMulti confirmation/cancel callback user pointer.**
   Previously, `cui_base_list_multi` replaced `options.activation_user` with
   its private stack reducer to intercept `on_activate`, while forwarding the
   caller's `on_confirm` and `on_cancel` callbacks unchanged. Both received the
   private reducer pointer instead of the caller's user object.
   All three callbacks now use trampolines that preserve the original user pointer.
   The original defect was at `src/base/cui_choice.c:1006` in the audited base. A callback
   which writes through its expected owner pointer could corrupt the reducer
   or adjacent stack memory. The regression safely compares pointers without
   dereferencing the unexpected pointer. It covers accept and restore/reject
   policies, confirmation order/count, Escape, and idle frames. The registered
   Choice suite additionally writes final selection through the actual owner
   object from confirmation and cancellation callbacks and verifies final
   completed-frame semantics. Disabled paths emit no notifications.

2. **Remaining: Radio publishes stale earlier-sibling semantics.**
   Render radio option0 followed by option1 sharing one `int *`, initially 0;
   click option1. The owner value becomes 1, but the completed frame reports both
   radios as checked. Only the newly activated radio's semantic is refreshed by
   `cui_base_radio` (`src/base/cui_base.c:156`). Accessibility consumers can
   observe mutually exclusive controls simultaneously selected. The source
   explicitly schedules a repaint for earlier siblings; that next event-free
   frame correctly reports only option1. The draw list also contains both
   selected indicators in the activation frame and only one after that natural
   corrective redraw. The regression fails on stale completed-frame semantics;
   it records existing delayed-paint behavior without claiming paint can be
   retroactively rebuilt by the per-radio API.

The original audit reported five failing observations across these two defects.
The default executable covers the fixed ListMulti behavior and other passing
controls; `--radio` still reports one failure. No Radio production change is
included in this follow-up.

## Covered behavior and API limits

| API | Actual external-owner scenario | Observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List | `on_activate` replaces selection or restores the original selection | Final same-frame semantics and subsequent render callback see the final owner value; callback runs once. |
| ListMulti | `on_activate` replaces the full boolean array, including the earlier sibling, or restores it | Final same-frame semantics and actual checkmark location follow the owner array; callback runs once. Confirmation/cancel preserve the caller user pointer after the fix. |
| Radio | Later option changes the shared integer | Earlier semantic stays checked until scheduled redraw, as above; disabled option does not change the value. |
| Checkbox | Individually caller-owned booleans | Completed-frame semantics match both independent values; disabled item is inert. There is no dedicated CheckboxGroup or change-request callback API in this snapshot. |
| Tabs | Later tab changes the shared stable ID | Earlier and later semantics reflect final selection in the activation frame. |
| Tree | Later row changes the shared node ID | Final semantics are correct in the activation frame and repaint is scheduled. |
| Stepper | Later item changes the shared index | Final semantics are correct; one actual `Current` label is painted; repaint is scheduled. |
| MenuTree radio entries | Later entry changes the shared integer while popup stays open | Both sibling semantics reflect final selection in the activation frame; disabled entry is inert. |

List callbacks are synchronous notifications after the reducer writes selection,
not dedicated cancellable requests. An owner can restore selection inside the
notification, which this suite tests. Radio, Checkbox, Tabs, Menu, Tree and
Stepper do not expose selection-request callbacks; the suite does not invent a
rejection contract for them. Custom content/render callbacks are not treated as
controlled change callbacks. No cross-widget retroactive repaint or arbitrary
owner-state tracking is claimed.

List, ListMulti, Tabs and MenuTree complete their same-group state/paint in the
activation frame and do not request another corrective frame in these fixtures.
The audit records this rather than requiring unnecessary redraws. An event-free
host repaint is also exercised to verify stable state and no duplicate callbacks.
Radio's explicit corrective redraw is checked before that event-free frame.
All fixtures use public APIs; disabled controls and disabled list items are
exercised through actual routed pointer events.

## Reproduction

From the isolated checkout:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja
cmake --build build
cc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -Iinclude \
  tests/unit/test_controlled_siblings.c build/libcui.a -lm \
  -o /tmp/cui-controlled-siblings
/tmp/cui-controlled-siblings
/tmp/cui-controlled-siblings --radio # intentionally fails for the known Radio gap
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
```

The default audit returns 0; the separate Radio diagnostic returns 1. The
existing CTest suite does not yet register this new audit. The Choice suite's
notification regression is registered through its existing target. A sanitizer
build of `cui` and both audit selections exercises all cases.

Validation: warnings-as-errors compilation passes. The existing CTest suite
passes 90/91; its only failure is `distribution`, because `dist/cui_choice.h`
needs regeneration after the base reducer fix. Distribution output belongs to
the integrator. The audit passes by default, and `--radio` preserves its one
expected failure. ASan/UBSan pass the default audit and registered Choice suite
without runtime errors.

# Foundational controls

## Switch

`cui_switch` retains the bool-pointer convenience interface and renders a real track and
thumb. `cui_switch_ex` adds sizes, disabled state, accessible-name override, optional
custom label content and tooltip, label placement, Tab exclusion, focus-ring suppression,
custom checked color, and persistent spring motion. Zero options select Medium and the
source defaults. Track sizes are 28×16 (Extra Small/Small), 36×20 (Medium), and 44×24
(Large); thumbs have a two-pixel inset. Theme radius below four preserves square themes.
Disabled tracks halve their alpha, while the thumb remains opaque.

Without `on_change`, activation writes the caller's bool. With it, the callback receives
the requested value and the bool stays controlled by the application. It may update the
bool synchronously; painting and checked semantics use the resulting actual value.
Callbacks and content userdata are borrowed for the call. Enter, Space release, pointer
activation on either track or label, and normal Tab traversal use the base Switch.
`skip_tab` removes sequential focus without removing programmatic/pointer focus.

A caller-owned, zero-initialized `cui_switch_state` enables the theme's `spring_move`
response/damping/epsilon policy. Supply monotonic `now_seconds`; the first paint is
immediate, changes retain position and velocity, and settled controls request no frames.
`next_wake_seconds` exposes the next suggested wake while core invalidation requests a
follow-up frame. Reduced motion, zero response, and disabled travel settle immediately.
The convenience function (and an extended call with null state) paints without animation.
The state also owns the optional tooltip reducer; its options need the normal viewport
and elapsed-time inputs described in the surface documentation.

Switch labels use explicit 16/20/24-pixel line heights, including wrapping. Tooltip hit ownership
covers the complete control, rather than only the source track. Font weight and native
SVG details remain dependent on the host text renderer. These are tracked gaps, not a
claim of complete source parity. `label_left` is a C convenience extension (the frozen
source has the field but exposes no public setter).

## Toggle and ToggleGroup

`cui_toggle` now paints its label without an invented indicator. `cui_toggle_ex` adds
Ghost (default) and Outline variants, four source sizes, arbitrary child content,
accessible-name override, tooltip, Tab exclusion, optional focus outline, independent
corner radii/edge widths, and the same controlled boolean callback contract as Switch.
Pressed and enabled-hovered toggles use accent/accent-foreground; disabled presentation
keeps the source colors and suppresses interaction. Extra Small/Small/Medium/Large have
20/24/32/36-pixel minimum widths and fixed heights, with horizontal padding 2/4/8/12.
A composed icon or long label can grow the width. No automatic focus outline is painted,
matching the frozen source; `focus_ring` is an explicit C accessibility option.

`cui_toggle_group_ex` is the richer source composition. The existing Choice module's
`cui_toggle_group` remains available with its older selection options. Supply stable,
unique item IDs, caller-owned values, and per-item label/content/tooltip configuration.
The passive horizontal Toolbar group overrides child size and variant and combines
group/child disabled state.
Selections are independent; it does not introduce radio exclusivity or roving focus.
Ordinary groups have an eight-pixel gap; segmented groups have zero gap, only outside
corners, and no repeated left border. `custom_gap` permits an explicit spacing override.

Without a group callback, activation writes `values`. With a callback, provide a separate
`requested_values` scratch array of at least `count` elements. Each activation copies the
current rendered vector, flips its corresponding entry, and synchronously reports that
request. The callback may update the owner values immediately. Callback vectors are
borrowed only during the callback. Do not replace item/value storage during rendering.
Child callbacks are superseded by the group, matching the source grouping contract.
Pointer, Enter and Space all report the group request; keyboard delivery fixes a frozen
source limitation. The arrays and tooltip reducers stay application-owned, and rendering
allocates no persistent group state. Invalid sizes, variants, numeric geometry, duplicate
IDs, malformed strings, and insufficient/overlapping request scratch suppress the call.

Toggle labels use the source 1.25 line-height multiplier, subject to core integer layout
quantization. Hosts provide icon content and font weight; these remain rendering gaps.
documents.docs/CORE.md:
# Core contract and limits

The core uses the pinned Clay implementation for sizing and draw generation. Public APIs contain C11 types only. Calls run on one UI thread; contexts may be interleaved, including open frames, because each layout operation selects its owning Clay context. Concurrent calls are unsupported.

Queue input before `cui_begin_frame`. Events resolve in order against enabled interactive regions from the preceding completed frame, intersected with ancestor clips. The first frame has no input targets. Pointer down captures and focuses the topmost submitted hit region; release activates only inside that same region. Cancel and Escape clear pointer and space captures. Tab and Shift+Tab follow previous submission order. Enter activates on non-repeated key down; Space activates on key up when its captured focus remains current. Repeated key downs do not activate. Disabled controls suppress pending activation; disabled and omitted controls lose focus and capture by frame end.

`cui_event_target` reports the target at dispatch time, allowing controls to process multiple down/move/up or focus/text events in a single frame. Key events target the focus before that event; pointer move and up target capture. `cui_interact` reports final held state and consumes pending activation once. Multiple queued activations for one control are coalesced to its boolean activation. `cui_update_semantic` updates a submitted controlled value after a same-frame change.

Text and semantic names are copied to the fixed frame string arena; draw lists and semantic names survive until the next begin. The default text measure uses approximate width `length * font_size * 0.6` and height `font_size * 1.3`; applications needing font metrics supply the callback. Draw conversion supports rectangles, per-edge borders, text, RGBA bitmaps, and clip push/pop. Unsupported Clay draw types are not exposed by the public composition API.

The configuration defaults to 4096 elements, 8192 commands, and 262144 string bytes. There are at most 256 queued events, ID scopes, and nested boxes. Capacity failures set a sticky error. String exhaustion produces empty strings. Command exhaustion returns an empty list to avoid exposing unbalanced clip commands. Skipped elements remain safely balanced by matching end calls. Errors can be explicitly cleared after inspection; frame lifecycle errors reject invalid transitions.

IDs use scoped 64-bit FNV hashing. Nonzero element IDs and semantic IDs must be unique within a frame. Clay internally receives a domain-mixed 32-bit ID; consecutive raw public IDs are avalanched before Clay derives its automatic text IDs. Distinct public IDs with equal internal IDs are reported as duplicates rather than silently aliased. ID zero creates an anonymous box and is not an interactive control ID. Semantic controls should be submitted inside their matching element box so clipped hit regions can be established. Bounds returned during submission refer to the previous completed frame; completed semantic bounds reflect the current layout.

Headless tests cover input ordering, first-frame input, reordered IDs, capture and cancellation, focus traversal, keyboard activation, disabled and omitted controls, string ownership, draw conversion, clipped hit testing, context interleaving, duplicate/scoped IDs, lifecycle errors, and capacity recovery. This is the core interaction and composition contract, not a claim of complete shadcn component parity.

Focus scopes are explicit, independently nested declarations. A successful `cui_begin_focus_scope` must be paired with `cui_end_focus_scope`; failed begins must not be ended. At most 256 scopes can be declared per frame. The last declared modal scope is active, including nested scopes; enabled descendants receive initial focus by frame end. On the next input dispatch, Tab traversal and pointer hit testing are restricted to its descendants. Pointer down outside an active modal targets the scope ID without activating the underlying control. Escape targets the focused control's innermost scope, or the last declared scope when focus is outside all scopes; this also supports nonmodal popup dismissal. Nonmodal scopes alone do not restrict traversal or pointer routing. Omitted scopes stop trapping after the frame completes.

`cui_focus_restore` checks that a trigger appeared as an enabled interactive semantic in the previous completed frame. It permits restoring a trigger while its former modal scope is being omitted. The completed frame clears focus if that trigger is now disabled or omitted, and an active current modal still enforces its own descendants. Scope IDs should be distinct from interactive control IDs when their dismissal events must be distinguished. These APIs provide routing and focus state; overlays own visibility, panel bounds, outside-dismiss policy, placement, and rendering.

## Floating layers and compound controls

`cui_begin_portal` opens a viewport-positioned box outside ancestor clipping and
normal layout flow. Positive layers sort painting and interactive hit regions by
layer, with later submitted regions winning ties. Close it with `cui_end_box`.
Portals can clip their own content. Bounds must be finite and nonnegative; a
malformed portal suppresses its subtree while preserving paired begin/end calls,
even at the nesting budget. A portal does not itself trap focus: use a modal
focus scope where appropriate. Passive portal content lets pointer events pass
through; an active modal scope blocks underlying interactive controls.

`cui_set_semantic_details` records expanded/selected/read-only/required/invalid
state, numeric ranges, descriptions and relationships independently of painting.
Description strings are frame-copied. Group, tab-list/panel, list/menu, status,
alert, image and other roles distinguish container/content from focusable controls.
`cui_set_tab_stop(false)` removes an item from Tab traversal while preserving
pointer/programmatic focus, so composite controls can use roving focus.

`cui_event_activation` preserves each validated pointer-release, Enter or
released-Space activation even after `cui_interact` consumes the aggregate flag.
Compound reducers process this alongside events in input order, so ArrowDown then
Enter selects the newly navigated item within one frame. Core target IDs still
refer to dispatch-time previous-frame focus; reducers apply their local cursor.

Call `cui_dismiss_focus_scope` after reducing closing popup behavior and before
painting it. It withdraws current semantic descendants, deactivates nested traps,
and restores an enabled previous-frame trigger. Paired scope begin/end calls
remain required. This avoids briefly forcing focus back into a closing popup.

Boxes expose portable `align_x`/`align_y` start, center and end values. They align
children inside the available content area after sizing/padding; default start
alignment preserves existing layout behavior. These are physical axes: `align_x`
always means horizontal and `align_y` vertical, regardless of `row`.
For a fixed or growing row, `.align_x = CUI_ALIGN_CENTER` centers the whole
child group horizontally; `.align_y` aligns children vertically. For a column,
`.align_y = CUI_ALIGN_CENTER` centers the group vertically and `.align_x`
aligns children horizontally. Centering needs spare space on that axis: a FIT
box or children that consume all available grow space leave none to distribute.

`padding` is the uniform shorthand. Set `custom_padding` to replace it with
`padding_edges` (left, right, top, bottom), preserving explicit zero edges.
Negative/nonfinite edges normalize to zero and use integer layout units.
Likewise, `custom_corners` replaces `radius` with `corner_radii`, and
`custom_border_edges` replaces `border_width` with `border_edges`; custom zeros
win over nonzero uniform values.

`CUI_STR("literal")` is a brace initializer usable for static `cui_str` objects.
Use `(cui_str)CUI_STR("literal")` in expressions. Length excludes the final NUL
and includes embedded NUL bytes; use `cui_string` for runtime C strings.

Clipped boxes accept `offset_x`/`offset_y` to translate children while preserving the box viewport and ancestor clips; negative offsets scroll content forward. Fractional offsets are retained. Secondary/middle pointer events carry `pointer_button`, hit-route to previous regions, and never change ordinary primary capture/focus/activation. SDL3 maps all three buttons.

`cui_box.fixed_width` and `fixed_height` explicitly constrain a dimension,
including exactly zero; without the flags, zero retains the existing FIT rule.
Negative/nonfinite explicit dimensions normalize to zero. This supports collapsed
viewports without a visible epsilon-sized remnant.

`cui_box.layout_only` measures its complete subtree but suppresses paint, semantic
nodes and routed input, including nested portals. Bounds tracking still works;
callbacks still execute and applications must avoid unrelated side effects.
Focus requests from the subtree are ignored; hidden modal scopes do not trap
outside focus. Clipping commands remain balanced even when all enclosed paint is
suppressed. This is useful for measuring a disclosure before animating its outer
viewport. The application retains measured bounds through `cui_track_bounds`.

`cui_box.inert` preserves layout and painting while suppressing semantics, hover,
routed events, focus requests and modal scope effects throughout the subtree,
including portals. It supports visible exit animations without leaving closing
controls interactive. `layout_only` implies inert behavior and also suppresses
painting. A hidden/inert subtree cannot dismiss an enclosing active focus scope.

`cui_set_semantic_role` refines an already-submitted current-frame semantic node
without replacing its name, state, range, parent or description. It rejects
missing IDs, out-of-range roles and calls from inert subtrees. `CUI_ROLE_LINK`
is focusable and participates in existing pointer/keyboard activation; the
application owns navigation, so no platform URL opener is implied.

Passive semantic nodes can set `details.focus_target` to a focusable control ID.
A primary pointer down resolves that target before subsequent queued keyboard or
text events are routed, including events in the same frame. Pointer events stay
addressed to the passive node and do not capture/activate it or move the target's
caret. Disabled, missing and modal-inaccessible targets are ignored. This supports
input addons and labels without exposing them as extra buttons or Tab stops.

`cui_focus_within(ui, scope_id)` checks actual focus-scope ancestry for the focused
semantic node, including nested scopes. It uses current submissions when
available and the retained frame before those nodes have been resubmitted.
Disabled nodes, inactive/dismissed scopes and calls from inert subtrees return
false. It does not infer ownership from overlapping rectangles; notification
stacks can use it to pause a timer when any custom child has keyboard focus.

`cui_box.max_width` and `max_height` cap natural (FIT), growing and explicitly
sized boxes when positive and finite. Caps constrain a fixed minimum as well;
short natural content stays short, and an explicit zero dimension stays zero.
Nonpositive/nonfinite caps mean unbounded. Combine a cap with `clip` to bound
arbitrary custom children without a previous-frame measurement flash.

`CUI_ROLE_LISTITEM` and `CUI_ROLE_LOG` describe passive list entries and append-oriented logs without adding automatic Tab stops. Optional `scroll_axis_lock` in semantic details uses the declared orientation to accept only dominant-axis wheel motion (ties count as vertical). Unlocked routing is unchanged; a locked region at its boundary still chains to a movable ancestor. Event deltas remain intact for the recipient.

`cui_color_mix_oklab(first, second, amount)` interpolates premultiplied alpha in perceptual Oklab space, then clamps the result to byte sRGB. Amount is the second color weight; finite out-of-range values clamp, and non-finite amounts select the first color. Transparent endpoints do not tint an opaque color while fading it.

Set `semantic_details.focusable` to opt a passive container (for example a Log viewport) into keyboard/programmatic/pointer focus without changing its semantic role. Defaults remain passive. `cui_set_tab_stop(false)` suppresses sequential Tab navigation while retaining pointer/programmatic focus; disabled/inert containers remain unavailable, and interactive children take hit precedence over their enclosing container.

`semantic_details.no_focus` suppresses a role's normal focus behavior, including Tab and known-node programmatic focus. Combine it with `pointer_activatable` for a pointer-only Button that retains its Button semantics. A `focus_target` can focus an associated editor while the pointer-only Button keeps its own capture and release activation. This supports numeric step buttons without stealing the editor's keyboard focus.

`semantic_details.pointer_activatable` makes a passive container receive primary pointer capture and validated release activation, without adding focus or a Tab stop. Its click preserves existing keyboard focus; nested interactive children take precedence. Disabled/inert guards, release outside and cancellation still apply. Set `focusable` independently only when the container should also support keyboard navigation.

`cui_set_underlay` paints one rounded rectangle below the children of the current box and above its background. Relative bounds resolve after current-frame layout. The paint is clipped to that box and all enclosing clips, contributes no layout/input/semantics, and respects layout-only suppression. Repeated calls replace the same underlay. Invalid geometry leaves the prior paint unchanged; normal draw-command capacity applies atomically.

`cui_paint_bitmap` emits a leaf `CUI_DRAW_IMAGE` from borrowed straight-alpha RGBA8 pixels. The source view supports padded rows, an explicit cache revision, a pixel crop, opacity, and grayscale. Zero source bounds select the entire image; FIT sizing defaults to the crop dimensions. Pixels must remain valid until renderer completion. Dimensions are bounded to 16384 per axis and invalid views/crops are rejected without opening a layout element. Rounded corners and ancestor clips apply normally. Software, SDL3, SDL_GPU/Vulkan, and Sokol render bitmap pixels with crop, grayscale, optional RGBA tint, opacity, and rounded clipping. Native adapters keep bounded 64-entry/64-MiB texture caches keyed by source pointer, revision, crop, raster size, corners, grayscale, and tint. Placement and opacity reuse the cached texture. Canvas renders the same RGBA draw commands with a bounded 64-entry/16-MiB raster cache. Rasterized rounded edges currently use pixel-center coverage; source alpha is preserved. This API does not decode files or fetch URLs.

`cui_set_underlay_ex` adds current-frame START/CENTER/END alignment and optional growth relative to the owning box. For a full-width bottom baseline, use bounds `{0,0,0,1}`, `grow_width=true`, and vertical END. Resizing resolves in the same layout pass without retained-size lag; offsets apply after alignment.

`cui_begin_absolute_box` opens a zero-flow child using a fixed rectangle relative
to its parent. It inherits ancestor clipping, inert/layout-only state and the
parent's layer, so overlapping resize handles stay beneath higher portals.
It requires an open parent and is balanced with `cui_end_box` even on invalid
bounds. `CUI_ROLE_SEPARATOR` is passive unless semantic details opt into focus.

Semantic `details.cursor` is a portable pointer hint. `cui_pointer_cursor` returns
the captured control's hint while dragging, otherwise the topmost enabled hit
in the completed frame, respecting ancestor clips and modal ownership. Hosts
apply it after `cui_end_frame`; unsupported hosts may retain their default.
The SDL3 host exposes `cui_sdl3_set_cursor` and also applies the last completed
frame's hint during polling. System cursors are cached and released with the
adapter; headless drivers report unsupported without failing event dispatch.

A box may set `custom_opacity=true` and `opacity` to multiply every descendant
paint's alpha, including text, bitmap, underlay and logically nested portals.
Nested factors multiply; default boxes preserve full opacity. Values clamp to
0..1, with nonfinite values treated as zero. This is per-draw alpha modulation,
not isolated group compositing. Opacity alone preserves semantics and input;
combine with `inert` when hidden content should stop receiving interaction.

Fractional font sizes and explicit line heights are preserved through measurement,
word wrapping and draw commands. A context-owned bounded style table supplies
stable Clay measurement identities; old generations are reclaimed only between
frames, avoiding stale metrics when a line height changes. Text stays vertically
centered in an explicit line box. Native font rasterizers may still quantize glyph
outlines independently of these float layout coordinates.

Pointer hit order follows each semantic's matching layout node, even when behavior
is registered before that box. Higher layers win, then floating-root paint order,
then child layout order. Ancestor clips and paint-time inert/layout-only state
apply to that matched node. Semantics without a matching box retain their
registration-parent fallback. Focus-scope ownership remains behavior-owned.

`cui_box.width_percent` and `height_percent` interpret the corresponding dimension
as a fraction of the current parent's inner extent. Fractions clamp to0..1 and
take precedence over fixed flags and max caps. This resolves proportional rows
on the first frame and after resize, without previous-frame measurements.
Absolute/portal bounds retain their explicit dimension semantics.

Cooperative event bubbling uses `cui_event_consumed` and `cui_consume_event`:
leaf controls handle input before ancestor callbacks inspect it. Consumption does
not erase the original target or activation diagnostics and resets each frame.
Both editor event paths consume Left/Right, including at the text boundary.
`cui_focus_step_within` traverses current submitted, enabled Tab stops inside a
focus scope and wraps; call it after children. Nested scopes participate, while
inert content, disabled controls, explicit non-Tab stops and controls outside
the active modal are excluded. Missing scopes or removed focused children leave
focus untouched. This is an opt-in traversal primitive; ordinary Tab is unchanged.

`cui_resource_get` supplies stable zero-initialized context storage keyed by an
owner ID and a namespace ID. The default limits are 128 entries and 1 MiB of
payload bytes; configure `max_resources` and `resource_bytes` independently.
Payload-owned allocations need their own limits. Reusing a key requires the
same size and callbacks, preventing accidental reinterpretation. Exhaustion
reports `CUI_ERROR_CAPACITY` without discarding another component's live data.

Finish rendering each draw list before the next `cui_begin_frame`. At that
boundary, the resource collector runs for entries used in the preceding frame;
entries omitted for an entire frame are destroyed and their capacity reclaimed.
`cui_destroy` releases every remaining entry exactly once. Callbacks must not
reenter the context. This supports immutable bitmap versions until rendering
finishes, without global mutable component caches.

`cui_frame_time` accumulates validated frame deltas; `cui_frame_delta` exposes the
current delta. Failed begins do not advance the clock or collect resources.
Hosts set `cui_set_reduced_motion`; changes request redraw, and components query
`cui_reduced_motion` to choose static presentation. Animated components still
request their next frame explicitly through `cui_invalidate`.

`cui_set_bitmap_underlay` paints a borrowed bitmap above the current box's
background and below its children, with the solid-underlay alignment/grow rules.
It supports source cropping, tint, opacity and corner radii through the normal
image renderer path. Inherited alpha is applied once. Invalid bitmap geometry
leaves an existing underlay intact; a later solid underlay replaces the bitmap.
This permits image/gradient backgrounds without floating over interactive text.

After `cui_end_frame`, `cui_semantic_parent(ui, id)` returns the explicit semantic parent when supplied, otherwise the closest layout ancestor whose box is owned by that semantic ID. A control registered without its own layout box does not become the semantic owner of its surrounding box. Explicit parent links must be acyclic. It returns zero for roots, unknown IDs and while a frame is open. Hosts can use this alongside `cui_semantics` to build the accessibility tree without guessing parentage from rectangles. `CUI_ROLE_RADIOGROUP` is appended to the role enum, preserving earlier role values.

`cui_set_outline` paints an outside border band for the current open box using its current-frame bounds, independent corner radii and inherited opacity. It consumes no layout space, preserves the interior, follows ancestor clipping, and can coexist with a solid/bitmap underlay. Zero width clears the band; invalid geometry leaves the prior setting intact. Like underlays, command-capacity failure produces an empty draw list and a capacity error.
Hosts may supply `cui_event.click_count` on pointer events. Zero and one preserve ordinary click behavior; larger values retain the host’s multi-click sequence metadata. The SDL adapter forwards SDL’s count directly, and the core queue preserves it unchanged. Text selection policies remain the component’s responsibility.

`cui_pointer_position` returns the latest Move/Down/Up coordinates processed by `cui_begin_frame`; queued events wait until then, idle frames retain the position and a new context starts at `(0,0)`. It does not infer pointer visibility, hover, clipping or occlusion. Invalid/nonfinite values preserve both output variables. Use the accessor for host-driven plot cursors; current-layout prepaint callbacks remain a separate missing Core seam.

Portable shortcut identities include `[` and `]` for Editor block-indent bindings. They are appended enum values, preserving existing host key numbers, and round-trip through `cui_key_from_character`/`cui_key_character`. Browser and SDL ASCII fallback mappings use these helpers. Character/IME text input remains separate from shortcut identity.

Retained text layout can cache `cui_text_metrics_revision(ui)` with its document,
width and complete text style. The context starts at generation1; a successful
`cui_text_metrics_changed` outside a frame resets Clay measurement and changes
this generation. Calls inside a frame are ignored. Null returns0. Compare by
equality: generations wrap while skipping0. Hosts must announce changes to font
registries or measurement policy before the next frame. Contexts are independent.

# Date locales and direct year selection

Calendar and DatePicker now expose an interactive year header. Activate it to
choose from a 20-year grid (four columns, five rows), page backward/forward in
20-year steps, choose a year, then a month and an actual day. Selecting the year
or month navigates without changing the selected date. A date in 1980 takes
three year-page clicks from the gallery's 2026 starting year, instead of hundreds
of month steps. The final page ends at 9999 and has one blank cell; year zero is
never selectable. Navigation uses icon chevrons, not text `<`/`>` characters.

The gallery adds a Date locale selector for Calendar and DatePicker. Its default
is ISO (legacy). Built-in locale tables provide English US, English UK, Italian,
French, German, Spanish and Japanese month/weekday labels, week starts, numeric
date ordering and accessible control labels. US starts on Sunday and formats
MM/DD/YYYY; UK/Italian/French/Spanish start on Monday and format DD/MM/YYYY;
German uses DD.MM.YYYY; Japanese starts on Sunday and uses YYYY/MM/DD.
The dates remain Gregorian model values, independent of presentation.

## Public API

Choose an explicit borrowed locale in Calendar options:

```c
cui_calendar_options options = {
    .locale = cui_date_locale_builtin(CUI_DATE_LOCALE_IT)
};
cui_calendar(ui, calendar_id, &theme, &calendar_state, &selection, options);
```

Or supply the same options to DatePicker:

```c
cui_date_picker_options options = {
    .calendar = {.locale = cui_date_locale_builtin(CUI_DATE_LOCALE_EN_GB)},
    .viewport = {0, 0, width, height}
};
cui_date_picker(ui, trigger_id, &theme, cui_string("Date"), &picker_state,
                &selection, options);
```

A NULL locale preserves the existing ISO trigger/day labels and caller's
`first_weekday` (including zero-initialized Sunday). With an explicit locale, its
week start wins unless `first_weekday_override` is true. For example, set the
flag plus `.first_weekday = 6` for Saturday. Existing zero initializers and
Calendar state initialization remain valid.

`cui_date_format_locale(date, locale, buffer, capacity)` returns the required
byte length excluding NUL, and NUL-terminates byte truncation when capacity is
small (a truncated custom UTF-8 separator may end mid-codepoint). Capacity
zero may use a NULL buffer. An invalid date returns zero and clears a supplied
buffer. `cui_date_locale_builtin()` returns NULL for an unknown enum value.

Custom `cui_date_locale` tables and their strings are caller-owned and borrowed.
Keep them alive while options reference them. Supply UTF-8 `months[12]` and
`weekdays[7]` (Sunday-indexed), week start, numeric `order` and a literal
`separator`. Missing labels fall back to English. Calendar, year/month choice
and four navigation labels can also be customized. A zero order is ISO; supported
other orders are month/day/year, day/month/year and year/month/day. The separator
is literal text, not a strftime/ICU pattern. This API does not parse localized
input, discover OS locales, handle alternative calendar systems or guarantee
fonts covering every label. Supply suitable fonts for Japanese/custom scripts.

## Interaction, constraints and focus

Year and month cells use stable `cui_calendar_year_id()` and
`cui_calendar_month_id()` IDs. The year header is navigation part 5; existing
parts 1–4 retain their month/year behavior in day view and parts 1/4 page the
active year grid. Calendar state records the view, year page and keyboard cursor.
Initialize state with `cui_calendar_init()` or `cui_date_picker_init()`.

Arrows move by one cell horizontally or four cells vertically in the grids.
Home/End move to the page's first/last eligible entry. PageUp/PageDown change the
year page by 20 years, or change the displayed year in month view. In day view,
PageUp/PageDown change month (Ctrl/Meta changes year); existing arrow and
Ctrl/Meta-arrow behavior remains available. Enter/Space use ordinary control
activation. Focus follows the selected year, month and first enabled day.
Escape returns from a year/month view to days; in DatePicker, a second Escape
closes the popup and restores trigger focus.

Disabled controls cannot change view or selection. A year/month is enabled only
if it contains at least one date passing disabled/minimum/maximum/filter rules.
Date filters remain caller callbacks and can be consulted repeatedly when
checking a grid; keep them pure and inexpensive. Range selection is unchanged:
only actual enabled day activation starts/completes a range, and the popup closes
after the second day. Hard boundaries 1 and 9999 remain respected.

## Verification

`test_picker.c` covers all seven built-in formats and week starts, explicit week
start overrides, custom UTF-8 separators/labels, safe truncation, ISO fallback,
actual year/month/day controls, leap-day 1980 selection, min/max/filter and
disabled rejection, range selection, keyboard navigation, focus transitions,
Escape and year boundaries. Existing Picker coverage is retained.

Run the strict real browser suite after building the gallery:

```sh
uv run tests/web/test_date_locale_year.py --directory build/web \
  --chromium /path/to/chromium
```

It exercises all seven locales in both Calendar and DatePicker with mouse and
actual Chromium CDP touch (28 cases), checks centered/equal-width year grids,
localized month and weekday ordering, actual selected model value 19800229,
localized trigger paint/accessibility, popup closing and two-stage Escape.
It uses configuration DOM controls and real component input, never direct
reducer calls. Screenshots/reports are written to `/tmp/cui-date-locale-year`.
This does not establish physical mobile device, OS IME or every font coverage.

Warning-enabled native build and the two documented API examples compiled. Full
CTest passed 93/94; only root-owned generated distribution was stale pending
regeneration. Picker/base-only passed ASAN/UBSAN (2/2). The strict locale/year
suite passed 28/28, existing touch coverage 42/42 and 16/16, and the full browser
suite rendered all 78 stories, compiled all 78 excerpts and passed its 390 px
layout and hosted-path checks.
