# DatePicker with Calendar options

Include `cui/cui_date_picker_calendar.h` and rebuild with matching headers/library. This additive value record forwards Calendar presentation and behavior through DatePicker; zero preserves the legacy DatePicker path without resizing existing public records.

```c
#include "cui/cui_date_picker_calendar.h"
bool reservation_date(cui_context *ui, const cui_theme *theme,
    cui_date_picker_state *state, cui_date_selection *selection,
    cui_rect viewport, cui_date host_today) {
    return cui_date_picker_ex(ui, 100, theme, cui_string("Reservation date"), state, selection,
        (cui_date_picker_options){.viewport = viewport,
            .calendar = {.range = true, .locale = cui_date_locale_builtin(CUI_DATE_LOCALE_IT)}},
        (cui_date_picker_calendar_options){
            .presentation = {.month_toggle = true, .today = host_today, .neighboring_days = true},
            .behavior = {.range_transition = CUI_CALENDAR_RANGE_RESTART_EARLIER,
                .year_destination = CUI_CALENDAR_YEAR_OPEN_DAYS,
                .recenter = CUI_CALENDAR_RECENTER_SELECTION_START,
                .range_validation = CUI_CALENDAR_VALIDATE_RANGE_ENDPOINTS}});
}
```

Call `cui_date_picker_init(state, popup_id, initial_date)` once, then submit each active frame. The caller retains state and selection. Supply a finite positive viewport and a distinct popup ID. Locale/custom labels, first weekday, 1–3 months, cell size, range, bounds and disabled-date predicate already belong to `options.calendar`; they are not duplicated in the new record. Today is a host-supplied civil date, with no clock lookup; invalid/zero omits its paint. Month toggle is effective only for one month. See [Calendar presentation](CALENDAR_PRESENTATION.md) and [behavior policies](CALENDAR_BEHAVIOR.md) for exact normalization, occurrence IDs, eligibility and paint precedence.

DatePicker reduces Calendar exactly once, then closes after the entire queued Calendar input when an accepted single selection or completed range remains. An earlier endpoint restart remains open; a rejected completion remains open. A same-date single activation closes even when the bool is false because the final selection did not change. Queued targets use the original grid and panel identity even when an earlier activation recenters. Completion followed by another start in the same queue remains open. Opening, rendering or supplying policies does not reset Calendar state or synchronize range phase.

The existing pass order remains Escape-from-month/year handling, overlay dismissal/trigger toggles, Calendar reduction, close, trigger and popup submission/paint. These are separate passes, not a globally chronological dispatcher. Two Escapes queued in a selector frame are handled by the existing selector prepass; they are not equivalent to Escape in two successive frames. Closing restores trigger focus; a newly opened Styled popup focuses the existing Calendar cursor or selector. Outer disabled closes the popup; Calendar-only disabled leaves the trigger operable while suppressing Calendar actions. Omitted components do not reduce input or manufacture close events.

The Styled bool is the exact legacy result. In particular, an invalid viewport or late overlay-begin failure can return false after a selection edit; inspect caller state/selection when handling such errors. `cui_base_date_picker_ex` returns the full aggregate Calendar result but owns neither layout nor popup submission. A Base host calls it once, then positions/begins its overlay and calls `cui_calendar_submit_ex` with the same presentation record; do not reduce a second time. `cui_date_picker_calendar_id(trigger)` exposes Styled's unchanged Calendar ID for `cui_calendar_cell_resolve`; zero trigger or zero derived ID returns zero, and ordinary ID collision discipline still applies.

Extension values are copied and not retained. Keep state/selection, locale strings, predicate and user resources alive under existing submission/frame/render-consumption lifetimes. Disabled predicates must be pure and must not mutate active UI or recursively submit. The existing typed CHANGE wrappers retain their legacy path, final-value comparison and callback timing; they do not accept these options. There is no new selection observer, open/close notification, cancellation cause, event-source attribution or binding-builder support in this slice. Full DatePicker time editing, presets, cleanable controls, arbitrary styling and browser extension parity remain separate work.

The browser gallery uses this API with the separate month menu, selectable adjacent-month days and host-local today marker enabled. Its copyable example calls the same additive entry point. Headless desktop and touch checks in `tests/web/test_date_picker_presentation_gallery.py` cover month navigation without changing the selected value, adjacent-day selection and popup close, two-stage Escape and disabled triggers. The locale/year-grid suite separately covers localized 1980 leap-day selection. These checks do not establish the remaining editing, preset or styling capabilities.
documents.docs/DATE_TIME_PICKER.md:
# Single-date time picker

This opt-in portable C11 API composes one civil date and time. It implements the
Base/value/synchronization and Styled slices of `design/DATE_PICKER_DATETIME.md`.
No timezone/range editor, arbitrary date parser/formatter, typed event
wrapper or binding builder is included. Existing
DatePicker/actions and TimeField calls keep their behavior.

Include `cui/cui_date_time_picker.h`; link `src/base/cui_date_time_picker.c` along
with the normal picker/actions/Calendar sources. Canonical builds register the Base and Styled sources, standalone optional
`CUI_DATE_TIME_PICKER_IMPLEMENTATION` and `CUI_IMPLEMENTATION_ALL` distribution
paths. Native source SDKs carry the API; language builders do not expose it.

## Ownership and frame order

Retain `cui_date_time_picker_state` and `cui_date_time_value` for one UI context,
on its owner thread. Initialize with a stable popup ID and initial valid month.
NULL init is a no-op; all-zero/uninitialized state cannot reduce or assign.
`cui_date_time_value.date` is a valid Gregorian date or all-zero absence; partial
invalid dates reject preflight. `time` must always be valid 00–23:00–59:00–59,
even with no date. It exposes retained time that upstream's empty DateTime hides;
check date presence before using it as a committed date-time.

Call `cui_base_date_time_picker` once per frame, passing stable distinct trigger,
Calendar and TimeField IDs plus state/value/options. It reduces once, submits
trigger/optional clear semantics, and returns result flags. Caller owns all paint
and the popup. Do not call public `cui_time_field` or `cui_base_time_field` again:
those functions both reduce and submit.

For an open popup, the exact order is:

1. Set bounds and begin the existing `state.actions.picker.overlay` once; begin
   the caller's portal/layout inside that scope.
2. `cui_calendar_submit_ex` using `state.actions.picker.calendar` and retained
   `state.actions.calendar_value.dates`, with the same Calendar options/extensions.
   Combine outer disabled into Calendar disabled. This submits without reducing.
3. `cui_date_time_picker_submit_time(ui,time_id,&state,&value,options)`.
4. `cui_date_time_picker_submit_presets(ui,&state,options)` even if preset_count=0.
5. Paint/layout these submitted IDs; end the portal and overlay scope once.

Both helpers are semantics-only and require this frame's successful Base call,
the same valid options/value and the caller's real open popup scope. Time submission
must precede preset submission: the latter publishes bounded actual Calendar,
preset and TimeField target identities for the next frame. Time segments require
both successful helper stamps from the immediately preceding frame; omission,
failed/duplicate helper, omitted frame or close/reopen expires admission. Helpers
never replay input/state edits/callbacks. Core capacity errors after submissions
are not rolled back; failed helper stamps publish no partial identity set.

`cui_date_time_picker_time_id(trigger)` supplies a stable optional derived time
root; Base also accepts a caller-supplied time ID. Segment IDs are the existing
`cui_time_segment_id(time_id,0..3)`. All four are reserved during preflight,
including currently hidden second/AM-PM segments. Caller global ID discipline is
still required. Existing modal outside-clear restrictions apply: dismiss the
popup before using the separate clear button outside it.

## Values, synchronization and drafts

MINUTE truncates seconds to zero; SECOND retains them. Twelve-hour appearance
never changes civil storage. No timezone, UTC offset, DST, leap-second or implicit
clock service exists. First valid reduction uses supplied time for a present date,
and configured default time for an absent date. Options are validated atomically
before predicates, normalization, input or state changes.

Repeated unchanged controlled values preserve draft digit count/segment, Calendar
view and rejected-child divergence. A changed external value is setter intent:
reset draft, truncate supplied time (empty assignment uses default), sync child
if eligible, close directly and emit no source Change. Between frames,
`cui_date_time_picker_assign(&state,&value,next)` queues identical setter intent
as well: it validates next atomically and sets a pending flag, consumed only by a
valid Base call. Invalid options leave pending assignment intact. It does not
require a UI context or touch focus/semantics between frames.

Default-time changes reset current time; precision changes truncate it; hour-cycle
changes reset draft while preserving civil time. Changes apply once before input;
external setter intent wins over simultaneous default changes. Ordinary close,
reopen and idle frames do not push a time value into a pending draft. Disabled
popup omission retains draft but rejects user input; Calendar-only disabled gates
day edits and does not disable the time field, presets or clear.

## Source behavior and results

Frozen authority is `87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`,
`crates/component/src/time/date_picker.rs:215–227,261–291,327–447,484–538`.

- Different accepted day adopts child into outer date, preserves time and stays
  open. Same accepted day closes and confirms without a source Change. Comparison
  uses outer date: an unchanged retained child can still replace a divergent outer.
- Actual TimeField change stays open, preserving date. A present date reports
  source Change; an absent date only changes retained time storage.
- Date-only preset preserves current time. Timed preset replaces/truncates it and
  resets draft. Both close, emit source Change even if identical and explicitly
  focus trigger. SOURCE may accept outer date despite child matcher/bounds
  rejection; MATCH_SHAPE_ENABLED pre-rejects ineligible assignments. Shape matching
  alone is vacuous for this single-only facade. Changing matcher or reopening
  does not silently resynchronize rejected child; an actual later day edit does.
- Clear/Delete restores default time, clears outer/child date and draft, preserves
  Calendar view/month, closes without an explicit focus request, and reports source
  Change even if already empty. `cleanable` controls visibility independently of
  Delete OFF/TRIGGER/SCOPE. Outer disabled gates every user action.

`valid` is preflight success, not rollback of later Core/layout failures.
`value_changed` compares final date AND time against entry storage, including
normalization/external-empty/default changes. `source_change` coalesces accepted
source Change causes; it is not a callback stream or Change count. Repeated preset
or clear can report source_change=true with value_changed=false. A time edit then
preset can restore the entry value with source_change=true. An empty-date time
edit has value_changed=true but source_change=false. `time_edited` means the
TimeField actually changed storage; `action_activated` means accepted clear/preset;
`confirmed` means same-day confirmation. `calendar` is the one reduction result.

Phase order: configuration/external sync; Escape/overlay/trigger pass; Calendar;
TimeField if still open and admitted; first eligible action in queued order.
There is no global chronological interleaving of Calendar/time/action events.
Escape/trigger transitions invalidate old popup action/time admission. Scope
Delete accepts only actual previous submitted enabled targets still eligible in
the current view/list/precision. Popup root or generated namespace IDs alone do
not qualify. Core may redirect invalid programmatic focus before key dispatch;
the resolved real target is authoritative.

## Validation and lifetimes

Preflight bounds: at most 8 presets, 96-byte nonempty scalar UTF-8 action labels;
empty time_label falls back to Time. Reject malformed active time, date, precision,
policy, dimensions/viewport, min/max, range=true, duplicate/reserved IDs, invalid
active UTF-8 or NULL preset storage before mutation/predicates/input. Ignored
has_time=false preset time is not inspected. Bounds/predicate checks on assignment
are inherited CUI extensions; predicates are pure, owner-thread only.

Arrays/options are borrowed for calls. Strings, locale tables and predicate/user
resources remain valid through frame/render consumption. State stores copied
values/IDs only and allocates nothing. Reinitialize before moving to a different
context; do not edit bookkeeping, manually force reopen or reuse state roots in
the same frame. Legacy public record layouts stay unchanged; new record users
must rebuild with matching headers.

Private fixture: `cmake -S tests/fixtures/date_time_picker -B BUILD -G Ninja`,
then build `test_date_time_picker test_date_time_picker_styled test_picker
test_date_picker_actions date_time_picker_header date_time_picker_guide date_time_picker_guide_cpp`.
Run through `python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir BUILD -- -V -R
'^(date_time_picker|date_time_picker_styled|picker|date_picker_actions)$'`. Repeat in a separate
`-DCUI_SANITIZE=ON` build. `tests/fixtures/date_time_picker/test_wasi.py --build-dir
BUILD` uses the repository's existing pinned offline WASI driver. The Base/Styled checks alone add
no live-AT or full source-parity evidence. Final worker results will be
reported with the signed checkpoint. Configure a separate fixture with
`-DCUI_DATETIME_BUILD_STYLED=OFF` to build/run the Base test without the optional
Styled source.

Accepted Calendar selections are evaluated in queue order against the immediately
preceding outer date. A→B→A remains open with source_change true and
value_changed false. A→B→B confirms B; A→A→B confirms A and skips later
Calendar events. The private synchronous visitor uses constant stack storage;
close occurs once after Calendar reduction. Legacy Calendar entry points have
no visitor and preserve their existing queue behavior. This stop-first-confirmation
rule describes CUI routing, not GPUI scheduler equivalence.

TimeField source_change uses the existing reducer's net phase result: Up then
Down restoring the entry time does not report a time source change. There is no
ordered callback stream or per-intermediate-time-edit notification claim.


## Styled composition

`cui_date_time_picker` calls Base once and owns the single popup scope, Calendar,
paint-only TimeField, and preset/clear paint. Use this instead of manually calling
Base/helpers in that frame. Calendar root is `cui_date_picker_calendar_id(trigger)`;
time root is `cui_date_time_picker_time_id(trigger)`. No extra resources are retained.
The trigger displays a bounded locale date plus 12/24-hour minute/second time;
there is no chrono pattern API. This display is separate from its accessible
name supplied by the caller. `time_label` labels both the visible row and group.

Styled validates theme metrics and rejects a popup larger than the supplied
viewport before reducing input or mutating value/state. It does not silently
clip away time/actions or add scrolling. Supply enough room, fewer months/presets,
or smaller Calendar cells. DatePicker has no `design_size` field: actual supported
metrics are Calendar cell_size (20–128, default32), 1–3 months, and finite theme
font/padding/gap/radius; XS–9XL enums from other components are not accepted here.
A bounded formatter can truncate very long localized date labels; custom source
format patterns remain unsupported. Native/browser text shaping follows the
existing host; software geometry tests omit glyph rasterization without a font.

The following complete C11/C++11-compatible example is compiled by the standalone
fixture. The application calls init once, retains both objects, and calls frame
inside its own begun CUI frame. It links the Base source plus optional
`src/components/cui_date_time_picker.c` and ordinary components/Calendar sources.

<!-- datetime-example-begin -->
```c
#include "cui/cui_date_time_picker.h"
#include <string.h>

void example_datetime_init(cui_date_time_picker_state *state,
                           cui_date_time_value *value) {
    cui_date initial;
    initial.year = 2024; initial.month = 2; initial.day = 15;
    memset(value, 0, sizeof *value);
    value->date = initial;
    value->time.hour = 9; value->time.minute = 30;
    cui_date_time_picker_init(state, 702, initial);
}

cui_date_time_picker_result example_datetime_frame(cui_context *ui,
    const cui_theme *theme, cui_date_time_picker_state *state,
    cui_date_time_value *value, cui_rect viewport) {
    cui_date_time_picker_options options;
    cui_date_time_preset preset;
    memset(&options, 0, sizeof options);
    memset(&preset, 0, sizeof preset);
    preset.id = 704; preset.label = cui_string("Tomorrow");
    preset.date.year = 2024; preset.date.month = 2; preset.date.day = 16;
    options.picker.viewport = viewport;
    options.precision = CUI_DATE_TIME_SECOND;
    options.default_time.hour = 8;
    options.presets = &preset; options.preset_count = 1;
    options.cleanable = true;
    options.clear_id = 703; options.clear_label = cui_string("Clear");
    options.delete_policy = CUI_DATE_PICKER_DELETE_SCOPE;
    return cui_date_time_picker(ui, 701, theme, cui_string("Appointment"),
                                 state, value, options);
}
```
<!-- datetime-example-end -->

The local preset array is borrowed only during submission; its literal label
remains readable for rendering. Application-owned dynamic strings must follow
the frame lifetime rules above. Bindings remain separate; the gallery mode below uses the C API directly.

Styled slice validation: focused native and ASan/UBSan wrapper checks each pass
4/4 suites; pinned WASI passes Base579 and Styled695 assertions. Base-only
configuration passes its 579 assertions without the optional Styled source.
Software tests cover 1–3 months, minute/second and 12/24-hour segments, actual
popup containment, supported cell metrics/theme variants, eight presets, narrow
rejection, draft/Tab/preset/clear behavior, and legacy TimeField memberwise
semantics/nontext pixel equivalence. Existing date-only actions tests retain
legacy zero-option picker equivalence. Guide/header compile as C11/C++11.
These are headless software/semantic checks, not browser, live-AT or GPU proof.


Canonical integration additionally compiles and executes the exact guide example
in the native and WASI Styled suite (701 assertions including that example).
Standalone optional-module and CUI_ALL fixtures create a real popup, edit its
TimeField, and confirm the selected date. The packaged Python source tree omits
docs, configures and builds both native DateTime tests, and runs them through the
private-display wrapper. Consumer SDK/distribution headers are generated; language
builder/bridge omissions remain explicit above. This stays within the existing
DatePicker family; it does not add a 79th manifest entry or claim complete parity.


For standalone header implementation, emit the ordinary Core, Base, Theme and
Components implementation macros once, then `CUI_DATE_TIME_PICKER_IMPLEMENTATION`
and include `cui_date_time_picker.h`. The exact independent recipe is compiled
and executed in `tests/distribution/date_time_picker.c`; its CUI_ALL mode uses
`CUI_IMPLEMENTATION_ALL` instead. Declarations alone do not enable implementation.


## Browser gallery mode

The DatePicker story defaults to its existing date-only presentation. Enable
**Date + time** for the single civil date/time facade; only then do Include
seconds, 12-hour clock and optional clear/Delete controls appear. Configure those
controls while the popup is closed. Date-only actions are hidden during time mode
and restored when it is turned off. The current date transfers between modes;
entering time mode retains its last time, while clear restores 09:30 and precision
reduction permanently drops seconds. Time mode is single-date and discards a
range end; the gallery does not offer a date-time range control.

Launch day preserves time; Timed review replaces date/time (and truncates seconds
at minute precision). A changed day leaves the popup open for time editing;
selecting that same day confirms. Clear/Delete empties the date and resets time.
The visible date/time label follows the selected date locale and time appearance;
Time/segment names and preset labels are explicit English sample strings. The
copied complete C11 snippet reflects precision, period, clear/Delete and locale.
No timezone conversion or localization service is involved.

`tests/web/test_date_time_picker_gallery.py` uses actual headless Chromium mouse/
keyboard and CDP touch input to exercise numeric drafts across idle frames,
seconds/AM-PM, changed/same-day confirmation, timed/date-only presets, clear and
scope Delete from a time segment, disabled state, EN_US/FR and mode transfers.
It copies and strictly compiles the displayed snippets. Existing date-only
presentation/actions desktop/touch tests remain passing. This is sample/browser
host evidence, not Safari/mobile-OS keyboard/live-AT or full event-stream parity.
documents.docs/DEBUGGING.md:
# Debug a native CUI app

Start with the smallest failing frame and check the installed revision's public
headers. [Layout](LAYOUT_GUIDE.md) and [IDs/lifetimes](IDS_AND_LIFETIMES.md) explain
the contracts most often involved. The feature manifest remains the authority
for incomplete behavior across all 78 entries.

After `cui_end_frame`, inspect `cui_last_error(ui)` before rendering. Errors are
sticky: record the failure before explicitly clearing it with `cui_clear_error`.
A draw-command capacity failure returns an empty draw list so clips remain
balanced; an empty frame is not proof of a renderer failure. Check configured
element, command and string capacities rather than repeatedly clearing errors.

`cui_first_diagnostic(ui, &diagnostic)` preserves the first failure and
`cui_latest_diagnostic(ui, &diagnostic)` tracks the most recent one. Both return
whether a snapshot exists. Snapshots include error/detail, subsystem, operation, bounded message, frame sequence, implicated
ID, optional used/requested/limit counts, and a bounded outermost-box ID path
with a truncation flag. Zero counts mean unspecified. `cui_clear_error` clears
both snapshots too. `cui_set_diagnostic_callback` installs an optional callback;
copy the borrowed snapshot if retaining it, and do not reenter/mutate the context
from that callback. The library does not print diagnostics automatically.
Application/component code can report a failure with `cui_report_diagnostic`.

For geometry inspection call `cui_set_layout_debug(ui, true)` before composition.
After `cui_end_frame`, and before the next begin, export using
`cui_debug_layout_export(ui, CUI_DEBUG_LAYOUT_JSON, buffer, capacity, &required)`
or `CUI_DEBUG_LAYOUT_TEXT`. A null/zero-capacity sizing query returns false and
sets `required` including the terminating NUL; allocate that much storage and
retry. Insufficient buffers remain untouched. Export covers boxes, not individual
text nodes: IDs, parent indexes, requested dimensions, resolved bounds/clips and
resolution status help distinguish sizing from paint failures. JSON IDs are
strings so all 64 bits survive JavaScript parsing. Export performs no file I/O;
the application owns persistence and buffer allocation. Disable capture when no
longer needed; opt-in snapshots are a debugging aid, not an accessibility tree.

| Symptom | First checks |
| --- | --- |
| Content too wide or not wrapping | Parent width constraint, FIT versus grow, text-line API, font measurement |
| Missing or cut-off content | Clip ancestors, fixed height, max dimensions, capacity errors |
| Wrong row activates after reorder | Persistent row key and local ID scope; duplicates |
| First click seems ignored | Input targets exist only after a completed frame |
| Missing icon | `cui_icon_query` distinguishes unknown, catalog-not-embedded and embedded assets; inspect `CUI_ICON_NOT_FOUND`; optionally enable `debug_placeholder` |
| Missing glyph or wrong weight | Font script coverage and registered style; no universal automatic fallback |
| Native app fails before first frame | Font path, SDL3 error, pkg-config prerequisites and actual host display |

Do not use emoji as an icon fallback: font coverage and appearance vary. Use a
registered icon name, a deliberate text label, or an application-owned bitmap.
A declared optional API does not prove its implementation is in the bundle.

For a reproducible report include revision, renderer, platform, window dimensions,
font files, triggering interaction, expected result, error, and bounded capture.
Consumer captures use `--frames 3 --capture frame.bmp`. Automated native Linux
runs must use invisible Xvfb; repository validation uses
`python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir build`. Never use `DISPLAY=:0` or the
maintainer's Wayland session. Browser tests run headless. GPU hardware behavior
unsupported by the virtual display remains explicitly deferred.

The bundle host registers a diagnostic callback that writes subsystem, operation,
message, error/detail, ID, frame and capacity counters to stderr. This covers
reported Core/component failures after context creation; font and SDL setup or
render failures use their own explicit host messages. It is not a universal
warning stream for every missing asset or every optional API.

```sh
./build/native_starter --frames 1 --debug-layout text
./build/native_starter --frames 1 --debug-layout json > layout.json
```

The option prints the first completed frame once, then continues the normal
bounded or interactive run. JSON goes to stdout; diagnostics go to stderr.

## Default context budgets

Zero-valued capacity fields in `cui_config` select these defaults:

| Field | Default | Budget |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `max_elements` | 4096 | Layout/component elements |
| `max_commands` | 8192 | Draw commands |
| `frame_bytes` | 262144 (256 KiB) | Copied frame data |
| `max_resources` | 128 | Context-owned resource entries |
| `resource_bytes` | 1048576 (1 MiB) | Context-owned resource storage |

Use a diagnostic's subsystem and used/requested/limit counters to choose which
budget needs attention. Raising draw-command capacity does not repair an
unbalanced scope or duplicate ID. These are defaults for this revision, not
promises that every application fits them.

Missing-icon availability is separate from context error reporting. Read
`cui_icon_query(cui_string("clock-3"))`: the default bundle reports
`CUI_ICON_CATALOG_NOT_EMBEDDED`; a full-assets build reports `CUI_ICON_EMBEDDED`.
Check the icon call's result, and use `.debug_placeholder = true` only when a
visible development outline is useful. It retains `CUI_ICON_NOT_FOUND` and the
full accessible name. See [Icon](ICON.md) for loader and asset limits.
documents.docs/DENSITY_INTEGRATION.md:
# Native density integration

The integration merges origin/main `30ec050b` into package integration `81a7fe89`.
SDL keeps logical layout/input coordinates while painting at renderer density.
The additive scaled text APIs leave shaped geometry and caret coordinates logical.

The merge preserves the existing per-face glyph raster cache, elapsed frame timing,
idle event waits, and bounded rounded-shape rectangle submissions. Cache keys use
physical character size (`logical size * paint scale`); using logical size alone
would incorrectly reuse rasters after density changes. Rounded strips use device
row height while retaining batches of at most 128 strips.

Core, browser/WASI sources and SDK copies are unchanged from `81a7fe89`. SDK copies
must be refreshed by the integrator. Native tests use `scripts/test_local.py` and
its private Xvfb display. Hardware display migration and GPU density checks are
not established by virtual-display coverage.

Validation on Linux: strict default native build passed. Eight targeted native
CTest entries passed through the invisible-display wrapper: raster cache,
density, shaping, native text geometry, SDL appearance, password bridge, SDL
services and rounded batching. A separate `CUI_BUILD_BIDI=OFF` strict build passed
both density and raster-cache CTest entries. The density runs explicitly selected
`/usr/share/fonts/noto/NotoSans-Regular.ttf` through `CUI_TEST_FONT`; no selected
test was skipped. Density coverage exercises 1x, 1.5x, 2x, then revisits cached
sizes while checking stable logical metrics/carets and device-pixel coverage.
documents.docs/DEPENDENCIES.md:
# Dependencies

Core: C11 compiler + pinned vendored Clay (zlib). Build: CMake >=3.20, Ninja or Make; Python 3 for generation/checks. Optional native gallery: SDL3 >=3.2, FreeType and HarfBuzz via pkg-config; system font or configured font path. Optional UTF-8 processing dependency utf8proc is available but is not automatically a grapheme/bidi implementation. No GPUI/Rust/JavaScript runtime required.
Development host observations: GCC 16.2.1; SDL3 3.4.16; FreeType pkg-config 26.6.20; HarfBuzz 14.5.1; utf8proc 2.11.3. System dependencies are discovered rather than downloaded; source snapshot versions and hashes are tracked in third_party/dependencies.json. Offline core builds need no network. Native CI dependencies must be pinned where downloaded.

The optional website documentation build uses `uv run scripts/build_docs.py`,
with PEP 723 pins for markdown-it-py 4.0.0 (MIT) and mdurl 0.1.2 (MIT).
They run only during generation; published pages contain rendered HTML and
require no Markdown runtime or Python environment. Raw Markdown HTML is escaped.
Run `uv run tests/test_docs.py` to check rendering, links, assets and document coverage.

Optional bidi analysis uses vendored SheenBidi 3.0.0, commit `cfe430e7375a7845b679adae9d51dac6deaa8858`, Apache-2.0, Unicode 17. All vendored files and normative conformance fixtures have checked SHA256 pins. `CUI_BUILD_BIDI=OFF` omits the compiled `cui_bidi` library. Core never links it implicitly. The optional static library includes its backend objects, so `pkg-config --libs cui-bidi` needs no additional runtime installation. CUI wrapper/tests use the normal warning policy; four specific unused/fallthrough warnings are suppressed only for unmodified upstream. See [BIDI.md](BIDI.md) for current analysis and integration limits.
documents.docs/DESCRIPTION_LIST.md:
# Description List

`cui_description_list` composes borrowed label/value strings or custom callbacks
into horizontal or vertical rows. Items have stable nonzero IDs; duplicate IDs
and invalid dimensions reject the call before it submits layout or semantics.
There is no persistent allocation or interaction state.

The frozen GPUI Kit 0.7.1 `description_list.rs` supplies the defaults: three
columns, horizontal bordered cells, a 120px label, medium 8px/4px padding, 14px
labels at the default 16px text size, and full-width 8px separators. Small and
extra-small use 4px/2px padding; large uses 12px/6px. Unbordered lists remove cell
padding and use size-dependent spacing between rows. Label backgrounds and
foregrounds are independent theme tokens.

The headless row iterator groups spans into 1–10 columns. Zero columns select
three; zero spans normalize to one. Separators occupy isolated rows. Oversized
spans retain proportional shrink, without the upstream empty leading row edge
case. In an incomplete row, CSS flex free space is shared equally: spans 1 and 2
in four columns receive 37.5% and 62.5%, respectively. Percentage box sizing
resolves these widths in the same frame, including after a parent resize.

Set `custom_label_width` to use `label_width` (including zero), and additionally
`label_width_percent` to interpret it as a fraction of the cell. Vertical mode
ignores label width. Callbacks receive a theme copy with the appropriate text
size and color; they own their semantics. Plain content exposes passive labels
inside a group and adds no Tab stops.

`tests/unit/test_description.c` covers grouping, oversized spans, separators,
first-frame and resized fractions, all four themes/sizes/layouts/border modes,
custom content, wrapped row height, percentage labels, and invalid IDs.

Remaining parity limits: CUI currently clips the outer list to a rectangle;
rounded clip masks and independent per-cell paint clipping are not implemented.
Custom overflowing children can cross a cell boundary before reaching the outer
clip. Rich Text values use host callbacks until the complete Text component is
available. The source's inherited font weight and application-level typography
are not yet represented by this API. No browser/native visual parity claim is
made from these headless tests.
documents.docs/DESIGN_SIZES.md:
# Design sizes

Styled controls accept an appended `cui_design_size design_size`. Zero
(`CUI_DESIGN_INHERIT`) keeps their previous legacy size and custom metric behavior.
Existing zero initializers remain valid. Public structs have grown: rebuild callers
when updating the library.

The shared scale is xs, sm, base, md, lg, xl, 2xl, 3xl, 4xl, 5xl, 6xl, 7xl,
8xl and 9xl. Base and md deliberately share metrics. Explicit sizes resolve the
existing public `cui_design_measure` table, including font, line height, control
height, horizontal/vertical padding, gap and indicator size. Normal styled density
is `theme.font_size / 16`; compact density changes those metrics once.

The newly supported options are Badge, Progress (including circular Progress),
Tag, Attachment model, DropdownButton, Tabs, DescriptionList, Icon, Toolbar,
Settings, Questionnaire and Speech button/waveform. These join the previously
supported Button, check/radio/switch/toggle, Input, Textarea, NumberInput, OTP,
List, Select, Combobox, Menu and Form families.

## Geometry and composition

Explicit design size replaces legacy size-derived metrics. Caller-provided widths,
height/diameter overrides, custom boxes and artwork transforms keep their existing
precedence. Invalid enum values submit no UI and perform no input reduction or
callback. Invalid density and bounded bitmap capacity failures remain explicit
failures. All public API types remain portable C11.

A Badge sizes its count/dot/icon indicator; the application still owns its wrapped
content dimensions. Linear Progress uses one quarter of the scale control height
unless a height is supplied. Circular Progress uses the scale control height unless
a diameter is supplied; raster storage remains caller-owned and capacity-checked. The bounded circle
geometry limit is 4096 pixels; raster scale is at most four (16384-pixel extent).
Insufficient capacity rejects before touching storage or motion state.
Tag padding also accommodates the enlarged font's vertical padding. DescriptionList
labels retain their 7/8 text ratio. Attachment preserves caller card width and
media aspect; its text, glyph, height and padding follow the scale.

Toolbar presentation metrics carry the resolved design size to nested groups and
custom children. Settings' built-in field controls use the original theme plus
the explicit size, avoiding a second density multiplication. Custom render callbacks
receive the original control theme and the design size in their render options;
they must apply that size to their own child controls.

Questionnaire root options propagate size and density to composable parts. Its
`density` defaults to the root theme density, or one for standalone parts. A part
with `custom_size` keeps its explicit size choice; an explicit positive density
overrides inherited density. Custom choice views carry the design size. Speech
waveform width defaults to six font units and height to the scale control height;
explicit waveform dimensions remain authoritative.

## Gallery and Tabs

The gallery exposes the shared fourteen-size selector for these families and hides
their old four-size selectors. A named size changes submitted canvas geometry and
text; it is not a label translation. Supersized controls can require scrolling or
more application layout space.

The Tabs overflow trigger has square geometry, a centered SVG chevron and a minimum
32-pixel hit area even at compact xs. Its semantic Button is named “All tabs”.
Horizontal and vertical overflow use the existing menu, keyboard and selection
reducer. This change does not alter shared host wheel routing.

## Validation

Headless regressions compare the private Base-only table with the public resolver
through all fourteen sizes at normal, compact and doubled density, then check
actual submitted dimensions, text fonts, invalid-input atomicity and compound
propagation. `tests/web/test_design_sizes.py` runs a built gallery in real Chromium,
checks all twelve newly exposed story families and both circular Progress variants at
every size, compact density,
and both overflow axes with centered SVGs and actual menu activation.

Run the ordinary warning build and CTest, build the gallery with
`python3 scripts/build_web.py`, then use
`uv run tests/web/test_design_sizes.py --directory build/web --chromium /path/to/chrome`.
Distribution regeneration belongs to the integrator; source-only worker validation
may report the expected stale-distribution check.

# Sizes, spacing and visual styling

Use a shared scale to keep a form, toolbar and application layout consistent.
CUI values are logical pixels: a renderer's display scale maps them to physical
pixels. The component gallery lets you compare sizes, corner radii and spacing
without changing your operating system's display scale.

## Control and typography sizes

Set `design_size` on Button, Checkbox, Radio, Switch, Toggle, Input, Textarea,
List, Select, Menu, Combobox, NumberInput, Form, InputGroup or OtpInput options. Zero (`CUI_DESIGN_INHERIT`) preserves the
existing GPUI size enum and its metrics. The shared scale is opt-in; existing
applications keep their current dimensions.

| Scale | Font | Line height | Single-line control height |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| xs | 12 | 16 | 20 |
| sm | 14 | 20 | 24 |
| base / md | 16 | 24 | 32 |
| lg | 18 | 28 | 40 |
| xl | 20 | 28 | 48 |
| 2xl | 24 | 32 | 56 |
| 3xl | 30 | 36 | 64 |
| 4xl | 36 | 40 | 80 |
| 5xl | 48 | 48 | 104 |
| 6xl | 60 | 60 | 128 |
| 7xl | 72 | 72 | 152 |
| 8xl | 96 | 96 | 200 |
| 9xl | 128 | 128 | 264 |

These are CUI's explicit logical-pixel metrics, inspired by utility design
scales. `md` is an alias of `base` in this scale. Metrics multiply by the theme's
root font density (`theme.font_size / 16`). The legacy GPUI Button Large remains
32 pixels; select `CUI_DESIGN_LG` for the new 40-pixel control.

```c
cui_button_ex(ui, save_id, &theme, cui_string("Save changes"),
    (cui_button_options){.design_size = CUI_DESIGN_LG});
cui_input_ex(ui, email_id, &theme, cui_string("Email"), edit, &input_state,
    (cui_input_options){.width = 320, .design_size = CUI_DESIGN_LG});
```

Single-line controls use the listed height. Checkbox/Radio indicators use the
font size; Switch tracks add four logical pixels to that indicator size.
Textarea grows by its row count using the shared line height and padding, plus
its border. Popup query fields and option rows share the same scale.
Explicit row-height overrides still take precedence. Supply enough width for
large text; a larger size does not increase an explicitly fixed container width.

`cui_design_measure(size, density, &metrics)` returns font, line height, control
height, horizontal/vertical padding, gap and indicator size. Invalid inputs return
false without writing the output. A base Textarea receives its metrics from the
caller; its legacy `cui_textarea_measure` helper continues to measure legacy sizes.
The styled Textarea applies `design_size` before submitting its base behavior.

## Spacing and corners

`cui_space(units)` maps one unit to four logical pixels. Fractions work:
`cui_space(0.5f)` is two pixels. Use negative units for offsets, and nonnegative
units for padding and gaps.

```c
cui_begin_box(ui, card_id, (cui_box){
    .width = 360, .padding = cui_space(6), .gap = cui_space(3),
    .radius = cui_radius(CUI_RADIUS_XL, 1), .background = theme.surface
});
/* Submit card children here. */
cui_end_box(ui);
```

The radius scale is none=0, xs=2, sm=4, md=6, lg=8, xl=12, 2xl=16,
3xl=24 and full=9999 logical pixels, multiplied by the supplied density.
Renderers constrain full rounding to each shape's bounds. Set the theme's
`radius` and `radius_lg` where appropriate, or a particular box's
`radius`. Comfortable/compact theme choices remain useful starting points;
these units give you finer control over an individual layout.

## Typography

`cui_text_ex` supports normal, medium, semibold and bold weights, italic and
monospace styles, explicit font size and line height. For example:

```c
cui_text_ex(ui, cui_string("Workspace"), 24, theme.text, 32,
    (cui_text_style){.weight = CUI_TEXT_WEIGHT_SEMIBOLD});
cui_text_ex(ui, cui_string("cui_begin_frame(...)"), 14, theme.muted, 20,
    (cui_text_style){.monospace = true});
```

The host owns font selection and measurement. Configure styled measurement and
font metrics alongside drawing, so the same font faces and styles determine both
layout and pixels. See [text adapter](TEXT.md) and
[editing](EDITING.md). The website's browser font registry is a host policy;
it does not install those fonts for a native application.

## Backgrounds, opacity and motion

A box's `background` accepts RGBA color. `custom_opacity=true` and `opacity`
apply inherited draw opacity to its children as well as the box. Use
`cui_paint_bitmap` for a generated gradient or other image fill; keep its pixels
alive until rendering completes and increment its revision after changing them.
Use the portable [background effects helpers](BACKGROUNDS.md) to generate
multi-stop gradients, apply opacity or blur caller-owned RGBA pixels.
The Theme gallery applies these helpers in C before painting its bitmap panels.
A backdrop effect needs a captured image supplied by the host; generic boxes do
not capture pixels behind themselves.

Progress supports indeterminate animation with host time. Sheet supports timed
entry/exit motion through `sheet_animation_seconds`, including reduced-motion
behavior. Tabs expose an application-owned spring indicator. See
[Progress](PROGRESS.md), [surfaces](SURFACES.md) and [choices](CHOICE.md) for their
actual APIs. Animate your own state using frame time and request another frame
with `cui_invalidate`; respect `cui_reduced_motion(ui)` in the host's motion policy.

## Font families and text styles

The Theme gallery includes an interactive typography specimen with system,
sans-serif, serif and monospace families, four weights, italic and xs–9xl sizes.
These browser families are host mappings of `cui_text_style.family`; they are not
font files bundled with CUI. A native application registers its own faces and
uses the same family ID for measurement and rendering. See
[TYPOGRAPHY.md](TYPOGRAPHY.md) for a complete native program and fallback rules.

## Motion examples

TextView exposes duration, word stagger and easing controls in its preview;
Sheet demonstrates entering and leaving, and Progress offers an indeterminate
mode. Examples forward the operating system's reduced-motion preference. See
[TEXT_VIEW.md](TEXT_VIEW.md) for a complete headless motion program and
[SURFACES.md](SURFACES.md) for sheet lifetimes and deferred callbacks. Motion is
explicit state driven by host time, rather than a stylesheet or a background
thread.

# Disclosure controls

`cui_disclosure.h` provides unstyled trigger behavior and styled Accordion and
Collapsible containers. The caller owns expanded booleans. No control allocates
persistent state. Trigger IDs must remain unique and stable across frames.

```c
cui_disclosure_item sections[] = {
    {11, cui_string("Account"), false},
    {12, cui_string("Advanced"), false},
};
bool open[] = {true, false}; /* keep in application state */
cui_accordion(ui, 10, &theme, sections, 2, open,
    (cui_accordion_options){.collapsible = true, .bordered = true},
    draw_section, application);
```

`draw_section(cui_context *, size_t index, void *)` runs synchronously only for
expanded panels. It can submit any CUI children, including nested accordions.
Children of collapsed panels are omitted from rendering and focus order.
Collapsible uses the same callback shape with index zero.

Accordion supports single or multiple expanded sections, optional collapse of the
last expanded section, group and individual disabled states, and optional borders.
Click, Enter and released Space activate a trigger. Up/Down wrap among enabled
triggers; Home/End jump to the first/last enabled trigger. Arrow traversal moves
focus without opening panels. The return value reports controlled state changes.
Applications can also change the booleans themselves between frames.

The base functions submit trigger semantics without painting. Custom designs can
call them and then submit boxes with matching trigger IDs. The styled functions
use theme colors, padding, gap, radius and control height; themes provide density
and high contrast without duplicating behavior. Trigger semantics expose
expanded state and the controlled panel ID. Mounted panels expose their trigger
relationship; an Accordion group supplies a semantic parent. Native accessibility bridges are separate
unfinished infrastructure.

The implementation derives panel IDs by XORing the trigger ID with
`0x1d8f322539deca61`; Collapsible derives its outer container using
`0xb7c1c9d453922783`. Reserve those IDs when composing children. Duplicate IDs
are diagnosed by the core rather than silently reused.

`tests/unit/test_disclosure.c` exercises all four supplied themes, actual pointer
clicks, Enter and Space, disabled triggers, single/multiple expansion, required
expansion, keyboard traversal, and removal of focused hidden content. Portable
C11 and renderer-independent draw lists are supported; OS accessibility is not
claimed. Compared with GPUI Kit 0.7.1, a demonstrated native/browser gallery remain unfinished.
Immediate mount/unmount behavior is implemented. Full family parity is not yet
verified.

Set Accordion `render_header` and `header_user` to compose a custom title, icon,
badge or other header body. `cui_collapsible_ex` exposes the same callback and
optional `borderless` appearance; `cui_collapsible` retains its existing defaults.
The callback replaces the default title/indicator body, receives the current
expanded state and effective disabled item, and executes inside the themed trigger
box. The original item's label remains the accessible name. Trigger activation,
keyboard navigation and panel mounting continue to use base behavior. Callback
item pointers are borrowed only for that invocation. Headless tests verify custom
headers, semantic names, individual/group disabled propagation and actual pointer
and keyboard activation of both components.

Accordion `trigger_boxes` and `panel_boxes` are optional borrowed per-item arrays
of full `cui_box` styles; `style_count` bounds both nonnull arrays, and later
items keep the theme defaults. `cui_collapsible_ex` accepts individual
`trigger_box` and `panel_box` pointers. These override layout/paint properties
without replacing base activation or accessible names. Header focus still uses
the theme focus color and border width; explicitly masked border edges remain
a caller style decision. Tests assert distinct overridden header/panel bounds
and colors, fallback styles beyond the array and pointer toggling in both APIs.

Opt into measured reveal with a zero-initialized `cui_disclosure_motion` kept in
application state. Collapsible accepts its pointer; Accordion accepts an array
and `motion_count`, with later panels retaining immediate mount/unmount. Set
`dt` to elapsed seconds; optional positive `response` overrides the theme spring
natural period in seconds. A reversible theme-configured spring drives a clipped viewport from zero to the
full measured panel height. Initial state snaps; `reduced_motion` also snaps.
Invalid/nonpositive dt leaves progress unchanged. Measurement updates at end_frame,
so changed content sizes affect the viewport on the following frame. The motion
state and array must remain valid through end_frame and be dedicated to stable
trigger IDs; reusing a state for another ID resets it.

With motion enabled, panel callbacks also execute while collapsed to measure their
full natural layout. They must submit UI rather than perform application side
effects. Settled collapsed bodies use layout-only boxes: no paint, semantics,
events or focus. Closing bodies keep painting inside the shrinking clip but
become inert immediately when the controlled boolean becomes false. Pending
animation and changed measurement invalidate the frame. Custom panel styles
remain inside the reveal viewport. Header and controlled expanded semantics change
immediately; the return value still reports only controlled state changes.

Headless tests exercise actual pointer/keyboard expansion, measured initial hidden
content, intermediate height, reversal, closing paint with immediate focus/event
withdrawal, dynamic content size, reduced motion and bounded Accordion storage.
Styled panels use `theme.spring_control` response/damping/epsilon/travel. Natural
frequency is TAU/response, as in the reference. A zero response or false travel
snaps even at zero dt. Damping below one may overshoot; the retained spring value
keeps that trajectory while reveal height clamps to zero/full height. Settings
with invalid response/damping/epsilon use safe defaults. Tests compare differently
configured response/damping, preserve underdamped overshoot, and verify theme
travel/zero-response snap through actual trigger clicks. The public `_step_ex`
accepts the same portable policy; the original `_step` keeps critical damping and
its legacy .2-second default response. A demonstrated gallery remains unfinished.

# Disclosure applied transitions

Include `cui/cui_disclosure_events.h`. `cui_base_collapsible_events` and
`cui_collapsible_events` add a synchronous observer to the existing owned bool.
They preserve the old return in `result.changed`; `change_count` counts actual
observer calls and saturates at SIZE_MAX with `count_overflow`. A missing observer
still permits editing and ignores its user pointer.

```c
static void expanded(void *user, const cui_disclosure_change *change) {
    bool *needs_save = user; /* unrelated application state */
    *needs_save = true;
    /* Copy *change here if needed after this callback. */
}
/* During the normal UI submission: */
/* cui_collapsible_events(ui, id, theme, label, &open, options, panel, panel_user,
                         (cui_disclosure_handler){expanded, &needs_save}); */
```

Each real bool write emits CHANGE immediately afterward. Two toggles in one frame
emit twice even when the final bool equals its initial value. `previous` and
`expanded` describe applied values, never a rejectable request. Collapsible uses
item_index 0. Notification precedes final expanded semantics and Styled header,
panel and motion work; those retain their original timing. There is no notification
for animation, passive/layout-only submission, disabled input or absent observers.

Metadata targets the compound identity. When Core supplies accepted activation
evidence, it is copied before the write; `event.activation.target` retains the
original activation identity. Otherwise only actual frame/input-index/type-source
facts are copied. Presence flags define what is available; no cause is invented.
Payloads contain no borrowed strings/pointers and may be copied by value.

The callback and user pointer are borrowed for the operation. The observer must
not mutate/rebind/free expanded state, active items/motion/style storage, input or
context, recursively submit UI, or destroy resources. Unrelated flags may change.
Defer omission, removal and teardown until the outer call returns and the frame's
renderer has consumed retained resources. Existing header/panel callback contracts
remain unchanged. This C facade adds no bridge or language-binding support.

## Accordion

`cui_base_accordion_events` takes an explicit nonzero compound target;
`cui_accordion_events` uses its container ID. Item IDs and required pointers must
be valid before admission; invalid required arguments return a zero result without
calling the legacy operation. Existing unique/stable ID preconditions apply.

`item` and `item_index` identify the affected model slot. Opening in single mode
closes each true sibling in ascending index order, including a disabled-open
sibling, then opens the chosen item. Already-false writes stay silent. Each callback
sees this intermediate array; there can temporarily be no open item or several
remaining old items. No normalization occurs just because input starts multi-open.
Multiple mode only changes the chosen slot. Noncollapsible open activation is silent.

The copied activation still identifies the originating trigger, even when keyboard
navigation redirects the reducer cursor or single-open policy closes another item.
`event.target` remains the compound. Notifications precede the existing final
semantic pass: Button checked values reflect initial registration and expanded
details have not yet been finalized. Do not infer finalized semantics, panel paint
or motion from a callback. No observers run for spring updates or passive cleanup.
documents.docs/DOCK_MODEL.md:
# Retained dock tree and panel model

`cui/cui_dock.h` provides an application-owned retained model for dock trees. Leaves are ordered tab groups; interior nodes are horizontal or vertical splits. Each panel/tab item has an application-supplied stable 64-bit key, including zero. Keys are globally unique within the model. Application content, labels, icons, and platform resources remain outside the model.

Tab groups and splits have generational node IDs. IDs remain valid while their nodes survive moves and reorders; collapsed/freed nodes reject stale IDs even if their storage slots are reused. Successful restore invalidates every previous node ID. Applications can rediscover a panel's current tab group by its stable key. Generation exhaustion rejects operations requiring new nodes.

Creation preallocates two node/panel state banks. Defaults are 128 nodes, 256 panels, depth 32, and 65536 serialized bytes. Explicit supported ceilings are `CUI_DOCK_NODE_LIMIT` (4095), `CUI_DOCK_PANEL_LIMIT` (4096), depth 64, and `CUI_DOCK_SERIALIZED_LIMIT` (1048576 bytes). Counts and allocation products are checked before allocation. Operations, geometry queries, serialization, and restore allocate no additional memory. `cui_dock_memory_bytes` reports requested handle/bank storage, excluding allocator bookkeeping. The initial model is an empty root tab group.

Insert creates a panel at a tab index; `SIZE_MAX` appends. Split wraps a nonempty tab group with a new split and a new tab group containing the supplied panel. Horizontal splits divide width; vertical splits divide height. Ratio refers to the first child's share of the available span after the gap. Move transfers a panel to another group and activates it there. Reorder uses its final index in the original group and preserves its active state. Removing or moving a group's last panel removes that empty leaf and promotes its sibling, collapsing the redundant split. An empty root is retained. Active-panel removal chooses its next neighbor, or previous neighbor at the end. Duplicate keys and invalid destinations reject without changing state.

Each node may declare nonnegative minimum dimensions up to 1e9 logical pixels. Child minima combine through the tree with the requested gap. Geometry returns one rectangle per tab group, with active key and panel count. Ratios clamp to child minima when those minima fit; otherwise children compress proportionally to their minimum spans and `fit_minimum` is false. When both minima are zero, the configured ratio applies. Gaps shrink to the available span. Geometry remains within the supplied rectangle even when the minimum requirements cannot be satisfied. NULL output queries the count; insufficient output capacity leaves geometry storage untouched.

The model uses fixed arrays and scans for panel/free-slot lookup. Most mutations are O(configured capacity), while linked tab insertion/reorder includes an ordinal walk. Layout computes minima through the bounded tree and may revisit subtrees, taking O(nodes * depth) work. Restore performs bounded scans for allocation and duplicate detection and has quadratic worst-case work in the configured node/panel counts. These deliberately modest caps suit desktop docking rather than huge datasets; the separate virtual-list model handles large row collections.

Serialization is deterministic for a given topology, panel order, active selection, ratios, and minima. Format version 1 is an ASCII prefix tree:

```text
CUIDOCK 1
T min_width min_height active_ordinal panel_count panel_key...
H ratio min_width min_height first_child second_child
V ratio min_width min_height first_child second_child
```

Whitespace separates tokens; the writer emits canonical whitespace, decimal numbers with 17 significant digits, and unsigned decimal keys. Split children recursively use the same grammar. The writer normalizes locale decimal punctuation without changing process locale. The parser validates bounded ASCII decimal tokens, translates their radix to the current locale in a bounded local buffer, and delegates conversion directly to `strtod`, without changing process locale. This avoids rounding decimal digit accumulation and power-of-ten multiplication when `long double` has the same precision as `double` (including macOS ARM). Integer overflow, nonfinite values, oversized tokens/input, unsupported versions, duplicate keys, invalid active ordinals, excessive depth/capacity, incomplete trees, embedded NUL, trailing tokens, and nonroot empty groups reject. The existing 17-significant-digit format remains unchanged. Roundtrip tests require equal canonical serialization and exact restored values for ordinary, adjacent representable, and subnormal binary64 values through the platform C library conversion.

Serialization first measures required bytes, excluding the terminating NUL. A NULL output queries that length; insufficient capacity or configured byte-budget exhaustion leaves the supplied buffer untouched. Restore parses into the preallocated scratch bank and only swaps the current tree after full validation. Failed restores preserve the entire current state and IDs. Calls belong on the owning UI thread; concurrent mutation and concurrent process-locale changes during serialization are unsupported.

Tests cover nested geometry and minimum compression, tab order/active selection, move/remove collapse, stale IDs, stable keys including zero and UINT64_MAX, deterministic roundtrip, transactional parser rejection, huge/deep inputs, explicit capacity rejection, 7000 deterministic mutations with tree/panel invariants, and 2000 malformed random restore inputs under ASan/UBSan.

This model does not implement styled Dock widgets, drag/drop targeting, resizing gestures, floating native windows, focus scopes, or panel rendering. It supplies the retained tree, operations, geometry, and persistence required for a later widget layer; it does not claim full Dock component parity.

## Browser demonstration

The Dock gallery paints visible panes from the retained tree. Select Panel 1 or Panel 2 to change the active tab, then use Split panel to divide that pane. The demo supports up to eight panes; Reset layout recreates the original two-tab pane. The region count and serialized size update with the same model.

This is a composed demonstration of the existing docking model. It does not implement a public styled Dock widget, tab drag-and-drop, divider dragging, floating windows, or persistence across a browser reload. The gallery painter lives in `web/gallery.c`; the retained model's public API remains `cui/cui_dock.h`.
documents.docs/DOCK_SCHEMA_ACCESS.md:
# Dock schema accessor failures

The schema writer checks `cui_dock_node_get`, `cui_dock_panel_at` and
`cui_dock_child_at` before using their outputs. These public accessors return false
for a stale node ID, an inappropriate node kind or an unavailable index; failure
does not initialize the caller's output. The writer now returns `CUI_DOCK_INVALID`
when a required read fails instead of consuming an uninitialized key, child or
slot size. This also resolves GCC 16's optimized release warning about the panel
key without substituting a fictitious zero key or size.

Export already traverses into private scratch nodes/sizes and publishes the caller's
buffers only after valid traversal. An accessor failure preserves those buffers
and the caller's count values. A callback's edits to its live model remain its own
edits; export does not roll them back. Callbacks must keep the model alive throughout
export, and this change does not provide thread safety or a general snapshot of
arbitrary concurrent/reentrant mutations.

The regression test uses only valid public operations. A dump callback for panel 1
removes upcoming panel 2, then supplies a valid leaf state. In a tabs-only model the
next panel index is unavailable; in a split model removing the second leaf collapses
the parent and makes the next child lookup unavailable. Both exports must stop with
`CUI_DOCK_INVALID`, invoke no second dump callback, and preserve output bytes and
counts. The remaining model is serialized and restored successfully. Existing
schema JSON fixtures, round trips, version-1 persistence and model equality tests
remain unchanged and run in the same suite.

Validation uses GCC 16 release optimization with warnings treated as errors,
headless CTest through the repository's invisible-display runner, and the complete
Dock test executable under ASAN/UBSAN. Distribution and SDK copies are regenerated
by the integrator.
documents.docs/DROPDOWN_BUTTON_STYLES.md:
# DropdownButton paint refinements

Include `cui_dropdown_button_styles.h` with matching rebuilt library sources.
The independent header leaves the legacy options/state layout unchanged. NULL
or an all-zero descriptor calls the existing paint path. This slice adds paint,
not metadata forwarding, arbitrary layout, or a binding facade.

```c
#include "cui/cui_dropdown_button_styles.h"
static void action_paint(void *user, const cui_button_style_info *info,
                         const cui_button_style_paint *current,
                         cui_button_paint_patch *patch) {
    (void)user;
    (void)info;
    (void)current;
    patch->fields = CUI_BUTTON_PAINT_FOREGROUND;
    patch->paint.foreground = (cui_color){250, 240, 210, 255};
}
void draw_commands(cui_context *ui, const cui_theme *theme,
                   cui_menu_tree_state *menu, cui_id *command) {
    static const cui_menu_entry entries[] = {
        {.id = 104, .label = {"Export", 6}, .kind = CUI_MENU_ACTION}};
    const cui_dropdown_button_styles paint = {
        .paint_policy = CUI_DROPDOWN_BUTTON_PAINT_BUTTON,
        .action = {.instance = action_paint}};
    (void)cui_dropdown_button_styled_ex(
        ui, 100, 101, 102, theme, cui_string("Save"), cui_string("More commands"),
        entries, 1, command, menu,
        (cui_dropdown_button_options){.width = 120,
                                     .variant = CUI_DROPDOWN_BUTTON_PRIMARY},
        &paint);
}
```

Initialize the caller-owned menu once with `cui_menu_tree_init(menu, 103)`.
Names, menu entries, callbacks and userdata follow the existing submission and
menu ownership rules. Style descriptors are copied before reduction; callback
arguments are borrowed for the synchronous call. Callbacks must be pure: no CUI
calls, input consumption, owner/options/style mutation or reentry. Only the
output patch changes the submitted paint. The legacy body still runs once,
after the same Base/event reduction; this API does not invoke Button reduction.

Each visible half gets an independent Button-style instance callback, then its
eligible pointer/selected/disabled callback. The instance patch is captured once
and replayed after selected and disabled, including an explicit transparent
color or zero radius/opacity. Loading applies its .8 opacity after replay;
focus is last. Hidden halves have no callbacks. Invalid callback patches are
discarded atomically; accepted input remains accepted. Geometry, clip, and border
width are inspectable but cannot be patched. To replace joined corners use the
CORNERS mask, since RADIUS alone retains the existing custom corner record.

The BUTTON policy uses existing CUI palette tokens with frozen Component state
ordering. Selected/open/loading/disabled suppress pointer refinements; only the
trigger treats an open menu as selected. Ghost action held-group backgrounds
use half hover alpha (dark: quarter accent alpha). Dark ghost hover uses half
accent alpha. Outlined state wins disabled paint, including transparent special
variants. Disabled filled intents use their normal token for both background and
border; Secondary retains alpha (source opacity clamps its 1.5 multiplier to 1).
Custom transparent mixes preserve RGB and scale alpha, with CUI's existing byte
truncation. Source theme token values and sub-byte color precision differ.

LEGACY policy retains old palette/state rules with optional refinements. A
nonzero descriptor with no callbacks may still request container paint. Container
patches accept the Button mask vocabulary except FOREGROUND: there is no implicit
text cascade. Invalid policy/container patches reject before state or input
reduction. Unknown masks and nonfinite/negative radius/corners or opacity outside
0..1 are invalid. An unmasked member is ignored.

Custom shadows require BUTTON, CUSTOM, `custom_shadow=true`, and
`host_shadows_enabled=true`. Both gates default false; they do not imply a global
theme setting. Enabled halves receive `CUI_SHADOW_XS` with resolved corners;
disabled suppresses it, loading retains it. The host renderer must support CUI
shadow commands. Focus paint uses focus-visible and `theme.hide_focus_ring` in
BUTTON; LEGACY preserves the old focus rule. No full DropdownButton parity is
claimed: metadata/name/tab/toggle forwarding remains a separate slice.

Canonical builds register the styles unit test, optional compiled guide and C++
declaration check. The portable WASI runner exposes `dropdown_button_styles`
and `dropdown_button_styles_{all,legacy,styles}_distribution` suites.
Standalone users may define `CUI_DROPDOWN_BUTTON_STYLES_IMPLEMENTATION` before
including `dist/cui_dropdown_button_styles.h`; it delegates to Choice once.
The legacy `CUI_CHOICE_IMPLEMENTATION` entry also defines these additive
functions, and `CUI_IMPLEMENTATION_ALL` includes their implementation. Include
the explicit styles header for declarations. Link the remaining required CUI
modules as usual; these entry points do not create a second Button reducer.
Source SDKs include the header and implementation. Python, JS/TS, Go and Rust
builders do not expose this style facade or its borrowed callbacks.

# Bounded portable drop shadows

`cui_set_drop_shadows` copies up to eight caller-owned layers onto the open box. They paint in supplied order before its background and before its child-overflow clip, under the current ancestor mask and opacity. `count=0` clears the list. Shadow pixels add no interaction or semantics. A layer contains logical pixel offset, signed spread, Gaussian standard deviation (`sigma`), and straight RGBA8 color. Original caster corner radii clamp against the original dimensions; spread changes bounds without changing those radii. Logical bounds preserve the source offset/dilation operation order. Physical covering floors the materialized near edge, ceils its stored origin plus stored size, then clamps the far edge to the near edge. A fractional logically collapsed dimension can therefore cover one physical pixel; only empty physical covering paints nothing.

`cui_prepaint_drop_shadow` emits the same value-owned primitive. It consumes one command per layer plus existing clip wrappers. Deferred paint inherits existing viewport/modal rules and ancestor opacity exactly once. It never borrows a caller layer list or performs layout, semantics, interaction, or invalidation. Existing component/prepaint emission rollback applies; renderer preparation, external callbacks and later device submission have their existing separate failure boundaries.

`cui_theme_popover_shadows(theme,strength,out)` copies the source popover's three layers: foreground at alpha `.1`, zero offset/sigma, spread `+1`; black alpha `.1`, offset `(0,4)`, sigma `3`, spread `-1`; black alpha `.1`, offset `(0,2)`, sigma `2`, spread `-2`. Finite strength clamps to `[0,1]`; output is unchanged on invalid input. Theme projection is consumed by both styled Chart tooltip composition and current-frame paint. `NULL` tooltip style retains its legacy behavior; bare style paints neither surface nor shadows. Projected boxed style has three copied layers. `ring_color` overrides every canonical sigma-zero, spread-one, zero-offset ring; non-ring custom layers use their own color. Explicit style with zero layers retains its previous sigma-zero ring fallback. All layer values are copied into deferred payloads, including when caller options/style are destroyed or relocated.

## Kernel and supported domain

`cui_effect_drop_shadow_query`, `sample`, and `raster` use the pinned GPUI 0.3.8 f32 renderer model: rational erf for the horizontal Gaussian integral, four vertical midpoint samples, and finite three-sigma support. Sigma zero fills the rounded SDF shape with a one-physical-pixel coverage ramp beneath translucent surfaces. This differs from CUI's existing separable **box** blur. It also differs from an infinite exact mathematical Gaussian convolution; the pinned shader itself is a bounded four-sample approximation.

Query/raster accept an explicit uniform logical-to-physical scale and physical origin. Scale is `[1/65536,64]`. Caster coordinates/dimensions and radii are finite and bounded to 16384; offsets/spread to absolute 4096; sigma is `[0,256]`. To prevent f32 underflow/division from publishing NaN coverage, positive physical sigma below `4*sqrt(FLT_MIN)` is rejected atomically; sigma zero is a separate supported case. Raster dimensions are at most 16384 per side and 16 million pixels. Invalid/capacity failures leave published query/sample output and caller raster storage unchanged. Raster uses caller storage and performs no allocation.

Query `covered_layer` reports the physical integer covered unblurred layer bounds, from the same checked calculation that supplies raster geometry. The bounded scale/origin/caster domain keeps these integer edges exactly representable as floats. Physical covering floors near edges and ceils far edges. Supplied radii retain their original caster clamp through spread. Scene culling mirrors the pinned source: it tests the **unblurred** covered layer bounds against the current covered mask; a tail-only intersection paints nothing. Prepared masks crop to covered physical near/far bounds. Source pixel-grid covering can intentionally expose a full boundary pixel beyond a fractional logical mask; generic logical clip rounding or Canvas clip antialiasing must not replace that rule.

## Adapter preparation and budgets

All native adapters prepare shadow pixels/resources before clearing/submitting target paint. Software coordinates already represent physical pixels and use scale 1. SDL Renderer derives actual render scale, viewport origin and logical presentation rectangle; SDL GPU derives acquired drawable/list projection; Sokol derives physical target/list projection. Canvas uses the actual `ctx.getTransform()` scale/origin, rather than backing-store/list ratios that include canvas-dimension rounding. A shadow frame with genuinely nonuniform or unsupported transform fails before clear; frames without shadows preserve their existing transform behavior. Uniformity tolerance is four float ULPs relative to the larger positive scale.

Each native adapter owns a bounded 64-entry coverage cache. CPU shadow storage is at most 32 MiB and uploaded shadow images at most 32 MiB, for at most 64 MiB owned cached pixel storage. Public raster query's 16M pixel limit is independent: a raster too large for an adapter's available cache fails explicitly. Frame-used entries cannot be evicted by later preparation. Integer device translations and opacity changes reuse coverage; fractional phase, dimensions, sigma/spread/radii, scale and colors distinguish entries. Actual covered dimensions/position are checked before normalized translation reuse, including large-coordinate f32 cancellation. Resource creation never holds a caller stack pointer. Transient frame command copies, upload staging, C raster caller buffers and graphics-driver overhead are separately bounded by their existing/declared budgets, not included in cached pixel accounting.

SDL Renderer suspends its rounded logical clip while painting a prepared, physically cropped shadow, then restores it; target viewport remains active. SDL GPU shadow scissors use actual target bounds and prepared physical crop. Ordinary draws keep their existing clip path. On predictable GPU preflight failure no swapchain is acquired. The separate lifecycle hotfix handles unavoidable post-acquisition resize races legally: it submits a blit of the previous completed offscreen surface when available. It never cancels an acquired swapchain. A first frame without a previous surface and device submission failure cannot promise unchanged presentation.

## Canvas host wiring

`web/modules/cui_shadow.js` exports `createCuiShadowRenderer` and `cuiShadowWasmRasterizer`. `web/modules/cui_shadow_bridge.c` is the standalone bridge/example schema for the existing pure C kernel; it is not automatically linked into applications. The gallery links this bridge, copies each shadow value command, preflights all rasters before either resizing or clearing its Canvas, and suspends ordinary fractional clips while drawing the prepared physical masks.

The host decodes commands to `{type:'shadow',values:[caster x,y,w,h; original radii TL,TR,BL,BR; offset x,y,sigma,spread; R,G,B,A]}`, clip commands to `{type:'clipPush',bounds:[x,y,w,h]}`/`{type:'clipPop'}`, and other commands to `{type:'other'}`. All 16 values are copied. Call `renderer.prepare(commands,ctx,logicalWidth,logicalHeight)` **before** clearing the target; errors leave target pixels unchanged. The checked C query and raster provider returns copied metadata and borrowed pixels used only synchronously during preparation. WASM memory views are recreated after each call to tolerate memory growth.

At each shadow command, suspend the host's generic Canvas clip stack, call `prepared.draw(index,ctx,{unclipped:true})`, then reapply that stack for subsequent ordinary commands. Prepared physical mask cropping owns shadow clipping; inherited `ctx.clip()` would antialias fractional boundaries incorrectly. The explicit flag documents this host responsibility; Canvas cannot inspect or reset an arbitrary caller clip stack itself. Prepared frames expire on the next `prepare` or `clear`; expired draws reject, and their retained pixel references are released even if a host keeps the old frame object. `draw` rejects transform changes after preparation. It performs no clear. Ordinary commands remain the host's responsibility and preserve their paint order. Cache clear/destruction releases module-owned references; Canvas/browser/driver resource retirement is managed by the browser.

Bridge exports are `cui_canvas_shadow_values` (pointer to16 writable floats), `cui_canvas_shadow_query`, `cui_canvas_shadow_prepare`, `cui_canvas_shadow_width`, `cui_canvas_shadow_height`, `cui_canvas_shadow_bound(index)`, `cui_canvas_shadow_layer_bound(index)` (physical unblurred bounds), `cui_canvas_shadow_pixels`. Query/prepare return 0 on failure and 1 on success. Pixels are straight RGBA8; copied metadata bounds are logical placement, widths/heights physical raster dimensions. The bridge's single reusable raster buffer is borrowed until its next prepare call and capped to 32 MiB. The renderer copies it synchronously into an offscreen Canvas; caller stack buffers are never retained.

## Verification scope

Headless tests compare the pinned four-sample model against independent exact rectangle Gaussian CDF, and exercise symmetry/cutoff, sigma-zero corners, signed spread, subnormal rejection, finite cancellation, atomic output, copied layers, source order/opacity, child overflow, tail-only exclusion and bounded frame/cache failure. Actual native SDL Renderer/Vulkan/Sokol readback and Chromium WASM tests cover both physical scales 1/2 and all three layers beneath translucent surfaces. Existing appearance proof retains both consumers, automatic/copied content, bare behavior, line boxes, corner geometry, progress/ancestor opacity and stationary move/resize.

Exact pinned native Metal/WGPU shader antialiasing/color-format image identity is not certified by these portable kernel and adapter tests. Public inset shadows, arbitrary nonuniform transforms, renderer-specific color spaces, and native GPUI image captures remain outside this bounded drop-shadow slice. No full BoxShadow or Chart family completion is claimed.

The covering regression fixture pins the dependency archive and geometry/window source hashes in `tests/unit/shadow_covering_source.json`. Tests cover high-origin f32 far-edge rounding, fractional negative-spread and zero-size covering, real Core node emission, Software pixels, cache reuse and unblurred-mask culling. SDL Renderer pre-Present readback, SDL GPU readback, Sokol GL readback and Canvas WASM probe each verify the formerly missing fractional pixel at uniform scales 1 and 2. These establish portable geometry and compositing behavior, not native GPUI shader AA identity. Inset shadows remain unsupported.
