# Go builders for the CUI bridge

For installable local wheel, npm, Go module and Rust crate artifacts, see the
[packaging guide](PACKAGING.md). Linux alpha packages are tested outside the
checkout; registry publication and other platform packages remain pending.

`bindings/go` is a cgo Go module for the portable CUI bridge ABI v1. Its builders cover the native bridge node kinds through Settings, from layout, controls, and overlays to data views and navigation; the sections below specify each implemented surface and its limits. Builders create a detached tree; `App.Mount` validates it and creates actual CUI nodes. `Step` submits the frame, `QueuePointer` and `QueueKey` send synthetic input, and `Dispatch` invokes Go callbacks after the native frame. Change events carry state and copied text captured when queued. Bridge node coverage does not imply full feature parity with the 78-component manifest.

Requires Go 1.23 or newer, a C11 compiler, CMake, Ninja, `CGO_ENABLED=1`, and a built CUI bridge shared library. On Linux, build and test from the repository root:

```sh
cmake -S bindings/bridge -B build-go-bridge -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS='-Wall -Wextra -Werror'
cmake --build build-go-bridge --target cui_bridge test_bridge_core test_bridge_components
python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir build-go-bridge -- -R '^bridge_'
cd bindings/go
CUI_BRIDGE_LIBRARY="$PWD/../../build-go-bridge/libcui_bridge.so" go test ./...
```

The Go package loads `CUI_BRIDGE_LIBRARY` at runtime with `dlopen` on POSIX or UTF-8 decoding and `LoadLibraryW` on Windows, verifies the ABI version and options size, and calls the C bridge through a small cgo shim. `go test` itself uses the headless backend and opens no window. The library path must be absolute (`.so` on Linux, `.dylib` on macOS, `.dll` on Windows). The first loaded bridge remains active for the process lifetime. Linux has been validated. The loader has POSIX and Windows branches; Windows cross compilation with Zig/MinGW succeeds; Windows runtime and macOS remain unvalidated.

Example native application, from `bindings/go`:

```sh
CUI_BRIDGE_LIBRARY="$PWD/../../build-go-bridge/libcui_bridge.so" \
CUI_TEST_FONT=/absolute/path/to/font.ttf \
go run ./examples/save_changes
```

The native example opens an SDL window and uses an existing TTF font. A finite native smoke check is available as `go run ./examples/native_smoke` inside Xvfb. For automated native checks on Linux, run it only inside an invisible Xvfb display; never point tests at the desktop display. For example: `xvfb-run -a env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY CUI_TEST_FONT=/absolute/path/to/font.ttf CUI_BRIDGE_LIBRARY=/absolute/path/to/libcui_bridge.so go run ./examples/native_smoke`. The bridge reports unavailable SDL or font failures directly.

For SDL glyph coverage, `Options.FontFallbacks` takes up to 32 absolute UTF-8 TTF paths, or call `App.SetFontFallbacks(paths)` to replace or clear the chain. Font loading is transactional: a failed replacement leaves the previous chain active. Font fallbacks require the native SDL backend. The finite smoke example installs its primary font as a fallback to exercise this API.

```go
app, err := cui.New(cui.Options{})
if err != nil { panic(err) }
defer app.Close()
status := cui.Label("Ready").Key("status")
button := cui.Button("save").Text("Save").Size(cui.MD)
button.OnClick(func(cui.Event) { _ = status.SetText("Saved ✓") })
err = app.Mount(cui.Column("root").GapUnits(2).Children(status, button))
if err != nil { panic(err) }
_ = app.Step(1.0/60)
```

`New` locks its goroutine to an OS thread. Call all methods for that app, including `Close`, on that same goroutine; `Close` unlocks it. Until the core's process-global Clay context is synchronized, callers must also serialize calls across separate apps, even when they use different OS threads. Go callbacks execute during `Dispatch`, outside C. Callback panics propagate as ordinary Go panics. Keep a reference to every app and close it explicitly. Strings are copied into C and limited to valid UTF-8, no NUL, and 4096 bytes. Handles are app scoped and rejected after removal or disposal. Gap values are logical pixels; `GapUnits(2)` equals eight pixels. Button design sizes span `Inherit`, `XS` through `Size9XL`. `Checked`, `Value`, `Range`, `Open`, and `Selected` configure selection, disclosure, and numeric components; `QueueText` sends host text input to the focused Input or Textarea. Hover colors use the bridge's existing palette mapping, and ghost custom hover remains unsupported by the bridge.

Grouped components use `Item` children. RadioGroup, Tabs, Select, and ComboBox expose a selected Item; Tabs and Accordion Item children form their panels. `Event.Selected` is a copied full handle snapshot for group changes. `Alert` takes title and message. Collapsible and Accordion Item state is available through `App.Checked`.

Select uses a name and placeholder; ComboBox uses a label and editable query. Their options are `Item` children. `App.Text(combo)` reads the current query.

DropdownButton has separate action and menu areas. Use `App.DropdownPartBounds(button, false)` for the action and `true` for the menu. `OnClick` receives action presses; `OnChange` receives selected `Item` snapshots from menu choices.

Dialog, AlertDialog, Sheet, and Popover have `Open` state and `OnClose` callbacks. `Event.CloseResult` reports accepted, cancelled, or closed. Popover requires `Anchor` with a live node before opening. Dialog, Sheet, and Popover children render inside their surfaces; AlertDialog uses its title and description.

Tooltip and HoverCard follow their anchor on pointer hover. Both require `Anchor`; HoverCard may contain child content. `App.Open` reads their hover state, and `OnChange` receives open/close snapshots.

Visual builders map to native CUI renderers. `VisualSize(width, height)` applies to Avatar, EmptyView, GroupBox, Skeleton, and Spinner, within 0–4096 logical pixels. Avatar and Spinner currently use the width; their height remains renderer-defined. GroupBox accepts children; EmptyView takes a title and description.

List, Menu, and Stepper use `Item` children and selected Item snapshots. Stepper Items accept `StepStatus(0..3)` and a detail description. Pagination and Rating expose `Total` and `Value`; `NumericPartBounds` locates a numbered native interaction part for host input and tests.

DescriptionList uses `Item(label).Detail(value)` children. Scrollable accepts children, `VisualSize` for its viewport, and `ScrollExtent` for content dimensions. `QueueScroll` sends host wheel input; `App.Value(scroll)` returns the vertical offset, with each change captured in `OnChange`.

StatusBar, Toolbar, and TitleBar use `Item` children. StatusBar Item `StepStatus(0/1/2)` chooses left/center/right. Toolbar Items may contain controls; disabling the Toolbar suppresses their actions. TitleBar Items render text labels and do not expose host window controls.

Icon takes a catalog name such as `check` and optional `VisualSize`; an unknown name is reported at `Step`. Message renders one filled message body with an optional header and configurable width. A failed mount removes its partial native tree, so a corrected tree can be mounted on the same app.

Attachment renders native status and progress metadata from a title, description, `AttachmentStatus`, `Value(0..1)`, and optional visual width. This bridge surface does not expose file transfer, remove, or retry actions.

Image accepts decoded RGBA8 pixels with `RGBA(pixels, width, height, stride)` and optional display `VisualSize`. Go copies the input immediately; the bridge copies it again for rendering, so callers may reuse their byte slice. Dimensions must be 1–2048 pixels, stride at least four bytes per pixel, and the exact buffer at most 16 MiB. `SetRGBA` replaces pixels on a mounted image. File decoding remains the application's responsibility.

Tree accepts up to 64 flat `Item` children in preorder. `Item.Depth(0..63)` sets indentation and `Item.Checked(true)` starts an item expanded. `Tree.Selected(item)` chooses an Item; `App.Selected(tree)` and `App.Checked(item)` read live state. `Tree.OnChange` receives selection snapshots from pointer or keyboard input. `VisualSize` sets the tree viewport; disabling Tree suppresses interaction.

TimeField renders an editable 24-hour `HH:MM:SS` value. Configure it with `Time(Time{Hour, Minute, Second})`, update it with `SetTime`, and read it with `App.Time`. Each native edit emits `OnChange` with a copied eight-character `Event.Text` snapshot; disabling the field suppresses edits.

ColorPicker accepts packed `0xRRGGBBAA` with `ColorRGBA`, updates via `SetColorRGBA`, and reads via `App.ColorRGBA`. `App.ColorPartBounds(picker, 1/2/3)` locates the hue, color plane, or alpha part for host input. Native changes emit `OnChange` with the exact packed value in `Event.Value` and a copied `#RRGGBBAA` string in `Event.Text`.

Calendar and DatePicker use a validated `Date{Year, Month, Day}`. Set one with `Date`, update with `SetDate`, and query with `App.Date`. `App.CalendarDayBounds` locates a visible day for pointer input. DatePicker can be opened or closed with `Open` and sized by width with `VisualSize`. Native selections emit `OnChange` with numeric `YYYYMMDD` in `Event.Value` and copied `YYYY-MM-DD` in `Event.Text`. The current bridge uses English single-date mode.

OTPInput uses `Total(1..256)` for its target cell count (default six), `Text` or `SetText` for its current value, and `App.Text` to read live edits. Queued text input to a focused OTPInput emits `OnChange` with a copied text snapshot. Configure `Total` before `Text`; changing `Total` on a mounted input resets its value.

Form accepts up to 64 `Item` children. Each Item's text and detail become a field label and description, and its children render as the field controls. `Form.VisualSize(width, 0)` sets its width. Disabling either the Form or an Item suppresses descendant control input. The bridge does not supply form validation or nested Forms.

InputGroup combines an editable value with `Item` button addons. Set its placeholder with `Detail`, width with `VisualSize`, initial value with `Text`, and read edits with `App.Text` or copied `OnChange` snapshots. Each addon may use `StepStatus(0..3)` for inline start/end or block start/end and `OnClick` for its native action. Disabling the group suppresses editor and addon input.

Notification creates one retained in-app card from a title and message. `Open(true)` presents it; `App.Open` reads its state. `OnClick` receives a card press, and `OnClose` receives its completed close transition. The bridge does not deliver OS notifications or provide action buttons or automatic hiding.

FocusTrap contains arbitrary child nodes. `Open(true)` activates a native modal focus scope that blocks pointer interaction outside its subtree; `Open(false)` restores ordinary input. `App.Open` reads its live state. It does not create a visual dialog surface by itself.

MessageScroller accepts up to 64 `Item` children. Item text is the message body, `Detail` is the sender, and `StepStatus(0/1)` selects incoming or outgoing. `VisualSize` sets the viewport. After the first `Step`, `App.Value(scroller)` reads the live vertical offset and `SetOffset` changes it; `OnChange` receives native offset changes. The initial frame follows the newest message.

Carousel accepts up to 64 `Item` slides with text or child content. `VisualSize` sets the viewport, `Selected(item)` changes the slide, and `App.Selected` reads it. Native wheel, drag, and keyboard navigation emit `OnChange` with a full selected Item handle snapshot. The bridge currently uses horizontal orientation and does not support nested Carousels.

Resizable accepts up to 64 `Item` panels in a horizontal split. Set an Item's initial width with `PanelSize(100..4096)`, read its live width with `App.Value(item)`, and locate a divider with `App.ResizableHandleBounds(group, precedingItem)`. Dragging a divider emits `OnChange` on the resized Item with numeric `Event.Value`. `VisualSize` configures the group and `Disabled(true)` suppresses dragging.

TextView renders owned Markdown (default), HTML, or plain source. Use `Format(Markdown/HTML/Plain)`, `Text` or `SetText`, and `VisualSize`. `App.SelectText(view, anchor, cursor)` selects rendered UTF-8 byte offsets; `App.CopySelection(view)` returns plain selected text. Pointer selection emits `OnChange` with a copied selected-text snapshot. Disabled TextView suppresses pointer selection.

Editor owns a multiline UTF-8 buffer. `Editor(key, source, language)` sets initial text and language metadata; `VisualSize` sets its viewport. `App.Text` reads live content and `OnChange` receives copied text snapshots. The current bridge limits content to 4096 bytes and 512 lines and does not expose completion, syntax callbacks, search, or clipboard actions.

Chart renders caller-supplied `ChartDatum{Label, Value}` data as line, area, bar, or pie via `ChartKind`; `Data` and `SetData` copy at most 64 points into native storage. `App.ChartDatum` reads a copied point back. Labels are valid UTF-8 up to 128 bytes, values are finite and within ±1e9, and pie values must be nonnegative. `VisualSize` sets its dimensions. The bridge draws a native raster with hover feedback and a "No data" empty state; it does not fetch data.

Table is a compositional native table: its `Item` children are rows, and each row's `Item` children are text cells. The first row renders as a header. `VisualSize(width, 0)` sets its width; cell `SetText` updates the next frame. Sorting, selection, and virtualization belong to DataTable rather than this basic Table.

DataTable uses `TableData(headers, rows)` or `SetTable` with 1–16 columns and up to 32 rows; every cell and header is valid UTF-8 up to 128 bytes. Go and the bridge copy the matrix. `SelectionMode(SelectRows/SelectColumns/SelectCells)` chooses native row, column, or cell selection. `App.DataTableCell`, `DataTableCellBounds`, `DataTableHeaderBounds`, and `DataTableState` expose live data and hit targets. Native selection and header presses emit `OnChange`; `DataTableState` reports one-based selected row/column and sort column/direction. Sorting is a signal: the application must reorder and re-supply its rows.

DataTable `OnChange` also includes a copied JSON `Event.Text` snapshot with `reason`, `row`, `column`, `sortColumn`, and `sortDirection`. Parse that payload when a callback needs the exact queued transition rather than a later live state.

Plot accepts up to 256 finite `PlotPoint{X, Y}` values within ±16384 via `Points` or `SetPoints`; Go and the bridge copy the points. `App.PlotPoint` reads one point and `VisualSize` sets the viewport. The native plot currently draws themed dots; axes, paths, and hit interactions are not exposed.

Command accepts up to 64 `Item` actions. Item text is the label and `Detail` supplies one filter keyword; `Command.Text` or `SetText` changes the query, and `App.Text` reads it. `App.CommandItemBounds` locates a visible action for pointer input. Native filtering and keyboard navigation update `App.Selected(command)` and emit `OnChange`; an Item's `OnClick` receives confirmation. Grouped/custom rows and host action execution are application responsibilities.

Sidebar accepts up to 64 `Item` navigation actions. `Open` controls the collapsed state, `VisualSize` sets its size, and `App.Selected(sidebar)` reads the active Item. A native press emits a Sidebar `OnChange` event with an exact `Event.Selected` snapshot and an Item `OnClick` event. Disabled Items do not activate.

`App.ThemePresets()` lists names from the loaded bridge. `SetThemePreset(index)` applies one to subsequent frames, and `ThemePreset()` returns the selected index plus a `bool` indicating whether an explicit preset was chosen. The default theme has no selected preset index.

`RootView(key)` can be mounted as the sole root container. It renders child widgets in the native root surface; `RootPadding(0..256)` sets its content padding before or after mounting. Row and Column roots remain available.

SDL apps expose the system clipboard with `SetClipboard(text)` and `Clipboard()`. Text is copied, valid UTF-8 without NUL, and limited to 64 KiB. Headless apps return a backend-unavailable error. The native smoke example checks small, empty, and exact 64 KiB Unicode SDL round trips under invisible Xvfb.

Speech renders a native speech button and retains a transcript. The host supplies recognition results through `StartSpeech`, `ReportSpeech(text, finalPhrase)`, and `FinishSpeech`; `SpeechTranscript` reads the current copied text. `OnChange` snapshots start, report, and finish transitions in `Event.Value` (0, 1, 2), with copied transcript text. The bridge does not capture microphone audio or run speech recognition. Reports are valid UTF-8 up to 4096 bytes.

Questionnaire accepts 1–16 `Item` questions, each with `Item` choices, up to 256 choices total. Configure question flags with `Item.Question(required, multiple)` before the first frame. `QuestionnaireState` returns the current question and completion flag; `ChoiceSelected`, `NextQuestion`, `PreviousQuestion`, and `SubmitQuestionnaire` expose native state/navigation. Submit rejects unanswered required questions, emits one completion event on the first successful call, and emits a submit event on each successful call. `OnChange` carries copied JSON in `Event.Text`: `event`, `item`, `current`, `complete`, and one-based `selected` choice indices. The schema freezes after its first frame; this bridge surface does not support dynamic question/choice edits.

Dock accepts up to 64 `Item` panels, whose child widgets render as panel content. `VisualSize` sets its viewport; after the first frame, `ActiveDockPanel`, `ActivateDockPanel`, `DockPanelBounds`, and `MoveDockSplit(panel, reference, DockHorizontal/DockVertical, ratio, before)` access the native model. `SerializeDock` returns a copied model string for inspection. Activating a panel emits `OnChange` with a full `Event.Selected` handle. Panel schema freezes after the first frame; serialized-model restore and drag docking are not exposed by this bridge API.

Settings contains up to eight `Item` pages, each with up to eight `Item` groups, containing Switch, Checkbox, Input, or NumberInput fields. Totals are limited to 32 groups and 128 fields, with at most 16 fields per group. Page/group text supplies headings; boolean field text supplies its title, while Input and NumberInput use `Detail(title)` so `Text` can hold the editable value. `Query(text)` filters native navigation using up to 256 UTF-8 bytes. After the first frame, `SettingsPage`, `SetSettingsPage`, `SettingsFieldBounds`, and `ResetSettingsPage` access native page and field state; page `OnChange` carries an exact selected handle and field changes use their existing copied event values. Reset restores values captured at first render and emits field changes. Page/group topology and titles freeze after that frame; only individual fields support `Disabled`. The bridge does not provide host persistence or custom fields.

VirtualList accepts up to 64 keyed `Item` rows with fixed 32-pixel height and an overscanned viewport. `VisualSize` sets its viewport, `Value` sets a vertical offset, and `App.Value` reads the live offset. `App.VirtualListItemBounds` returns bounds only for a visible row. Native wheel and keyboard scroll emit `OnChange` with the offset; disabling the list suppresses scrolling.

The composed workspace example lives at `bindings/go/examples/workspace`. From `bindings/go`, run `CUI_BRIDGE_LIBRARY=/absolute/path/to/libcui_bridge.so go run ./examples/workspace --headless` to validate native hit targets, Account/Preferences tab navigation, name editing, notifications checkbox, an older birthday, save dialog, and status update without opening a window. To use the SDL UI, run `CUI_BRIDGE_LIBRARY=/absolute/path/to/libcui_bridge.so go run ./examples/workspace --font /absolute/path/to/font.ttf`. Automated SDL runs on Linux must use invisible Xvfb, for example `xvfb-run -a env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY CUI_BRIDGE_LIBRARY=/absolute/path/to/libcui_bridge.so go run ./examples/workspace --font /absolute/path/to/font.ttf`; native mode remains open until the user closes its window.

## Packaged build-time CUI bridge

The canonical module path is `github.com/mattmezza/cui/bindings/go`. Linux cgo
builds compile separate CUI translation units from the tracked SDK and statically
link the bridge by default. `go build -tags cui_native` adds SDL3, FreeType and
HarfBuzz through pkg-config; portable builds open no window. A copied executable
needs no CUI checkout or runtime compiler, while native system libraries and a
font remain required.

Explicit `Options.Library` or `CUI_BRIDGE_LIBRARY` still selects a shared bridge.
The optional `cui_dynamic` build tag uses packaged shared-library discovery and
its verified cache. See [local artifact install commands](PACKAGING.md) for
source-only module ZIPs, optional prebuilt modules, and release/tag limitations.

# HoverCard desktop and tap policy

Include `cui/cui_hover_card_extended.h`. This additive C API combines explicit
tap-toggle policy, bounded outside taps and optional semantic relationships.
Existing HoverCard/Tooltip functions retain their behavior, including global
Escape dismissal for consumed, repeated and modified Escape. There is no new
input dispatcher, Core schema, AT adapter or foreign binding API.

Submit the trigger first. Pass its actual Button return value as
`accepted_trigger_activation`; the extension trusts this application assertion
and does not rescan consumed trigger events. A false assertion means no toggle.
Do not substitute pointer-up coordinates, raw focus or a queued activation request.
Keyboard/accessibility activation accepted by that trigger can toggle too.

Choose `CUI_HOVER_CARD_TAP_TOGGLE` explicitly for touch/mobile behavior. Hover,
focus and delays do not open or close this mode. One accepted trigger assertion
sets open to the inverse of entry open; outside release is applied first and the
trigger assertion uses that frozen entry value. Disabled or global Escape closes
last. Placement can subsequently close for invalid geometry. A zero/NULL policy
retains the existing desktop reducer and placement. No platform is auto-detected.

Keep a zero-initialized `cui_hover_card_contact` next to the caller-owned
`cui_hover_state`. Submit at most once each frame. Reset the workspace when the
context is recreated; neither structure owns callbacks or input pointers. Mode
change, frame omission, closed model and protected/frame-zero work discard a
pending contact. Do not share one workspace across simultaneous cards.

When `outside_tap` is enabled, the workspace must be provided. A primary down
outside both previous valid card and trigger bounds arms one contact identified
by type, device and contact ID. A matching unconsumed primary up outside both
regions closes only when movement stayed below eight logical pixels. Movement
at the threshold, even followed by a return to origin, cancels the pending tap.
Include displacement at release. Consumed matching input, cancellation, scroll
or gesture takeover cancels it. Unknown bounds, unmatched release and secondary
buttons never close. Ambiguous simultaneous contacts disable outside dismissal
until explicit workspace reset, card close or matching/global cancellation.
No event is consumed and no outside pointer capture is installed.

A child click retains the card. A press inside followed by a drag outside also
retains it. This is intentionally stricter than the frozen upstream mouse-up-out
handler, which does not require an outside press or a movement threshold. It
supports ordinary outside taps without claiming every host gesture or full
mobile parity. Modal permission uses existing Core policy; geometry and modal
checks do not establish exclusive ownership among unrelated overlays. Call the
helper after relevant leaf consumers; later consumption cannot undo an already
applied decision.

Enable `relationship` only when this card owns the submitted trigger's
`controls`/`expanded` fields. The extension copies all other semantic details.
An admitted panel sets controls to its ID and expanded true; rejection/closed
sets controls zero and expanded false. This reflects composition admission, not
only `state.open`: resource rejection may leave the model open. Missing current
trigger semantics yields `relationship_applied=false`; no node is fabricated.
The card retains its GROUP role, explicit name and parent=trigger. Tooltip
description behavior stays unchanged. Omission does not patch caller semantics.

Only `result.lifecycle.control_result` determines whether to compose children
and call the existing `cui_end_hover_card`, exactly once. The lifecycle result
uses existing observer meaning: changed is a final model transition independent
of handler; change_count counts actual callbacks. Callback runs after final
relationship work and before arbitrary children, with UNKNOWN source and genuine
eligible frame only. No input index, activation evidence, dismiss cause, veto,
completed visibility or physical AT announcement is claimed. Copy the payload
to retain it. Do not mutate/reenter the active model or input/options from its
callback; handlers are borrowed only for the call. Inert/layout-only work keeps
maintenance but emits no callback or relationship patch.

Core semantic snapshots can prove controls/expanded and preserved details. The
current AccessKit adapter emits expanded false for TREEITEM, but not ordinary
buttons, so explicit collapsed AT state remains unsupported by this slice.
Live screen-reader announcements, arbitrary overlay ownership, raw outside
mouse-up semantics and Python/Node/TypeScript/Go/Rust exposure remain separate.

The compiling headless example is
[`examples/hover_card_extended/main.c`](../examples/hover_card_extended/main.c).

# Hover model-open observers

Include `cui/cui_hover_events.h` for `cui_hover_update_events`. This additive pure
Base adapter preserves `cui_hover_update` and all its parameters, state and timing.
It observes actual model-open transitions for shared HoverCard/Tooltip policy.
It does not report painted visibility, rendered geometry, animation completion,
input acceptance or controlled requests. Styled `cui_tooltip_events` and
`cui_begin_hover_card_events` add final-model observation around existing
composition; see below and the [checkpoint](design/LIFECYCLE_RESULT_EVENTS_SLICE.md).

```c
#include <cui/cui_hover_events.h>

typedef struct { bool details_open; } model;
static void open_changed(void *user, const cui_hover_lifecycle_event *event) {
    model *app = user;
    app->details_open = event->open; /* Copyable notification, no acceptance return. */
}

cui_hover_event_result update_details(cui_hover_state *hover, model *app,
                                    bool trigger_hovered, bool content_hovered,
                                    bool focused, bool escape, bool disabled, float dt) {
    return cui_hover_update_events(90, hover, trigger_hovered, content_hovered,
        focused, escape, disabled, dt, .3f, .2f,
        (cui_hover_handler){open_changed, app});
}
```

The application owns persistent `cui_hover_state`; the function owns no context,
clock or listener. Supply timing and boolean facts as with the old pure reducer.
Do not call this and the old reducer on the same state/timestep merely to inspect
both results: that advances policy twice. Omission does not advance timers or
invoke a late callback. Multiple calls advance according to their supplied dt;
there is no implicit once-per-frame guard.

`valid` requires a nonzero metadata target and nonnull state. Invalid arguments
return a zero result before any state/callback work. Other parameters keep legacy
policy: finite positive dt advances elapsed, invalid/nonpositive dt does not;
nonfinite or negative delay becomes zero. `control_result` is the exact legacy
bool (entry open differs from final open), not successful submission. The explicit
`changed` flag independently records the same entry/final comparison even without
a handler; it is distinct from Styled composition admission. Pending,
target, elapsed or suppression-only changes are not open transitions.

One actual open transition invokes the optional handler once, after reduction,
with frozen `previous_open` and `open`. `change_count` counts actual observer calls,
zero or one; `count_overflow` is always false. Missing handler preserves ordinary
state mutation and `control_result`, with count zero and `changed` still observable. Reading a result does not
invoke another observer. Callback does not veto or confirm the state change.

Disabled pure policy closes an open state and may notify. Escape closes and
suppresses reopening until trigger/focus/content facts are absent. This function
has no UI ancestry or routing: disabled closing is a model transition, not accepted
user input; it cannot identify inert/layout-only frames or promise UI callback
suppression. The Styled adapters handle those boundaries separately, below.

Payload metadata is LIFECYCLE with the supplied target and UNKNOWN source. All
presence flags are clear: no context/frame/index/activation/reason is inferred
from policy booleans. The metadata target is application-selected stable identity,
not a new ID allocator. The pointer-free payload can be copied beyond callback and
state lifetime; it does not retain state, context or application resources.

Handler, user and payload pointers are borrowed only through the call. No handler
is retained while a delay is pending. The callback can update unrelated owner
state, but must not mutate the active hover state, recursively run its reducer,
free active storage or unwind a foreign exception through C. Defer active-resource
teardown until the call returns. No runtime lifetime/reentrancy guard is added.

Tests prove explicit delay/reversal/content-hold/close/suppression/reentry/focus/
disabled sequences, missing handlers and repeated-state counts; compare all state
fields and legacy bool across 576 combinations/steps with finite, negative, NaN
and infinite timing/delays; verify invalid target/null-state atomicity, metadata
absence and copied payload after state deallocation. Strict C11 Release/C++ header
and ASan/UBSan checks run alongside existing content regressions through the private
test wrapper. Sanitizer validation uses prebuilt instrumented Core/software archives,
not a new full-project sanitizer build.

No Focus Trap, virtual-window completion,
MessageScroller, bridge producer or language callback is added. Existing binding
notification allowlists remain unchanged. This is a bounded model observation
slice, not full-family or uniform coverage of all 78 manifest families.

The explicit `changed` field extends the unreleased event-result layout. Rebuild
consumers rather than mixing earlier objects; no legacy result/layout changed.

## Styled Tooltip and HoverCard

```c
cui_hover_event_result tooltip = cui_tooltip_events(
    ui, tooltip_id, theme, &tooltip_state, cui_string("Help"), options,
    (cui_hover_handler){open_changed, app});
(void)tooltip;

cui_hover_event_result card = cui_begin_hover_card_events(
    ui, card_id, theme, &card_state, cui_string("Details"), card_options,
    (cui_hover_handler){open_changed, app});
if (card.control_result) {
    /* Arbitrary child controls/content keep their own event contracts. */
    cui_end_hover_card(ui); /* Existing end, exactly once on true admission. */
}
```

Both functions call their legacy counterpart once, then compare the final model.
`control_result` is the exact old Tooltip bool or HoverCard begin admission;
`changed` independently compares entry/final open state, even without a handler.
`valid` requires nonnull context/theme/state and nonzero ID, not successful
geometry, resources, paint or full-frame completion. Invalid arguments reject
before model work. Missing observers preserve state/composition with count zero.
Callback count remains zero/one and overflow false.

Placement can force the model closed after delayed policy opens it. Closed→open→
forced-closed within one call is net-zero and silent. Conversely intrinsic card
measurement resource failure can return false with the model open: `changed=true`,
`control_result=false` and one OPEN model notification are valid. The callback does
not claim that a portal was composed or displayed. Never condition HoverCard end
on `changed` or callback count; pair only on `control_result`.

Notification follows the complete legacy Tooltip call or the legacy HoverCard
begin decision, **before arbitrary HoverCard children**. It is not a deferred end
callback. Do not call the new Base observer internally/on the same state first;
that would advance delay twice. Original content, placement, measurement redraw,
trigger description, child semantics and end balancing remain unchanged.

Styled metadata has only HAS_FRAME with the genuine nonzero local frame sequence;
UNKNOWN source, no source-presence/index/activation/reason. Delays, focus, geometry
fallback and several inputs may contribute. Frame-zero inert/layout-only/protected
work keeps legacy maintenance and `changed` results but suppresses observers.
Calling UI composition from protected measurement is still unsupported: the
adapter does not hide the old lifecycle diagnostic or grant permission to do it.

Legacy Escape policy scans globally without filtering consumed/repeated/modified
keys. This adapter preserves it rather than changing routing. Trigger focus opens;
HoverCard can hold open for panel hover/contained child focus, Tooltip cannot.
Omission does not close model state or retain handlers for a later close.
The original hover-state/options/text and arbitrary child storage obligations
remain; users/payloads are callback-borrowed, not retained during pending delay or
measurement redraw. Do not mutate active hover/trigger/input/options, recursively
compose, free active resources or destroy the context during callbacks.

Styled tests compare old/new paint command geometry/colors/text size, panel bounds,
state and semantics; prove pointer delay, contained child focus, global consumed
repeat Escape, disable close, missing handlers, omission, viewport/anchor fallback,
resource-capacity failure, inert/layout-only maintenance, protected-measurement
suppression with unchanged legacy diagnostic, and copied payload lifetime.
Strict Release and ASan/UBSan private-wrapper runs include Base and legacy content
regressions; sanitizer checks reuse instrumented Core/software archives. No actual
visibility/presentation, retained listener, bridge producer or foreign callback is
claimed.

# Icon

Icon renders named, host-loaded or raw SVG as a monochrome antialiased mask through
CUI's portable RGBA bitmap draw path. It is decorative by default: it contributes layout and
paint without a focus stop or pointer target. A nonempty `accessible_name` opts
into a noninteractive image semantic; `decorative = true` suppresses that name.

```c
#include "cui/cui_icon.h"

cui_icon_state check = {0};
cui_icon_set_name(&check, cui_string("check"), NULL, NULL);
/* Inside a frame, with a unique id and an existing theme: */
cui_icon(ui, 42, &theme, &check, (cui_icon_options){.size = CUI_ICON_MEDIUM});
/* After the renderer has consumed the returned draw list: */
cui_icon_state_collect(&check);
/* After the final draw list has finished rendering: */
cui_icon_state_destroy(&check);
```

Use one caller-owned state per widget. A zero-initialized state is ready to use;
`cui_icon_state_init` also initializes fresh storage. Do not copy an initialized
state or initialize it again without destroying it. State operations are not
thread-safe. Setters copy path/raw source bytes and replace the previous source.
`cui_icon_set_empty` retains the requested layout but paints nothing.

## Sources and assets

`cui_icon_set_name` accepts catalog names such as `check`;
`cui_icon_set_path` accepts paths such as `icons/check.svg` or host-specific paths.
An optional loader runs on the next preparation and again after
`cui_icon_reload`. Its returned SVG bytes must remain valid until preparation
returns. Returning false tries the embedded bundle. CUI performs no implicit
filesystem or network access. Raw data uses `cui_icon_set_data`.

The complete 1,830-name/path catalog remains available through
`cui_icon_catalog_*`. The default build embeds the 106 frozen upstream defaults plus 17 application essentials
from the same pinned archive (126 SVGs total). These include media controls `skip-back`, `skip-forward`, `gauge`, plus `pencil`, `pen-line`,
`funnel`, `archive`, `trash`, `mail`, `mail-open`, `paperclip`, `send`, `reply`,
`reply-all`, `forward`, `download`, `upload`, `link`, `log-out`, and `check-check`.
`filter`, `trash-2`, and `more-vertical` are accepted aliases for `funnel`, `trash`,
and `ellipsis-vertical`, including their `icons/*.svg` path spellings. Aliases do
not add catalog entries. Define `CUI_ICON_ALL_ASSETS=1` when compiling the implementation to embed all
1,830; other catalog paths require a host loader in the default build.
`cui_icon_asset` returns a borrowed static SVG string when embedded.

Query `cui_icon_query(name_or_path)` before selecting artwork:

| Result | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `CUI_ICON_UNKNOWN` | No catalog entry matches |
| `CUI_ICON_CATALOG_NOT_EMBEDDED` | Known name/path, SVG omitted from this build |
| `CUI_ICON_EMBEDDED` | SVG is embedded in this build |

The query accepts catalog names, paths and the aliases above. It reports build
assets, not whether an application loader can supply an SVG. For example,
`clock-3` is known but is not embedded in the default build. Handle the
`CUI_ICON_NOT_FOUND` result explicitly or supply a loader.

For development, opt into `.debug_placeholder = true` in `cui_icon_options`.
A missing named or state-backed icon then paints an outline inside its allocated
box, preserving `CUI_ICON_NOT_FOUND` and the decorative/named semantic contract.
The outline respects tint and custom opacity; it does not replace arbitrary SVG
parse errors. Default behavior remains no placeholder. Do not use emoji as a
fallback: font coverage and appearance vary.


`scripts/icon_assets.py` regenerates the bundle offline from the pinned JSON
catalog in `third_party/gpui_icons`; `--check` verifies reproducibility. Generated
assets retain the Lucide ISC, Feather MIT and upstream Apache notices. The private
NanoSVG parser/rasterizer is pinned and unmodified under its Zlib license.
Its external symbols use a CUI prefix, so an application may link its own
NanoSVG implementation in a separate translation unit. Implementation macros
introduced by CUI are removed afterward. Including both implementations in the
same translation unit is unsupported because their private types and static
functions share names.

Built-in artwork can be replaced across a theme by assigning `theme.icon_loader`
and `theme.icon_loader_user`. The callback receives a canonical path such as
`icons/close.svg` or `icons/chevron-down.svg`; return your SVG bytes and `true`
to replace it, or `false` to use the bundled default. `cui_icon_named` and
`cui_icon_spinner` use this provider, including the component controls that call
them. Increment `theme.icon_revision` when artwork changes without changing the
callback or user pointer. Cached masks otherwise survive ordinary redraws.
The theme is borrowed during rendering; its provider user data must stay valid
while the application uses that theme. SVG colors become a monochrome alpha
mask, tinted with the control's semantic foreground color.

## Size, color and transforms

Zero options inherit `theme.font_size` and `theme.text`. Hosts with their own text
scopes can supply `inherited_text_size` and `custom_inherited_color`/
`inherited_color`. General automatic text-style scope inheritance is not yet
provided by the core.

XS, S, M and L are 12, 14, 16 and 24 pixels at a 16-pixel theme font size, scaled by
`theme.font_size / 16` to represent source rem units. Custom size is an unscaled
pixel square. With inherited size, `custom_width`/`custom_height` enable independent
layout dimensions, including zero; an unspecified dimension becomes zero when the
other is explicit. An explicit preset or custom size overrides those dimensions.

SVG aspect ratio is scaled from the requested width and centered within the layout
height. Rotation or a center-relative affine transform changes paint bounds while
leaving layout unchanged, and may paint outside the icon's box subject to ancestor
clipping. `cui_icon_rotation` returns a replacement transform in radians.

SVG RGB colors are discarded; shape alpha becomes the mask. `custom_color` uses an
explicit tint, and `custom_opacity` clamps an independent paint opacity to [0, 1].
Changing tint or opacity reuses the raster. Source content, dimensions and affine
transform select raster cache entries. The counters in state expose parsing and
rasterization for diagnostics.

## Draw lifetimes and bounds

Preparation retains immutable masks: changing a source, size or transform does not
invalidate bitmap pointers already borrowed by a draw list. Call
`cui_icon_state_collect` only after **all** earlier draw lists using that state have
finished rendering. It frees retired masks and retains the active mask. Destruction
has the same renderer-completion requirement. Collection after each rendered frame
keeps steady-state memory small. Reusing one state for several icons in a frame is
supported, but consumes additional retained cache entries until collection.

`cui_icon_prepare` also works without a UI context. After it returns `CUI_ICON_OK`,
`cui_icon_state_bitmap` and `cui_icon_state_paint_bounds` expose the current borrowed
raster and relative paint bounds. Empty or singular transforms produce no bitmap.
After an error, do not paint a previously exposed bitmap as the new source.

Default limits are 256 KiB SVG input, 1,048,576 pixels per raster, 8 MiB retained mask
bytes and 16 retained versions. `cui_icon_set_limits` accepts smaller or bounded
larger limits; zero fields use defaults. Dimensions and raster sides are capped at
4,096 pixels, paths at 4,096 bytes, SVG dimensions/coordinates at 1,000,000, shapes
at 4,096 and total path points at 65,536. Affine coefficients and translation are
also bounded. Exhaustion returns `CUI_ICON_LIMIT`; allocation failure returns
`CUI_ICON_ALLOCATION`. Borrowed masks are never silently evicted to satisfy a new
request. Collect completed draws or increase the configured budget before retrying.

## SVG coverage and remaining differences

This implementation uses NanoSVG's supported SVG subset, rather than upstream
resvg. It supports the frozen catalog's paths, fills, strokes and opacity, including
tiny round-cap dots. It does not promise full SVG/CSS, text, filter, external image
or resvg feature parity. The parser is permissive for unsupported constructs;
resource checks bound accepted inputs and geometry but are not a complete XML
validator. DOCTYPE/entity declarations and embedded NUL bytes are rejected. Vendor
internal allocation failures may appear as parse failures or missing geometry;
explicit CUI buffer allocation failures are reported separately.

Headless tests inspect actual alpha geometry, aspect positioning, affine overflow,
size precedence, tint/opacity cache reuse, host reload/fallback, source replacement
and borrowed draw lifetimes. Both default and full-catalog configurations parse and
rasterize every embedded asset. Build-system, amalgamation and adapter wiring are
maintained by the integrator.

## Context-owned convenience icons

`cui_icon_named(ui, id, theme, name_or_path, options)` uses a bounded context
resource instead of caller-owned state. Equivalent name/path spellings retain the
same source and raster. `cui_icon_spinner` renders Loader with a repeating
0.8-second quadratic ease-in-out rotation; zero options use Medium size. Its clock
starts on first appearance and resets after absence for a complete frame. The
spinner overrides the paint transform, retains layout dimensions and requests
redraw while active. Host reduced motion makes it static and stops those requests.

Convenience resources use a 1 MiB/four-version raster cache budget per widget,
subject to the context's resource count and payload budget. Finish rendering before
`cui_begin_frame`: that call collects retired masks and eventually destroys omitted
widgets. Context destruction releases all caches. Source/raster preparation errors
are returned; context resource exhaustion also reports `CUI_ERROR_CAPACITY`.

## Handling missing icons

Check the result of `cui_icon_named` or `cui_icon`: `CUI_ICON_NOT_FOUND` means
no host SVG or embedded asset was available; no icon is painted. A successful
`cui_icon_set_name` only selects a catalog source and does not guarantee that its
SVG is embedded. Check `cui_icon_prepare` (or the widget call) as well. For example:

```c
cui_icon_error error = cui_icon_named(ui, 42, &theme, cui_string("mail"),
                                      (cui_icon_options){0});
if (error != CUI_ICON_OK) {
    /* Application policy: log error, report it in debug UI, or paint a fallback. */
}
```

Use `cui_icon_catalog_default` to inspect the default bundle, provide a theme
loader for other names, or enable the full bundle. CUI does not print diagnostics
implicitly; applications retain control of logging and fallback presentation.

## Numeric box styling

Use `options.style` for uniform/per-edge padding, borders, backgrounds, radius,
opacity and clipping. Padding does **not** inset SVG paint: the frozen GPUI SVG
paints its full final border-box bounds. Numeric width/height constraints apply
before a final minimum of the padding-plus-border sums. For example, a 16px Icon
with 24px padding on each edge occupies and paints a 48px square. Padding 4px
leaves that same 16px Icon's size and paint unchanged.

```c
cui_box style = {.padding = 4, .max_width = 32};
cui_icon_constraints limits = {
    .custom_min_width = true, .min_width = 20,
    .custom_max_height = true, .max_height = 0,
};
cui_icon_options options = {
    .size = CUI_ICON_MEDIUM, .rem_size = 16,
    .style = &style, .constraints = &limits,
};
/* During an active frame; state is retained until draw lists finish rendering. */
cui_icon_error error = cui_icon(ui, id, &theme, &state, options);
```

The explicit zero height maximum above is finally floored to the 8px vertical
padding sum. Descriptor flags distinguish explicit zero from an unset constraint.
Enabled descriptor maxima replace the corresponding positive legacy style caps;
minimum constraints win if larger than a maximum. Explicit preset/custom Icon
size overrides dimension options first, then constraints apply. Selected edge
values and enabled constraints must be finite [0,4096], and final dimensions
must not exceed 4096. Invalid numeric styling rejects before resource preparation.
Style/constraint pointers are synchronous and never retained.

Transforms change only SVG paint, around the resolved box center. Backgrounds,
layout, hit bounds and opt-in named image semantics remain untransformed. Parent
clipping and opacity continue to apply. You may submit one caller-owned Icon
state repeatedly with different sizes/colors/transforms in the same frame:
immutable raster versions remain valid together until renderer consumption.
Collect only afterward. The context-owned named cache accepts the same canonical
aliases as `cui_icon_set_name`, `cui_icon_query` and `cui_icon_asset`.

The gallery's **Icon box styling** control demonstrates padding and numeric caps
inside the existing Icon family. This batch does not add generic Styled margins,
flex/grid/percentage constraints, automatic ambient text inheritance, full resvg
features or a native raster-density key. DPR browser checks establish portable
bitmap presentation, not density-aware native Icon rasterization. These remaining
gaps preclude a full-family parity claim.

# Icon accessibility and source audit

Frozen reference: GPUI Kit commit
`87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`,
`crates/component/src/icon.rs`.

The reference Icon itself declares no accessible name, role, focus or input
behavior. Existing CUI icons remain decorative by default. CUI adds an optional
`accessible_name` application label: a nonempty label submits a noninteractive
`CUI_ROLE_IMAGE` semantic with the icon's layout bounds, no focus and no Tab stop.
`decorative=true` suppresses that semantic, including when a name was supplied.
Asset names, paths, SVG title elements and raw SVG bytes are never used as labels.
An empty source may still be intentionally labeled; its semantic uses layout
bounds although it paints no SVG. Parent inert/layout-only behavior remains Core's.

The audit covered all reference branches:

- Legacy and full-catalog names convert to an Icon path; entity view constructors
  build the same source. CUI retains catalog/path APIs and context-owned named cache.
- Default/empty path, path replacing data and data replacing path are handled by
  existing owned source state. Data is copied; masks are immutable across source
  replacements until collection after renderer completion. CUI does not expose
  Rust Entity or Arc cloning; initialized state must not be copied.
- `same_layout` excludes source/color/transform. CUI layout uses the resolved
  numeric border-box size; transformation changes absolute paint bounds rather than semantic size.
- `into_svg` inherits text size unless either style dimension exists; explicit
  size replaces both dimensions. Existing width/height/custom flags preserve
  these rules, including an explicit zero and a missing opposite dimension.
- Presets use .75/.875/1/1.5 rem. New positive `rem_size` separates rem metrics
  from inherited text size; zero keeps legacy theme-font-based preset scaling.
  Custom pixels, inherited text size, dimension overrides and design metrics retain
  their existing precedence. Explicit size wins over style dimensions.
- Explicit text color overrides fallback. RenderOnce falls back to inherited text
  color; entity Render falls back to theme foreground. CUI's existing
  `custom_inherited_color` bridges RenderOnce scopes; omitting it selects theme
  foreground as the entity branch does. `custom_color` wins over both. SVG masks
  are tinted with this current color; the supported parser does not preserve a
  multicolor SVG palette.
- Rotation and affine transformation replace one another via options. Existing
  center-relative transforms preserve layout and allow paint overflow.
- Source `Styled` accepts generic refinements. New optional `style` supports Core
  box decoration (background, border, radius, clip, opacity, inert/layout-only,
  offsets), while explicit icon dimensions remain authoritative. Uniform or per-edge padding participates in the border-box sizing floor.
  SVG paint covers the complete resulting bounds, without a content inset. This does not reproduce arbitrary GPUI flex properties, margins, every
  SVG feature or automatic ambient style inheritance. Callers supply inherited
  metrics/colors explicitly; no global ambient style stack is introduced.

Validation of the new fields occurs before state preparation, cache allocation,
layout or semantics. Decorative labels are ignored entirely, so they need not
carry valid text. Nondecorative nonempty labels require a valid borrowed pointer.
Core copies the label into frame storage; the `style` pointer is synchronous and
not retained. Existing opacity normalization and source parser errors keep their
legacy behavior.

`tests/unit/test_icon_accessibility_source.c` checks actual draw tint/background,
layout and semantic dimensions, color precedence, independent rem presets,
explicit sizing priority, label privacy/decorative suppression, pointer/focus
ineligibility, invalid preflight atomicity and owned custom-SVG replacement
lifecycle. Existing icon tests cover catalog assets, raster geometry, affine
transforms, parser limits, explicit-zero dimensions and loader caching. The
the new test is registered in CMake and generated distribution headers include the API.

## Numeric styled bounds

`cui_icon_options.constraints` optionally supplies `cui_icon_constraints` with
explicit per-axis minimum and maximum flags. Zero is a valid explicit maximum.
Unset descriptor maxima use positive `style.max_width`/`max_height`; zero legacy
style caps remain unbounded. Minimum constraints win over maxima, then sums of
padding and border edges floor the resulting axes. A cap smaller than the
padding/border sum therefore does not shrink the final box below that sum.
Explicit Icon size still replaces both style dimensions before constraints.

The resolver runs before parsing/rasterization or semantics. It accepts finite
nonnegative enabled constraints/selected padding/border edges up to 4096 and
rejects a resulting dimension above 4096. Descriptor and style pointers are
borrowed synchronously. These numeric constraints do not imply percentage, flex,
grid, margin or automatic ambient style support.

`tests/unit/test_icon_style_source.c` covers padding/border floors, numeric caps,
explicit zero and conflicting min/max, full-box paint, unchanged named semantic
bounds, aliases and immutable simultaneous raster versions from one caller-owned
state. `tests/web/test_icon_style.py` compiles the assertion-enabled contract into
a dedicated real-WASM fixture and checks visible software-rendered SVG pixels,
clipping and named semantics at desktop/390 and DPR1/2. This is not a proof of
resvg equivalence or density-aware native SVG rasterization.

# IDs and lifetimes

The declarations and comments in `include/cui/cui.h` are authoritative. Layout,
semantics and interaction share stable application identity across frames.
Nonzero layout IDs must be unique within a frame; semantic IDs must also be
unique. A semantic control normally owns the box with its matching ID. Zero is
an anonymous layout ID, not an interactive identity. Duplicate public IDs and
collisions in the internal layout ID mapping report errors.

For repeated rows, scope by a persistent record key, not its display position:

```c
if (cui_push_id(ui, message_key)) {
    cui_begin_box(ui, cui_id_from(ui, "row"), (cui_box){.width = -1});
    /* Submit this record's children using local keys such as "subject". */
    cui_end_box(ui);
    cui_pop_id(ui);
}
```

Keep `message_key` distinct for each record. Reordering records then preserves
identity. Generating an ID does not open an ID scope; nesting boxes does not
replace explicit scoping. Balance only successful `cui_push_id` calls.

| Data | Required lifetime |
| --- | --- |
| Application values, editable buffers, controlled models | Across frames while used; application owns them |
| Submitted text and semantic names | Copied into bounded frame storage during submission |
| Draw list and semantic snapshot | Borrowed until the next `cui_begin_frame`; render/read first |
| Bitmap pixel data | Borrowed until renderer completion; update its revision when changing cached content |
| Callback user data | Alive whenever the callback can run; follow each component's contract |
| Font and host/context objects | Font alive during measurement/rendering; destroy in reverse ownership order |

Queue host events before beginning the frame. Interaction targets and bounds
queried during submission come from the previous completed frame; the first
frame has no targets. Completed semantics describe current layout. Render the
completed draw list before beginning another frame. Do not retain pointers into
frame strings or snapshots as durable app state. Component models and optional
resource/session APIs have additional ownership rules in their public headers.

# IME composition

CUI supports a reusable single-selection composition session for Input, Textarea,
Editor and Questionnaire input controls. Native SDL and the web gallery transport
preedit updates, the selected preedit range, commit and cancellation. Preedit is
rendered with an underline and selected range; it does not modify the edit document
or emit document-change callbacks until commit. Commit is one undo step when edit
history is enabled. Cancellation leaves document, original selection and history
intact. Starting composition separates typing groups on either side.

## Public byte offsets and bounded ownership

`CUI_EVENT_COMPOSITION_START`, `UPDATE`, `COMMIT` and `CANCEL` use `text_data` and
`text_length` for arbitrary-length UTF-8 within configured bounds. Legacy inline
`text[64]` remains available. `composition_anchor` and `composition_cursor` are
UTF-8 byte offsets in preedit, not offsets in the document. They must lie on scalar
boundaries. `cui_queue_event` deep copies payload bytes before returning; caller
storage can immediately be changed or released. Dispatched payloads remain valid
until the next `cui_begin_frame`, including while queuing that next frame.
`cui_config.event_text_bytes` bounds aggregate queued bytes (zero defaults to
65536). Queue overflow/allocation failure returns false and reports
`CUI_ERROR_CAPACITY`, without partially enqueueing an event.

`cui_edit_composition_event` uses a caller-owned `cui_edit_composition` with separate
preedit and rendered snapshot buffers. Buffers must remain alive and disjoint from
the model and session. Set `buffer`/`capacity`, `view_buffer`/`view_capacity`, and
zero the remaining fields before first use. Capacities include a trailing NUL.
Attach its pointer to `cui_input_state.behavior.composition` or
`cui_textarea_state.composition` (Editor uses `editor.view`). Leave
`composition_owned` false for caller-owned storage.

Built-in controls lazily allocate a retained default resource when composition
first arrives, bounded to 4095 preedit bytes. Styled Input, Textarea, Editor and
Questionnaire enable `grow_view`: their edit model privately owns rendered storage
sized from the actual document plus preedit and grows geometrically when needed.
There is no 65535-byte document limit for these built-in consumers. Growth is
bounded by the model's configured document capacity plus bounded preedit capacity;
overflow or allocation failure returns `CUI_EDIT_CAPACITY` before changing the
previous visible preedit or document. Snapshots are built only on successful
composition updates; idle view reads reuse the existing snapshot.

The default UI resource remains included in `resource_bytes`; dynamic rendered
storage is owned by the edit model and freed by `cui_edit_destroy`, independently
of UI resource collection. Its borrowed view is valid until the next composition
update/growth or model destruction. The session's original `view_buffer` remains
caller/UI-resource owned and never points at freed model storage. A retained
session rebound to a replacement model discards its old active composition.
Keep session and preedit buffers alive during use, and do not use borrowed views
after model destruction. Caller-owned sessions retain their explicit fixed
rendered-buffer bound unless they opt into `grow_view`; this flag also allows an
initially null rendered buffer. Applications needing larger preedit must attach
appropriately sized caller buffers. Fixed rendered capacity failure likewise
preserves composition and document. No adapter truncates text to 63 bytes.
A reusable headless consumer can call `cui_edit_composition_view` and
`cui_edit_composition_selection` to paint the temporary document and caret.

`composition_target` optionally identifies the originating focused control; the
core drops stale host updates/commits addressed to another focus. SDL captures
this owner and rejects text input between window focus loss and regain; the
browser rejects composition commits after a canceled session. Untagged manually
queued events use the current focus.

Read-only, disabled, unfocused and removed controls cancel their session. External
document revision or selection changes invalidate the old replacement range.
Keys and ordinary text events yield while composition is active. Pointer selection
cancels preedit before moving the document selection. Multiple active selections
reject composition with `CUI_EDIT_INVALID_ARGUMENT`; CUI does not claim multi-cursor
IME parity. Token annotations and folds are temporarily excluded from preedit layout;
committing retains the model's normal atomic token replacement policies.

## Host adapters and validation

`cui_set_text_input_rect` / `cui_text_input_rect` expose the last painted focused
caret in logical pixels. SDL polling forwards this rectangle to
`SDL_SetTextInputArea`; browser input positions its native textarea at this caret.
SDL `TEXT_EDITING` selection offsets are Unicode scalar counts: the pinned SDL
source converts Cocoa UTF-16 to UTF-32 counts and Wayland byte positions with
`SDL_utf8strnlen`. CUI converts those counts to UTF-8 bytes. Provenance:
[SDL Cocoa keyboard](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/blob/7f3ae3d57459e59943a4ecfefc8f6277ec6bf540/src/video/cocoa/SDL_cocoakeyboard.m),
[SDL Wayland events](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/blob/7f3ae3d57459e59943a4ecfefc8f6277ec6bf540/src/video/wayland/SDL_waylandevents.c).
The browser bridge converts native textarea UTF-16 selection offsets to UTF-8
bytes, commits `compositionend` once and excludes composing key shortcuts.
The host receives the preceding frame's caret rectangle; candidate presentation
and virtual keyboard behavior remain browser/OS dependent.

Numeric uses an optional `cui_number_state.composition` caller session or a lazy
UI-owned default with 4095 preedit bytes and model-owned rendered storage. It
renders arbitrary valid preedit without changing the numeric draft/value. Commit
uses the existing normalization (ASCII plus the already-supported fullwidth
digits/signs/decimal point and ideographic decimal point), existing prefix grammar
and 127-byte draft bound. Invalid commit leaves the previous preedit and draft
intact. One successful composition commit is one edit history transaction;
Ctrl/Meta-Z, Shift-Z and Y support Undo/Redo. Existing Enter/blur clamping remains
in effect. Read-only/disabled/focus loss and controlled-source or edit-model
replacement cancel composition, and stale commits remain suppressed until a new
start/update. Caller sessions keep the reusable edit-session lifetime rules above.

OTP uses `cui_otp_state.composition`, optionally pointing to a zero-initialized
caller-owned `cui_otp_composition` with `buffer`/`capacity` (including NUL). Keep
both alive and disjoint from the OTP value/state during use. Otherwise it lazily
retains a UI-owned default with 4095 preedit bytes, accounted in `resource_bytes`.
The default pointer is internal to the UI resource lifetime; do not dereference
it after UI destruction or retain it outside the widget state. Each frame renews
the resource, so omitted-widget collection cannot leave a dereferenced old
resource. Caller-owned sessions and buffers remain caller-owned.

OTP deliberately preserves its existing first-scalar filtering: only the first
ASCII or fullwidth digit in a commit is normalized and appended. Trailing scalars
are ignored (`"34"` appends `3`, `"2x"` appends `2`); an invalid first scalar
(`"x3"`) is ignored. Multi-digit composition commits are therefore limited to one
digit, as in the pinned reference `crates/base/src/otp_input.rs`, `edit_value`
(`chars().next()`). Preedit paints only the first eligible proposed scalar in the
next cell; masked preedit reuses the existing `*` rendering and never draws raw
preedit digits. Selected ranges use UTF-8 byte boundaries; the cell caret is
clamped to that proposed scalar and published for the host candidate rectangle.
Full OTP targets ignore further input. Buffer exhaustion reports `CUI_EDIT_CAPACITY`
before any append/callback and preserves preedit. A successful append reports one
change and, when it fills the target, one completion. OTP has no Undo history.
Cancel, disabled/focus loss, and document pointer/length/content fingerprint
changes discard preedit without modifying the value. Normal composing shortcuts
yield; stale commits after source replacement or a successful commit are ignored
until the next start/update. OTP has no read-only option.

Reference behavior was inspected in the frozen GPUI source
`crates/base/src/input/base/state.rs` (`marked_text_range`, `unmark_text`,
`replace_text_in_range`, `replace_and_mark_text_in_range`). GPUI may mutate marked
text transactionally; CUI's explicit virtual snapshot keeps document mutation at
commit. This is substantive single-selection input support, not full SDK parity
with surrounding-text reconversion, platform replacement ranges or candidate UI.

Headless unit tests cover Unicode/emoji ranges, queue deep-copy lifetime, bounded
failure, large caller buffers, cancellation, external drift, single undo and
multiple-selection rejection. Large-document tests cover more than 200000 bytes,
owned allocation growth, idle reuse, scrolling, commit/Undo and model rebinding. `tests/web/test_ime.py` uses Chromium CDP native
`Input.imeSetComposition` and `Input.insertText` for all four text consumers;
it also checks read-only and blur/disabled cancellation.
`tests/web/test_ime_additional.py` covers Numeric/OTP/Combobox through real CDP
composition, Numeric Undo, masked OTP first-scalar commit, cancel and disable.
Native headless Numeric/OTP tests cover filtering, trailing payload, callback
counts, caller capacity, source replacement and stale-focus rejection. SDL injected preedit
checks scalar-to-byte conversion with an emoji and an accented scalar. Linux and
Chromium are exercised here; macOS/Windows native IME UI remains unverified.

# Additional text consumer IME audit

Audited source: `b6fbb70`, isolated branch `audit/ime-additional`. The initial audit
added no implementation changes; the follow-up below records the scoped fix. The existing four-consumer IME test does not
establish IME support for Numeric or OTP.

| Consumer | Browser native composition | Commit/cancel | Candidate caret | Disabled/read-only |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Numeric (`NumberInput`) | Focus reaches the bridge; preedit is missing | Composing `57` leaves initial value `42`; cancel preserves it | Available from input painting | Disabling releases the bridge and preserves value; read-only source policy only |
| OTP (`OtpInput`) | Focus reaches the bridge; preedit is missing | Composing `7` leaves digit count zero; cancel preserves it | Missing (`gallery_ime_rect(0) == -1`) | Disabling releases the bridge and preserves value; no read-only option |
| Combobox | Preedit `ap` appears without changing query | Commit produces two query bytes exactly once; cancel preserves query; one Undo restores empty query | Available | Disabling active composition preserves query and releases the bridge; no read-only option |

These results use Chromium's `Input.imeSetComposition` and `Input.insertText`,
which dispatch real DOM composition events to the focused host textarea. The
script records native start/update/end events, including nonempty commit and
empty cancellation. It does not fabricate CUI mode flags or DOM composition
objects. Tests select Numeric's existing draft before committing a different
value, avoiding a false pass when initial and committed values match. OTP uses
one ASCII digit so the failure cannot be explained by unsupported nonnumeric
characters. The Combobox check exercises the single-selection gallery story;
multiselect and large-query capacity are not established by this audit.

Run the strict regression with an existing gallery build and installed Chromium:

```sh
uv run tests/web/test_ime_additional.py --directory /tmp/cui-next16-integration/build/web \
  --chromium /home/matteo/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1228/chrome-linux64/chrome
```

The observed result is **five failed requirements**, collected before exit status
1: Numeric preedit and commit; OTP preedit, caret and commit. Combobox's checked
requirements pass. Cancel and disabled-state checks pass, but do not prove a
working composition session for consumers that ignored its creation. Browser
runtime errors were absent. The failures intentionally remain strict assertions
for future fixes; this script is not registered as a passing CTest check.

## Source findings and native implications

* `src/base/cui_numeric.c`, `cui_base_number_input`, handles `CUI_EVENT_TEXT`
  and keyboard editing directly. It neither creates a composition session nor
  reduces composition events. It reads the legacy inline text array rather than
  the variable payload. Its existing numeric grammar, draft/controlled-value
  transition and Enter/blur commit behavior need an explicit composition policy.
  Numeric's `readonly` option blocks its editing loop and stepping; the gallery
  does not expose that option, so this audit makes no browser read-only claim.
* `src/base/cui_otp.c`, `cui_base_otp`, handles only ordinary text and Backspace.
  The ordinary-text branch converts one accepted digit per event from the inline
  text array. Composition events are ignored. OTP also lacks a model composition
  session and candidate caret publication. A future commit path must define how
  multiple digits, capacity and completion callbacks are processed atomically;
  this audit does not infer those policies from ordinary typing.
* `src/base/cui_choice.c`, `cui_choice_reduce_combobox`, delegates query editing
  to `cui_base_input_ex` with retained `query_behavior`. The default composition
  session is therefore available. `src/components/cui_choice.c`,
  `cui_choice_paint_query`, passes that behavior to `cui_input_paint`, which renders
  preedit and publishes the caret. Filtering uses the committed query, preserving
  document/query semantics during preedit. The base-created default retains its
  fixed rendered buffer; it does not opt into the new styled Input default's
  dynamic snapshot sizing. This audit does not claim large-query support.
* `backends/sdl3/cui_sdl3.c` converts active SDL text editing into composition
  update/cancel, and the following SDL text input into composition commit. Numeric
  and OTP's shared reducer omissions therefore also affect native SDL IME input.
  Native SDL injection was not added in this two-new-file audit scope; this is a
  source-supported implication, not a measured platform IME result.
* `web/gallery.js`, `syncImeTarget`, enables the native bridge for every focused,
  enabled semantic textbox. Bridge focus alone does not imply that its CUI
  consumer handles composition. Numeric and OTP are concrete examples.

OTP and Combobox public options have no read-only field. Disabled controls were
checked through the existing gallery control. Numeric read-only coverage requires
a dedicated host fixture or an authorized gallery option addition.

## Validation

Fresh portable warning build succeeded without warnings. Full native CTest ran
90 checks: 89 passed; only `distribution` failed because the base's generated
headers are stale. Distribution regeneration belongs to the integrator and was
not performed in this audit. The strict browser audit fails for the five product
gaps above. Only this document and `tests/web/test_ime_additional.py` were changed.

## Scoped Numeric/OTP follow-up

The isolated implementation branch starts at `46d7010`. Numeric now retains an
edit composition session, renders it through existing input painting, normalizes
commit through existing Numeric filtering and groups it into one Undo transaction.
OTP now retains bounded preedit, paints the first eligible proposed scalar using
its existing mask, publishes the focused cell caret and consumes composition
commit. Source/focus/disabled changes cancel; Numeric also cancels for read-only.
OTP retains the pinned reference's first-scalar policy: trailing scalars ignored,
invalid first scalar ignored, full target ignored, actual buffer exhaustion
atomic. This does not promise whole-string or multi-digit OTP composition.

The strict CDP audit now passes all original requirements and additionally checks
Numeric one-step Undo plus masked fullwidth OTP commit (only its first digit).
The mask control is an HTML checkbox: the test explicitly refocuses the canvas OTP
before invoking native composition, so it exercises the intended host textbox.
The original four-consumer native CDP regression also passes. Headless tests cover
ASCII/fullwidth/trailing/invalid-first filtering, callback counts, capacity and
UTF-8 boundaries, masking, composing shortcuts, stale focus and source/model
replacement. Four focused ASAN/UBSan tests pass. Warning build is clean; full
CTest passes 90/91, with only expected stale generated distribution failing.
No shared Core/SDL/browser implementation or distribution files were changed.
The Combobox large-query and Numeric browser read-only fixture limitations above
remain unverified. Native platform UI behavior remains source-supported rather
than tested through an OS IME in this follow-up.

# Input behavior and presentation

`cui_input_ex` combines the editor with an application-owned `cui_input_state` and options for size, width, placeholder, appearance, text alignment, disabled, readonly, required, invalid and an optional synchronous `cui_platform` clipboard interface. The convenience `cui_input` supplies defaults. Retained state preserves horizontal scrolling and pointer selection across frames. Applications own the editor and buffer.

Single-line inputs paint a caret and a selected-text background, clip text to the viewport, and adjust horizontal scrolling to keep the caret visible. Pointer placement measures UTF-8 scalar prefixes using the same configured font measurement as layout. Shift-click extends selection and captured dragging continues across frames. Secondary buttons do not mutate selection. Measurement is based on logical text order; shaping clusters, bidi and grapheme boundaries remain separate unfinished work. The renderer paints one unbroken text node with a selection underlay, preserving the same text measurement across selection boundaries. The legacy multiline rendering path still lacks caret painting, pointer placement and vertical movement; use the independent Textarea module for its bounded multiline engine.

The drawing-free `cui_base_input_ex` accepts a host-defined pointer-to-byte-offset callback and reduces pointer, keyboard, text and clipboard events in order. Readonly fields allow navigation, selection and copying while rejecting mutations. Disabled fields ignore input. Semantics carry readonly, required, invalid and multiline states. Validation flags are controlled by the application; this API does not infer validation rules.

Control/Meta+C copies the selection; X removes it only after a successful copy; V validates and inserts the returned UTF-8 text atomically. Missing/rejected clipboard access reports `CUI_EDIT_CLIPBOARD_UNAVAILABLE`, preserving the text. Control/Meta+Z, Shift+Z and Y use bounded editor history. `cui_edit_apply_event` lets other compound inputs preserve their own event ordering. Browser clipboard permissions and asynchronous integration belong to the browser adapter; supplying the native synchronous interface does not establish browser clipboard parity or IME support.

`tests/unit/test_input.c` checks UTF-8 clipboard round trips, copy failure, invalid paste, readonly and disabled behavior, semantic state, ordered undo/redo, variable-width pointer selection, captured dragging, all four themes, caret/selection draw geometry and horizontal scrolling. Its base-only target links core/base/editor without styled or theme objects. Existing editing property tests continue to exercise history and UTF-8 validity.

`cui_input_paint` exposes presentation without reducing events or registering a second textbox semantic. Compound components can run their own reducer once and reuse the caret/selection appearance. `cui_input_viewport_id` and the drawing-free `cui_base_input_hit_test` geometry helper let their reducers share measured pointer positioning. Tests prove painting alone leaves queued edits untouched and composition inserts each character once.

## Source sizes and fixed-height centering

`cui_input_options.size` defaults to `CUI_INPUT_MEDIUM` (zero), with SMALL, LARGE, XSMALL and CUSTOM choices. `cui_input_measure` exposes the exact renderer metrics before layout. Presets use `density` when positive, otherwise `theme.font_size / 16`:

| Size | Height | Font | Horizontal padding | Vertical padding | Line box |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| XS | 20 | 12 | 4 | 0 | 20 |
| S | 24 | 14 | 8 | 2 | 20 |
| M | 32 | 14 | 10 | 8 | 20 |
| L | 44 | 16 | 12 | 10 | 20 |

Custom size sets the height directly and font to `custom_size * .875`, with horizontal/vertical padding 8/2 at the selected density. A positive `height` refines the frame height; `custom_height` also allows exact zero. Invalid/nonfinite metrics are rejected before interaction. The horizontal text inset includes the one-pixel border when present. The source single-line child has a fixed 20px line height and its row frame centers it on the cross axis: Medium's vertical padding does not enlarge its 32px frame. Actual glyph measurement is centered inside that line box. Numeric and custom compound renderers can reuse this through `cui_input_paint`.

`name` labels the semantic node and is no longer painted as a second row. This corrects the previous Input appearance. `no_appearance` suppresses the frame surface/border; `no_border` keeps the surface. Focus/invalid border colors remain separately controlled. There is no outer source focus shadow yet. `text_align` supports Start, Center and End. Both growing and fixed-width fields align text in the current layout pass. Selection uses `theme.selection` without changing the foreground, and the caret uses independent `theme.caret` with source height 85% of the line box. Disabled appearance uses input background at 20% alpha and muted foreground at 50% alpha. Source caret blinking, IME, shaping and native context menus remain separate gaps.

Growing single-line inputs now align text through the current layout pass. Their inner content no longer uses a previous-frame viewport width as a minimum, so changing parent width or horizontal padding does not force a stale viewport size. Headless tests cover left, center and right alignment on the first frame and after shrink/grow transitions with changing padding; the regression fails against the previous implementation.

Single-line inputs render both their value and placeholder as one unwrapped line,
including when the host supplies only a measurement callback. The content viewport
clips overflow; focused values scroll horizontally to keep the caret visible.
A long placeholder does not increase the input height or wrap into extra lines.

Growing single-line fields (`width = -1`) constrain long populated values to the
resolved frame width on the first frame and after parent resizing. The outer and
text-viewport clips remain active; InputGroup prefix/suffix segments retain their
widths. An extra internal layout row provides this containment.

Remaining resize limitation: horizontal scroll, caret/selection projection and
host IME geometry can use the previous frame's viewport during a width change.
A focused end caret may be clipped for the first shrinking frame, or retain excess
scroll for the first growing frame; the next frame converges. Width containment
does not fix that separate projection defect. See
[the characterization and opt-in failing probe](design/INPUT_GROW_WIDTH.md).
