# Whole-value Input acceptance

The contract follows pinned GPUI Kit commit
`87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`,
[replacement and preedit validation](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-kit/blob/87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34/crates/base/src/input/base/state.rs)
(`is_valid_input`, `replace_text_in_range`, `replace_and_mark_text_in_range`).
This implements a bounded predicate for the single-line composed Input, not full
Input-family parity or source regex/mask/content-type behavior.

Set `cui_input_options.validate` and `validate_user` (or the corresponding Base
options). The callback receives the complete proposed UTF-8 value, never merely
the inserted payload. Empty candidates are implicitly valid. Otherwise call the
candidate predicate first; only if it returns false is the previous value tested.
Reject only when that previous value is valid. This permits repairing invalid
programmatic defaults without trapping the user. Programmatic legacy edit APIs
remain unvalidated; history Undo/Redo bypass acceptance, as does a multiline model.
Multi-selection attachment is currently a multiline extension, so it retains its
existing behavior without this source single-line predicate; no validated
multi-cursor extension is claimed.

```c
static bool digits(void *unused, cui_str value) {
    (void)unused;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < value.length; ++i)
        if (value.data[i] < '0' || value.data[i] > '9') return false;
    return true;
}
/* state and edit are retained caller-owned objects. */
cui_input_result result = cui_input_ex(ui, id, theme, cui_string("Digits"), edit,
    &state, (cui_input_options){.validate = digits});
if (result.rejected) { /* An edit was declined, without changing the value. */ }
```

A declined edit sets `result.rejected` with `error == CUI_EDIT_OK`; it does not
implicitly mark the control invalid. `invalid` remains an explicit semantic/paint
flag and `required` remains semantic metadata. UTF-8, boundary, capacity and
forbidden single-line line-break errors remain distinct and publish the existing
same-frame error appearance. The source strips CR/LF from single-line insertion;
CUI retains its explicit `CUI_EDIT_LINE_BREAK` engine policy in this batch.

## Engine and host dispatch

`cui_edit_apply_checked` takes a by-value request and acceptance policy, returning
`{error, rejected}`. EVENT delegates existing keyboard/text behavior, INSERT is
atomic clipboard insertion, DELETE_SELECTION removes a selected cut range, and
COMPOSITION applies the reusable IME session. Invalid request kinds/null models
fail without callback invocation. Raw legacy APIs and null-policy checked requests
keep their existing behavior; no permanent callback/userdata is retained in the
model. Invalid UTF-8/boundaries/capacity fail before a predicate is invoked.

The actual Input reducer routes typing, paste, selected/grapheme/word erasure and
composition through this seam. Copy is unchanged. Cut copies first, then attempts
validated deletion, matching source `cut`: a rejected cut can still copy its
selection. Clipboard failure leaves the document unchanged and does not invoke
the predicate. Readonly/disabled controls retain existing mutation guards.

IME UPDATE validates a complete provisional view without changing committed text
or history. The previous predicate value is the prior composed view when active,
not merely the committed document. Rejected updates preserve that view. Engine
COMMIT rejection also preserves session state; its standalone caller may retain
or cancel it. The built-in Input reducer then explicitly cancels a rejected host
COMMIT as a subsequent lifecycle transition: native/browser composition has ended,
corresponding to source `unmark_text`. Committed text, selection and history remain
unchanged, and following typing/shortcuts work. A successful commit is one Undo step.
START/CANCEL and history replay do not invoke the predicate. Existing focus-loss,
readonly/disabled and source-revision cancellation policies remain intact.

## Ownership, bounds and rollback

There is no additional acceptance allocation or caller preview buffer. Ordinary
edits/commit reuse the model's existing creation-time scratch, bounded by document
capacity. Provisional views reuse existing fixed caller view storage or the opted-in
model-owned `grow_view` cache, bounded by document capacity + preedit capacity - 1.
The existing grow cache can allocate on necessary growth, not on every edit.
Fixed-view capacity remains an explicit error; oversized preedit is not truncated.
The engine validates known workspace/session/model aliases before writes. Payload
slices of the stable document or preedit buffer are supported; payloads overlapping
the working candidate workspace are invalid.

Each predicate borrows an immutable value only for that synchronous call. On a
failed candidate the shared view may be rebuilt from unchanged document/preedit
storage for the old-value predicate, then restored or rebuilt for acceptance.
Predicates are never replayed as part of commit. Rejection preserves logical model
metadata, coalescing, selection, history/redo, annotations and session ownership,
and the previous view's defined bytes through its NUL terminator. Internal scratch
and unused capacity tails are unspecified; this is not an entire-allocation byte
identity promise. No idle-frame document copy is added.

Same-model mutation during a predicate is guarded: mutating APIs and scratch/cache
operations return INVALID_ARGUMENT; void destroy/detach/coalescing setters do
nothing and record the violation. The outer checked request rejects with
INVALID_ARGUMENT, restores its logical prepared state and leaves the model alive.
Destroy it normally after the checked call returns. Pure getters for text/state,
content, selections and columns remain available. Nested same-model checked calls
are rejected. Other models, UI/host callbacks and external side effects are not
blocked or rolled back. Direct writes to caller buffers or borrowed strings,
freeing caller storage, retaining candidate pointers and cross-thread model access
violate the borrowing contract and cannot be protected by a C callback guard.

## Validation and integration

`tests/unit/test_input_acceptance.c` exercises actual composed Input/Core dispatch
for typing, paste/copy-first cut, grapheme/word/selected erasure, healing, history
replay/redo retention, readonly/disabled/error separation and IME host lifecycle.
It also checks same-model mutation/destruction guards, malformed/capacity/alias
requests, fixed/growing provisional views larger than committed capacity, prior
view restoration, rejected growth, a 200 KB whole-value candidate and multiline
bypass. Register it linked only to `cui`, including
WASI. Root owns CMake, distribution and registry changes; this source batch does
not claim full native/browser accessibility or all Input reference features.

# InputGroup addon and text observers

Include `cui/cui_form_events.h`. `cui_base_input_group_events` and
`cui_input_group_events` mirror the legacy arguments plus a borrowed
`cui_input_group_handler`, returning `cui_input_group_event_result`.
`control` is the unchanged legacy result, including the last activated addon in
descriptor order and aggregate Input changed/submitted/error/rejected fields.
`addon_count`, `change_count`, `submit_count` count actual callbacks; counts saturate
with `count_overflow`. Reading results never replays callbacks or mutations.

```c
static void addon_activated(void *user, const cui_component_event_metadata *event) {
    bool *work_after_frame = user;
    *work_after_frame = true; /* Identify action using event->target. */
}
static void text_changed_or_submitted(void *user, const cui_component_text_event *event) {
    bool *work_after_frame = user;
    *work_after_frame = true;
    /* Inspect event->event.kind: CHANGE or SUBMIT. Text is borrowed/redactable. */
}
/* During submission with existing caller-owned model/state/addon descriptors: */
/* cui_input_group_event_result result = cui_input_group_events(
       ui, group_id, input_id, theme, edit, &state, addons, count, options,
       (cui_input_group_handler){.on_text = text_changed_or_submitted,
                                .on_addon = addon_activated, .user = &pending}); */
```

Base preserves addon source traversal. Each built-in Button addon first runs its
old interaction and last-addon write, adds its existing semantic details, then
notifies once per actual accepted activation in that addon's input order. Two
activations of B and one of A may dispatch A then B then B when A precedes B in
the descriptors. They are not sorted into global input order. Metadata kind is
ACTIVATE, target is the actual addon ID, with genuine accepted snapshot evidence.
If snapshot data is unavailable but accepted input identity is proven, only actual
frame/index/type facts are supplied; no activation is fabricated. A legacy
aggregate boolean alone does not invent a callback without accepted input evidence.

All addon notifications precede the nested Input reducer. `on_text` reuses
`cui_base_input_events` exactly once, preserving its per-event committed CHANGE and
eligible Enter SUBMIT notifications, revisions, rejection/errors, composition and
history behavior. Its metadata target is the nested **Input ID**, not the group.
Multiple inputs/submits can each notify; preedit and unchanged revisions do not
become CHANGE. A failure after earlier edits retains earlier notifications and the
old aggregate error. No extra whole-group final-text comparison or replay occurs.

Callbacks run before the group's final input-parent association and before Styled
paint. Missing handlers still permit all old work. Readonly input does not disable
otherwise enabled addon Buttons; disabled input, disabled/loading addons retain
their existing separate policies. Passive/layout-only/inert submissions preserve
old work but emit no new observation. Text/custom addons have no built-in action
notification; controls in custom renderers keep their own APIs. Later custom
renderer edits are not synthesized as nested Input events.

Text payloads inherit Input's secure redaction: masked or password-purpose inputs
have `has_text=false` and empty text; scalar snapshots remain available. Otherwise
UTF-8 is borrowed only through the callback. Use `cui_component_event_copy_utf8`
with explicit storage/byte limit and check `CUI_COMPONENT_EVENT_COPY_OK` to retain
it. Copy metadata/scalar snapshots by value. Handler/user/descriptors and all
active model/state/frame resources must remain live. Do not mutate/free/rebind
active model/state/descriptors/input/context, recursively submit UI or destroy
context in observers. Unrelated flags and copying are allowed; defer omission and
teardown until outer return plus frame/renderer consumption. Notifications cannot
reject already applied changes, consume by return or imply COMMIT/form submission.

Styled InputGroup now shares standard Input's mask preparation and checked resource
gate before its single nested reduction, then paints once in the existing Group
layout. Masked committed text and preedit use bullets; source-byte selection and
caller-provided hit testing retain their existing model-offset policy. The default
plain hit fallback is replaced with masked mapping. The actual caller-owned Group
behavior remains current inside text callbacks; temporary Styled configuration does
not redirect state ownership. No public layouts or event timing change.

Masked Styled InputGroup rejects an actual custom `presentation.prepare` or
`presentation_complete` with `CUI_EDIT_INVALID_ARGUMENT`: the mask stage needs the
single checked presentation gate. Rejection registers a disabled, secret, readonly,
invalid input without reducing or exposing raw text. Earlier addon work remains
applied. Failure after accepted text progress retains those changes/notifications
and the last valid mask; the failing edit is atomic. Custom Base and unmasked
presentation policies remain supported. Password purpose alone intentionally uses
visible-password painting while semantics and text events remain redacted.

`tests/unit/test_input_group_events.c` compares legacy/facade state, aggregate
results, focus/redraw, semantics and paint for Base/Styled, including addon ordering,
text/submit multiplicity, secure event redaction, IME/undo, validation rejection,
progress before capacity error, readonly addons, disabled/loading, custom children,

regressions through `scripts/test_local.py`. No browser or full-family parity claim.
Bridge and language wrappers retain existing queued generic text notifications;
this does not expose synchronous typed addon/per-event handlers through bindings.

Focused regressions inspect committed/preedit draw commands, secret semantics,
custom model-offset hit testing, forbidden custom presentation, actual owner state
inside callbacks, visible-password behavior, and progress before format-capacity
failure. These are headless command/semantic tests, not GPU pixel acceptance.

# Bounded Input normalization

Source pin: GPUI Kit `87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`,
[state.rs normalize_input](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-kit/blob/87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34/crates/base/src/input/base/state.rs#L3520).
Its single-line path removes CR and LF before replacement and validation. Number
mask Unicode normalization is separate. This slice implements only explicit
CR/LF removal; it does not implement format masks, regex or password presentation.

Set `.normalization = CUI_EDIT_NORMALIZE_SINGLE_LINE_CRLF` on styled/Base Input
options or a `cui_edit_request`. Zero preserves existing `CUI_EDIT_LINE_BREAK`
errors. Multiline checked edits retain CR/LF and bypass this single-line policy.
Raw edit APIs and model creation retain their existing behavior. Applications
must explicitly opt into source-compatible normalization; no automatic seed
conversion is claimed.

For a bounded initial value, call:

```c
char seed[128];
cui_str value;
cui_edit_result error = cui_edit_normalize_text(cui_string("a\r\nb"),
    CUI_EDIT_NORMALIZE_SINGLE_LINE_CRLF, seed, sizeof seed, &value);
/* On success value borrows seed and contains "ab". Create the model from seed. */
```

The helper validates the complete original UTF-8 value and enum, checks all known
source/destination/output-descriptor overlaps, then verifies capacity including
NUL before writing. Failure leaves destination and output unchanged. No in-place
or overlapping operation is supported. It owns no storage; source remains
immutable and the returned value lives as long as destination. Unicode scalar
bytes are unchanged: removal matches ASCII CR/LF only, not U+2028, U+2029 or other
whitespace. Empty normalized output is valid. This helper is independent of a
model; writing any caller-owned model buffer during a predicate remains forbidden
by the existing borrowing contract.

Checked edits use existing engine/session workspaces without additional staging
allocation. Ordinary document capacity applies to the normalized resulting value,
so a long CR/LF-rich original payload can fit a smaller document. IME original
payload length must first fit caller-owned preedit capacity; removal does not
bypass that input bound. Fixed/growing rendered-view capacity applies to the
normalized full view. Existing lazy growth occurs only when that view needs it.

For IME, anchor/cursor are validated against the original UTF-8 payload first,
including scalar boundaries. Each endpoint maps to the count of surviving bytes
before it. The resulting session stores normalized preedit and normalized byte
ranges, not original-host provenance. Neither original Core event strings nor
host offsets are rewritten. UPDATE does not mutate the committed document;
COMMIT creates one Undo step. Empty updates preserve the existing CUI active-empty
session contract until explicit CANCEL/COMMIT; this does not claim source empty
marked-text lifecycle equivalence.

Whole-value acceptance sees normalized candidates and the previous visible value.
Rejected updates retain prior preedit/view bytes and ownership. Engine rejected
COMMIT retains its prepared session; the built-in host reducer subsequently
cancels because the host ended composition. UTF-8, range, capacity and alias
errors precede mutation where possible. Same-model predicate mutation remains
guarded, and no callback is replayed while committing. Undo/Redo restore recorded
values without normalization or acceptance. Normalized typing coalesces using its
existing intent; paste and IME retain atomic history behavior.

The composed test `test_input_normalization.c` covers typed/pasted selection
replacement, grouped Undo/Redo, normalized rejection, readonly/disabled and zero
policy, Unicode/emoji endpoint mapping, fixed/growing IME views, empty update and
cancel, helper aliases/rollback, model capacity and guarded destruction. It runs
through CTest and the portable WASI runner. The website's validated Input example
also exercises ordinary typing and native browser IME rejection/recovery on
desktop and a 390px viewport. Browser clipboard paste, physical keyboard
candidate windows, autofill and complete Input parity remain unverified.

# Input Number formatting

`CUI_EDIT_FORMAT_NUMBER` is an opt-in single-line, single-selection checked-edit formatter. Zero initialization keeps existing editing behavior. Styled `cui_input_ex` and Base Input forward `.format` and caller-owned `.format_workspace`; no locale, floating-point parser, extra dependency or per-edit allocation is required.

```c
char formatting[256];
cui_input_options options = {
    .format = {.kind = CUI_EDIT_FORMAT_NUMBER,
               .has_separator = true, .separator = ',',
               .fraction_limited = true, .fraction_digits = 2},
    .format_workspace = {formatting, sizeof formatting},
    .normalization = CUI_EDIT_NORMALIZE_SINGLE_LINE_CRLF,
};
```

The workspace must hold the final UTF-8 value and terminator and remain disjoint from the model, payload, composition buffers and declared presentation resources. It is borrowed only during the synchronous call. Invalid configurations and insufficient capacity fail before predicates or document/history/selection changes. Presentation prepares the final grouped value before acceptance callbacks, including masked display resources; failure preserves logical state and prior committed presentation. Scratch and unused capacity tails are unspecified.

The implementation follows pinned gpui-component 0.7.1 commit `87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`, `crates/base/src/input/base/mask_pattern.rs`: validity lines 189–245, formatting 286–340, unmasking 375–393, numeric normalization 428–458; `input/state.rs` normalization orders numeric conversion before single-line line-break removal.

A configured separator is removed before formatting. Integer scalars group from the right in threes, with the rightmost sign moved to the front. Fraction length truncates only when a separator is configured; zeros are never padded. Without a separator, formatting is identity even with a fraction limit. Empty text, `+`, `-`, `.`, `-.` and `.5` are valid intermediate values. Multiple dots, misplaced integer signs and other characters are invalid, except that configured separators are permitted in integer/fraction parts. This deliberately preserves source quirks, including special separators such as `.` or `+`, rather than parsing a numeric value.

`cui_edit_format_valid`, `cui_edit_format_text`, `cui_edit_format_placeholder` and `cui_edit_unformat_text` accept the Number descriptor. Its placeholder is empty. Unformatting removes configured separators and, if a dot remains, trailing ASCII zeros: `1,234.00` becomes `1234.`. Pure formatting does not validate automatically, allowing the source's invalid-old-value healing policy. The checked engine normalizes the candidate, prepares the final presentation, calls the user predicate on the unformatted candidate, then checks Number validity. If that fails but the previous value was already invalid, the edit can heal it under the existing acceptance contract. Empty candidates bypass predicates. Replay restores recorded values without formatting or acceptance replay; presentation still prepares replayed values.

Fullwidth digits, plus, minus, dot and comma convert to ASCII; U+2212 converts to `-`, and U+3002 to `.`. Other Unicode stays unchanged. `cui_edit_normalize_number_text` performs this conversion for explicit seed setup, optionally removing CR/LF; `cui_edit_number_offset` maps an original UTF-8 scalar-boundary byte endpoint to the normalized byte endpoint. Pure helper output descriptors and buffers are unchanged on errors, and input/output aliasing is rejected. A seed is not automatically normalized, formatted or validated when creating a model.

IME UPDATE applies numeric normalization and optional CR/LF removal but keeps preedit unformatted and committed text unchanged. Selection endpoints are mapped from original host UTF-8 bytes. COMMIT formats once and creates one history edit; CANCEL restores the committed view. The original preedit payload must fit the configured preedit storage before shrinking normalization: this is a bounded ownership rule, not a promise that normalized size alone controls capacity. The final grouped value must fit both model capacity and formatting workspace. Existing source byte-based caret adjustment is retained and snapped to valid UTF-8 boundaries.

CUI differences are explicit: embedded NUL remains unsupported by the editing engine, so an enabled NUL separator is rejected; checked single-line formatting also rejects CR/LF separators. Disabled separator requires `separator == 0`; unlimited fraction requires `fraction_digits == 0`. Single-line CR/LF removal remains opt-in rather than changing legacy controls. Multiline models, multiple selections and inline tokens reject enabled formatting atomically. Raw engine APIs are unchanged. This slice does not implement regex validation or all source content-type builders, and does not claim complete Number-mask or Input parity.

Coverage is in `test_input_number_engine.c`, `test_input_number_control.c` and `test_input_number_native.c`: source intermediate/grouping/unmask cases, UTF-8 endpoint conversion, alias/config/capacity failures, callback order/reentry, invalid-old healing, actual styled paste/IME/semantic state/history, fixed bullet-storage failure and actual-font bullet pixels/factory rollback. Native font test accepts argv font or `CUI_TEST_FONT`, returning 77 when unavailable. Integrators must register these new tests; generated distributions require regeneration after the appended public descriptor fields.

For a registered native build, the engine and control tests link only `cui`; the font test links `cui_text`, `cui_bidi` and `cui`, and uses the optional native text dependencies already pinned by the project. All three compile with `-std=c11 -UNDEBUG -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror`. The font test must have CTest skip return code 77. A WASI engine probe uses the engine test plus `cui_edit.c`, `cui.c` and `cui_effects.c`; it requires no filesystem, environment or platform services.

# Pattern formatting for single-line Input

This opt-in feature formats the stored value. It is independent of password bullet
display, regular-expression matching, numeric grouping, and semantic content type.
Legacy zero options are unchanged. No full Input parity claim follows.

```c
char formatted_workspace[128];
cui_input_options options = {
    .format = {.kind = CUI_EDIT_FORMAT_PATTERN, .pattern = {"99-99", 5}},
    .format_workspace = {formatted_workspace, sizeof formatted_workspace}
};
/* Paste 1234 stores/paints 12-34; the final caret is byte 5. */
cui_input_result result = cui_input_ex(ui, id, &theme, label, edit, &state, options);
```

The appended fields also exist in `cui_base_input_options` and `cui_edit_request`.
Use `cui_edit_apply_checked` for an independent reducer. Direct raw edit functions
have no retained format policy. Pattern/configuration changes never eagerly rewrite
existing text or history. Pure helpers support seed/readback setup:
`cui_edit_format_valid`, `cui_edit_format_text`, `cui_edit_format_placeholder`,
and `cui_edit_unformat_text`. Seed creation itself still does not automatically
validate or format; call the pure helper explicitly if that is the desired policy.

## Source behavior

Pinned reference: `87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`,
`crates/base/src/input/base/mask_pattern.rs` and `state.rs:3534–3553,4109–4198`.
The source's incomplete builder comment is not the token contract:

| Token | Consumes |
| --- | --- |
| `9` | One ASCII digit, not a dot or fullwidth digit |
| `A` | One ASCII letter |
| `#` | One ASCII letter or digit |
| `*` | One Unicode scalar, not one grapheme |
| Other scalar | Literal separator |

Validation scans tokens, skipping mismatches and consuming matching scalars; all
input must be consumed, but not every token must be filled. Formatting inserts
unmatched separators, consumes matching separators, and stops at the first
unmatched input token or exhausted input. It does not append trailing separators.
These source rules are intentionally preserved, including `A9` accepting `1`
while formatting it to empty. There is no token escaping syntax.

Unformat walks token positions and removes literal positions, rather than stripping
all punctuation. Placeholder uses `_` for input tokens and preserves literals.
For `9999年99月`, `202412` formats to `2024年12`; placeholder is `____年__月`.
An empty pattern behaves as NONE. Styled Input uses the generated placeholder
when no explicit nonempty `.placeholder` is supplied; an explicit placeholder wins.
This frame-options rule is distinct from the reference's ordered builder setters.

For each checked committed edit: normalize insertion if requested; build whole
unformatted candidate; compute formatted final text in caller workspace; hard
prepare final presentation resources; then run custom validator followed by token
validity on the original candidate. Empty bypasses both. If invalid, run that same
chain on the old visible value; reject only when old is valid. Thus invalid seeded
text remains editable. Hard capacity/resource errors never use invalid-old healing.
The user predicate is not replayed for formatting. Masked Input prepares only final
bullet geometry; no plaintext geometry fallback is introduced.

IME UPDATE validates/prepares an unformatted composed view and never mutates the
committed document in CUI. COMMIT formats once and creates one Undo transaction.
Rejected UPDATE preserves prior visible preedit; host COMMIT rejection cancels its
ended session afterward. START/CANCEL/PRESENT do not format. Undo/Redo restore exact
recorded bytes and selection, bypassing format/validation while retaining resource
preparation. A formatting rewrite breaks typing coalescing and records a whole
document change; unchanged formatting preserves ordinary typing grouping.

Caret adjustment preserves the source byte-length formula, then snaps an interior
UTF8 endpoint backward to a scalar boundary. This additional CUI safety rule keeps
the portable byte-offset contract valid with Unicode literals.

## Ownership and failure rules

Pattern bytes are immutable synchronous borrowed input. Engine workspace is caller
owned and includes NUL. It must be disjoint from pattern, event payload, every model
allocation, IME descriptor/buffers, and all declared presentation spans. No hidden
per-edit allocation is added. Model scratch bounds the unformatted candidate too:
an insertion that exceeds model capacity fails even if formatting could truncate
it to fit. Formatting never silently truncates for destination capacity.

Pure helpers require disjoint destination/result descriptors and input bytes;
malformed input, alias and insufficient capacity leave output unchanged. Internal
scratch/workspace tails are unspecified; rejection preserves document, history,
selection, coalescing, session and the prior view's defined bytes plus terminator.
Active stale/wrong-model checked composition requests reject before implicit session
cancellation, preserving prior preedit on hard failures; Base still performs its
normal explicit focus/selection lifecycle cancellation. Known same-model mutators
invoked from predicates/presentation are guarded.
Caller writes and external callback side effects remain outside rollback.

For styled Input, keep workspace alive and unchanged through frame draw consumption:
its generated placeholder can be frame-borrowed. Styled placeholder capacity is
preflighted before reduction, and reused afterward. Base/engine usage only borrows
workspace during the synchronous request. No workspace pointer is retained by the
engine. Presentation resources follow their existing caller completion contract.

Nonempty patterns reject multiline models, multiple selections and inline tokens
with INVALID_ARGUMENT before writes or callbacks. Checked single-line patterns
containing CR/LF also reject before reduction, preserving CUI's existing single-line
document invariant; pure helpers may still format those literals. These are explicit
bounded CUI restrictions. Unicode `*` can split a grapheme in source formatting;
grapheme navigation otherwise keeps its established editing policy.

## Registration and proof

Integrator registers `test_input_format_engine` and `test_input_format_control`
against `cui`, and native optional `test_input_format_native` against shaped-text
libraries. The native test accepts argv font or CUI_TEST_FONT and exits 77 without
a usable font. It paints actual NotoSans bullet pixels and forces a geometry factory
failure before value/history/selection mutation. After changing host factory
availability, it sends `cui_text_metrics_changed`, honoring existing font-cache
generation invalidation. Unit scenes cover real Core/styled Input paste, paint,
semantics, IME, history, readonly and password-copy policy, plus pure source cases,
Unicode, alias, capacity, predicate/guard and prior-preedit rollback tests.

Independent public headers affected: `cui_edit.h`, `cui_base.h`,
`cui_components.h`. No additional private source/header or dependency registration.
Distribution regeneration remains integrator-owned. Numeric formatting, regex,
broader content purposes and the remaining source Input lifecycle/platform features
remain separate work.

Worker validation: strict full native build passed; CTest 142/143 passed, with
only the expected stale distribution headers failing. Three new tests passed
strict manual compilation and ASan/UBSan with leak detection. The engine test
also passed wasm32-wasi with Wasmtime49; independent public-header checks passed.
These new tests are not yet in worker CTest because registration is integrator-owned.
Logs: `/home/matteo/.cache/cui-validation/input-pattern-{build,ctest}-final.log`.

# Single-line Input pointer selection

The stateful Base Input reducer and styled `cui_input_ex` now consume host click counts for ordinary single-line text. Count zero/one preserves caret placement and Shift extension. A double click selects the source-defined word/whitespace range; a triple click (or higher count) selects the whole single line. Shift does not override double/triple selection. Masked double/triple click retains whole-value selection, avoiding disclosure of plaintext word boundaries.

This follows gpui-component 0.7.1 commit `87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`: `crates/base/src/text_boundary.rs:1–47`, `input/base/selection.rs:25–91`, and `input/base/state.rs:2297–2415,3190–3240`. The word classifier is deliberately distinct from Unicode word-navigation primitives: ASCII letters/digits/underscore, Latin U+00C0–024F and U+1E00–1EFF, Cyrillic U+0400–04FF and combining U+0300–036F connect; Unicode whitespace connects separately; punctuation, CJK and other scalars select individually. At most128 previous and128 following scalars connect. A400-character run clicked at byte200 therefore selects bytes72–329. End-of-value double click has no word and leaves selection unchanged. UTF-8 byte endpoints remain scalar boundaries; this is not an arbitrary grapheme/Unicode word-classification claim.

A double-click drag keeps its original selected word covered while extending the moving endpoint. Crossing left reverses the anchor; returning inside the original range retains the word; extending right uses the original start. It does not snap the moving endpoint to the whole destination word. The source clears sticky word state on triple-click: subsequent drag moves the line selection's end and may shrink it. This implementation preserves that behavior rather than inventing persistent whole-line drag.

Readonly controls permit selection; disabled controls suppress it. Consumed presses (including inline-token actions) do not reposition the caret or start word selection. Existing token-safe atomic selection expands token-interior endpoints. Consumed primary release still clears drag state. Keyboard/text events, cancel, blur, disable, model rebind and document revision invalidate the sticky range. No document mutation, validator/presentation call, hidden allocation or extra history edit occurs; normal selection breaks typing coalescing through the existing edit API.

Keep one zero-initialized `cui_input_behavior_state` per stable ID/model session, or one styled `cui_input_state`. Appended internal fields retain only offsets, numeric revision and an active flag; they never borrow text or retain the model pointer. Keep the model alive during reduction; reset caller state when destroying/recreating a model at a reused address, as with existing model identity contracts. The stateless legacy Base wrapper cannot retain a word-drag range between calls; use the stateful ex/reducer API for this interaction. Existing multiline reducers are unchanged: new word/line branches explicitly require a single-line model. Host adapters must provide actual click counts; zero remains an ordinary click.

`tests/unit/test_input_pointer_selection.c` exercises actual Core event targeting and Base composition: both drag directions/return, Shift, source triple-click shrink, end boundary, readonly/disabled/masked, consumed annotated-token press/release, Latin/combining/CJK/emoji/punctuation/whitespace, bounded long word, cancellation and model rebind. The initial ordinary double-click assertion fails against pre-change `c866950` and passes afterward (`input-pointer-before.log` records the failure).

`tests/integration/test_input_pointer_native.c` drives actual styled Input using real shaped caret positions and native font geometry, checks byte selections and painted selection widths against native geometry, and verifies glyph alpha pixels. It accepts argv font or `CUI_TEST_FONT`, returning77 when unavailable; register with skip return code77 and link `cui`, `cui_text`, `cui_bidi`. Headless unit links `cui`; it also runs without host dependencies under WASI. No browser fixture, global registration or generated distribution is changed in this scoped slice.

Remaining Input wheel/menu/clear/reveal/loading, regex and most content-purpose gaps are recorded separately. This change is not a complete Input parity claim.

Validation for this scoped commit: strict C11 warning build passes; existing CTest144/145 passes, with only the inherited generated-distribution stale check failing. Scoped unit and actual NotoSans native-font tests pass under ASan/UBSan with leak detection; the unit scene passes Zig0.16.0 WASI under Wasmtime49.0.0 without filesystem or environment access. Independent public Base header compiles. Logs use `/home/matteo/.cache/cui-validation/input-pointer-*`; integrator must register the two new tests and regenerate distributions. No browser/runtime parity proof beyond these native/headless paths is claimed.

# Input reference contracts

Audit pin: GPUI Kit commit `87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`.
Primary source: [movement](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-kit/blob/87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34/crates/base/src/input/base/movement.rs),
[state/validation](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-kit/blob/87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34/crates/base/src/input/base/state.rs),
[styled Input](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-kit/blob/87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34/crates/component/src/input/input.rs), and
[history contracts](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-kit/blob/87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34/crates/kit/tests/input/history.rs).
This change addresses two widget behavior gaps and adds tests through the actual
styled `cui_input_ex` control. It does not establish full Input-family parity.

The source `crates/base/src/input/base/movement.rs` `move_vertical` returns
immediately for a single-line Input; `state.rs` `select_up`/`select_down` do too.
CUI's single-line Input now leaves selection unchanged for Up/Down, including
Shift/Ctrl modifiers and read-only inputs. Its Base reducer consumes those keys
unless `delegate_up_down` explicitly yields to a popup/list owner. Multiline
edit models retain existing vertical movement. The generic edit engine's line
movement APIs remain unchanged.

Source `state.rs` `on_blur` breaks undo transaction coalescing while preserving
selection. CUI's retained `cui_input_behavior_state` now records focus and numeric
model identity, splitting coalescing on focus transitions, first binding and model
rebinding. It never dereferences an old model. These operations do not change
document revision, clear history or discard selection. Zero-initialize state and
retain it with its Input; reset state when replacing a model if the allocator can
reuse the exact old address, or when transferring state to a different UI/ID.
The state observes transitions when the widget is submitted: applications that
omit it or change focus away and back entirely between submissions must explicitly
call `cui_edit_break_coalescing` at that application lifecycle boundary. This is
not an OS focus subscription or engine-wide focus observer. The legacy stateless
`cui_base_input` wrapper preserves its prior engine grouping; use retained
`cui_base_input_ex` state for observed focus-transition grouping. The styled
`cui_input` convenience wrapper already retains state through Core resources.

Existing composed paths covered by the new tests include grouped consecutive
typing Undo/Redo, Ctrl-Z/Ctrl-Y/Meta-Shift-Z, grapheme arrow/backspace over combining
marks and regional-indicator flags, history separation after blur, model rebinding,
multiline selection, delegated popup keys, readonly/disabled mutation guards,
required/invalid semantics, same-frame error presentation and IME commit/Undo plus
focus-loss cancellation. IME preedit remains outside committed document/history;
commit is one Undo step. Existing size/geometry/IME APIs remain intact.

## Whole-value validation

The previously missing source predicate is now implemented by the checked engine
seam and composed Input options; see [Input acceptance](INPUT_ACCEPTANCE.md) for
exact callback, healing, IME, borrowing and rollback contracts. Explicit `invalid`
and `required` flags remain distinct from edit acceptance. Source preedit updates
also run the predicate; CUI preserves provisional rendering without committed
mutation while providing that validation. This does not implement regex/mask
constraints or source content-type roles.

Other source-specific gaps are deliberately preserved: source single-line
normalization strips CR/LF while CUI's edit model rejects them with
`CUI_EDIT_LINE_BREAK`; mask/regex validation, source content-type/password roles,
context-menu capabilities and source lifecycle event callbacks are not supplied
by these two fixes. This guide does not claim those behaviors or full parity.

Integrator: register `tests/unit/test_input_reference_contracts.c` linked only to
`cui`, including portable/WASI configurations. Strict warnings and CTest are
required; root owns registration and generated distribution regeneration.

# Optional Input regex acceptance

The portable matcher is an opt-in synchronous whole-value gate in `cui_edit_apply_checked` and Base/styled Input `.matcher`. A zero descriptor preserves existing behavior and requires no Rust. Public `cui_text_match.h` contains only C11 types; any host/provider can implement its by-value begin/match/end operations.

The source contract is gpui-component0.7.1 at `87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`: nonempty single-line candidate predicates run custom acceptance, token/number validity, then regex boolean matching, with short circuits. Empty values pass without predicates. A failing candidate rejects only if the previous visible value passes; an invalid old value can heal. Hard provider errors never become a false match or healing permission. Final formatting and secure presentation resource preparation happen before the lease or custom callback. IME UPDATE gates normalized unformatted composed text; COMMIT formats once and creates one Undo step. Replay, PRESENT, START/CANCEL and multiline edits do not invoke matching. Host COMMIT rejection ends the host session through the existing Base lifecycle; engine checked rejection preserves the prior prepared session.

A nonempty candidate acquires one lease before the custom predicate; candidate and old evaluation share it. End runs exactly once before adoption, including rejection and hard-error paths. End failure is a hard error while document/history/selection/coalescing and the prior defined IME view remain unchanged. `CUI_EDIT_MATCHER` denotes provider FAILED; STALE and BUSY have separate appended error tags. Invalid provider result codes become INVALID_ARGUMENT. Existing same-model mutation and cache-getter guards cover begin/match/end; unrelated side effects and direct caller-buffer writes are outside protection.

Declare the actual object and optional scratch extents. They must be valid, disjoint from each other and all known model, event payload, session, format and presentation storage. Ops live by value, avoiding a borrowed ops-table pointer. The descriptor is borrowed only during the checked call. A successful begin must publish a non-null lease; a failed begin leaves it untouched. No matcher descriptor or callback is retained in the model after return. Matcher-enabled single-line multi-selection/inline-token requests are explicitly unsupported; raw engine APIs and zero-matcher requests keep their existing behavior. This is partial Input parity, not a full-family claim.

Portable proof: `tests/unit/test_input_matcher.c` covers lease order/counts, custom/mask/regex short circuits, empty/replay bypass, invalid-old healing, all hard errors, unsupported result codes, aliases, callbacks attempting model destruction/insertion, and IME update/rejection/commit/Undo. It passes strict C11 warnings and ASan/UBSan. Unchanged registered CTest passes155/156; the sole failure is expected stale generated distribution after public header/source edits. Root owns regeneration/registration. No global build files or distribution were edited.

Registration needed: include the standalone public `cui_text_match.h` in header/package/amalgamation checks; register `test_input_matcher` linked to ordinary `cui`. Default Core/Base/Components must remain Rust-free. The optional provider is described in the follow-up section once its independent proof is frozen.

## Pinned optional provider

`cui_regex.h` exposes caller-owned zero-initialized compiled and session handles containing opaque state/generation only. Compile copies the pattern and performs the **actual source RegexBuilder admission before** reduced capture-free runtime compilation. Flags cover Unicode (default on), case, multiline, dot-newline, CRLF, greed, whitespace, octal and custom byte line terminator. Explicit limits cover source size/DFA-cache/nesting admission. Zero options preserve source defaults: nest250, NFA10MiB and facade DFA-cache2MiB. Bounded adapter pattern/text limits default1MiB each and can be configured; resource errors are separate from false matching. Pattern/text are UTF-8 spans, including empty/NUL where supported by the provider; the editing model keeps its independent input restrictions.

Create a session with a hard cache heap-byte budget; it owns the prepared runtime cache and retains compiled ownership. Destroying the compiled handle does not invalidate existing sessions. `cui_regex_matcher(&session)` borrows the public session extent/generation. Destroy/rebind while leased returns BUSY without mutation. Rebind prepares a replacement first; failed preparation leaves the session and generation intact. Success changes generation and makes old descriptors STALE; callers refresh their Input `.matcher`. Destroying a session leaves its caller-owned handle alive for stale-descriptor rejection. Generation allocation never wraps; exhaustion returns CAPACITY. The compiled/session handles must remain valid until operations finish; direct pointer tampering and unsynchronized concurrent access are outside the contract.

```c
cui_regex compiled = {0};
cui_regex_session session = {0};
if (cui_regex_compile(cui_string("^[0-9]*$"), (cui_regex_options){0}, &compiled) == CUI_REGEX_OK &&
    cui_regex_session_create(&compiled, 1024 * 1024, &session) == CUI_REGEX_OK) {
    cui_input_options options = {.matcher = cui_regex_matcher(&session)};
    /* Keep session alive while rendering/reducing Input with options. */
    (void)options;
}
/* After the last checked call: */
(void)cui_regex_session_destroy(&session);
(void)cui_regex_destroy(&compiled);
```

Build the optional archive with `scripts/build_regex.py` and the pinned private toolchain/cache as described in `backends/regex/README.md`. Its `pin.json` and lock preserve exact source archive/patch/toolchain provenance. No Rust dependency is introduced into default builds. Default-OFF native Linux CMake/package integration, generated declarations and dependency notices are registered separately from the optional compiled archive.

Measured provider proof uses its actual exported compile/session/begin/match/end API against source Regex1.13.1 across385 successful config/pattern combinations,63 equivalent compile rejections and58,520 matches. Every match makes zero allocator calls, including first use; all eight session allocation positions are forced to fail and restore tracked heap. Source captured-NFA admission limit rejection is explicitly retained even when reduced runtime could fit. Tests preserve the custom line-terminator LookMatcher configuration required for source semantics. Production code never logs text; test failure assertions use synthetic public fixtures.

Native strict C tests cover 1,000 lifecycle loops, leased BUSY, atomic failed rebind, stale/destroyed handles, compiled-owner destruction, malformed UTF-8/options/span/aliases and output preservation. Actual composed styled Input covers typing/paste/cut/delete, Undo/Redo, empty/invalid-old healing, Unicode, readonly, secure masking, IME update/rejection/commit and stale-provider hard failure before custom acceptance. The standalone prebuilt consumer CMake harness passes3/3 CTests. C-side Core/engine/provider/control ASan/UBSan+leak checks pass; Rust itself is not sanitizer-instrumented (allocator-spy/leak accounting covers its tested fallible allocation boundary).

`tests/web/build_regex_fixture.py` builds a real Core/Base/Components Input plus the optional Rust archive into a Zig0.16 WASI **reactor**; global gallery files are untouched. `test_regex_wasi.py` executes the composed C test entrypoint in Wasmtime49 after `_initialize`, with no `_start`. The same module runs in actual Chromium1208 (Playwright1.58). Its existing reusable secure proxy reads finalized Core owner/type/purpose/generation, and CDP `Input.imeSetComposition`/`Input.insertText` exercise real DOM composition through Core events to the CUI Input and provider. Browser assertions cover rejected candidate/provisional view preservation, commit exactly once, rejected host-end cancellation and following typing, Undo/Redo, masking, readonly proxy removal, and Greek Unicode matching. JavaScript performs no regex acceptance.

Reproduce browser proof with `python3 tests/web/build_regex_fixture.py --library WASI_ARCHIVE --output FIXTURE`, then `uv run --offline tests/web/test_input_regex.py --fixture FIXTURE` and `uv run --offline tests/integration/test_regex_wasi.py FIXTURE/regex.wasm`. Provider oracle: use task-local cargo `test --offline --locked --release --manifest-path CACHE/source/Cargo.toml -- --nocapture --test-threads=1` after the build script. Native harness: configure `backends/regex` with `CUI_REGEX_LIBRARY` and `CUI_REGEX_CORE_LIBRARY`, build, run CTest. Optional provider/native/package/browser tests and both public headers are registered; the isolated browser fixture is separate from the production gallery story.

PikeVM's prepared memory is bounded; execution is not deadline-bounded and may be slower than the source facade's adaptive engines for large/dense patterns. Pattern/NFA/cache/text limits control memory and accepted input size, not a guaranteed UI latency. The oracle/fault tests establish this boolean/resource slice; remaining Input contracts and other native platforms are separate work.

## Build and link the optional native provider

Ordinary CUI builds require no Rust toolchain. The portable caller-provided matcher is available in the default C11 library. Enable the regex backend only when you need its Unicode regular-expression implementation.

For the currently verified native Linux target, use an official Rust 1.85.1 prefix and build the separately pinned archive into a private cache:

```sh
python scripts/prepare_regex_toolchain.py --cache build/regex-toolchain
python scripts/build_regex.py --cache build/regex-cache --toolchain build/regex-toolchain/rust-1.85.1
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCUI_BUILD_REGEX=ON \
  -DCUI_REGEX_LIBRARY="$PWD/build/regex-cache/target/release/libcui_regex.a"
cmake --build build
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
cmake --install build --prefix "$PWD/install"
```

The private preparation script verifies the pinned official manifest and both toolchain archives before extraction and installs into the specified cache with ldconfig disabled. The archive build script checks the compiler version and commit, archive checksums, lock and private cache patch before building offline. It does not install Rust or change global Cargo/rustup configuration. Obtain and verify the official toolchain against `backends/regex/pin.json`; the supplied installed prefix is caller-owned tooling. Compiler/target std must match. Native Windows/macOS package acceptance remains unfinished.

Within this source build, link a CMake target against `cui::regex`. Installed consumers use `find_package(CUIRegex CONFIG REQUIRED)` and `target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE CUI::cui_regex)`, with `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` pointing to the installed prefix. The package carries the Core dependency and the Linux archive's system link dependencies. For a direct compiler invocation:

```sh
PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$PWD/install/lib/pkgconfig" \
  cc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic app.c -o app \
  $(PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$PWD/install/lib/pkgconfig" pkg-config --static --cflags --libs cui-regex)
```

Include `cui/cui_regex.h`. Generated distribution headers also contain the matcher and regex declarations, but the optional compiled Rust archive remains a separate link dependency. Defining a distribution implementation macro does not generate the regex engine.

# Optional Unicode regex Input gallery

The Input story's mode 9, **Unicode letters · regex**, uses the compiled optional
provider and anchored pattern `^[\p{L} ]*$`. It accepts Unicode letters and ASCII
spaces, including an empty value, and rejects digits and punctuation through
CUI's existing candidate acceptance. JavaScript does not validate text.

Default browser builds remain C11/Zig builds without Rust or a regex archive:

```sh
python scripts/build_web.py --output build/web
```

`gallery_regex_available()` returns zero and the mode is visibly disabled as
unavailable. The C mode setter also refuses mode 9 when no prepared provider
exists. The other Input modes keep their existing behavior.

To include the real provider, first build the pinned WASI archive using the
optional backend instructions in [INPUT_REGEX.md](INPUT_REGEX.md), then pass it
explicitly:

```sh
python scripts/build_web.py --output build/web-regex \
  --regex-library build/regex-wasi/target/wasm32-wasip1/release/libcui_regex.a
```

The archive must target wasm32-wasip1 and use the pinned backend/toolchain.
`build_web.py` does not invoke Rust or silently download/build a provider. A
missing archive or incompatible link fails the build. This path defines only
the gallery's optional provider seam and exports availability in both builds.

The story prepares its compiled expression and session outside UI frames after
successful gallery setup. Pattern admission is bounded to 64 bytes, candidate
text to 1024 bytes and session cache heap bytes to 1MiB. Failure destroys any
partial session and compiled handle, leaving the option unavailable. Successful
handles occupy stable global storage for the WASM instance lifetime; the matcher
borrows that persistent session, not a stack handle. Candidate acceptance, IME,
Undo and input error behavior are the existing Input/provider contracts.

Selecting this mode produces a complete copyable C11 translation unit, including
zero-initialized caller-owned handles, preparation, persistent-session drawing,
failure cleanup and shutdown cleanup outside a matcher lease. The application
must initialize successfully before drawing and retain its edit/state and
session across frames. The copied unit is a portable API example; link the
optional archive to execute it.

Proofs:

- `tests/test_selected_usage.py`: 270 complete strict C11 units across joined
  Button and Input modes, all 15 design choices and both disabled states.
- `tests/web/test_selected_usage_gallery.py`: actual desktop/mobile clipboard
  equality and strict compilation, including mode 9 when the provider is linked;
  a default build asserts unavailable mode and exercises the other examples.
- `tests/web/test_input_regex_gallery.py`: Wasmtime49 actual gallery initialization,
  typing and rejection with/without the provider (deterministic native-fallback
  metrics), followed by actual linked and default Chromium galleries,
  Unicode typing, rejected punctuation/digits preserving the committed value,
  accepted/rejected provisional IME text, one-step commit Undo/Redo and disabled
  no-archive mode at desktop/mobile widths. It uses finalized CUI text semantics
  and Chromium CDP events rather than a JavaScript acceptance substitute.

Run the browser fixtures with their pinned Playwright environment, passing
`--directory build/web-regex`, `--default-directory build/web`, and an optional
`--chromium` path to the regex interaction fixture. The clipboard fixture takes
`--directory` and `--chromium`.

This demonstrates one real optional provider in the gallery. It does not complete
Input or native provider/platform parity; backend packaging and general matcher
contracts remain documented in the separate regex guide.

# Unwrapped Input visual geometry

An optional `cui_config.text_geometry` factory lets unwrapped styled Input use
host-supplied visual caret, pointer-hit and selection geometry. Core and Base
contain only portable CUI types; they do not depend on native fonts, HarfBuzz or
platform APIs. Existing measurement-only configurations keep their established
Input path. Textarea and automatically wrapped paragraph provenance are separate
integration work.

Native hosts using a `cui_font *` as `measure_user` can register:

```c
cui_config config = {
    .measure_user = font,
    .measure = cui_font_measure,
    .measure_styled = cui_font_measure_styled,
    .font_metrics = cui_font_get_metrics,
    .text_geometry = cui_font_text_geometry,
};
```

Register explicit font fallbacks on `font` before use. The callback shares
`measure_user`, so a host using a wrapper object for measurement must supply a
matching geometry adapter that calls `cui_font_text_geometry(wrapper->font, ...)`.
No OS font discovery occurs. Native BIDI-off builds retain the factory symbol
and return `CUI_TEXT_LAYOUT_UNAVAILABLE` without changing output.

## Factory and query contract

`cui_get_text_geometry` calls the optional factory with original UTF-8 bytes,
size and style. It preserves the caller's output on failure and rejects malformed
or nonfinite session metadata. A successful `cui_text_geometry` owns its session
and exposes an operation table that stays valid until release. Text is borrowed
only during factory creation: the factory must retain everything its later
queries need. Each successful session requires one
`cui_release_text_geometry`; the helper zeros the handle so a second release is
harmless. Core defensively releases a partial session returned with a failure
when it supplies a valid release operation.

Queries use original byte offsets. Carets report at most two affinities at an
exact supported boundary: upstream attaches to the preceding logical cluster,
downstream to the following cluster. Native dual caret positions come from the
actual bidi runs and shaped cluster advance pens. Hit tests choose the nearest
visual cluster edge. Selection queries normalize reversed endpoints in the
native implementation and return complete-cluster rectangles in visual order;
a mixed-direction logical range can have disconnected coverage. NULL output
with zero capacity queries the required count. INVALID and CAPACITY preserve
both output buffers and counts; buffers/counts must be disjoint. Hit-test
failure preserves its output. Native queries reject nonfinite points.

`cui_font_text_geometry` wraps the existing owned native line layout. It retains
the actual root/registered/fallback faces and shaped arrays, and does not retain
or reread the caller's text buffer. Its queries remain usable after source
mutation, owned fallback replacement, or closing the root font. A font handle
is still required for future factory, measurement and raster calls; this does
not authorize closing a host font before ordinary rendering finishes. Native
factory input is one unwrapped line: hard paragraph separators and U+2028 are
rejected. Empty text has two affinities at x=0.

## Input lifetime and behavior

Input owns a private immutable source copy and the session in a context
resource, keyed by widget ID. Caller `cui_input_state` receives no new handle or
cleanup duty. Reduction and paint share one session for matching bytes/size in
that frame. A same-frame text mutation releases it and builds a fresh session
before further hit testing or painting. Beginning the next frame releases the
previous session, so font registration changes are observed; omitted widgets
and context destruction also release it exactly once. Model rebinding clears
stored affinity, and text revision changes invalidate that affinity. Resource
collection never dereferences a previous model pointer.

The visual session supplies caret x, pointer hit, selection spans, horizontal
reveal and the IME candidate-window x. Pointer-selected upstream/downstream
positions persist through event-free repaint, including a boundary whose two
affinities have different visual x positions. Logical keyboard movement keeps
its existing edit model behavior; a new logical boundary defaults to downstream
(or the sole available edge at a line end). Geometry does not implement visual
arrow navigation.

Selection and composition underlines use individual visual spans. Their
vertical extent uses the existing Input line box, while the native text path
keeps its common fallback baseline. Text and placeholders use one unwrapped
line on the visual path. IME geometry resolves the actual painted caret child's
final bounds after layout through `cui_set_text_input_geometry_rect`, so changes
in size, alignment and viewport origin do not use the previous frame's position.
Query the final candidate rectangle after `cui_end_frame`.

The context resource requires one additional slot when geometry is configured.
Its private source copy is bounded to 65,535 bytes; selection/composition
workspace is bounded to 4,096 rectangles each. These nested allocations are
released with the resource. Failure to allocate or exceeding these bounds uses
the documented legacy geometry fallback. A context resource capacity error
remains observable through `cui_last_error`.

Host font/style registrations must remain consistent between measurement,
geometry creation and ordinary rasterization of a completed draw list. After
changing host font metrics outside a frame, call `cui_text_metrics_changed` to
refresh Core's measurement cache before the next frame.

## Explicit limits and fallback policy

Native geometry accepts complete shaped-cluster boundaries. A UTF-8/grapheme
boundary inside a ligature or merged mark cluster can return INVALID. Input
then uses its measurement-only geometry for that whole painted line, preserving
the editor's original logical anchor/cursor bytes. It does not silently snap
editing offsets to a nearby glyph or claim that this fallback is visually correct
for interior ligature carets. Factory/query UNAVAILABLE, INVALID, MEMORY,
MISSING_GLYPH and CAPACITY likewise use the legacy path. The public factory and
query APIs expose those statuses for callers requiring strict geometry.

`cui_base_input_hit_test` tries the optional visual host for reusable callers;
`cui_base_input_measured_hit_test` explicitly requests the legacy scalar prefix
path. `cui_base_input_visual_hit_test` consumes a borrowed session, maps viewport
and scroll coordinates, and returns the original byte offset; an optional
caller affinity output is unchanged on failed or nonfinite hits. Native
cluster-edge hits are still checked by the editor's UTF-8/grapheme selection
rules.

This is not full international editing parity: no GDEF interior ligature
carets, cross-run grapheme analysis, visual arrow navigation, multi-line
geometry, automatic Unicode line breaking or Textarea integration is claimed.
Automatically wrapped Core commands still lose original paragraph context;
the audit preserves that evidence separately.

## Validation

Portable headless tests exercise owned session cleanup, malformed/nonfinite and
capacity results, unchanged caller outputs, model rebinding, size changes,
private source copies, same-frame edits, omitted-widget cleanup and explicit
interior fallback without changing logical selection. Native tests compare the
factory with styled metrics and keep querying after owned fallback replacement
and root close. Enabled and BIDI-off API checks are included.

`tests/integration/test_native_text_geometry.c` defaults to a passing unwrapped
Input suite with actual Hebrew, Hebrew marks, mixed Latin/Hebrew/numbers,
dual-affinity idle repaint and supported Arabic joining/mark fixtures. It
compares real selection paint/IME/hits to native geometry, verifies HarfBuzz
source glyph/cluster/advance data and actual nonzero raster pixels, and reports
optional font cases explicitly. `--audit` retains the known Textarea and
wrapped-paragraph failures. No missing-glyph raster counts as success.

# Bounded inset shadows

`cui_set_box_shadows` copies up to eight total DROP and INSET layers onto the open box. It replaces the complete list. Zero count clears both phases; the existing drop-only setter also replaces the complete list, so it clears previous insets. Invalid kinds, counts, dimensions, radii or nonfinite values fail before changing the owner. Existing drop APIs and enum values retain their behavior.

```c
cui_box_shadow layers[] = {
    {.layer = {.offset_y = 2, .sigma = 3, .color = {0, 0, 0, 64}},
     .kind = CUI_BOX_SHADOW_DROP},
    {.layer = {.spread = 2, .sigma = 1, .color = {0, 0, 0, 96}},
     .kind = CUI_BOX_SHADOW_INSET}
};
/* Between begin_box and end_box. Failure leaves the previous list intact. */
bool ok = cui_set_box_shadows(ui, layers, 2, (cui_corner_radii){4, 4, 4, 4});
```

DROP layers paint before the background. INSET layers paint after the background, before local mesh/underlay/prepaint content and children. Supplied order survives within each phase. Both use ancestor opacity and the current ancestor mask, before the box's own child-overflow clip. Shadows create no interactions or semantics. The existing outline and ordinary content/border paths keep their prior ordering.

The source hole is the original caster offset by the layer, dilated by **negative** spread. Positive spread shrinks the hole. Original radii clamp against the original caster; hole radii are `max(original_clamped_radius - spread,0)`, with no second hole-size clamp. Materialized source f32 origin/size determine the far edge before physical floor/ceil covering. Even a logically collapsed hole can cover a physical pixel. Sigma-zero coverage uses the source SDF ramp and unrounded `max(qx,qy)` fast path. Gaussian coverage uses source erf/four-midpoint integration without a DROP support-rectangle cutoff. The result complements the raw hole convolution and multiplies independent element SDF coverage, then clamps/quantizes for straight RGBA8 storage.

Scene insertion/culling uses the **covered hole**. Rasterization and final cropping use the **covered element**, intersected with the covered ancestor mask and target. An empty or mask-disjoint hole suppresses the whole primitive even if the element overlaps. An intersecting hole can produce inset pixels in element regions outside that hole. This intentionally follows pinned gpui-pre 0.3.8 Scene behavior; it is not an unconditional mathematical complement for an empty hole.

`cui_effect_inset_shadow_query` returns logical raster placement, physical integer `covered_hole` and `covered_element`, and raster dimensions/bytes. The raster is the covered element, without Gaussian tail expansion. Query validates before publishing output. `cui_effect_inset_shadow_sample` evaluates a physical point and returns zero outside the element or for an intrinsically empty hole. These pure functions have no ancestor-mask input; mask-dependent insertion culling belongs to the prepared renderer. `cui_effect_inset_shadow_raster` validates the entire caller-owned buffer before writing. No pure operation allocates or retains caller pointers.

`CUI_DRAW_INSET_SHADOW` is appended; its `shadow` field stores the paint by value. `cui_prepaint_inset_shadow` emits this value into the existing bounded writer and supports deferred output. Count the emitted command and its clip wrappers in the callback's budget. The payload registration copies values; contained host pointers remain borrowed under the existing prepaint contract. Manual callbacks choose their own surface/layer order. They cannot call layout, semantics or Core mutation during prepaint.

The portable supported domain matches DROP: finite caster coordinates/dimensions up to16384 (dimensions nonnegative), absolute offset/spread up to4096, radii in[0,16384], sigma in[0,256]; uniform scale[1/65536,64], origin magnitude up to1048576. Positive physical sigma below `4*sqrt(FLT_MIN)` is explicitly rejected; sigma0 is separate. Raster sides are at most16384 and total raster area at most16M texels. Hole geometry is not charged as a raster allocation. DROP/INSET share the eight-layer limit,64 cache entries and combined64MiB owned CPU/upload budget. Unsupported nonuniform shadow transforms and resource failures reject before target resize/clear or swapchain acquisition. Frames without shadows keep their existing transform behavior. Existing late SDL GPU acquisition failures retain their legal-submit/previous-surface boundary.

Software uses existing physical coordinates. SDL Renderer derives actual presentation/scale/viewport; SDL GPU and Sokol derive actual target/list projection. All native paths preflight resources, then paint the prepared cropped physical bitmap without applying another rounded element clip. Cache keys distinguish kind, paint values, transform and f32 phase; alpha-only changes reuse coverage. Normalized translation reuse requires both hole and element geometry to agree with actual checked covering. All prepared resources remain pinned until their frame submission; an earlier prepared frame expires when preparing another frame.

Canvas's reusable module recognizes `type:'insetShadow'` alongside `'shadow'`, with the same sixteen copied paint values. Its rasterizer/query accept an optional fifth argument `kind` (0 DROP,1 INSET). Existing DROP calls remain unchanged. New C bridge exports are `cui_canvas_inset_shadow_query`, `cui_canvas_inset_shadow_prepare`, and `cui_canvas_inset_shadow_element_bound`. Existing layer-bound getter returns the covered hole for inset; existing raster getters return the covered-element raster. Prepare reads the actual `ctx.getTransform()` uniform scale/origin before backing-dimension assignment or clear. Draw requires ordinary Canvas clips suspended/restored because prepared crops own physical mask coverage. WASM pixels are copied into cache-owned images before subsequent bridge calls. Gallery serialization/export wiring belongs to the integrating host.

Headless proofs cover literal square inset pixels, asymmetric independent radii, source square SDF diagonal, element AA, Gaussian complement versus independent double rectangle convolution, beyond-hole support, fractional collapse, zero/invalid/small-sigma atomics, copied Core/prepaint values, mixed phase/translucent/ancestor composition, legacy clearing, hole-mask culling, cross-kind and translation cache reuse, and bounded cache-slot failure preserving pixels. Native integration probes preserve actual DROP compatibility and compare INSET pixels through SDL Renderer pre-Present readback, SDL GPU Vulkan and Sokol GL at scales1/2. Canvas WASM covers DPR1/2, literal pixels, Gaussian/asymmetric composition and rejection before clear. The inset source fixture pins exact dependency/file hashes.

This capability follows the pinned public inset contract within the declared portable domain. Native GPUI Metal/WGPU shader/target-format/Hsla/transcendental/AA image identity remains unverified. Named convenience shadow factories and unrelated component owners remain separate contracts; no full BoxShadow or Chart family completion is claimed.

Small uniform target scales retain the checked physical raster budgets. A normalized translation that exceeds the public caster domain falls back to the original validated paint and origin; it does not widen that domain. Shadow bitmap dimensions use the already checked physical raster rather than the ordinary logical bitmap size cap. The headless cache, actual SDL Renderer, and Canvas probes cover this fallback and rejected-frame preservation.

SDL Renderer draws prepared shadows in physical target coordinates and restores logical presentation, scale, viewport, and clip before subsequent commands. Real OpenGL and software readback fixtures cover the tiny-scale edge oracle and normal-scale ordinary drawing after shadow emission; this does not change ordinary command geometry at extreme SDL scales.
