# Installed native text validation

Run on Linux with native FreeType, HarfBuzz and SDL3 development/runtime dependencies available:

```sh
python tests/packaging/test_installed_text.py \
  --artifacts /path/to/native-artifacts \
  --font /usr/share/fonts/noto/NotoSans-Regular.ttf \
  --rtl-font /usr/share/fonts/noto/NotoSansHebrew-Regular.ttf \
  --build-dir /tmp/cui-installed-text
```

The artifact directory must contain exactly one Python wheel and one prebuilt npm
`.tgz`. This test never installs packages, downloads dependencies or starts a
window. It removes display variables, selects SDL's dummy driver, extracts only
ordinary archive files/directories into a temporary directory and compiles the
existing `sdk_text_fixture.c` against each package's headers and bundled
`libcui_bridge.so`. No package source is rebuilt or substituted for those libraries.
The canonical reference is built from this checkout with native text and bidi
support. `--reference-build DIR` can reuse a matching canonical build containing
`libcui_text.a`, `libcui.a` and `libcui_bidi.a`; the caller must ensure that build
matches the source being validated.

The shared fixture asserts contextual bidi geometry, invalid byte-range rejection,
RTL runs, fallback faces, nonzero glyph IDs, selection/caret behavior and colored
raster coverage. UNAVAILABLE results and missing RTL/fallback/color coverage fail
its assertions. Choose a primary font without Hebrew coverage so the fallback
assertion is meaningful. All printed fixture values must match canonical output
using exactly the same fonts on the same host. Font, artifact and library SHA256
values are printed. Library hashes are checked against wheel RECORD and any
provided build-info library SHA256 metadata; explicitly non-native metadata fails.

This proves packaged C text behavior. It does not prove Python/Node wrapper text
API coverage, package installation behavior, SDL rendering, GPU behavior or
cross-host raster reproducibility. Run `scripts/test_binding_packages.py --native
--require-prebuilt` separately for actual installed binding UI consumers under
its dedicated invisible Xvfb display.
documents.docs/INTERACTION.md:
# Interaction and touch routing

## Custom clickable rows

Register interaction before opening the box, using the same stable, nonzero ID
for both. The box supplies geometry; `cui_interact` supplies semantics and routed
input. Register each ID once per frame. For an action row without child controls:

```c
bool mail_row(cui_context *ui, cui_id id, const cui_theme *theme,
              cui_str sender, cui_str preview, bool selected) {
    cui_interaction in = cui_interact(ui, id, CUI_ROLE_BUTTON, sender,
                                      false, false, 0);
    cui_color fill = in.pressed ? theme->accent
                     : in.hovered ? theme->surface
                     : selected ? theme->accent : theme->background;
    cui_begin_box(ui, id, (cui_box){.width = -1, .padding = 8,
        .background = fill, .border_width = in.focus_visible ? 1 : 0,
        .border = theme->focus});
    cui_text(ui, sender, theme->font_size, theme->text);
    cui_text(ui, preview, theme->font_size, theme->muted);
    cui_end_box(ui);
    return in.activated;
}
/* During a frame: if (mail_row(...)) open_message(...); */
```

`hovered` paints hover, `pressed` paints the held pointer/keyboard state,
`focus_visible` requests the keyboard focus indicator, and `activated` triggers
the action once. Selection remains application state. Input uses completed-frame
hit geometry, so submit the same IDs every frame and establish a frame before
injecting pointer input. A button role provides ordinary Tab/Enter/Space action
behavior. `CUI_ROLE_LISTITEM` describes passive list membership; it does not
automatically add button keyboard behavior or list selection/navigation. Prefer
an existing choice/list component when you need that interaction model. Keep
nested interactive children out of this simple row recipe.

Core accepts mouse, touch, and pen pointer events. Existing zero-initialized
`cui_event` callers remain mouse callers. Touch adapters supply a stable
`pointer_id` until up/cancel, paired with portable `pointer_device` (zero
when the host has no device namespace). SDL preserves both `touchID` and
`fingerID`; identical finger IDs on two devices remain separate contacts. Core retains at most 16 contacts; excess contacts
are ignored. The public queue accepts 256 events per frame; separate bounded
512-event dispatch storage reserves room for every possible touch-capture
cancellation without dropping queued events. SDL finger coordinates are normalized by SDL and converted to
logical window pixels. The browser uses PointerEvents and pointer capture,
with `touch-action: none` on the canvas. Both adapters suppress compatibility
mouse clicks generated by touch.

One contact presses and taps through the ordinary focus/activation path.
Movement beyond eight logical pixels prevents tap activation; ordinary control
drag events remain available when no scroll/viewport owner claims the gesture.
Sliders, scrollbars, and focusable Separator resize handles retain pointer
drag ownership over their scroll ancestors. A custom draggable ID can use
`cui_set_touch_drag_priority(ui, id, true)` after registration; this preserves
its other semantics and takes priority over ancestor scroll/viewport pan.
Cursor selection does not affect drag policy. Pan takeover sends a targeted
Cancel event to the formerly pressed control before later queued contacts,
clearing retained selection/drag flags. A second contact cancels primary activation. Lifting one finger does not turn
the remaining finger into a new tap. Cancel/focus loss clears capture.

Scroll owners accept touch scrolling by default, or can opt out using
`touch_scroll_disabled` in semantic details. Once the eight-pixel threshold is
crossed, touch moves become precise `CUI_EVENT_SCROLL` events. Their deltas are
logical pixels with the same sign convention as wheel input. The initially
hit owner is retained by ID; routing can chain only to its actual ancestors
when its configured range reaches an edge. Hit routing respects clipping,
modal scopes, disabled owners, and higher interactive portal layers. Scroll
end/cancel events carry zero deltas. Reducers must use one pixel per precise
delta instead of their ordinary wheel line size. There is no inertial fling. Internal contact subtraction, centers and pinch
distances use double intermediates; generated deltas/scales saturate to the
finite float range. Non-finite input contact positions are ignored while
cancel can still terminate their lifecycle.

Viewport panning and pinch zoom are explicit opt-ins, independent of scrolling:

```c
cui_id plot = cui_id_from(ui, "plot");
cui_rect previous_bounds = cui_bounds(ui, plot);
size_t count;
const cui_event *events = cui_frame_events(ui, &count);
for (size_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    if (events[i].type != CUI_EVENT_GESTURE ||
        cui_event_target(ui, i) != plot || cui_event_consumed(ui, i))
        continue;
    cui_plot_pan(&scale, events[i].dx);
    cui_plot_zoom(&scale, events[i].gesture_scale,
                  events[i].x - previous_bounds.x);
    cui_consume_event(ui, i);
}
cui_plot_view(ui, plot, &theme, &view);
cui_set_gestures(ui, plot, true, true);
cui_set_cursor(ui, plot, CUI_CURSOR_GRAB);
```

`gesture_scale` is relative to the previous contact positions (one for pan
or end/cancel); `x/y` are the current center in window coordinates. `dx/dy`
are center movement when pan is enabled. `scroll_phase` carries started,
moved, ended, or cancelled. Pinch requires exactly two contacts owned by the
same viewport. Zoom is disabled unless `gesture_zoom` is explicitly enabled.
The gallery Plot opts in and applies both transformations to its scale.

Every registered interactive ID can use the shared hooks after its component
has built, including IDs inside compound controls:

```c
cui_id button = cui_id_from(ui, "run");
cui_theme styled = theme;
cui_interaction before = button_state; /* Caller-retained state from last frame. */
if (before.pressed) styled.primary = theme.danger;
else if (before.hovered) styled.primary = theme.info;
if (cui_button(ui, button, &styled, cui_string("Run"), false)) run_action();
cui_set_cursor(ui, button, CUI_CURSOR_CROSSHAIR);
button_state = cui_interaction_state(ui, button);

cui_id toggle = cui_id_from(ui, "pin");
cui_toggle_ex(ui, toggle, &theme, cui_string("Pin"), &pinned, NULL,
              cui_toggle_options_default());
cui_set_cursor(ui, toggle, CUI_CURSOR_HELP);
cui_interaction state = cui_interaction_state(ui, toggle);
```

`cui_set_cursor`, `cui_set_gestures`, and `cui_set_touch_drag_priority` change only their named fields and
preserve the component's scroll range, role, focus behavior, relationships,
and accessibility details. Apply them each frame after the component.
`cui_interaction_state` does not register semantics or consume activation.
It reports hover, pressed, focus, focus-visible, and activation for an ID
already registered in the current frame (previous frame when outside a frame).
Hover follows clipped/modal hit visibility and can apply to passive registered
viewport IDs. Pointer activation is a tap/click released over its captured
control, or the existing keyboard activation. A queried activation remains
visible after `cui_interact` consumes it; explicit
`cui_cancel_event_activation` removes it. Build a component before querying it during a frame. For styling before its
build, query the preceding completed frame and retain the result in caller
state. `cui_interact` remains the registration/activation-consuming API.

Built-in cursors include default, pointer, text, horizontal/vertical resize,
move, not-allowed, crosshair, grab, grabbing, zoom-in, zoom-out, wait, and help.
Browser mappings use matching CSS cursor names. SDL has no corresponding
system cursors for grab/grabbing, zoom, or help: its fallback is move for
hands, crosshair for zoom, and default for help. Its cursor cache is bounded
by the built-in enum count and is destroyed with the adapter. Caller-owned
custom RGBA cursor images/hotspots are not implemented by this API.

## Coverage inventory

| Path | Shared behavior and evidence | Remaining coverage limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Registered interactive controls (Button, Toggle, Checkbox, Radio, Switch, choice rows, toolbar items, numeric controls, and compound child IDs) | Core identity/tap/press/cancel, state query, and cursor hooks; Core tests verify tap, repeated non-consuming state query, cursor override, multi-contact ghost suppression, drag versus tap and cancel | Each of the 78 families is not separately touch/device tested; dragging controls keep their ordinary pointer reducers |
| Scrollable, Sidebar, VirtualList | Shared precise-scroll reducer used by these scroll owners; styled/base Scrollable tests verify threshold, exact pixel offsets, release, and no row activation, including a full 256-event input queue with targeted cancellation; nested actual Slider/Resizable and custom drag-policy tests verify the ancestor does not steal their drag | Device tests directly exercise Scrollable; Sidebar/VirtualList reuse the reducer but are not independently touchscreen tested |
| Textarea and Editor | Textarea precise pixel scrolling (Editor uses its text view); Textarea tests verify fractional precise delta and cancellation of retained selection dragging on pan takeover | Editor touch selection/completion/folding interactions are not separately device tested |
| Table | Existing Table reducers already consume scroll deltas as pixels; Core routes contact pans to registered body/header owners | Table-specific touchscreen scrolling has not been added |
| MessageScroller | Precise delta respects pixels; Message tests verify fractional offset | Touch prepend anchoring and jump actions are not separately device tested |
| Tree, tabs, choice/list/menu panels, Surface bodies | Precision-aware existing reducers; Tree/Tab/Surface tests verify fractional pixel deltas; row-window choice/menu converts pixels to retained row units | Variable-height menu touch sequences and every popup combination are not separately device tested |
| Nested ownership, clipping, portal/modal routing | Core tests combine touch threshold with nested range chaining, portal occlusion, disabled viewport and cancel; existing hit-routing tests remain in suite | No cross-device full interaction matrix is claimed |
| Opt-in viewport | Core tests verify relative scale/center, zoom disabled by default, cancellation, disabled owner; Plot gallery applies pan/pinch | Applications must implement domain transformations and consume gesture events; other views do not automatically zoom |
| Native SDL adapter | Native SDL event injection tests verify normalized finger coordinates/identity and exclusion of touch-generated mouse events, including two device namespaces sharing a finger ID; cursor enumeration/cache checks | System cursor fallbacks listed above; no custom RGBA cursor. The legacy poller consumes the process-wide SDL event queue and scales fingers using its own window; multiwindow routing is not validated |
| Browser adapter | `tests/web/test_touch.py` drives real Chromium CDP touch tap, drag suppression, cancel, threshold pixel pan, and two-contact Plot pinch | No physical-device, Safari, or Firefox claim; existing mouse/keyboard/wheel browser suite is separate |

This inventory describes shared infrastructure and the tested cases. It does
not establish complete source parity or verification of all manifest families.

# Frozen initial integration contract
Core types in include/cui/cui.h; core implementation src/core/cui.c. Public C11, no Clay/platform types. All dimensions logical pixels. Width/height 0 fits contents, negative grows, positive fixed. Explicit begin/end element composition backed by Clay. Frame strings copied to context frame arena; draw-list/semantic pointers valid until next begin. Context fixed capacities reported by errors, no per-frame allocation. Single UI thread across contexts: Clay's current context is switched by adapter, not safe concurrent calls. Input events queue before begin, dispatched against previous frame regions in order; first frame has no targets. Controls consume per-ID activation exactly once. Focus is retained only for submitted enabled controls; cancellation clears capture. Stable scoped 64-bit IDs with debug duplicate detection; Clay uses a folded internal ID.
Renderer vtable consumes draw list synchronously; returns bool and reports actual backend/capabilities. Platform produces generic events and owns OS resources. Text measurement callback is independent, default approximate metrics explicitly documented. Base owns interactions; style wrappers call base and theme tokens. Worker changes to public contract require integrator coordination.

Ownership: core worker core header/source/tests; base/style worker base/theme/components and tests; graphics worker backends/text/gallery. Integrator build/scripts/docs/manifest. Workers use isolated git worktrees and commit scoped changes; no direct mainline edits.

# Keyboard shortcut hints

`cui/cui_kbd.h` adds `cui_kbd_ex` for a typed **single chord**, preserving the
existing literal `cui_kbd` and byte-preserving `cui_kbd_format` APIs unchanged.
It displays hints only: no shortcut registration, action lookup, sequence
recognition, activation or global event dispatch occurs.

The frozen source stores one Keystroke. Binding lookup takes the first stroke;
several hints in its story are ordinary sibling components. The earlier
“grouped shortcut rendering” manifest phrase does not identify a missing
multi-shortcut source API. See the pinned [audit](design/KBD_SOURCE_AUDIT.md).
Compose hints normally, as in this complete C11 draw function:

```c
#include "cui/cui_kbd.h"

bool draw_shortcut_hints(cui_context *ui, const cui_theme *theme,
                          bool mac_symbols) {
    cui_begin_box(ui, 100, (cui_box){.row = true, .gap = 8});
    bool palette = cui_kbd_ex(ui, 101, theme,
        (cui_kbd_stroke){.modifiers = CUI_MOD_META | CUI_MOD_SHIFT,
                         .key = CUI_STR("p")},
        (cui_kbd_options){.mac_symbols = mac_symbols});
    bool escape = cui_kbd_ex(ui, 102, theme,
        (cui_kbd_stroke){.key = CUI_STR("escape")},
        (cui_kbd_options){.outline = true, .mac_symbols = mac_symbols,
                          .accessible_name = CUI_STR("Escape key")});
    cui_end_box(ui);
    return palette && escape;
}
```

Call inside an active frame. The host selects platform convention explicitly:
CTRL/ALT/SHIFT/META display in that order, as text with `+` or macOS symbols
without separators. `META` is Win or Command. Host parser aliases such as
`secondary` must be resolved by the host; the component does not guess a keymap.
ASCII first letters become uppercase; known lower-case key names map to source
labels, including Esc, Enter/⏎, Backspace/⌫, Delete/⌫, arrow names/symbols and
Page Up/Page Down. Function keys and literal `+`/`-` work without a parser.

`cui_kbd_format_stroke` returns required bytes **excluding NUL**. It accepts
NULL output for size queries and capacity0 without writing; positive capacity
always NUL-terminates valid output within that capacity, truncating only complete
UTF-8 scalars. Invalid input returns SIZE_MAX and leaves the output unchanged.
Input key must be nonempty strict single-line UTF-8, at most128 bytes, with no
embedded NUL or ASCII control characters. Unknown modifier bits are invalid.
The four existing portable flags are the only accepted mask. The longest result
is147 bytes, so internal required-count arithmetic cannot overflow. The output
buffer may overlap the input key. Non-ASCII casing is preserved: full Unicode
uppercase conversion from the Rust source is not implemented.

Zero options draw the source-shaped muted pill: muted foreground/background,
12-unit text at16-unit rem, horizontal padding4, vertical padding2, minimum
width20 and half theme radius. Outline adds a1-unit border and uses the theme
background. `plain=true` wins over outline and renders text at the theme font
and color without pill padding/border/minimum. CUI maps rem to
`theme.font_size/16`; the font must be finite(0,512], radius finite/nonnegative.
It does not provide arbitrary GPUI Styled modifiers or a general inherited
parent text-style stack. CUI solid theme tokens are the supported palette;
this is not proof of every upstream theme/background representation.

Hints are noninteractive LABEL semantics, excluded from tab traversal. The
accessible name defaults to formatted text; an explicit name overrides it.
Names must be strict single-line UTF-8 up to1024 bytes, without embedded NUL
or ASCII controls. Invalid arguments fail before layout or semantics. Input
strings and local formatted output are copied into Core frame storage at
submission and survive through that frame's renderer consumption. No retained
component state, allocator or cleanup is required.

Ordinary row composition fits its contents; it does not automatically turn a
shortcut list into a responsive wrapping grid. For narrow help panels, let the
owner split rows using the host's available-width/layout policy. Joining multiple
strokes into one sequence or looking up host Action/context/focus/global
bindings remains outside this API. Do not promote full Kbd parity from these
formatting and presentation additions.

The standalone worker fixture compiles the exact example and tests named-key
formatting, all output capacities, UTF-8/control rejection and overlap, normal/
outline/plain geometry, theme scaling, actual software fill pixels, text draw
colors, semantics and ordinary sibling composition. It checks legacy helpers
remain unchanged. Text rasterization is not claimed by portable pixel tests.
New sources require root-owned canonical source/test registration and matching
SDK/consumer-resource regeneration before distribution.

Worker validation used strict C11 Release (`-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror`):
`kbd_source` and the existing `content` regression passed through the private
headless wrapper. The exact guide example compiled against the real header,
and strict C++11 header syntax passed. No native windows or browser were opened.

```sh
cmake -S tests/fixtures/kbd -B /path/to/private-build -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS='-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror'
cmake --build /path/to/private-build --target test_kbd kbd_guide test_content
python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir /path/to/private-build -- -R '^(kbd_source|content)$'
```

# Source label contract

The additive `cui_label.h` API complements the legacy `cui_label` plain text wrapper.
`cui_label_prepare` produces caller-owned display bytes and sorted nonoverlapping
color spans. `cui_label_source` copies those bytes into Core frame storage.
Initialize options to zero and provide `primary`. `has_secondary` adds exactly
one ASCII space even if either string is empty. Secondary text and its preceding
space use theme muted foreground. Matches override either foreground with theme
info (the semantic blue). `custom_color` changes primary foreground. A supplied
`color` is inert unless `custom_color` is true; zero initialization uses theme text.
Caller-selected error presentation uses `custom_color = true` and `color = theme.danger`.
Secondary text stays muted and matches override either foreground, including
matches that cross the primary/secondary separator. Masked bullets use the selected
base foreground uniformly and never emit secondary/highlight spans. Font size,
weight, italic, monospace and family are forwarded; line height defaults to
20 logical pixels, matching the source's 1.25rem at its 16px root size.

The frozen `crates/component/src/label.rs:53-59,61-91,192-215` has no disabled or
error state flags; it accepts inherited Styled text color. Its website error
example (`website/component/label.md:231-233`) selects `theme.destructive` through
`.text_color(...)`. C's caller color option covers that presentation rather than
adding an invented validation/disabled API. Required/optional markers likewise
remain ordinary secondary text. `test_label_source` checks prepared spans and real
Core draw commands for default and caller error foregrounds, muted secondary text,
a Unicode highlight crossing the separator, alpha preservation, default theme font
and 20px line metrics, and masked display/semantic privacy with a custom color.

Matching uses Unicode 17.0.0 default, locale-independent lowercase, including
one-to-many mappings and contextual Greek final sigma. Full matching finds all
overlapping occurrences; prefix matching considers only the start. Empty matches
are inert. Matching performs no normalization or full case folding: sharp-s and
SS are distinct. Lowercase positions map back to original UTF-8 scalar boundaries,
so expanding mappings and byte-width changes cannot split a scalar or shift later
matches. This deliberately repairs the source implementation's reuse of lowercase
byte offsets and original search length, which can miscolor or split Unicode text.
A match covering part of an expanded lowercase scalar colors that whole scalar.

Masking emits one U+2022 bullet per Unicode scalar of the combined text, including
the separator. It emits no highlight spans, and neither draw paragraph nor optional
semantic name contains original bytes. Inputs remain owned by the caller; this API
is not a secret-storage or memory-erasure facility. Optional `semantic_id` creates
a label node; `control` sets Core controls and focus_target relations. Masked nodes
are marked secret. Applications set the controlled widget's `labelled_by` relation
when they need that reverse accessibility relation.

All input strings require strict UTF-8. Prepare rejects invalid arguments, overflow,
allocation failure and insufficient capacity without changing text, spans or the
result structure. Output buffers must not overlap each other or input strings.
The text output is length-delimited with no NUL terminator. Span capacity is bounded
by Core's 4096 span maximum. Renderer failures are returned; an allocation failure
inside Core after beginning an optional semantic box can leave an empty box.

Rendering now submits a complete colored text paragraph through Core, wraps at
its current-frame parent width, and stacks hard paragraphs and empty lines.
CRLF is one break; LF, CR, NEL, paragraph separator and the Core information
separators also start new paragraphs. U+2028 starts a visual line while preserving
the full original bidi paragraph for shaping. Spans crossing either explicit or
automatic line boundaries are clipped and rebased to each draw command's original
UTF-8 paragraph. Blank and trailing lines contribute their configured line height.
`no_wrap` disables automatic wrapping while retaining explicit line breaks.
Masking occurs before line layout, so original paragraph separators become bullets
and reveal neither source text nor original newline structure.

The frozen Label source uses StyledText from its pinned gpui-pre 0.3.8 dependency.
That measured layout chooses the definite current parent width when normal white
space is enabled. The additive Core paragraph API supplies that available-width
behavior without relying on previous-frame label bounds. The prior single-line
and hard-separator rejection restrictions are removed.

Core now uses the pinned measured wrapping candidates, including punctuation,
Unicode word ranges and fallback inside long tokens. Trailing spaces remain in
the preceding visual row. Unicode 17 graphemes and provider shaping clusters
are kept intact during fallback; this deliberately strengthens the source's
individual-glyph fallback. See [the wrapping contract](UNICODE_WRAP.md) for the
exact policy, resource limits and measurement-only host limitations.
`alignment` supports physical left (default), center and right per visual row,
using current-frame available width. See [the alignment contract](TEXT_ALIGNMENT.md).
Arbitrary GPUI style refinement remains incomplete. Root-relative rem scaling
must be supplied through line_height when the application's root size differs
from 16. The legacy wrapper remains unchanged.

The general `cui_text_paragraph_colored` Core API validates all UTF-8 and full-text
color spans before publication. Invalid input and conservative storage/element
preflight failures publish no layout. Per-draw clipped spans require bounded frame
storage during final layout; exhaustion empties the draw list under Core's usual
capacity-error contract. The pre-existing unwrapped contextual APIs retain their
validation rules. `test_contextual_wrap_source` covers paragraph-relative spans,
Unicode separators, empty lines, current-frame reflow, measurement identity and
preflight failures. With `CUI_TEST_WRAP_RENDERER` it additionally renders colored
wrapped text through the real software font renderer and verifies a copied draw
snapshot after frame invalidation.

## Pinned Unicode provenance

Generated tables in `src/components/cui_label.c` derive from official Unicode 17:

- https://www.unicode.org/Public/17.0.0/ucd/UnicodeData.txt
  SHA256 `2e1efc1dcb59c575eedf5ccae60f95229f706ee6d031835247d843c11d96470c`
- https://www.unicode.org/Public/17.0.0/ucd/SpecialCasing.txt
  SHA256 `efc25faf19de21b92c1194c111c932e03d2a5eaf18194e33f1156e96de4c9588`
- Vendored `third_party/unicode/17.0.0/DerivedCoreProperties.txt`, pinned by its
  adjacent manifest, supplies Cased and Case_Ignorable properties.

Generation reads field 13 (simple lowercase mapping) from UnicodeData, overrides
with unconditional SpecialCasing lowercase mappings, and extracts the two sorted
property range sets. Final_Sigma is implemented contextually; language-dependent
Turkish, Azeri and Lithuanian conditions are excluded by default lowercasing.

# Python, Go, Rust, Node JavaScript and TypeScript with CUI

For installable local wheel, npm, Go module and Rust crate artifacts, see the
[packaging guide](PACKAGING.md). Linux alpha packages are tested outside the
checkout; registry publication and other platform packages remain pending.

For UI trees authored directly in Python, JavaScript or TypeScript, use
[the component builders](BINDING_BUILDERS.md). They expose the real C bridge
components in Python, JavaScript and TypeScript, with dedicated
[Go](GO_BUILDERS.md) and [Rust](RUST_BUILDERS.md) APIs as well. See the
[coverage table](BRIDGE_COMPONENTS.md) for the current component scope and limits.
The examples below also demonstrate hosting an existing C-authored application.

The examples below remain useful for embedding an application whose UI is
written in C.

These runnable examples call the actual CUI library through a small C host. Each
creates a styled **Increment** button, renders a counter, and calls your language
synchronously when the button changes it. With SDL3 and shaped text available,
the same clients open a native desktop window. Without a font argument they run
a deterministic headless interaction check instead.

This is an integration starting point, not a complete binding of CUI's 78
manifest entries. UI construction currently lives in `host.c`; application
callbacks live in Python, Go, Rust or Node. Extend that host ABI to expose the controls
and state your application needs. No Clay or SDL types cross this example ABI.

## Build and run

### Python only: standard-library ctypes

Use Python 3.9+, CMake 3.20+, Ninja and a C11 compiler. Python needs no pip
packages, Node, Go or Rust. Native windows additionally need installed SDL3
3.2+, FreeType, HarfBuzz and a TrueType/OpenType font. Build just the shared host:

```sh
cmake -S examples/foreign_languages -B examples/foreign_languages/build -G Ninja
cmake --build examples/foreign_languages/build --target cui_example_host
# Headless: two actual CUI button activations and Python callbacks.
python3 examples/foreign_languages/python/main.py
# Native: click Increment in the actual SDL3 window; close the window to return.
python3 examples/foreign_languages/python/main.py /usr/share/fonts/noto/NotoSans-Regular.ttf
```

For another build directory, pass `--library /absolute/path/libcui_example_host.so`.
Python imports the [small ctypes wrapper](../examples/foreign_languages/python/main.py):

```python
from main import run

def changed(count):
    print("Application callback:", count)

run(changed, font="/path/to/your/font.ttf")
```

Place this Python code beside the wrapper or import it from your application's
module path. The callback stays alive throughout the synchronous C call.
Python exceptions are captured in the callback and re-raised after the host
returns; they never unwind through C. The native loop blocks the calling Python
thread until close, just like the small Node host below. A production application
should expose a per-frame host API appropriate to its runtime.

### Node JavaScript and TypeScript only

Use the CMake/compiler and native dependencies above, plus Node 22.18+ and
Node development headers (`node_api.h`). Go and Rust are unnecessary for these
clients. No npm packages or node-gyp are required:

```sh
cmake -S examples/foreign_languages -B examples/foreign_languages/build -G Ninja
cmake --build examples/foreign_languages/build --target cui_node
node examples/foreign_languages/node/main.cjs
node examples/foreign_languages/typescript/main.ts
# Open the same native CUI window from either runtime:
node examples/foreign_languages/node/main.cjs /usr/share/fonts/noto/NotoSans-Regular.ttf
node examples/foreign_languages/typescript/main.ts /usr/share/fonts/noto/NotoSans-Regular.ttf
```

The TypeScript sample uses Node's built-in type stripping; it does not perform
static type checking. Both clients use the same N-API addon and C host.

### All five clients

From the repository root, install/use CMake 3.20+, Ninja, a C11 compiler,
Go 1.22+, Rust 1.85+ and Node 22.18+ (with Node development headers containing
`node_api.h`). TypeScript runs through Node's built-in type stripping; no npm,
Cargo or Go packages are downloaded. The examples add no third-party dependencies.
The repository pins Clay and optional fetched SDL3. This build uses installed
SDL3 3.2+, FreeType and HarfBuzz for native windows; if they are unavailable it
prints `headless only`.

```sh
examples/foreign_languages/build.sh
examples/foreign_languages/check.sh
```

The build compiles the C bridge and Node addon with `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic
-Werror`, Go's C trampoline with warnings as errors, and Rust with `-D warnings`.
It places all artifacts in `examples/foreign_languages/build/`, including the
shared C host used by all five clients. The CMake subproject builds CUI directly
from this checkout with position independent code. Run on Linux with GCC/Clang;
`build.sh` uses ELF rpath linker flags and needs adaptation for other platforms.

To force a portable headless build, pass `-DCUI_EXAMPLE_NATIVE=OFF` to
`build.sh`. Passing a font to that build returns status 4. To enable repository
pinned SDL fetching when system SDL3 is absent, pass `-DCUI_FETCH_SDL=ON`;
FreeType and HarfBuzz still need to be installed.

Choose an existing TrueType/OpenType font on your machine, then open a native
window with any client. The example below uses the font present on our Linux
validation machine:

```sh
FONT=/usr/share/fonts/noto/NotoSans-Regular.ttf
python3 examples/foreign_languages/python/main.py "$FONT"
examples/foreign_languages/build/go-demo "$FONT"
examples/foreign_languages/build/rust-demo "$FONT"
node examples/foreign_languages/node/main.cjs "$FONT"
node examples/foreign_languages/typescript/main.ts "$FONT"
```

Close each window before starting the next command. Add a positive frame count
(e.g. `"$FONT" 120`) to close automatically; zero runs until window close.
Click **Increment** to update the on-screen count and print the callback value.
Native SDL3 event dispatch, CUI layout, font shaping and rendering run on the
calling thread. Go locks its goroutine to that OS thread. Node runs this loop
synchronously: timers and other JS event-loop work wait until the window closes.
For a production app, design a per-frame host API integrated with your runtime's
main-thread event loop.

## C host contract

[host.h](../examples/foreign_languages/host.h) deliberately exposes a small ABI:

```c
typedef void (*cui_example_changed)(void *user, int count);
int cui_example_run(const char *font, unsigned frames,
                    cui_example_changed callback, void *user);
```

The callback is invoked on the calling thread and is never retained beyond the
call. Its `user` storage must remain alive through `run`. Headless mode lays out
the real button, obtains its hit bounds, queues pointer down/up events twice,
and verifies two state changes and nonempty draw lists with no CUI errors.
The native mode polls SDL3, renders CUI draw commands and optionally captures its
last bounded frame when `CUI_EXAMPLE_CAPTURE` names a BMP output path. Text backing
storage remains alive while the renderer consumes the draw list.

Status zero means success; 2 is font failure, 3 backend creation failure, 4 native
support unavailable, 5 CUI creation failure, 6–8 headless validation failure and
9 native layout/render failure. Native window initialization does not silently
fall back to a headless test.

## Language examples

[Go](../examples/foreign_languages/go/main.go) uses cgo and an exported Go callback:

```go
//export changed
func changed(count C.int) {
    observed = int(count)
    fmt.Println("Go count:", observed)
}
```

A C trampoline passes that callback to the host. No Go pointer is stored in C.
`runtime.LockOSThread()` keeps SDL operations on one OS thread. The build script
links the host shared library through `CGO_LDFLAGS`.

[Rust](../examples/foreign_languages/rust/main.rs) uses the C ABI directly:

```rust
extern "C" fn changed(user: *mut c_void, count: i32) {
    unsafe { *(user as *mut i32) = count; }
    println!("Rust count: {count}");
}
```

The `i32` lives on the caller's stack throughout the synchronous host call.
The narrow unsafe boundary covers the FFI call and pointer conversion. A
production callback must avoid panicking across the C boundary.

[JavaScript](../examples/foreign_languages/node/main.cjs) uses a locally built
[N-API addon](../examples/foreign_languages/node/addon.c), with no node-gyp:

```js
const { run } = require('../build/cui.node');
let observed = 0;
const callback = count => { observed = count; console.log(`Node count: ${count}`); };
const status = run(callback); // Omit font for the headless test.
```

The addon invokes JS only synchronously on Node's calling thread, propagates
callback exceptions and never retains a JavaScript callback after return.

[TypeScript](../examples/foreign_languages/typescript/main.ts) declares the addon
shape, then uses the same N-API implementation:

```ts
interface Host {
    run(callback: (count: number) => void, font?: string, frames?: number): number;
}
const host = require('../build/cui.node') as Host;
const status = host.run(count => console.log(`TypeScript count: ${count}`));
```

Node strips erasable TypeScript syntax; this run does not perform static type
checking. Use your project's pinned TypeScript compiler for type checking if
integrating the sample into an application.

## Validation and limits

Validated on Linux with Go 1.27.2, Rust 1.99.0, Node 25.8.0, SDL3 3.4.18,
FreeType and HarfBuzz. The C host check verifies callback order, repeated independent runs and optional
callbacks, in both native-enabled and core-only builds. Headless clients
verify counts 1 then 2. Python additionally
checks exact callback order, exception identity and a subsequent independent run.
JavaScript also checks rejected arguments, a thrown callback and a subsequent
successful run.

Native Linux/X11 checks use Xvfb, xdotool and xwininfo to click the actual window button,
verify that the foreign-language callback prints `count: 1`, and save a BMP of
the final frame. They exercise a native window and SDL event dispatch, rather
than merely generating headless commands:

```sh
FONT=/usr/share/fonts/noto/NotoSans-Regular.ttf
EXAMPLES=examples/foreign_languages
# Use TMPDIR pointing to a writable directory if your /tmp quota is constrained.
timeout 15 xvfb-run -a "$EXAMPLES/native-check.sh" "$FONT" python python3 "$EXAMPLES/python/main.py"
timeout 15 xvfb-run -a "$EXAMPLES/native-check.sh" "$FONT" go "$EXAMPLES/build/go-demo"
timeout 15 xvfb-run -a "$EXAMPLES/native-check.sh" "$FONT" rust "$EXAMPLES/build/rust-demo"
timeout 15 xvfb-run -a "$EXAMPLES/native-check.sh" "$FONT" node node "$EXAMPLES/node/main.cjs"
timeout 15 xvfb-run -a "$EXAMPLES/native-check.sh" "$FONT" typescript node "$EXAMPLES/typescript/main.ts"
```

Each check writes `build/<language>-native.log` and `build/<language>-native.bmp`.
The fixed click coordinates belong to this sample's 480×240 layout. Xvfb tests
use a virtual Linux display; physical-display behavior, Wayland, macOS, Windows
and performance across language boundaries have not been validated here.
The examples do not implement a browser renderer or promise complete bindings,
IME support or native operating-system widgets. The button is a CUI control
rendered into an SDL desktop window.

# Layout and custom content

Use `include/cui/cui.h` as the exact field/signature authority. This guide is the
canonical introduction; [Core](CORE.md) records advanced contracts. Dimensions
are logical pixels. A box is a column unless `.row = true`.

| Intent | `cui_box` fields | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FIT | `.width = 0` | Natural content width; the default |
| Grow | `.width = -1` | Share available parent space |
| Fixed | `.width = 120` | Request 120 pixels |
| Exactly zero | `.width = 0, .fixed_width = true` | Collapsed width |
| Maximum | `.max_width = 320` | Cap FIT, grow or fixed width |
| Clip | `.clip = true` | Clip child paint and hit regions to the box |

The same rules apply to height and its corresponding fields. Positive finite
maximums constrain even fixed minimums; other maximums are unbounded. A maximum
is a cap, not a request to grow. Give an ancestor a constrained width before
expecting descendants to wrap. Padding and gaps consume available space.
`align_x` and `align_y` use physical axes; centering needs unused space.

```c
cui_begin_box(ui, cui_id_from(ui, "message"),
    (cui_box){.width = -1, .max_width = 480, .padding = 12,
              .gap = 8, .clip = true});
cui_text(ui, cui_string("A paragraph that may wrap within this card."),
         16, (cui_color){30, 30, 30, 255});
cui_end_box(ui);
```

`cui_text`/`cui_text_ex` use normal layout wrapping. `cui_text_line` preserves an
unwrapped line; put it inside a clipping ancestor if overflow must be hidden.
`cui_text_paragraph_colored` explicitly selects word wrapping with its `wrap`
argument and supports hard paragraphs. Clipping alone does not insert an
ellipsis or reflow text. Font registration must precede measurement/layout.

Compose arbitrary content with boxes and public leaf/component calls. A
convenience component that takes a label does not automatically accept arbitrary
children. For a custom card or mail row, compose the surface yourself rather than
inventing a component content callback. Balance every `cui_begin_box` with
`cui_end_box`, including skipped/capacity-failed boxes; APIs returning a boolean
begin result have their own documented successful-begin balancing rule.

For a mail row, use a growing row with a fixed avatar, a growing text column and
a fixed trailing timestamp. Constrain the text column, clip long single-line
subjects, and wrap the preview only when its row height may grow. Do not size a
whole row from last frame's measured width: resize should resolve in this frame.
See [IDs and lifetimes](IDS_AND_LIFETIMES.md) before repeating the row.

## Container-responsive layouts

Use [responsive containers](RESPONSIVE_LAYOUT.md) for Tailwind-style named
breakpoints in C. Query the current available **logical** width every frame;
window framebuffer density is a separate host concern. A main pane can use its
own query after subtracting sidebar/padding/gaps.

```c
#include "cui/cui_responsive.h"

cui_responsive size = cui_responsive_query(main_width, NULL);
if (size.valid) {
    bool row = cui_responsive_fits(size, 260, 260, 12);
    float padding = cui_responsive_value(size, CUI_BREAKPOINT_MD, 12, 24);
    cui_begin_box(ui, 200, (cui_box){.width = -1, .row = row,
                                   .padding = padding, .gap = 12});
    /* Submit the same application-backed cards in either arrangement. */
    cui_end_box(ui);
}
```

The selector arguments are query, threshold, base value, expanded value. Use
`cui_responsive_at_least(size, CUI_BREAKPOINT_LG)` to choose a persistent sidebar;
conditionally submit a closed drawer's controls so hidden input/semantics do not
remain active. Keep one state tree across breakpoint changes. Width policies
supply no CSS parser, automatic drawer/modal scope, or host event loop. The
[dashboard fixture](../examples/responsive_dashboard/app.c) demonstrates the
working composition; its guide includes native and headless run commands.

Text can use [body/heading/code role tokens](TYPOGRAPHY_TOKENS.md) inside these
containers. Wrapping still requires a constrained parent and matching measurement
and renderer fonts; tokens do not replace those contracts.

## Single-line ellipsis with fixed trailing controls

Use `cui_text_ellipsis` from `include/cui/cui_text_overflow.h` when a single-line
subject must shorten visibly. It resolves width in the current frame, preserves
extended grapheme boundaries, and keeps the full text as its semantic name.
Unlike clipping, it paints a trailing ellipsis when enough space remains.

```c
cui_begin_box(ui, cui_id_from(ui, "mail-row"),
    (cui_box){.width = -1, .row = true, .gap = 8});
cui_text_ellipsis(ui, cui_id_from(ui, "subject"), subject,
    (cui_text_ellipsis_options){.width = -1, .font_size = 16,
                              .color = theme->text});
cui_begin_box(ui, cui_id_from(ui, "star-slot"),
    (cui_box){.width = 32, .height = 32, .fixed_width = true});
/* Submit a star button/icon with another unique ID here. */
cui_end_box(ui);
cui_end_box(ui);
```

Constrain an ancestor's width. A positive helper width is fixed; negative grows;
zero is invalid. Height uses natural font metrics. Newlines are rejected, and
prefix/ellipsis are shaped separately. The helper does not provide paragraph
reflow, font fallback, or contextual shaping across the ellipsis boundary.
Check its boolean result and the context diagnostic after submission. Give each
repeated row a persistent ID scope as described in [IDs and lifetimes](IDS_AND_LIFETIMES.md).

![Native constrained subject rows with fixed star actions and a deliberate missing-icon outline](screenshots/developer-usability.png)

A real SDL3 software capture of an external application using these APIs.
The [evaluation record](validation/developer-usability-agent.md) contains its
source and observed limits; it is a correctness smoke test, not a blind usability study.

# Letter spacing

Set `cui_text_style.letter_spacing` to a signed distance in logical pixels. A
value of `2` adds two logical pixels between eligible visual shaping clusters;
`-1` compresses them by one. Density scales the distance with the rest of the UI.
Zero preserves the existing natural shaping and layout path.

This changes the C ABI: rebuild Core, providers, renderers and applications
against the same headers. Zero-initialize style/config values before setting
individual fields, or use designated initializers. `cui_text_style`, embedded draw commands and
`cui_config` have grown. Do not mix prebuilt libraries or generated bindings
from an older build. The flat bridge style API does not yet expose tracking.

## Configure the provider

Tracking is opt-in. The provider must measure, shape contextual lines and draw
with the same cluster policy. Native `cui_text` with Bidi enabled supports it:

```c
cui_config config = {
    .measure_user = font,
    .measure_styled = cui_font_measure_styled,
    .text_geometry = cui_font_text_geometry,
    .text_geometry_line = cui_font_text_geometry_line,
    .text_capabilities = cui_font_text_capabilities(),
};
cui_context *ui = cui_create(config);

/* Inside a frame, within the desired available width. */
cui_text_style style = {.letter_spacing = 1.5f};
bool ok = cui_text_paragraph_colored(
    ui, cui_string("Clear typography"), 24,
    (cui_color){255, 255, 255, 255}, 30, style, true, NULL, 0);
```

`cui_text_capabilities(ui) & CUI_TEXT_CAP_LETTER_SPACING` reports the configured
provider promise; it requires both styled measurement and contextual geometry.
Custom providers may set the bit only when all their measurement, geometry and
rendering paths implement this contract. Their caches must include tracking
where they retain positioned shapes. A legacy measure callback is insufficient.
The capability does not guarantee that a particular font covers the text.

| Provider / renderer | Nonzero tracking |
| --- | --- |
| Native HarfBuzz + Bidi, software and SDL3 | Supported |
| Native build without Bidi | Unavailable |
| Canvas gallery provider | Unavailable |
| Sokol / SDL_GPU adapters | Rejected during preflight |

The native bridge host configures the capability, but its foreign style
representation still needs a separate additive tracking API. Other native hosts
must opt in through the configuration above. Manual glyph callbacks receive
already positioned glyph coverage; do not add spacing again.

Unsupported geometry returns `CUI_TEXT_LAYOUT_UNAVAILABLE`; measurement returns
zero, boolean submission/drawing returns false, and void text helpers submit
nothing. Prefer boolean paragraph/contextual APIs when failure matters. Invalid
values return the existing invalid/failure result. No provider silently counts
UTF-8 bytes, draws individual characters or substitutes solid default text.
Canvas `letterSpacing` is deliberately not used: it has not been verified to
match this shaping-cluster policy and the native caret/ligature contract.

## Shaping and negative values

HarfBuzz shapes complete directional/script runs first, preserving required and
optional ligatures, kerning, Arabic joining and combining-mark placement. A
ligature remains one cluster; tracking does not split it into individual letters.
Spacing is then inserted between positive-advance clusters in visual order,
including spaces and across visual run boundaries. Zero-advance clusters,
including standalone default-ignorables, earn no gap. Combining and emoji
sequences follow the shaper's cluster boundaries. This is cluster tracking, not
CSS per-character spacing.

There is no gap after the final eligible cluster of a visual line. Hard breaks
reset spacing; empty lines and a single cluster gain no width. Tabs retain the
provider's existing shaping behavior; this API introduces no tab stops.

Negative tracking can overlap glyph ink. Each eligible cluster's advance after
its following gap must remain nonnegative and all geometry must remain finite.
A value that would reverse progression rejects the line; it is never clamped.
Glyph ink may extend outside advance bounds, as it already can for italic text.
Cluster-edge carets and selection include the following gap. Hit testing remains
based on those edges, with its existing affinity rule for coincident positions.
Original glyph advances remain available in `cui_text_glyph`; adjusted glyph
positions, cluster spans and layout width describe the tracked result.

Wrapping measures the exact contextual candidate line, so its last cluster has
no trailing gap. It never breaks an intact shaped cluster. Tracked wrapping may
shape multiple candidate lines and cost more than natural wrapping; the zero
path retains its existing algorithm. As with ordinary contextual wrapping,
joining or ligatures can change at a chosen line boundary.

Color spans, gradients, alignment, clipping and inherited opacity use the same
tracked geometry. Paint changes do not change shaping. Native glyph raster
cache keys stay unchanged because tracking moves glyph origins and does not
change their glyph IDs, faces or raster sizes.

## Verification scope

`test_letter_spacing.c` checks real-font cluster and glyph identity, positive and
negative widths, no final gap, combining marks, ligatures, zero-width text,
caret/hit/selection consistency, narrow/wide reflow, unsupported providers and
software pixels. An optional Arabic font argument exercises joining, RTL and
mixed-direction runs. `test_letter_spacing_sdl.c` checks actual SDL pixels at
1×, 1.5× and 2×, including gradient coverage. Native tests run only through the
private-display wrapper. GPU hardware and unimplemented Canvas tracking are not
claimed as verified.
documents.docs/LINUX_LIVE_RESIZE.md:
# Linux live-resize evidence

The callback-driven SDL3 host is tested on Linux independently of macOS modal
resize behavior. The automated test uses X11 on the private Xvfb display created
by `scripts/test_local.py`. It does not connect to the maintainer's desktop.

## What the test does

`tests/integration/test_continuous_resize.c` runs the real responsive dashboard
through `cui_sdl3_run`, using the pinned Inter font and SDL software rendering.
It presents an initial 800-by-760 frame before resizing begins. The separate
Python parent in `tests/packaging/test_continuous_resize.py` finds that process's
uniquely named X11 window through libX11 and sends a timed sequence of
`XResizeWindow`/`XFlush` requests: 360, 800, 1400, 480, 1100 and 640 pixels, repeated
four times. Requests arrive while the callback runner is already running. The
UI callbacks neither wait for the parent nor sleep/block waiting for resize.

Each callback obtains current host dimensions, submits the scene and captures its
real rendered BMP before emitting a presentation record. The parent collects
records during the burst, requiring at least six presentations and captures at
360, 800 and 1400 widths **before the burst ends**. A final-only redraw cannot
satisfy this test. It verifies:

- Window dimensions and root layout dimensions agree for every sampled frame.
- Main content stays within the current width; cards stack at 360 and sit beside
  each other at 800/1400. The sidebar becomes persistent at the LG breakpoint;
  narrow frames submit Menu and omit the closed navigation subtree.
- Captured BMP dimensions match that frame's dimensions. Actual pixels sampled
  inside both current card rectangles equal the theme's card color; screenshots
  also contain rendered UI variation. This checks fresh scene geometry against
  raster output rather than accepting a stretched old frame.
- The original Reports page, signed-in account and closed-drawer state survive
  all breakpoint crossings.

The baseline `5a76db06` passed: **24 actual presentations at six distinct widths
while a 1.46-second burst was ongoing**. This scoped callback-runner path did not
require a production fix. It does not establish that an older manual loop or
another host integration handles the user's resize path correctly.

## Run safely

After the integration target is registered, configure native SDL3/text support
and use the isolated wrapper:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCUI_REQUIRE_NATIVE=ON
cmake --build build --target test_continuous_resize
python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir build -R '^linux_continuous_resize$' -V
```

The Python driver requires the wrapper's `CUI_TEST_VIRTUAL_DISPLAY=1`, a private
X11 DISPLAY and no Wayland display; unsupported platforms/drivers return 77.
The child independently checks the isolation flag. The driver selects X11 and
SDL software rendering. libX11 is loaded dynamically through Python's standard
`ctypes`; no Python package or new production dependency is introduced. CTest
applies `SKIP_RETURN_CODE 77` and a finite timeout. Temporary screenshots and
the child are cleaned up on success or failure.

Never replace the wrapper with `DISPLAY=:0` or the user's Wayland session.

## Coverage boundaries

Xvfb has no physical desktop window manager in this test. Programmatic X11
requests prove continuous external resize dispatch, current-size layout and
real presentation while the process runs. They do **not** prove physical mouse
window-border dragging, compositor-specific event scheduling, Wayland, hardware
GPU rendering, macOS live resize or HiDPI behavior. No custom window manager or
its potential autostart programs are launched. Those paths need separate
controlled evidence before claiming coverage.

See [responsive containers](RESPONSIVE_LAYOUT.md) for the layout policy and
[callback host lifecycle](LIVE_RESIZE.md) for runner versus manual-pump behavior.
documents.docs/LIST_EVENTS.md:
# Typed List transitions

Include `cui/cui_list_events.h`. `cui_base_list_events` adds an explicit compound
control ID to the old Base arguments; `cui_list_events` uses the Styled container
ID. Both accept the existing `cui_selection_handler` and return `events` plus
`legacy_activated`, the original activation bool. A missing callback ignores user
and preserves reduction and old callbacks.

Each actual selected-ID transition delivers `cui_selection_change` after the
owner write and existing `on_activate` then `on_confirm`. Multiple transitions
can return to the initial owner and still notify separately. Reconfirming the
same item invokes the old callbacks but emits no CHANGE unless they redirect the
owner. Navigation, typeahead, secondary highlight, Escape and scroll-window state
are not selection CHANGE. Old cancel/confirmation and popup behavior are retained.

Payloads are pointer-free ID snapshots, copyable beyond the call. Metadata keeps
the existing private forwarding seam: root target, actual frame/index/source,
and activation snapshot only if available. List registration follows reduction,
so HAS_ACTIVATION is often absent. Ordinary OPTION accessibility ACTIVATE is not
supported by Core's current allowlist; MENUITEM differs. No accessibility parity
or new input-routing behavior is implied. Non-pointer activation still uses the
legacy active cursor; this facade does not redefine its item resolution.

Callbacks/user borrow synchronously. During typed callbacks do not mutate/rebind
owners, state, descriptors or borrowed resources; recurse; destroy storage/context;
or unwind foreign exceptions. Copy payloads/change unrelated application state.
As with existing selection forwarding, consuming later queued events is allowed;
it does not authorize arbitrary model/resource mutation. Defer edits/removal and
teardown until submission and renderer consumption finish. Legacy callbacks keep
their existing owner-update timing; typed changes read the resulting owner after
them. Disabled/inert/layout-only calls retain old behavior without typed events.

List multi adds `cui_base_list_multi_events`/`cui_list_multi_events`, accepting
`cui_choice_item_handler`. Each actual bool transition delivers a pointer-free
`cui_choice_item_change` with affected `item`, causal `trigger_item`, `previous`
and `value`. The adapter captures the bool before its flip, then preserves legacy
activate/confirm order and observes the resulting bool. Legacy callbacks may
redirect that bool and cancel its net transition; unrelated writes by legacy
callbacks get no fabricated notifications. Repeated toggles remain distinct even
when the final array matches entry. Item/selected-array ordering and storage stay
borrowed throughout submission/paint. The result's `legacy_result` preserves the
old activation bool; `change_count` counts actual typed callbacks with saturation.

ToggleGroup adds matching Base/Styled `_events` functions with the same bool
payload and result. Unlike List multi, it notifies immediately after each actual
write. Single-mode selection clears previously true entries in array order, then
sets the chosen entry; callbacks deliberately see intermediate arrays. Sibling
clears use the affected `item` and causal activated `trigger_item`, sharing input
metadata. False-to-false stores produce no event. Disabled siblings can be cleared
by an enabled item's single-mode selection, preserving the legacy array policy.
`allow_empty` rejection emits nothing. Multiple mode emits only the chosen flip.
No workspace or array snapshot is allocated. `legacy_result` here is the old
accepted-change bool, which can remain true after returning to the initial array.
BUTTON activation support differs from ordinary List OPTION; no role remap occurs.

New facades require a nonzero compound ID. Descriptors, strings and bool arrays
must keep identity/order/storage throughout the call and rendering. Initial
multi-true arrays retain their old behavior; no normalization policy was added.
Bridge and Python/Node/Go/Rust behavior is unchanged.
documents.docs/LIVE_RESIZE.md:
# Native live resize and pointer motion

Use `cui_sdl3_run(argc, argv, callbacks)` for native applications. Initialization
creates the backend and Core context; the frame callback composes and presents
one frame using freshly queried `cui_sdl3_size`; quit releases application
resources. Return zero from frame to continue, positive to finish successfully,
negative on failure. The starter and native gallery show the complete pattern.
All callbacks run on the main thread. Do not call event waits or nest a runner
inside these callbacks. `cui_sdl3_poll` remains valid there for IME/cursor
synchronization and does not recursively pump SDL.

The runner uses SDL's supported callback entrypoint `SDL_EnterAppMainCallbacks`.
The existing ordinary `main` entrypoints remain code-driven; no SDL types enter
CUI's public APIs and no extra SDLMain library is required. The existing macOS
bundle font lookup and static SDL dependency linkage remain in place.

This distinction matters during native resize. Pinned SDL 3.4.18 implements
`SDL_OnWindowLiveResizeUpdate` in `src/video/SDL_video.c`: callback-main apps get
`SDL_IterateMainCallbacks(false)` while ordinary loops only receive a queued
EXPOSED event. Cocoa's live-resize timer calls that function at approximately
60 Hz; Windows' modal size/move timer calls it too. A conventional poll loop can
remain inside the OS event pump until dragging stops, so invalidating it alone
cannot guarantee intermediate composition. The runner lets SDL invoke composition
from its main-thread modal-loop iteration, without drawing in an event watcher.
A reentrancy guard prevents nested frame callbacks. Foreign-thread lifecycle
notifications never mutate Core or draw through the adapter.

Custom poll/step loops remain supported. They must adopt callback-main scheduling
to obtain this modal live-resize behavior; calling `cui_sdl3_size` more often or
reducing a sleep interval does not replace that scheduling change. Logical resize,
pixel-size change, display-scale change and expose notifications invalidate Core.
Density-aware text rasterization, rounded-strip batching and elapsed frame timing
remain enabled. Idle callback scheduling uses SDL's event wait; active animations
keep continuous iteration. Call `cui_invalidate` for main-thread model changes or
when a frame-limited capture needs another frame.

The adapter coalesces consecutive mouse motion before forwarding it to Core's
bounded event queue. It flushes the latest position before clicks, leave, focus
and other non-motion events, preserving ordering. This prevents a burst of old
positions from filling the queue and dropping the latest hover position. It does
not coalesce touch motion or discard click transitions.

`cui_bridge_run(app, after_frame, user)` exposes the same native scheduler through
the canonical C bridge. Its optional callback dispatches language/application
events after each successful frame; return OK to continue or a status to stop.
Catch foreign exceptions before returning through C. Nested run/step returns
INVALID_STATE. Closing during the callback ends with CLOSED. Destroy during the
callback requests close and defers release until the runner exits; that pointer
must not be used afterward. Otherwise the terminal app must still be destroyed
by its owner. The native host is released at run completion. Portable builds
return BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE. Existing language `App.run` loops must call this new
symbol to benefit; retaining a sleep/step loop does not enable live modal resize.
Older bridge libraries require a clear missing-symbol/unavailable fallback.

Headless Linux coverage exercises real SDL frames after a 320x160 to 480x240
resize, main-thread callback dispatch, and a 3000-motion burst reaching the next
frame. Bridge cases cover close, callback error, reentrant calls, deferred destroy
and a null callback. These tests run through `scripts/test_local.py` in private
Xvfb. Cocoa/Windows source inspection supports the scheduling contract; actual
macOS/Windows drag responsiveness remains host acceptance, not a Linux runtime
claim. Hardware/GPU display migration remains deferred.

Linux additionally has a [continuous X11 resize test](LINUX_LIVE_RESIZE.md): an
external process resizes an already-running responsive dashboard through repeated
breakpoint crossings. Captures and geometry prove intermediate presentation while
the resize burst is ongoing, including sidebar/card adaptation and retained app
state. This is stronger than a final-size assertion, but does not establish
physical window-manager dragging or Wayland behavior.
documents.docs/MACOS.md:
# Native macOS applications

CUI's portable library has macOS CI evidence. The native workflow below adds the
SDL3/text adapters and a `.app` starter. A configured CI job or a successful Linux
build is not evidence that the app runs correctly on macOS. Record the revision,
Mac architecture, macOS version, dependency receipt and results when validating.

## Build on your Apple Silicon Mac

Install Xcode Command Line Tools, CMake 3.20+, Python 3, Git, pkg-config and a build
tool. Use an arm64 terminal (`uname -m` should print `arm64`), rather than a
Rosetta x86_64 shell. The commands below use Makefiles, so Ninja is optional. Run from the repo.
Dependency sources are pinned in `tools/native-deps/CMakeLists.txt`; this avoids
relying on changing Homebrew library versions. The initial build needs network
access. SDK and compiler remain your local Xcode tools.

```sh
cmake -S tools/native-deps -B build/macos-deps \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCUI_DEPS_PREFIX="$PWD/build/macos-prefix"
cmake --build build/macos-deps --parallel 4
python3 tests/test_native_deps.py --prefix "$PWD/build/macos-prefix"

PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$PWD/build/macos-prefix/lib/pkgconfig" \
cmake -S . -B build/macos \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCUI_REQUIRE_NATIVE=ON -DCUI_BUILD_NATIVE_STARTER=ON \
  -DCUI_HEADLESS_NATIVE_TESTS=ON -DCUI_BUILD_CPP_EXAMPLE=OFF \
  -DCUI_TEST_FONT="$PWD/third_party/inter/Inter-Regular.otf" \
  -DCUI_MACOS_DEPENDENCY_LICENSE_DIR="$PWD/build/macos-prefix/share/licenses"
cmake --build build/macos --parallel 4
python3 scripts/test_local.py --build-dir build/macos
cmake --install build/macos --prefix "$PWD/build/macos-installed"
```

The installed starter is `build/macos-installed/cui_native_starter.app`.
Installation deploys non-system dynamic dependencies into the bundle on a native
Mac, then applies and verifies ad-hoc development signatures without a signing
identity or keychain. Inspect installation output and test the installed app away from the build
prefix before distributing it. The build-tree bundle still references build
libraries. `CUI_REQUIRE_NATIVE=ON` makes missing native dependencies a configure
error instead of silently building only portable targets.

The bundle includes pinned Inter regular/bold fonts and their license. The
starter locates its default regular font relative to its executable, independent
of the launch directory; `--font PATH` overrides it. The larger starter currently
uses the regular face; bundling the bold face does not automatically register a
bold style. An application icon and your own bundle identifier/branding are
application work. See `examples/native_starter/README.md` for copied projects.

## Automated checks without desktop windows

`CUI_HEADLESS_NATIVE_TESTS=ON` forces the dummy SDL video driver and software
renderer for registered CTest tests. GPU checks cannot be enabled in this mode.
Use `scripts/test_local.py`, which recognizes this configuration on macOS and
preserves CTest's exit code. This exercises native adapter services without
validating Cocoa windows or Metal. Some shaping tests need additional distinct
family/Hebrew/Arabic font fixtures and can report skips; inspect the test output.
Do not treat skipped coverage as a pass.

A bounded headless starter capture can additionally verify packaged resources:

```sh
SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy SDL_RENDER_DRIVER=software \
  build/macos-installed/cui_native_starter.app/Contents/MacOS/cui_native_starter \
  --frames 3 --capture "$PWD/build/macos-starter.bmp"
```

## Manual Mac acceptance

These are intentional interactive launches, outside automated tests:

```sh
open build/macos-installed/cui_native_starter.app
```

Check the installed app from Finder and a different working directory. Verify:

- Navigation, editable settings, keyboard focus, shortcuts and clipboard.
- Window close/minimize/maximize/fullscreen behavior and native traffic lights.
- Rendering and text at Retina scale, resizing, and moving between displays.
- Input-method marked text, candidate placement and committed text.
- System appearance changes, sleep/resume and relaunch.
- Launch with the dependency prefix unavailable, proving deployed libraries and
  resources are sufficient. Use a copied bundle on another Mac for best evidence.

Record failures rather than assuming SDL's platform support proves CUI behavior.
The dedicated SDL_GPU adapter still lacks Metal shaders. Native macOS AX/VoiceOver
integration remains unfinished and requires separate implementation and acceptance;
this starter workflow does not establish accessible production-app support.

## Distribution and cross compilation

The installed app is a development artifact. Choose a deployment target and
architecture policy, add branding, and establish Developer ID signing,
entitlements as needed, notarization and release testing before public release.
Dependency fixup changes Mach-O files; sign after deployment, including nested
libraries. No signing identity or notarization credentials are requested by these
build scripts. Ad-hoc signatures are for local development; [Apple’s distribution
signing guidance](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/creating-distribution-signed-code-for-the-mac/)
describes the separate release identities. Universal apps require every dependency and executable to include
the same architecture slices; this workflow starts with one architecture.

See [Linux to macOS](MACOS_CROSS.md) for the cross-toolchain workflow. Cross-built
artifacts still require validation on a Mac; local Linux tests cannot execute
Mach-O binaries or establish Cocoa/Metal behavior.

# Linux to macOS native starter

This is a caller-provisioned cross-build path, not an SDK downloader or a
self-contained macOS release pipeline. No Apple SDK or OSXCross installation is
bundled. Without those inputs only the host-side guard tests can be validated.
The Linux build does not establish macOS runtime, graphics or accessibility parity.

## Provision the inputs

1. Build [OSXCross](https://github.com/tpoechtrager/osxcross) on Linux using an
   explicitly selected full Git commit and record that commit, compiler/linker
   versions and build options in your build provenance. Obtain an Apple SDK under
   its applicable license, following the upstream
   [SDK instructions](https://github.com/tpoechtrager/osxcross/blob/master/README.SDK.md).
   Record the SDK version and archive SHA-256. This repository deliberately does
   not select or download someone else's SDK or a floating toolchain revision.
2. Choose one architecture (`arm64` or `x86_64`) and deployment version. ARM64
   requires macOS 11.0 or newer; the deployment version must not exceed the SDK
   version. Use a separate build directory and dependency prefix per architecture.
3. Cross-build and install **macOS** SDL3 (>= 3.2), FreeType and HarfBuzz into an
   absolute prefix such as `/opt/cui-deps/arm64`. Pin and record source revisions
   or archive hashes for every dependency and its transitive dependencies.
   Use the same compiler, SDK, architecture and minimum macOS version for all.
   Disable dependency examples/tests and optional platform backends you do not
   need; never run configure-time target executables on Linux. The repository's
   Linux packages and Linux AccessKit archive cannot be reused.

The pinned dependency builder in this repository installs shared SDL3, FreeType
and HarfBuzz and their license files into a dedicated target prefix:

```sh
cmake -S tools/native-deps -B build/macos-deps -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE="$PWD/cmake/toolchains/macos-osxcross.cmake" \
  -DCUI_DEPS_PREFIX="$PWD/build/macos-prefix" \
  -DCUI_MACOS_CC=/opt/osxcross/target/bin/arm64-apple-darwin24-clang \
  -DCUI_MACOS_SDK=/opt/osxcross/target/SDK/MacOSX15.sdk \
  -DCUI_MACOS_PREFIX="$PWD/build/macos-prefix" \
  -DCUI_MACOS_ARCH=arm64 -DCUI_MACOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.0
cmake --build build/macos-deps --parallel 4
```

Use `--prefix "$PWD/build/macos-prefix"` in the starter helper below when using
this builder. It forwards the toolchain and target settings into each dependency.

For CMake-based dependency builds, reuse `cmake/toolchains/macos-osxcross.cmake`
with the five `CUI_MACOS_*` values shown below and an absolute
`CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX`. HarfBuzz/FreeType bootstrap and feature choices depend
on your selected pinned releases; provision their complete transitive closure.
Supply `sdl3.pc`, `freetype2.pc`, `harfbuzz.pc` and transitively required `.pc`
files under `<prefix>/lib/pkgconfig` or `<prefix>/share/pkgconfig`. Their absolute
include/library paths must point to your macOS prefix, never Linux `/usr`.
Use shared dependencies for this helper; fully static builds may need additional
private link flags and are not automatically supported. Stage dylibs separately
and adjust install names/rpaths for redistribution on macOS.

## Configure and compile

```sh
python scripts/macos_cross.py \
  --cc /opt/osxcross/target/bin/arm64-apple-darwin24-clang \
  --sdk /opt/osxcross/target/SDK/MacOSX15.sdk \
  --prefix /opt/cui-deps/arm64 \
  --arch arm64 --deployment-target 11.0 \
  --build-dir build-macos-arm64
```

Replace the illustrative compiler/SDK paths with your actual installation. The
helper requires host CMake, Ninja, Python and pkg-config. It verifies SDK layout
and target dependency metadata, clears common host compiler/pkg-config overrides,
configures with native adapters required, disables SDL fetching and the C++
example, and builds only `cui_native_starter`. `--configure-only` stops after
configuration. Use a fresh directory when changing compiler, SDK or architecture.

The equivalent toolchain parameters for dependency builds are:

```text
-DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=/absolute/path/to/cui/cmake/toolchains/macos-osxcross.cmake
-DCUI_MACOS_CC=/opt/osxcross/target/bin/arm64-apple-darwin24-clang
-DCUI_MACOS_SDK=/opt/osxcross/target/SDK/MacOSX15.sdk
-DCUI_MACOS_PREFIX=/opt/cui-deps/arm64
-DCUI_MACOS_ARCH=arm64
-DCUI_MACOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.0
```

CMake searches target roots for headers, libraries and packages; host programs
remain discoverable. pkg-config searches only the supplied target prefix, with
no Linux fallback. This cannot repair malformed `.pc` files pointing outside the
prefix: audit dependency metadata and actual link commands. The Apple linker is
the final check that supplied libraries are compatible Mach-O artifacts.

Do **not** run CTest in the macOS cross-build directory on Linux: it contains
macOS executables. Host-only tooling checks are `python tests/test_macos_cross.py`.
Transfer the resulting executable and required dylibs to an actual compatible
Mac for launch, font, input, rendering and deployment validation. Developer ID signing,
notarization, universal binaries and public distribution remain separate
release work; a successful cross compile alone validates none of these.

## Deploy on your Mac

The build produces `build-macos-arm64/cui_native_starter.app`. Transfer this
bundle and the complete **target** dependency prefix to your Mac, preserving
symlinks (for example, with a tar archive). On the Mac, with this checkout:

```sh
cmake -DAPP=/absolute/path/cui_native_starter.app \
  -DDEPENDENCY_PREFIX=/absolute/path/macos-prefix \
  -P scripts/deploy_macos_bundle.cmake
python3 tests/packaging/verify_macos_app.py /absolute/path/cui_native_starter.app
```

Deployment copies target dylibs, adjusts their install names using macOS
tools, and applies ad-hoc development signatures. Developer ID signing is a
separate release step. Validate away from the dependency prefix,
then follow [Mac desktop acceptance](MACOS.md#manual-mac-acceptance). A development
bundle is produced; public release signing/notarization remain application work.
