# Image and Attachment

The comparison is frozen to gpui-component 0.7.1 and its local source/docs snapshot.
Image is a re-export of GPUI's image element, rather than a kit-defined widget.
Attachment is a composed, application-controlled presentation of file lifecycle.

Image source descriptors distinguish embedded asset keys, file paths, URIs,
encoded bytes and custom loaders. CUI supplies the portable host-loader boundary,
not a decoder, filesystem reader or HTTP client. Assign a stable source identity;
change it when the source or retry attempt changes. The host callback must reuse
its request/cache. Resource success and failure are retained until identity
changes or state is explicitly reset. Custom loaders are polled each frame and
may supply a new frame collection. Source descriptor memory is borrowed for the
callback. Ready frame arrays and pixels must remain alive while retained by state,
and through completion of every renderer consuming their draw commands.

A load returns Pending, Ready or Failed. Ready validates up to 4096 borrowed
RGBA8 frames with positive dimensions, stride of at least four bytes per pixel,
finite nonnegative durations and no addressable stride overflow. Pixels are
straight alpha; changing them requires changing the revision. CUI keeps loading
and failure replacement callbacks within the reserved image box. Identified
pending images show the loading replacement after 200ms; unidentified images do
not show it. A fast success skips that replacement. Failure callbacks do not
initiate retries. Returned `next_wake_seconds` lets the host schedule delayed
loading or animation. Call the update/render function when host loading completes.

Image geometry supports centered Contain (default), Cover, Fill, ScaleDown and
None. Cover and overflowing None crop the source, preserving real bitmap pixels.
A zero dimension means automatic sizing: an explicit opposite dimension and ratio
resolve it, otherwise decoded intrinsic dimensions resolve it. An explicit aspect
ratio reserves height before decoding. Without reserved dimensions, decoding can
change layout. Grayscale, opacity and independent corner radii are passed to the
bitmap renderer. Informative descriptions create a passive semantic label;
interactive image commands belong inside a real application Button or Link.

Animation advances decoded frames only when identified, active and not reduced
motion. Inactive/reduced-motion periods do not accumulate catch-up time. A zero
frame duration uses a 10ms minimum to prevent an unbounded advancement loop. Frame
selection is bounded by the supplied frame count even after long elapsed times.

Attachment defaults to Complete, Medium and Horizontal. The application controls
Pending, Uploading, Processing, Failed and Complete; CUI never starts an upload or
mutates lifecycle state. Named sizes follow the reference rem geometry (at root16:
40/48/56/64px chip heights, 176/200/232/272px content widths and 28/32/38/44px media).
Custom density scales Medium geometry from an explicit pixel base. Vertical cards
without metadata are flush square media tiles; vertical metadata cards use a
120px default width and independently configurable media aspect ratio.

Typed metadata retains ordering, inherits lifecycle unless explicitly overridden,
and supports custom child callbacks. Typed children may override color/font size
and supply Marker shimmer duration/spread/highlight/direction options. Uploading/Processing titles use Marker
shimmer; Failed descriptions use destructive color. Known Uploading progress is
clamped to 0–100, appears as a determinate media ring and horizontal bottom bar,
and appends a rounded percentage to typed descriptions. Processing ignores known
progress and remains indeterminate. Media uses real image rendering when a host
loader/state is supplied. Custom media children and centered overlays compose
existing controls. Image status scrims are 35% while in progress and 55% on failure.

Stable identified cards may expose a pointer-only whole-card action, leaving focus
and keyboard activation to real child controls. The actions cluster captures its
gaps so pressing them does not arm the card. Remove is a 20px control with 6px
upper/trailing overhang, visible on desktop hover and always on explicit touch
mode. Failed retry appears over media and after the first typed description.
Callbacks report actions; ownership, removing records and retry requests remain
with the application. Keep states and borrowed child arrays alive through frame
completion. Tooltip composition reuses the existing Tooltip and requires the
caller to provide viewport and timing options.

AttachmentGroup retains a horizontal scroll offset, or uses an explicit external
scroll state. Its default gap is 12 and vertical padding is 4. Dominant horizontal
wheel input updates it, while ties remain vertical for the parent chain. Optional
24px edge fades appear only while content is hidden, with independent 200ms cubic
transitions and reduced-motion settling. Each fade uses 24 bounded strips and
claims no pointer target. Retained bounds measure overflow on a follow-up frame.

Current integration limits: no built-in raster/SVG decoding, remote transport,
HTTP cache, shared/scoped decoded asset cache or encoded animation parser. Host
adapters supply those; decoded-frame playback is implemented here. True font
weight and automatic ellipsis are absent in the existing text primitive; metadata
is clipped to a single line. The progress ring uses 36 bounded samples; the bottom
bar samples rounded clipping with six strips. Remove/retry shadows and automatic content ellipsis are not implemented.
Pending dashed borders are bounded
samples rather than a general dashed-path primitive. Arbitrary source style
builders are exposed as composition callbacks and explicit geometry, not a full
GPUI style language. These limits preclude a full-parity claim.

Integration: compile `src/base/cui_media.c` and `src/components/cui_media.c` into
the styled library. The independent base test needs only its test source, media
base source and math, with `CUI_MEDIA_BASE_ONLY`; no core/theme implementation is
linked. Styled code needs core bitmap commands, pointer-only semantic activation,
focus-scope hover ancestry, Theme, content helpers/Tooltip, Marker, and scroll base.
Each Attachment state is bounded by 128 metadata entries; Marker state is retained
per entry so its tracked text bounds remain valid through frame completion. State
may be heap allocated by the application to avoid large automatic objects.

# Message and MessageScroller

Contracts were audited against the frozen gpui-component 0.7.1 Message and
MessageScroller sources and website documentation in the local reference checkout.
These components leave application message data, formatting and actions with the
caller.

`cui_message_options_default()` uses start alignment, width 480, avatar-row gap 8,
vertical gaps 10 and metadata gap 4. Avatar content reserves at least 32 pixels of
width and aligns to the bottom of the header/body stack. End alignment reverses
that row. Footer content is outside that row and indents 40 pixels on the avatar
side. Header/footer use muted 12-pixel text at the default theme font size and
12-pixel horizontal insets. A typed ghost Bubble anywhere in the body suppresses
both default metadata insets; explicit ON/OFF wins. Arbitrary callbacks do not
participate in typed Bubble inference. A message is passive by default; opt into
`CUI_ROLE_LISTITEM` with an application name and stable ID when appropriate.

Slots accept borrowed text or a rendering callback with available width, color,
font size and alignment. Body slots may wrap an existing typed Bubble or render
arbitrary children. Callbacks may create real interactive controls. Borrowed text,
body arrays and callback users must remain valid through `cui_end_frame`.
`cui_begin_message_group` opens a vertical container; pass gap 8 for the reference
default. Caller supplies width and closes it with `cui_end_message_group`.

Create a scroller with an explicit capacity, item count and estimated raw row
height. Allocation is bounded at creation; capacity is 1–1,000,000 items and no
operation grows it. Heights and spacing are finite and at most 1,000,000 pixels;
estimates must be positive. `memory_bytes` reports retained allocation. State
retains layout keys and heights, never message records. Destroy it explicitly.
The application updates its collection and performs matching reset/splice/append/
prepend operations between frames. Splice ranges are half-open. Invalid ranges,
capacity overflow and invalid geometry leave the model unchanged.

Initial/reset position follows the tail. Appends follow only while that mode is
active. Prepending and splicing preserve the surviving item anchor, including
remeasurement of the previous last row's missing trailing gap. Scrolling to an
item disables following even when the content fits. Scrolling to the end resumes
following. Global remeasurement restores proportional position; selective
remeasurement keeps the item anchor and cached height until its replacement is
measured. Styled width changes request global remeasurement. Retained row bounds
supply measurements on the next frame; explicitly invalidate selective ranges
when application content changes.

Scroller defaults are 480×320, horizontal insets 12, top/bottom padding 8, row gap
32 except after the final row, and 400 pixels of overdraw on each side. Rendering
calls only this bounded visible range. Row callbacks receive the inner width and
stable internal row ID. Do not mutate collection/state until frame completion.
The owner has a focusable LOG role. Vertical dominant wheel events (vertical on
ties), arrows, PageUp/PageDown, Home/End and the optional scrollbar update position.
At scroll edges the normal core parent chain applies. Hiding the scrollbar does
not disable these interactions.

The jump button is enabled by default, named “Jump to latest”, and retains its
built-in action when custom content/size is supplied. It fades with 200ms cubic
ease-out by default, disables during exit, and exposes `next_wake_seconds` for
host scheduling. Reduced motion and zero jump duration settle immediately. An
optional 48-pixel bottom fade has its own 200ms transition. The renderer samples
that fade with 32 bounded strips. Overlays need one initial bounds-tracking frame.

The base composition/model and drawing-free scroller do not link theme
implementation. The base UI needs core, virtual-list base, scroll base and math.
Styled code additionally needs theme, content/Bubble and styled scrollbar code.
Core must include LISTITEM/LOG roles, dominant-axis scroll routing, retained bounds
and opt-in semantic container focus.

Known differences remain: built-in Image, TextView and Attachment dependencies are
absent and require application callbacks; font weight and true rounded image
clipping are unavailable in the current primitives; avatar background uses the
available surface token. Existing Bubble spacing is reused. Arbitrary source
style refinements are represented by slots and geometry rather than a complete
GPUI style builder. Jump tooltips and a configurable button variant are not yet
provided. The accessible jump name deliberately improves on the source's empty
icon-only default. No full rendering or native dependency parity is claimed.

# MessageScroller exact offset and following-tail observers

Include `cui/cui_message_events.h`. `cui_base_message_scroller_events` and
`cui_message_scroller_events` append a borrowed `cui_message_scroller_handler` to
the old arguments. Their result carries the exact old return in `control_result`,
`valid`, independent `offset_changed`/`tail_changed`, delivered zero/one
`offset_change_count`/`tail_change_count`, and `count_overflow` (always false).

Offset payload `cui_message_offset_change` contains metadata and double
`previous,value`. Tail payload `cui_message_tail_change` contains metadata and bool
`previous,value`; tail means the model's following policy, not proximity, rendered
visibility or receipt of a message. Exact double inequality determines offset
change; the existing reducer's tail tolerance remains unchanged. Float scrollbar
and semantic coordinates do not replace the double snapshot.

Each wrapper snapshots before any legacy maintenance, including Styled width
remeasure and Base previous-row-bound reconciliation/layout. It executes the old
operation exactly once and freezes both payloads after completion. Offset callback
runs first, then tail callback if each changed and its handler exists. Styled
observers run after legacy row/jump-content callbacks, tracked-bound registration,
paint and box closure. Base observers run after the complete old reducer. There is
no nested Base observer, second layout call or new allocation/listener storage.

`control_result.changed` includes row measurement and opacity animation; it does
not gate these observers. Offset can change during reconciliation before the
legacy reducer's local old-offset snapshot. Conversely, animation-only changed,
wake scheduling, or total/window changes with stable offset/tail emit nothing.
Tail can change while offset stays zero. Both payloads describe the same completed
operation, independently of callback activity on unrelated application state.

Metadata is CHANGE, UNKNOWN source, with genuine nonzero frame only. Aggregate
layout/measurement/wheel/key/bar/jump effects do not establish one input cause,
index or activation. Non-submission entry rejects before work. Ordinary admitted
inert/layout-only frame-zero maintenance preserves legacy results and change flags
but suppresses callbacks. Missing handlers also leave flags intact and counts zero.
Invalid legacy operations emit nothing; unsupported nonfinite internal offsets do
not generate fabricated previous values. Omission retains no handler.

Explicit reset/splice/append/prepend/measure/remeasure/to-item/to-end/scroll/layout
operations remain synchronous and result-only. Their changes before wrapper entry
are the new baseline, without a delayed event on the next draw. Changes caused by
maintenance inside the observed call are included with UNKNOWN origin. Repeated
submissions observe each call independently; result reads never replay callbacks.
Choose results or observers for application side effects.

Payloads are pointer-free values: copy by assignment into caller storage and use
the copies after callback, frame or context destruction. This does not extend
active model lifetime. Handler/user are borrowed only through return. New observers
may copy payloads and mutate unrelated application data, but cannot mutate/free
active state, records, options/theme or input, recursively submit or destroy
context. Existing legacy renderer/jump callback behavior and restrictions remain
unchanged. State and collection must still agree and remain stable until
`cui_end_frame` completes because tracked bounds write into live state then.
Defer teardown accordingly. Later bounds reconciliation does not retain handlers.

There is no data-received/read, renderer completion, network, GPU, capture/bubble,
veto, context-destruction or foreign-language callback API. VirtualList's pending
window contract is separate; MessageScroller does not gain a deferred finish.

`tests/unit/test_message_events.c` compares legacy and observed Base/Styled results,
row counts, consumed input and exact offsets through anchor/layout/width changes.
It exercises double offsets beyond float precision, tail-only changes, frozen
callback order, animation-only silence, passive/missing/invalid/omitted calls and
copied payload lifetime, and runs existing message regression assertions. Native
execution uses `python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir build -- -R message`.

# Multiline aggregate CHANGE observers

Include `cui/cui_multiline_events.h` for `cui_base_textarea_events` and
`cui_textarea_events`. Each mirrors its existing Textarea entrypoint, appends a
`cui_component_text_handler`, and returns `cui_multiline_event_result`:

```c
cui_multiline_event_result result = cui_textarea_events(
    ui, id, &theme, cui_string("Notes"), edit, &state, options,
    (cui_component_text_handler){on_change, app});
/* result.control is the existing cui_textarea_result. */
```

This facade deliberately aggregates notification: **at most one CHANGE per
submission**, after Base Textarea finalizes its event loop, semantics and scroll
state, and before Styled Textarea performs its remaining layout and paint. Several
text edits, newline insertion, indentation, paste or Undo/Redo can coalesce into
one notification. It is not the per-event timing of
[Input observers](TEXT_INPUT_EVENTS.md). Existing Textarea entrypoints, options,
mutation timing, aggregate results and rendering behavior remain unchanged.

`change_count` counts actual callbacks, zero or one. A missing callback does not
make the control readonly: edits still apply, with zero callback count. A callback
receives the scalar committed `before` and `after` state, including primary
selection and revision. Revision change is the criterion: typing then Undo in one
submission can notify even if final bytes equal initial bytes. Selection, scrolling,
preedit or external edits completed before submission do not themselves notify.

Metadata has CHANGE kind, the target and actual frame sequence, UNKNOWN source,
and HAS_FRAME only. There is no event index or activation: a batch can have many
causes. Do not interpret default scalar index fields when HAS_INDEX is absent.
There is no SUBMIT event. Legacy `pressed_enter`, `enter_secondary` and
`enter_shift` remain in `result.control` with their existing aggregate semantics.

IME START/UPDATE/CANCEL normally changes only preedit presentation and does not
notify. A committed revision change on IME COMMIT notifies; a failed commit with
no revision change does not. Disabled/readonly behavior remains the legacy behavior.

Notifications describe committed edits, not successful layout or validation. If
an edit succeeds and a later row-capacity/layout failure occurs, the observer still
runs and `result.control` retains the legacy error. Initial validation/layout
failure before mutation produces no CHANGE. The Base facade observes every return
from the existing reducer, so an applied edit is not hidden by a subsequent error.
The Styled facade preserves this count even if its later layout/painting fails.

The event's committed text is borrowed only during the callback. Retain it with
`cui_component_event_copy_utf8` and caller-owned bounded storage; copying the event
struct alone does not retain text. Textarea has no password/masking option: its
text payload is not redacted. Hosts handling sensitive documents should avoid
retaining text and use scalar metadata as appropriate.

Observers may set unrelated application flags. They must not mutate, rebind or
destroy the context, edit, state, buffers, history/selection arrays, layout rows,
composition storage, theme or other borrowed descriptors; recursive UI submission
and painting are also unsupported. This is a caller precondition, not a runtime
guard. To close or remove the control, set an application flag and omit it on a
later frame; defer destruction until the frame and renderer have consumed borrowed
resources. An observer cannot reject an already committed edit.

These facades do not add multi-cursor selection notifications, REQUEST, COMMIT,
SUBMIT, or language-binding observers.

`tests/unit/test_textarea_events.c` checks old/new text, selection, revision/history,
aggregate results, semantic identity/value and draw-command equivalence; multiple
updates coalesce; IME preedit, success and capacity failure; absent observers;
readonly/disabled and Enter behavior; bounded copies; deferred omission; committed
edits followed by row-capacity failure; and the direct Base type-then-Undo case.
Legacy Textarea and Editor tests remain required. Native test execution uses the
private-display `scripts/test_local.py` wrapper. No browser/binding parity is claimed.


## Editor observers

Include `cui/cui_editor_events.h` for `cui_base_editor_events` and
`cui_editor_events`. They mirror the corresponding legacy signatures, append the
same text handler, and return `cui_multiline_event_result`. Editor's committed text
is borrowed and not redacted, with scalar primary-selection snapshots only.

Base Editor notifies after the entire existing call, including completion,
multi-cursor, nested Textarea and final search/cursor synchronization. Styled
Editor notifies after its **whole call**, including main painting and completion
popup pointer acceptance. This timing differs from Styled Textarea, which notifies
at its Base seam before paint. The nested Textarea is never observed or replayed.
Keyboard and pointer completion acceptance and simultaneous multi-cursor edits all
coalesce into at most one final revision notification.

Editor metadata uses UNKNOWN source, no index/activation, and HAS_FRAME only when
the actual frame sequence is nonzero. Its callback count derives from committed
revision change even when the legacy result contains an error; `control` remains
exactly the original result. Existing popup paint and mutation timing is preserved:
the observer does not force a new paint to show a just-accepted completion. A later
frame follows the existing invalidation behavior. Initial validation failures with
no revision change do not notify. No cause is inferred from consumed events.

The same no-mutation/reentry/destruction preconditions apply to Editor and its
completion items, search matcher, folds, multi-cursor anchors/history/selection
storage, clipboard scratch and highlight resources. Defer teardown until the outer
facade returns and renderer consumption finishes. Set unrelated flags in the
callback to omit the editor in a later frame.

`tests/unit/test_editor_events.c` checks legacy result/paint/semantic equivalence,
aggregate text batches, keyboard and pointer completion, multi-cursor edits, IME
success/failure, null observer editing, copy lifetime, deferred omission, row
capacity errors after mutation and failures before mutation. It also checks the
Base facade with type-then-Undo returning to the same bytes. Legacy Editor and
Textarea suites remain required; no browser or foreign-binding coverage is implied.

# Optional Linux native accessibility, phase 1

This backend publishes completed CUI semantic snapshots through pinned AccessKit
and executes targeted Focus/Click through Core's accessibility action queue.
The automated Linux X11 test uses a real SDL3 window and independent libAT-SPI
client over DBus. This is transport and action coverage, **not** full native
accessibility, editable-text support, or an Orca/physical screen-reader claim.
Windows/macOS adapters and Wayland screen extents are not implemented here.

## Build and use

Ordinary builds keep `CUI_BUILD_ACCESSIBILITY=OFF` and do not inspect the cache,
invoke Rust or fetch dependencies. Explicitly prebuild the pinned archive with
Rust 1.85+/Cargo, then enable the optional Linux adapter:

```sh
python3 scripts/build_accesskit.py
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCUI_BUILD_ACCESSIBILITY=ON
cmake --build build --parallel 6
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure -R accessibility
cmake --install build --prefix /your/local/prefix
```

CMake imports the existing archive; it never invokes Cargo or downloads a missing
dependency. Missing or mismatched archive, lock, ownership extension or private
header fail configuration. The binary SHA is recorded in installed
`share/cui/licenses/accesskit/accesskit-build.json`; it identifies the local
artifact, rather than claiming a reproducible upstream binary. Run the pinned
builder before configuring to establish its provenance. This is a host-built
Linux package; cross compilation is rejected. Native runtime tests additionally
require SDL3/Freetype/HarfBuzz, libAT-SPI, DBus/gdbus and Xvfb. CMake reports when
those tests are omitted, while the portable snapshot/action tests remain available.

The standalone harness also remains available via
`cmake -S backends/accesskit -B build-accesskit -G Ninja`. It is a validation
harness rather than the installation/package entry point.
Use `--cache PATH` and `-DACCESSKIT_CACHE=PATH` together for another private cache.
Nothing installs globally. The script verifies the archive, every cached source
file and Cargo.lock, and uses `cargo build --release --locked`. The private
ownership module and exact entry-point extension have separate hashes in
`backends/accesskit/extension.json` and the cache's `cui-extension.json`.
See [dependency metadata](../third_party/accesskit/README.md) for licenses and
binary-distribution notice requirements.

Create one `cui_accessibility` per window. On the UI thread:

```c
cui_accessibility *a = cui_accessibility_create((cui_accessibility_config){0});
/* Each frame, before begin_frame: */
cui_accessibility_drain(a, ui);
/* poll host input, begin/build/end the ordinary CUI frame */
cui_accessibility_window window;
if (cui_sdl3_accessibility_window(host, &window))
    cui_accessibility_update(a, ui, window); /* after end_frame */
/* On close, before destroying host/callback user: */
cui_accessibility_destroy(a);
```

Publish **every completed frame**, including removal frames. `update` rejects
Core errors and invalid UTF-8/NUL/nonfinite metadata atomically. Core errors are
sticky: handle them and call `cui_clear_error` according to Core's existing
contract. Never call update during a frame or race public operations with destroy.
The SDL helper only returns portable metadata; it adds no Rust/native bridge
linkage to the SDL library. Its borrowed title is copied by update. Other hosts
supply equivalent title/focus/outer/inner metadata themselves. Window coordinates
and semantic bounds must use the same logical units. X11 1x is tested; mixed-DPI
and decoration behavior require additional platform validation.

## Ownership, generations and actions

Defaults allocate two banks of up to 2048 semantic records and 65536 string bytes
per bank, plus 128 requests. Callers can configure larger bounds before create.
Creation returns null on size overflow/C allocation failure. `stats.native_active`
reports observed native activation; successful creation alone does not prove a
working desktop accessibility bus/client. Snapshot overflow
preserves the previous tree/tokens and reports `CUI_A11Y_CAPACITY`; it never
truncates. Names/descriptions/title are deep copied, with no retained Core pointer.
Unchanged snapshots skip native tree allocations. Published changes currently
use full bounded tree updates; record/relationship lookup is linear, so large
trees should be profiled before increasing the default limit. AccessKit/Rust has
its own allocation behavior; native allocator exhaustion can abort and is not
covered by CUI's recoverable C allocation contract.

A native token is never reused within a bridge. Removing/reintroducing an ID or
changing its role generates a new token, so old queued requests cannot activate
its replacement. Applications must change the CUI ID for a same-frame logical
replacement with the same role; Core exposes no identity stronger than ID/role.
Skipping removal snapshots would also erase this distinction. Public token and
request helpers use the same bounded mailbox as native callbacks, useful for
portable host adapters and tests.

Foreign-thread AccessKit handlers only read the locked copied snapshot and enqueue
Focus/Click tokens. They never call Core or SDL. The optional wake callback must
be thread safe, must not reenter this backend/wait for the UI thread, and must not
call Core/SDL. Main-thread drain revalidates token and Core capability, discards
stale/disabled/modal-obscured requests, and preserves unqueued requests on Core
backpressure. Invalid/stale requests never enter Core. Core queue capacity errors
retain Core's normal observable/sticky error contract. Multiple Click requests
remain individual Core events; the existing boolean interaction API may coalesce
same-control activations within one frame.

`destroy` closes the mailbox and disables wake synchronously. Pinned Unix adapter
removal is asynchronous: the private Rust Arc ownership wrapper retains C storage
until the last activation/action/deactivation handler drops, then releases it once
on that thread. Callers may destroy Core/window/wake userdata after public destroy
returns. No process-lifetime tombstone pool or dangling frame strings are used.

## Mapping and limits

All current CUI roles map explicitly to AccessKit roles. Generic containers can be
flattened by the platform. The tree includes parent/child order, names and copied
descriptions, checked/selected/expanded/disabled/readonly/required/busy/invalid
states, orientation, numeric range metadata, collection positions/table indices,
scroll metadata, live-region policy, focus and window-relative semantic bounds.
Static Label names use AccessKit's label-value convention. `controls` and
`labelled_by` map to native-node references; missing targets are omitted and parent
cycles are rejected. This is metadata mapping, not a claim that every property is
exposed identically by AT-SPI. Core does not expose an OS modal marker or clipping
metadata: the navigation tree retains behind-modal nodes and full semantic bounds;
Core suppresses their actions. OS modal tree hiding/precise clipping need a later
portable semantic extension.

Only Core-supported Focus/Activate are advertised. Focus changes Core focus;
OS window focus remains host metadata, and this bridge does not raise windows. Button, Checkbox, Switch,
Radio, Link and eligible menu items use the ordinary activation path. Tab/Option/
Tree/table compound reducers have conservative Focus-only support; merely showing
a role does not enable its domain action. There is no SetValue, editable text,
selection/caret, document text ranges, scroll action, or increment/decrement bridge.
Read-only scalar/static-label metadata does not imply native Value/Text editing.
See [Core action contract](ACCESSIBILITY_ACTIONS.md).

Pinned `accesskit_atspi_common` 0.20.0 exports `controls` as ControllerFor; its
`relation_set` does not export LabelledBy. The tree stores labelled-by references,
but an AT-SPI LabelledBy claim would be false. Installed libAT-SPI 2.62.1 also
warns about AccessKit's cache signal signatures; direct query/actions pass after
explicit cache refresh. Cache/screen-reader compatibility remains a limitation.

Primary provenance: [accesskit-c pin](https://github.com/AccessKit/accesskit-c/tree/0824c4a1e3a4d13ce5582df20e394fba49485a15),
[Unix adapter ownership](https://docs.rs/accesskit_unix/0.23.0/src/accesskit_unix/adapter.rs.html),
[AT-SPI relationship mapping](https://docs.rs/accesskit_atspi_common/0.20.0/src/accesskit_atspi_common/node.rs.html),
[SDL window bounds](https://wiki.libsdl.org/SDL3/SDL_GetWindowBordersSize).

## Validation

Headless tests cover copied-string lifetimes, unchanged frames, UTF-8 rejection,
atomic string/node capacity failure, configured larger capacity, generations,
missing/stale/disabled/modal targets, invalid actions, threaded mailbox overflow,
Core backpressure, exactly-once drain and boolean coalescing. Private counters
check release exactly once after repeated create/destroy and async native teardown.
The real native test queries roles, screen extents, ControllerFor target and checked
state; requests Component Focus/Action Click and observes actual Core effects;
checks disabled actions and removed/reintroduced nodes. It holds a real native
action pending during destruction and verifies wake runs off the UI thread. The frame label is
intentionally overwritten immediately after snapshot publication.

```sh
cmake -S backends/accesskit -B build-accesskit-asan -G Ninja -DCUI_SANITIZE=ON
cmake --build build-accesskit-asan
ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1 ctest --test-dir build-accesskit-asan --output-on-failure
ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 backends/accesskit/run_native.sh ./build-accesskit-asan/test_accessibility_native
```

C Core/backend/SDK code is ASan/UBSan instrumented; the pinned Rust release
library is not. Native leak detection is disabled for host libraries; C backend
release counters remain checked. The runner isolates DBus/Xvfb and uses in-memory
GSettings, never changing desktop accessibility settings. It starts the installed
registry explicitly because service activation may require a systemd user manager.
Installation includes the portable accessibility header, production adapter,
private static AccessKit archive, CUI Core, AccessKit C/Rust notices and the
aggregate inventory of all ninety pinned Linux dependency notices. Private
test hooks and the upstream AccessKit header are not installed.

A relocated installation supports either:

```cmake
find_package(CUIAccessibility CONFIG REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE CUI::cui_accessibility)
```

or `pkg-config --static --cflags --libs cui-accessibility`. CMake links Core,
the imported Rust archive, Threads, dl and m transitively; pkg-config includes
the static dependency flags. Set `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` or `PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR` to
the installation. Neither interface references the original private cache.

`tests/packaging/test_accessibility_package.py --build build` installs into a
temporary prefix, relocates it, compiles/runs strict C11 consumers through both
interfaces, checks real Focus/Activate effects, all ninety notices, artifact SHA
and absence of private test symbols. It also builds ordinary Core with a
nonexistent cache while the option is OFF and checks missing/corrupt-cache
configuration failures. The optional root CTest suite registers this proof.
Full native runtime coverage still has the phase1 limits documented above.
The reserved distribution check may remain stale until integration regenerates
the global bundles.

# Build your first native CUI app

For the smallest standalone build, use the **native source bundle**.
[Download the archive](https://matteo.merola.co/cui/downloads/cui-native.tar.gz)
and its [SHA-256 checksum](https://matteo.merola.co/cui/downloads/cui-native.tar.gz.sha256). Given a C11
compiler, GNU Make, `ar`, pkg-config, SDL3 >= 3.2, FreeType and HarfBuzz development
packages, unpack it and run:

```sh
tar -xzf cui-native.tar.gz
cd cui-native
make
./build/native_starter
```

This path includes CUI's portable sources, native SDL3 adapter, text/bidi
implementation, generated assets, and Inter 4.1 Regular/Bold fonts with licenses.
It requires no installed CUI package or repository checkout. The default renderer
is SDL3's `SDL_Renderer`; Sokol and SDL_GPU are separate optional integrations.
Linux X11 is the validated native target; Windows, macOS and Wayland native
runtime support remains unverified. External system libraries remain prerequisites. See [macOS native builds and bundles](MACOS.md) and [Linux-to-macOS cross compilation](MACOS_CROSS.md) for the new workflows and their validation limits.

Before building, check their visibility:

```sh
cc --version
make --version
ar --version
pkg-config --atleast-version=3.2 sdl3
pkg-config --modversion sdl3 freetype2 harfbuzz
```

The archive's README explains the dependency layers and font policy. Ordinary
application edits compile only app objects and relink; compiler-generated header
dependencies trigger the appropriate CUI recompilation when headers change.
`make` never acquires dependencies. To produce the archive from this checkout,
run `make native-dist` (Python 3.9+ for this workflow), which writes `build/cui-native.tar.gz`.
The shared `cmake/sources.json` drives CMake, the portable header generator and
native source selection. Native packaging tests generate twice, compare bytes,
unpack outside the repository, verify checksums, build, check incremental rebuilds
and render a bounded Xvfb capture through `scripts/test_local.py`.

## Edit the two-file bundle app

The archive's `main.c` is the host: it loads both font faces, creates the context,
polls input, begins/ends each frame, renders and cleans up. `app.c` is the portable
UI: `app_frame` submits boxes, text and the button. Its `bool *clicked` points to
state owned by the host across frames. Change the greeting or button in `app.c`,
then run `make`; only that application object and executable rebuild.

```sh
make APP_SOURCES="main.c app.c" TARGET=build/my_app
./build/my_app
```

Add new relative `.c` paths to `APP_SOURCES`. Keep the executable directly in
`build/` for automatic font discovery, or provide both font paths explicitly.
The [bundle README](../examples/native_bundle/README.md) is the canonical consumer
build contract. Read [Layout](LAYOUT_GUIDE.md), [IDs and lifetimes](IDS_AND_LIFETIMES.md)
and [Debugging](DEBUGGING.md) before growing the application.

The existing installed-library starter below remains useful for projects that
prefer an installed CUI package and a larger three-page example.

Start with [examples/native_starter](../examples/native_starter/README.md). It is
an ordinary C11 desktop app: a left sidebar selects Home, Projects and Settings;
an account menu stays at the sidebar bottom; Settings edits a name, toggles
notifications and saves local state. Sign-in/out is a demo state change, with no
credentials or network request.

![Native starter Home page](../examples/native_starter/screenshots/home.png)

## Prerequisites

Use a C11 compiler (GCC, Clang or another conforming compiler), CMake 3.20 or
newer, Ninja, pkg-config, SDL3 **3.2 or newer**, FreeType and HarfBuzz development
packages, and a readable `.ttf` or `.otf` font. The Make path additionally needs
Make. Building CUI itself also needs Python 3; its optional C++ ABI example can
be disabled as below, so this path only requires a C compiler. SDL2 is not interchangeable with SDL3. A desktop display/session is needed
to open a window; Xvfb can provide an automated Linux test display.

The commands below assume those tools and libraries are already installed. Check
what pkg-config sees before building:

```sh
cc --version
cmake --version
ninja --version
pkg-config --atleast-version=3.2 sdl3
pkg-config --modversion sdl3 freetype2 harfbuzz
```

## Get the source

```sh
git clone https://github.com/mattmezza/cui.git
cd cui
```

## Build CUI, then the app

From the CUI repository root, install into a directory owned by your user:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCUI_BUILD_NATIVE=ON \
  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=cc -DCUI_BUILD_CPP_EXAMPLE=OFF \
  -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="$PWD/build/prefix"
cmake --build build
cmake --install build
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$PWD/build/prefix/lib/pkgconfig${PKG_CONFIG_PATH:+:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH}"
pkg-config --exists cui-sdl3
cmake -S examples/native_starter -B build/starter -G Ninja
cmake --build build/starter
python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir build/starter
./build/starter/native_starter --font /absolute/path/to/your/font.ttf
```

For example, this machine uses `/usr/share/fonts/noto/NotoSans-Regular.ttf`.
Choose a font that exists on your machine; CUI does not discover an OS font by
family name. If `cui-sdl3` is missing, inspect CUI's CMake output and confirm the
SDL3/FreeType/HarfBuzz development packages are visible through pkg-config.

The starter opens one regular face. CUI does **not** synthesize bold, semibold or
italic. Register the matching files before measuring or drawing styled text;
otherwise an unavailable style falls back to the regular face:

```c
/* font is the regular face returned by cui_font_open. Check both results. */
bool bold_ok = cui_font_register_style(font,
    (cui_text_style){.weight = CUI_TEXT_WEIGHT_BOLD}, "/path/to/NotoSans-Bold.ttf");
bool semibold_ok = cui_font_register_style(font,
    (cui_text_style){.weight = CUI_TEXT_WEIGHT_SEMIBOLD}, "/path/to/NotoSans-SemiBold.ttf");
if (!bold_ok || !semibold_ok) { /* report missing assets to your host */ }
```

Ship these faces with your app or supply explicit paths; filenames vary between
font families and installations. For a single-executable distribution, compile
font bytes into static arrays and open them with `cui_font_open_memory` instead.
See [embedding fonts](TEXT.md#embed-fonts-in-a-native-executable) for a complete
header-generation example, buffer lifetime rules, and style/fallback registration.

The example's CMake project consumes **installed** packages and does not build
the repository as a subdirectory. You can copy the whole `native_starter` folder
elsewhere and run `cmake -S /path/to/copied/folder -B /path/to/app-build -G Ninja`
with the same `PKG_CONFIG_PATH`.

## Make or a direct compiler command

With the same installed prefix exported above:

```sh
make -C examples/native_starter
make -C examples/native_starter test
./examples/native_starter/build/native_starter --font /absolute/path/to/your/font.ttf
```

Or, from the example directory, compile the two app sources directly:

```sh
cc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic \
  $(pkg-config --cflags cui-sdl3) main.c app.c \
  $(pkg-config --static --libs cui-sdl3) -o native_starter
./native_starter --font /absolute/path/to/your/font.ttf
```

Choose Clang with `-DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang` when configuring a fresh CUI build
and `CC=clang` for Make; `cc` normally selects your system compiler. CMake uses
C11 without compiler extensions.

Keep libraries **after** source/object files. CUI installs static archives, so use
`--static`: it includes private adapter/font dependencies. In the tested prefix,
the output included `-lcui_sdl3 -lcui_text -lcui -lm`, `-lcui_bidi`, `-lSDL3`,
FreeType/HarfBuzz and their platform dependencies. Use pkg-config's actual output
rather than copying one machine's entire linker line. This includes `-lm` where
required. The CMake example likewise uses `CUI_STATIC_*` results.

![Bottom account popup](../examples/native_starter/screenshots/account.png)

## Where to change the app

Read [app.h](../examples/native_starter/app.h) for the small application state and
stable control IDs, then [app.c](../examples/native_starter/app.c) for layout and
callbacks. Each frame submits the current page. The sidebar uses actual
`cui_sidebar_menu` activation callbacks; the account popup uses `cui_menu` with
an above-trigger anchor. A growing spacer places its trigger at the bottom.
Settings uses `cui_input_ex`, `cui_checkbox` and `cui_button`. `changed()` in
[main.c](../examples/native_starter/main.c) is a concrete callback seam for your
persistence or application services. State currently lasts only until exit.

`main.c` opens the font, installs styled measuring and font metrics, creates the
SDL3 host and Core context, then polls input, gets the logical window size,
submits the app, applies its cursor and renders. The clipboard interface is
passed into the text input. The SDL adapter starts native text input, forwards
composition/commit events and synchronizes the prior frame's caret rectangle on
poll; the input owns its preedit state. This uses the supported SDL adapter,
without asserting every OS IME has been tested. Rendering and all font/SDL
operations stay on the main thread. Destruction runs in reverse ownership order.

The loop uses a simple 16 ms step to keep the starter readable. A production app
can use an actual clock delta, persist state, add scrollable content and responsive
navigation, and supply fonts covering its text. The fixed 220 px sidebar targets
desktop-sized windows; this starter does not implement mobile navigation.

## Verify it

`test_app.c` exercises real Core/component reducers without opening a window:
navigation callbacks, bottom-account geometry, sign-in/out, menu settings,
Escape dismissal, text-model editing, notification changes and save callbacks.
Run the app for a bounded native capture with:

```sh
./build/starter/native_starter --font /absolute/path/to/font.ttf \
  --frames 3 --capture build/starter/home.bmp
```

Linux automation can prefix that command with
`xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1600x1000x24" env SDL_VIDEODRIVER=x11 SDL_RENDER_DRIVER=software`.
Use a screen at least as large as the app window for coordinate-based interaction.
The screenshot above is from the actual SDL3 window, not a browser mockup.

Historical starter validation (before the current usability additions) checked an actual local installation:
standalone CMake/CTest, Make with warnings treated as errors, the direct compiler
command, and a Core-only build of `app.c` plus `test_app.c` all passed. At that historical checkpoint, integrated repository
CTest passed 96/96, sanitizer checks 96/96 and portable WASI suites 80/80. An Xvfb SDL3 window exercised Projects navigation, bottom-menu
sign-in/out, Settings navigation, editing the name to Grace, disabling
notifications and saving; callbacks reported the resulting state. These checks
cover the starter, not every platform, font or IME.

![Actual native settings after saving](../examples/native_starter/screenshots/settings.png)

# Native text integration audit

At integration/next18 `b291765`, native font shaping and explicit line geometry
worked, but ordinary wrapping and editor geometry did not preserve that result.
`tests/integration/test_native_text_geometry.c` reproduces four observable
mismatches using supported Hebrew glyphs and an explicitly registered fallback
face. The follow-up implements the unwrapped Input host geometry seam described in
[INPUT_VISUAL_GEOMETRY.md](INPUT_VISUAL_GEOMETRY.md). The default executable now
verifies fixed Input behavior and returns 0; `--audit` preserves the remaining
Textarea and automatic wrapped-paragraph observations and returns 1. It returns
77 when optional native bidi or actual supported font fixtures are unavailable.

## Runtime evidence

With Noto Sans as the primary and Noto Sans Hebrew as an explicit fallback:

| Operation on `אבג` at size 14 | Original editor result | Native shaped result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Caret at original UTF-8 byte 0 | x=0 | x=22.094, the visual right edge |
| Hit at visual left edge | Input byte 0, Textarea byte 0 | byte 6, the logical end |
| Select first Hebrew character, bytes 0..2 | Highlight x=0 | Highlight x=13.250, over the actual rightmost character |

The current Input path matches all of these results when its geometry hook is
configured. Textarea still produces the prefix-based results in `--audit`.
These are shaped cluster edges, so no interior ligature/GDEF caret policy is
needed to reproduce the mismatch. The Textarea IME input rectangle follows its
incorrect prefix caret position as well. The test compares the actual painted
selection rectangle, not just the underlying owner's selection state.

The second fixture submits ordinary `cui_text("אבג 123 !")` in a narrow box.
Core emits a wrapped `CUI_DRAW_TEXT` command containing `123 !`. Drawing that
command through the renderer's actual native font entry point yields a raster
identical to independently analyzing `123 !` as a new LTR paragraph. It differs
from `cui_font_layout_line` on the original paragraph with scalar range 4..9:
that wrapped line retains RTL paragraph context and moves punctuation to the
other side of the number run. The command's independently analyzed paragraph
level is 0; the original paragraph's level is 1.

Before reporting gaps, the test independently shapes the Hebrew fixture using
HarfBuzz with explicit RTL/script/language/cluster flags. It compares nonzero
source glyph IDs, original byte clusters, glyph positions, and advance width.
Ordinary native font drawing matches explicit layout rasterization and emits
110 nonzero pixel samples for this fixture. Thus this audit does not mistake
missing-glyph tofu, an unshaped native measure callback, or a missing font for
an integration defect. Exact coordinate/pixel values depend on the selected
fixture; the comparisons derive expected values at runtime.

## Actual path through the code

- `src/core/cui.c` installs `cui_core_measure`, which forwards to the host's
  styled measurement callback. The native examples register
  `cui_font_measure[_styled]`. Those native callbacks already shape bidi text;
  this is not a claim that they use unshaped metrics.
- `cui_text` selects Clay word wrapping. The pinned Clay measurement cache
  measures word slices and spaces separately (`third_party/clay/clay.h:1717`).
  Core's text command conversion (`src/core/cui.c:1773`) copies the emitted
  line substring, size/style and bounds, but no original paragraph or line
  range. Merely switching the scalar font measurement implementation cannot
  restore context once that information is gone.
- SDL3 (`backends/sdl3/cui_sdl3.c:517`), SDL GPU
  (`backends/sdl_gpu/cui_sdl_gpu.c:433`), Sokol
  (`backends/sokol/cui_sokol.c:594`) and software rendering
  (`backends/software/cui_software.c:272`) call `cui_font_draw_styled` per text
  command. The audit invokes this common entry point headlessly; it does not
  claim to open a GPU window or test GPU pixels.
- The native font path correctly separates actual hard paragraphs and preserves
  U+2028 line context inside its own whole-string input (`src/text/cui_text.c`,
  `text_lines_create`/`text_paragraph_append`). It cannot reconstruct context
  already removed by Core or Textarea automatic wrapping.
- The original Input hit testing (`src/base/cui_base.c:399`) binary-searched logical prefix
  widths and immediately returned byte 0 at the left edge. Its legacy fallback
  still does; configured unwrapped Input now consumes host geometry. Original
  Input paint and IME rectangles also used prefix measurements (`src/components/cui_components.c`,
  `cui_input_paint`). Textarea's public row-x/row-offset and pointer hit functions
  use the same monotone-prefix assumption (`src/base/cui_textarea.c:408`).
- Textarea measures and paints each selected wrapped byte slice separately and
  draws one prefix-based selection span (`src/components/cui_textarea.c:150`).
  Caret painting, reveal, vertical preferred-x navigation and IME rectangles
  follow those prefix coordinates. It does not call the native cluster geometry
  APIs. The runtime test verifies row geometry, IME rectangle and actual
  selection paint on an unwrapped RTL line; the wrapped Textarea context loss
  follows the inspected slice submission, rather than a separate GPU test.

The edit model continues to own valid UTF-8/grapheme selection and logical
movement. This audit does not equate native shaped clusters with every editor
grapheme or claim visual keyboard navigation already exists.

## Narrow next implementation ownership

The reproductions justified two independent changes. The first is now
implemented for unwrapped Input, with the explicit cluster-interior fallback
limits documented in INPUT_VISUAL_GEOMETRY.md. The second remains pending.

1. Implemented: **unwrapped Input visual geometry** through a portable host
   callback seam rather than making Core depend on native text/font types.
   The implementation covers the geometry callback public/config seam in
   `include/cui/cui.h` and `src/core/cui.c`, its native implementation in
   `include/cui/cui_text.h`/`src/text/cui_text.c`, Input geometry plumbing in
   `include/cui/cui_base.h`/`src/base/cui_base.c` and Input painting in
   `src/components/cui_components.c`, with focused headless/native integration
   tests. Caret, pointer hit, selection rectangles, horizontal reveal and IME
   rect now use a retained session while measurement-only hosts keep their
   existing path. Exact shaped-interior offsets deliberately use the documented
   legacy fallback without changing logical selection. Textarea remains a
   separate follow-up.
2. Separately preserve **original paragraph plus chosen line range** through
   wrapping and renderer submission. Initial ownership requires Core text
   command metadata/layout, native text, and the SDL/GPU/Sokol/software text
   adapters plus source/raster regressions. The public metadata must remain
   portable CUI types. The existing `cui_font_layout_line` already accepts full
   paragraph context and selected scalar ranges; adapters should receive enough
   original information to use it. Re-shaping each emitted substring cannot
   satisfy the reproduced UAX9 line-context behavior. Word-breaking policy and
   capacity/lifetime contracts need explicit tests; font fallback alone does
   not fix the handoff.

Full grapheme editing parity, interior ligature carets using optional GDEF,
visual arrow navigation, multi-line affinity policy, OS font discovery and
Unicode line-break parity remain beyond those narrow changes. The confirmed
fixtures need none of those claims. The relevant existing primary models are
[UAX9 line reordering](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/tr9-51.html#Reordering_Resolved_Levels)
and [HarfBuzz cluster semantics](https://harfbuzz.github.io/working-with-harfbuzz-clusters.html).

## Reproduction and validation

```sh
cmake --build build
cc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -Iinclude \
  $(pkg-config --cflags freetype2 harfbuzz) \
  tests/integration/test_native_text_geometry.c \
  build/libcui_text.a build/libcui_bidi.a build/libcui.a \
  $(pkg-config --libs freetype2 harfbuzz) -lm -o /tmp/cui-native-text-audit
/tmp/cui-native-text-audit
/tmp/cui-native-text-audit --audit # preserves remaining known gaps

```

Use `CUI_TEST_FONT` and `CUI_TEST_HEBREW_FONT` to select explicit supported

not registered by this worker because CMake belongs to the integrator. Its
default verifies fixed Input behavior; `--audit` still preserves four remaining
Textarea/wrapping observations rather than declaring full native integration.

Validation at this snapshot: portable warnings-as-errors native build and the
new manual integration compile pass; existing CTest passes 92/93. The sole
failure is the expected distribution regeneration check for changed Core/Base/
Components headers, which is integrator-owned. The enabled default
passes using actual Noto fallback fixtures; `--audit` retains the four remaining
Textarea/wrapping observations.

returns 77 with an explicit unavailable message. The follow-up changes only its

# Opt-in source Notification motion

After initializing the caller-owned state, select source motion explicitly:

```c
cui_notification_state state;
/* entries, settings and host are application-owned. */
if (cui_notification_init(&state, entries, capacity, settings, host)) {
    state.motion_policy = CUI_NOTIFICATION_MOTION_SOURCE;
}
```

Zero-initialized state and initialization retain `CUI_NOTIFICATION_MOTION_LEGACY`.
Reinitialization resets this opt-in. Motion and `settings.shadow_policy` are
independent: use SOURCE shadows as well when both source behaviors are wanted.
No Theme, Core, Base lifecycle or renderer API is changed by this policy.

SOURCE follows the pinned gpui-component 0.7.1 implementation at
`87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`:

| Transition | Duration | Translation | Opacity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Enter | 400ms | 96px outside the edge → 0 | 0 → 1 |
| Exit | 200ms | 0 → 96px outside the edge | 1 → 0 |

Top-left/center/right move upward outside the stack, bottom-left/center/right
move downward, and left/right-center have zero translation. Elapsed time is
mapped through CSS cubic-bezier `(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1)`, solving its x coordinate
before sampling y. SOURCE uses the source's bounded eight-step Newton and
32-step bisection solver; LEGACY retains its existing six-step solver and 16px
distance. Measured animated card bounds, custom content, interactions and copied
shadow casters all follow the same translated card.

The source locations are `crates/component/src/notification.rs:30–32,485–529`
and `crates/base/src/animation.rs:14–64`. SHA-256 respectively:

- `09010c94024ee6e2580ecf557d97dcf276512a52be8cf298e0936088df0afeca`
- `b17a0e92d239c4f947373f6ebf699e3fde7c83f13e2f96e979ada8b823eef44d`

Reduced motion samples the oneshot end state, matching GPUI's
`AnimationExt` contract and implementation at
`gpui-pre-0.3.8/src/elements/animation.rs:78–80,407–413`
(SHA-256 `117a4b1a580382b21accce30308f0480853c1e9372220566748dcb5f74d5793e`).
Thus enter is immediately at rest and fully opaque; exit is immediately at its
translated, transparent end state. Stack springs already snap under the existing
reduced-motion setting. SOURCE requests the remaining lifecycle deadline instead
of 16ms animation wakes. It does not invent immediate removal: the source
ToastManager retains its 400ms/200ms transitions independently
(`crates/base/src/toast.rs:234–266`). Presented results and close callbacks retain
those deadlines. Autohide deadlines and hover/focus pause behavior are preserved.

Render once per active UI frame through `cui_notifications_checked`, passing a
stable overlay ID and monotonic finite owner clock. Unknown motion enum values
fail before reductions, callbacks, output publication or UI emission. SOURCE
also checks the initialized owner's fade phase and finite timing/visibility
state. Existing shadow-policy validation and checked-render transaction limits
remain as documented in [NOTIFICATION_SHADOWS.md](NOTIFICATION_SHADOWS.md): later
UI/frame/renderer errors cannot undo previously accepted host callbacks. No new
borrowed buffers, sampler callbacks or resource lifetime are introduced.

The effective SOURCE shadow opacity remains transition opacity to the fourth
power, multiplied by independent stack visibility, then inherited Core opacity
once. Motion does not change the two copied source layers or their quantization.

Evidence:

- `test_notification_source_motion.c`: all eight placements at five actual enter
  times, an intermediate exit, exact completion/removal boundaries, legacy
  compatibility, reduced deadlines/no animation redraw, close callback timing,
  independent shadow policies, invalid policy/NaN rejection and Software pixels
  distinguishing 96px source movement from the old 16px card location. The exact
  pre-change component source fails its new source-distance assertion; the
  external reproduction keeps the appended header solely to select that policy.
- `test_notification_source_motion_sdl.c`: actual SDL Renderer OpenGL and software
  drivers, 32 controlled placement/enter/exit/scale frames per driver. Pixel
  capture happens before real Present; assertions abort rather than show modal
  ignore workarounds. A GNU/Clang native fixture needs `--wrap=SDL_RenderPresent`.
- `test_notification_source_motion.py`: actual WASM component commands and Canvas
  pixels for 64 controlled enter/exit/placement/reduced cases at DPR1/2, including
  legacy/source position distinction. Independent double-precision Bezier
  inversion checks geometry; the shared raster independently checks composition.
  No wall-clock sleeps drive these transitions.

Strict C11, scoped GCC ASan/UBSan and portable Wasmtime checks exercise the new
headless fixture. The worker does not register global tests or regenerate
headers; integrator regeneration is required for the appended state member.
The browser fixture takes `--output` and optional `--chromium` arguments.

This is a bounded motion slice, not Notification-family completion. Arbitrary
source style refinement and renderer-native GPUI AA/color/shader identity remain
separate boundaries. Native GPU/Sokol source-shadow coverage is from the prior
shadow slice; this motion fixture adds actual SDL Renderer and Canvas proof.

# Notification source shadows

Set `settings.shadow_policy = CUI_NOTIFICATION_SHADOW_SOURCE` before initializing
the notification state. Zero-initialized settings and
`cui_notification_settings_default()` retain `CUI_NOTIFICATION_SHADOW_LEGACY`.
SOURCE replaces the sixteen decorative rectangles with two copied drop-shadow
layers on each visible card's final, animated bounds:

| Order | Offset | Sigma | Spread | Color at rest |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | (0, 10) | 7.5 | -3 | black, alpha 26/255 |
| 2 | (0, 4) | 3 | -4 | black, alpha 26/255 |

The caster uses `theme.radius_lg`. Core paints both shadows before the card
surface; content clipping and the ordinary border retain their existing order.
Source-invisible collapsed cards and system-only notifications emit no shadows.
The popover surface palette, custom content, stacking, dismissal controls,
deadlines and existing slide distance remain the Notification renderer's current
behavior.

The pinned source is gpui-component 0.7.1, commit
`87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`,
`crates/component/src/styled.rs:85–95` (ordered layers),
`crates/component/src/notification.rs:494–495,518–528` (transition ink), and
`crates/base/src/toast.rs:514–534` (independent stack visibility).
Source shadow ink uses transition alpha cubed, then element opacity adds another
transition-alpha factor. CUI projects the resulting ink as
`round(255 * 0.1 * transition_alpha^4 * stack_visibility)`.
Stack visibility is an independent ancestor factor, not raised to the fourth
power. External Core ancestor opacity applies once after this projection.
The source floating alpha 0.1 becomes 26/255 at rest; this is an explicit
8-bit projection rather than floating Hsla identity.

```c
cui_notification_settings settings = cui_notification_settings_default();
settings.shadow_policy = CUI_NOTIFICATION_SHADOW_SOURCE;
/* Initialize caller-owned entries/state using these settings. */
cui_notification_advance next;
bool accepted = cui_notifications_checked(ui, overlay_id, theme, &state,
                                          viewport, now_seconds, &next);
/* End the active frame and check Core/renderer errors separately. */
```

`cui_notification_settings_valid` rejects unknown policies. Reducer operations
also reject invalid settings before changing state or invoking callbacks.
The checked render entry requires an active UI frame, valid initialized state,
independent output storage, finite viewport/time and, in SOURCE mode, valid
shadow radius and finite owner fade state. Rejected inputs leave its output,
owner reductions, callbacks and UI emission untouched. SOURCE setter failure
returns false without publishing the output. Already accepted reductions or
host/custom-content callbacks cannot be rolled back by later UI capacity,
`cui_end_frame`, or renderer-preflight failure. The compatibility wrapper returns
a zero advance on checked failure. This API does not certify frame submission.

The two local layer values are copied by Core; neither the stack array nor the
temporary theme is retained by a deferred renderer. Existing caller ownership
of notification strings, content callbacks, state entries and host userdata is
unchanged. Custom content must continue honoring the supplied opacity and its
existing borrowed-lifetime contract. Renderer budgets, supported shadow domain,
pre-clear rejection and copied cache keys use the shared drop-shadow capability.

Evidence includes meaningful headless geometry/order, invalid-policy/radius/fade
rejection, controlled exit, independent stack opacity, translucent surface and
ancestor composition, hidden/system delivery and custom disabled/loading
children. Software and actual SDL Renderer (OpenGL and software drivers), SDL
GPU (Vulkan), Sokol (Mesa GL), and Canvas exercise actual component commands in
light/dark themes at scales 1 and 2. Failed shadow preparation preserves previous
pixels; native SDL captures occur before Present because accelerated backbuffers
need not retain pixels after presentation.

This slice does not complete Notification parity: the source's 96px slide,
arbitrary source style refinement and exact GPUI native shader/AA/color identity
remain separate work. Source behavior is not inferred from the private shadow
helper's name. The unchanged LEGACY approximation remains available explicitly.

The native/unit/WASI/browser fixtures are registered by the integrator; generated
headers include the optional policy and checked entrypoint. The four GNU SDL
wrap flags capture actual completed drawing before presentation. Reproduce
Canvas with `uv run tests/web/test_notification_shadows.py --output build/notification-shadow-probe`.

# Aggregate NumberInput CHANGE observation

Include `cui/cui_number_events.h` and use `cui_base_number_input_events` or
`cui_number_input_events` with the existing arguments plus a
`cui_number_event_handler`. Both return the unchanged native `control` result and
an actual `change_count` of zero or one. The callback is
`void callback(void *user, const cui_number_change_event *event)`.

The pointer-free payload contains shared `event` metadata and finite double
`before`/`after` values. It observes the final committed numeric owner, not draft
revision or intermediate steps. Exact numeric inequality is used: signed zeros
compare equal, adjacent finite doubles and subnormals remain distinct, and changes
that cancel within a call do not notify. Invalid/nonfinite entry owners are still
rejected by the native reducer. No epsilon, float narrowing or extra formatting
is introduced.

```c
static void number_changed(void *user, const cui_number_change_event *event) {
    double *last_observed = user;
    *last_observed = event->after;
}
cui_number_event_result result = cui_number_input_events(
    ui, id, theme, cui_string("Quantity"), state, value, options,
    (cui_number_event_handler){number_changed, last_observed});
/* result.control retains changed/submitted/invalid/step_direction/error. */
```

An absent callback accepts and ignores user data and still performs ordinary
reduction. `step_by/step_user` remain the existing step-magnitude policy with the
same invocation order; they are not observer conflicts or requested-value
callbacks. Missing observers never make the control readonly.

Delivery occurs after Base reduction's final bookkeeping/semantics/invalidation,
before Styled painting. A numeric change already committed despite an edit error
still notifies; neither `error` nor callback count promises successful rendering
or rollback. In particular, failed clamp-draft normalization can preserve the
parsed draft value rather than the entry owner. The original result is returned
without suppressing its error. Enter without numeric change does not notify;
`submitted` remains its legacy aggregate flag. This API adds no REQUEST, COMMIT,
SUBMIT or per-event notification.

Only ordinary active, enabled, editable submissions notify. Inert/layout-only,
outside-frame, disabled and readonly calls do not notify. They still execute the
legacy reducer once: draft synchronization/normalization and any legacy owner
mutation remain compatible, so zero callbacks does not imply no model changes.
External owner synchronization completed before entry is not a numeric change of
this call. Draft-only edits, preedit and invalid drafts also do not establish one.

Metadata is CHANGE at the NumberInput root ID, source UNKNOWN and HAS_FRAME only.
The same nonzero `cui_frame_sequence` before/after reduction proves the current
ordinary completion frame, excluding passive/protected phases. No input index,
source or activation flag is inferred. This is not a physical-input audit log.

Callback/user are borrowed only during this call; no registration is retained.
The payload may be copied. Keep context, state, editor, composition resources,
owner value and user storage alive until the outer call returns and applicable
frame rendering consumes its borrowed data. No recursive submission, edit/state/
selection/composition mutation, rebind, destruction or exception unwinding through
C during notification. Updating unrelated application state is allowed.

The observer may assign a finite new owner value through its own captured pointer.
The event remains the frozen native before/after snapshot and does not recursively
notify. Current semantics and Styled paint retain the already-reduced draft;
the next submission notices the owner mismatch and synchronizes normally without
notification for that synchronization alone. No hidden post-callback draft rewrite
or `last_value` adjustment is performed. Nonfinite observer assignments are outside
the supported update contract and cause native validation failure next time.

Unit coverage compares Base/Styled facades with legacy passive/disabled/readonly
reduction, checks multi-step coalescing, Enter/blur normalization, finite precision,
real edit-capacity failure after owner mutation, policy call counts, owner updates
and ignored user data without a callback. Existing numeric tests remain unchanged.
Bridge NumberInput still uses its existing queued LEGACY payload; this C API does
not add typed bridge scalar events, bindings or full input-family parity.

# Numeric and sequence controls

`cui_numeric.h` provides NumberInput, Pagination, Rating and Stepper. Values and changes belong to the application; a true result signals a controlled value/index change. Theme values define typography, surfaces and spacing. Each styled function calls its corresponding `cui_base_*` reducer exactly once, then paints without adding semantics or mutating state. Base reducers are independently usable with custom layouts and emit no draw commands. `cui_numeric_part_id` exposes stable child IDs for these layouts. Button/page/star/step activations are processed in input order, including multiple activations in one frame. The implementation is portable C11 and uses semantic snapshots and common draw commands, without platform or Clay types.

## NumberInput

Create a single-line `cui_edit` attached to an application-owned NUL-terminated buffer, then zero-initialize `cui_number_state` with its borrowed editor. The editor must outlive the state. Drafts are bounded to 127 bytes; a 128-byte buffer accommodates every supported draft. Editor history/scratch allocation remains explicit in its configuration.

`cui_number_input` accepts a finite `double *value`. Initialization and subsequent external value replacements synchronize the draft. Valid typing updates the value immediately; incomplete drafts such as `-` or `.` stay visible without replacing the last accepted value. Default typing admits an optional leading sign, digits and a decimal point; optional exponent typing admits incomplete exponent drafts until they become valid. Full-width digits, signs, decimal point and ideographic full stop normalize to ASCII. Other characters, malformed UTF-8, invalid prospective syntax and oversized insertions are rejected atomically. Existing editor selection, left/right/home/end, shift-selection, backspace/delete and select-all are supported.

Enter submits, and Enter or blur clamps valid drafts to optional finite min/max bounds. Up/Down and plus/minus buttons use fixed positive `step` or an application callback receiving value/direction. Invalid/nonpositive steps do not mutate the value; `step_direction` still reports an attempted step for application-owned handling. Stepping below the minimum downwards or above the maximum upwards does nothing. Crossing a bound clamps in the requested direction; finite overflow without a bound is rejected. Draft formatting failures do not commit a button step. Disabled suppresses editing and focus; readonly keeps readable/focusable text while suppressing editing and stepping. Prefix, suffix and field width are configurable.

Standalone `cui_number_parse` recognizes strict ASCII decimal/exponent grammar without whitespace, hexadecimal, comma, NaN or infinity. It validates before adapting the single decimal point to the current C locale's radix for one correctly rounded `strtod` conversion. `cui_number_format` reverses locale radix adaptation and emits 17 significant digits, preserving finite double round trips, including signed zero and nonzero subnormals. Underflow to zero is rejected. These functions never mutate global locale; concurrent changes of the process locale remain unsupported. Semantic float values/ranges saturate at `FLT_MAX` when the accepted double exceeds semantic storage precision.

NumberInput renders the decrement button, centered editable value and increment button inside a single themed frame. Its `name` is an accessible label rather than a painted legend. Source Minus/Plus SVGs use the theme asset provider; no textual +/- stand-ins are painted. Step buttons remain pointer-only and route pointer focus to the editor, with accessible Increment/Decrement names. They stay enabled at configured bounds; an attempted step reports its direction while the clamped value stays unchanged. Arrow-key stepping still belongs to the focused editor. Step buttons have only the outer corners rounded, one pixel inside the frame radius, and fill the frame's inner height. Normal is transparent, hover uses input at40% alpha and held uses60%; glyphs use secondary foreground. Disabled dims the whole frame to50%, with the source disabled input/border tokens inside. `no_appearance` suppresses the frame surface/border. The renderer shares Input's selection and caret painting, with retained horizontal scrolling.

`cui_number_options.size` defaults to `CUI_NUMBER_MEDIUM` (zero); SMALL, LARGE, XSMALL and CUSTOM are available. `cui_number_measure` exposes the complete metrics. Preset metrics scale by positive `density` or `theme.font_size / 16`: XS/S/M/L heights20/24/32/44, fonts12/14/14/16 and line box20. Step widths24/24/32/32 and SVG sizes12/14/16/24 follow the frozen source. Custom size is the frame height, step width and icon size, with font87.5% of that size. The frame width defaults200; negative width grows. Fixed-width values center correctly on the first frame. The inner field uses Source Input padding without another border or surface.

Remaining GPUI options include thousands-separator masks, custom pattern validation and fully composed prefix/suffix elements. NumberInput still has pointer text positioning, undo shortcuts, native clipboard and IME gaps in its base reducer. Its semantic field is currently Textbox rather than a native SpinButton role; there is no outer focus shadow or caret blinking. For editing automatically formatted scientific values, enable `allow_exponent`.

## Pagination

Pages are one-based, with zero representing an empty result. Current page clamps to `[1,total]` or zero when no pages exist. Buttons support First, Previous, Next and Last, and visible numbered pages. A compact mode shows the current/total count. Boundaries and the current page disable redundant activation.

The allocation-free item model emits endpoints and a radius-bounded neighborhood, fills single omitted pages, and inserts ellipses for larger gaps. Radius is capped at three, with at most eleven items. Arithmetic remains bounded for `SIZE_MAX` totals. The styled control uses radius two. All page buttons use the ordinary pointer/keyboard button routing; selected semantic details reflect the controlled page. Layout wrapping, configurable label slots, exact GPUI compact typography and arbitrary visible-page budgets remain pending.

## Rating

Rating accepts a controlled floating value, clamps to the configured maximum and quantizes to integer or half steps. The default maximum is five; the bounded renderer caps it at one hundred. Pointer activation selects a star; left/right halves select half/integer values when enabled. Keyboard arrows change by one step and Home/End select zero/maximum. Optional Clear supports both a pointer button and Delete/Backspace. Individual stars use pointer focus with no extra Tab stops; choosing a star returns keyboard focus to the rating group. Disabled and readonly suppress activation; readonly remains identified by semantic details. Full, half and empty indicators use antialiased SVG star masks, tinted by the theme. Half values crop the filled star mask. Custom icon/color slots and hover previews remain pending.

## Stepper

Stepper uses a controlled zero-based selected index, bounded to existing items. Each item has title, optional description, explicit pending/active/complete/error status and disabled state. Pointer or Enter/Space activation updates the index. Whole-group disabling suppresses all items. Horizontal and vertical layouts use the same model. Selected semantic details and the visible Current label update in the activation frame. The selected button uses the primary variant; other buttons use the outline variant. Explicit complete/error statuses remain visible on other steps; an inactive active status displays Pending. Status text includes non-color meaning. Empty arrays are supported, and this convenience renderer bounds arrays to one hundred items. Custom icons, connector lines and exact size variants remain pending.

Headless tests cover real routed key/pointer events, controlled replacement, draft rejection and CJK normalization, blur/Enter clamping, disabled/readonly behavior, half-star selection and clearing, page navigation, disabled step activation, all four themes, strict finite parsing and extreme double round trips. Exhaustive small pagination windows and `SIZE_MAX` boundaries test overflow/ordering invariants. New sources compile with strict C11 warnings; existing CTest and instrumented ASan/UBSan tests run before submission. Source/test/distribution registration belongs to the integrator.

Compile `tests/unit/test_numeric.c` with `-DCUI_NUMERIC_BASE_ONLY` to run the same routed-event assertions against base reducers, bare geometry, and no theme/components link. The worker validates this separate executable as well as the styled path, including a Last-then-Previous activation sequence in one frame.

For per-activation requests with application-owned validation, use the additive [controlled Stepper navigation API](STEPPER_NAVIGATION.md). It preserves the legacy mutating reducers and aggregate change observers; the guide provides a compiling owner-validation example.
