# Numeric selection CHANGE observers

Include `cui/cui_numeric_selection_events.h`. Pagination's additive Base and
Styled `_events` entrypoints accept `{change, user}` and return the original
aggregate bool as `control`, plus actual synchronous `change_count` (zero or one).
A missing callback ignores user and preserves normal reduction.

```c
static void page_changed(void *user, const cui_pagination_change_event *event) {
    size_t *last_page = user; /* Separate application storage, not the owner. */
    *last_page = event->after;
}
/* During the ordinary active UI frame: */
/* cui_pagination_events(ui, id, theme, &page, total, false, false,
 *     (cui_pagination_event_handler){page_changed, &last_observed_page}); */
```

The event contains pointer-free shared `event` metadata and exact native
`size_t before`, `after`, `total`. Pages are one-based, or zero when empty.
Normalization is part of the aggregate change. Multiple operations coalesce;
returning to the entry value produces no notification. Numbered-button mapping
continues to use the legacy normalized entry window.

Callbacks run after Base reduction/semantics and before Styled paint. Metadata
has CHANGE, root target, UNKNOWN source and HAS_FRAME for the current active
completion frame. It does not claim input index, activation count or physical
origin. Disabled, inert and layout-only submissions retain legacy normalization
and bool behavior but never notify: zero callbacks does not mean zero mutation.
`control` is not a validation or paint-success result.

Handler/user are borrowed for the outer call; no registration or replay occurs.
Copy events for later use. Do not change the owner, recursively submit, mutate
borrowed descriptors, destroy storage/context, or unwind foreign exceptions from
the callback. Request teardown or owner updates in separate application state
and perform them after the outer call returns. Styled paint rereads the owner;
owner mutation during observation has no supported rendering contract.

Stepper adds the same Base/Styled `_events` pattern with a distinct
`cui_stepper_change_event`: exact `size_t before`, `after`, `count`. Indices are
zero-based; an empty list normalizes to zero. Descriptors, titles and descriptions
remain borrowed through the call. Selection does not rewrite explicit statuses;
Styled paint still shows Current only on the selected item, retains Complete and
Error, and shows an unselected ACTIVE descriptor as Pending. Counts above 100 or
missing nonempty descriptor arrays retain legacy rejection. Disabled items cannot
activate, while list-wide normalization still occurs when disabled or passive.

Rating adds a distinct `cui_rating_change_event` containing native `float before`
and `after`, `bool before_finite`, and effective defaulted/capped `unsigned maximum`.
The legacy reducer normalizes NaN and infinities to zero; an eligible observation
preserves that nonfinite `before` and sets `before_finite=false`. Do not compare
NaN using ordinary equality or assume canonical NaN payload bits. The committed
`after` is finite. Finite values compare exactly, with no epsilon; signed zeros
compare equal. Whole/half-step rounding and range clamping can cause CHANGE even
without input. Readonly suppresses callbacks while preserving normalization.
Pointer half-star selection and keyboard/full-star activation retain their
existing differences; Home still clears regardless of `clearable`, while
Delete/Backspace clearing requires it. Rating is a float API, unlike NumberInput's
double API. Failed later icon preparation does not undo a committed change.

Legacy entrypoints remain unchanged. These facades do not expose per-event
REQUEST, COMMIT or SUBMIT, and add no bridge notification tags or binding wrappers.
The native `size_t` payload is not a guarantee about legacy bridge float transport.

Verification uses actual reducers, unchanged legacy tests, and paired Base/Styled
submissions comparing scalar owners, bools, semantics, focus, geometry, draw text,
colors and Rating bitmap pixels. Tests include queue-rejected disabled accessibility
actions, input coalescing/cancellation, nil handlers, passive normalization, and
callback payload copies with teardown deferred until the outer call returns.
Native test execution uses `scripts/test_local.py` with a private display; hardware
GPU behavior is outside this portable slice.

# Repeatable human and agent onboarding tasks

This is a task protocol, not a measured usability result. Run the same tasks for
a human and an agent against the same revision, extracted native bundle, machine
and installed prerequisites. Start timing after prerequisite verification; record
installation time separately. Keep the documentation available in both runs.

| Task | Completion evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Build unchanged bundle outside repository | `make` exit status and bounded capture |
| Change greeting in `app.c` | Capture shows new text; vendor object timestamps unchanged |
| Add a second portable `.c` file and rename target | Build using `APP_SOURCES`/`TARGET`, capture from renamed executable |
| Compose a mail row | Fixed avatar/trailing timestamp, growing text, constrained narrow-window content |
| Repeat and reorder three rows | Stable record-key scopes; correct row activates after reordering |
| Diagnose a missing icon and duplicate ID | Correct registry lookup, observed error and repaired submission |

Record elapsed time, build attempts, compiler errors, invented API names,
documentation pages opened, interventions, final test evidence and unresolved
limitations for each task. Do not count a screenshot alone as interaction proof.
For mail rows test long subjects and narrow widths; for identity test activation
before and after reorder. Keep benchmark application experiments outside vendor
sources. Automated Linux captures must run on invisible Xvfb; repository tests
use `python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir build`. Defer GPU-only observations.

Report raw observations before comparing human/agent outcomes. This protocol
makes no claim that the tasks have been run or that onboarding is universally
fast. The full catalog retains 78 entries and their recorded limitations.

## Automated observations for this milestone

The native-bundle consumer test builds the unchanged two-file app outside the
checkout, verifies UI-only incremental compilation, builds a source in a
subdirectory with a renamed executable, and captures both that app and the mail
fixture. The mail Core fixture drives Compose/Discard, selects and stars the
second repeated row, verifies its reader text, and scrolls the list while the
folder pane stays still. The exact four-argument sidebar content callback is
compiled with warnings treated as errors. Text/JSON layout export is exercised
through the native command line. These are automated correctness observations;
human elapsed time, agent elapsed time and independent usability outcomes have
not been measured.

# OtpInput

CUI implements the frozen 0.7.1 numeric OTP interaction and grouped presentation
with portable application-owned state. `cui_otp_init` borrows a valid
NUL-terminated buffer and a target of at most 256 cells. There is no per-frame
allocation. The buffer remains valid while state is used; only the OTP API should
mutate it. `cui_otp_set_value` validates UTF-8/capacity transactionally and preserves
arbitrary or overlength programmatic values, matching the upstream compatibility
contract. It does not emit user editing notifications; invalidate your context
after programmatic changes.

`cui_base_otp` submits a single accessible textbox and reduces actual routed
pointer/keyboard input without theme painting. ASCII digit and fullwidth digit
text events append one normalized digit. Other text and arrow/delete keys are
ignored. Each text event uses its first scalar, matching the reference's per-key
editor; bulk clipboard paste is not an OTP feature. Backspace removes the final
UTF-8 scalar, including arbitrary programmatic values. Typing stops at the target
length; storage exhaustion reports capacity without losing the prior value.
Disabled state suppresses editing and focus presentation.

The result distinguishes `changed`, `complete`, `focused`, and `blurred`, with
counts for accepted editing/completion events within one frame. This follows the
frozen source's `OtpEvent::Change` and `OtpEvent::Complete` distinction rather than
the website's older completion-only summary. Backspace is an accepted edit even
on an empty value, as in the source. Programmatic updates do not set these flags.
`cui_otp_value` and `cui_otp_count` expose the current borrowed text/scalar count.

`cui_otp_options_default()` requests two visual groups. Explicit zero clamps to
one, excessive group counts clamp to the target length, and an empty target uses
one empty group. Groups contain ceiling(target/groups) cells, with remaining
cells in later groups. Options select extra-small/small (24), medium (32), large
(44), or a custom cell size; custom pixel sizes default text to half that size.
Default within-group gap is four pixels and between-group gap is twenty. Masking
replaces every displayed scalar with `*`; draw commands and semantics do not
include the raw masked value. The focused cell is the next empty cell, or the
last cell for a full code. Focus-ring suppression is explicit.

Pass host monotonic `now_seconds` for cursor blink; the interval defaults to half
a second. Retained blink phase resets on focus and accepted editing. The result's
`next_wake_seconds` supplies an absolute deadline while an empty focused cell has
a visible caret. Schedule a host frame at that deadline. Visibility changes
invalidate the context, while unchanged frames stay idle. Filled/disabled inputs
do not request a caret wake. Window activation and native scheduling belong to
the host; this API does not pretend to provide an OS timer or IME bridge.

The styled `cui_otp` renders the same base state with theme colors, rounded square
cells, grouped gaps, focus border, and caret. The headless test links core, edit
(for shared UTF-8 validation), and OTP base only. Styled linkage adds OTP component
and a supplied theme; no separate input reducer is used.

Tests cover real pointer focus, ordered text/key events, ASCII/fullwidth digits,
rejection and target bounds, UTF-8 Backspace, completion/change/focus/blur counts,
programmatic arbitrary values, storage errors, disabled input, host-clock blink,
group clamping, all four themes/densities, exact cell/group geometry, and masking
without raw-value draw commands. Native accessibility bridge coverage remains
that of core, and OS OTP autofill is not implemented.

# OTP CHANGE observation

Include `cui/cui_otp_events.h`. `cui_base_otp_events` and `cui_otp_events` add a
synchronous `{change, user}` observer to the existing Base/Styled signatures.
Their result contains the unchanged legacy `control` plus actual callback
`change_count`, zero or one. A missing callback ignores user and reduces normally.

```c
static void changed(void *user, const cui_otp_change_event *event) {
    size_t *accepted = user; /* Separate application state. */
    *accepted += event->accepted_count;
}
/* Within the normal active frame: */
/* cui_otp_events(ui, id, theme, &state, options,
 *     (cui_otp_event_handler){changed, &accepted_operations}); */
```

CHANGE means accepted operations in this submission, including empty Backspace
and changes that return to the entry text. It does not mean final text inequality.
The payload snapshots entry/final UTF-8 byte and code-point counts, target cell
length, accepted-operation and completion counts, and final completeness.
`completion_count` is the old per-operation length-match count: it can exceed one,
include deletion from overlength to target or empty Backspace at target zero,
and coexist with a finally incomplete value. No SUBMIT, verification, validity,
per-event completion callback or input-origin claim is added. Enter is unchanged.
Programmatic setters alone do not cause these notifications.

Observers run after the single real Base reduction and final semantics, before
Styled paint. Earlier accepted changes still notify if later operations report
capacity/session errors; the original error remains in `control`. Disabled,
inert and layout-only calls retain old bookkeeping/reduction without notifying.
Metadata is CHANGE at the root ID, UNKNOWN source, with only HAS_FRAME for the
active completion frame. Counts do not establish an event index or activation.

Text is final committed model bytes, borrowed only through the callback when
`has_text=true`. Masked state sets `has_text=false` and empty `text`, and never
exposes preedit. Scalar length information is retained; masking is not encryption
or length secrecy. Do not log codes/preedit or automatically persist/forward them.
Copying the event struct does not retain its text. To retain unmasked text, call
`cui_component_event_copy_utf8` inside the callback into caller-owned storage,
with an explicit maximum and capacity including NUL; check its status. Copy
failure does not reject the edit. No silent truncation or allocation is added.
The target is capped at 256 cells, but programmatic UTF-8 text can be arbitrarily
long within the supplied buffer; there is no implied 256-byte text bound.

Handler/user are borrowed only for this call; no registration/replay occurs.
Do not mutate/rebind/destroy the model, state, composition/session, context or
borrowed buffers; recursively submit; or unwind foreign exceptions during the
callback. Changing unrelated application state or setting a deferred-work flag
is allowed. Defer model changes, removal and teardown until outer submission
and renderer consumption complete: drawing may borrow model/preedit bytes.

Tests use actual queued text, keys and composition events, with paired legacy/new
semantics, focus, text-input rectangles, draw commands and consumption checks.
They cover accepted no-ops, net-zero changes, target zero, overlength deletion,
multiple completions/final incomplete text, stale duplicate commit, redaction,
explicit copies, passive/disabled behavior, bounded invalid buffers, and accepted
progress followed by errors. Native execution uses the private-display wrapper.
The old APIs, bridge LEGACY notifications and Python/Node/Go/Rust wrappers remain
unchanged; this slice adds no typed binding completion transport.

# Overlay behavior and focus scopes

`cui_overlay.h` provides persistent application-owned open/dismiss state. It
uses core focus scopes; it does not implement an independent hit-test or focus
traversal system. The panel's layout and appearance remain application-owned.

Initialize a stable scope ID with `cui_overlay_init`, then open it with
`cui_overlay_open`. Supply an explicit trigger ID, or zero to remember current
focus. After each `cui_begin_frame`, call `cui_overlay_update` before submitting
controls, processing nested overlays innermost first. If `cui_overlay_begin`
returns true, submit the panel and its controls, then call `cui_overlay_end`.
After layout, save the panel's resolved bounds with `cui_overlay_set_bounds`.
Outside dismissal arms only after bounds are supplied for the current opening,
so opening a popup cannot dismiss against stale or absent panel geometry.
The existing `cui_popup_place` model can determine an overlay's desired bounds;
absolute positioning/portals are not currently supplied by this module.

A modal scope confines forward and reverse Tab traversal to enabled descendants.
The core establishes initial focus inside a newly submitted modal. Nested modal
scopes trap to the innermost scope and restore focus to their remembered trigger
when dismissed. Pointer input outside a modal is blocked from underlying
controls and routed to the modal scope, allowing outside-click dismissal.
Nonmodal popups permit the underlying outside click to activate while dismissing.
Escape dismisses the top open scope. Dismissal policies are independently
configurable. Focus restoration validates that the trigger was enabled in the
previous completed frame; final submission validation also clears focus if the
trigger has since become disabled or disappeared.

Input is routed against the preceding completed frame and its scope ancestry.
Opening affects dispatch from the next frame. Dismissal consumes the routed
scope event; later queued events retain the routing established at frame begin.
There is no post-Tab focus repair. A scope supplies keyboard and pointer
isolation, but currently adds no platform accessibility modal relation,
semantic dialog role, scrim, z-order, animation, scroll lock, or native window.
These are reusable behavior primitives, not a complete styled Dialog.

`test_overlay` verifies nested scopes, initial focus, forward/reverse traversal,
disabled descendants, Escape, trigger restoration, disabled/removed triggers,
and modal versus nonmodal outside-click activation.
documents.docs/PACKAGING.md:
# Install local alpha binding artifacts

Current artifact examples use prepared alpha.2 versions (`0.1.0-alpha.3`, Python
`0.1.0a3`). Metadata preparation is not publication or a final source freeze;
see [RELEASING.md](RELEASING.md). Existing alpha.1 tags/assets stay immutable.


The packages expose the [tested binding subset](BRIDGE_COMPONENTS.md), not full
GPUI feature parity. Commands below build and consume local files; no registry
publication or public Go tag is assumed. npm is `private: true` and Cargo has
`publish = false`. Linux x86_64 is validated; registry ownership, public release
versions, other platforms and native runtime bundling remain release work.

Run artifact build commands from the CUI repository root. The artifact producer scripts require Python 3, CMake
3.20+, a C11 compiler and build tools. Node builds also require Node >=18 and
Node-API headers; Go requires Go 1.23+ with cgo, and Rust requires Cargo/Rust.
Builds default to Release with strict warnings. Use
`CUI_PACKAGE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug` explicitly for diagnostic builds.

**Portable is the default:** an App computes layout and processes input but
opens no window. Build with `CUI_PACKAGE_NATIVE=1`, then select the SDL backend
in the application for a native window. Keep portable and native artifacts in
separate output directories; their versions and filenames currently coincide.
Native builds need SDL3 >=3.2, FreeType and HarfBuzz development packages.

## Python: wheel, virtualenv and native counter

```sh
CUI_PACKAGE_NATIVE=1 python scripts/package_bindings.py python --output /tmp/cui-python-native
python -m venv /tmp/cui-python-consumer
/tmp/cui-python-consumer/bin/python -m pip install --no-deps /tmp/cui-python-native/*.whl
```

Save this as `/tmp/cui-python-consumer/counter.py`. It creates a real native UI;
the callback updates mounted label state. Closing the window ends `app.run()`.

```python
import os
from cui_bridge import App, button, column, label

count = 0
status = label("Clicks: 0")
def increment(event):
    global count
    count += 1
    status.label(f"Clicks: {count}")

click = button("increment").label("Click me").on_click(increment)
with App(backend="sdl", title="CUI Counter", font_path=os.environ["CUI_FONT"]) as app:
    app.mount(column().children(status, click))
    if os.environ.get("CUI_EXAMPLE_SMOKE") == "1":
        app.step()
        x, y, w, h = app.bounds(click)
        app.queue_pointer("down", x + w / 2, y + h / 2)
        app.queue_pointer("up", x + w / 2, y + h / 2)
        app.step()
        app.dispatch()
        assert count == 1
        app.step()
    else:
        app.run()
```

Choose an existing font covering your application's text, then run:

```sh
CUI_FONT=/path/to/font.ttf /tmp/cui-python-consumer/bin/python /tmp/cui-python-consumer/counter.py
```

For portable layout/input only, omit `CUI_PACKAGE_NATIVE=1` when building and
use `App()` instead of the SDL options. The platform wheel includes its compiled
bridge, source roots, pinned dependency manifest and licenses. It is not a pure
Python wheel or a manylinux claim. No checkout/PYTHONPATH or separate library path
is needed. Explicit `library=` and `CUI_BRIDGE_LIBRARY` overrides retain precedence;
a broken override fails rather than hiding the error with a default library.

## JavaScript: prebuilt tarball and native counter

```sh
CUI_PACKAGE_NATIVE=1 python scripts/package_bindings.py node --prebuilt --output /tmp/cui-node-native
mkdir -p /tmp/cui-node-consumer
cd /tmp/cui-node-consumer
npm init -y
CUI_PACKAGE_NATIVE=1 npm install /tmp/cui-node-native/cui-native-0.1.0-alpha.3.tgz
```

Save this as `/tmp/cui-node-consumer/counter.cjs`:

```javascript
const {App, button, column, label} = require('@cui/native');
let count = 0;
const status = label('Clicks: 0');
const click = button('increment').label('Click me').on_click(() => {
  status.label(`Clicks: ${++count}`);
});
const app = new App({backend: 'sdl', title: 'CUI Counter', fontPath: process.env.CUI_FONT});
app.mount(column().children(status, click));
if (process.env.CUI_EXAMPLE_SMOKE === '1') {
  app.step();
  const {x, y, width, height} = click.bounds();
  app.pointer('down', x + width / 2, y + height / 2);
  app.pointer('up', x + width / 2, y + height / 2);
  app.step();
  if (count !== 1) throw new Error('counter callback failed');
  app.step();
  app.dispose();
} else {
  app.start();
}
```

```sh
CUI_FONT=/path/to/font.ttf node /tmp/cui-node-consumer/counter.cjs
```

For portable behavior build without `CUI_PACKAGE_NATIVE=1` and use `new App()`.
`--prebuilt` carries a hashed Node-API 8 addon and bridge; the consumer needs
Node >=18 and system runtime libraries, without Python or a C compiler. Omit `--prebuilt` for a source tarball whose
install hook requires Python 3, CMake, a C11 compiler, build tools and Node headers. Install scripts must be enabled.
`CUI_PACKAGE_BUILD_FROM_SOURCE=1` explicitly rebuilds bundled source. TypeScript
declarations are inside the package and validated using strict TypeScript 5.8.3.
`CUI_NODE_ADDON` remains an explicit override; missing installed binaries fail
without a checkout fallback.

## Go: local module proxy and executable

Build a portable artifact at the repository root:

```sh
python scripts/package_bindings.py go --output /tmp/cui-go-artifacts
mkdir -p /tmp/cui-go-consumer
cp tests/packaging/go_smoke.go /tmp/cui-go-consumer/main.go
cd /tmp/cui-go-consumer
go mod init example.local/cui-counter
go mod edit -require=github.com/mattmezza/cui/bindings/go@v0.1.0-alpha.3
GOPROXY=file:///tmp/cui-go-artifacts GOSUMDB=off go mod tidy
GOPROXY=file:///tmp/cui-go-artifacts GOSUMDB=off go build -o counter .
./counter
```

This example renders a portable frame, sends a click and asserts the callback.
The canonical module path describes this repository; these commands use a local
proxy ZIP, not an unpublished registry/tag. The default artifact includes a tracked source SDK and separate C translation
units. cgo compiles and statically links CUI at `go build`; the executable needs
no checkout, CMake, compiler or extracted CUI library cache at runtime. Native
system libraries remain required.

To validate native rendering, build the consumer with `go build -tags cui_native`.
This build requires SDL3 >=3.2, FreeType and HarfBuzz development packages through
pkg-config. Run the smoke example with
`CUI_PACKAGE_SMOKE_BACKEND=sdl CUI_PACKAGE_SMOKE_FONT=/path/to/font.ttf`.
For an interactive application, see the [Go workspace UI](GO_BUILDERS.md).
The portable default opens no window and reports a clear error if native options
are requested without the native build tag.

`--source-only` remains an alias for the default source module. For optional
embedded shared-library packaging, use `--prebuilt` and build the consumer with
`-tags cui_dynamic`. That mode extracts its hashed bridge into a locked, atomic
private cache, validating SDK/backend/ABI/OS/architecture receipts. Dynamic source
fallback exists only under this explicit tag; it may require a runtime compiler
if the artifact has no prebuilt library. Explicit `Library` and
`CUI_BRIDGE_LIBRARY` overrides retain precedence in both modes. A process keeps
one selected bridge, so switching between static and dynamic paths requires a
new process.

Go resolves this public repository directly; it needs no Go registry account.
A repository commit or `@main` becomes fetchable when those files are published.
The versioned `v0.1.0-alpha.3` tag used above remains a local artifact version;
no command here assumes that public tag has been created.

## Rust: local crate and statically linked executable

At the repository root:

```sh
python scripts/package_bindings.py rust --output /tmp/cui-rust-artifacts
mkdir -p /tmp/cui-rust-consumer/vendor
cp tests/packaging/rust_smoke.rs /tmp/cui-rust-main.rs
tar -xzf /tmp/cui-rust-artifacts/cui-builders-0.1.0-alpha.3.crate -C /tmp/cui-rust-consumer/vendor
cd /tmp/cui-rust-consumer
cargo init --name cui-counter
cp /tmp/cui-rust-main.rs src/main.rs
cat >> Cargo.toml <<'TOML'
cui-builders = { path = "vendor/cui-builders-0.1.0-alpha.3" }
TOML
cargo build --offline
./target/debug/cui-counter
```

Cargo compiles the bundled SDK and statically links CUI during the developer build.
The copied executable needs no CUI checkout, CMake or compiler at runtime.
The example asserts portable geometry and a callback. For native rendering,
add `features = ["native"]` to the dependency entry, then run it with
`CUI_PACKAGE_SMOKE_BACKEND=sdl CUI_PACKAGE_SMOKE_FONT=/path/to/font.ttf`.
Native system libraries are still dynamically required. The existing
`CUI_BRIDGE_LIB_DIR` shared-library override remains available. See the
[Rust workspace UI](RUST_BUILDERS.md) for a complete interactive application.

## Headless checks and runtime requirements

Automated native checks must use a dedicated invisible Xvfb session, never the
maintainer desktop. These runners create it automatically:

```sh
python scripts/test_binding_packages.py --artifacts /tmp/cui-native-artifacts --native --require-prebuilt --font /path/to/font.ttf
python scripts/test_compiled_binding_packages.py --go-artifacts /tmp/cui-go-native --rust-artifacts /tmp/cui-rust-artifacts --native --font /path/to/font.ttf
```

The first directory must contain both the native wheel and prebuilt npm tarball;
build both there using the earlier commands. The Go directory must contain a
native Go artifact. Rust's consumer selects its native feature. For the standalone
counter examples, `CUI_EXAMPLE_SMOKE=1` sends and checks a synthetic click and
exits; wrap their invocation in `xvfb-run -a env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY`.

The installed artifact tests use clean temporary consumers without checkout or
library-path overrides, exercise real frames/callbacks, and block compiler tools
at runtime. Python native validation also checks captured Button pixels.
The text smoke includes `✓`; fonts must cover submitted text. This host validates
`/usr/share/fonts/Adwaita/AdwaitaMono-Regular.ttf`; plain NotoSans lacks that glyph
here. Missing glyph errors remain visible. Full workspace examples and supported
options are in [Python/JavaScript/TypeScript builders](BINDING_BUILDERS.md),
[Go builders](GO_BUILDERS.md), and [Rust builders](RUST_BUILDERS.md).

SDL builds require system SDL3 >=3.2, FreeType, HarfBuzz and their development
headers/pkg-config metadata. These system libraries are **not bundled or pinned**
by this alpha packaging. Their transitive runtime libraries and an explicit font
must exist on the target host. Therefore SDL artifacts are source-complete but
are not self-contained native runtime distributions. `_native/build-info.json`
(Python) and `native/build-info.json` (npm) record the actual built shared-library
runtime dependency names, development versions and source revision. Source
file hashes are recorded in `SOURCE_FILES.sha256`, alongside the pinned
third-party manifest and license texts. Portable builds need the host's
standard C/math runtime; native builds add the precise dependencies in that file.
Linux x86_64 is locally validated. macOS/Windows, manylinux repair, dependency
runtime bundling, cross compilation and registry publication remain unvalidated.

C/CMake warnings stay enabled and errors remain fatal. Artifact builders default
to Release; `CUI_PACKAGE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug` explicitly selects a diagnostic build.
Vendored source versions/licenses remain in `third_party/dependencies.json`.
The configured SDL fetch pin remains in the bundled source, but packaging does
not enable network fetching or silently replace system development dependencies.


## Source receipts and release work

Artifacts include tracked source only, file hashes, pinned dependency manifests
and license texts. The npm source snapshot intentionally omits `.gitignore` files
before hashing because `npm pack` excludes them; these files do not participate
in consumer builds. Python retains these canonical tracked files. The installed
package validator verifies every source manifest hash against actual archive
contents and rejects missing, changed, unlisted or unsafe source entries before
installation. The source file inventory excludes its own `SOURCE_FILES.sha256`
and `bindings/go/sdk/source/SOURCE_FILES.sha256` and
`bindings/rust/sdk/source/SOURCE_FILES.sha256` from recursive hashing, matching
the producer; all other archived source files must be listed. Use
`python scripts/test_binding_packages.py --artifacts DIR --verify-only` to run
only these offline archive checks, without installing packages, building code or
opening a display. Revision receipts include dirty-source information so a
revision is not mistaken for an exact clean snapshot. Go and Rust use minimal
SDK snapshots: after canonical changes run `python scripts/generate_go_sdk.py`,
then `python scripts/generate_go_sdk.py --check` to validate freshness/provenance.
No packaging command publishes. Public tag/registry release, Linux runtime
bundling, manylinux compatibility and cross-platform binaries are pending.

Authoritative packaging references: [Python packaging flow](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/flow/),
[npm pack](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/commands/npm-pack/),
[npm lifecycle scripts](https://docs.npmjs.com/misc/scripts/),
[Cargo native build scripts](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-scripts.html),
[Go module ZIP rules](https://go.dev/ref/mod#zip-files), and
[Go embedded files](https://pkg.go.dev/embed).

# Password engine prerequisite, Stage 1

This batch adds pure U+2022 scalar masking/offset helpers and hard presentation
preparation to `cui_edit_apply_checked`. It supplies no password Input widget,
secure semantics, clipboard policy, browser/native secure bridge or reveal UI.
Those remain coordinated Stage 2 work. The source mask character/scalar behavior
comes from GPUI Kit `87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`,
[masked display](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-kit/blob/87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34/crates/base/src/input/base/element.rs#L2548).

`cui_edit_mask_text` emits three UTF-8 bytes per Unicode scalar, including combining
marks and each scalar of a ZWJ/flag sequence. It is not grapheme counting. Capacity
includes NUL; whole-source UTF8, checked scalar multiplication and known
source/destination/output aliases precede writes. Failure preserves destination
and output. Mask/unmask offset helpers require original scalar boundaries or
three-byte bullet boundaries; outputs are atomic and disjoint from the source.
Storage remains caller-owned, and helper outputs borrow caller bytes. Ordinary
edit movement/grapheme rules are unchanged by these pure mappings.

A checked request may provide `cui_edit_presentation`: synchronous `prepare`, user
pointer/exact byte extent, optional descriptor extent and zero to three exact
caller workspaces. All declared spans must be accurately sized, disjoint from
each other/model/session/original request payload. Unused array entries are zero;
non-NULL user requires nonzero extent. Invalid configuration is rejected before
callback. Allocated/private callback resources are caller-owned too, but need no
span declaration when freshly allocated disjoint storage; they must never alias
model storage. Direct caller-buffer mutation, undeclared aliases, retained candidate
pointers, external side effects and cross-thread access violate the borrowing
contract and cannot be globally protected in C.

Preparation receives complete real candidate text (after opt-in normalization),
not bullets. It returns only OK, CAPACITY or appended PRESENTATION; other codes
become INVALID_ARGUMENT. Use CAPACITY for allocator/fixed-budget failure and
PRESENTATION for an installed geometry factory failing to create a representation.
No factory or frontend allocator is called by the engine itself. The callback is
responsible for cleaning partial resources before returning a failure. Same-model
mutators/void destroy/cache-writing getters are guarded; attempted mutation causes
INVALID_ARGUMENT and preserves logical state. Pure getters remain available.

The gate runs before acceptance predicates and model mutation. Resource failure
is `rejected=false` and does not invoke acceptance or invalid-old healing.
Successful preparation is followed by the original candidate predicate, and by
the previous-value predicate only when candidate fails. Empty acceptance bypass
remains; hard preparation still applies to an actual edit resulting in empty text.
An unchanged no-op range has no candidate/stage. No callback replay occurs during
commit. Zero presentation preserves the legacy path; hard presentation currently
rejects multiline models explicitly, while ordinary multiline APIs stay unchanged.

Replacement prepares its normalized full candidate before cursor/history/document
writes. IME UPDATE prepares the full prospective composed value, and COMMIT
prepares once before document commit, with original UTF8 endpoint validation and
normalization mapping unchanged. Failed preparation restores reused prior view
bytes and frees only unbound engine grow storage. Preedit/document/session remain
unchanged. With NULL preparation, START retains its legacy bypass. With opt-in
preparation, START now stages the exact prefix/suffix view around an empty preedit
before mutating the session. Failed preparation preserves the prior session and
selection. CANCEL publishes the retained committed view without another allocation.
The styled Input lifecycle is described in [Password Input](PASSWORD_INPUT_STAGE2.md).
Undo/Redo prepare the target recorded full value before saving history state or
changing index/selection. They bypass acceptance/normalization as before. A hard
budget may block replay with CAPACITY without discarding its history entry.

Returned `presentation_prepared` means prepare returned OK, even if a later
predicate/reentry failure rejected the operation. `presentation_applied` means the
checked operation adopted that candidate. Consume/publish or discard caller staging
before another request. No completion callback runs inside the engine; publication,
cache release and other frontend effects lie outside engine rollback. All borrowed
presentation fields are removed/restored when the checked call returns. Do not
promise unchanged external callback state or entire-allocation identity: rollback
preserves logical document/history/selection/coalescing/session ownership and prior
view defined bytes/NUL, while internal scratch and unused tails are unspecified.

`tests/unit/test_password_engine.c` covers independently enumerated scalar maps,
alias/capacity/output rollback, prepare→predicate ordering and invalid-old healing,
normalized candidate, unsupported callback codes, same-model destroy, fixed-budget
and injected preparation/allocator failures, exact replay/IME prepare counts,
typing grouping across failure, prior fixed/growing view ownership, three declared
workspaces/descriptor, and a rejected 4500-byte preedit requiring staged grow
allocation. Factory-failure coverage is a callback spy returning PRESENTATION,
not an actual native font/backend password validation. Frontend forced-factory
lifetime/pixel/secure-host tests remain Stage 2 requirements.

Integrator registers `test_password_engine` linked only to `cui`, including WASI,
and regenerates distribution. No global build files or generated headers were
modified by this worker.

# Single-line masked Input

This implements the pinned `87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`
Input password slice, together with the checked engine Stage 1. It does not
complete Input parity: regex, mask formatting, and other content types remain
separate. Multiline masking/password purpose and inline token content are
explicitly unsupported; invalid options return INVALID_ARGUMENT before reduction.
Ordinary multiline Input/Editor/Textarea host input remains available.

```c
cui_input_options options = {
    .masked = true,
    .content_type = CUI_TEXT_INPUT_PURPOSE_PASSWORD,
    .normalization = CUI_EDIT_NORMALIZE_SINGLE_LINE_CRLF,
};
cui_input_result result = cui_input_ex(ui, id, theme, label, edit, state, options);
```

Zero options preserve ordinary Input behavior. Masking and purpose are independent:
masked alone paints bullets and denies Copy/Cut, but keeps the Textbox accessibility
role. PASSWORD/NEW_PASSWORD purpose marks protected accessibility state even when
revealed. Reveal (`masked=false`) deliberately paints the actual value and allows
the established clipboard callback. Masked Copy/Cut are denied before calling that
callback; Paste still follows editability, normalization and acceptance. Word
motion/selection/delete uses whole-value endpoints while masked; double/triple
click selects all. Scalar/grapheme movement retains the existing engine policy.

The mask is one U+2022 per Unicode scalar, including combining marks, matching the
source. Selection, caret, pointer hit testing, horizontal scroll and IME underlines
map original UTF8 byte endpoints to/from three-byte bullet endpoints. The geometry
factory and text draw commands receive only bullet text in masked mode. Entering
masked mode releases previous plaintext geometry sessions and their text copies.
Painting failures never fall back to plaintext. Public placeholder/label strings
remain the application's responsibility; never put a secret in either.

## Hard resource staging

The styled control retains three display/geometry slots: safe committed value,
current visible preedit, and unused candidate stage. Its initial/current seed is
prepared with CUI_EDIT_REQUEST_PRESENT before reducing events. For replacement,
normalized IME UPDATE/COMMIT, Cut/delete and Undo/Redo, the engine prepares the
prospective whole value before document/history/selection writes and before the
acceptance predicate. Preparation failure invokes no predicate and leaves logical
model/session state unchanged. Acceptance rejection discards the prepared stage;
it does not publish it or replay the predicate. Empty values still require a safe
empty presentation. Undo/Redo prepares its historical target without predicate or
normalization replay.

Default slots lazily grow to actual mask bytes plus NUL, bounded by the model's
caller-chosen document capacity. Three display slots, geometry copies and host
sessions remain owned by the UI resource. Idle frames reuse them. After changing a font registry or measurement policy,
call `cui_text_metrics_changed(ui)` outside the frame to invalidate retained
geometry; ordinary control size changes also trigger preparation. An optional
`cui_input_mask_allocator` controls display-buffer allocation only; geometry text
copies and factory sessions keep their existing ownership. Both callbacks must be
present or absent; successful allocation must return fresh disjoint storage. Its
user/callbacks must remain alive until context destruction/resource collection.

For allocation-free display storage, supply `cui_input_mask_storage` with three
disjoint buffers and their capacities including NUL. The smallest capacity is the
hard per-candidate budget. Buffers and their descriptor remain caller-owned and
must stay unchanged/alive through resource release. Accurate descriptor/workspace
extents are declared to the checked engine; known model/session/payload/workspace
aliases reject before preparation. Rebinding these resources drops their previous
owned sessions. Cancel composition and reset the Input state before destroying/replacing
its model; the reset state forces initial resource preparation even if an allocator
reuses the same model address. Reset the host proxy when replacing its bound model; a retained session's numeric model binding must never be reused across
model lifetimes. IME retains the existing one-primary-selection constraint; no
multi-cursor IME support is claimed. Retained resource callbacks never dereference a destroyed model.

If the optional visual factory exists, it must successfully prepare immutable
bullet geometry; failure returns PRESENTATION before committing the edit. Without
one, measured bullet geometry is the legacy fallback. Factory limits remain host
limits. There is no secret-safe rollback promise for direct application writes to
model buffers or raw engine edits outside this checked control. Completion is
caller-owned and outside engine rollback. Base exposes presentation/prepared/applied
completion so a custom frontend can implement the same three-slot publication;
Base alone does not paint a mask for it.

Engine PRESENT is nonmutating and ignores editability. NULL/inactive composition
prepares committed text; an inactive previously-bound session must belong to this
model. Active composition must have a valid materialized composed view, matching
model revision/selection/binding and disjoint buffers; stale views reject before
callbacks. No predicate, normalization, session start/cancel, history or selection
mutation occurs. Successful preparation reports prepared/applied=true even though
the logical value stays unchanged. Known same-model mutation during preparation
fails the outer request. Caller buffer writes and unrelated callback side effects
remain outside that guard.

With a hard presentation callback, START prepares its prospective empty-preedit
view (the current selected range is replaced by empty text) before mutating the
session or coalescing state. It invokes no acceptance/normalization and requires
an empty START payload. Null presentation preserves the old START bypass exactly.
Failure preserves the prior session and safe committed view; success publishes
matching prefix/suffix bullets immediately. CANCEL needs no allocation because the
committed slot remains intact.
UPDATE rejection preserves prior visible preedit. A rejected or resource-failed host COMMIT first
preserves engine logical state, then Base cancels the session because the host IME
has ended. Mode/purpose changes, readonly/disabled and focus loss cancel composition.
Following typing/shortcuts remain available. Ordinary zero configuration is unchanged.

## Finalized host configuration

Core owns portable type/purpose enums, `cui_set_text_input_config` and
`cui_get_text_input_config`. Register against an already-submitted textbox during
the frame. The getter is available only after end_frame and validates the actual
eligible focused owner, current modal scope, readonly/disabled and no-focus state.
Failure leaves output unchanged. It borrows no strings/models/platform pointers.
Missing explicit registration yields ordinary TEXT/UNSPECIFIED for eligible
textboxes, including existing Editor/Textarea/Numeric/OTP and text children.
Finalized `multiline` selects ordinary textarea behavior. Explicit secure types or
purposes reject multiline atomically. Generation changes on owner/config/explicit
versus implicit/multiline/removal transitions; UINT64_MAX exhaustion fails closed
until context recreation. Host reset must discard old proxy/preedit when it changes.
An application replacing its Core context must explicitly reset/dispose the bridge.

SDL poll consumes the finalized state, stops input for absent/ineligible focus and
restarts on generation changes, cancelling the old tracked IME session and dropping
text/editing events already queued for that superseded host configuration. It uses
SDL_StartTextInputWithProperties, TEXT_PASSWORD_HIDDEN/VISIBLE and disabled
AUTOCORRECT for secure purposes, plus MULTILINE for ordinary multiline text. These
are verified against repository SDL pin
[`7f3ae3d57459e59943a4ecfefc8f6277ec6bf540` keyboard header](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/blob/7f3ae3d57459e59943a4ecfefc8f6277ec6bf540/include/SDL3/SDL_keyboard.h).
They exist since SDL3.2; SDL explicitly does not promise every input type on every
platform. NEW_PASSWORD cannot be distinguished from PASSWORD through this SDL
keyboard type. Physical OS keyboard suggestions/IME privacy are not proven by
injected events or Xvfb. SDL's global queue is not a per-window multicast service.

The optional AccessKit bridge maps password purpose to PASSWORD_INPUT and observes
secret/protected changes. It remains phase 1: no editable text/value support or
full screen-reader claim. CUI semantic value is zero for secret Inputs.

## Browser module and proof

`web/secure_input.js` is a reusable ES module. Pass parent, UTF8 `text`,
`composition(kind, bytes, anchorByte, cursorByte, owner)`, `key(event,owner)`,
`focusLost(owner)` and `changed()` callbacks. Call `sync` after finalized Core frames
with `{owner,type,purpose,generation,multiline,label}` and logical caret rectangle.
Use opaque stable owner/generation values without lossy conversions. The module
never seeds the committed value into DOM. Hidden passwords use a password input,
revealed passwords use text input, and ordinary multiline uses textarea. Purpose
selects current-password/new-password autocomplete. It disables spelling/correction,
converts DOM UTF16 scalar endpoints to UTF8, suppresses the composition-end duplicate
input, and clears transient value/preedit on blur, generation rebind/reset/dispose.
Composing shortcuts yield to the browser IME. Native DOM selection represents the
range the browser exposes; no claim of every platform's internal IME clause range.
The module provides no async clipboard implementation or cross-platform virtual
keyboard guarantee. The website Input preview exposes hidden, revealed, and new-password modes through this bridge. Its finalized owner and generation preserve all 64 bits across the WASM host boundary.

The standalone fixture uses actual CUI Core/styled Input compiled to WASM, with
real Chromium CDP imeSetComposition/insertText and actual canvas font measurement
and painting of Core draw commands. It checks identical pixels for distinct
equal-scalar-count passwords, selected Unicode START prefix/suffix, bullet draws,
unchanged preedit document, exactly-once commit/Undo, fixed-capacity host rejection
followed by ordinary typing, cancel, reveal/purpose, readonly, blur, and
generation-switched input/textarea. Run:

```sh
uv run tests/web/test_secure_input.py --output build/secure-proof --chromium /path/to/chrome
```

Headless tests: test_password_present, test_password_start, test_password_input, test_secure_focus,
test_secure_focus_generation and optional test_password_accessibility. Native font
proof: test_password_native (actual NotoSans bullets, plaintext cache teardown,
factory failure before writes); SDL proof: test_password_sdl3 (real SDL property
calls and queued Unicode editing/commit, Xvfb). These tests are registered in CMake; portable tests also run under WASI. Generated distribution headers include these APIs.

# Measured performance

Development host: Intel Core Ultra 5 235U (14 logical CPUs), Arch Linux x86_64 kernel7.2.8, GCC16.2.1, default unoptimized CMake build. `./build/cui_bench`:500 frames composing100 boxes+text at800×600, Clay culls outside viewport;28000 visible draw commands total. CPU `clock()` measurement:98.079ms total /0.196ms per composed frame in the initial run. This is CPU layout/draw-list generation, not end-to-end GPU frame time, and excludes renderer/text shaping and OS scheduling. Reproduce with `make bench`; numbers are not a comparison to other frameworks.

SDL_Renderer has bounded persistent glyph textures (256 LRU entries,4MiB coverage budget), text tint reuse tested. SDL_GPU has a1024×1024 grayscale atlas with4096 cached masks and32768 per-frame quad entries; uploads only after newly cached glyph masks. Atlas exhaustion returns failure instead of claiming successful output. GPU batching/regression thresholds and workload-specific measurement remain pending.

# Date and time pickers

`cui_picker.h` provides Calendar, DatePicker, TimeField and ColorPicker. Core date/time structures and base reducers contain no platform, theme or Clay dependencies. Styled wrappers use common box/text/portal commands and cached SVG icons. Selected dates/times and retained navigation state are application-owned.

Calendar renders one to three actual month grids, with configurable first weekday, selected date/range, minimum/maximum endpoints, disabled predicate and whole-widget disabled state. The grid model exposes 42 consecutive cells including neighboring dates and zero cells at Gregorian year boundaries. The legacy styled view leaves neighboring cells blank; opt-in presentation renders distinct selectable occurrences as described below. Canonical date IDs remain stable across navigation/reordering. Each day has a full ISO date semantic name by default, or numeric locale-formatted full date when a locale is supplied, disabled/selected details, and a roving Tab stop. The model supports years 1 through 9999. An invalid initial date defaults deterministically to 2000-01-01; applications provide their own current date.

Month/year buttons navigate by one/twelve months. Arrow keys move one day or one week, Home/End move to weekday-aligned row boundaries, and Control/Meta with arrows moves months/years. Disabled candidates are skipped with a bounded 366-attempt search. Navigation changes the displayed month when the cursor leaves the visible months. Enter/Space or a day pointer click selects the cursor/date. Range mode takes two activations, sorts reverse selections, and keeps a pending endpoint between frames; disabled predicates constrain endpoints, not every interior date. Navigation never implicitly changes selection. Styled cell size defaults to 32 logical pixels and is bounded to 20..128 pixels. Seven builtin locale tables and custom borrowed labels/order/separator are available through cui_date_locale. Arbitrary month counts and arbitrary source item styling remain unsupported; frozen Calendar does not implement week-number columns, hover-range previews or a dedicated arrow-key map.

The additive `cui_calendar_presentation.h` API enables independent month headers, a host-supplied today marker and selectable neighboring-day occurrences through `cui_calendar_ex`. Zero presentation options preserve legacy behavior. Use matching rebuilt headers/library, keep the canonical day ID for in-month cells and query neighboring occurrence IDs with `cui_calendar_cell_resolve`. DatePicker and typed CHANGE wrappers remain separate from these extensions. See [Calendar presentation](CALENDAR_PRESENTATION.md) for input ordering, policy checks, focus, borrowed lifetimes and explicit CUI range/recentering differences from frozen source. New presentation behavior is headless-tested; no browser or language-builder coverage is implied.

The base Calendar offers reduction and semantic submission separately, plus a combined convenience function. DatePicker uses this separation to close a selected popup before submitting its modal scope. Closing on selection, Escape, outside click or disabling restores a valid trigger focus; this avoids leaving a closed modal scope in the activation frame. It uses the same `cui_overlay` focus/dismissal state and `cui_popup_place` collision model as choice popups. Its actual calendar renders as a viewport portal beyond ancestor clips, flips/clamps to the supplied viewport, and confines Tab focus while open. Range pickers close only after the second endpoint. Trigger semantics report expanded/controls. Calendar day and weekday labels are centered in their cells; month/year navigation uses SVG chevrons and retains accessible navigation names. DatePicker shares this renderer and uses a centered trigger with a calendar SVG. The current appearance uses ISO labels, a selectable calendar, and placeholder text; editable date masks, clear controls, custom locale/date formats and preset ranges remain pending. Small viewports clip a calendar rather than resize or scroll it.

TimeField stores a valid 24-hour `cui_time` and displays segmented hours/minutes, optional seconds and optional AM/PM. Each segment has a name, numeric value/range and readonly/parent details; one active segment participates in Tab navigation. Left/Right changes segments, Up/Down wraps the active unit, Home/End selects its limits, and digit input advances after two digits. Two-digit drafts persist across frames. AM/PM accepts A/P or keyboard toggling. Twelve-hour display preserves the 24-hour model. Disabled/readonly suppress mutations. Strict standalone parse/format functions accept/emit ASCII `HH:MM[:SS]` and reject out-of-range units. Custom min/max times, typed separators, full-width normalization, configurable formats and native input/IME integration remain pending.

Meaningful tests exercise leap years and weekday grids over forty years, minimum/maximum/disabled dates, actual routed multiple-arrow navigation, weekend skipping, year controls, reverse range selection, all four themes, persistent segmented digits, hour/minute rollover, 12-hour periods and disabled/readonly behavior. DatePicker tests cover actual portal geometry outside a clipped parent, selection close with trigger focus restored in the same frame, seventeen trapped Tab events, Escape and outside dismissal. The same Calendar/TimeField event suite compiles with `CUI_PICKER_BASE_ONLY`, no theme/components linkage, and bare geometry; base drawing remains empty. Strict warnings, fully instrumented ASan/UBSan, and existing CTest pass before submission. Root owns build/distribution registration.

ColorPicker includes a retained HSV model controlled by application RGBA bytes, a two-dimensional saturation/brightness surface, hue and alpha controls, numeric RGBA channel sliders and up to 64 palette swatches. Arrow/Home/End keys adjust named channel semantics. Pointer capture survives separate down/move/up frames and is cancelled explicitly. Readonly/disabled suppress changes. HSV conversion handles negative/wrapped hues and sanitizes nonfinite components; strict `#RRGGBB[AA]` parsing and formatting are allocation-free. A 12×8 common-rectangle grid approximates the SV gradient and shows a selected-cell outline; hue uses 24 bands and alpha uses 16 bands. Channels display their numeric values and horizontal ranges. Palette clicks and external replacements synchronize HSV; achromatic channel edits preserve hue. The current widget lacks editable hex/channel text, exact continuous shader gradients, a native eyedropper and upstream popup presentation/options. It is an inline, real interactive color control rather than a claim of complete ColorPicker parity.

Color tests add 20,000 deterministic RGBA→HSV→RGBA and hex round trips, primary/wrapped-hue/nonfinite boundaries, channel/palette keyboard/pointer behavior, cross-frame captured SV release, readonly/disabled checks, semantic ranges, all themes and measured gradient geometry. The base-only flavor exercises the same color reducer without theme/components. Twelve-hour TimeField semantics expose the displayed 1..12 range; Home/End preserve AM/PM while choosing 1/12.

## Picking a screen color

The website's **Pick from screen** button uses the browser EyeDropper API. Select any screen pixel; Escape cancels without changing the controlled color. The chosen sRGB bytes replace RGB and preserve the current alpha. Unsupported browsers show an availability message. Navigation or disabling the component cancels an outstanding request. Screen access belongs to the host, so no browser or operating-system type enters CUI's public API.

Native hosts can open their platform picker from a button callback, then assign the returned color to their application-owned `cui_color` and schedule a frame:

```c
/* Run after your host picker completes successfully, on the UI thread. */
cui_color sampled;
if (cui_color_parse_hex(cui_string("#1A8F64"), &sampled)) {
    sampled.a = color.a; /* Optional: preserve the existing opacity. */
    color = sampled;
    cui_invalidate(ui);
}
/* The next cui_color_picker call synchronizes its retained HSV state. */
```

The browser requires a secure context and a user gesture; call `new EyeDropper().open()` directly in the click handler before awaiting anything or scheduling a C frame. A resolved `sRGBHex` can be parsed with `cui_color_parse_hex`; cancelled or rejected requests must leave the value unchanged. See the [Chrome EyeDropper guide](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/capabilities/web-apis/eyedropper) and [API specification](https://wicg.github.io/eyedropper-api/). CUI's native adapters currently do not implement an OS screen picker; applications provide that host capability.

Optional single-date time editing uses the separate `cui_date_time_picker.h` model and Base/Styled facade, not legacy DatePicker selection storage. See [DateTime picker](DATE_TIME_PICKER.md) for explicit sync, ordered day confirmation, draft preservation, presets/clear, popup-fit policy and binding/source-event limitations. No timezone or date-time range is supported.

# Picker applied observers

Include `cui/cui_picker_events.h` for additive applied date-selection observers:
`cui_calendar_reduce_events`, `cui_base_calendar_events`, and `cui_calendar_events`.
Each mirrors its legacy operation, appends `cui_date_selection_handler`, and returns
`cui_calendar_event_result` with the exact legacy `control` and `change_count`.

```c
static void selected_date(void *user, const cui_date_selection_change *event) {
    app_state *app = user;
    app->last_selection = event->value; /* Pointer-free copy. */
}
cui_calendar_event_result result = cui_calendar_events(
    ui, calendar_id, &theme, &calendar, &selection, options,
    (cui_date_selection_handler){selected_date, app});
```

This slice does not add TimeField, navigation, popup lifecycle or controlled-request
observers. A CHANGE reports an already-applied
date selection and cannot reject it. The existing disabled-date predicate remains
an enablement policy, not a notification or a newly rejectable transaction.

## Delivery and comparison

Each facade invokes its corresponding legacy operation **once** and compares
selected start/end at the outer return. Reduce-only does not submit semantics;
Base does; Styled completes painting before the observer. No nested observer or
reduction replay occurs. Custom popup hosts may use reduce-only and submit later,
preserving their own modal/close ordering. There is no submit-only observer.

At most one callback runs per operation. Multiple changes coalesce, and returning
to the initial selection produces no CHANGE. `change_count` counts actual callback
invocations; a missing handler still permits editing and yields zero count. Its
unused user pointer is ignored. Reading `control` never dispatches again.

Comparison uses `cui_date_compare` for each endpoint, exactly as the legacy
Calendar change calculation does. It compares date fields rather than struct bytes
or formatted strings. Zero/end-unset dates remain part of the legacy selection
representation; the facade adds no validity check, selection normalization or
range ownership rule. Range first selection starts/restarts the range, and range
completion can reorder endpoints. Same-date activation can set `control.activated`
without a CHANGE.

Displayed month, cursor movement, DAYS/YEARS/MONTHS chooser state, year page and
range-in-progress are distinct presentation state. Navigation may set the legacy
`navigated` flag without changing selected dates. Repairing invalid month/cursor
presentation also does not produce selection CHANGE. External assignments completed
before entry are not component-applied changes.

The copied payload contains previous/final `cui_date_selection`, CHANGE kind and
the calendar ID. Metadata is UNKNOWN source, HAS_FRAME with the actual nonzero
active frame, no event index, activation, cause or host timestamp. Aggregate
flags are not evidence from which these missing facts can be reconstructed.

## Passive work and resource ownership

Required context/state/selection pointers, Styled theme and nonzero ID are checked
before calling legacy code; failed admission has no maintenance, callbacks or
state writes. Otherwise existing passive maintenance remains intact. Notifications
are suppressed outside active painted submission, under layout-only ancestry or
when Calendar is disabled. Inert/modal routing is still Core's existing behavior;
this API adds no routing or propagation policy and does not claim every reducer
branch uniformly checks input consumption.

Observer/user are borrowed through the call. Keep selection, state, theme, locale
strings, options and disabled-policy userdata alive and unchanged. Existing policy
calls can occur repeatedly during scanning and painting; there is no one-call-per-
action guarantee. The facade does not copy/retain policy userdata. Observers must
not mutate, free or rebind active resources, destroy context, or recursively submit
UI. They may set unrelated flags; apply omission/removal after outer return and
defer teardown through frame/renderer consumption. Payload fields themselves are
pointer-free and remain safe when copied after later frames or context destruction.

`tests/unit/test_picker_events.c` compares old/new selections, state, policy call
counts, focus, legacy result, semantics and draw commands for all three entrypoints.
It covers multiple/net-zero changes, same-date activation, keyboard navigation,
reversed range completion, year/month chooser silence, disabled-day bounds/policy,
passive presentation repair, disabled/inert/layout-only silence, missing observer,
copy lifetime, deferred omission and atomic pointer/ID admission. Callback-time
checks distinguish reduce-only semantics from Base/Styled completion. Legacy
`picker` and `picker_base_only` suites remain required. Tests use the private native
display wrapper. No browser, host accessibility or foreign binding proof is implied.


## DatePicker selected dates

The same header provides `cui_base_date_picker_events` and
`cui_date_picker_events`, mirroring the old arguments plus date handler. Base
returns `cui_calendar_event_result`; Styled returns `cui_picker_event_result` with
its exact old bool in `changed` and zero/one actual `change_count`. Base requires
both trigger and calendar IDs nonzero; Styled requires its trigger ID and theme.
Required pointers/IDs are checked atomically before legacy code.

Each wraps the complete original operation once, with no nested Calendar observer.
The event target is the **outer trigger ID**, even though Base also takes a separate
calendar ID. The observer runs after all original popup dismissal, focus restoration,
trigger formatting, layout and paint work (or the original early return). Opening,
closing, navigating and activating the same selected date do not alone notify.
A first range selection may notify while the popup stays open; completing a range
can notify after it closes. Only selected start/end date comparisons decide CHANGE.

A late Styled failure can return false even after Base has changed dates: for
example, first range selection followed by invalid popup viewport placement.
The facade preserves that bool and still delivers the applied date CHANGE after
close/focus restoration. Do not treat `changed` as a callback count or successful
render signal, and do not gate applied notification on that bool. There is no
invented error or close reason in the payload.

Global disabled or Calendar-disabled options suppress observers while keeping old
trigger/overlay maintenance. Active painted/frame, UNKNOWN/no-index evidence,
missing-handler editing, copied payload, borrowed policy/locale data and deferred
teardown rules match Calendar above. DatePicker overlay state retains its existing
lifetime and the standalone trigger has no date observer API.

DatePicker tests pair legacy/facade results, state, focus, locale/policy calls,
semantics and draw commands. They cover Italian locale labels, same-date close,
range completion, invalid viewport after mutation, close/focus at callback time,
null handler, multiple Base inputs with one callback, passive/disabled/inert/layout
silence, payload copying after destruction, deferred omission and atomic calendar-ID
admission. These remain native source proofs, not foreign or browser coverage.


## ColorPicker applied RGBA

`cui_base_color_picker_events` and `cui_color_picker_events` mirror the respective
legacy signatures and append `cui_color_handler`. Each returns
`cui_picker_event_result`, preserving the exact legacy bool in `changed` and
counting zero/one actual callbacks. The typed `cui_color_change` contains metadata
and previous/final `cui_color` RGBA bytes. All fields are pointer-free and copyable.

Each whole legacy operation runs once, including final HSV/drag/last_color state,
semantics and (Styled) painting, before notification. Comparison explicitly checks
r/g/b/a fields; it does not compare padding, formatted text or HSV. Several changes
coalesce and net-zero RGBA means no callback. A latent hue change while black or
achromatic need not change RGBA and is not an applied color event. External color
assignment before entry resynchronizes HSV without a component CHANGE.

A palette selection preserves the old alpha when alpha editing is off; the payload
reports that actual final RGBA, not the palette entry's unused alpha. Missing
handler does not inhibit edits. The unused user pointer is ignored. Required
context/state/color pointers, nonzero ID and Styled theme are checked before
legacy code. All other legacy validation remains unchanged.

Delivery requires active painted submission, a proven nonzero frame, enabled and
non-readonly options. Passive maintenance still runs, including HSV synchronization
and readonly/disabled drag cleanup. Metadata has CHANGE and outer picker ID,
UNKNOWN source, HAS_FRAME only, no index/activation/cause. There is no rejection,
BEGIN/COMMIT/CANCEL or owner-controlled color contract added here.

Keep palette/color/state/theme and callback userdata alive through the call. Do
not mutate/free/rebind active resources or recursively submit UI in the observer;
set unrelated flags and defer omission/teardown until return and frame/render
consumption. No payload points into the palette or retains userdata.

Color tests pair Base and Styled legacy/facade contexts for real palette clicks,
channel keys and saturation/value-plane pointer drags, comparing RGBA, HSV/capture,
semantics, results and draw commands. They verify alpha-off preservation, net-zero
updates, latent HSV silence, external RGBA resynchronization, absent-observer
editing, readonly/disabled cleanup, inert/layout-only silence, copied payload after
context destruction and deferred omission. Together with the original Picker and
Base-only suites these are native source proofs; foreign/browser parity is not
implied. The existing time field remains a separate future slice.

| Target | Status | Evidence and limits |
|---|---|---|
| Linux Xorg | tested partial | Native SDL_Renderer OpenGL, independent Sokol GLCORE and SDL_GPU Vulkan on Intel Graphics; actual frames/readbacks, pointer/key model and clipboard tests. SDL composition/candidate-rectangle forwarding has injected service tests; real OS IME/candidate-window acceptance and native screen readers remain unverified. |
| Linux headless | tested partial | GCC C11/software renderer, behavioral suites, ASan/UBSan, SDL dummy services. |
| Linux Wayland | untested | SDL supports host integration; no compositor smoke run yet. Xorg is not Wayland evidence. |
| Windows | tested portable subset | Published67d86ed4: hosted MSVC19.51.36260.0 passes145/145 portable checks on [CI run38488091130](https://github.com/mattmezza/cui/actions/runs/38488091130). Native adapters are disabled; native GUI/Direct3D, OS IME, accessibility and app packaging are unverified. |
| macOS | tested portable subset | Published67d86ed4: hosted Apple Clang21.0.0.21000101 passes145/145 portable checks on [CI run38488091130](https://github.com/mattmezza/cui/actions/runs/38488091130). Native adapters are disabled; native GUI/Metal, OS IME, accessibility and app packaging are unverified. |
| Browser WASM | tested partial | Actual Chromium runs CUI WebAssembly with Canvas/input host, including pointer/keyboard, scalar input, popup focus/Escape, themes and 390px bounds. See [browser gallery](WEB_GALLERY.md). Native text shaping/OS accessibility remain separate. |
| Android | untested | No wrapper/device validation. |
| iOS | untested | No wrapper/simulator/device validation/signing. |
| WASM/WASI | tested headless WASI subset | Zig0.16/Wasmtime49 portable behavioral/embedding suites compile and run; current source/counts are recorded in validation logs; see [WASI.md](WASI.md). |

Optional unavailable integrations are explicit. Compilation will be recorded separately from runtime tests. SDL_GPU SPIR-V shader support currently confines that adapter to Vulkan-capable devices; D3D12/Metal formats are pending. Sokol GLCORE is tested on Linux Xorg; its other backends and platforms are pending.

Linux X11 also has [continuous external resize evidence](LINUX_LIVE_RESIZE.md)
under private Xvfb/software rendering: intermediate captures follow window size,
responsive sidebar/card changes and retained application state while a resize
burst is ongoing. This does not establish physical window-manager dragging or
Wayland behavior. Linux resize support is a separate acceptance scope from the
Cocoa/Windows callback scheduling contract.

The optional pinned Unicode regex archive is currently validated on Linux native and WASI only. Portable Core/Base/Components need neither that archive nor Rust. Developing on Linux does not prevent macOS support: hosted macOS runners can compile/test the native integration once implemented. Full platform acceptance also requires actual macOS window/render/input/accessibility and hardware/session testing, which can use a remotely accessible Mac rather than the maintainer's laptop.

Linux hosted GCC and Clang passed their configured native/sanitizer checks on CI run38225532353 plus Xvfb gallery smoke and Sokol pixel/cache tests. The CI GL driver reported **llvmpipe**, a software driver; this is API/readback coverage and is separate from the actual Intel/Mesa hardware evidence on the development Xorg host. Saved [previous CI summary](validation/ci-01865d5.txt) and [latest published-source job metadata](validation/ci-3ef6c49.json) record exact source and outcomes.

Native macOS build/bundle and headless adapter CI are now authored; they have not yet been observed running for this change. See [the Mac workflow](MACOS.md) and [Linux cross compilation](MACOS_CROSS.md). Cocoa/Retina/Metal, IME and accessibility acceptance remain separate.
