# Popover source anchors

Semantics are audited against GPUI reference commit
`87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`, especially component Popover,
base Popup live anchor positioning and Positioner corner clamping.

`cui_popover_begin` is an additive C API for source-style Popover positioning and
arrows. Existing `cui_surface_begin` retains its legacy side placement, 6px gap,
opposite-side overflow selection and size reduction. Existing public state and
options structs have unchanged ABI. Recompile/link against the new library to
use the added symbols. This API is C-only until binding coverage is explicitly
updated; family catalog presence does not imply binding option parity.

```c
cui_surface_options options = {
    .viewport = {0, 0, 640, 480},
    .anchor = {120, 80, 100, 32}, /* current-frame trigger rectangle */
    .width = 240,
    .height = 160,
    .margin = 4,
    .hide_close = true,
    .popover_appearance = CUI_POPOVER_APPEARANCE_SOURCE,
};
cui_popover_position position = {
    .mode = CUI_POPOVER_POSITION_ANCHOR,
    .anchor = CUI_POPOVER_TOP_LEFT,
    .reference_rem = 16,
    .arrow = true,
};
if (cui_popover_begin(ui, theme, state, cui_string("Details"),
                      (cui_str){0}, options, position)) {
    cui_text(ui, cui_string("Popover content"), theme->font_size, theme->text);
    cui_surface_end(ui);
}
```

Read `include/cui/cui_surface.h` for the complete contract. Initialize state with
`CUI_SURFACE_POPOVER` and open it with `cui_surface_open` as for existing surfaces.
Always balance a successful begin with `cui_surface_end`; a false begin has no
caller-owned boxes to close. Supply updated trigger bounds each submitted frame.

Anchor names identify the popup's own anchor: TopLeft/Center/Right open below the
trigger, BottomLeft/Center/Right open above it. LeftCenter opens to its right;
RightCenter opens to its left. Alignment follows the named trigger edge/corner.
Anchor mode clamps without flipping or shrinking the chosen dimensions. Width/
height <=0 select 420/260; invalid active geometry is rejected before overlay state
updates. `cui_popover_surface_geometry` exposes these defaults and placement as a
pure helper with unchanged output on failure.

`reference_rem` is a logical size from app/host root sizing configuration. Zero
selects 16. Never infer it from a theme font. Default offset is reference_rem/4;
arrow depth is reference_rem*3/8 and is added to surface distance. With
`custom_offset=true`, signed offset including 0 replaces the default gap. Finite
negative gaps may overlap the trigger. Clamping may alter the apparent gap. Source
logical placement retains fractional coordinates; host pixel snapping is separate.

Arrow base inset uses the theme radius, even if the surface radius is refined.
Fill follows the effective refined background. Appearance NONE without explicit
background refinement uses theme popover for the arrow. The 1px outline uses theme
text at alpha 26/255 and is absent for NONE. Arrow triangle and ring seam patch
paint after panel contents at its layer, inherit panel opacity and clip to both
the supplied viewport and host viewport. Decoration does not enlarge the panel
hit/dismiss bounds, create semantics or receive focus. It remains visible with
an inert ancestor and while another modal owns input. A separate inert paint
portal uses local prepaint so visual painting does not require input eligibility.

Geometry and vertices are copied into context-owned frame storage; do not retain
draw-list pointers across the next begin-frame. Arrow payload/paint-command
capacity failure balances internal boxes and
suppresses the final draw list. Ordinary layout-node capacity follows Core
semantics: failure remains balanced but ordinary paint may be partial. Retry on
a later adequately sized frame.

The portable outline uses a bounded 2px miter and triangle meshes. GPUI's external
PathBuilder tessellation/raster AA is not reproduced exactly. Source fill, anchor,
tip and seam equations do not establish exact pixel parity. Software, SDL_GPU and
Sokol support Core mesh commands. SDL3 now supports bounded analytic meshes
through prepared CPU coverage textures; see `design/SDL3_MESH.md` for its limits.
The browser Canvas adapter has exact headless mesh-mask and opacity evidence at
DPR 1 and 2. The gallery additionally tests all eight anchors, signed offsets,
clamping, opacity, inert paint and modal ordering with desktop and touch input.
Physical GPU hardware checks remain separate from Xvfb/software validation.
This slice does not cover
Popover transition, right-click trigger or focus/control parity.

## Browser gallery

The Popover story starts with its existing legacy account card. Select **Source
anchors (opt in)** to use `cui_popover_begin` and a real centered CUI trigger.
All eight names identify the popup's own anchor. Controls map directly to
`mode`, `anchor`, `custom_offset`, signed scalar `offset`, `arrow` and
`reference_rem`. The latter is explicit application/host root sizing: zero means
16 logical pixels; the sample also offers 16, 24 and 32. It is never inferred
from the theme font. Inactive controls are disabled in legacy mode.

Edge clamp moves the actual trigger to the lower corner. The gallery schedules
one settling frame when the newly laid-out trigger differs from the bounds used
for composition, then returns to idle. It retains popup size and anchor direction.
Opacity and inert controls wrap the real stage. Open the card first to observe
paint persisting under an inert ancestor while child semantics/input disappear.
The modal demonstration uses a separate ordinary dialog at explicit layer 200,
above the card's default layer; it does not implement automatic overlay ordering.
Closing that dialog updates its control. Route changes close both surfaces and
reset the demonstration controls. The complete C11 snippet reflects the current
positioning and stage settings.

`tests/web/test_popover_anchor_gallery.py` drives actual mouse/CDP touch input,
checks all eight source equations against real CUI bounds and mesh vertices,
compiles the displayed snippets with strict C11 warnings, and reads actual Canvas
pixels for centered arrow joins, opacity, inert persistence and modal backdrop
ordering. Fractional clamped Canvas rectangle edges can still antialias the join
differently from mesh pixel-center coverage: a dark fill value 10 can read 9 at
an adjacent join pixel. Clamped geometry is checked separately; exact centered
join assertions retain exact values. This known raster difference is not claimed
as GPUI pixel parity. Browser font, accessibility and focus limitations remain.

# Opt-in Popover source appearance

This slice implements consumed surface appearance against gpui-component 0.7.1 commit `87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`, `crates/component/src/styled.rs:16–125,186–194` and `crates/component/src/popover.rs:355–361`. It does not complete the Popover family.

Append `popover_appearance = CUI_POPOVER_APPEARANCE_SOURCE` to `cui_surface_options` for a POPOVER. Zero/LEGACY preserves the existing surface background, text, padding and 1px border with no shadows. SOURCE uses theme popover/popover_foreground, theme radius, 12 logical pixels padding (p_3 at the pinned 16px rem baseline), no ordinary border and these ordered DROP layers:

| x | y | sigma | spread | ink |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | theme text RGB, alpha26 |
| 0 | 4 | 3 | -1 | black alpha26 |
| 0 | 2 | 2 | -2 | black alpha26 |

The first layer is an expanded filled rounded caster, not an outline. Original caster radii are retained before spread. Core copies the three layers onto the actual portal node; ancestor opacity is applied by Core once. Layer alpha is the nearest byte to 0.1. This is numerical CUI raster parity, not certification of GPUI's GPU kernel/AA/color identity.

NONE skips background, padding, radius, border and shadow defaults. Explicit refinement flags apply afterward in every policy, including NONE: background/foreground/radius/padding/border and a replacement ordered list of up to eight mixed DROP/INSET layers. A zero-count SHADOWS refinement explicitly removes default shadows. Values are owned copies; no layer pointers remain borrowed. Unflagged properties do not override defaults. Unknown flags/policy, count overflow, invalid finite geometry or invalid layer kind/geometry reject before Base input reduction or decision callbacks. The pure `cui_popover_style_resolve` leaves output untouched on failure. Styled and Base begin return false for invalid Popover configuration. Other surface kinds ignore these Popover-only options.

Host rem changes require an explicit padding refinement; theme font size is not a rem proxy. CUI retains its automatic title/Close/body composition, whereas source Popover content is arbitrary caller content. NONE uses theme text as the fallback for that explicit title; source would inherit the enclosing element's foreground. An explicit foreground refinement overrides this fallback. Body children keep their caller-specified colors. General inherited text styling, arbitrary source StyleRefinement, arrows/anchor policy and appearance-off parent-color identity are not completed here. Appearance does not alter outside-dismiss policy. Public Popover does not receive an invented 150ms animation: the source's private dropdown helper is a separate consumer.

## Tests and registration

Root registers these new files; this worker does not edit global build or distribution files:

* `tests/unit/test_popover_appearance.c`: strict composed Core/Popover commands, light/dark distinct semantic colors, exact caster/order/radii, legacy and NONE custom shadows, resolver invalid geometry/count/kind, pending-dismiss callback/state atomicity.

# Progress

Progress uses a controlled normalized fraction (`0..1`). Submit it each frame;
its numeric semantic value is the target fraction even while the visible bar
animates. Indeterminate progress is busy and has no numeric value in the browser
accessibility bridge. It never adds a Tab stop.

```c
#include <cui/cui_components.h>

void draw_download(cui_context *ui, const cui_theme *theme,
                   cui_progress_motion *motion, float fraction, double now) {
    cui_progress_options options = cui_progress_defaults();
    options.name = cui_string("Downloading assets");
    options.size = CUI_CONTROL_SMALL;
    options.motion = motion;
    options.now_seconds = now;
    cui_progress_ex(ui, cui_id_from(ui, "download"), theme,
                     fraction, 240, options);
}
```

Keep a zero-initialized `cui_progress_motion` in application state and supply a
monotonic host clock in seconds. The first submission displays the value
immediately. Later changes animate over 180ms by default, and reversing a target
continues from the currently displayed value. Set `duration` to customize it;
zero selects the default. `reduced_motion`, or context reduced motion, snaps to
the target. The return value reports whether another animation frame is needed;
CUI also invalidates the context while moving.

For a loading bar, set `indeterminate = true`. The defaults use the frozen
one-second cycle: the segment grows from the left, then contracts toward the
right using quadratic ease-in-out. Reduced motion produces a static centered
35% segment. Invalid or negative clock values also select that static segment.
A zero-initialized options struct preserves the earlier CUI 1.6-second,
fixed-width 30% loading cycle; explicitly set `source_motion = true` or use the
constructor to select the source-style cycle.

Extra-small/small/medium/large heights are 4/6/8/10px; positive `height` overrides
them. The bar radius is half its height, except that a square theme remains
square. `custom_corners` and `corners` refine each corner on both track and fill.
`custom_color` and `color` override the solid fill, including transparent color;
the track uses 20% of its alpha. Zero/negative/nonfinite width selects 160px.
Nonfinite fractions become zero; finite fractions clamp to `0..1`. CUI uses
fractions rather than the reference's `0..100` percentage API.

## Base composition

`cui_progress_measure` is allocation-free, independent geometry in normalized
track units. It returns the clamped fraction, segment start/length and whether
loading needs another frame. An application can scale the geometry to pixels and
paint its own track, indicator or arbitrary child content with Core boxes.

Inside the root box, call `cui_base_progress` with the same ID to register
progress semantics without painting. The styled adapter uses this same base
behavior. There is no independent interaction reducer in the styling layer.

`cui_progress_animate` is a caller-owned deterministic value transition, also
usable by custom styling. Its duration is explicit, with zero meaning instant;
invalid arguments preserve the state and output. A regressing clock is held at
the last observed time. The move easing is cubic-bezier `(0.2,0,0,1)`; arbitrary
easing/theme-motion-token overrides remain a separate API gap.

The loading formula and sizes follow the [frozen Progress source](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-kit/blob/87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34/crates/component/src/progress/progress.rs).
The quadratic easing was checked against its pinned `gpui-pre 0.3.8` dependency
(crate SHA-256 `d7f0bc3ebba070f8981b3f8e905a12f47d27794a30d029e59cdb9edf7a4b3360`).
No engine or runtime dependency is added. Base and styled tests cover geometry,
cycle boundaries, reduced motion, colors/sizes, reversal continuity, clock
regression, invalid-state transactionality and controlled semantics.

## ProgressCircle

`cui_progress_circle` uses the same controlled fraction, semantic behavior,
caller-owned value motion and source loading cycle. Start from
`cui_progress_circle_defaults`. Its nested `progress` options supply size,
name, clock, loading/reduced-motion flags and color; bar height/corner/style
fields do not affect the ring. Extra-small/small/medium/large diameters are
8/12/16/20px. A positive `diameter` overrides them up to256px.

Keep a `cui_progress_circle_state` with writable RGBA storage, capacity and a
zero initial revision. Defaults rasterize at twice logical size; required storage
is `ceil(diameter*raster_scale)^2*4` bytes. Scale must be greater than zero and at
most4; output is bounded to512px per side. Pixels are borrowed by the draw list:
retain them unchanged until rendering completes. Use distinct state/storage for
simultaneously displayed circles. Insufficient capacity submits no UI, invokes
no child callback and preserves motion, pixels and revision.

The optional content callback composes children at the ring's center. Use a
larger custom diameter for a text label. It runs synchronously; its user data and
borrowed strings follow normal Core frame/render lifetimes. The circle is a
progress indicator, with no automatic interaction or Tab stop.

`cui_progress_circle_measure` exposes pure annulus/start/end geometry;
`cui_progress_circle_raster` produces a portable4x4 antialiased RGBA bitmap
without allocating. Stroke width is `min(diameter*0.15,5)`, with clockwise arcs
starting at12 o'clock and a20%-alpha track. Transparent/custom colors remain
explicit. CUI uses its raster sampling rather than GPUI vector paths; the
reference's0.0001-radian path-closing seam for spans at least half a turn is not
reproduced. Arbitrary vector/style refinement and child clipping are application
composition, not automatic source tree reproduction.

# Questionnaire source audit

Questionnaire is registered in the main library and distribution. Its interactive gallery story is implemented; full source parity remains unfinished. The retained model and initial composable styled parts are implemented; this is not full parity. Reference commit: `87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`, `crates/base/src/questionnaire/{types,state,keyboard,control}.rs` and `crates/component/src/questionnaire/components.rs`.

## State and answers

Ordered item definitions have a unique name, accessible label, optional description, required/multiple/disabled flags, choices, an optional retained Input editor and a validator. Choice values are unique within an item. Single-answer definitions reject multiple defaults even if one default is disabled. Disabled default choices do not enter the initial answer. A nonblank enabled initial input replaces defaults for single-answer items. Preserve the original input draft separately from the effective answer, including when a choice supersedes the freeform answer.

Effective answers always use schema choice order. Disabling a choice hides it from the effective answer without deleting the retained selection; enabling restores it. Disabled items have empty effective answers and are excluded from totals and submission. Multiple-answer items may include both choices and freeform; single-answer items may include only one source. Whitespace-only freeform is absent. Setters validate names, choices and capacities atomically before changing model/editor/history. Programmatic setters are silent; user changes emit AnswerChanged. Reset restores initial answers and original input drafts while retaining current disabled flags and external errors.

## Validation and navigation

Unanswered, Answered and Skipped are distinct states. An empty optional item is invalid until explicitly skipped. Internal errors distinguish Required, Unanswered and validator text; external errors take precedence. Disabled and skipped items suppress errors. After the first validation attempt, answer edits revalidate immediately. Any answer change clears completion and cancels pending confirmation.

Current position and total refer to enabled items. Disabling the current item chooses the next enabled item, then the previous one; enabling an item when none is current selects it. Previous navigation does not validate; Next validates the current item. Submit validates every enabled item and returns to the first invalid one. A valid submission emits Completed once per completed state, then Submit every time. Changes allow a later Completed again. CurrentItemChanged is emitted by user navigation but not silent setters. Submission and validation snapshots preserve schema order.

## Activation, focus and timing

Single-choice user activation selects then confirms after 150 ms, letting the selection become visible. Reduced motion still defers confirmation until after AnswerChanged callbacks, with no time delay. Activating the already-selected answer confirms immediately. Multiple-choice activation only toggles. Radio arrow movement changes selection without confirming. Another answer/current-item change cancels the pending confirmation; event subscribers may enable follow-up items before it runs.

Enabled choices receive A–Z or 1–9 shortcuts by enabled position, skipping disabled choices. Focus moves between choices and the optional Input with the source's radio-group behavior. A selected choice owns Enter confirmation; an unselected choice owns activation. A focused nonempty Input retains arrows and text, while empty Input Up/Down may leave it. Ctrl/Command+Enter confirms; unrelated modifiers, repeats, IME composition and preferred character input must not trigger shortcuts. Rendered controls must use real Checkbox/Radio/Input behavior and graphical marks, with accessible names, description, set position and focus ownership.

## Verification requirements

Port source behavioral cases for schema rejection, silent setters, draft preservation, reset, disabled restoration, schema order, external errors, cross-item validation, first-invalid focus, completion ordering, shortcuts, disabled-current fallback, delayed choice confirmation and no confirmation from radio arrows/typing. Add transactional capacity/UTF-8 and standalone base-link checks. Styled composition needs its own source audit and actual pointer/keyboard, four-size, disabled/error and focus tests before being called implemented. Full parity is not established by a state reducer or a static wizard screenshot.

## Current implementation evidence

The portable retained model tests cover schema errors, disabled answer restoration, effective-answer change detection, input drafts, capacity/UTF-8 atomicity, optional skip validation, delayed/reduced-motion confirmation, and completion-before-submit ordering. Styled tests exercise all four card sizes, pointer activation and updated checkbox semantics, minimum card height, error/action visibility, Skip completion, actual text editing into a freeform answer, and disabled input suppression. Standalone strict C11 and ASan/UBSan checks pass; the existing branch CTest suite passes73/73.

Remaining work includes typography/general layout refinements, comprehensive keyboard/callback coverage and platform accessibility integration. Bounded box-slot refinements and action/error localization are implemented below; ordered text/key reduction is also documented below. Existing styled code is a development checkpoint, not evidence that these gaps are complete.

Input Enter confirmation and radio Left/Right wrapping now have native and sanitizer tests, including disabled-choice skipping, repeat suppression, event consumption, and no delayed confirmation from arrow selection. The explicit radio key helper must be called before choice rendering; complete root keyboard/callback coverage remains unfinished.

The root now owns a nonmodal focus scope. The explicit answer-key helper traverses enabled choices and an empty input with Up/Down, wraps in schema order, selects radios without confirming, and preserves cursor movement for nonempty drafts. Call it inside the root before answer parts. Native and sanitizer tests cover the choice/input boundary. Automatic root capture and initially focused-answer restoration remain unfinished.

The explicit confirm-key helper supports Enter on a focused filled choice/input and a host-selected Ctrl/Meta+Enter modifier. Modified submission owns and cancels the core activation token even when validation fails, preventing accidental radio selection. The native regression verifies this fallback failure and successful confirmation; sanitizer and existing73CTest gates pass.

The browser story now exercises required validation, delayed radio navigation, optional Skip, typed freeform submission, reset, disabled controls and all four sizes. The integrated library passes 77 native and 75 sanitizer suites. Gallery coverage does not establish complete keyboard, styling, accessibility or composition parity.

`cui_questionnaire_shortcut_keys` routes bare A–Z or 1–9 key identities to enabled choices by their visible shortcut position, focuses the chosen card, and uses the same delayed/repeated-choice confirmation model as pointer activation. Invoke it inside the root before input and choice parts. It ignores consumed events, repeat, modifiers, focused text input, disabled root/item, IME composition and preferred character input. The other explicit key helpers also yield to the two host keyboard-context flags. SDL tracks composition start/end when forwarding keys, and core default Enter/Tab/Space behavior yields to those flags. This prevents shortcut/default activation during composition; complete IME preedit rendering and automatic root keyboard capture remain unfinished.

Arrow entry from a non-answer control now restores the first (Down) or last (Up) filled answer in schema order before choosing an unfilled answer. Restoring focus leaves the answer unchanged and does not schedule confirmation. A failing-before/passing-after headless regression covers both directions from an action button.

Choice-card paint now follows the pinned selected/hover/invalid/disabled colors, transparent light or 20%-input dark idle background, size-specific card/indicator/shortcut radii and shortcut font sizes. The shared theme exposes explicit palette mode and the muted background token, populated from all 38 pinned palettes. Headless draw assertions exercise four sizes and idle/selected/hover/disabled states across every palette. The later focus band and bounded slot refinements below extend this checkpoint; arbitrary instance style refinement remains unfinished.

Choice options now accept `render_indicator`, `render_content`, and `render_shortcut` callbacks plus a shared `render_user`. Each receives a borrowed `cui_questionnaire_choice_view` snapshot (item/choice indices, size, selected/multiple/disabled/invalid/focused state and shortcut character) and a stable slot ID. Callbacks emit balanced CUI child elements. Content replaces the default label/description rendering while the card retains its definition's accessible name, role and behavior. Indicator and shortcut wrappers apply the pinned source's offset from the answer line using the default adornment size, including when custom artwork has a different intrinsic height. A custom shortcut renderer still runs when the default shortcut is unavailable. Disabled opacity is inherited across custom content.

Headless composition tests cover both radio and checkbox cards at all four sizes, intrinsic-size alignment, replacement precedence, pointer selection/focus, retained semantics, disabled/invalid snapshots and opacity. Null callbacks retain the default graphical parts, already covered across all 38 palettes. Bounded box-slot refinement is implemented below; typography/general layout refinement, comprehensive root event coverage and full accessibility remain unfinished. Source contract: pinned `crates/component/src/questionnaire/components.rs` choice renderers and `center_on_answer_line`.

`cui_questionnaire_item_begin`, `cui_questionnaire_choices_begin`, and `cui_questionnaire_actions_begin` provide source-aligned composition containers. Pair each successful begin with `cui_questionnaire_part_end`. Item and Choices omit unknown, inactive and disabled items without opening layout nodes. Item carries the definition's accessible label/description and accepts programmatic focus while staying outside Tab order. Choices uses a Group for multiple answers and the appended RadioGroup semantic role for single answers. Item gaps are XS/S/M/L 8/12/16/24; choice and action gaps are 4/6/8/10. Actions arrange children horizontally with centered cross-axis alignment and remain renderable without an active item.

The core `cui_semantic_parent` query exposes the completed frame's nearest semantic layout ancestor, with explicit parent metadata taking precedence. Native tests cover transparent intermediate boxes, reparenting and unavailable-frame queries. Container tests verify all sizes, radio/checkbox group roles, nested parent relationships, item focus restoration and Tab exclusion, child spacing/action alignment, inactive/disabled visibility and empty-item action composition. Root capture and inherited part sizes provide automatic composition; standalone parts retain explicit helpers. Arbitrary style refinement remains unfinished.

Default shortcut badges paint the theme background independently of selected/hovered card fills; disabled cards halve the entire badge opacity. Draw-list regressions cover all 38 preset palettes and all four sizes.

`cui_questionnaire_choice_position` returns the one-based position and total among enabled choices without allocating. Disabled/unknown choices or invalid arguments leave both required outputs unchanged. Styled radio/checkbox answers publish this position together with their definition description; runtime disabled changes recompute the enabled set. This semantic coverage does not imply a verified native screen-reader bridge.

Focused answer cards now tint their existing border with the focus token and paint the pinned source’s 3px, half-opacity outside band. The band preserves translucent card interiors and does not alter card or sibling layout. `theme.hide_focus_ring` suppresses the band while retaining the focused border. Headless draw tests cover all 38 palettes and all four sizes; this does not complete root keyboard routing or platform accessibility.

Questionnaire parts now inherit the root size through a context-owned, bounded 128-entry state-address table. Non-medium part sizes remain explicit overrides; `custom_size` permits an explicit Medium override. Parts outside a registered root use Medium. Publishing a 129th distinct root clears the bounded table before recording the new root, matching the source cache policy. Separate contexts do not share sizes. Draw-list tests compare all parts across all four sizes and verify overrides, context isolation and cache eviction; the same tests fail against the previous implementation. Root capture and basic cross-item focus routing are implemented below; full event/callback coverage remains incomplete.

The root now captures unconsumed keys before child reducers using the preceding frame’s submitted part bindings. It handles answer/radio arrows, item navigation, alphabetic/numeric shortcuts, filled-answer Enter and Ctrl/Meta+Enter, while respecting input focus, unrelated modifiers, repeats, IME and preferred character input. Parts publish bindings through bounded context resources; the current list replaces the previous list each frame so omitted controls are reclaimed safely. Root numeric mode supplies part shortcut labels. Navigation restores the new Item focus; failed confirmation prefers the invalid item’s filled input/selected choice, then the first enabled answer. Native tests cover automatic composition without helper calls, cross-item focus, event guards, input cursor ownership, disabled roots, invalid confirmation, omission/reintroduction and resource-capacity failure. The regression fails against the previous root. Nested roots and comprehensive callback choreography still need source-level verification.


## Ordered input batches

Questionnaire input now reduces queued events in order. A `TEXT` or clipboard
paste followed by Enter in one frame synchronizes the new answer before
confirmation. Enter followed by text confirms the answer that existed at Enter;
remaining events targeted at the old input do not edit either the old answer or
the next item. Completing the last item likewise stops the old input batch.
Selection replacement and multiple text events each emit their answer change
before the current-item/completion event. An empty Enter does not retroactively
confirm text arriving later in the queue.

Automatic root capture defers focused-input keys to this ordered path. An
explicit confirm helper used inside the root also leaves focused-input Enter to
`cui_questionnaire_input_control`. Filled-input arrows remain editor-owned;
empty-input navigation keeps the root behavior. IME composition, preferred
character input and repeated Enter do not confirm; disabled roots/inputs do not
edit or confirm. Reduced motion does not reorder input events.

`cui_base_input_reduce_event` exposes the shared single-event reducer for other
composite controls. Register the textbox with `cui_interact` first, call the
reducer once per event in increasing queue order, aggregate errors, then publish
final semantics and paint. It does not submit semantics or process other queue
entries. Borrowed clipboard and hit-test geometry are used synchronously. Invalid
indices/NULL arguments leave editor, drag state and events unchanged. The ordinary
`cui_base_input_ex` uses the same reducer and retains readonly, pointer selection,
clipboard, IME, repeat, and delegated navigation behavior.

Headless regressions cover text/paste plus confirmation, confirmation plus later
text, empty Enter plus text, select-all replacement plus multiple edits, callback
ordering, final completion, old-item event isolation, disabled/reduced-motion
behavior, and single-event invalid/delegated-key handling. The text-plus-Enter
regression fails against the previous Questionnaire component implementation.
This fixes batch ordering; it does not establish full Questionnaire parity.


Bounded choice slot refinements and localized labels
---------------------------------------------------

`cui_questionnaire_options` accepts optional `indicator_style`, `content_style`
and `shortcut_style` pointers to `cui_questionnaire_slot_style`. These refine a
bounded subset of the existing portable `cui_box`: dimensions, uniform padding,
gap, radius, background, border color/width, physical alignment and opacity.
`fields` selects independent overrides, including transparent colors, zero border
or radius and zero opacity. Unmasked values are ignored. Width/height accept
`-1` for grow, explicit fixed `0`, or positive logical pixels through4096. Other
lengths accept0..4096, opacity0..1, and alignment START/CENTER/END. The content
wrapper retains its default grow width unless WIDTH is selected.

Refinement follows the frozen source's three distinct seams: indicator and
shortcut styles affect only their default elements; a custom renderer replaces
that default element and therefore its style. Content style affects the wrapper
around either default text or custom content. The adornment's vertical offset
continues to use the default size metrics, so changing its dimensions does not
recenter it against a multiline description. Card input, role, accessible name,
selected/invalid state and disabled ancestor opacity stay independent. Slot
opacity multiplies inherited opacity. No text color/font/weight inheritance,
percentage/flex policy, per-edge styling or general GPUI `StyleRefinement`
parity is claimed by this box-only descriptor.

```c
cui_questionnaire_slot_style content = {
    .fields = CUI_QUESTIONNAIRE_SLOT_BACKGROUND | CUI_QUESTIONNAIRE_SLOT_PADDING,
    .box = {.background = {240, 245, 255, 255}, .padding = 4}
};
cui_questionnaire_labels labels = {
    .fields = CUI_QUESTIONNAIRE_LABEL_SUBMIT | CUI_QUESTIONNAIRE_LABEL_REQUIRED,
    .submit = {"Absenden", 8},
    .required = {"Bitte beantworten", 17}
};
cui_questionnaire_options options = {.content_style = &content, .labels = &labels};
/* Pass options explicitly to the relevant parts; root options do not publish
 * styles or translations to child submissions. */
```

`cui_questionnaire_labels` independently masks Previous, Skip, Next, Submit,
Required and Unfilled labels. Missing fields keep existing English defaults;
a masked empty UTF-8 string deliberately supplies an empty label. A nonempty
explicit label passed to `cui_questionnaire_action_control` wins over localization.
Custom validator/external MESSAGE text stays exact. The progress sentence,
item/choice text, input labels and keyboard identities are not translated by this
bundle; applications already own their definition strings. There is no ambient
locale registry or retained translation callback.

Every options-taking part copies all supplied descriptor values at entry and
validates them before routing, tick, model interaction or custom renderers.
Unknown mask bits, invalid active dimensions/alignment/opacity and invalid active
UTF-8 strings (including NULL data with nonzero length) reject the entire
submission. This applies even to descriptors unused by that part, or refinements
replaced by custom renderers. Bool entry points return false, input returns
`CUI_QUESTIONNAIRE_INVALID`, and void entry points emit nothing; invalid options
consume no events or opening scopes. As with other borrowed C inputs, descriptor
pointers must address readable storage while copied. String bytes remain borrowed
through completed-frame draw consumption. Root size inheritance is unchanged;
these styles and translations have no root-to-part inheritance.

Appending these fields preserves source defaults for zero/designated-initialized
options but changes `sizeof(cui_questionnaire_options)` and its by-value ABI.
Rebuild C consumers and use matched SDK/distribution snapshots; this is not an
old-binary ABI compatibility guarantee.

The headless `test_questionnaire_styled.c` regressions cover all four sizes,
independent slot geometry/paint, default-based offsets, custom replacement,
content grow/zero dimensions, transparent/zero overrides, disabled opacity and
semantics, descriptor copying before a renderer mutates the original, translated
action/error paint and semantic names, explicit/default/custom-message precedence,
and invalid-option rejection before automatic root routing and callbacks. These
are portable headless contracts, not browser/native screen-reader acceptance or
complete Questionnaire source parity. Nested roots, comprehensive callback
choreography, broader part/style methods and platform integration remain open.

Optional [progress presentation](QUESTIONNAIRE_PROGRESS.md) now supports localized
accessible/visible text, decorative children and explicit bounded progress text
metrics via an independent C header. The legacy helper keeps its English sentence
and previous paint. This does not change other-part typography or add a Form role.

# Questionnaire geometry and numeric metrics

Include `cui_questionnaire_geometry.h` with matching CUI sources/library. This
additive API does not resize legacy options, choice views or state. NULL and
all-zero geometry preserve the original layout tree, text paint and reduction.
No layout/paint option changes model events or disabled eligibility.

Pass an independent descriptor to each `_ex` part. Root publishes its existing
size/density only: numeric metrics and refinements never implicitly inherit.
Existing keyboard policies can be passed independently; NULL retains the existing
route inheritance. Existing progress, named presentation and observers are
unchanged. The complete checked resolver lets the owner reuse numeric values
explicitly, including with custom children.

```c
#include "cui/cui_questionnaire_geometry.h"
void questionnaire_geometry_example(cui_context *ui, const cui_theme *theme,
                                    cui_questionnaire_state *state) {
    cui_questionnaire_options options = {.design_size = CUI_DESIGN_BASE};
    cui_questionnaire_geometry_options geometry = {
        .metric_fields = CUI_QUESTIONNAIRE_METRIC_MINIMUM_HEIGHT,
        .metrics = {.minimum_height = 64},
        .card = {.fields = CUI_QUESTIONNAIRE_BOX_PADDING,
                 .padding = {.left = 12, .right = 16, .top = 8, .bottom = 8}},
        .answer = {.fields = CUI_QUESTIONNAIRE_TEXT_SIZE |
                            CUI_QUESTIONNAIRE_TEXT_LINE_HEIGHT,
                   .font_size = 18, .line_height = 28}};
    if (!cui_questionnaire_begin_ex(ui, 100, theme, state, options, NULL, &geometry))
        return;
    size_t item = state->current;
    if (cui_questionnaire_item_begin_ex(ui, 101, state, item, options, &geometry)) {
        if (cui_questionnaire_choices_begin_ex(ui, 102, state, item, options, &geometry)) {
            for (size_t choice = 0; choice < state->items[item].choice_count; ++choice)
                (void)cui_questionnaire_choice_control_ex(
                    ui, 200 + choice, theme, state, item, choice, options, NULL, &geometry);
            cui_questionnaire_part_end(ui);
        }
        cui_questionnaire_part_end(ui);
    }
    cui_questionnaire_end(ui);
}
```

Use application-owned collision-free IDs and schema lifetime as in the original
Questionnaire API. The example assumes a valid initialized model and submissions
inside a frame. No event facade, binding wrapper or automatic arbitrary text
cascade is supplied.

## Resolution and validation

Resolve existing legacy size/shared XS–9XL and density first. With shared size
INHERIT, nonzero `custom_scalar` supplies a complete source numeric profile;
non-INHERIT shared size wins. Scalar is finite (0,256]. Individual masked metrics
then override that profile, including zero gaps/padding/minimum. No additional
four-size enum or numeric inheritance cache is introduced. Lengths must be finite
[0,4096]; font sizes finite (0,512]. Width is grow(-1), FIT(0), positive fixed;
`fixed_zero_width` makes a masked zero width fixed zero. Scalar is independently
validated even when shared size wins. Unmasked values are ignored.

| Numeric custom V | Formula |
| --- | --- |
| root/item/choices/answer/content gaps | V / V / .5V / .625V / .125V |
| card horizontal/vertical padding; minimum height | .75V / .625V; 2.75V |
| indicator / radio mark / checkbox check | V / .5V / .875V |
| shortcut box / text | 1.25V / .625V |
| answer text / line box | V / 1.5V |
| secondary / title / progress text | .875V / 1.125V / .75V |
| card / shortcut radius | theme large / theme regular |

Custom secondary/title/progress line boxes are natural(0), reflecting source
branches that set size without a guaranteed explicit line box. Existing named
presentation/progress APIs remain independently configured; this helper does not
silently restyle them. Legacy helper values extract existing CUI paint, including
legacy heading line+4 and natural shortcut/progress lines. Shared scales retain
existing CUI geometry; their higher steps are CUI extensions. Fractions undergo
Core layout quantization, not arbitrary fractional-pixel parity.

Answer/secondary/shortcut refinements use the existing text masks. Resolved text
views include color/style. They affect the default paint branch of the existing
choice reducer. Effective answer first-line height aligns indicators/shortcuts;
natural0 uses the configured font metrics. Invalid/missing metrics reject before
interaction when a natural active answer requires them. No text/style cascade
into custom children or editors is implied.

The five box patches apply after built-in geometry/state paint. Card gap patches
only the actual answer row; outer gap remains0. Explicit disabled opacity paint
can be overridden without reenabling interaction. Ancestor opacity multiplies.
Existing indicator/shortcut styles still patch their default elements; content
style patches its wrapper, including around custom content. New card patches do
not leak into those children.

Unknown masks, nonfinite active values, invalid text styles and conflicting
fixed card height reject before bindings, input reduction, callbacks or model
mutation. Fixed height must be at least the resolved minimum and vertical
padding; no maximum-height field is offered. The checked resolver leaves output
untouched on failure. Entry bool meanings remain legacy: choice returns changed,
container returns accepted/opened, so false on choice is not an error report.

## Minimum bounds and callbacks

Opt-in cards use physical padding around a gap0 row, with a zero-width minimum
spacer and the real answer row. The same outer ID owns paint, pointer/key/AT,
focus ring and semantics; minimum blank area is interactive. FIT cards grow with
long content. Fixed heights may overflow; ancestor clipping clips paint and
pointer hits while semantic layout bounds can extend beyond the visible region.
Very narrow widths/adornments retain ordinary layout overflow. No silent resize.

New indicator/content/shortcut renderers take an immutable extended snapshot:
old choice view, fully resolved numeric metrics and three text views. New wins
over the corresponding old renderer. Old receives its unchanged legacy view;
custom numeric values are never misrepresented as a legacy size. All descriptors
are copied before children run. Callbacks run once in existing order and derived
namespaces; shortcut OFF suppresses both new and old shortcut children. Snapshot,
function and userdata are borrowed for synchronous submission only. Children
balance boxes, avoid model mutation/input dispatch, and do not retain views.
Drawn strings survive completed-frame consumption. Caller avoids namespace
collisions, as for existing composition. No retained attachment or dispatch layer.

Frozen source reference: `87d10ae5`,
`crates/component/src/questionnaire/components.rs:85-253,297-364,527-678,772-975`.
This covers bounded container/card/numeric/default-choice text geometry. Input
left-only padding, independent editor paint/shaping, Button/trailing actions,
Form role, arbitrary Styled inheritance and binding facades remain separate
required followups. All78 entries remain; this is not full Questionnaire parity.

# Questionnaire keyboard policies

Include `cui_questionnaire_keyboard.h` with a matching library revision. These
additive entry points preserve the existing options/model layout. They provide
keyboard policy, not a snapshot/event facade. Existing APIs remain available.

Zero/NULL preserves the corresponding legacy entry point. The three enum fields
normalize unknown values independently to legacy. A copied options record carries
no callbacks, strings, allocation, platform types or retained caller pointers.
Root policy is copied before capture and applies to ordered input routing, including
confirmation routed through an editor. Existing choice parts inherit the matching
active root's shortcut mode; explicit standalone overrides are documented in the
header. The host must keep per-part and root activation policies consistent.
Legacy matching-root inheritance predates this API: the active root's
`numeric_shortcuts` supplies ordinary choice badges even when the choice's own
boolean differs. A zero-valued extension root preserves that behavior in both
directions. Standalone choices retain their own boolean; a non-NULL explicit
choice keyboard record follows the override rules in the header.

Frozen source `87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34` defaults shortcuts to
absent (`base/questionnaire/state.rs:121,343–348`). OFF must suppress both key
activation and the default/custom shortcut adornment. It does not disable actual
choice controls. Letters/numbers retain enabled-position ordering.

Source adjacent-answer restoration applies only from item focus
(`state.rs:894–975`). The opt-in item-focus policy preserves selected-answer
restoration there, but enters the first/last enabled answer from action/root focus.
Legacy action-focus restoration remains unchanged. The standalone helper takes an
explicit item ID because the existing helper does not know that container's ID.

Source keyboard submission uses the host platform secondary modifier. The new
record explicitly chooses Control, Meta or unmodified-only; it never guesses the
platform. Exact modifier matching preserves rejection of Shift/Alt combinations.
Bare Enter still requires a filled focused answer. Automatic-root legacy accepts
Control or Meta; standalone legacy preserves its existing explicit modifier input.

Nested roots currently share a context route stack. Each begin captures before
pushing itself; therefore an outer root may inspect events before a later inner
begin. A stack is not evidence of nearest-root dispatch isolation. The
characterization test with distinct states confirms that outer capture can consume
the key before the inner root sees it. Existing consumption order remains. No
nesting architecture change is part of this slice; source capture ordering must
be measured before claiming parity.

The focused fixture covers queued keys for OFF/letters/numbers, item versus action
focus, host modifiers, independent enum fallback, IME/repeat/modifier guards,
standalone helper policies, real badge pixels, semantic names, custom renderer
calls, zero-policy pixel/semantics/callback equivalence, and pointer/accessibility
activation with shortcuts OFF. Existing Styled regressions cover editor ownership,
disabled transitions and delayed confirmation. Validation uses strict Release via
the private headless wrapper, focused WASI, compiled C guide and C++ header, and
actual pinned repository formatting after the final source edit. Canonical registration,
generated distributions, metadata and skills remain integrator-owned.

## Consumer composition

The host chooses its submit modifier explicitly. Submit the policy once on the
root; ordinary choice parts inherit its shortcut mode. OFF suppresses shortcut
adornments (including custom shortcut callbacks) and letter/number activation,
while pointer, focused-control keys and accessibility activation remain enabled.
A standalone choice override only changes that part's display; it does not change
root-wide shortcut routing. Keep root and part policies consistent.

```c
#include "cui/cui_questionnaire_keyboard.h"
void questionnaire_page(cui_context *ui, const cui_theme *theme,
                        cui_questionnaire_state *state) {
    const cui_questionnaire_keyboard_options keyboard = {
        .shortcuts = CUI_QUESTIONNAIRE_SHORTCUT_OFF,
        .answer_entry = CUI_QUESTIONNAIRE_ENTRY_ITEM_FOCUS_ONLY,
        .submit = CUI_QUESTIONNAIRE_SUBMIT_CONTROL
    };
    const cui_questionnaire_options options = {.width = 300};
    if (!cui_questionnaire_begin_with_keyboard(ui, 100, theme, state, options, &keyboard))
        return;
    size_t item = state->current;
    if (cui_questionnaire_item_begin(ui, 101, state, item, options)) {
        cui_questionnaire_heading(ui, 102, theme, state, item, options);
        for (size_t choice = 0; choice < state->items[item].choice_count; ++choice)
            (void)cui_questionnaire_choice_control(ui, 1000 + choice, theme, state,
                                                   item, choice, options);
        cui_questionnaire_part_end(ui);
    }
    cui_questionnaire_end(ui);
}
```

Definitions and caller workspace still outlive the retained state. The record is
copied synchronously and may be stack allocated. IDs must remain stable and unique
in the host tree; the example uses a single active item. Root capture uses previous
frame bindings, so draw an initial frame before sending keyboard input. Standalone
helpers do not inherit root options; pass their record explicitly. Their LEGACY
shortcut mode preserves both `numbers=false` (letters) and `numbers=true`.

The worker fixture registers the focused test and compiles this example without
changing canonical build files. The private WASI driver extends the existing
suite list in memory; canonical registration is an integrator follow-up. This
slice does not complete the family's payload, compound presentation, localization,
Form semantic or general styling gaps.

The interactive gallery exposes an Enable choice shortcuts control alongside the existing numeric-hints switch. Its actual C composition uses `cui_questionnaire_begin_with_keyboard` and the matching standalone shortcut helper, so OFF applies to both rendering and activation. The copyable usage example shows explicit OFF. Headless `tests/web/test_questionnaire_shortcuts_gallery.py` checks actual Tab focus, ignored shortcut keys, default/custom hint suppression, letter/number selection and genuine touch selection while shortcuts are off. It does not establish the remaining snapshot, localization, style or binding surfaces.

# Questionnaire typed observation

Include `cui_questionnaire_observer.h`. Rebuild every consumer/binding with matching
headers and library: `cui_questionnaire_state` gained one observer pointer. Legacy
initialization clears it; reset retains it. Legacy event/user fields, synchronous
callback mutations, reducer return values and routing stay in place. No new input
dispatch architecture or foreign-language callback bridge is provided.

The observer is persistent but entirely caller-owned. Attach only after model init
and while idle. A zero-initialized observer and immutable frame-array/arenas remain
alive until fully detached and the outermost model/Styled operation returns.
The handler/user pointers are retained across calls; their pointees stay host-owned.
All records/text/frame regions and observer/model/schema/editor storage must be
disjoint. Overlap/provenance and idle attachment to an unobserved model are caller
preconditions, not runtime-detected safety guarantees. Do not move/copy attached
models/observers, reinitialize them, or overwrite private bookkeeping.

## Basic lifetime

This bounded recorder copies a name into separate host storage for retention. It
never retains a callback pointer or a shallow payload view. Call `recorder_start`
after model init, keep the recorder at the same address, and detach while idle
before its storage goes away. Example capacities are application bounds; payload
failure is explicit, never silently truncated.

```c
#include "cui/cui_questionnaire_observer.h"
#include <string.h>
typedef struct {
    cui_questionnaire_observer observer;
    cui_questionnaire_observer_frame frames[3];
    cui_questionnaire_item_snapshot records[3][16];
    cui_str choices[3][64];
    char text[3][2048];
    char last_answer_item[128];
    bool name_too_large;
    cui_questionnaire_payload_status last_payload_status;
} questionnaire_recorder;

static void record_questionnaire(void *user, const cui_questionnaire_observation *event) {
    questionnaire_recorder *recorder = user;
    recorder->last_payload_status = event->payload_status;
    if (event->kind != CUI_QUESTIONNAIRE_ANSWER_CHANGED ||
        event->payload_status != CUI_QUESTIONNAIRE_PAYLOAD_READY)
        return;
    cui_str name = event->answer.name;
    recorder->name_too_large = name.length >= sizeof recorder->last_answer_item;
    if (recorder->name_too_large)
        return;
    memcpy(recorder->last_answer_item, name.data, name.length);
    recorder->last_answer_item[name.length] = 0;
}

cui_questionnaire_observer_result recorder_start(cui_questionnaire_state *state,
                                                questionnaire_recorder *recorder) {
    /* recorder must already be zero-initialized and neither attached nor in flight. */
    for (size_t i = 0; i < 3; ++i)
        recorder->frames[i].workspace = (cui_questionnaire_snapshot_workspace){
            .items = recorder->records[i], .item_capacity = 16,
            .choices = recorder->choices[i], .choice_capacity = 64,
            .text = recorder->text[i], .text_capacity = sizeof recorder->text[i]
        };
    return cui_questionnaire_observer_attach(state, &recorder->observer, 900,
        recorder->frames, 3,
        (cui_questionnaire_observation_handler){record_questionnaire, recorder});
}
```

## Delivery and copied payloads

Each active legacy emission produces one synchronous typed attempt **before**
the original legacy callback. The typed callback is observational: copy bytes and
update unrelated host bookkeeping only. Do not mutate/submit model/UI, invoke
validation or observer configuration, or destroy/rebind resources from it. Legacy callbacks retain
existing model mutations, nested calls and replacement of event/user. Subsequent
legacy follow-up eligibility is checked as before. Silent setters/reset remain
silent; attaching does not synthesize changes or lifecycle events.

CurrentChanged copies optional previous/current names; AnswerChanged copies item
name, effective choices/freeform and status. Presence booleans distinguish absent
from empty names. Completed and Submit share one submission frozen after successful
validation, before either legacy callback. If Completed edits, disables, resets,
replaces the legacy handler or performs a guarded nested submit, the outer Submit
still carries the same original data. Nested submissions receive different frames.
Repeated successful submit still emits Submit; failed validation emits no success
pair. No copied editor draft, custom validation-message or schema-edit event exists.

Snapshots follow the existing copy-out rules: schema order, selected enabled choice
values in definition order, skipped/unanswered entries included, disabled items
omitted from submission, copied strings with length-excluded NUL terminators.
Current model UTF-8 validation rejects embedded NUL. Frame arenas and observation
views are borrowed through their callback only. A shallow structure copy is not a
deep retained event; copy all required strings/arrays into separate host storage.
The outer pair's backing frame is pinned through the entire outer submit, including
intervening legacy callbacks, but its stack-local observation pointer is not retained.

Metadata maps current/answer to CHANGE, completed to COMMIT, submit to SUBMIT;
family `kind` preserves exact meaning. The nonzero application target does not
register an element. Origin is UNKNOWN and evidence flags are zero even for actual
pointer/key/accessibility/input/timer paths. A Base hook has no proven causal
frame/index/activation; do not infer one from nearby queued events. Genuine Styled
metadata forwarding would require a separately audited API.

## Bounds, detach and errors

One frame is reserved per active emission; a submit pair holds one across both
notifications. Nested legacy emitting calls use extra frames. NO_FRAME gives
honest empty copied fields; CAPACITY gives exact requirements and unchanged arena
bytes; OVERFLOW and defensive INVALID give empty data/zero requirements. Failure
is shared by an outer pair, with no retry against later mutated state. There is no
allocation, event replay, legacy event loss, rollback or altered model return.
A missing typed handler counts attempts but performs no copy/delivery. Statistics
count active attempts, deliveries and failed payloads, saturating with an overflow
flag. Removed/inactive observers do not count later emissions.

Idle detach returns OK. Detach from a legacy callback returns BUSY to report pending
removal: later typed attempts stop immediately, but existing frames remain pinned
until final in-flight return. BUSY does not reject removal. Reattach/reconfigure
while known in-flight returns BUSY, including a different observer attempting to
replace a pending detached one. Already attached idle state returns ATTACHED.
Once drained, the model association clears; the caller can attach again while idle.
No destruction notification is emitted. Keep all users/frame/model/schema/editor
storage alive through outer return and renderer consumption before freeing it.
There is no arbitrary destruction guard or concurrent-use contract.

The focused tests compare attached/unattached legacy mutation traces, immutable
outer versus nested submit data, event/user replacement, live choose/skip follow-up,
capacity/depth errors, detach pinning, copied names including empty identity,
ordered input plus actual key/pointer/accessibility routes and delayed timer.
Existing Questionnaire, Styled, keyboard and snapshot suites remain regressions.
Canonical CMake compiles this example and a C++ header consumer. The worker
fixture delegates to those canonical registrations. The pinned WASI runner includes
the observer suite and fingerprints its private header. The all-in-one distribution
runs the same focused observer regression suite; direct observer, legacy model,
keyboard and snapshot implementation entries have strict declaration checks. General event/binding uniformity, physical AT
acceptance and the family's presentation/localization/Form/style gaps remain open.

# Questionnaire named text presentation

Include `cui_questionnaire_presentation.h` with its matching library revision.
Title, Description and ChoiceDescription use independent explicit text options;
there is no style cascade or state/options ABI extension. Existing heading stays
unchanged. Zero named options extract its title/description text metrics; two
separate wrappers do not recreate heading's internal gap automatically.

`TEXT_TOKENS` opts into default token tiers for four legacy sizes: title
14/20,16/24,18/28,20/28 and secondary 12/16,12/16,14/20,16/24
(XSmall,Small,Medium,Large). Title is medium weight; secondary normal. It adds
an item-gap spacer after title when schema description is absent. Shared XS–9XL
uses proportional title 1.125/secondary.875 font and line scale, a CUI extension.
Explicit masked refinements win, including natural line height zero, normal
style and transparent color. Font family IDs require matching host font support.

Title/Description check schema existence, independently of current/disabled
status. Use a successful Item container to gate them, as below. Empty schema
Description omits its wrapper unless explicit visible content or child exists.
ChoiceDescription takes explicit content without state. Error retains legacy
current-item/invalid gating and one Alert named by localized model error.
Custom decorative content replaces paint, not the Alert name. Token Error adds
an 8px top spacer and secondary typography; zero Error preserves legacy paint.

```c
#include <cui/cui_questionnaire_presentation.h>
static void custom_description(cui_context *ui, cui_id id,
                                const cui_questionnaire_text_view *view, void *user) {
    (void)user;
    cui_begin_box(ui, id, (cui_box){.width = -1});
    cui_text_ex(ui, view->text, view->font_size, view->color,
                view->line_height, view->style);
    cui_end_box(ui);
}
void draw_question(cui_context *ui, const cui_theme *theme,
                   cui_questionnaire_state *state, size_t item) {
    cui_questionnaire_options base = {0};
    cui_questionnaire_text_options text = {.policy = CUI_QUESTIONNAIRE_TEXT_TOKENS};
    if (cui_questionnaire_item_begin(ui, 100, state, item, base)) {
        (void)cui_questionnaire_title_ex(ui, 101, theme, state, item, base, text);
        text.render_child = custom_description;
        (void)cui_questionnaire_description_ex(ui, 102, theme, state, item, base, text);
        /* Compose existing choices/input here with the same state. */
        text.render_child = NULL;
        (void)cui_questionnaire_error_ex(ui, 103, theme, state, item, base, text);
        cui_questionnaire_part_end(ui);
    }
}
```

Masked visible strings accept explicit empty, require valid UTF-8 without NUL,
and remain borrowed through completed-frame draw use. Descriptors are copied at
entry. Callback/view/user are borrowed synchronously and not retained; callback
must balance child boxes and must not mutate state, route input or close owner.
Use the supplied child namespace and avoid collisions with application IDs.
A child wins over visible override; resolved view retains that override for use
by the child. Invalid active options reject before output or callbacks. True
means accepted, including omission, not a transaction over child/layout errors.

No model events, validation or editor flushing occurs from these parts. This is
bounded text composition, not arbitrary Styled: card/container/input/Button,
action trailing layout, Form role and full binding presentation remain separate.

The focused unit suite compares independent extracted pre-change text bodies to
zero presentation using draw values, memberwise Alert checks and actual software
pixels. The deterministic test glyph provider proves metrics/style/color transport,
not native font shaping. Token tables, first-line line boxes, long copy wrapping,
explicit empty/custom precedence, descriptor snapshots and passive routed
pointer/key/AT behavior are covered. Native host screen-reader acceptance and
browser presentation controls are not claimed by this slice.

Canonical builds register this implementation with the existing Questionnaire
module. Standalone `CUI_QUESTIONNAIRE_IMPLEMENTATION` includes the presentation
implementation needed by legacy Error; the new
`CUI_QUESTIONNAIRE_PRESENTATION_IMPLEMENTATION` entry redirects once to that same
module. Both require matching generated headers. `CUI_IMPLEMENTATION_ALL` also
includes it. Packaged C headers do not provide language-builder callbacks.

The gallery's independent named-text picker offers extracted legacy parts,
localized token text, explicit 17px/26px refinement and decorative Error content.
The default still uses the existing heading/Error helpers, and the progress
picker remains independent. The long localized description is example content,
not a translation service. Real WASM desktop/touch checks validate through Next,
retain one localized Alert ID across mode changes, verify decorative paint and
bounds, compile all selected C11 examples and navigate choices/back. Presentation
mode changes emit no model events. This evidence does not cover the deferred
container/card/input/action layout or a language-builder presentation facade.

# Questionnaire progress presentation

Include `cui/cui_questionnaire_progress.h`. `cui_questionnaire_progress_ex` adds
explicit progress text/children without changing legacy options or state layout.
Zero progress options preserve legacy drawing and semantics. Rebuild matching
headers/library to use the added symbol. This is bounded progress presentation,
not a full family typography cascade or language-builder facade.

```c
#include "cui/cui_questionnaire_progress.h"
#include <stdio.h>
/* Application-owned storage must survive completed-frame consumption. */
typedef struct { char label[96]; } progress_text;
bool paint_progress(cui_context *ui, const cui_theme *theme,
                    const cui_questionnaire_state *state, progress_text *storage) {
    size_t position = cui_questionnaire_position(state);
    size_t current = position == SIZE_MAX ? 0 : position + 1;
    int n = snprintf(storage->label, sizeof storage->label, "Frage %zu von %zu",
                     current, cui_questionnaire_total(state));
    if (n < 0 || (size_t)n >= sizeof storage->label)
        return false;
    return cui_questionnaire_progress_ex(
        ui, 71, theme, state, (cui_questionnaire_options){0},
        (cui_questionnaire_progress_options){
            .fields = CUI_QUESTIONNAIRE_PROGRESS_LABEL,
            .label = {storage->label, (size_t)n},
            .text = {.fields = CUI_QUESTIONNAIRE_TEXT_SIZE |
                               CUI_QUESTIONNAIRE_TEXT_LINE_HEIGHT,
                     .font_size = 14, .line_height = 20}});
}
```

LABEL replaces the accessible name and default visible sentence. VISIBLE replaces
only visible text. A custom `render_child` replaces visible content altogether;
its callback receives current/total and resolved text metrics. Numeric progress
semantics always come from enabled item position/total, never supplied text.
No current means zero. This is not completion percentage. The role remains a
passive progress bar, with minimum zero and maximum enabled total.

The callback runs once inside the full-width progress wrapper, with a stable,
nonzero child namespace distinct from the root semantic ID. Like existing child
composition, callers avoid collisions with their other IDs; derived IDs are not
a global collision-free allocator. Balance child boxes;
do not close the wrapper, mutate the model or dispatch input. View/user are
borrowed for the call, not retained. Use the view's metrics explicitly when
rendering text; CUI does not inherit an implicit text cascade. Ordinary decorative
children avoid duplicate progress nodes; custom interactive descendants own their
separate semantics. No model events, validation/editor flush or input consumption
are added by this helper.

Masked empty text is explicit empty, including `{NULL,0}`. Empty VISIBLE can hide
the sentence while keeping an accessible label/numbers. Normally keep LABEL
meaningful. Strings require valid UTF-8 with no embedded NUL and remain borrowed
through completed-frame draw/semantic consumption. Descriptors are copied on
entry; root options do not publish these strings or refinements to other parts.
Unmasked values are ignored. The host formats/pluralizes labels with public
position/total queries before submission; no locale registry is retained.

Text masks independently set font size, line height, color and the complete
`cui_text_style`. Explicit normal weight/false flags/family zero/letter spacing
zero work. Font size is finite (0,512]; line height finite [0,4096], zero natural.
Known weight and finite tracking are required. Shaping/font-family fallback and
negative tracking constraints still belong to the host/Core. Source typography
token relationships can be supplied explicitly; legacy sizes and XS..9XL/root
inheritance retain their existing metrics. No arbitrary Styled inheritance,
other-part typography, Core Form role or language presentation API is supplied.

Unknown masks/invalid active values reject before any draw, semantics or callback.
False reports invalid arguments/options. True means accepted submission, not
rollback of custom child layout errors; use normal frame error reporting. Even a
custom child must supply valid masked fields. All existing callbacks and observers
retain their previous behavior.

The focused tests use deterministic metrics and a test-only rectangular-glyph
coverage provider with the actual software renderer. This proves layout/style/
color transport and pixels, not FreeType shaping, system fonts or physical AT.
Headless actual-WASM gallery tests additionally cover opt-in localized/short/custom/
text-metric modes, stable numeric semantics, unchanged default presentation,
compiled selected C snippets and desktop pointer/touch model advancement. This
does not establish native font shaping or full family browser parity.

# Questionnaire snapshots

Include `cui_questionnaire_snapshots.h` and rebuild with the matching library.
These pure Base helpers copy effective answers into caller-owned item records,
choice descriptors and text storage. They do not validate, submit, call handlers,
synchronize an editor draft, service pending confirmation or change the model.
They do not provide event observation or freeze a legacy callback sequence.

Measure reports item/choice counts and text bytes including one NUL per copied
string. Copy always measures again, then checks every capacity before writing to
any workspace region. CAPACITY returns exact current requirements and an empty
new output while preserving all prior workspace bytes. INVALID/UNKNOWN_ITEM/
OVERFLOW clear requirements and output. Null mandatory output pointers are INVALID.
No truncation occurs, including when a positive text capacity is insufficient.

All supplied workspace regions, required/output records and model/schema/editor
storage must be mutually disjoint. This is a caller precondition; arbitrary pointer
overlap/provenance is not detected. No concurrent model mutation is allowed during
a call. Successful workspace reuse invalidates older snapshots; failed copies do
not. A structure copy alone does not clone its pointed-to strings/arrays, and a
memcpy-relocated arena does not automatically rebase them.

## Caller-owned retained copy

This example retains a submission independently of subsequent model edits and
source definitions. The bounded application workspace may be too small; the result
and measured requirements tell the caller that explicitly. The saved object must
stay at the same address while its snapshot is in use. Publishing only after a
successful copy preserves the previous saved record and its storage on failure.

```c
#include "cui/cui_questionnaire_snapshots.h"
typedef struct {
    cui_questionnaire_item_snapshot items[16];
    cui_str choices[64];
    char text[4096];
    cui_questionnaire_submission_snapshot snapshot;
} saved_questionnaire;

cui_questionnaire_snapshot_result save_questionnaire(
    const cui_questionnaire_state *state, saved_questionnaire *saved,
    cui_questionnaire_snapshot_requirements *required) {
    if (!saved)
        return CUI_QUESTIONNAIRE_SNAPSHOT_INVALID;
    const cui_questionnaire_snapshot_workspace workspace = {
        .items = saved->items, .item_capacity = 16,
        .choices = saved->choices, .choice_capacity = 64,
        .text = saved->text, .text_capacity = sizeof saved->text
    };
    cui_questionnaire_submission_snapshot next = {0};
    cui_questionnaire_snapshot_result result =
        cui_questionnaire_submission_copy(state, workspace, required, &next);
    if (result == CUI_QUESTIONNAIRE_SNAPSHOT_OK)
        saved->snapshot = next;
    return result;
}
```

For one item use `answer_measure`/`answer_copy`, with at least one workspace item
record and a separate `cui_questionnaire_item_snapshot` output. That record includes
a copied identity name, original schema index, status, disabled flag and answer.
Individual disabled items retain name/status but expose an empty answer. Submission
copies omit disabled items, include unanswered and skipped enabled items, and use
schema order. They are available before validation/completion; copying a submission
does not certify that it is valid.

Selected enabled choice values use definition order, not selection order. Labels,
descriptions and validation messages are not included. Freeform comes from the
retained effective answer; an unsynchronized editor draft is excluded. Whitespace
normalization remains the model's responsibility. `has_freeform=false` has a NULL
zero-length string; zero choices/submissions have NULL array pointers.

Text is packed as each name, its choices, then present freeform, with an appended
NUL for each string. cui_str lengths exclude appended NUL; empty names/values
still consume one byte. The current model rejects embedded NUL in its UTF-8
validation, so initialized valid models cannot supply embedded-NUL values.
Use length-aware consumers. There is no deduplication or borrowed schema string in
a successful snapshot. Buffers survive model reset, edits and source teardown for
as long as the caller keeps the snapshot workspace alive and unchanged.

`query_copy` needs no workspace. It reports enabled progress, current schema index,
action visibility, confirmability and completion. No current enabled item gives
SIZE_MAX item/position, progress zero and false action/confirmability flags. A
filled invalid answer remains confirmable; this flag means answered/skipped, not
validated. Visibility reflects model policy, not disabled ancestors or host-omitted
buttons. Failed query resets the same sentinels.

Existing model bounds remain: 4096 items and default4096/max1MiB input answer bytes.
Snapshot counts/string totals and record extents use checked size_t arithmetic,
without a new fixed choice/string cap. The arithmetic test probes private helpers
at SIZE_MAX boundaries without forging a publicly valid model or reading fictitious
string storage. Portable C cannot validate arbitrary source pointer provenance.

Worker validation includes strict Release headless model/Styled regressions,
focused snapshot tests, compiled C example and C++ header, plus focused WASI. Pure
copy-out has no pixels; actual WASM execution verifies portable buffer behavior.
No generic bridge or binding API is added. Snapshot query/copy support does not
complete Questionnaire's event payload, compound presentation, localization, Form
semantic or broader style gaps.

# RadioGroup

`cui_radio_group` supplies a bounded collection of up to 64 radio options. Each
item has a stable, unique, nonzero `cui_id`, a label and an optional disabled flag.
The application owns one selected ID (`0` means no selection) and persistent
`cui_radio_group_state`. Existing `cui_radio` and `cui_radio_ex` remain compatible.

```c
#include <cui/cui_radio_group.h>

typedef struct {
    cui_id selected;
    cui_radio_group_state radio;
} settings;

static void accept_delivery(void *user, cui_id requested) {
    settings *model = user;
    model->selected = requested;
}

void delivery_settings(cui_context *ui, const cui_theme *theme, settings *model) {
    cui_radio_group_item items[] = {
        {cui_id_from(ui, "standard"), cui_string("Standard"), false},
        {cui_id_from(ui, "priority"), cui_string("Priority"), false},
        {cui_id_from(ui, "express"), cui_string("Express unavailable"), true}};
    cui_radio_group(ui, cui_id_from(ui, "delivery"), theme, items, 3,
        &model->selected, &model->radio,
        (cui_radio_group_options){.name = cui_string("Delivery options"),
            .vertical = true, .on_change = accept_delivery, .change_user = model});
}
```

With a callback, each validated request invokes it once; the group does not write
the selected model. Accept by updating the selected ID synchronously, or reject by
leaving it unchanged. Without a callback, the group updates the selected ID.
Activating the already selected option produces no callback. Requests are resolved
before any option is painted, so accepted and rejected state produce coherent
checked snapshots and selected marks in the same frame. Multiple queued navigation
events advance in order. A callback must not change the item array or destroy its
model during the call. Labels/items are borrowed for the synchronous frame build;
retain ordinary Core text lifetimes through rendering as required by the host.

Arrow keys move focus and request selection, skipping disabled items and wrapping.
Home and End choose the first and last enabled option. Enter/Space activate the
focused option. One enabled item is in the Tab sequence: the focused item while
focus is within the group, otherwise the selected enabled item or first enabled
item. `skip_tab` removes all group options from that sequence while pointer focus
and explicit keyboard focus remain available. Disabled groups have no tab stop and
reject activation. A removed or newly disabled focused item moves focus to an
enabled fallback, without inventing a selection callback. An empty/all-disabled
group clears its own focus. External focus is retained.

Selection IDs are stable across reorder. A removed selection stays caller-owned
and paints no selected option; a disabled selected option remains checked but
cannot activate. The application decides whether to clear or replace those model
values. This preserves controlled callback semantics during collection changes.
Invalid inputs (duplicate/zero IDs, more than 64 items, invalid sizes or gaps) return
`valid=false` before registering the collection. No heap allocation is performed.

The collection emits RADIOGROUP semantics with orientation/name/required/invalid;
children emit RADIO with parent, checked, disabled, position and set size. These
are portable snapshots, not a native OS accessibility bridge. Shared cursor and
interaction queries can be applied to stable item IDs after submission.

The component supports four legacy control sizes and all 14 design sizes,
including theme density. It uses the existing selection mark renderer and the
same indicator/font/theme colors as the standalone radio. The separate base API
registers/reduces behavior without styled layout; a custom renderer must submit
boxes with the same IDs. Do not register another interactive radio with the same
ID after calling the base API. The reference's richer child composition, tooltip
builder, spring mark animation and unrestricted style refinement are not provided
by this initial group API. Full Radio-family source parity is not claimed.

The headless test asserts same-frame selection paint, semantic set relationships,
callback rejection/acceptance, selected no-op, keyboard wrap/disabled skipping,
queued navigation, one tab stop, touch drag/cancel suppression, focus cleanup,
bounded validation and all 14 design sizes at two densities. The browser suite
uses actual mouse, keyboard and CDP touch events on the gallery's visible options.
Chromium touch emulation is not evidence from a physical mobile device.
