# Optional regex allocation oracle: CI failure and validation

The optional-regex job in CI run 38557271424 failed at `backends/regex/src/tests.rs:362` with `match allocated \\Aabc\\z` (observed 2, expected 0). The old test allocator used process-wide `TRACK`, `CALLS`, and `FAIL` atomics. `--test-threads=1` serializes Rust test functions, but it does not prevent other harness or runtime threads from allocating while the oracle measures `matching`. Those unrelated calls could enter both the zero-allocation count and the fault-injection sequence.

The allocator probe now uses a constant-initialized thread-local `Cell` for the measurement flag, allocation count, failure position, and live-byte balance. The `matching` assertion still requires exactly zero allocations on the calling thread. Fault injection still rejects each measured allocation position on that same thread, and the live-byte comparisons still check that failed preparations release their allocations. The new regression allocates on a worker thread while the test thread measures zero, then allocates on the test thread and verifies a positive count.

Validation used the exact pinned Rust 1.85.1 toolchain and existing verified crate archives in `/dev/shm/cui-next33-regex-native`:

```sh
python scripts/build_regex.py --cache /dev/shm/cui-next33-regex-native --toolchain /dev/shm/cui-next33-regex-toolchain/rust-1.85.1
CARGO_HOME=/dev/shm/cui-next33-regex-native/cargo RUSTC=/dev/shm/cui-next33-regex-toolchain/rust-1.85.1/bin/rustc /dev/shm/cui-next33-regex-toolchain/rust-1.85.1/bin/cargo test --offline --locked --release --manifest-path /dev/shm/cui-next33-regex-native/source/Cargo.toml --target-dir /dev/shm/cui-next33-regex-native/target -- --test-threads=1
```

Build succeeded; both tests passed. The same locked offline test command also passed ten consecutive runs with `--test-threads=2`. The vendored `regex-automata` emits its existing unused-method warning; no new warnings were observed from `cui-regex`.

# Checked accessor callers

Dock and table components check model getter results before reading output values.
Visibility and render callbacks can change the model between traversal steps; a
failed getter skips the unavailable item or reports an error where traversal is
required to complete.

Dock lifecycle capture builds its next snapshot in temporary storage. Allocation
failure returns `CUI_DOCK_CAPACITY`; invalidated traversal returns
`CUI_DOCK_INVALID`. Both preserve the previously pending snapshot and clear the
capture guard. Callback edits to the model itself are not rolled back. Capture
sets the existing dispatch guard while evaluating callbacks to prevent reentrant
capture or dispatch from publishing incomplete data.

`tests/unit/test_release_accessors.c` uses explicit checks that remain active in
optimized builds. It covers unchanged outputs on failed getters, visibility
callbacks removing panels, lifecycle snapshot preservation after callback edits
and allocation failure, and table header/label callbacks shrinking bound data.
On GNU-compatible ELF linkers, define `CUI_TEST_ALLOCATOR` and link with
`-Wl,--wrap=malloc` to enable the allocation failure case. Other platforms can run
the remaining cases without this definition.

This is focused traversal hardening, not a guarantee that arbitrary mutation of
all borrowed application data during callbacks is supported.

# Prerelease preparation: v0.1.0-alpha.3

This document prepares **v0.1.0-alpha.3**. It does not establish publication,
a frozen release revision or validated release artifacts. The current batch adds
civil DateTime selection, date-only picker actions, Questionnaire observations,
snapshots, keyboard policies, progress, presentation and checked geometry, plus
explicit Popover anchors/arrows. SDL3 and the browser gallery gain bounded
analytic mesh consumers with pixel and failure-path evidence. The gallery has
actual desktop/touch controls and compiled usage examples for the new options.

The batch also includes Avatar metrics, identity palettes, SVG placeholders and
typed activation observers; reusable VideoPlayer defaults, seek icons,
player-only browser fullscreen and an audible sample; and optional bounded
native video/audio and macOS Speech host integrations. Injected Apple fixtures
are separate from physical microphone, permission and recognizer acceptance.
Linux/Windows speech recognizers and broader native media support remain gaps.

Rebuild consumers with matching headers and libraries: the Questionnaire state
and several by-value options changed since alpha.2. Read the current binding
coverage for C-only options; source packaging does not imply equivalent foreign
APIs or registry publication. All 78 baseline families remain present, with
feature-level omissions documented. Full parity is unfinished. Final integrated
validation, release source freeze and artifact checks remain pending. Describe
the actual frozen revision and supported subset in the published release notes.

Published alpha.2 (`v0.1.0-alpha.2`, Python `0.1.0a2`) remains immutable. This document prepares the next development version, not another publication claim.

Keep alpha.1 (`v0.1.0-alpha.1`, Python `0.1.0a1`) and any associated published
assets immutable. This version update does not retag or replace alpha.1. No
package-name ownership, registry authentication, trusted publisher configuration,
or cross-platform native compatibility is established by changing metadata.
Publish a coherent release after each major completed body of work; batch related
commits together. Do not turn each implementation commit into a release.

## Version and source freeze

| Surface | Prepared version |
| --- | --- |
| Repository/GitHub release | `v0.1.0-alpha.3` |
| CMake ABI/base project version | `0.1.0` |
| Public C `CUI_VERSION` | `0.1.0-alpha.3` |
| Python / wheel metadata | `0.1.0a3` |
| npm / Cargo | `0.1.0-alpha.3` |
| Go proxy version | `v0.1.0-alpha.3` |
| Public nested Go module tag | `bindings/go/v0.1.0-alpha.3` |

The Go module is `github.com/mattmezza/cui/bindings/go`; its public Git tag needs
the subdirectory prefix. A repository release tag alone does not publish this
module version. See the [Go module tag rules](https://go.dev/ref/mod#vcs-version).
CMake's base version does not promise stable alpha ABI or full binding parity.

Choose one reviewed commit, finish metadata changes, regenerate SDK copies, and
commit them **before** building final assets. Require a clean checkout and clean
source provenance. Record the full commit SHA, compiler/toolchain versions,
architecture, build options, dependency receipts, and validation logs. Do not
publish packages staged from a dirty checkout just because packaging allows it.

The audited tree repeats versions in Python project metadata, wheel backend NAME
and METADATA, npm, Cargo, the Go packaging function, and CI artifact filenames.
The Go `.info` timestamp is derived from the packaged Git revision. Verify it
against the frozen revision before publishing a proxy bundle.
Future version bumps must audit these literals or centralize their generation.
The checker below requires Python 3.11 or newer and deliberately checks the
existing format rather than rewriting binding manifests:

```sh
python scripts/test_release_metadata.py --tag v0.1.0-alpha.3
python scripts/test_release_metadata.py --self-test
```

## Build and review the assets

Use a frozen checkout and an external build/output directory. The commands here
are preparation examples; substitute approved absolute paths. Final artifact
builds must wait until the integrator declares the source frozen.

```sh
cmake -S . -B "$build_dir" -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCUI_BUILD_NATIVE=ON
cmake --build "$build_dir"
python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir "$build_dir"
CUI_PACKAGE_NATIVE=1 python scripts/package_bindings.py python --output "$assets/native-python"
CUI_PACKAGE_NATIVE=1 python scripts/package_bindings.py node --prebuilt --output "$assets/native-node"
python scripts/package_bindings.py go --source-only --output "$assets/go-source"
python scripts/package_bindings.py rust --output "$assets/rust-source"
```

Run SDK generator freshness checks and the installed-package, installed-text, and
binding-run validators against these **exact** outputs. Consult
[PACKAGING.md](PACKAGING.md), [INSTALLED_TEXT_VALIDATION.md](INSTALLED_TEXT_VALIDATION.md),
and [BINDING_NATIVE_RUN.md](BINDING_NATIVE_RUN.md) for commands and prerequisites.
Actual-font checks must pass rather than silently skip. Native Linux tests use
the private Xvfb wrapper; never the maintainer's DISPLAY or Wayland session.
Hardware GPU validation remains explicitly deferred where unsupported by Xvfb.
Source-module validation alone does not validate exported archives.

Review this asset inventory before creating a release:

- A source archive from the frozen tag, with the full modular `include/cui`
  headers, sources, dependency manifest, licenses and build instructions. If
  shipping generated distribution headers, check their freshness separately.
- An installed C library/header bundle labelled with OS, architecture, build
  configuration and shared/static flavor; include runtime dependency information
  and the license/notices for every included component. Test its consumer path.
- The native Linux Python wheel and prebuilt npm tarball, with embedded source
  receipts and build information. Preserve valid original package filenames.
- The Go source proxy `.zip`, `.mod`, `.info` as one labelled archive; the verified
  Rust `.crate`. Source packages can require local native development libraries.
- Release notes, an asset manifest mapping every file to commit/build/flavor,
  SHA256SUMS, dependency/runtime reports, and validation logs or linked CI runs.

Portable and native wheel/npm builds currently have identical basenames and
versions. Keep separate output directories; for GitHub, put them inside clearly
labelled outer archives if publishing both. Never overwrite one flavor with the
other, or rename a wheel's compatibility tag to imply broader portability.
The alpha wheel is host Linux tagged, **not manylinux certified**. Native assets
currently have Linux validation only; label the actual tested architecture,
not “all Linux” or “cross-platform”. Document SDL >= 3.2, FreeType, HarfBuzz and
actual dynamic dependencies from the produced binary. Bundling a bridge does not
bundle all its runtime dependencies. Keep the CUI MIT license and applicable
third-party licenses/notices from `third_party/dependencies.json`; do not reduce
third-party licensing to the top-level MIT license.

## GitHub prerelease publication

The integrator executes these steps after checking the final manifest and tests.
Set `release_sha` to the full frozen commit and `assets` to the reviewed output.
Generate checksums over the final uploaded files, excluding SHA256SUMS itself;
verify them after downloading the draft assets. Avoid uploading duplicate asset
basenames. Prepare release notes describing the tested subset, explicit platform
and runtime requirements, known limitations, and source revision.

```sh
tag=v0.1.0-alpha.3
git tag -a "$tag" "$release_sha" -m "CUI $tag"
git push origin "refs/tags/$tag"
gh release create "$tag" --repo mattmezza/cui --verify-tag --draft --prerelease \
  --title "CUI $tag" --notes-file "$assets/RELEASE_NOTES.md" "$assets/upload/"*
# Inspect/download the draft and verify its manifest and checksums first.
gh release edit "$tag" --repo mattmezza/cui --draft=false --prerelease
```

The source archive served by GitHub and any custom source bundle must resolve to
the same tag SHA. Deploy the website from the corresponding reviewed source and
verify its revision; a successful Pages deployment does not publish any registry
package. Do not move a published tag to accommodate later website corrections.

## Registry gates (separate publication decisions)

At the audited revision, npm has `private: true` and Cargo has `publish = false`.
These intentionally prevent publication. The existing CI packages and tests
local artifacts; there is no registry release workflow. Pages' `id-token: write`
permission is for Pages deployment and proves nothing about registry trust.
`python scripts/test_release_metadata.py --registries` rejects these observable
manifest blockers; passing it would still not prove the gates below.

**PyPI:** establish ownership/availability of `cui-bridge`, approve the distribution
policy and Linux compatibility, and configure the exact GitHub repository,
workflow filename and environment as a trusted publisher. Give only the publish
job `id-token: write`, with environment protections and pinned actions; test a
separate TestPyPI publisher first if desired. Review metadata, license contents,
wheel RECORD, native dependencies and install tests. Current packaging does not
establish manylinux policy compliance. See
[PyPI publisher setup](https://docs.pypi.org/trusted-publishers/adding-a-publisher/)
and [publishing permissions](https://docs.pypi.org/trusted-publishers/using-a-publisher/).

**npm:** verify control of `@cui`, explicitly approve removing `private`, choose
public scoped access, and configure a supported trusted publisher for the exact
workflow/environment. Publish the reviewed native flavor only after deciding its
runtime policy; an alpha should use an explicit `alpha` dist-tag rather than
silently replacing `latest`, e.g. `npm publish reviewed.tgz --access public --tag alpha`.
See [npm trusted publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/) and
[public scoped packages](https://docs.npmjs.com/creating-and-publishing-scoped-public-packages/).
No npm login or ownership check was performed in this audit.

**crates.io:** verify `cui-builders` ownership/availability and publisher
credentials, explicitly approve enabling publication, inspect `cargo package
--list`, and run `cargo publish --dry-run` with the intended features and clean
consumer builds. The current packaging helper uses `--allow-dirty --no-verify
--offline`; a generated crate is not evidence that registry verification passed.
See [Cargo manifest publication controls](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html#the-publish-field).

**Go:** validate a clean external consumer without local `replace` paths, then
push the separate `bindings/go/v0.1.0-alpha.3` tag at the same release SHA if
publishing that module is intended. Check public source retrieval and module
checksums. A local proxy archive is not proof that public proxy ingestion works.

## Corrections and rollback

Keep published versions and tags immutable. Before publishing a draft, replace
incorrect draft assets and regenerate checksums. After publication, document the
problem, use registry-supported deprecation/yank mechanisms when appropriate,
and issue a new version (for example, `v0.1.0-alpha.3`, Python `0.1.0a3`)
with corrected assets. Never retag,
force-push, or upload different bytes under an already published version. A
website rollback can deploy a known-good revision independently while clearly
identifying which library release its instructions describe.

# Resizable panels

This module follows the frozen GPUI Kit 0.7.1 Resizable group, panel, state and
handle sources. Base owns sizing and interaction; components paint the theme's
hairline and engagement indicator. It uses portable C11 and caller-owned bounded
storage, with no platform types or allocation during layout/drag.

```c
cui_resizable_slot slots[3];
cui_resizable_state state;
cui_resizable_state_init(&state, slots, 3); /* once, outside rendering */
cui_resizable_panel panels[] = {
    {.id = 101, .has_initial_size = true, .initial_size = 240,
     .content = sidebar, .content_user = app},
    {.id = 102, .content = main_content, .content_user = app},
};
cui_resizable_options options = cui_resizable_options_default();
options.now_seconds = now_seconds; /* monotonic host time */
options.reduced_motion = reduced_motion;
/* Between begin_frame/end_frame, inside a sized parent: */
cui_resizable(ui, 100, &theme, &state, panels, 2, options);
```

`disabled` freezes handle input while panel content remains usable. Whole-subtree
inert presentation can be selected through the normal group box option.

The state and slots must remain valid through `cui_end_frame`, which writes
retained group/panel bounds. Capacity is fixed on initialization, at most 1024.
Configure core `max_elements`, command and frame capacities for the composed
content as well: slot capacity does not reserve renderer/layout capacity. Slot
fields and measured bounds are exposed for inspection, not arbitrary mutation.
Reusing a state for unrelated simultaneously rendered groups is unsupported.

Horizontal is the default sizing axis; Vertical stacks panes. `extent` sets the
size along that axis, and `cross_size` sets the other dimension, matching the
source group's cross-axis `size` option. Zero selects automatic parent sizing;
box fixed-zero flags permit explicit collapsed dimensions. Group/panel box styles
permit padding, colors and borders, while group direction/gap and panel axis
size/min/max stay managed. Panel callbacks run inside their available content
area and may compose further Resizable groups with distinct IDs and states.
IDs are stable and unique across the UI; reserve the IDs returned by
`cui_resizable_handle_id` for this group.

Default ranges are 100 pixels to the largest float. Explicit initial preferences
are used when a stable panel ID first appears; otherwise remaining space is shared
by flexible panes. Automatic layout reads its actual first-frame panel bounds
before settling the retained model, preserving a 240-pixel sidebar beside a
flexible pane. Later container resizing preserves proportions subject to
constraints, with no second-frame divider jump. Both axes, nested groups and
first-frame full-cross-axis handle bands use real layout rather than root portals.
`hidden` removes a pane's body and adjoining handle while retaining its slot for
later reuse. Visible neighbors receive its available space.

`cui_resizable_sync` is the pure model entry point. It validates declarations before
mutation, preserves state through stable-ID reorder/replacement, and reports
`CAPACITY`, `INVALID` or `INFEASIBLE`. Infeasible minima deliberately overflow;
insufficient maxima deliberately leave unused space. Sizes still respect declared
ranges; `fit_constraints` exposes whether the full extent can be filled. This is
an improvement over the frozen source's unconstrained proportional scaling and
recipient growth beyond its maximum. Core clipping is a caller policy.

Dragging expands the preceding pane by borrowing from subsequent visible panes
in order. Shrinking can cascade into earlier panes at their minima and distributes
freed space to subsequent panes subject to maxima. Pointer capture continues when
the pointer leaves the nine-pixel band; a hard constraint remains fixed until the
pointer returns past that constraint. A primary drag release emits one completed
resize via `state.on_resize`; Escape, cancellation, disabling or removing the
active handle cancels ownership without a completion callback. Completion follows
the initiating primary button, rather than the source's global any-mouse-up hook. The observer and
userdata are borrowed, called synchronously, and must not replace state/storage
or declarations during rendering.

`cui_resizable_resize_panel` uses the same redistribution rules and emits a
completion even when a valid request is constrained to the existing size. The last
visible pane is driven through its previous sibling. Invalid indices/values are
no-ops. `insert`, `remove`, `reset` and `clear` provide explicit lifecycle operations;
keep the next rendered panel declarations in agreement with the state. Reset
preserves size and the currently declared ranges while clearing motion and active
ownership; it does not invalidate a collapsed pane's legal zero minimum. Lifecycle operations do not emit completed user-resize events.

`save` writes sizes in current stable-ID order; store matching IDs alongside them
in application preferences. `restore` validates the whole vector, applies current
constraints/proportions and emits one completion. This is a portable snapshot
boundary, not an implicit filesystem or JSON service.

Pane IDs have passive Group semantics, with an optional `accessibility_label`.
Handles are focusable Separators with the controlled pane ID, current size,
reachable range, visual divider orientation and resize cursor hint. Native/browser
cursor adapters are supplied by core. Horizontal handles accept Left/Right;
Vertical handles accept Up/Down. The step defaults to ten pixels; Shift multiplies
it by ten. Home collapses preceding panes as far as constraints permit; End grows
the controlled pane as far as it can borrow. These keyboard alternatives are a C
accessibility improvement: the frozen source implements pointer resizing only.
`cui_base_resize_handle` submits semantics and consumes actual targeted events
without painting; applications draw its band at the same ID.

The styled divider is a one-pixel theme border line. Its three-pixel rounded pill
has idle/hovered/pressed/dragging lengths 0/20/28/44 and opacities 0/.35/.6/.9.
Supply monotonic `now_seconds`. The persistent indicator retargets from its current
sample, including fade-out,
and requests frames only during motion. Defaults match the source's 120ms
cubic Bézier (.2,0,0,1). `duration_seconds` and `reduced_motion` are explicit host
options because C Theme currently has no shared fast-duration/easing tokens.
Use the constructor for source defaults; zero-initialized options select immediate
motion. `appearance` may replace the paint and can decline to retain the default;
its band uses -1 for a cross dimension that fills the current parent. It does not
replace hit testing, cursor, constraints or ownership.

`cui_resize_handle_rectangles` exposes source nine-pixel straddling and five-pixel
leading/trailing bands with exact outermost-pixel seams. The reusable
`cui_resize_handle_appearance` paints inside an application-owned open band. Unlike
the source's deferred hugging-edge pill, this helper respects ancestor clipping;
a host that needs the outer overhang may compose its own overlay appearance.
Clipping a following panel also clips its straddling handle, as the frozen source's
panel-style warning describes. Do not set panel clipping when that outside half
must remain grabbable; group/ancestor clipping safely constrains the whole layout.

Tracked boundaries: shared theme motion tokens and arbitrary native GPUI drag
payload objects are not built-ins here. Applications retain state and provide
content/callbacks; durable preference storage is host-owned. This implementation
provides substantive sizing, composition, painting and real input, not a claim of
complete native API equivalence.

The gallery demonstrates a small workspace with selectable files, a read-only code preview, contrasting pane backgrounds and live pane dimensions. Drag the divider or focus it and press arrow keys; the browser checks both the retained sizes and the visible pane widths/positions. The vertical mode demonstrates the same model with pane heights.

# Resizable visible-divider regression

The reported failure reproduced on the actual HTTPS gallery revision `44819c1`
at a 1920 × 1080 viewport. Normal desktop mouse and actual Chromium CDP touch
contacts began on the visible divider. Both pane bounds stayed at Explorer
300 px and Editor 600 px, with zero width change after dragging. Before/after
screenshots and pane rectangles were captured in `/tmp/cui-resizable-wide` during
the audit. At 1280 px, the same gestures worked (212 → 260.5 → 300 px), explaining
why previous narrower browser tests missed the problem.

The gallery configured hard maxima of 300 and 600 px while its responsive group
could be wider than their combined 900 px. Both panes reached their maxima. A
split conserves space by transferring it between panels; neither pane had any
capacity to accept the transfer. The model correctly returned `INFEASIBLE` and
preserved the declared constraints. This was gallery configuration, not a mouse
capture or Core touch routing defect.

The Explorer keeps its 80–300 px range. The Editor now has maximum capacity equal
to the responsive group extent, so it can fill and accept transfers at large
widths. Vertical mode starts with a balanced 105/105 px split in its 210 px group;
changing orientation resets that story's split to the appropriate initial sizes.
Resizing within the same orientation retains user state. Both minima remain 80 px,
and normal movement stops at a bound. The underlying `INFEASIBLE` policy, callback
semantics, capture and touch drag priority are unchanged.

## Strict browser checks

Run against a locally built gallery:

```sh
uv run tests/web/test_resizable_drag.py --directory build/web \
  --chromium /path/to/chromium
```

Without `--directory`, the script uses the actual HTTPS gallery. It fails on any
geometry assertion. It uses DOM controls only to configure the story, real mouse
input for desktop cases and `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` for touch cases; it never
calls reducer exports to resize. The touch cases focus the keyboard fallback
with a real touch tap.

The matrix contains 24 independent cases: 390/1280/1920 px viewport widths ×
horizontal/vertical × comfortable/compact density × mouse/touch. Each asserts
actual Explorer growth, Editor shrinkage and boundary movement, enabled content
following horizontal pane widths, disabled geometry remaining fixed, and arrow-key
resizing. The wide cases save actual screenshots before/after. The JSON report
records pane rectangles. Resizable does not expose a size variant or rounded
option in its API/story; these were not fabricated as tested selectors. The
integrator is handling separate gallery option presentation.

## Headless and sanitizer checks

`tests/unit/test_resizable.c` adds eight actual styled split scenes: narrow/wide
extent × both orientations × mouse/touch. They assert changed panel bounds,
content bounds following the panel, conserved total extent, and exactly one
completion callback on release. Existing disabled, keyboard, overlays, clipping,
nested geometry and model constraint tests remain intact. These verify the
responsive configuration contract; the pre-fix production failure is the strict
HTTPS wide browser reproduction, not a claim that valid Core constraint behavior
needed changing.

Warning-enabled native build passed. Full CTest passed 93/94, with only the
root-owned generated-distribution check stale after the public header comment.
Resizable and base-only Resizable passed ASAN/UBSAN (2/2). The fixed local strict
browser matrix passed 24/24; the existing component touch suite passed 42/42
and rendered all 78 stories. Headless Chromium/CDP does not establish physical
mobile device coverage or every consumer's custom appearance/constraint setup.

# Responsive containers

Use `cui/cui_responsive.h` to make layout decisions from a container's current
logical width. Named mobile-first breakpoints resemble familiar utility-class
systems: BASE, SM (640), MD (768), LG (1024), XL (1280), and 2XL (1536).
This header-only utility needs no backend, allocation, or additional library.
Like Tailwind's `md:` and `lg:` variants, `at_least(query, MD/LG)` applies a
policy at that width and above. BASE is the unprefixed/mobile policy. Unlike a
global browser viewport query, each query uses the logical width you pass: the
window, a sidebar, or the remaining main-content area. C layout properties remain
normal designated initializers; no class strings or generated styles are needed.

```c
#include "cui/cui_responsive.h"

/* Product-specific tokens. Keep them ordered; units are logical pixels. */
const cui_breakpoints app_breakpoints = {
    .sm = 560, .md = 720, .lg = 1000, .xl = 1280, .xxl = 1536
};
cui_responsive container = cui_responsive_query(available_width, &app_breakpoints);
bool persistent_nav = cui_responsive_at_least(container, CUI_BREAKPOINT_LG);
/* Selector order: query, breakpoint, base value, expanded value. */
float padding = cui_responsive_value(container, CUI_BREAKPOINT_MD, 12, 24);

cui_begin_box(ui, 100, (cui_box){.width = -1, .row = persistent_nav, .gap = 12});
if (persistent_nav || app.drawer_open)
    submit_navigation(ui, &app);
submit_main(ui, &app, padding);
cui_end_box(ui);
```

Pass NULL for standard thresholds. `at_least` includes the threshold itself.
Thresholds must be finite, nonnegative, and nondecreasing; equal thresholds skip
intermediate classes. Widths must be finite and nonnegative. Invalid input
returns `valid=false`, width zero, and BASE; **every** `at_least` predicate then
returns false, including BASE. Check `valid` before submitting a container.
`value` chooses its base argument for invalid queries. It does not validate the
two caller-provided values or change their units.

For content constraints, `cui_responsive_fits(query, first_min, second_min, gap)`
answers whether two panes can sit side by side. Query the main area's width after
subtracting sidebar and spacing, rather than reusing the window breakpoint:

```c
cui_responsive main = cui_responsive_query(main_inner_width, NULL);
bool row = cui_responsive_fits(main, 260, 260, 12);
cui_begin_box(ui, 200, (cui_box){.width = -1, .row = row, .gap = 12});
submit_summary(ui);
submit_activity(ui);
cui_end_box(ui);
```

`fits` rejects negative/nonfinite minima and gaps. Its comparisons avoid overflow
when adding large finite dimensions. Breakpoints select policy; normal CUI GROW
(`-1`), explicit dimensions, padding, rows and columns perform layout. Recompute
queries each frame, including when only a nested container changes width. Width
queries do not read a window, multiply by display density, or schedule work.

The `examples/responsive_dashboard` fixture keeps one `dashboard_app` state while
resizing: navigation stays beside content at LG, becomes a Menu disclosure below
LG, and the cards stack when their minimum widths no longer fit. The disclosure
occupies layout space above the main content, so it cannot overlap active content
beneath it. Hidden navigation is omitted from submission, including its input and
semantics. Closing it keeps page/account state. Applications that want an overlay
drawer should additionally use the existing modal/overlay scope APIs.

This helper supplies width policies, not CSS media-query or browser-layout parity.
The example and tests cover live container resizing, boundary crossings,
navigation/account callbacks, state preservation, and clicks at removed targets.

## Build and run

Portable assertions, including repeated resizing without a window:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCUI_BUILD_NATIVE=OFF
cmake --build build --target test_responsive test_responsive_dashboard
python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir build -R '^responsive(_dashboard)?$'
```

Interactive native example (requires the existing SDL3, FreeType and HarfBuzz
adapters). Run from the repository root or supply an absolute `--font` path:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build-native -G Ninja -DCUI_REQUIRE_NATIVE=ON -DCUI_BUILD_RESPONSIVE_DASHBOARD=ON
cmake --build build-native --target cui_responsive_dashboard
./build-native/cui_responsive_dashboard --font third_party/inter/Inter-Regular.otf
```

Resize the window through 360, 800 and 1400 logical units, open/close Menu,
choose Reports, and sign in. Page/account/disclosure state survives resizing.
The callback runner owns native event dispatch, including redraw during resize;
the application submits one frame using the current logical container dimensions.
On macOS the target follows the existing bundle configuration and locates its
bundled Inter font. `--frames N --capture PATH.bmp` provides a finite smoke run;
automated runs must use an isolated display rather than the desktop session.

The WASI harness also registers the responsive policy and dashboard interaction
suites. With the pinned Zig/wasmtime tools:

```sh
uv run scripts/test_wasi.py --suite responsive --suite responsive_dashboard
```

Omit `--suite` to exercise all portable suites. WASI validates portable layout and
interactions; it does not emulate a browser or native resize event loop.

# Root

`cui_root` is a caller-owned, per-window content and overlay host. Zero-initialize it before `cui_root_init`, and call `cui_root_dispose` before reinitializing. Base owns the root and its ordered plugin registry. Applications register plugins during initialization, then create one root and a separate plugin-instance array for each window. Registration uses an application-defined numeric key: registering the key again replaces its factory in place for future roots, while existing roots keep their snapshot and state. Factories receive a per-window pointer and return caller-owned state that must outlive the root.

Each frame runs plugin `prepare` callbacks in registration order, then `style` callbacks, then applies an optional instance style refinement. Set the corresponding flag for each override field so unspecified plugin defaults remain intact. `decorate_begin` callbacks wrap the root in reverse registration order and matching `decorate_end` callbacks close the wrappers in registration order: the last plugin is outermost. Application content renders once; plugin overlays render once in registration order inside an absolute, full-root overlay host above it. Ordinary plugin children do not consume application layout space; they start at the root origin independently of root padding and follow outer decorators. Plugins may still open viewport portals for floating content. All callbacks run synchronously. Root requires a viewport starting at `(0, 0)` with positive finite dimensions. The plugin registry and root arrays have caller-specified capacities; invalid root capacity is rejected before any factory executes. If a later factory fails, Root calls each earlier plugin's optional `destroy` hook in reverse order and leaves the root uninitialized. `cui_root_dispose` calls those hooks for a completed root; factories that allocate resources must provide a matching hook.

For a styled window, initialize and bind caller-owned Dialog slots and an initialized Notification state once with `cui_root_bind_facilities`. Pass a `cui_surface_state` initialized as a Dialog or Alert to `cui_root_dialog_open`, or a Sheet to `cui_root_sheet_open`; both accept a content callback. `cui_root_render` mounts the active Sheet, Dialog stack and Notifications after application content on every frame. The app content callback never needs to mount those layers. Dialogs keep their own focus scopes and Escape handling; nested dialogs paint above their parents. At most eight dialogs can be bound so all Dialog layers remain below the Notification layer. Notifications are laid out in the remaining window area outside the active Sheet, using its current size and edge. Closed Dialog slots are reclaimed on the next open. The root does not own the surfaces, notification entries, plugin state, strings or callbacks.

For Base-only composition, call `cui_base_root_render` with application content and optional facility callback. It has no dependency on a styled plugin. A host can install `cui_root_set_copy_hook` to copy its current selection on an unconsumed Ctrl/Cmd-C event. The callback retrieves selected text and writes to the host clipboard; Root does not infer selection from widgets. Input and Textarea consume their own copy events before this fallback runs.

This covers the source Root's per-window state, registry snapshots, render stages, instance style precedence and automatic Sheet/Dialog/Notification mounting. The source's entity observation, deferred notifications, OS window helper, platform window chrome, global text-selection scope, tooltip/native-menu/touch-selection hosts, and copy selection layer remain unimplemented in this module. Applications currently drive frame scheduling and window lifecycle explicitly; completing those facilities remains part of the parity target. This root does not yet establish complete upstream parity.

# Rust CUI builders

For installable local wheel, npm, Go module and Rust crate artifacts, see the
[packaging guide](PACKAGING.md). Linux alpha packages are tested outside the
checkout; registry publication and other platform packages remain pending.

The `cui-builders` crate is a native Rust authoring layer over `libcui_bridge`. Its `Kind` enum follows the public bridge kind list in [`cui_bridge.h`](../include/cui/cui_bridge.h), including the native components delivered through Settings. This is the current bridge scope, not full parity with all 78 CUI manifest entries. Its node handles are app-scoped; calls reject handles from another app, and the C bridge rejects removed nodes. The `App` contains an `Rc` marker and cannot be sent or shared across threads. C strings are checked for interior NUL and the bridge's 4096-byte limit before FFI. Rust callbacks execute during `dispatch()` after `step()` returns from C; no Rust closure is passed into native frames.

Build from the repository root with CMake, Ninja, Rust 1.85.1 or newer (validated with 1.85.1 and 1.99). The crate uses no external dependencies:

```sh
cmake -S bindings/bridge -B build-bridge -G Ninja
cmake --build build-bridge --target cui_bridge test_bridge_core
CUI_BRIDGE_LIB_DIR="$PWD/build-bridge" cargo test --manifest-path bindings/rust/Cargo.toml -- --test-threads=1
```

Serialize all calls across all apps, including apps created on separate threads: the current core uses a process-global Clay context. The crate tests enforce this contract with a process mutex. `build.rs` adds `CUI_BRIDGE_LIB_DIR` to the native linker path and Linux runtime path; use an absolute path. On other platforms, place the shared library on the platform dynamic library search path. The crate checks the bridge ABI version and `cui_bridge_options` size at creation. The C library itself needs its pinned SDL3 dependencies as configured by CMake. Native SDL rendering needs a TTF file. Run the example only on a display you intend to use:

```sh
CUI_BRIDGE_LIB_DIR="$PWD/build-bridge" CUI_TEST_FONT=/path/to/font.ttf cargo run --manifest-path bindings/rust/Cargo.toml --example save_changes
```

The example authors a column, label, row and Button in Rust. A click changes shared Rust state; the label is updated after event dispatch. For a finite SDL smoke under an invisible Xvfb, set `CUI_TEST_FONT` and run `bindings/rust/scripts/test_sdl_smoke.sh`; it fails closed if Xvfb is unavailable. For automated native CTest checks, use `python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir build` from a configured top-level build. It provides an invisible Xvfb on Linux; never use `DISPLAY=:0` or the maintainer's Wayland session. GPU hardware checks remain deferred under Xvfb.

`App::headless` is suitable for deterministic bounds and host input fixtures. Queue pointer or keyboard events, call `step`, then `dispatch` (or `frame` for both). `on_change_event` receives each frame's copied checked, numeric, UTF-8 text, and selected Item snapshot. `queue_text` feeds the focused editable node; `editable_text` reads its current text. Button callbacks receive no `App` borrow; update an `Rc<Cell<_>>` or queue a message and apply UI mutations after dispatch. `Size` covers inherit, XS through 9XL. `gap_px` is logical pixels; `gap_units` multiplies by four.

Grouped `Item` handles in RadioGroup, Tabs, Select, and ComboBox can be selected with `select`; `selected` returns `None` before a choice. `detail_text` sets Alert body text, Select placeholder, or DropdownButton menu label; `open` controls disclosure state. `dropdown_part_bounds` locates split action and menu targets for host input.

Surfaces expose `open`/`is_open`, `on_close_event`, and typed `surface_result()`; Popover, Tooltip, and HoverCard require a live anchor via `anchor`. Hover transitions arrive through `on_change_event`.

`visual_size` sets explicit dimensions for Avatar, EmptyView, GroupBox, Skeleton, and Spinner. `total`, `step_status`, and `numeric_part_bounds` expose native pagination, rating, and step interactions. `scroll_extent` sets Scrollable content dimensions and `scroll` queues a host wheel fixture; offset changes arrive through `on_change_event`.

StatusBar, Toolbar, and TitleBar use Item children; StatusBar Item `step_status` chooses left (0), center (1), or right (2). Icon `text` is a catalog name; an unknown name fails the frame. Message `text` is body and `detail_text` is header.

Attachment uses `text` title, `detail_text` description, `value` progress 0..1, and typed `attachment_status`; this bridge component is a metadata chip. `image_rgba` copies RGBA8 pixels into the bridge (maximum 16 MiB, 2048 pixels per dimension), so the caller can release its buffer after the call.

Tree uses flat preorder Item children; Item `step_status` is depth 0..63, `checked` controls expansion, and `select` chooses the active Item. TimeField uses a portable `Time { hour, minute, second }` in 24-hour format; edits deliver HH:MM:SS text snapshots.

ColorPicker uses packed `0xRRGGBBAA` values; `color_part_bounds` exposes hue, plane, and alpha hit targets (parts 1–3), and change events carry copied `#RRGGBBAA` text. Calendar and DatePicker use a portable `Date { year, month, day }`; `calendar_day_bounds` finds a rendered day. The current native mode is English single-date selection. OtpInput uses `total` for 1–256 cells, `text` for its current value, and queued host text for one cell at a time; changes carry copied text snapshots.

Form uses Item fields; each Item may contain native controls. A disabled Form suppresses its controls. The bridge currently has no built-in Form validation or nested Form support.

InputGroup owns editable text and Item button addons; Item `step_status` selects inline start/end or block start/end positions (0–3). Notification is a retained in-app card: `text` title, `detail_text` message, `open` visibility. Its close callback fires when the closing animation finishes; there is no OS delivery. FocusTrap accepts child nodes and uses `open` to enable a native modal focus scope that blocks outside pointer actions.

MessageScroller uses Item messages (`text` body, `detail_text` sender, `step_status` incoming 0/outgoing 1) and `value` for its scroll offset.

Carousel accepts Item slides and uses `select`/`selected`; native wheel, drag, and keyboard navigation emit selected Item snapshots.

Resizable accepts Item panels with pixel widths in `value`; `resizable_handle_bounds` locates a draggable divider and change events carry new sizes.

TextView owns Markdown, HTML, or plain source in `text`; `text_view_format` selects its parser. `text_view_select` uses rendered UTF-8 byte offsets, and `text_view_selection` copies plain selected text. Native pointer selection delivers a copied text snapshot through `on_change_event`.

Editor owns a multiline UTF-8 buffer; `text` supplies initial source, `detail_text` sets the language name, `editable_text` reads the current document, and queued host text generates copied change snapshots. The bridge currently supports up to 4096 bytes and 512 lines, without completion, syntax callbacks, search, or clipboard APIs.

Chart accepts up to 64 caller-supplied label/value pairs through `chart_data`; the bridge copies them. `chart_kind` selects line, area, bar, or pie rendering, and `chart_datum` reads one retained pair. This native chart is a basic raster/hover view, with no streaming data API.

Table is compositional: Table children are Item rows and each row contains Item text cells. The first row is the header. This bridge Table has no sorting, selection, or virtualization.

DataTable accepts copied UTF-8 headers and row-major cells (up to 16 columns and 32 rows) through `data_table`; its bounds helpers locate cells and headers for host input. `data_table_state` reports selected one-based row/column and requested sort column/direction. Sort is a request: re-supply rows in the desired order. Change callbacks expose the raw native `checked_raw` field as well as its Boolean convenience form; DataTable CHANGE callbacks include a copied JSON text snapshot with reason, row, column, sortColumn, and sortDirection; `data_table_state` reads current state.

Plot accepts up to 256 copied finite `PlotPoint { x, y }` values through `plot_points` and supports readback via `plot_point`. The current native Plot draws themed dots without axes, paths, or hit-testing.

Command accepts up to 64 Item actions; each Item uses `text` as label and `detail_text` as one filter keyword. Command owns the query through `text`/`editable_text`; `command_item_bounds` locates a filtered action for pointer input. Native selection produces CHANGE events and confirmation produces an Item CLICK callback. There are no grouped or custom result rows.

VirtualList accepts up to 64 keyed Item rows, renders a fixed 32-pixel vertical viewport with overscan, and exposes its scroll offset through `value`/`current_value`. `virtual_list_item_bounds` succeeds only for currently rendered rows. Native wheel and key scrolling emit offset CHANGE events; there is no unbounded data source callback.

Sidebar accepts Item navigation actions; `open` controls disclosure, `selected` reads the active Item, and native activation emits a selected CHANGE plus Item CLICK. DataTable also supports typed row, column, or cell `data_table_selection_mode`; cell selection snapshots preserve columns beyond the first in copied event JSON.

RootView is a sole root node that composes regular child widgets and accepts `root_padding` from 0 to 256 logical pixels. `App::theme_presets` lists native preset names; `set_theme_preset` changes the theme for one app and `theme_preset` returns `None` before an explicit selection.

SDL apps also expose `clipboard_set` and `clipboard_get` on the owner thread outside a frame. Clipboard text is UTF-8 and limited to 64 KiB; headless apps return backend unavailable.

Speech is a host-reported lifecycle view: `speech_start`, partial or final `speech_report`, `speech_finish`, and copied `speech_transcript`. It does not capture microphone audio or run recognition; CHANGE callbacks copy lifecycle and transcript snapshots.

Questionnaire composes Item questions and nested Item choices. `questionnaire_question` configures required and multiple selection before the first frame, which freezes the schema; `questionnaire_next` enforces required answers, `questionnaire_previous` navigates back, and state/choice getters read current progress. Its CHANGE callbacks contain copied JSON snapshots of choices, navigation, completion, and repeated `questionnaire_submit` actions.

Dock composes Item panels with optional child content; `dock_activate`, `dock_move_split`, `dock_active`, `dock_panel_bounds`, and `dock_serialize` expose the native panel model. Dock panel schema freezes after the first frame. `DockAxis` selects horizontal or vertical splits; serialized layout is copied UTF-8.

Settings composes Item pages, nested Item groups, and Switch/Checkbox/Input/NumberInput fields. `settings_query` filters pages (up to 256 bytes), `settings_page`/`settings_set_page` control navigation, `settings_field_bounds` locates visible fields, and `settings_reset_page` restores first-frame defaults with copied field events. The page/group schema freezes after the first frame; Input and NumberInput titles use `detail_text`. All fallible setters return the bridge status as `Error(code)`.

## Composed workspace example

`bindings/rust/examples/workspace.rs` authors a navigable Account/Preferences workspace entirely in Rust. Account has an editable name and a DatePicker initialized to an older birthday; Preferences has a notifications Checkbox. The Save Button callback records shared Rust state; after dispatch, the loop changes the status label and opens a Dialog. `--headless` drives native bounds and pointer input, edits the name, switches tabs, toggles the Checkbox, and verifies the Dialog without opening a window:

```sh
CUI_BRIDGE_LIB_DIR="$PWD/build-bridge" cargo run --manifest-path bindings/rust/Cargo.toml --example workspace -- --headless
```

For a desktop SDL session, set an explicit font and omit `--headless`:

```sh
CUI_BRIDGE_LIB_DIR="$PWD/build-bridge" CUI_TEST_FONT=/path/to/font.ttf cargo run --manifest-path bindings/rust/Cargo.toml --example workspace
```

A finite SDL smoke must use an invisible display on Linux. From the repository root with `xvfb-run` available:

```sh
CUI_BRIDGE_LIB_DIR="$PWD/build-bridge" CUI_TEST_FONT=/path/to/font.ttf CUI_RUST_SMOKE_FRAMES=3 env -u DISPLAY -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY xvfb-run -a env CUI_TEST_VIRTUAL_DISPLAY=1 cargo run --manifest-path bindings/rust/Cargo.toml --example workspace
```

The SDL workspace also accepts `CUI_FONT_FALLBACK=/path/to/another.ttf`, which calls `App::font_fallbacks` with an explicit fallback font path. The smoke path rejects a missing virtual-display marker. It exercises SDL construction and rendering for three frames; the deterministic `--headless` path verifies interaction.

For a Rust SDL clipboard round trip under an invisible Linux display, use an explicit font and the virtual-display marker:

```sh
CUI_BRIDGE_LIB_DIR="$PWD/build-bridge" CUI_TEST_FONT=/path/to/font.ttf env -u DISPLAY -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY xvfb-run -a env CUI_TEST_VIRTUAL_DISPLAY=1 cargo run --manifest-path bindings/rust/Cargo.toml --example clipboard_smoke
```

# Scrollable content

`cui_scrollable_begin`/`cui_scrollable_end` wrap caller content in a fixed-size clipped viewport with application-owned horizontal/vertical offsets. Content dimensions are explicit by default; the kit clamps offsets, translates children with fractional precision, and draws optional themed scrollbars. `cui_base_scrollable` performs the same reductions and semantic submission without drawing. Negative or nonfinite sizes use documented defaults (320×240 viewport, 10-pixel bars, 48-pixel wheel steps); axes not enabled remain at zero.

Wheel events route to the innermost eligible clipped semantic scroll region under the pointer. A container at a boundary passes the event to an eligible parent based on the preceding frame's offsets. Higher interactive portals and unrelated modal scopes block background scrolling. Initial routing uses preceding-frame geometry. A child may explicitly defer an unconsumed scroll to an eligible layout ancestor with `cui_defer_scroll_event`. Prefer `cui_scrollable_end_ex` with mutable state: it handles deferred events after children and updates the current frame's viewport offset and scrollbar paint. Handled wheel events are consumed, so the finish phase does not replay begin-phase movement. The original const-state `cui_scrollable_end` remains a paint-only compatibility API and cannot process late deferrals. Custom base compositions can call `cui_base_scrollable_finish` and `cui_set_box_scroll_offset` after children.

`hide_scrollbars` keeps the full viewport available without drawing tracks. `axis_lock` routes each event by its dominant axis (ties are vertical). `trap_horizontal` consumes horizontal-dominant movement even at the horizontal boundary, matching embedded table masks. Optional `gesture_lock` retains the initial precise-scroll axis across frames by stable semantic ID: a 28 ms quiet interval or an explicit gesture boundary starts a new gesture; a sufficiently strong perpendicular turn releases the lock. Ordinary line wheels remain unchanged. The persistent lock is disabled on WebAssembly to match the pinned upstream behavior. Routing filters only eligible, visible owners and supplies the filtered event to child/parent reducers consistently. Removing or disabling the owner clears its retained state.

Scrollbars expose their controlled value, range, orientation and related content. Arrow keys step, PageUp/PageDown move one viewport, and Home/End select an endpoint. Clicking a track pages toward the click; captured thumb dragging preserves the initial grab offset across frames. Secondary-button events do not change primary dragging. Disabled scrolling preserves the caller's current offsets after clamping; callers independently control the disabled state of their children.

`tests/unit/test_scroll.c` exercises both axes, wheel routing, translated row geometry and clipped hits, scrollbar keyboard and captured dragging, semantics, all four themes, invalid offsets and small content. A separate base-only executable links only core and the scroll reducer. Bare layout fixtures emit their own clip commands; a behavior-only frame proves the reducer paints nothing. Core tests independently cover nested boundary routing and higher-portal blocking.

Grow-sized viewports, inertial/touch scrolling, auto-hidden/system-style bars, accessibility platform bridges, fractional DPI pixel snapping and exhaustive upstream integration remain unfinished. Existing virtual tree/table models can provide content dimensions and visible ranges; this container does not imply those models are rendered automatically.

The browser gallery forwards pixel wheel deltas as precise CUI scroll events for Scrollable, Sidebar and VirtualList. Fractional deltas retain their distance rather than being multiplied by the widget's discrete wheel step. Native hosts can opt into the same contract with `cui_event.scroll_precise = true`; discrete wheel events continue to use the configured step. Sidebar's absolute content position follows its scroll model, while the scrollbar stays anchored in the viewport.

Set `auto_measure_content` to measure ordinary laid-out children on enabled axes
whose `content_width`/`content_height` is omitted (nonpositive or nonfinite).
Explicit positive finite dimensions take precedence, including virtual content.
The container retains the FIT content box extent through its stable owner ID and
uses the preceding frame's layout for ranges, clamping, and scrollbar geometry.
The first frame has zero range; additions, removals, and wrapped text changes
update the range on the following frame. Width stays constrained to the viewport
when only vertical measurement is enabled, so wrapped text contributes its laid-out
height. Enable horizontal measurement for content that should fit its natural
width. Out-of-flow absolute boxes and portals do not enlarge the FIT extent.
The drawing-free base API continues to require explicit content dimensions.

# Scrollbar appearance and idle hiding

Set `theme.scrollbar` once for all themed scrolling owners, or pass a borrowed
`scrollbar_style` override in the relevant options. An override replaces the
shared skin; it is read only during the widget call/frame and is never retained.
Surface begin copies its skin and palette until the paired footer/end calls.

```c
theme.scrollbar = (cui_scrollbar_style){
    .visibility = CUI_SCROLLBAR_AUTO_HIDE,
    .thickness = 8,
    .min_thumb = 24,
    .thumb_radius = 4,
    .no_track = true,
    .idle_seconds = 1,
    .fade_seconds = .15f,
};
```

`INHERIT` is the zero-initialized compatibility policy: existing bars remain
available, and owners that previously had no bars remain barless. `VISIBLE`
adds bars to overflowing formerly barless viewports. `HIDDEN` omits their paint,
pointer/keyboard bar semantics and drag handling. It preserves the content's
scroll owner and wheel, touch and existing keyboard behavior. A legacy explicit
`hide_scrollbars` option still wins over the skin.

Positive finite thickness/minimum values override the owner's defaults.
Thickness is capped at half the smaller viewport dimension. Thumb minimum is
capped at track length. Thumb and track radii are independent, with zero choosing
square corners. Existing Tabs retain their legacy rounded bar under a zero skin.
`custom_thumb_color` and `custom_track_color` allow RGBA overrides, including
transparent colors; otherwise the owner's palette supplies colors. `no_track`
removes the painted track without removing its visible thumb's hit region.

Existing gutter bars keep their gutter during auto-hide, avoiding reflow as
opacity changes. HIDDEN releases their gutter. Newly added bars are overlays and
never reserve a gutter. Overlay corners use the horizontal bar's hit region
where both axes meet. Bars are bounded by the owner's clip and stay fixed as
content translates.

## Owners and axes

| Owner | Actual axes | INHERIT availability | Style route |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Scrollable | Caller-selected horizontal/vertical | Existing gutter bars | `cui_scroll_options`, theme |
| Sidebar body | Vertical | Existing gutter bar | Sidebar options, theme |
| DataTable / virtualized table | Horizontal/vertical, preserving pinned columns | Existing `scrollbars` option | Table options, theme |
| VirtualList | Horizontal/vertical according to its model | Existing gutter bars | Its nested scroll options, theme |
| MessageScroller / conversation | Vertical | Existing `scrollbar` option | Message scroller options, theme |
| Tabs and Dock tab strip | Active horizontal or vertical tab axis | Existing `scrollbar` option | Tabs options, theme; Dock forwards theme |
| Textarea and Editor | Vertical; horizontal when no-wrap | No bars | Textarea options, theme |
| Tree | Vertical | No bars | Tree options, theme |
| List, ListMulti, searchable/choice/combobox popup lists | Vertical when windowed | No bars | List/popup options, theme |
| MenuTree, nested Menu, ContextMenu, split/dropdown and overflow menus | Vertical per overflowing popup level | No bars | Menu options, theme |
| Dialog, AlertDialog, Sheet, Popover body | Vertical | No bars | Surface options, theme |
| Command palette | Vertical | Existing Scrollable bar | Theme through common Scrollable |
| Settings body | Vertical | Existing Scrollable bar | Theme through common Scrollable |
| TextView body | Vertical when explicitly scrollable | Existing Scrollable bar | TextView options, theme |
| TextView wide table | Horizontal | No bars | TextView options, theme |
| AttachmentGroup | Horizontal | No bars | Explicit `scrollbar_style` and optional `scrollbar_theme` |
| Finite Carousel | Its configured horizontal or vertical axis | No bars | Carousel options, theme |

AttachmentGroup's existing API has no theme argument. Its optional borrowed
`scrollbar_theme` supplies the application palette and shared policy; absent
that pointer it uses the light palette and the inherited no-bar policy. Explicit
skin colors work without a palette pointer.

Lists and menus preserve discrete row windows. Bar movement changes the window,
not the selected value or action. Their active keyboard row is kept in the new
window so the existing next-frame reveal does not undo bar movement. Menu rows
use their actual varying heights. Finite Carousel bar movement uses the model's
nearest slide and normal change callback; it does not create a second scroll
model.

Looping Carousel has no finite beginning/end, and intentionally has no bar even
with VISIBLE/AUTO_HIDE. A raw `cui_table_begin` composition, resizable/dock content
callbacks and plain boxes do not create scroll models; use Scrollable inside
them. Single-line Input caret reveal is not a general panel scroll owner. Plot
domain pan/zoom is a separate interaction model and is unchanged by this skin.
No unsupported horizontal axis is invented for Tree, Surface or row lists.

## Auto-hide and lifetime

The portable timer uses `cui_frame_time`, one context resource per auto-hide bar,
and no OS clock or per-frame allocation. Initial submission, a scroll value
change, owner hover entry/movement and owner/bar scroll or keyboard activity
refresh the idle deadline. Bar hover, capture, drag, direct owner/bar focus and
an applicable named focus scope keep it visible. Arbitrary focused descendants
of an ordinary box do not hold an overlay visible indefinitely.

Default idle/fade durations are 1/.15 seconds. Positive finite durations are
capped at 60/5 seconds. The helper requests redraw only before the idle/fade
deadline. The final zero-opacity frame requests no further redraw. A held bar
requires no timer frames; releasing it starts a fresh finite idle period.
`no_fade`, skin reduced motion, component reduced motion where exposed, and
context reduced motion remove fading while retaining the idle deadline. Hosts
must honor ordinary `cui_needs_redraw` invalidations and advance frame time.

Visible/hidden/inherited common bars allocate no timer. Formerly barless overlay
owners use one bounded context drag resource while opted in. Surface additionally
uses one bounded stack of 64 paired submissions, allowing nested inactive and
active skins without retaining caller state past frame completion. An inherited
Surface with no prior opt-in stack allocates nothing. Capacity exhaustion uses
the existing context capacity error; Surface refuses begin before opening its
composition if its stack cannot be obtained. Never pair footer/end with a failed
begin. Resource cleanup follows the existing complete-frame omission rule.

The new `cui_resource_find` is an in-frame lookup of an existing resource. It
never allocates and reports no error for missing/invalid input. A successful
lookup marks the resource used this frame. Returned memory remains owned by the
context and follows the existing renderer-completion/next-begin lifetime.

The split overlay helpers reduce before content layout and paint afterward.
Paint receives final offsets explicitly, so wheel correction and discrete row
quantization use the actual model position. Its local viewport coordinates must
cancel any ancestor content translation; built-in callers do this. Invalid
nonfinite geometry/offsets leave caller offsets unchanged. These helpers add bar
interaction, not wheel/touch ownership or automatic wrapping.

## Validation

Headless tests cover shared colors/radii/thickness/minimums, hidden hit regions
and wheel movement, finite fade completion/no perpetual redraw, reduced motion,
capture retention, list/menu window movement without selection callbacks, both
tab axes, tree and editor bars, fixed Surface footers, Surface allocation failure
and inherited zero allocation, finite Carousel selection, and wide TextView
table geometry. Existing interaction suites retain legacy INHERIT coverage.

`tests/web/test_scrollbar_appearance.py` drives the actual WASM gallery and CDP
touch contacts. It checks common families, hidden semantic ownership and real
wheel/touch scrolling, plus idle/capture behavior. The gallery controls apply
one shared policy to the current example and respect light/dark palettes. This
does not claim OS-native scrollbar rendering, infinite-range scrollbar support,
or new scrolling behavior for components without a scroll model.

# Final-offset scroll observers

Include `cui/cui_scroll_events.h`. Drawing-free `cui_base_scrollable_events` /
`cui_base_scrollable_finish_events` and Styled `cui_scrollable_begin_events` /
`cui_scrollable_end_events` observe one final offset per pair. Legacy Scrollable
APIs, public state/options layouts and reduction timing are unchanged. Scrollbar
overlays, virtual widgets and MessageScroller have no new observer facade. See the
[checkpoint](design/SCROLL_EVENTS_SLICE.md).

```c
static void scrolled(void *user, const cui_scroll_change *change) {
    cui_scroll_offset *last = user;
    *last = change->value; /* Copyable values; not a request to accept/reject. */
}

/* During one frame; state/options/last belong to the application. */
cui_scroll_event_scope scope = {0};
bool begin_changed = cui_base_scrollable_events(ui, owner, &state, options, &scope);
(void)begin_changed; /* False can mean valid no-change; still finish. */
/* Compose the owner's same-ID layout and children here, as with the legacy Base
 * reducer. Children may defer wheel input back to this owner. */
cui_scroll_event_result result = cui_base_scrollable_finish_events(
    ui, owner, &state, options, &scope, (cui_scroll_handler){scrolled, &last});
/* Base does not update your viewport translation or paint. Use final state.x/y
 * for that work as in your existing custom layout. */
```

Base begin returns the exact old `cui_base_scrollable` bool, including offset
normalization, and does not mean successful submission. A nonnull context/state/
token, nonzero owner, zero-initialized inactive token and active ordinary or passive
submission admit the pair. Invalid arguments, outside-frame/protected phases or
an already-active token reject before reducer work. After an admitted begin,
finish once after children even if begin returned false. Calling finish on an
unadmitted token is harmless and returns `valid=false`; do not read private token
fields to decide application control flow. Reuse a consumed token or zero-initialize
new caller storage; never copy a live token or share it between owners.

Finish calls the existing wheel-only finish once, then freezes entry/final offsets,
consumes the token and optionally notifies. `valid` reports pairing and finite
final-state admission, not frame/layout success. `changed` compares the whole pair,
not only the finish delta. `change_count` counts actual callbacks (zero or one);
`count_overflow` is always false for this bounded aggregate. Reading a result never
replays dispatch. Missing handler still performs all old reduction and reports
changes with count zero. Net-zero offset sequences, drag-state-only changes and
unchanged offsets are silent, even if individual input operations occurred.

This is an applied final-offset notification, not a user gesture or controlled
value request. It includes clamping from range shrink, disabled axes, negative
entry values and nonfinite entry repair. The new payload has `has_previous=false`
and zero `previous` when either entry coordinate was nonfinite; otherwise both
previous coordinates are preserved exactly. Finite final values are copied into
`value`. An external assignment before begin becomes the baseline, not its own
event. Do not mutate active state between the pair to manufacture an event.

Disabled ordinary submission can normalize state and dispatch CHANGE. Inert or
layout-only scopes preserve the existing reducer's maintenance/layout behavior,
and can return `valid=true, changed=true`, but callbacks are suppressed because
the public frame sequence is zero. This does not introduce user requests under
inert ancestry. No callback means neither rollback nor absence of maintenance.

Metadata uses CHANGE and the public owner target. The only evidence flag is
HAS_FRAME with the genuine matching nonzero frame sequence. Source is UNKNOWN;
there is no HAS_SOURCE, event index or activation snapshot. Several inputs or
normalization can contribute, so guessing a final wheel/key cause would be false.
Payload is pointer-free and safe to copy beyond frame/context lifetime; it does
not keep the owner or context alive.

Same context, owner, state address, effective options, frame and ancestry must
surround the pair. Runtime checks reject identity mismatch, token reuse, outside
submission, differing nonzero frame identities, and zero/nonzero scope transitions
before finish effects. With both sequences zero the existing public API cannot
prove same-frame identity: crossing frames/scopes is unsupported caller misuse
without a guaranteed diagnostic. Same effective options/style lifetime is a caller
obligation, not a runtime descriptor-equality check. Keep each nested token separate.
A wrong pair is not automatically repaired or cancelled; an admitted layout must
still follow its legacy balancing obligations. Nonfinite final state from forbidden
caller mutation returns invalid after token consumption; no callback is invented.

Handler and user data are borrowed only through finish. They are never stored in
the scope or context. Callback may update unrelated application state, but must
not recursively submit this control/frame, mutate active input/scroll state/options,
destroy the context or free active resources. Defer teardown until existing frame
obligations complete. No lifetime guard or general event routing is added.

The focused tests compare old/new state, semantics, consumption and begin bool;
cover multiple wheel events, net-zero changes, omitted observer, normalization,
nonfinite repair, inert/layout-only maintenance, invalid/mismatched/repeated pairs,
nonzero wrong-frame rejection, overlapping owner tokens, real child-deferred wheel
routing, scrollbar keyboard/drag, and copied payload lifetime. Existing Scrollable,
virtual widget and MessageScroller tests remain separate regression evidence.
No completion callback, virtual-window rerender, precision conversion, bridge
producer or foreign-language handler is introduced. Bindings retain their existing
manual notification allowlists. This slice is not full-family or 78-family parity.

## Styled composition

```c
cui_scroll_event_scope scope = {0};
if (cui_scrollable_begin_events(ui, owner, theme, &state, options, &scope)) {
    /* Compose ordinary child content here. */
    cui_scroll_event_result result = cui_scrollable_end_events(
        ui, owner, theme, &state, options, &scope,
        (cui_scroll_handler){scrolled, &last});
    (void)result;
}
```

Styled begin's bool is successful composition admission, not Base's changed bool.
False means no new boxes/pair were opened and no end is required. True always
requires end, including unchanged, disabled, inert and layout-only submissions.
Do not condition end on offset change. Use the same effective options/theme/state
and ancestry across the pair; Styled's legacy previous-frame auto-measure resolution
still runs at its original begin/end points.

Styled end executes the existing mutable `end_ex` once: child-deferred wheel
reduction, current viewport translation, scrollbar paint and owner box closure.
Only afterward does it freeze final offsets, consume the token and invoke the
observer. It never calls the Base event finalizer, so there is no repeated finish
or double notification. Counts/normalization/metadata/passive suppression and
callback mutation/lifetime rules are the same as Base. `valid` describes admitted
pairing and finite final state, not transactional painting success; existing layout
errors are retained and do not undo already-required balancing.

The token now distinguishes Base and Styled pairs. Cross-layer finalization is
rejected before reducer or box effects: Base finish cannot consume a Styled pair,
and Styled end cannot close boxes for a Base pair. Correct finalization is still
required after a rejected attempt. The added private layer bit extends the
**unreleased** scope layout; rebuild consumers rather than mixing old objects.
No legacy public layout changed.

Styled tests compare legacy/new draw command geometry/colors, child/sibling
bounds, semantics, consumed input and final state; exercise deferred child routing,
net-zero and missing observers, disabled/passive normalization, cross-layer/owner/
repeated-token rejection, keyboard and scrollbar drag, and copied payload lifetime.
The bounded strict Release and ASan/UBSan harnesses also run the Base event and
legacy scroll/virtual/message tests. Sanitizer proof reuses prebuilt instrumented
Core/software archives; it does not claim a fresh full-project sanitizer rebuild.
