# Native SDK contextual text build

Native Go and Rust SDK builds now enable the same `CUI_TEXT_BIDI` implementation
as the default canonical native text target. The generated minimal SDK builds
`cui_bidi` from `src/text/cui_bidi.c` and pinned SheenBidi unity objects, then links
it into `cui_text`. The generator copies the pinned dependency manifest, complete
SheenBidi headers/sources/license and local patch pin. Portable SDK builds retain
their previous dependency scope; native mode enables this additional analyzer.

Go native mode defines `CUI_TEXT_BIDI`, supplies the private SheenBidi header paths,
and compiles text, analyzer and SheenBidi in separate generated translation units.
`SB_CONFIG_UNITY` belongs only to the vendor unit. That unit applies the exact four
existing canonical vendor warning exceptions with a diagnostic push/pop:
unused parameter/value/function and implicit fallthrough. CUI source warnings
remain errors. Rust native packaging enables bidi in both staged SDK and canonical
fallback builds; its static archive link order includes `cui_bidi` after `cui_text`.

Before this change the SDK native build compiled only the legacy FreeType/HarfBuzz
path. `cui_font_text_geometry_line` returned `UNAVAILABLE`, mixed-paragraph layouts
were unavailable, and contextual colored drawing returned false without emission.
This was a packaging build gap, not a separately documented native feature limit.
Ordinary button smoke tests did not exercise it. The public text API still permits
explicitly disabled bidi builds, with their documented legacy behavior.

Run the comparison with host development packages for SDL3 >=3.2, FreeType,
HarfBuzz, CMake/Ninja and a C11 compiler:

```sh
python tests/packaging/test_sdk_text.py \
  --build-dir /tmp/cui-sdk-text \
  --build-type Release \
  --font /usr/share/fonts/noto/NotoSans-Regular.ttf \
  --rtl-font /usr/share/fonts/noto/NotoSansHebrew-Regular.ttf \
  --bindings
```

CI can substitute equivalent explicit font paths. Choose a primary face covering
Latin but lacking Hebrew and a fallback covering Hebrew, so the fixture actually
requires a second face. All three implementations receive the same files; the
script records their SHA256 values and combined text source fingerprints. It
checks freshly generated SDKs before building and compares canonical, Go SDK and
Rust SDK results. Font names, exact metrics or raster values are not hardcoded;
results must agree within this host. The current fixture specifically exercises
Latin/Hebrew, not all Unicode scripts or every font.

The fixture asserts contextual paragraph-relative byte identity, invalid UTF-8
boundary rejection without output mutation, caret/hit/selection geometry, four
Hebrew selection clusters, actual odd-level RTL and fallback runs, nonzero shaped
glyphs and two colored glyph groups with real coverage pixels. Missing bidi cannot
silently pass: contextual status must be OK and colored emission must succeed.
`--bindings` additionally copies Go/Rust modules into private consumers, builds
native mode, and runs real SDL frames and click callbacks with mixed Latin/Hebrew
button text and an explicit fallback. Only the repository invisible Xvfb runner
launches those consumers; the C font fixture itself opens no display or window.
No package publication or desktop-session fallback occurs.

Validation covers native build fidelity for these text facilities. It does not
claim complete Editor behavior, full native accessibility, all renderer/platform
parity, or self-contained font/system-library distribution. Root integration must
regenerate SDK receipts after canonical Text/SheenBidi/Dock patches and rebuild
published artifacts; copying an old prebuilt bridge retains its old capabilities.
documents.docs/SDL_SYSTEM_APPEARANCE.md:
# SDL system appearance observation

`cui_sdl3_appearance` returns a copied, portable `cui_platform_appearance` on
 the main thread. Creation queries the real SDL system theme and starts revision
at 1. `cui_sdl3_poll` consumes system-theme notifications, re-queries SDL, increments
the revision (saturating at UINT64_MAX), and requests Core redraw. Idle polling
keeps the revision stable. Notifications contain no theme payload; repeated
notifications may produce the same appearance with a new revision. Poll retains
its usual continue/quit return contract. No callback or UI pointer is retained.

`CUI_APPEARANCE_SYSTEM_THEME` indicates API/notification availability, including
when the answer is `CUI_SYSTEM_APPEARANCE_UNKNOWN`. Unknown does not mean light:
the application must choose its own fallback or retain its last known choice.
There is no reduced-motion or high-contrast OS detection in this seam. Those
preferences remain explicit application inputs. The adapter has no Theme link
and does not change an application's explicit light/dark choice.

SDL has a process-global event queue. The backend which polls a notification
consumes it; this is not per-window multicast. Applications with several SDL
backends should designate an event owner and distribute its copied appearance
snapshot to other windows. Revisions are local to each backend instance and reset
on recreation; do not compare them across instances or after saturation.

A native Theme application can map the observation explicitly:

```c
/* After normal cui_sdl3_poll(host, ui), on the main thread. */
cui_platform_appearance appearance;
if (cui_sdl3_appearance(host, &appearance) &&
    appearance.revision != last_observation_revision) {
    last_observation_revision = appearance.revision;
    if (appearance.appearance != CUI_SYSTEM_APPEARANCE_UNKNOWN)
        preferences.dark = appearance.appearance == CUI_SYSTEM_APPEARANCE_DARK;
    /* Application revision also accounts for explicit preference changes. */
    if (preferences.revision != UINT64_MAX) preferences.revision++;
    cui_theme_host_update(&resolved, &registry, selection, preferences, 16);
}
```

Initialize the caller's revision sentinel to zero for first resolution; define
an explicit unknown fallback in `preferences.dark`. `selection.mode` may remain
`CUI_THEME_FORCE_LIGHT`/`CUI_THEME_FORCE_DARK`: observation updates the system
preference input but does not overwrite that selection. Registry/Theme headers
and linkage are only needed by the application using this example.

Provenance: repository SDL fetch pin
`7f3ae3d57459e59943a4ecfefc8f6277ec6bf540`,
[SDL video source](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/blob/7f3ae3d57459e59943a4ecfefc8f6277ec6bf540/src/video/SDL_video.c)
updates system state before sending the notification;
[pinned event definitions](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/blob/7f3ae3d57459e59943a4ecfefc8f6277ec6bf540/include/SDL3/SDL_events.h)
provide a common event without appearance data.
[Official API documentation](https://wiki.libsdl.org/SDL3/SDL_GetSystemTheme)
requires main-thread use and SDL 3.2.0 or newer. Validation uses installed SDL
3.4.18. Driver/desktop support varies; this does not claim every OS discovers a
known theme, or validate a physical desktop preference change.

`tests/integration/test_sdl3_appearance.c` uses actual SDL dummy/software drivers,
compares the initial observation with `SDL_GetSystemTheme`, queues two real SDL
notifications, and checks monotonic revision/redraw, idle stability, null-output
atomicity and destruction/recreation. It does not fabricate light/dark data.
Integrator: register this test linked to `cui_sdl3` and SDL3; default builds remain
unaffected when SDL is disabled. Generated distribution remains integrator-owned.

## Compiled native consumer

`examples/system_theme/main.c` is a complete application, defaulting to Follow
System with a light fallback for an initially unknown appearance. Later unknown
observations retain the last known preference. Two custom named themes are loaded
through the actual ThemeSet importer into owned bounded registry entries. Sidebar,
content, palette status and three real buttons expose Follow System, Always Light
and Always Dark. Notifications update the system preference while retaining an
explicit mode choice; selecting Follow System later uses the newest observation.
Application state must stay at a stable address because its registry borrows inline
entry storage. State transitions reject stale generations, invalid enums and
revision overflow without applying partial changes.

The static scene blocks on `SDL_WaitEvent(NULL)` when Core needs no redraw. SDL
leaves the notification queued for the adapter to dispatch; there is no periodic
polling spin. A finite `--frames` mode deliberately renders consecutive frames
for reproducible smoke/capture and does not wait. An application adding timed
animations must replace indefinite waiting with its earliest animation deadline.
No reduced-motion/high-contrast OS values are manufactured.

Example manual build from the configured native tree (root owns target registration):

```sh
cc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -Iinclude \
  $(pkg-config --cflags sdl3) examples/system_theme/main.c \
  build/libcui_sdl3.a build/libcui.a build/libcui_text.a build/libcui.a \
  build/libcui_bidi.a $(pkg-config --libs sdl3 harfbuzz freetype2) -lm \
  -o build/system_theme
build/system_theme --font /usr/share/fonts/noto/NotoSans-Regular.ttf
xvfb-run -a build/system_theme --font /usr/share/fonts/noto/NotoSans-Regular.ttf \
  --frames 3 --capture build/system-theme.bmp
```

`tests/integration/test_system_theme_app.c` compiles the same original example
state/frame functions with its native entry point disabled. It tests actual
Core button activation, palette changes, unknown/stale/invalid observations,
explicit modes and bounded revision failure. Link it only to `cui`; the headless translation excludes SDL headers and
native entry-point code, so it remains portable and can run under WASI. Native Xvfb smoke verifies the compiled renderer
and actual font capture; a physical desktop preference event remains outside this
validation. The adapter's queued SDL notification test covers the notification path.

At the adapter revision saturation boundary, the example still accepts a changed
appearance with the same UINT64_MAX observation revision. Identical saturated
observations remain idle. The separate application preference revision is checked
before every transition; if that sequence itself reaches UINT64_MAX, further
changes reject atomically and the native entry point exits with its update error.
Repeated equal appearances at saturation cannot reveal distinct OS notifications.
documents.docs/SETTINGS_EVENTS.md:
# Settings applied events

Include `cui/cui_settings_events.h`. `cui_settings_events` preserves the existing
Styled Settings operation and adds navigation and built-in value observers.
`on_navigation` reports applied page/group selection, not an owner-rejectable request. Missing observers permit all legacy
work and ignore user. Legacy Base filter/reset helper and field callback contracts stay unchanged.

```c
static void navigation_changed(void *user, const cui_settings_navigation_change *change) {
    bool *save_navigation = user; /* unrelated application flag */
    *save_navigation = true;
    /* Copy *change to retain its pointer-free page/group and metadata values. */
}
/* During UI submission with existing caller-owned pages/state/options: */
/* cui_settings_events(ui, id, theme, pages, count, &state, options,
       (cui_settings_handler){.on_navigation = navigation_changed, .user = &save_navigation}); */
```

The payload contains `previous_page`, `previous_group`, `page`, `group` using
source indices; `CUI_SETTINGS_NO_GROUP` selects the page as a whole. Filtering
does not renumber indices. Reordering caller arrays changes their meaning.
Notifications run immediately after the existing navigation writes, pending-group
scroll policy and invalidation, before content/filter-scroll resolution and paint.
A group callback can see pending scroll true even when content clears it later.
A same-pair activation can still restore pending scrolling without emitting CHANGE.
Defaults, query reconciliation, search/filter repair, scrolling, resizing, reset
and field callbacks never become navigation events.

`result` is the exact legacy aggregate `cui_settings_result`, including filter
selection repair. `navigation_count` counts actual observer calls, saturating at
SIZE_MAX with `count_overflow`. Real A→B→A navigation emits both transitions even
when the final pair equals entry; the legacy selection flag is preserved. Sidebar
processes items in traversal order, each scanning its own inputs in order. Across
items callback input indices therefore need not increase. This facade does not
reorder dispatch into global input order or replay reducers.

Metadata targets the Settings compound. The private navigation descriptor matches
each existing Sidebar callback to its next actual same-trigger activation; accepted
snapshot evidence is frozen before writes when available. Copied `activation.target`
retains the original derived page/group navigation ID. If no accepted snapshot is
available, only actual frame/index/type facts are attached. An unexpected callback/
activation mismatch has proven frame only, UNKNOWN source and no index/activation.
Presence flags are authoritative. No early semantic registration, consume, extra
reduction or invented activation is used. Passive/layout-only/inert submissions
produce no observation while retaining legacy maintenance and rendering behavior.
Sidebar TREEITEM accessibility ACTIVATE is not currently supported by Core; this
facade adds no accessibility routing or promise beyond existing Sidebar behavior.

New admission requires nonnull context/theme/state, a nonzero compound ID, and a
page array when count is nonzero. Old validation/filter behavior then applies.
Handler/user/payload pointer are borrowed synchronously. Do not mutate/rebind/free
active page/group/item arrays, values/editors/states, dropdown workspace, labels,
callback resources, input or context, or recursively submit UI in the observer.
Unrelated application flags may change; defer removal/omission/teardown until outer
return plus renderer consumption. Legacy custom search/render/change/reset callbacks
keep their timing and must preserve resources needed by the remaining old operation.

Navigation and built-in scalar/text changes, including explicit resets, are typed
here. Search and viewport observers remain outside this facade. C bridge and Python/JS/TS/Go/Rust still use their existing
Settings callback/polling paths; no per-navigation foreign callback or synchronous
request is implied. Focused C tests do not establish browser or binding parity.


## Built-in scalar fields

Set `on_boolean`, `on_number` and/or `on_choice` in `cui_settings_handler` for the
corresponding `cui_settings_bool_change`, `cui_settings_number_change` and
`cui_settings_choice_change`. They share the borrowed handler user pointer.
Each payload identifies `page`, `group`, `item` source indices and the derived
`field_id` (`cui_settings_part_id(root, page, group, item, 24)`). Metadata target
remains the Settings compound. Payloads are pointer-free and copyable by value.

Boolean covers built-in Switch and Checkbox; Number carries actual doubles; choice
carries owner choice IDs for both Menu-backed dropdown and legacy Select. Custom
render overrides bypass these observers even when host rendering edits an owner.
Scalar adapters do not invent requests, COMMIT or per-input events. Text and RESET
observations have the separate contracts below.

Capture occurs immediately before one existing built-in adapter. The adapter runs
once, records the existing first edit error, and invokes the old item `on_change`
at its original point. Only then does the typed observer compare/read the actual
final owner. A legacy callback restoring entry value produces no typed CHANGE;
redirecting it reports the redirected value. Callback count does not replay effects.
Two nested edits ending at entry produce no aggregate CHANGE. Existing Switch may
coalesce several activations into one flip; the facade preserves that behavior.
Each adapter emits at most one typed callback in existing content order. Scalars
are **aggregate notifications**, unlike per-navigation transitions.

`boolean_count`, `number_count`, `choice_count` independently count actual calls,
saturating at SIZE_MAX and setting shared `count_overflow`. Missing typed handlers
preserve all old writes/callbacks. Disabled fields and passive/layout-only/inert
submissions retain legacy maintenance, including Number bounds/last-value writes
and old callbacks, but emit no new typed scalar EDIT notification. Enabled real final
owner changes can be notified even with a nested edit error; errors and invalid
flags are preserved, never used as an artificial change gate.

Scalar EDIT metadata has a proven nonzero active frame, UNKNOWN source and no input
index/activation. A whole adapter and its legacy callback may combine inputs or
apply bounds without input, so a unique causal event cannot honestly be inferred.
An enabled bounds adjustment is an applied change, not proof of user interaction.

Number equality treats both NaNs as unchanged and signed zeros as equal. Payload
`previous_finite` and `value_finite` describe the actual numeric values, not their
acceptance by Number. Settings initially validates finite owners, but old callbacks
can redirect a valid edit to infinity/NaN or change a later field after validation.
These facts remain visible; the observer does not clamp again, repair the owner,
resynchronize the draft or rewrite `number_state.last_value` after the callback.
Settings' existing extra bounds/last-value pass stays before old `on_change`;
therefore the callback's final owner can intentionally differ from draft/last_value
until later old synchronization. Invalid nonfinite owners may fail the next filter.

Old callbacks must leave observed scalar owner pointers readable through typed
notification. The new observer cannot mutate active owners or other active model
resources; use unrelated flags and defer teardown. Entry is captured at each field,
not at Settings-call entry, so earlier host changes are not independently reported.
Reset-button effects are described separately below.
This extends the new C structs and requires rebuilding consumers with this header;
existing legacy Settings options/state/result layouts and function remain unchanged.


Built-in Input EDIT observations use `handler.on_text` and `result.text_count`.
They compare committed revisions immediately around the old adapter and its old
`on_change` callback, then report once at most. Two inputs in one adapter remain
one notification; callback redirects and byte-net-zero edits still notify when the
revision differs. IME preedit, selection and unchanged revisions stay silent.
An earlier successful edit is observable even if a later input reports an error.
Missing observers preserve editing. Disabled, passive and inert submissions do not
notify. Custom renderers remain outside the built-in observer contract.

`cui_settings_text_change` includes before/after revision and byte counts, field ID
and source page/group/item indices. `text` is final committed UTF-8 borrowed only
for the callback; no previous text is copied internally. Use
`cui_component_event_copy_utf8(event->text, limit, storage, capacity, &owned)` and
check for `CUI_COMPONENT_EVENT_COPY_OK` to retain it. Settings supplies no secure or
masked Input configuration, so this payload is actual committed text without
implicit redaction. Metadata is proven active frame plus UNKNOWN cause, without
an invented input index, activation or submit. The editor and its storage must
remain live and unchanged by observers until the outer call and renderer finish.

Bool, number, choice and text payloads now expose `reason`, currently EDIT.
The explicit reset helper reports RESET as described below. These **unreleased event structs** changed size: rebuild all C
consumers. Legacy Settings options/state/results and entrypoints are unchanged.


`cui_settings_reset_page_events(root, page_index, page, query, handler)` is the
explicit programmatic reset facade. `reset` is the exact old helper result;
`boolean_count`, `number_count`, `choice_count` and `text_count` count actual typed
callbacks. Root must be nonzero; page must be supplied; `page_index` is your real
source page index. Metadata has SOURCE_PROGRAMMATIC only, without input index,
frame or activation. Payload target is root; field IDs use the original item index.

Each matching built-in is reset once, its old `on_change` runs at its old time,
then the observer compares the final owner/revision. Disabled fields are included.
Same-value defaults still run old callbacks but produce no typed callback unless
that callback changes the final value. Number equality and finite flags match
EDIT. Text compares revision even if final bytes equal entry; UTF-8 is borrowed.
No draft, Number bounds or `last_value` synchronization is added by the helper.

Custom `reset` wins, returns legacy success, does not call old `on_change`, and has
no typed observation, even if the item has scalar pointers. Custom rendering alone
does not disable a built-in reset. Missing defaults and unmatched items are silent.
A failed text replacement preserves its old failure/no-callback behavior and later
items still run. A malformed later group returns `reset=false` after prior effects;
counts and notifications remain, with no rollback. Missing handlers preserve all
old work. The old helper remains available unchanged.


The Styled reset button uses this same reset operation once, at its original place
before field submission. RESET callbacks therefore precede any ensuing EDIT
callbacks. For example, a Number default of 20 with maximum 10 reports RESET to 20,
then the old adapter bounds pass reports EDIT to 10; no bounds or draft work moves.
Reset success and old callback ordering remain unchanged, including same-value
callbacks and custom-reset omission. Counts in `cui_settings_event_result` include
both reasons and saturate independently.

UI reset metadata is frozen before the first reset write. Exactly one matching
activation with a genuine accepted snapshot retains its source/index/activation;
`activation.target` stays the reset button ID while metadata target is Settings.
Multiple matching activations, or unavailable snapshot evidence, get only the
proven frame with UNKNOWN cause. The old Button aggregate remains one reset; input
is never replayed. Passive/layout-only/inert calls preserve legacy work but do not
notify. Disabled **fields** remain eligible for an explicit enabled reset action.
No reset activation/lifecycle/COMMIT event or rejection semantics is introduced.
documents.docs/SIDEBAR.md:
# Sidebar

The module follows the frozen GPUI Kit 0.7.1 `component/src/sidebar` family:
Sidebar, SidebarHeader, SidebarFooter, SidebarGroup, SidebarMenu,
SidebarMenuItem and SidebarToggleButton. There is no separate frozen base
Sidebar; CUI separates its pure cache/motion model and event behavior from
styled rendering.

`cui_sidebar_state_init` attaches a caller-owned cache with capacity 1..1024.
The cache and state must remain valid through `cui_end_frame`; they allocate no
memory. Entries, menu descriptors and callbacks are borrowed for their render
call. Each entry is a top-level virtual-list item with a unique wrapper ID,
positive estimated height, revision, content callback and user pointer. Wrapper
IDs must differ from the IDs of controls/components submitted by their callback.
Cached fields are inspection-only. Change an entry revision when content outside
the rendered range changes its height. Stable IDs retain measurements through
reordering; changing list count resets scroll position, matching source list
reset behavior.

The virtual list renders the visible range plus 30% of host-window height on
either side. Supply `viewport_height` for a sidebar inside a shorter pane;
otherwise the sidebar height is the fallback. Unknown entries use declared
estimates. Rendered entries receive actual measured heights after layout and
schedule a follow-up frame only when retained bounds change. Tall custom entries
can render their own inner virtual list. Header and footer stay outside the
scrolling body; the body handles wheel, draggable scrollbar and scrollbar
keyboard input through the existing Scroll primitives. First layout and changed
header/footer/available extent use retained geometry for scroll metrics, then
correct it in the measurement frame. The scrollbar's right edge follows parent
layout immediately, including percentage widths. The application drives frames
until `cui_needs_redraw` is false.

Defaults are width 255, left side, expanded, Icon collapse mode and a 200ms cubic
in-out transition. Icon collapse renders children at 48px immediately and animates
only the surrounding clip width. Offcanvas renders at the expanded target width,
clips/slides to 0, and removes children after the transition; their focus and
activation remain available while closing, as in source. None ignores collapsed
state. Left Offcanvas aligns the child to the end of its shrinking wrapper;
right Offcanvas aligns it to the start. Icon mode reverses those alignments.
Reopening during close cancels unmounting. Retargeting samples the current width
to avoid discontinuities; the frozen source instead starts at the previous
target. Reduced motion or duration 0 applies the target and unmount immediately.
`now_seconds` is caller-owned; backward timestamps hold the last sample. There
are no detached timers, and settled animation does not invalidate continuously.

A negative width grows within its parent; `width_percent=true` uses a fraction
in 0..1. These nonpixel widths skip width animation, matching source. Zero plain
width means the 255px default. Height 0 fills the parent. `custom_box` supplies
surface appearance; layout, collapse dimensions and padding remain controlled
by Sidebar. Source clears root padding, so CUI does too. The default background,
foreground, border and accent use the five Sidebar Theme tokens. The left side
has a right border; the right side has a left border.

Header/footer callbacks receive effective Icon-collapse state. The sidebar's
outer header inset is top 12/horizontal 12 expanded,8 collapsed. Footer uses
bottom 12/horizontal 12 expanded and top 8/horizontal 8/bottom 12 collapsed. Icon
mode adds 8px between header/body/footer. `cui_sidebar_header` and
`cui_sidebar_footer` provide the separate source 8px padded rounded hover/selected
surface. Their content owns layout and decisions about hiding its labels. An
optional `on_activate` is a pointer-only Group action for host dropdown/menu
composition; it introduces no Tab stop. Descendant controls keep activation
priority. Header/footer content gets a temporary Theme copy with `text` set to
the inherited Sidebar foreground/accent foreground. Do not retain that pointer.

`cui_sidebar_group` exposes a labelled Group and a 32px label row with font 12,
horizontal 8 inset and 70% Sidebar foreground. Icon collapse omits that row.
Group callbacks can compose `cui_sidebar_menu`; the menu uses 8px item gaps.
Menu items expose TreeItem semantics with accessible-name override, controlled
active selection, expanded/level/controls metadata, source 28px expanded rows,
8px padding/gap and rounded corners. Icon collapse centers the icon, omits label,
suffix, caret and descendants, and preserves submenu state. Nested descriptors
can retain their own collapsed flag; the top-level menu overrides it with the
menu's collapsed argument, as in source.

A submenu requires persistent `cui_sidebar_item_state`. `default_open` initializes
it once when the item first has children. Removing and re-adding children retains
that state. An optional `expanded` pointer supplies a controlled value; requests
go to `on_expand` and the owner updates the pointed value. `click_to_open` takes
precedence over `click_to_toggle`; neither is enabled by default. Row activation
always invokes `on_activate`, while a caret toggles expansion without invoking
the row callback. Validated queued activations are reduced in input order rather
than collapsed to a single action. The source disabled flag suppresses only row
activation and hover: the separate caret and suffix controls stay independently
enabled. `disable_caret` is an explicit additional option. The submenu rule sits
at 14px and children start at 25px, including its 1px border and 10px inset; children
have 4px gaps and 2px vertical padding.

For an account tree, retain one state per expandable account in your application
struct. Initialize it to zero once, rather than resetting it in the frame loop:

```c
typedef struct { cui_sidebar_item_state account; } mail_sidebar_state;

void draw_accounts(cui_context *ui, const cui_theme *theme, mail_sidebar_state *state) {
    const cui_sidebar_menu_item folders[] = {
        {.id = cui_id_from(ui, "account/inbox"), .label = CUI_STR("Inbox"),
         .icon = CUI_STR("inbox")},
        {.id = cui_id_from(ui, "account/archive"), .label = CUI_STR("Archive"),
         .icon = CUI_STR("archive")}
    };
    const cui_sidebar_menu_item account = {
        .id = cui_id_from(ui, "account"), .label = CUI_STR("alice@example.com"),
        .state = &state->account, .default_open = true, .click_to_toggle = true,
        .children = folders, .child_count = sizeof folders / sizeof folders[0]
    };
    cui_sidebar_menu(ui, cui_id_from(ui, "accounts"), theme, &account, 1, false);
}
```

Add `on_activate` and `user` to folder descriptors to select a mailbox. Descriptor
arrays may be rebuilt each frame; their state pointers must remain valid. Omitting
`state` does not create context-owned expansion state. `CUI_STR("Inbox")` also
works in a static descriptor initializer; runtime strings use `cui_string`.

Named icons use the actual context-owned Icon resource helper; no text glyphs
or rectangle placeholders represent them. The four panel toggle icons and
ChevronRight are in the default embedded bundle. The caret is 16px and rotates
90 degrees when open. Menu named icons default 16px; `icon_content` supports an
application-owned custom Icon/path/state/style. It receives the row foreground
through the temporary Theme's `text`. `label_content` and `custom_label_box`
bridge source label styling, with accessible text still supplied by the label
or accessibility override. Suffix content gets the same inherited foreground.
Callbacks own any further controls, loaders or persistent state they compose.
The current text API does not expose font weight, so source active-item
`font_medium` emphasis is represented by its accent colors, without fake bold.

Collapsed icon items use the real delayed Tooltip primitive. Supply
`tooltip_options.viewport` with the host viewport; the default side is Right,
including a right-side Sidebar, as in source. Default open delay is 500ms. An item
state is needed for this lifecycle; iconless items have no collapsed tooltip.
`context` runs after the item and can compose the existing ContextMenu helper
with application-owned menu state/actions. Header/footer host actions can open
those menus or other popup components; the module does not invent a second
menu manager. Popup helpers retain their own viewport/activation contracts.

The toggle is a 24px Small ghost button with a 16px panel-left/right-open/close
icon, controlled collapsed state and `on_change`. Supply an accessibility label:
the source toggle has no implicit accessible name. Its owner updates the
Sidebar's collapsed option. Ordinary Tab and Enter/Space activate item/caret
controls in CUI; the source row only supplies pointer click behavior, so row
keyboard activation is an explicit accessibility improvement. No invented
roving arrow-key tree policy replaces the source's composition. Sidebar widths
and row sizes follow source; it does not claim four selectable sizes where the
frozen API has no Sizable interface.

The browser gallery forwards pixel wheel deltas as precise CUI scroll events for Scrollable, Sidebar and VirtualList. Fractional deltas retain their distance rather than being multiplied by the widget's discrete wheel step. Native hosts can opt into the same contract with `cui_event.scroll_precise = true`; discrete wheel events continue to use the configured step. Sidebar's absolute content position follows its scroll model, while the scrollbar stays anchored in the viewport.

# Sidebar ancestral clipping

Scrolled sidebar SVG icons could overlap the fixed header/footer even though the
body viewport already clipped ordinary rows and text. The pinned Clay renderer
paints absolute descendants as separate floating roots. Its synthetic scissor
command has `userData == NULL` and the bounds of only the nearest clipping
ancestor (often a menu row). The body scissor belongs to another root and is no
longer active when that icon is painted. Intersecting the renderer's current clip
stack alone therefore cannot recover the missing body constraint.

Core draw conversion now resolves that synthetic command through the pinned
Clay floating-root metadata and its existing derived command ID. It intersects
the nearest clip bounds with all clipping ancestors recorded in the CUI node
chain. Ordinary scissor commands receive the same intersection. Clip push/pop
structure, draw order and icon bitmap geometry remain unchanged; a completely
hidden descendant receives a zero-area clip. No backend, Sidebar layout, public
API or vendored Clay changes are required.

Explicit detached portals retain their escape behavior: their CUI parent chain
ends at the portal root, so descendants inherit clips inside the portal but do
not inherit the original sidebar/body clip. Absolute children remain attached
and inherit the full chain. This follows the same ancestry already used for CUI
hit bounds, bringing icon paint clipping into agreement with hit testing.

## Regression evidence

`test_sidebar` renders actual registered folder SVG bitmaps through a real
Sidebar with fixed header/footer, ten menu rows and an expanded nested folder.
It samples nonzero source alpha at destination pixel centers under the emitted
clip stack and rejects any visible icon pixel outside the body viewport. It also
checks visible text bounds and clicks hidden rows above/below the viewport.
Expanded and icon-collapsed sidebars are tested at two scroll positions. The
final test fails against the original `ddd0ae3` Core at the assertion that a
visible folder pixel lies within the viewport's vertical extent, and passes with
the conversion fix. A rect-only regression would miss this separate-root case.

`test_core` independently checks an absolute child nested under an oversized
clipping row: its effective clip must equal the outer viewport intersection.
The same scene opens a detached portal and an absolute child inside it outside
the original viewport, and verifies that its own clip remains visible.

The browser regression builds the actual WASM gallery and tracks the Files
folder bitmap's nonzero alpha through its emitted clip stack while scrolling in
expanded/collapsed modes. It checks top/bottom leakage without treating the
fixed header toggle or footer settings icon as body content:

```sh
python3 scripts/build_web.py --output build/web
uv run tests/web/test_sidebar_clipping.py --directory build/web --chromium /path/to/chrome
```

Validation on this branch: strict-warning native build; 93/94 CTests pass (the
only failure is the expected stale generated `dist/cui.h`, owned by the
integrator); ASAN/UBSAN Core and Sidebar tests pass; the browser regression
passes against pinned Zig 0.16.0 output and Chromium. The integrator must
regenerate the distribution header before publication. The test requires
Playwright 1.58.0 and an installed Chromium fixture; it does not install a browser.

The metadata lookup intentionally targets the pinned Clay implementation already
used privately by Core. A Clay version update must retain or revise the
synthetic-scissor lookup and rerun these paint-stack/pixel and detached-portal
regressions. This fix does not change viewport sizing, virtualization estimates,
row layout, portal focus behavior, or scrolling policy.

# Sidebar row activation events

This additive C slice provides Base and Styled **row activation notifications**
and typed item expansion and collapse requests. Header/footer actions remain later
slices. Legacy Sidebar callbacks, results, layouts and retained cache lifetimes are
unchanged; no component parity or binding coverage is promoted.

```c
#include <cui/cui_sidebar_events.h>
static void opened(void *user, const cui_sidebar_activation *event) {
    cui_id *last_item = user;
    *last_item = event->item; /* Application-owned output, not active item storage. */
}
static void render_menu(cui_context *ui, const cui_theme *theme,
                        const cui_sidebar_menu_item *items, size_t count,
                        cui_id *last_item) {
    cui_sidebar_menu_event_result result = cui_sidebar_menu_events(
        ui, 100, theme, items, count, false,
        (cui_sidebar_item_handler){.on_activate = opened, .user = last_item});
    (void)result;
}
```

Call the render helper during normal frame composition. The existing
`cui_sidebar.h` also exposes the new declarations. The Base entrypoint is
`cui_base_sidebar_item_events(ui, item, collapsed, level, handler)` and returns
`cui_sidebar_item_event_result`, containing the unchanged legacy `control` result.
The Styled menu returns `cui_sidebar_menu_event_result`, not one row's open state.
`valid` means argument/tree validation succeeded. Styled `submitted` is the old
menu submission bool, including inert/layout-only composition; neither flag implies
an activation. `activation_count`, `request_count` and `change_count` count actual typed observer
calls, zero for each missing observer. Saturating counts expose `count_overflow`.

Each `cui_sidebar_activation` contains pointer-free common metadata, actual `item`
ID and nesting `level`. Its kind is ACTIVATE, including repeated invocations of the
same row. Base metadata targets the row; Styled metadata targets the public menu ID.
A copied activation snapshot, when available, retains its original row target.
Do not sort by event index: Styled reduces/paints in item traversal order, so input
indices can decrease across rows. Every actual row invocation notifies; there is no
aggregate-last reconstruction or after-frame dispatch.

Evidence is frozen at the existing row branch **before** expansion or legacy
callbacks. Existing expansion write/request and `on_expand` run first, then existing
`on_activate`, then the typed observer synchronously, before final semantics/paint.
There is no second reduction, early semantic registration, acceptance decision or
observer veto. Legacy owner redirection of uncontrolled state is preserved. A missing
old activation callback does not prevent typed notification; a missing typed handler
does not prevent normal legacy mutation. Caret-only expansion is not row activation.
Defaults/initialization, disabled rows, inert/layout-only work and omitted children
do not generate activation notifications.

Real pointer, touch and keyboard paths use genuine accepted snapshots when available.
The existing Core has a tested accessibility-focus/Enter transition where legacy row
activation exists but a copied accepted snapshot is unavailable. The fallback carries
only genuine local frame/index and explicit input source; HAS_ACTIVATION remains
absent. Presence flags alone establish evidence; empty snapshot fields prove nothing.
TREEITEM accessibility **ACTIVATE is unsupported** and rejected at queue ingress.
Accessibility FOCUS followed by keyboard activation is tested separately; this does
not establish accessibility activation parity. No Core allowlist or routing changes.

Existing callback input mutation remains existing behavior. In particular, consuming
later ordinary mouse input does not cancel its cached activation at this seam;
explicit `cui_cancel_event_activation` does. Tests preserve both outcomes. The new
observer does not reinterpret consumption as a notification veto.

## Expansion ownership and order

Set `on_expand_request` and/or `on_expand_change` on `cui_sidebar_item_handler`.
Both receive `const cui_sidebar_expansion_event *` containing copied metadata,
actual item ID/level and `previous`/`value` booleans. These handler and result fields
extend an **unreleased branch API**: rebuild consumers together with the library.
Zero and designated initializers remain source compatible; legacy Sidebar public
layouts are unchanged.

With `item.expanded != NULL`, the existing operation remains a controlled request.
The legacy `on_expand` runs first, followed by typed REQUEST with the frozen previous
owner value and requested next value. The component never assigns owner storage.
The typed request handler may synchronously assign **that explicit expanded bool**;
rejection simply leaves it unchanged. Each later input rereads actual owner state.
Repeated rejected toggles therefore request the same next value; accepted toggles
alternate. Even if the legacy callback already accepts, the typed event remains a
request, not a confirmed CHANGE. A click-to-open attempt already at open does not
invoke either old or typed expansion callbacks.

With `expanded == NULL`, the existing state write and old callback happen once.
Typed CHANGE reports the actual final `state.open`, only if it differs from the
frozen previous state. Legacy redirection back to the previous value emits no CHANGE,
even though the old `expansion_changed` attempt flag remains true. Initialization,
owner-only programmatic changes and maintenance do not notify. The typed CHANGE
observer cannot mutate active state.

For a row that expands, order is old expansion → typed expansion → old activation →
typed activation. Caret-only expansion invokes no row activation observer. Metadata
is frozen before old callbacks, even if they cancel the current input afterward.
Base expansion target is the item ID and Styled target is the menu ID; copied
activation.target remains the actual row or caret Button. Caret accessibility
ACTIVATE is genuinely supported and tested separately from unsupported TREEITEM
activation. Existing `disable_caret`, collapsed/omitted and passive policies remain;
a disabled row does not implicitly disable its separate caret in the legacy API.

## Collapse toggle requests

`cui_base_sidebar_toggle_events(ui, id, options, handler)` and
`cui_sidebar_toggle_button_events(ui, id, theme, options, handler)` return
`cui_sidebar_toggle_event_result`. Its `activated` is the unchanged legacy toggle
bool; `valid` records argument validation. `request_count` counts actual typed calls
and `count_overflow` reports saturation. A valid inert/layout-only submission has
no activation or request count. A missing handler still permits normal legacy work.

Use a separate `cui_sidebar_collapse_handler` with `on_request`/`user`. The callback
receives `cui_sidebar_collapse_request { event, previous, value }` with REQUEST
metadata targeting the public toggle ID. For example:

```c
static void collapse_requested(void *user, const cui_sidebar_collapse_request *request) {
    bool *owner_collapsed = user;
    *owner_collapsed = request->value; /* Optional acceptance of the request. */
}
```

The reducer starts a local bool at the entry `options.collapsed`, then flips that
local bool for each existing activation. With entry false and three inputs, requests
are `(false,true)`, `(true,false)`, `(false,true)`. The old `on_change` runs before
the typed request for each activation. Both callbacks may assign an external owner
collapsed bool, but **neither assignment redirects the active local flip sequence**.
The caller supplies an updated owner value in a later submission. These are requests,
not notifications of confirmed owner changes; no collapse CHANGE is emitted.

Genuine metadata is captured before the old callback. The original semantics
`expanded = !options.collapsed` and the Styled icon/paint also retain the entry
snapshot for that submission, even after an owner accepts or rejects. The toggle
has already claimed its same-ID mouse activations before callbacks;
late explicit cancellation does not clear those claimed slots. Consuming an
accessibility action still clears it, preserving existing Core behavior. No silent
semantic/visual resynchronization, second reduction or aggregate reconstruction is
introduced. The narrow permitted typed mutation is assignment of the external
collapsed owner bool; active options/input/item storage and context teardown remain
unsupported. Handler/payload copies have the same lifetime rules below.

Tests compare old/new local value sequences, aggregate bool and Styled command
geometry/colors; prove legacy-then-typed ordering despite divergent owner writes,
entry-snapshot semantics, repeated requests, pointer/touch/keyboard/genuine Button
accessibility, missing handlers, disabled/inert/layout-only work, invalid arguments,
frozen current evidence after legacy consumption of accessibility activations, and
copied metadata after context destruction. Header/footer observers are documented below.

Handler, user and payload pointers are borrowed only during submission. Copying the
pointer-free payload preserves it through later frames, omission and context teardown;
IDs do not retain live rows. Typed observers may update unrelated application outputs,
but, apart from the controlled expansion/collapse REQUEST assignments above, must not mutate active item arrays/labels/child state/input storage, recurse into
UI composition, remove active storage or destroy the context. Context destruction
during dispatch remains unsupported; there is no fake teardown guard. Defer structural
changes and resource teardown until outer submission and renderer consumption finish.

`tests/unit/test_sidebar_events.c` proves repeated/net-zero Base activations,
legacy expansion/activation/typed order, old/new results and callback counts, pointer,
touch, keyboard, rejected accessibility activation, focus+keyboard, missing handlers,
legacy state redirection, caret exclusion, disabled/passive/omitted paths, nested
levels, traversal with decreasing indices, preserved consume/cancel behavior and
copied lifetime. Expansion tests cover controlled rejection/new-handler acceptance/legacy acceptance, repeated requests, actual changes and redirected net-zero suppression, precise callback order, frozen evidence after legacy cancellation, missing observers, passive work, genuine caret accessibility/touch and Styled forwarding. Styled legacy/new paint command types/bounds/colors are compared;
this is scoped geometry/paint evidence, not full renderer parity. Existing Sidebar
and Settings tests and strict C++17 header compilation also pass. Native CTest runs
only through `python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir <external-build>` (private Xvfb).

Bridge Sidebar has separate retained state and queued generic notifications. No
Python/JS/TS/Go/Rust API automatically gains these immediate per-item notifications
or synchronous expansion requests. SDK/module/export wiring is integrator work.

## Header and footer actions

`cui_sidebar_header_events` and `cui_sidebar_footer_events` take the existing
section options plus `cui_component_activation_handler` and return
`cui_component_action_result`. There is no Base section counterpart.

```c
cui_component_action_result result = cui_sidebar_header_events(
    ui, header_id, theme, header_options,
    (cui_component_activation_handler){on_header_action, app});
```

Each actual activation freezes ACTIVATE metadata before the existing
`options.on_activate`, then calls the typed observer. Repeated invocations notify
separately. `activation_count` counts observer calls; a missing observer reports
zero while legacy callbacks and content still run. A typed-only handler works
without a legacy callback. `submitted` reports successful section composition,
including inert/layout-only submissions; it does not imply an action.

These GROUP surfaces set `pointer_activatable`: existing Core routing supports
pointer/touch and accessibility ACTIVATE. The earlier pointer-only checkpoint
wording was incomplete. No keyboard routing or new focusability is introduced.
Legacy accessibility consumption can suppress later actions; already frozen
current evidence remains intact. Handler/user/payload borrowing and unsupported
active-context destruction follow the same lifetime rules above. No retained
handler, queued foreign callback, or binding export is added.

Focused tests cover both surfaces, repeated mouse activation, touch, genuine
accessibility activation and consumption, old-before-new ordering, typed-only
and legacy-only paths, omitted handlers, inert/layout-only work, invalid arguments,
and copied payload lifetime. Existing Sidebar and Settings regressions remain
part of the bounded verification.

# Simple Menu command notifications

`cui_menu_events` adds synchronous per-command notifications to Styled Simple Menu. It takes the same arguments as `cui_menu`, followed by a `cui_menu_command_handler`, and returns `cui_menu_command_result` from [MenuTree events](MENU_EVENTS.md). Existing List options/layout, Select and Combobox observers, legacy Menu behavior and the 78-family manifest remain unchanged. This is not a DropdownButton facade or a binding API.

```c
static void activated(void *user, const cui_menu_command *event) {
    cui_id *last = user;
    *last = event->command;
}
cui_menu_command_result result = cui_menu_events(
    ui, trigger, &theme, cui_string("Commands"), items, count, &action,
    &popup, options, (cui_menu_command_handler){activated, &last_command});
```

Submit either the legacy or new Menu entry point once per frame. Opening the trigger emits no leaf command. Each accepted flat-list activation writes the caller's action and active cursor, runs existing List activation then confirmation hooks, and finally notifies the command observer. The command ID and input metadata are frozen before those callbacks. This private seam does not expose new public List callback fields.

Command notifications are ACTIVATE, including repeated same-ID activation: A→A→B reports three commands even when the initial action was A. The full flat-list pass completes before Menu closes and restores focus. This differs from MenuTree's closing-command early return; forwarding does not transfer that policy. Owner updates during a callback can affect later reduction; consuming later events suppresses their subsequent handling. A notification cannot veto or roll back applied state. Missing handlers preserve normal mutation and closing with `command_count == 0`. `legacy_activated` retains the aggregate bool, even if a handler writes the action back to its original value. Counts saturate and overflow does not stop dispatch.

`event.target` is the public trigger; `command` is the reducer's actual confirmed item. Real mouse/touch, keyboard and supported MENUITEM accessibility events retain their genuine source, frame and event index. Current registration follows reduction, so ordinary dispatch has no copied activation snapshot. No trigger-opening event, focused target or programmatic state write is invented as activation evidence. Existing flat-list non-pointer confirmation uses its active cursor; accessibility target identity does not independently replace that cursor. This slice preserves that behavior and does not claim complete accessibility parity. Flat descriptors do not gain MenuTree check/radio/submenu features.

The payload is borrowed synchronously and pointer-free copies survive the frame/context. Keep descriptor/value/state/user/render storage alive through submission. Direct mutation of in-flight navigation, freeing active storage, recursive submission and context destruction during callbacks remain unsupported; defer removal/shutdown until submission/frame completion. Existing disabled/inert/layout-only, popup dismissal and scrolling invalidation rules apply. Existing custom row rendering remains in the same painting phase; a closing frame completes reduction without repainting the closed popup.

[test_simple_menu_events.c](../tests/unit/test_simple_menu_events.c) proves repeated A/A/B, complete-pass close timing, pointer/touch/key/accessibility commands, actual legacy-hook ordering and frozen command identity, owner writes/later consumption, missing/disabled/inert/omitted handlers, custom row rendering through old/new paths, scroll rejection and copied lifetimes. Legacy Choice plus Select/Combobox event tests protect neighboring reducers. Native validation uses the invisible wrapper:

```sh
python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir build -- -R '^(simple_menu_events|choice|select_events|combobox_events)$'
```

The integrator registers the test and documentation exports; no generated artifacts or parity promotion are included.
documents.docs/SLIDER_EVENTS.md:
# Controlled Slider events

Include `cui/cui_slider_events.h` for `cui_base_slider_events`. This additive,
drawing-free facade uses the existing controlled double-precision Slider reducer.
Submit it inside a box with the same ID. The legacy
`cui_base_slider_controlled`, `cui_slider_options` binary layout, phase timing and
capture/presentation state remain unchanged.

```c
static void position_request(void *user, const cui_component_slider_request *r) {
    double *owner = user;
    if (r->phase == CUI_SLIDER_UPDATE)
        *owner = r->requested; /* Accept. Leave unchanged to reject. */
    /* COMMIT is a final proposal, not proof the owner accepted an UPDATE. */
}
/* Persistent state: */
cui_slider_state drag = {0};
double position = 0.25;
/* During submission inside a same-ID track box: */
cui_component_slider_result result = cui_base_slider_events(
    ui, track_id, cui_string("Position"), position, &drag,
    (cui_slider_options){.minimum=0, .maximum=1, .step=0.01},
    (cui_component_slider_handler){position_request, &position});
```

This header exposes the Base reducer. Use the separate
[Styled facade](STYLED_SLIDER_EVENTS.md) for themed track/thumb rendering. Source bounds,
clamping, step rounding, pointer capture and normalized float semantics match the
old controlled reducer; requested values and owner snapshots remain double.

## Typed phases and owner decisions

| Phase | Shared metadata kind | `requested` | Result count |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BEGIN | LIFECYCLE | Current owner value at gesture/key start | `begin_count` |
| UPDATE | REQUEST | Proposed clamped/snapped value | `request_count` |
| COMMIT | COMMIT | Final proposed gesture/key value | `commit_count` |
| CANCEL | LIFECYCLE | Gesture starting value | `cancel_count` |

No confirmed CHANGE notification is emitted. BEGIN/CANCEL describe lifecycle,
not proposed UPDATEs; COMMIT does not imply application acceptance. CANCEL does
not restore external owner storage: the owner decides whether to restore its
value from `requested`. State `preview/start/dragging` belongs to the reducer;
do not mutate it from the handler. It is presentation/capture state, not a hidden
confirmed value.

`current` is the immutable value passed to this invocation, including for later
callbacks after an owner assignment. For two Right keys in one submission both
propose from that same entry value, preserving the existing controlled policy.
An active gesture's cancel value can differ from that invocation's `current`.
Owner acceptance is observed on the next submission. Same-call semantics also
retain the entry value. Request input consumption and application acceptance are
separate; rejection does not unconsume or propagate anything.

The old `on_request` and `user` options must both be NULL. Conflicts reject before
submission, state mutation or callback dispatch. A missing new handler is read-only.
Disabling, making read-only, removing the handler or making the range zero-width
cancels an active drag according to the old reducer. If a handler remains, an
option-driven CANCEL is delivered with its precise reason. Removing the handler
cannot deliver a callback; capture still stops and counts stay zero.

## Genuine evidence and copied lifetime

Each input-driven callback carries the actual local frame sequence/event index,
known pointer/keyboard source and a pointer-free scalar input snapshot. All
callbacks from a single key or pointer-down/up event share that input identity;
counts are phase callback counts, not distinct input counts. No activation
snapshot is fabricated for pointer movement, release, generic cancel or keyboard
phase dispatch. `HAS_ACTIVATION` is absent even for BEGIN/COMMIT.

A generic `CUI_EVENT_CANCEL` has UNKNOWN source and no `HAS_SOURCE`; its actual
input type/index still exist. Do not infer a pointer origin just because unused
pointer fields have defaults. Option-driven cancellation has `has_input=false`,
UNKNOWN source and no frame/index/activation presence flags. Its reason is
DISABLED, READONLY or ZERO_SPAN (that precedence if several apply). It is not an
input event or an invented programmatic action. Input-driven reasons are INPUT.
Only presence flags establish shared evidence; zero unused fields are not proof.

The input snapshot deliberately excludes text pointers, inline text, composition
and unrelated event payloads. The entire `cui_component_slider_request` is thus
copyable by value beyond callback/frame lifetime; frame identity remains local
to that context. Handler/user are borrowed for the call only. No registration,
retained callback or event queue is added by the facade.

Do not recursively submit frames/controls, destroy context/state/users, free
active storage or mutate drag state during dispatch. Record teardown/omission
requests in app state and apply them after frame completion/renderer consumption.
Changing the application's owner value is supported; general reentrancy is not.

## Results and verification

`valid/submitted` are true when the existing reducer admitted this active
submission, including disabled/read-only submissions; outside active submission
or on invalid arguments they are false. Later rendering can still fail under
Core's existing frame contract. Counts increment only when the new callback is
actually invoked and saturate at SIZE_MAX with `count_overflow`; dispatch is not
stopped by saturation. Reading/copying results never invokes a callback. Do not
perform the same side effect in both the handler and the frame-count consumer.

`tests/unit/test_slider_events.c` checks actual queued pointer/key batches,
ordered phases, double values, genuine frame/index/source and contact data,
absence of invented activation, owner rejection/acceptance and immutable
same-call values, passive idle frames, copied payload lifetime, semantic snapshots,
Escape/generic/option-driven cancellation, missing-handler read-only cleanup and
invalid/conflicting-option atomicity. Existing `test_slider_controlled.c` and
`test_base.c` remain behavioral regressions for the original path. Native tests
run through `python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir <build>`.

Base and Styled tests establish portable reducer behavior and software rendering.
They do not establish all-family uniformity, browser/physical-touch/GPU acceptance
or bridge/binding exposure. Headers and sources are distributed through the normal
source metadata/amalgamation/SDK tooling.

For themed rendering with the same double-valued phases, use the implemented
[Styled Slider facade](STYLED_SLIDER_EVENTS.md). Foreign request handlers remain unsupported.
