# Software triangle meshes

The deterministic software adapter implements `CUI_DRAW_MESH` and advertises
`CUI_RENDER_MESH`. Expanded vertex triples are borrowed and never modified.
Only XY is transformed by positive scale and origin; ST is interpolated in
screen space. Command bounds do not crop mesh geometry: ancestor clip commands
and the framebuffer viewport determine clipping.

Each pixel is sampled at its center. Triangles are oriented consistently and
use a top-left edge rule, so opposite sides of an exactly shared edge cannot
both blend the same center. Degenerate triangles are empty geometry. Double
precision edge, derivative, and interpolation calculations avoid float product
overflow; bounding boxes are intersected with the clip and viewport before any
integer conversion. Extremely ill-conditioned geometry remains subject to
finite floating-point precision.

Analytic coverage follows GPUI's pre-WGPU 0.3.8 `fs_path_rasterization` shader:
when `length(vec2(dSdx, dSdy)) < .001`, coverage is one. Otherwise it is
`clamp(.5 - (S*S-T)/length(2*S*gradS-gradT), 0, 1)`. Both screen derivatives
participate. At an exactly zero gradient, where shader division is undefined,
the software adapter defines coverage as one for negative `S*S-T`, zero for
positive, and one half for zero. Triangle boundaries themselves are sampled
without extra geometric antialiasing.

Uniform linear premultiplied color is unpremultiplied, clamped to SDR RGB,
sRGB encoded, and quantized to bytes; source alpha is multiplied by analytic
coverage and rounded to a byte. Rendering then uses the adapter's existing
straight-alpha byte-domain source-over blend. This does not provide linear-light
composition, HDR output, GPU bit identity, or full GPUI path API parity.

All meshes in the list are validated before clearing the framebuffer. Invalid
vertex counts, nonfinite inputs, invalid alpha/scale, and transformed bounds
outside the public mesh validity contract return false and preserve the target.
Other command failures retain the software adapter's existing partial-render
behavior. Borrowed arrays must remain valid through render completion.

`tests/unit/test_render.c` checks numeric sRGB/alpha oracles, partial and opaque
coverage with horizontal and vertical S derivatives and nonconstant T, shared
edges in both windings, transforms, clipping, immutable inputs, degenerate and
extreme geometry, and rejection before any framebuffer mutation.
documents.docs/SPEECH.md:
# Speech

The portable provider lifecycle, PCM level meter, SVG SpeechButton and waveform are implemented and tested. An optional SDL input-host example now implements the capture boundary with bounded PCM delivery; real-device operation and system recognizers remain unverified or unimplemented. The following audit records the frozen source contract and the remaining target. Reference: commit `87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`, `crates/component/src/speech/{state,recognizer,level,button,waveform,microphone}.rs`.

The portable layer must model Idle, Connecting, Recording and Stopping. A session owns capture and recognition separately: start recognition first, then capture; stop capture before requesting recognition finish; tear down capture before recognition. Failed starts report an error and preserve the previous transcript. Every asynchronous delivery carries a session generation, and stale deliveries must be ignored. Synchronous provider callbacks must defer their changes until start/push/finish returns. Started precedes provider results. Partial replaces the current hypothesis; Phrase appends literally to committed text and clears the hypothesis. Final keeps the transcript, Cancel clears it, and session teardown clears waveform history. Stop defaults to a three-second timeout and returns the current transcript when it expires. Repeated start/stop/cancel calls must preserve their source no-op semantics.

Providers consume interleaved signed 16-bit PCM, default 16 kHz mono. Recognition availability is distinct from provider presence. An active session stays stoppable if the provider becomes unavailable. Custom capture and recognizer providers are required APIs; platform microphone capture, resampling and system recognizers remain part of the complete target, not implied by a portable fake provider test. Windows system recognition may use an online service; explicit system fallback control must be preserved. Unsupported platforms must report unsupported without fabricating transcripts.

The input meter retains 256 levels, one per 80 ms of audio, carrying partial intervals across pushes. RMS maps -50 dBFS to 0 and 0 dBFS to 1; mapped values below .06 are silence. Attack is .85 and release .3. The waveform clock follows arrivals with phase gain .1 and pace gain .01, bounded to .04–.16 seconds per level, lag 1.75 levels and maximum lead 3. It must remain stable across late/bunched audio deliveries and finite caller timestamps.

SpeechButton is a ghost icon button: microphone at rest, selected stop square while capturing, spinner while Stopping. It hides without providers unless show-unsupported is enabled, then remains disabled. Sizes and accessible labels follow the existing Button APIs; use customizable SVG icons, never text substitutes. SpeechWaveform defaults to width 96 and heights 12/16/20/24. Its capsule width is rounded height/8, clamped 2–4; gap is rounded width times 2.5. Newest levels enter at the trailing edge, silence is a dot, short histories leave the leading edge empty. Clip partial bars and preserve subpixel movement; reduced motion disables between-level scrolling. Capturing uses the primary color, otherwise muted foreground.

Required tests include provider start failure cleanup, synchronous callbacks during every lifecycle call, stale generation rejection, partial/phrase ordering, stop timeout and late final suppression, cancellation and transcript lifetime, PCM batching equivalence, RMS/smoothing thresholds, waveform clock/geometry, unsupported/unavailable button semantics, physical pointer and keyboard toggles, four sizes and reduced motion. Real platform capture/recognition needs separate platform evidence; model tests cannot establish it.


## Portable API and verified boundary

Zero-initialize `cui_speech_state`, provide nonoverlapping caller-owned transcript, message and queue buffers in `cui_speech_workspace`, and call `cui_speech_init` with recognizer and input callbacks. Successful provider starts return non-null session tokens; `close` releases them. Failed starts may return a token for cleanup. All callbacks and reports run on one owner thread. Marshal background audio/recognition to that thread before reporting; these APIs are not a cross-thread queue. Keep state storage alive until every retained sink is retired.

Provider sinks copy UTF-8 text and PCM into the bounded queue, including reports issued inside start/push/finish callbacks. `cui_speech_pump(state, now)` applies queued reports in order; call it when the host receives provider work and at the stopping deadline. One pump processes its initial queue length so a provider cannot recurse indefinitely. Queue overflow terminates an active session with Capacity; transcript overflow preserves the prior complete transcript. Malformed UTF-8 and stale-generation reports are rejected. Dispose invalidates sinks and preserves the generation counter across reinitialization. Completion listeners may start another session; disposal during pumping is ignored. Provider callbacks must only report through their sink, not invoke lifecycle functions.

`cui_speech_button` uses existing themed SVG icon controls and four Button sizes. Localized start/stop/unavailable labels are accepted. `cui_speech_waveform` draws clipped capsule bars with floating-point positions, source size metrics, explicit dimensions/color and reduced-motion control. Both the per-waveform option and the Core host preference suppress continuous animation. Hosts own scheduling and call `cui_speech_pump`; rendering controls alone does not process asynchronous reports or implement a microphone. The provider-free button hides by default or renders disabled when requested.

Tests cover lifecycle event order, PCM copying, synchronous callbacks, failed input cleanup, transcript preservation, stale delivery across both sessions and dispose/reinit, stop timeout, cancellation, reentrant completion/restart, bounded storage, UTF-8 rejection, meter batching/history/smoothing, waveform geometry/capacity, real SVG draw commands, four sizes, pointer activation, keyboard stopping despite provider unavailability, loading and unsupported semantics. Both standalone base and styled tests pass strict C11 and ASan/UBSan; the isolated worktree CTest run includes both new tests.

Remaining parity work: real-device capture acceptance, platform recognizers and fallback policy, application event-loop/device-removal integration and automatic stop-deadline scheduling, button tooltip composition, inherited layout/style refinements, and live-device/browser verification. No fake transcript or deterministic provider test establishes any of these capabilities.


## Optional SDL input host

The independently buildable [SDL input-host example](../examples/speech_sdl_input/README.md) supplies the existing input-provider interface. Its private SDL callback converts to requested signed interleaved PCM16 and writes a fixed-capacity C11 SPSC ring. The UI thread polls copied samples into CUI and pumps the existing Speech state. Audio callbacks never call CUI. Ring overflow and wake failure terminate the session explicitly; the bound covers host PCM storage, not SDL or operating-system buffers.

```sh
cmake -S examples/speech_sdl_input -B /tmp/cui-speech-input-build -G Ninja
cmake --build /tmp/cui-speech-input-build
python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir /tmp/cui-speech-input-build
```

This requires CMake 3.20+, a C11 compiler, pkg-config and SDL3 development files (SDL >= 3.2). These commands run four offline Linux fixtures and never open a microphone. They test injected lifecycle/error handling, real unbound SDL conversion, intercepted SDL device operations and concurrent producer delivery. The example's CMake file records exact compiler and linker settings. It is an optional application-host example, not a new Core API or a built-in recognizer.

For actual capture, the application supplies a recognizer and explicitly initializes SDL audio. See the example's integration section for start/poll/pump/shutdown ordering, timer and wake obligations, device-removal handling and OS permission limits. The host must outlive all provider callbacks; generation checks do not make reports safe after state storage is freed. macOS/Windows compilation, microphone hardware and recognition accuracy still require separate evidence.

## Optional macOS recognizer host

The [macOS recognizer host guide](../examples/speech_macos_recognizer/README.md)
provides a bounded C11 mailbox/lifetime layer and a private Objective-C
Speech/AVFoundation transport. The C11 provider uses the existing Speech API;
no platform types enter public headers. Actual Apple Debug/Release compilation
and injected transport tests pass. It requires explicit application consent,
on-device service availability and a separate PCM input provider. Live consent,
microphone capture and recognition acceptance remain unverified. Windows/Linux
system recognizers and full Speech family parity remain unfinished.
documents.docs/SPINNER.md:
# Spinner

Use `cui_spinner_ex` for the frozen source-style decorative loading icon. It
paints the Loader SVG at 16 logical pixels in `theme.text` by default, rotating
through one turn every 0.8 seconds with quadratic ease in/out. Sizes 12, 14, 16
and 24 correspond to source presets at a 16-pixel rem. Existing `options.size`
remains explicit logical pixels; any positive size up to 4096 is allowed.
The application owns whether loading is happening and when to stop submission.
Spinner adds no status role, busy relationship, focus stop or completion event.
Announce the actual operation using the application's semantic tree when needed.

```c
/* Persistent application state: one instance per independent spinner. */
cui_loading_motion loading_motion = {0};

/* During an active frame: */
cui_spinner_options options = cui_spinner_options_default();
options.now_seconds = host_now_seconds;
options.size = 24;
options.custom_color = true;
options.color = (cui_color){220, 40, 90, 255};
options.reduced_motion = user_reduced_motion;
cui_loading_motion_result result;
if (cui_spinner_ex(ui, loading_id, &theme, &loading_motion, options, &result)) {
    /* Absolute deadline in host_now_seconds' clock domain; zero means idle. */
    next_wake_seconds = result.next_wake_seconds;
} else {
    /* Report submission failure; inspect the Core frame error as appropriate. */
}
```

Keep motion state between frames. Initial zero state starts at the first
successful supplied time; explicitly zero it to restart. Time is finite [0,1e12],
rewinds clamp to the last sample, and duration zero selects 0.8 seconds. Explicit
durations must be finite [0,60]. Context or option reduced motion samples raw
phase zero, **calls custom easing at zero**, and returns inactive/deadline zero
with no perpetual invalidation. A shifted easing therefore freezes at its shifted
angle. This corrects the earlier `cui_spinner_ex` behavior that skipped easing
under reduced motion; a nonfinite reduced easing now fails atomically rather than
being silently bypassed. The legacy pure `cui_loading_motion_sample`, Skeleton
and the eight-dot `cui_spinner` keep their prior contracts. Moving results request the next sample at 60 Hz. Hidden
or clipped submission does not automatically cancel application scheduling; omit
hidden spinners when appropriate. Stop scheduling when the operation completes.

## Named rem sizes and custom pixels

An optional descriptor preserves the source distinction between named rem sizes
and fixed custom pixels:

```c
cui_spinner_sizing sizing = {.size = CUI_SPINNER_LARGE, .rem_size = 20};
options.sizing = &sizing; /* Large = 1.5 * 20 = 30 logical pixels. */
/* Or fixed pixels, unaffected by rem or theme font changes: */
sizing = (cui_spinner_sizing){.size = CUI_SPINNER_CUSTOM, .pixels = 64};
```

XS/S/M/L multiply rem by .75/.875/1/1.5. A zero named `rem_size` selects 16 logical
pixels; applications pass their root rem explicitly. This is independent of the
theme's text font size. Named rem must be finite [0,4096] and the resolved size
must be in (0,4096]. CUSTOM uses only finite `pixels` in (0,4096]; its rem is ignored.
When `sizing` is non-NULL it overrides `options.size`, even if the latter is
invalid. NULL retains the old explicit-pixel/default behavior. No automatic
ambient rem scope is introduced. The descriptor is copied synchronously and not
retained; keep it alive through the call. Custom paint callbacks receive the
same resolved logical size as the default Icon painter.

`cui_spinner_options` grew: rebuild libraries, generated distributions and callers
with the same headers. Zero-initialize options or use `cui_spinner_options_default`;
old positional/binary layouts must not be mixed with new builds.

## Custom icons and styling

A synchronous paint callback receives the selected size, color and center
rotation in radians. Use any available named icon or a caller-owned Icon state.
Host-loaded icons retain their existing loader/asset lifetime requirements.

```c
static bool paint_loading_icon(cui_context *ui, cui_id id, const cui_theme *theme,
    float size, cui_color color, float radians, void *user) {
    (void)user;
    return cui_icon_named(ui, id, theme, cui_string("loader-circle"),
        (cui_icon_options){.size = CUI_ICON_CUSTOM, .custom_size = size,
            .custom_color = true, .color = color,
            .custom_transform = true,
            .transform = cui_icon_rotation(radians)}) == CUI_ICON_OK;
}
/* Before submission: */
options.paint = paint_loading_icon;
```

`paint_user` and `ease_user` are borrowed only for the call and never retained.
`ease(phase,user)` receives normalized raw phase and may return **any finite
number of turns**, including negative turns and overshoot. `result.phase` keeps
that value; the painter receives its equivalent rotation reduced to [0,2π)
before multiplication, so even very large finite values cannot overflow radians.
At large float magnitudes fractional turns may already be lost to float precision.
NaN and infinity reject before paint. The shared legacy sampler and Skeleton
still require finite [0,1] easing and skip easing under reduced motion. A
failed easing/paint call preserves motion state/result; paint callbacks must
leave their own submission unchanged on failure. Core capacity errors retain
Core's existing failed-frame contract. Borrowed bitmap data in successful draw
lists expires at the next frame as with other Icon commands.

Compose a parent `cui_box` for placement, padding, backgrounds, borders, opacity
and clipping. Supported Icon style fields can also be supplied inside a custom
callback. Icon padding and borders floor the allocated dimensions while the SVG
paints the complete box; see the Icon guide for numeric constraints. Arbitrary
inherited source Icon styling remains an explicit parity limitation.
This guide does not claim complete Icon styling or complete renderer/platform
parity from Spinner tests. Parent composition also supports content-inset padding.
Explicit transparent color remains transparent; it is not a fallback sentinel.

## Source boundary and legacy API

The reference is GPUI Kit 0.7.1 commit
`87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`, `crates/component/src/spinner.rs`
and its `Icon`/`Sizable` implementations. Spinner exposes icon, color, easing
and size. Its source duration is private; CUI additionally exposes a bounded
duration option. Spinner itself has no general Styled implementation, but its
custom Icon can carry style. Default easing comes from pinned GPUI 0.3.8.

The older `cui_spinner` is a compatible eight-dot phase ring with legacy Loading
status semantics and continuous invalidation while moving. It remains available;
use `cui_spinner_ex` for the source-style SVG, decorative semantics and explicit
wake scheduling. The two APIs intentionally have distinct contracts.

## Gallery and verification

The existing **Spinner** gallery entry offers source preset/custom sizes,
Loader/Loader circle/Arrow right, theme/custom/transparent colors, and default
quadratic/linear easing. Copy its example and open this guide from the component.
No extra catalog family is introduced.

`tests/unit/test_spinner_contract.c` verifies all source pixel sizes plus custom
64, default color, transparent color, actual rotated custom SVG pixels, static
reduced-motion restoration, supported Icon background/radius styling, ancestor
opacity and clipping, and decorative/quiescent behavior. Existing
`test_status_motion.c` covers clocks, callbacks, custom easing and rejection.
`tests/web/test_spinner_gallery.py` loads real WASM and exercises controls,
bitmap/pixel changes, reduced-motion quiescence, desktop/390px and DPR 1/2,
copyable usage and guide navigation. Native tests run through
`python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir <build>`; browsers stay headless.
These tests are evidence for the listed behavior, not hardware/GPU acceptance.

The native contract regression additionally compares real asymmetric Arrow right
pixels for quarter-turn/1.25-turn/negative equivalent turns, opposite turns and
large finite whole turns. It checks reduced custom ease(0), nonfinite failure
atomicity, live-to-reduced transitions and named rem/default/custom pixel sizing
through both default and custom Icon painters. These additions do not establish
browser coverage of the new descriptor/overshoot cases; the existing gallery
continues to use explicit pixel sizes and default/linear easing. Complete inherited
Icon styling, source-style bridge Spinner and broader host acceptance remain open.
documents.docs/START_HERE.md:
# Start building with CUI

CUI composes a user interface in portable C11. Your application supplies state and calls components during a frame; CUI produces a draw list and a semantic tree. A renderer paints the list, and a host supplies window events, time, clipboard and other platform services.

CUI is experimental. The gallery contains all 78 comparison entries, but the [feature manifest](gpui-parity.json) records incomplete behavior. Begin with the controls you need and check their documented limits.

## Start with a native application

Follow [Build your first native CUI app](NATIVE_APP_STARTER.md) for a complete
three-page desktop starter, sidebar navigation and a bottom account menu. It
explains dependencies, compiler choice, CMake, Make, static linker flags and
native launch commands. The source is small enough to copy into your own app.

## Try a headless C program

From the repository root:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCUI_BUILD_NATIVE=OFF
cmake --build build
python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir build
./build/hello_world
```

This portable example creates real CUI draw commands and prints their count. It exercises layout without opening a window. A C11 compiler, CMake, Ninja and Python3 are needed for these commands; core CUI itself uses the standard library and vendored Clay.

## Choose your host

| Path | What it does | Next reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Existing native application | Send events to a context and paint its draw list in your renderer | [Embedding contracts](INTERFACES.md) |
| SDL3 workbench | Opens the native gallery when SDL3, FreeType and HarfBuzz are available | [Repository setup](../README.md) |
| Browser | Compiles C to WebAssembly; JavaScript supplies browser input and canvas rendering | [Web gallery build](WEB_GALLERY.md) |
| Portable/headless | Runs layout, interaction and renderer tests without a window | [Core lifecycle](CORE.md) |

The browser gallery is an example host. Applications using CUI do not need a browser engine. Native adapter availability and actual runtime evidence are listed in the [platform matrix](PLATFORM_MATRIX.md).

## Compose a frame

The following function belongs in a host that already created `ui` and a theme. The host owns `clicks`, calls this function for each frame, then passes the returned draw list to its renderer before the next frame starts.

```c
#include "cui/cui_components.h"

cui_draw_list draw_counter(cui_context *ui, const cui_theme *theme,
                           unsigned *clicks, float width, float height,
                           float elapsed_seconds) {
    if (!cui_begin_frame(ui, width, height, elapsed_seconds))
        return (cui_draw_list){0};
    cui_begin_box(ui, cui_id_from(ui, "counter"),
        (cui_box){.width = -1, .height = -1,
                  .padding = 24, .gap = 12,
                  .background = theme->background});
    if (cui_button(ui, cui_id_from(ui, "increment"), theme,
                   cui_string("Increment"), false)) {
        ++*clicks;
        cui_invalidate(ui);
    }
    cui_end_box(ui);
    return cui_end_frame(ui);
}
```

Stable IDs connect this frame's controls to the previous frame's hit regions. Keep domain state outside this function. Frame-owned draw data remains borrowed until the next frame; render it before advancing the context.

## Adapt a real application

Use [responsive containers](RESPONSIVE_LAYOUT.md) for named mobile-first width
policies, container-local pane fitting, and a runnable dashboard with
navigation/account callbacks. Keep one application state while switching between
stacked content, a Menu disclosure and a persistent sidebar. The guide explains
native launch and headless geometry/interaction tests.

Use [reusable typography tokens](TYPOGRAPHY_TOKENS.md) for body/heading/code
roles and per-call overrides; [Typography](TYPOGRAPHY.md) explains actual family
and variant registration. These shipped helpers compose existing CUI layout/text
APIs. They do not imply a CSS engine or advanced typography roadmap completion.

## Learn the interaction model

Read [state and callbacks](IMMEDIATE_AND_STATE.md) for immediate frame composition, retained values/models, return-value events and controlled callbacks. Component headers and the gallery Usage section show the concrete types for each control. Each code block in website documentation has a Copy button.

## Work with an AI coding agent

Use the [copyable agent setup prompt](AI_AGENTS.md). The website also publishes `llms.txt` as a documentation index and `llms-full.txt` as a plain-text bundle. Both are generated from these repository documents, alongside the component-status manifest. The requested `llm.txt` and `llm-full.txt` names are aliases.

## Build with another language

Use [Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go or Rust component builders](BINDING_BUILDERS.md)
to author UI trees and callbacks in your own language. The guide includes native
window build commands and examples; the [coverage table](BRIDGE_COMPONENTS.md)
records supported controls and the limits of each binding. The full component
catalog is still being bound and validated. The [C-host examples](LANGUAGE_BINDINGS.md)
also demonstrate embedding an existing C-authored application.

For composition, start with [Layout](LAYOUT_GUIDE.md), then [IDs and lifetimes](IDS_AND_LIFETIMES.md) and [Debugging](DEBUGGING.md). The [two-file native bundle](NATIVE_APP_STARTER.md) is the standalone consumer path; [agent guidance](AI_AGENTS.md) separates consumer and maintainer workflows.

# Status components

Tag follows the frozen 0.7.1 Tag implementation: `cui_tag_options_default()` is
secondary, medium, filled. Primary/danger/success/warning/info use semantic theme
colors and readable foregrounds. Outline uses a transparent background and intent
foreground. Secondary uses independent secondary/secondary_foreground theme tokens and muted outline text.
Custom colors preserve all three application colors. Palette tags accept the exact
50/200/300/600/800/950 scale colors and explicit dark mode, so applications can
supply their named palette without silently substituting a different palette.
`cui_tag_named_palette` supplies all 21 named frozen palettes, including white
and black, from the pinned default-colors.json six required scale colors.

Small and extra-small use 10px text, 6px horizontal/2px vertical padding, and half
theme radius; medium uses 12px text and 10px/4px padding; large uses 14px text.
Typography scales with the theme font size (14px corresponds to a 16px root).
Explicit radius zero is supported; pill rounding takes priority. Hover reduces
paint alpha to 90 percent. Tags have no built-in click or keyboard action.

`cui_tag` submits a passive label semantic and text. For arbitrary rich children,
call `cui_begin_tag`, submit children using its returned style, then call
`cui_end_tag` with the same ID/style. The style is a plain value owned by the caller;
no callbacks or strings are retained. Begin failure must not be paired with end.
The component style resolver allocates nothing and has no theme implementation
function link dependency. Styled tags require core and status base defaults.

Tag and Marker are implemented in this checkpoint.

Marker accepts up to 32 ordered children: typed icon, typed text, rich content,
and direct custom children. Callback IDs are reserved child IDs, not the enclosing
slot ID. Callback/user/string lifetimes last through the render call. The retained
`cui_marker_state` must remain alive through `cui_end_frame`, because tracked text
bounds update after layout. Initialize it to zero. Explicit widths for custom
children let separator/alignment geometry reserve their space; callback layouts
remain application owned. Default width is 480; set it to the host container width.

Plain and Border start-align by default; Separator centers. Explicit start/end
alignment leaves only the divider on the opposite side. Border adds an 8px bottom
inset and a single bottom edge. Typed icon slots suppress automatically inserted
spinner loading; direct children do not. Typed text shimmer uses twelve nested
clipped glyph overlays, matching the frozen source's twelve-layer feathered band.
Relative spread defaults to 0.3 and clamps to 0.05–1; absolute spread clamps to at
least 1px. Duration defaults to two seconds, with a minimum 1ms. Reverse and once
are supported. The default highlight mixes 20% muted text with 80% of the light/dark theme endpoint in alpha-premultiplied Oklab. If the endpoint has similar HSL lightness, it switches to the opposite endpoint. Applications can override the highlight color. Rich-only content receives
its 0.6–1 opacity pulse in the callback; apply it to that content's paint alpha.
Direct children and icon slots receive opacity 1. Reduced motion paints static text
and provides no animation wake deadline. The base plan returns the next absolute
60Hz host wake while animation runs; the host schedules and invalidates at that
deadline. Passive Marker emits no semantic node by default; an explicit role/name
creates a stable-ID node (for example Status).

Status base now owns only theme-independent defaults/motion validation. Tag style
resolution and palette choices live in components. Marker styled rendering adds
existing `cui_content` spinner dependencies. The base links only math.
Notification manager and rendering are implemented below. Text wrapping and inherited font refinements
are bounded by the existing core text API; custom content can provide its own layout.


## Notification

Initialize `cui_notification_state` with application-owned entry storage (1–128
entries), settings, and optional host hooks. Initialize each descriptor with
`cui_notification_default`, assign a nonzero `{type,key}` ID, then push it with
monotonic host seconds. Distinct keys can share an application type; exact-ID
close and type-wide close are separate operations. Anonymous IDs are generated
by the application. A repeated ID replaces its entry, moves it to newest, and
restarts enter and timeout; replacement does not fire the old close callback.
Capacity rejection and rejected host delivery leave the manager unchanged.

Descriptors, strings, callback code, and callback users are borrowed. They remain
valid while an entry is mounted, and while its system registry record remains
registered. An auto-hidden in-app toast can still have an OS record, so its close
callback does not by itself end these borrowed lifetimes. An explicit dismiss,
clear, replacement, or registry aging ends the corresponding registry borrow.
Do not initialize, push, or advance the same manager from a render callback;
queue structural changes until `cui_end_frame` completes, so tracked retained
bounds still refer to the same entries. Callbacks may request
`cui_notification_dismiss`; action callbacks choose whether to dismiss.
Custom rendering receives a reserved ID, font/color, and opacity; multiply custom
paint alpha by that opacity. No callback or label is retained by core beyond its
ordinary frame semantics.

The pure base manager matches frozen lifecycle rules: 400ms enter, five seconds
present for autohide, then 200ms exit. Each advance crosses at most one phase;
excess time at a phase boundary is discarded. Present timers pause together when
any stack is hovered or contains keyboard focus, including arbitrary custom
children through core focus-scope ancestry. Enter/exit continue while paused.
Window activity is not a pause input. Persistent-only settled stacks have no
wake deadline. Close callbacks fire after exit removal, once. Manual dismissals
remain mounted while ending; visible selection is the newest global
`max_visible` active entries plus every ending entry. It is then grouped into
separate stable stacks for all eight supported anchors.

Render once per frame after application content with `cui_notifications`, a
stable overlay ID, explicit viewport, and host seconds. Schedule the returned
absolute wake deadline and invalidate at that deadline. Per-card placement
can override global settings. Defaults are top right, width 382, ten visible
active entries, margins 16, and top margin 48 (16 plus the reference 32px title
bar); hosts without a title bar can set top margin 16. Auto height is measured
through retained bounds and schedules a follow-up frame when it changes; fixed
height is optional. Entry arrays and state must remain alive through frame end.

Collapsed stacks show three layers, 14px peeks, and 5 percent width reduction
per layer; expanded stacks use actual heights and 14px gaps. A taller rear card
contributes to collapsed stack height. Stack height, item offset, width, and
visibility use bounded critically damped springs with reference 400ms response,
0.1px geometry settling and 0.001 visibility settling. Enter/exit use the
reference cubic Bezier curve and 16px directional slide. Reduced motion uses
settled geometry and static transition paint while retaining lifecycle deadlines.
Body clicks dismiss before calling the click handler. Close buttons appear on
hover or expanded keyboard focus. Middle clicks require matching down/up inside
the card; cancelled captures do not dismiss. Built-in action buttons keep their
own focus and do not automatically dismiss. Titles, messages, custom content,
custom action controls, typed intent icons and custom icon text compose together.
Typed intent overrides custom icon, as in the reference.

To use OS delivery, explicitly configure portable host `send`, `retract`, and
`activate` callbacks and select System or Both delivery. No native OS adapters are
provided by this module. A failed/missing send callback rejects the push. Host
code owns OS availability, stable namespaced tags, activation, and cross-window
ownership. Report OS responses through `cui_notification_system_click`; unknown
or aged-out IDs are ignored. A separate registry retains the newest 100 system
records, including records whose in-app toast auto-hid. Auto-hide does not retract
OS delivery. Explicit exact/type/clear dismissal retracts it; response activates
the host window, retracts, closes any in-app toast, and calls the click handler.

Base status links only math; styled Notification additionally uses core,
existing components buttons, content spinner, and status base. No allocation,
platform, renderer, or default-theme implementation is required by the base.
Renderer limits remain explicit: shadows are two bounded eight-layer rounded
rect approximations of the reference blur/spread/offset, intent icons use portable
text symbols and title font weight uses the current core font. Custom content can supply more
specific icons/typography. Core text wrapping refinements remain limitations described above; this does not establish full native
platform or renderer parity.

Notification cards consume independent `theme.popover` and `theme.radius_lg` tokens for card fill, corners and shadow shape. Marker default highlight now uses the frozen perceptual blend and lightness fallback; exact custom highlight remains supported.


Standalone Shimmer uses `cui_shimmer_text` with caller-owned retained bounds and
`cui_shimmer_options_default`. It paints the unchanged base glyphs plus twelve
clipped highlight layers, using the same alpha-aware perceptual highlight as
Marker. Custom highlight alpha multiplies layer opacity. Duration, relative or
absolute spread, reverse, once and reduced motion follow the frozen source;
`cui_base_shimmer` returns the next absolute host deadline, or zero when settled.
The host supplies elapsed animation seconds and schedules redraws. Explicit IDs
allow identical sibling labels to animate independently. Font size/color may be
set per instance; otherwise theme text styling is used. Optional maximum width
clips the single line without changing glyph positions. Default Label semantics
can be disabled with role None. State must live through `cui_end_frame`.

Standalone Shimmer remains partial: inherited styled-text runs, wrapping,
truncation/ellipsis and font weight depend on the future rich text pipeline.
Reduced-motion text remains visible and settles without continuous redraw.

# Loading motion contracts

The pinned GPUI Kit 0.7.1 source at
`87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34` defines Spinner in
`crates/component/src/spinner.rs`, Skeleton in `skeleton.rs`, and linear Progress
in `progress/progress.rs`. Its GPUI dependency is exactly `gpui-pre=0.3.8`;
`src/elements/animation.rs` defines quadratic `ease_in_out` and the forward/reverse
`bounce` used here.

Spinner defaults to a medium 16-pixel Loader in foreground color, with a
repeating .8-second quadratic rotation. Its source
public customization is icon, color, easing and size; speed is private. Skeleton
is a decorative styled rectangle using the theme skeleton color (secondary by
fallback), a two-second bounced quadratic opacity from 1 to .5, and an optional
secondary half-opacity. It has no loading boolean, busy/status role, accessible
name, completion event, or focus stop. Adding those semantics to the placeholder
would misrepresent the source. Associate loading status with the actual operation
in the application's semantic tree.

CUI's legacy `cui_spinner` dot-ring and `cui_skeleton` cosine/phase APIs retain
existing dimensions, semantics and invalidation. The opt-in `cui_spinner_ex`
and `cui_skeleton_ex` paint the source-style Loader and bounced placeholder.
Neither adds semantics. CUI has no dedicated skeleton theme token, so the new
placeholder uses `theme.secondary`; the secondary option halves alpha again.
Progress's existing determinate cubic-bezier transition and one-second
indeterminate quadratic segment are unchanged. Reduced-motion indeterminate
Progress retains its centered 35% segment and busy progressbar semantics.

## Ownership and scheduling

Use one zero-initialized caller-owned `cui_loading_motion` per independent
animation; it has no allocations. Zeroing it explicitly restarts the timeline.
The first successful sample starts at the supplied clock value. Subsequent
backward time clamps to the last sample. Time must be finite and in [0,1e12];
period must be finite and in (0,60]. For the component options, duration zero
selects the source .8/2-second period; negative, nonfinite and over-60 durations
reject atomically. Changing duration applies the new period to the same origin.

The component returns `active` and an absolute `next_wake_seconds` in the
**supplied clock's domain**. Moving primitives return the next 60 Hz sample;
reduced motion returns phase zero, full base opacity, false activity and deadline
zero. Context reduced motion also overrides the option. Custom easing is not
called while reduced. These APIs do not request perpetual Core invalidation.
Schedule the returned deadline and paint again then, as the gallery does:

```c
options.now_seconds = cui_frame_time(ui);
if (cui_spinner_ex(ui, id, &theme, &motion, options, &result))
    host_deadline = result.next_wake_seconds > 0
        ? host_now + fmax(0, result.next_wake_seconds - cui_frame_time(ui)) : 0;
```

If supplying host time directly, use the result directly. Repeating loading has
no inherent completion; stop submitting it when the operation stops. Activity
means submitted motion is enabled, not that pixels are visible: clipping and
parent visibility do not automatically stop caller scheduling. Hosts may omit
hidden primitives and restart/reset state as appropriate.

Custom easing receives normalized phase (Skeleton first applies its triangular
bounce). It must return finite [0,1]; invalid output preserves state/result and
paints nothing. The custom Spinner paint callback receives color, size and
center rotation in radians; its userdata is borrowed for the synchronous call
and never retained. The default uses the existing bounded context-owned SVG icon
cache, with draw-list bitmap lifetime unchanged. A paint callback returning false
must leave its own paint unchanged; CUI cannot roll back arbitrary user callback
side effects. State/result commit only after success. General Core frame-capacity
errors still follow Core's existing frame error contract.

## Validation

`tests/unit/test_status_motion.c` checks clock start/reset/rewind, default and
invalid durations, callback rejection, finite wakes, reduced quiescence, no
invented Skeleton semantics, custom paint pixels, default SVG/software pixels,
and unchanged Progress transition/indeterminate behavior. It links `cui`,
`cui_software` and native text dependencies. Root owns CMake registration.

`tests/web/test_status_motion.py` runs real WASM in Playwright 1.58.0 with pinned
Chromium 1208 by default (`--chromium` may select 1228). It checks animated frame
progress with finite gallery wake deadlines and no perpetual redraw, actual
canvas/mask pixels, reduced-motion frame and pixel stability, decorative
semantics, and existing Progress busy/reduced-motion behavior. Distribution
regeneration is integrator-owned; stale distribution checks are expected until
that step.

# Application-controlled Stepper navigation

Include `cui/cui_stepper_navigation.h` for `cui_stepper_navigation` and its
unstyled Base sibling. They take a selected index by value and report a typed
REQUEST for each accepted item activation. The application decides whether to
update its own selection. The existing Stepper functions still mutate their
selected-index pointer and the existing aggregate CHANGE observers retain their
timing and meaning.

This closes a specific frozen-source gap: upstream's controlled selected_index
and on_click let the application decide navigation, including a click on the
already selected step. Upstream has no built-in validator or next/back controller.
The compiling [`examples/stepper_navigation/main.c`](../examples/stepper_navigation/main.c)
rejects a confirmation request while payment data is invalid, then accepts a
later request after the application validates it.

The callback receives captured `selected`, `requested` and `count`. A same-index
activation is still a request. Several accepted activations produce several
requests in event order, even when their final target equals the entry selection.
All requests use the same captured selected value. The current call registers
semantics and paints that captured selection throughout; owner updates become
visible on the next submission. A rejected request simply leaves the owner's
selection unchanged. There is no veto return, automatic selection, normalization,
async validation, form ownership or automatic error-status mutation.

`result.valid` means argument preflight succeeded, not completed layout or visible
rendering. `request_count` counts accepted requests independently of a handler.
A missing handler leaves selection untouched and still counts input. Preflight
requires nonzero ID, count <=100, structurally valid title/description pairs and
valid status enums. For nonempty steps selected must be in range; for empty steps
it must be zero. Invalid input registers nothing and dispatches nothing. This is
deliberately stricter than legacy clamping and upstream unchecked high indices;
invalid-input equivalence is not claimed.

Current semantics must successfully accept the activation. Current disabled or
omitted items, cancellation, inert/layout-only work and rejected accessibility
actions do not generate requests. Consumption follows Core's exact policy:
consuming accessibility input cancels its acceptance; consuming an ordinary
already generated Enter activation does not universally revoke it. This helper
does not consume input. Each request freezes its genuine accepted activation
snapshot before calling the application. Metadata targets the Stepper; the
embedded activation targets its item. Frame, index and pointer/keyboard/
accessibility source are evidence, not inferred cause. Copied payloads remain
usable after callback, frame and context lifetime.

Handler/user, steps, strings and theme are borrowed through the call and never
retained. Keep the borrowed array, strings and theme stable until return. The
handler and by-value arguments are captured before callbacks. Store validation
errors in separate owner fields, then rebuild step descriptors on the next
submission; changing a borrowed status in a callback would mix old semantics
with new paint and is unsupported. The example follows this owner pattern.
The callback runs after current semantic registration and before styled painting.
It may update unrelated application form/selection state. Do not mutate the
borrowed descriptors or active input routing/options, recursively submit the
component, destroy the UI/storage, or unwind a foreign exception. Updating the
application owner cannot change this call's captured selection. Further callbacks
still carry that captured value. Later mutation cannot rewrite a payload already
delivered; future input acceptance is not promised to survive forbidden routing
changes.

Styled rendering reuses the legacy private paint path, including horizontal and
vertical layout and explicit caller error/complete statuses. This API does not
add upstream icons, arbitrary children, sizing, checked separators, ListItem
hierarchy or live AT announcements. There is no Python/Node/TypeScript/Go/Rust
binding surface for these requests yet. Source and platform parity remain partial.

# Styled double Slider

Include `cui/cui_styled_slider_events.h` for `cui_slider_events`. This additive
controlled Slider paints a horizontal bar and optional label, using the existing
[Base double event reducer](SLIDER_EVENTS.md) exactly once. The old float-pointer
`cui_slider` API, layout and behavior are unchanged.

```c
static void position_request(void *user, const cui_component_slider_request *r) {
    double *owner = user;
    if (r->phase == CUI_SLIDER_UPDATE)
        *owner = r->requested; /* Accept; leave unchanged to reject. */
}
/* Persistent caller-owned data: */
cui_slider_state drag = {0};
double position = 10000000000.25;
/* During UI submission: */
cui_component_slider_result result = cui_slider_events(
    ui, slider_id, &theme, cui_string("Position"), position, &drag,
    (cui_slider_options){.minimum=10000000000., .maximum=10000000001., .step=.125},
    (cui_slider_style_options){.width=240},
    (cui_component_slider_handler){position_request, &position});
```

`result` has the Base facade's admission flags and actual callback counts;
reading it never dispatches another effect. BEGIN/UPDATE/COMMIT/CANCEL and their
copied evidence retain the Base contract. UPDATE is a request, not proof of owner
acceptance; no confirmed CHANGE is emitted. Legacy `options.on_request` and
`options.user` must both be NULL. A missing new handler is readonly.

## Geometry and style

The public ID identifies the fixed-width hit rectangle. The centered painted bar
has exactly its x and width, so its endpoints map to minimum and maximum. Its
default visual height is 8 logical units inside a 24-unit-high hit area. The label
sits above it and is noninteractive; hiding it does not remove the semantic name.
`cui_bounds(ui, slider_id)` reports the hit rectangle, not the private outer column.

Style zero values select defaults: width240, track_height8, hit_height24 and
font_size from the theme. Positive overrides are logical units, finite and <=4096;
hit_height must be at least track_height. Negative, nonfinite or oversized values
reject the call. Theme radius must be finite, nonnegative and <=4096; it is clamped
to half each painted shape's height. Zero radius stays square.

The default fill uses theme primary; the default track uses primary at 20-percent
alpha. `custom_colors` selects explicit track/fill colors. Disabled controls use
theme muted and its 20-percent-alpha track, including when custom colors exist.
Keyboard/pointer focus adds a 15-percent-alpha theme focus background to the hit
rectangle without a border or padding that could shift normalization endpoints.
No thumb, vertical variant, preset size or animation is implied.

Input uses **previous completed layout** bounds, as Base does. Submit once to
establish geometry. On a width change, this submission's queued input still uses
the last completed width; new paint/layout uses the new width. The next submission
uses that completed geometry. The facade does not rerun layout or dispatch.

## Confirmed value and drag preview

Owner value, range, step, preview and gesture start stay double. The range and its
span must be finite, ordered, with the confirmed value inside it; step is finite
and nonnegative. For rendering only, clamp the selected paint value within bounds,
compute a ratio in double, clamp it to [0,1], then convert that bounded ratio to
float for the logical fill coordinate. No confirmed or proposed value is cast
through float. Zero span paints zero fill. Semantic numeric values remain Base's
normalized float0..1; supply `value_description` for application units.

While `drag.dragging` remains true after reduction, paint its preview. Otherwise
paint the immutable confirmed value passed into the call. A rejected drag thus
previews while held and returns to confirmed paint on release. Keyboard requests
do not paint an unaccepted proposal. Accepting in the callback updates external
owner state, observed on the next submission; same-call semantics also retain the
entry snapshot. Two keys in one call propose from that same snapshot.

Escape/generic cancel and disabled/readonly/zero-span transitions retain Base
cancellation behavior. CANCEL offers the captured start to the owner; it does not
write owner storage. When capture ends, paint uses the confirmed entry value,
even if different from start. Removing the handler ends capture without delivering
callbacks to a missing handler. Omission itself dispatches no synthetic cancel.

Keep one zero-initialized caller-owned state per stable ID. During submission,
Base owns its capture/preview fields. Handlers may accept/reject through external
owner state, but must not mutate active state, theme or borrowed data, destroy
context/state/users, or recursively submit UI. Defer omission/destruction until
return and renderer consumption. All invalid public inputs are checked before
opening boxes: no callbacks, capture mutation or UI submission on rejection.

`tests/unit/test_styled_slider_events.c` uses software pixels for bar endpoints,
preview/rejection/acceptance and finite extreme ranges, plus real queued touch,
keyboard and cancellation input. It compares Base/Styled phases, exact doubles
above float precision, normalized semantics, resize boundaries, missing handlers,
invalid-input atomicity and deferred omission. The label test inspects text command
placement; its font-free pixel fixture does not claim glyph raster coverage.
Legacy Slider and component tests remain required. Browser/foreign bindings and
full Slider-family parity are outside this slice.

# Dialog, AlertDialog, Sheet and composed Popover surfaces

`cui_surface.h` adds application-owned surface state, drawing-free reducers and paired styled composition. A surface ID and its derived close, confirm, cancel and title IDs must be unique within the UI. Applications call `cui_surface_open` with a valid trigger, submit open surfaces every frame, and consume explicit outcomes with `cui_surface_take_result`. `cui_surface_request_close` queues a programmatic close safely between frames and applies the decision policy once on the next submission. `on_close` runs after state changes and focus restoration, including direct child-action closure. Call `cui_surface_close` during an active frame; if begin succeeded, its matching end remains required even after closing from a child action.

Dialogs, alerts and sheets trap focus. Popovers are nonmodal by default, with an explicit modal option. Already-consumed events are ignored by the reducer. Escape and outside primary pointer presses can dismiss an open surface; the options disable either policy independently. Alerts suppress outside dismissal and their header close button by default. A decision callback can reject confirm, cancel or close before state changes. Closing withdraws current scoped semantics and restores an enabled trigger, including when a nested dialog closes back into its parent.

The styled begin/end accepts arbitrary CUI children. `cui_surface_footer_begin` ends the body and opens a fixed footer row, keeping its controls visible even when the body contains oversized content; the regular surface end closes that footer. The body measures its own content through completed-layout bounds tracking, routes wheel events to its clipped viewport and clamps retained scroll when content shrinks. Changed geometry schedules correction frames and unchanged surfaces return to idle. Custom base layouts use parts 6/7 for the viewport/content and submit body semantics with `cui_base_surface_submit_body`. It draws a backdrop, title, optional description, close button and clipped body as viewport portals. `cui_alert_dialog` composes destructive confirm and outline cancel buttons. Alert title, description and actions share one vertically centered content block when it fits the panel. Overflowing alert content switches to a clipped, scrollable layout starting at the top, so the full content remains reachable. Each alert has an alertdialog semantic role; other surfaces use dialog, with a copied description and stable title relationship. A caller can compose its own alert actions using the documented derived IDs. Results persist until consumed or the surface is opened again.

Dialog dimensions clamp within an explicit viewport and optional uniform margin. Sheets support left, right, top and bottom placement with explicit width/height. Their inner edge has a captured pointer resize control, directional arrow sizing, Home/End limits and semantic size/range. Resize is enabled by default; options disable it or configure minimum/maximum extents. The application-owned `sheet_size` retains user sizing; set it to zero to return to option sizing. `cui_surface_current_geometry` includes that retained size. Custom base-only layouts submit the resize semantic inside its own box using `cui_base_surface_submit_resize`; the helper draws nothing. Popovers use the existing side-based flip/clamp popup geometry. Nested surfaces require distinct IDs and explicitly increasing layers (default 100); the root does not yet provide an automatic overlay stack.

`test_surface` exercises actual styled confirmation buttons, rejected acceptance, pointer cancellation, all four themes, all four sheet edges, header close, Escape, outside dismissal, nested focus isolation/restoration and portal escape from an ancestor clip. The same behavior fixtures also run as `surface_base_only`, linking only core, models, overlay and surface base sources. Those fixtures emit only their own clipping commands, demonstrating no theme or component dependency in surface behavior.

This is partial GPUI Kit 0.7.1 parity. Remaining upstream scope includes automatic Root overlay management, custom title/header parts and styling options, body scrollbar chrome and keyboard focus reveal, configurable backdrop appearance, default viewport margins and top offsets, animated transitions and the complete Popover anchor/offset/arrow positioning contract. Existing popover flip behavior differs from upstream's anchored clamp-only default. Native platform accessibility and IME behavior remain separate unfinished requirements.

For a child such as a command palette that handles Escape first, set `no_escape_dismiss` on its surface. Let the child consume Escape while clearing its query; on its empty-query cancel callback, call `cui_surface_request_close`. The next submission applies the decision callback and restores focus before registering modal content. Begin-phase dismissal cannot inspect event consumption that occurs later in child rendering.

## Sheet motion

Set `options.sheet_animation_seconds = 0.22f` to slide a sheet in and out from its configured edge. The default zero keeps immediate behavior. Motion reads `cui_frame_time(ui)`, which advances from the delta passed to `cui_begin_frame`; continue scheduling invalidated frames. `cui_surface_current_geometry` reports the moving bounds. Resize controls appear once entry completes.

With animation enabled, closing keeps the modal mounted during its exit and consumes input events. Focus returns to the trigger, `on_close` fires, and a result becomes available only when the exit completes. `state.sheet_closing` exposes this phase to application composition. Calling open during exit reverses toward the open position. Pass `options.reduced_motion = true` to snap directly to the destination; changing it during exit completes the close in the next submitted frame. Duration is finite, positive and capped at ten seconds; invalid values disable animation. Dialog/AlertDialog/Popover behavior remains immediate.

AlertDialog with unspecified/nonpositive finite height fits its measured title,
wrapped description and action row plus theme padding. The first frame measures
content; the next invalidated frame settles its height. Viewport margins still
cap the dialog, and overflowing content remains scrollable. Explicit positive
heights retain the fixed viewport contract. Resize, font or content changes can
require another measured frame.

## Independent Popover geometry

`cui_popover_position_resolve` calculates an anchor-mode rectangle without opening
a surface or modifying state. It supports eight anchors named for the popup's
own edge, signed explicit offsets, nonzero viewport origins and no-flip/no-shrink
clamping. Set `reference_rem` from application root sizing; zero selects 16 logical
pixels. The default gap is one quarter rem; enabling the arrow adds three eighths
rem. `cui_popover_arrow_resolve` calculates the triangle and border join patch for
the final clamped rectangle. Read `cui_surface.h` for finite-input, overflow and
output-preservation rules. Geometry remains fractional; host pixel snapping is
separate.

Use `cui_popover_begin` to apply this positioning and paint an optional arrow,
then balance a successful begin with `cui_surface_end`. Existing
`cui_surface_begin` retains legacy placement. See [Popover anchors](POPOVER_ANCHORS.md)
for ownership, failure, rendering and adapter limits. SDL3 and browser mesh adapters have bounded analytic coverage; exact
reference raster antialiasing remains unfinished. This is scoped C support, not
complete family or language-builder parity.

# Retained completed-close observers

Include `cui/cui_surface_events.h` for additive Base and Styled surface facades.
They observe completed closes; they do not control close acceptance or notify
opening, destruction, dismissal attempts or vetoes. Existing surface state/options
layouts and entrypoints are unchanged.

```c
static void closed(void *user, const cui_surface_lifecycle_event *value) {
    cui_surface_result *last = user;
    *last = value->result;
}
/* These objects must remain at stable addresses through every possible close. */
cui_surface_event_state surface;
cui_surface_result last = CUI_SURFACE_NONE;
cui_surface_events_init(&surface, surface_id, CUI_SURFACE_DIALOG);
cui_surface_events_set_handler(&surface,
    (cui_surface_event_handler){closed, &last});
/* On each submitted frame: */
cui_surface_event_result result = cui_surface_begin_events(
    ui, theme, &surface, cui_string("Title"), cui_string("Body"), options);
if (result.control_result) {
    /* Compose the body. */
    cui_surface_end(ui);
}
```

`cui_base_surface_update_events`, `cui_base_surface_begin_events`,
`cui_surface_begin_events` and `cui_alert_dialog_events` each refresh the retained
registration in a by-value copy of options before native update. All other options,
including `decide` and `decision_user`, pass through unchanged. Do not separately
update then begin on the same input. `control_result` preserves the native bool;
for the void Alert composition it is always false. `valid` describes adapter
preflight only, not geometry/render success. `close_count` counts actual observer
invocations during that call, including a close before subsequent native failure.
An absent observer still closes normally and yields zero count. No result replay
occurs when replacing a handler or submitting another frame.

Use existing `cui_surface_open`, `cui_surface_close`,
`cui_surface_request_close` and `cui_surface_take_result` on `&surface.control`.
Direct close bypasses decision policy, exactly as before; request-close waits for
submission and consults the existing decision callback. Pending requests are one
slot, not a queue. The observer runs after the result is committed, focus is
restored and the overlay closes. Taking the persistent result neither triggers
nor cancels notification. Direct close within a valid active frame invokes the retained observer but returns
no facade-local callback count. Only request-close is documented safe between
frames. The existing imperative close calls active-frame focus-scope dismissal:
calling it outside a frame can commit/notify while reporting CUI_ERROR_LIFECYCLE.
This facade preserves that diagnostic; it does not make that operation safe.

The payload's `event` is shared LIFECYCLE metadata with the surface ID and UNKNOWN
source. It carries no frame, event index or activation flags: an imperative call or
animated completion does not establish an input cause. The pointer-free
payload can be copied beyond callback/context lifetime. It does not keep the
surface or context alive. Result is the existing ACCEPTED/CANCELLED/CLOSED value;
imperative legacy close retains its existing handling of other supplied values.

Storage and handler user data must outlive all possible closes. Never copy or move
an attached `cui_surface_event_state`, edit adapter fields, or replace its retained
`control.on_close/close_user`. A Sheet observer runs only at completed exit, with
the latest handler installed between calls; it can outlive the request's frame.
`set_handler` replaces one listener, never appends, and ignores user data
when no function is supplied (the stored user pointer is cleared). An empty handler keeps the adapter installed.

Incoming options with either legacy close callback field populated are rejected
before any state/UI mutation. `decide` is allowed. Reentrant wrapper calls,
handler replacement and detach during notification fail preflight. Surface/context/
registration destruction, raw reentrant surface operations, and foreign exception
unwinding during callbacks are unsupported. Mutate unrelated application owner
state and defer teardown until the outer component call returns.

`cui_surface_events_detach` succeeds only when closed, not exiting, outside an
active call, and still holding the matching registration. It clears that
registration and handler without closing, taking the result or freeing anything.
After detach ordinary legacy calls may use `control`. Reinitialize closed detached
storage to use events again; init is not teardown of a live surface.

Plain legacy update/begin with ordinary options on attached storage is unsupported:
it overwrites the retained callback. Use the event-aware wrappers. Custom legacy
composition can call `cui_surface_events_options` and pass its transformed options
to that exact surface call. The helper preserves all other options, leaves output
untouched on failure, and provides no wrapper-local count. Never pass those
transformed options to another surface. A later wrapper detects overwritten
registration and fails; it cannot recover notifications already missed by an
unsupported legacy call. Keep the owning storage alive if mixing invalid calls;
there is no implicit recovery or safe teardown promise.

The test suite covers all wrapper refresh paths, actual callbacks/counts,
decision veto, imperative close, no-handler reduction, conflicts without mutation,
helper-driven legacy composition, stale registration detection, Sheet exit and
handler replacement, detach and reuse. Existing surface tests remain unchanged.
This C facade does not add bridge notifications or binding subscriptions.

# NanoSVG transform validation patch

The pinned parser previously left `nsvg__parseMatrix` output unchanged when fewer
than six arguments were present. Its caller then multiplied an uninitialized
local matrix, or reused a prior transform. Translate, scale and skew read missing
arguments directly; rotate read an absent angle or a missing second center
coordinate when given two arguments. These are genuine undefined reads, beyond
GCC's optimized maybe-uninitialized warning.

The local patch preserves the pinned upstream revision. Rejected matrix, translate,
scale, rotate and skew argument counts now initialize output to identity. Missing
parentheses and excess arguments take the same safe branch. A failed operation
therefore leaves the accumulated transform unchanged, while subsequent valid
operations remain effective. Numeric overflow to infinity is rejected in argument
parsing. Identity fallback is consistent with the parser's tolerant handling of
unsupported or malformed transform text; it does not create a new public status API.

The patch does not claim strict SVG grammar validation. The existing scanner can
skip arbitrary nonnumeric text, and finite matrices can still overflow when
composed. General SVG validation remains the icon adapter's responsibility.
Valid matrix values, one/two-argument translate/scale, one/three-argument rotate,
one-argument skew and transform-list composition retain their geometry.

A separate explicit size_t cast for the existing ftell error sentinel fixes a
preexisting signed-comparison diagnostic found by whole-header strict compilation.
There are no warning suppressions or dependency bumps. `third_party/nanosvg/PIN.md`
records original/patched hashes and patch provenance. The integrator updates the
manifest hash and regenerates the generated icon header outside this worker's scope.

Private `tests/unit/test_svg_transform_validation.c` directly includes the pinned
implementation. It checks every malformed helper, missing delimiters, excess or
missing arguments, malformed center rotation, overflow arguments, valid transforms,
valid-invalid-valid composition (no stale transform reuse), and parsed SVG path
bounds. Assertions remain active under compilers that define NDEBUG for -O3.

Validation commands (all tests headless):

```sh
cc -std=c11 -O3 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror tests/unit/test_svg_transform_validation.c -lm -o /tmp/test-svg-transform-gcc
/tmp/test-svg-transform-gcc
zig cc -std=c11 -O3 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror tests/unit/test_svg_transform_validation.c -lm -o /tmp/test-svg-transform-zig
/tmp/test-svg-transform-zig
cc -std=c11 -O1 -g -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer tests/unit/test_svg_transform_validation.c -lm -o /tmp/test-svg-transform-sanitize
/tmp/test-svg-transform-sanitize
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja
cmake --build build
python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir build
```

The Clang-family optimized check uses pinned Zig 0.16.0 `zig cc`, not a system
Clang installation. Integrator must register the private test in CMake.

# Table and DataTable

The frozen GPUI Kit 0.7.1 Table is a stateless composition of sections, rows and
cells. DataTable adds a data delegate, scrolling, selection and column management.
This module provides both composition primitives and a retained data model, with
portable C11 public types and independent base behavior.

`cui_table_begin`, `cui_table_begin_row`, `cui_table_begin_cell` and
`cui_table_end` compose a themed table containing arbitrary caller content. Every
begin requires a matching end. These register passive table, row and cell roles;
callers can set semantic parent and descriptive details using core setters. Head-cell, header/body/footer section and caption helpers preserve that composition. Validated cell-span helpers sum explicit column widths; failed validation does not begin a box. Callers place captions after their sections and provide accessible head-cell names. There are no implicit data cell labels.

`cui_table_column_default(key, label)` supplies a 100-pixel, resizable, movable column with a 20-pixel minimum and optional sorting disabled. `cui_table_options_default()` enables border and scrollbars with row selection and no stripes, matching the supported reference defaults. Zero initialization remains available for applications choosing their own configuration. Widths remain bounded by CUI's 65,536-pixel safety limit.

Create `cui_table_model` with a bounded row capacity, then bind borrowed rows and
mutable columns. Rows and columns need nonzero unique keys within each dimension.
Binding rejects invalid labels, duplicate keys, excessive counts, invalid widths
and invalid width limits transactionally. Maximum capacity is one million rows
and 128 columns. The model allocates two row-key hash banks once at creation;
rendering, navigation, resize and movement do not allocate. Caller metadata stays
valid until a successful bind. Rebind after changing row ordering or keys; the
caller implements sorting/filtering and may keep selection keyed through both.
Columns may be mutated through resize and move functions between frames. Columns marked fixed_left must form a contiguous prefix. Their header and cells remain fixed horizontally, with separate clip scopes preventing scrolling cells from receiving input beneath pinned cells. Column movement cannot cross the pinned boundary. Keep the total pinned width below the viewport width to leave space for scrolling columns. The column viewport describes the scrolling suffix; fixed columns are available through dedicated count/width accessors.

`cui_table_state` is caller controlled: selected row/column, keyboard cursor, sort
column/direction, horizontal/vertical scroll and transient resize gesture. Row,
column and cell selection use the same state; zero keys mean no selection. The
reducer returns change flags and activated keys. Sort activation cycles default,
ascending and descending; a newly activated column starts ascending. Sorting is
requested by the result, without rearranging caller data automatically. On `sort_changed`, sort your application records, reorder the borrowed row array, then call `cui_table_bind` and invalidate the UI. Resolve cell labels from the newly ordered row keys, rather than from the original position. The gallery demonstrates ascending/descending/default ordering for Name and numeric Size, with stable key order for equal Status values.

The pure base API separates input reduction from semantic submission. A custom
renderer can call `cui_table_reduce`, submit the root outside clip scopes, submit
headers inside their pane clips, and submit body semantics inside its translated
body clip. Per-column/row/cell submission helpers support distinct pinned and scrolling clip scopes. Lay out the public stable header, resize, row and cell IDs. The
`cui_base_data_table` convenience registers all semantics without drawing; it
links only core and table base. `cui_data_table` performs that separation and
paints the fixed header and virtual rows using theme tokens. Sortable headers show SVG indicators for unsorted/ascending/descending states, with centered labels and a pointer cursor. The icons use the theme icon loader, so applications can replace their SVGs. A label callback
supplies borrowed accessible cell names. An optional render callback runs inside
each clipped cell and can draw arbitrary content; the application must govern
interactive children and disabled behavior consistently.

Up/Down skip disabled rows, Left/Right skip disabled columns, and Home/End move to
the first/last enabled row in row mode, or the first/last enabled column in the current row in cell/column mode. Escape clears controlled selection and range anchors while retaining the keyboard cursor; disabled/loading tables ignore it. PageUp/PageDown move a viewport of physical rows and skip disabled destinations. Navigation does not wrap unless requested. Multiple
events in one frame operate in queue order. Roving cell Tab focus follows the
cursor; the header cursor is a separate Tab stop, with Left/Right/Home/End navigation skipping disabled columns. Headers support Enter or pointer
sort activation, and Ctrl+Left/Right moves movable columns without crossing an
immovable column. Primary pointer dragging past four pixels reorders at header midpoints on drop; it respects pinned regions and immovable columns, suppresses sort activation, and cancels on Escape/cancel or release outside the header. Resize grips accept pointer dragging and Left/Right in eight
pixel increments. Secondary clicks return a contextual row/column request without changing selection; the application composes and controls the menu. Widths clamp to configured bounds; secondary button gestures
do not resize. Manual selection moves the cursor without changing selection.
Disabled state prevents reducer mutation.

The body uses fixed row heights, fractional scroll offsets, bounded row and column overscan and
real ancestor clipping. The header remains fixed vertically and shares horizontal
scroll with the body. Width-aware horizontal column virtualization includes partial edge columns. An optional pinned row-number header selects whole rows and navigates enabled rows. Its result requests ROW selection mode; the caller applies that request to the controlled options. Row headers continue working when all data columns are disabled. Result fields report actual visible row/column windows (without overscan), changes to those windows, and an opt-in load-more request near the end. Load requests fire once per threshold entry or changed row count; applications append rows and rebind. They are suppressed while disabled. Both grid and body expose scroll extents for core wheel routing and boundary bubbling. Wheel scrolling can move the cursor offscreen without
forcing it back into view; keyboard navigation reveals the cursor again. Grid,
row, column-header and grid-cell semantics include hierarchy, selection, row and
column indices, and total grid counts. Indices are one based data indices and
exclude the header. IDs are stable keyed hashes; applications must avoid hash/ID
collisions with other controls as required by the core.

Custom leaf-header, group-header, row-header, whole-row and trailing-column render hooks use option userdata. Group headers accept up to sixteen levels of bounded spans. Every level must cover all data columns exactly, and no group may cross the fixed-column boundary; `cui_table_group_headers_valid` lets applications validate a configuration before rendering. Group cells expose column-header semantics at their first column; the callback receives the complete span. Whole-row callbacks run only for virtualized rows and can add row-level decoration or content before the cells. The optional trailing column uses a caller-selected width (12 logical pixels by default) and participates in horizontal scroll extent; its callback runs for each header level, the leaf header and visible rows. Loading replaces body rows with a busy status and suppresses input/load requests; empty and loading placeholders have optional render hooks and accessible default labels.

Set `scrollbars` to reserve scrollbar gutters only when an axis overflows. `bar_thickness` controls their logical thickness. The drawing-free reducer delegates keyboard, track and thumb behavior to the reusable Scroll base primitive, while the styled table paints the same scrollbar state. The grid and scrollbar semantics share the table as their scroll owner. Applications that build a custom renderer can use `cui_table_scroll_layout` to obtain the reduced viewport and scroll maxima.

Tests cover four-theme static sections/spans/caption geometry, multi-level group geometry and semantics, virtual whole-row and trailing-column callbacks, row-header selection mode requests, drag reorder/cancellation, empty/loading/custom hooks, bounded row/column/cell ranges, toggles, capacity rejection, and transactional validation, keyed lookup in 10,000 rows, fractional
viewport arithmetic, clipped overscan, callback count and accessible labels,
fixed header geometry, pinned header/cell geometry and clipping/hit behavior, horizontal clipping/virtualization, load request deduplication, ordered keyboard events, disabled skipping, manual
selection, sorting, column reorder, keyboard/pointer resize, width clamps,
secondary gestures, wheel/focus interaction, scrollbar keyboard/thumb behavior and semantic hierarchy. The same
behavior tests run with a base-only core link; sanitizer validation instruments
both layout and reducer.

This is not full GPUI family parity. Remaining features include composed menus, cell Tab traversal, double-click events, per-column padding/default sort configuration, and variable row heights. Selection defaults to a single controlled keyed item in each dimension. An opt-in multiple-selection mode uses a caller-provided buffer of at most 4096 keyed items, with Ctrl/Meta toggles and Shift row/column/rectangular ranges. Disabled rows and columns are excluded from ranges. Capacity failures preserve the prior selection and keep the table rendered; callers may enlarge the buffer and retry. The anchor and buffer are controlled state, and callers must retain unique normalized keys in the buffer. Caller
sorting/filtering is supported but this module does not provide a comparator or
filter engine. Native accessibility adapters must map the portable grid roles.
