# Table and DataTable behavior contracts

Source reference: GPUI Kit 0.7.1, commit `87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`, `crates/component/src/table/{table,column,state}.rs`. These are original portable C implementations. This guide describes the implemented subset and compatibility choices, not full family parity or native accessibility certification.

## Selection and action columns

`cui_table_column.nonselectable = true` prevents column/cell selection without disabling the column. Header sorting, resizing, reordering and focus remain available; custom child buttons keep their independent base behavior. Whole-row selection still highlights cells in that column, matching the source's action-column granularity. `disabled` retains its separate existing behavior.

`cui_table_options.row_selection_disabled`, `column_selection_disabled`, and `cell_selection_disabled` independently block the corresponding selection mode. They suppress selected presentation for that mode while preserving stored selected keys, so re-enabling the policy restores controlled selection. They do not disable sorting, cursor navigation or custom row/cell controls. Row-header activation does not request row-selection escalation while row selection is blocked. Nonselectable cells remain focusable grid cells with readonly selection semantics, enabling navigation through a row containing custom action controls. Activation result fields can still report a clicked cell; `selection_changed` stays false when selection is rejected.

Range selection skips nonselectable columns in cell/column mode before counting required capacity. It does not insert phantom action-column selections. Application-provided selection storage remains bounded by its declared capacity. The model-free `cui_table_is_selected()` helper sees mode policies and stored keys; because it has no model argument, callers implementing custom paint must additionally check `column.nonselectable` outside row mode. Styled DataTable applies this check itself.

```c
columns[1].nonselectable = true;
cui_table_result result = cui_data_table(ui, id, theme, model, &state,
    (cui_table_options){
        .width = 480, .height = 240,
        .selection_mode = CUI_TABLE_SELECT_CELL,
        .row_selection_disabled = true,
        .sort_cycle = CUI_TABLE_SORT_CYCLE_SOURCE,
        .accessible_name = cui_string("Workspace files")
    }, label_cell, render_cell, userdata);
```

## Sort requests and borrowed data

Zero-initialized `sort_cycle` remains `CUI_TABLE_SORT_CYCLE_LEGACY`: Default→Ascending→Descending→Default. Explicit `CUI_TABLE_SORT_CYCLE_SOURCE` follows the pinned source: Default→Descending→Ascending→Default. Both mouse/header activation and keyboard activation use the same reducer. Switching to another column begins at that policy's first direction. Invalid sort-cycle enums reject submission before layout/state changes.

Sorting updates `state.sort_column`/`state.sort` and returns `sort_changed`; it does not mutate borrowed row data. The application handles the request, reorders/rebinds its rows, and retains stable row keys. Selection and semantic row indices reconcile against those keys. Result flags describe the final state for one frame; multiple queued input events may coalesce into one flag, so this is not an event-by-event callback log. A frame without a new sort event does not repeat the request.

The styled implementation invokes the supplied label callback once per rendered cell for semantic and default visible text, rather than twice. Custom render callbacks also run once per rendered cell. Hosts may themselves call the label callback within custom rendering; CUI does not prevent that application choice. Models, callback userdata and arrays stay borrowed according to the existing bind contract; no ownership transfer or implicit async work occurs.

## Named composable Table and cell sizing

`cui_table_begin_ex()` adds an explicit root accessible name and row/column counts. `cui_table_begin_cell_ex()` supplies header/body role, accessible name, parent ID, one-based row/column indices, alignment and sizing. `cui_table_begin_row_checked()` validates row options before opening a row. End these checked begins only when they return true. A caption remains visible descriptive content; it does not replace the explicit root name.

Names are synchronously copied by Core into its bounded frame storage; input string bytes need only remain valid during submission. Root counts and cell/row indices must fit `INT_MAX`. Dimensions are finite 0..65536, padding finite 0..4096, and enums must be defined values. Invalid checked inputs, including a self-parent relationship, add neither layout nor semantics. Legacy void begin/end helpers retain their existing defaults and normalization behavior, including the generic `Table`/`Cell` names and 4px cell padding.

Explicit positive cell height overrides design sizing. A non-INHERIT `design_size` with zero height uses `cui_design_measure()` control height at density `theme.font_size / 16`. Default design padding uses its vertical control padding so the design line height fits; an explicit `custom_padding` override wins. This is an intentional symmetric padding adaptation, not the source's independent edge-padding API. Row design sizing follows the same height rule. Child typography is host-owned: derive font and line height through `cui_design_measure()` and use those when submitting the child text. Choosing a design size does not silently resize arbitrary nested controls.

```c
cui_design_metrics metrics;
cui_design_measure(CUI_DESIGN_LG, theme->font_size / 16, &metrics);
if (cui_table_begin_cell_ex(ui, cell_id, theme,
        (cui_table_cell_options){.width = 220, .design_size = CUI_DESIGN_LG,
          .name = cui_string("Paid"), .parent = row_id,
          .row_index = 1, .column_index = 2})) {
    cui_text_with_line_height(ui, cui_string("Paid"), metrics.font_size,
                              theme->text, metrics.line_height);
    cui_table_end(ui);
}
```

Column spans continue to use `cui_table_span_width()` and the existing span begin helper. Core has no row/column-span semantic fields, so this change does not invent them or claim span announcements. Independent per-column edge padding, full source Table flex/minimum-size behavior, dedicated Table palette tokens and independent scrollbar-axis visibility remain gaps. The source's pinned feature is fixed-left columns; no pinned-row feature is introduced.

## Evidence

`tests/unit/test_table_selection_contracts.c` tests source/legacy cycles, borrowed-data immutability and stable-key rebind, selection-only opt-outs, restored stored keys, header sort/resize and custom child pointer/Enter activation, range capacity, label/render callback counts, strict invalid-input behavior, explicit header/root/row/cell semantics, and actual nested text containment at all 14 design sizes in two densities. Existing `test_table.c` retains legacy navigation/resize/move/virtualization/selection coverage.

The real WASM gallery exposes canvas buttons for selection, action-column and sort-policy choices. Its Table story uses named parts, actual design typography and horizontal scrolling for large text. `tests/web/test_table_selection_contracts.py` checks Chromium 1208 source sort cycling, action-button touch activation with selection blocked, readonly action-cell semantics, all-size metadata/text sizing, mobile touch and disabled controls. Worker validation passed strict C11 warning builds, the scoped headless suite and ASan/UBSan with leak detection. Standard CTest passed 102/103; only stale generated `dist/cui_table.h` failed its distribution check, which the integrator owns. Browser evidence uses the approved generated-JS bridge for the integrator-owned Table selector/height and DataTable420 preview. The integrator owns test registration. Native screen-reader output and per-platform accessibility bridges remain separately unverified.

# DataTable transitions

Include `cui/cui_table_events.h`. The additive `cui_table_reduce_events`,
`cui_base_data_table_events` and `cui_data_table_events` take a `cui_table_event_handler`
and return unchanged legacy `control`, validity/submission flags and actual
`selection_count`, `sort_count`, `column_width_count`, `column_move_count`,
`activation_count` and `context_request_count`
(saturating with `count_overflow`). A missing callback ignores user and preserves
reduction, including multi-selection behavior.

Each applied sort key/direction transition notifies inside reduction, before
final semantics and every Styled render callback. Three cycles can return to the
entry state while producing three typed events and preserving the legacy
`sort_changed` flag. Both legacy ascending-first and source descending-first
cycles remain unchanged. This changes sort state only; caller rows are not sorted.
Earlier successful notifications remain delivered if later input fails.

The pointer-free payload preserves exact native `cui_id` keys and direction
values. Shared CHANGE metadata has the table root target and genuine current
frame/index/source; HAS_ACTIVATION is present only when a real snapshot exists.
Do not assume final semantics, geometry or paint are available during callbacks.
Disabled/loading/inert/layout-only paths preserve legacy bookkeeping without
sort callbacks. No new consumed-event filtering is applied.

Handler/user are borrowed synchronously. Copy payloads/change unrelated application
state, but do not mutate/rebind the model, rows, columns, state or workspace;
recurse; destroy storage/context; or unwind foreign exceptions during callbacks.
Defer model edits/removal/teardown until outer submission and renderer consumption
finish. Existing render/label callback arguments and virtual-window timing remain
unchanged. New facades require a nonzero root ID; legacy APIs remain unchanged.

Single selection emits `cui_table_selection_change` for each actual primary
row/column pair transition, with the effective operation mode. Navigation in
manual mode does not select; activation may still select. Same-pair activation
emits no CHANGE, while A->B->A emits twice even though the legacy final
`selection_changed` is false. Escape clearing is observed. Row-header operations
can apply ROW selection while also producing the old mode-request result; the
callback precedes later result bookkeeping and does not reject that selection.
A column activation can emit selection then sort in the existing write order.
Selection-disabled/nonselectable policies do not disable independent sorting.

A non-NULL `on_selection` with `multiple_selection=true` returns `valid=false`,
`control.error=CUI_TABLE_INVALID` before reduction, state/column mutation or paint.
There is no silent primary-only multi observation. Nil selection/sort-only handlers
still support legacy multi reduction, including accepted progress before errors.
The separate set-observation API below supports complete multi selection. Column
movement/resize and activation/context are covered below; mode requests remain
a separate slice, while viewport/load remain aggregate result observations. Existing bridge V1 table notifications remain aggregate post-step snapshots; native multiplicity and
64-bit keys here do not imply binding parity.


## Multi-selection snapshots

Use `cui_table_reduce_set_events`, `cui_base_data_table_set_events` or
`cui_data_table_set_events` with `cui_table_set_event_handler` and
`cui_table_selection_workspace`. The handler supports selection, sort, column-width and column-move callbacks;
its selection callback receives `cui_table_selection_set_change`, not the scalar
payload. Its return is `cui_table_set_event_result`: `events` contains the same
legacy result and actual callback counts as above, and `preflight` distinguishes
workspace/argument failure from a later legacy capacity error. This requires
`multiple_selection=true` when `on_selection` is non-NULL. Scalar facades keep
their existing explicit multi-observer rejection.

```c
cui_table_selection before[32], after[32]; /* Each >= state.selection_capacity. */
cui_table_selection_workspace scratch = {before, after, 32};
cui_table_set_event_handler handler = {
    .on_selection = on_set_change, .on_sort = on_sort_change, .user = application
};
cui_table_set_event_result result = cui_base_data_table_set_events(
    ui, table_id, model, &state, options, scratch, handler);
/* Keep scratch and all owner resources alive until this call completes. */
```

Each actual selection operation snapshots the multiset and primary pair before
and after the old mutation. Payload `previous`/`value` spans are sorted by exact
unsigned `(row,column)` keys; duplicates retain multiplicity. Storage-order-only
changes do not notify; primary-only changes do. Ctrl toggles, range replacement,
row-header mode and Escape follow their existing policies. Repeated/net-zero
transitions notify separately; rejected operations with no change do not. Earlier
notifications survive a later capacity error, while old flags/errors remain
unchanged. Callbacks run before final semantics and Styled rendering. No per-item
delta or transaction rollback is provided.

Both scratch arrays have `capacity` writable entries; capacity must be at least
`state.selection_capacity` and at most 4096. Zero capacity permits NULL arrays.
An iterative heapsort canonicalizes only scratch: O(n log n) observation time,
O(1) auxiliary storage and exactly two caller buffers, with no allocation or
owner-array sorting. This does not change the complexity of legacy range selection.
Spans are borrowed **only during the callback** and reused at the next operation;
copy entries into application-owned storage to retain them. Copying the payload
struct alone does not retain the text-free spans. Handler/user borrow synchronously.
No mutation of active owner/model/scratch, recursion, destruction or foreign unwind
is supported; defer edits and teardown until submission/render consumption finish.

Preflight checks all arguments/counts/extents/alignment before any bookkeeping,
input consumption, callbacks or painting. Full declared scratch ranges must be
disjoint from each other, state, its full selection buffer, model object and bound
row/column descriptor arrays. Invalid arguments/extents take precedence over short
capacity, then overlap. Failure returns `events.valid=false`, no submitted/counts,
`events.control.error=CUI_TABLE_INVALID` and INVALID, WORKSPACE_CAPACITY or OVERLAP
in `preflight`, leaving owner/columns/scratch/input consumption unchanged. Success
sets `preflight=OK`, including a subsequent operation's CUI_TABLE_CAPACITY error.
Scratch allocations must additionally be exclusive of context/internal allocations,
label/string/group bytes, userdata and other resources: opaque aliases, dangling
pointers and actual allocation lengths cannot be universally checked. They remain
caller preconditions, not a runtime memory-safety guarantee.

A NULL selection callback ignores workspace entirely, preserves single/multi
legacy reduction and still supports optional sort observation; unused userdata is
ignored. Passive/disabled/loading behavior and bridge omissions above also apply.


## Column width and movement

Both scalar and set handlers add optional `on_column_width` and `on_column_move`.
Use designated initializers for these unreleased structs and rebuild clients when
updating the header. Legacy state/options/result layouts and entrypoints are
unchanged. The shared result adds saturating `column_width_count` and
`column_move_count`, with the existing `count_overflow` flag.

`cui_table_column_width_change` copies `{event, column, previous_width, width}`
with exact float widths after the old helper's clamps. It observes each successful
pointer-move resize or grip Left/Right key resize. Repeated clamped no-ops do not
notify. `cui_table_column_move_change` copies `{event, column, previous_index,
index}` after a successful Ctrl+Left/Right header reorder or actual pointer drop.
Indices are operation-time array positions; the stable exact `cui_id` identifies
the column after subsequent moves. Both payloads are pointer-free. Capture facts
inside the callback or copy the struct for later use.

Notifications run immediately after the successful helper mutation, before later
gesture cleanup, semantics and Styled paint. A drop callback still sees the active
drag state; it must not mutate it. Event metadata is frozen before descriptor
movement, uses the table root target and genuine triggering frame/index/source;
a pointer-move resize has pointer provenance without inventing an activation.
Callback order follows the reducer's existing operation order, including repeated
changes and cycles returning to the entry width/order. No extra consumed-event
filtering, focus changes or legacy result-flag reinterpretation is added.

Programmatic `cui_table_resize`/`cui_table_move_column` calls stay silent. Fixed
regions, immovable/disabled columns, finite/clamped widths, >4px drag threshold,
passive/layout-only/loading and missing callback behavior remain unchanged.
A below-threshold header gesture may still sort as an ordinary click; an actual
drag suppresses that click. Cancel/Escape ends the existing gesture without
rolling back an already-applied resize; no begin/commit/cancel event is invented.
Handlers/user remain borrowed, and the mutation/reentrancy/teardown restrictions
above apply. Base only submits semantics, so pointer routing requires actual
caller-provided geometry (the tests prime with Styled geometry). No new dispatch,
GPU validation or bridge/binding event coverage is implied.


## Activation and context requests

Both scalar and set handlers add optional `on_activate` and `on_context_request`.
`activation_count` and `context_request_count` count actual synchronous calls,
saturating with `count_overflow`. Missing callbacks ignore unused userdata and
preserve all legacy writes. Set facades with no set-selection callback need no
workspace to observe these actions; existing preflight rules remain unchanged.

`cui_table_activation` copies ACTIVATE metadata, `area`, `row` and `column` for
each accepted cell or row-header activation. CELL uses both effective cursor keys;
ROW_HEADER always has column=0. A repeated same-item action still activates even
when selection is unchanged, nonselectable, selection-disabled or rejected for
capacity. It does not imply selection applied/committed. Header sorting remains
covered by sort/selection events; no generic header action is added.

Facts and metadata freeze before selection observers run. Notification follows
that branch's selection attempt/CHANGE and legacy activated-field writes, before
later mode-request bookkeeping, focus/reveal work and final semantics/paint.
Keyboard facts use the effective cursor, which can differ from the original
routed child after earlier navigation. The old result remains a last-write
aggregate: row-header activation writes only activated_row, so activated_column
can carry from an earlier cell action. Typed ROW_HEADER payloads explicitly use
column=0 without altering that legacy behavior.

`cui_table_context_request` copies REQUEST metadata, `area`, `row` and `column`
for each eligible secondary POINTER_DOWN on a cell, row header or column header.
COLUMN_HEADER uses row=0, ROW_HEADER column=0. It notifies immediately after the
old context fields are written, before subsequent cursor/selection handling.
The context item need not be selected. A request neither selects it nor opens a
popup, and has no rejection return. Disabled row/column and global/passive policies
keep their existing distinctions; nonselectable alone does not suppress context.

Metadata has the table root target and genuine frame/index/source. Secondary
press is POINTER source without fabricated activation evidence. HAS_ACTIVATION
is present only when the existing accepted-activation snapshot API supplies it;
absence does not invalidate an accepted raw Table action. Callback facts survive
an earlier selection observer consuming input; no new consumed-event filter is
introduced. Standard Table roles support accessibility focus but currently reject
ACTIVATE without a pointer_activatable override; no role remap or parity claim.

Both payloads are pointer-free and copyable beyond the callback/frame/context.
Handler/user and active resources retain the borrowed lifetimes and mutation/
reentrancy/destruction restrictions above. Record intent and defer teardown.
Read viewport/load observations from
`control` after submission: they remain completion aggregates, not per-input
callbacks or a networking API. The bridge/bindings do not gain these native events.

## Row-mode intent requests

Both handler types accept `on_mode_request(user, const cui_table_mode_request *)`;
`mode_request_count` counts actual synchronous calls, saturating with
`count_overflow`. The pointer-free REQUEST contains `current` (the submitted
options selection mode), `requested` (ROW), effective `row`, and `reason`
(`CUI_TABLE_MODE_FROM_ACTIVATION` or `CUI_TABLE_MODE_FROM_NAVIGATION`).

Row-header activation runs selection CHANGE, ACTIVATE, legacy mode-request flag
writes, then mode REQUEST. Automatic row-header navigation runs selection CHANGE,
flag writes, REQUEST, then the existing focus/reveal work. Facts and real input
evidence freeze before the first selection observer. Requests survive failed or
unchanged selection, including repeated HOME and already-ROW intents. This is
notification of existing intent: no options mutation, veto, commit or rollback.
Manual navigation and disabled row selection do not request mode; manual
activation retains the legacy request behavior. Disabled/loading/inert/layout-only
paths remain unchanged. Missing callbacks ignore user; a set facade with no
selection observer ignores its workspace even with a mode observer installed.

Callbacks run before paint and may copy facts or update unrelated state. Do not
mutate active options/owner/model/workspace, recurse, destroy resources or unwind
across C. Defer teardown until submission and renderer consumption finish.
Viewport/load remain result-only completion observations. No bridge/binding API
or accessibility ACTIVATE support is added by this slice.

# Tabs aggregate selection observers

Include `cui/cui_tabs_events.h` for `cui_base_tabs_events` and `cui_tabs_events`.
They add an optional applied selection CHANGE observer to existing Base/Styled
Tabs, preserving the old APIs, options, bool results, input handling and painting.

```c
static void tab_changed(void *user, const cui_tabs_selection_change *event) {
    app_state *app = user;
    app->last_tab = event->value; /* unrelated application state */
}
cui_tabs_event_result result = cui_tabs_events(
    ui, container_id, &theme, items, count, &selected, options,
    render_panel, panel_user, (cui_tabs_handler){tab_changed, app});
```

The Base variant draws nothing and takes an explicit nonzero compound `target`
before the item array; Styled uses its nonzero container ID. These IDs identify
the aggregate event, not an invented activating tab. Null context, zero target or
null selected storage reject before calling the legacy reducer. Other legacy
validation and maintenance remain unchanged. `result.changed` is the exact old
bool, which is not a successful-admission/submission signal.

At most one callback runs after Base finishes its selection and semantic/roving
focus finalization, before Styled reveal/animation updates, paint, render slots
and panel callback. The selected pointer has already been written. A missing
observer still permits legacy writes and has zero callback count; its unused user
pointer is ignored. Reading either result field does not dispatch again.

Payload `previous` and `value` are stable selected IDs. All payload fields are
pointer-free and may be copied. Metadata has CHANGE, the compound target, UNKNOWN
source and HAS_FRAME with the actual active frame sequence. There is no event
index, activation or reason: overflow MenuTree reduction and direct tab navigation
are separate passes, so a final selection cannot honestly identify one input.

This is an explicit aggregation exception. Multiple transitions coalesce; if the
final ID equals the initial ID, there is no callback. Selecting the same tab,
manual focus-only navigation, opening/closing overflow, scrolling and reorder
requests do not by themselves report selection CHANGE. Existing drag request
fields remain separate and the caller still applies reordering after the frame.
The observer cannot reject selection that has already been applied.

No callbacks are delivered outside an active painted submission, from layout-only
work or when globally disabled. The wrapper still calls the legacy Base reducer
for its normal maintenance, including disabled drag cleanup and empty overflow
cleanup. Inert/modal/consumed-input behavior remains Core's routing behavior;
there is no new readonly/inert policy and no synthesized input for maintenance.
Invalid or disabled selected IDs remain caller-owned as before; no repaired value
or synthetic change is introduced.

Observer/user are borrowed during submission. Keep selection, item arrays, labels,
state, theme, render/panel users and overflow scratch alive and unchanged. Do not
mutate/free active resources, destroy the context or recursively submit UI from the
observer. Set unrelated flags to request omission/removal after the outer call;
wait through frame/render consumption before teardown. The indicator's measured
bounds and other retained state keep their existing longer lifetimes. Omission
does not dispatch cancellation of retained work. Render/panel callbacks retain
legacy order; their own arbitrary model mutations are not Tabs reducer events.

`tests/unit/test_tabs_events.c` compares old/new selection, focus, panel choice,
semantics and draw commands. It covers queued pointer/key selection, same-tab
silence, multiple/net-zero transitions, manual navigation, absent observer,
callback-before-panel order, consumed input, disabled/inert/layout-only work,
invalid selected IDs, copied payload lifetime, deferred omission, overflow
selection, real reorder-request silence, and disabled/empty Base maintenance.
Legacy `test_choice.c` remains required. Native tests run through the private
display wrapper. No new browser, host accessibility or foreign-binding proof is
claimed; this slice adds no REQUEST/COMMIT/ACTIVATE or popup lifecycle facade.

# Tabs scroll ownership and boundary handoff

Scrollable Tabs now consume each wheel or touch-converted SCROLL event when their bounded offset actually changes. A refused event is offered to an eligible ancestor through the existing `cui_defer_scroll_event` API. Public options, zero-initialized behavior and selection callbacks are unchanged.

This matters to browser page fallback: before the fix, a vertical touch move changed the Tabs offset by 30 pixels but left the event unconsumed. The existing `web/touch_page_host.h` policy consequently made the page eligible and the browser scrolled the page by the same 30 pixels. A parent following Core targets did not automatically double-scroll; the observed leak was the host page fallback. Wheel events had the same missing consumption signal, although the production gallery's wheel preflight can prevent page scrolling independently of that signal.

A second case occurs when several events share one frame. Core initially routes them using the previous layout snapshot. If the first reaches the Tabs edge, the second now defers to the parent rather than disappearing with the retained child target. An event that moves the child partially is consumed entirely, matching shared Scrollable behavior; this change does not recover its residual delta. Boundary handoff therefore happens on a later refused event. No inertia or momentum behavior is added.

The source change is restricted to the Tabs scroll loop in `src/base/cui_choice.c`. Core pointer presence, capture, modal routing, native adapters, browser production handlers, DataTable and shared scrollbar visibility/timing are unchanged.

## Regression evidence

`tests/unit/test_choice.c` adds an actual styled Tabs scene inside a shared Scrollable. Both orientations and precise/line deltas assert child movement and consumption, no parent movement for accepted deltas, ignored already-consumed input, disabled child routing, and two events in one frame with the second moving the parent exactly once. The accepted-event assertion fails on the original source; the failure is preserved in `/home/matteo/.cache/cui-validation/tabs-before.log`.

`tests/web/tabs_scroll_probe.c` composes public styled Tabs and Scrollable APIs and the unchanged page-host policy. `test_tabs_scroll_chaining.py` builds this source as strict C11 WASM with pinned Zig 0.16.0, then drives actual Chromium mouse-wheel/Shift-wheel and CDP touch contacts. It asserts current first-tab bounds and changed canvas pixels, child-to-parent boundary handoff, page remaining stationary, disabled wheel/touch behavior, cancellation without selection, and one selection from the next real touch tap. No test invokes a model mutation or reducer export to substitute for user input. Reset is fixture initialization between independent cases.

Before-fix CDP evidence is preserved in `tabs-before-touch.log`: Tabs offset 30, parent offset 0, consumption 0, page scrollY 30, one fallback. After-fix tests report PASS in `tabs-final-browser.log`; the screenshot is `tabs-final-browser/tabs-scroll.png`, under `/home/matteo/.cache/cui-validation/`. This is a controlled real browser fixture, not a claim that every gallery mode or physical device was tested. The Canvas2D fixture draws ordinary Tabs rectangles, borders and text; it is not a general CUI renderer conformance test.

Run the browser proof from the repository:

```sh
TMPDIR=/home/matteo/.cache/cui-validation/tmp-storage/tabs \
  uv run tests/web/test_tabs_scroll_chaining.py \
  --output /home/matteo/.cache/cui-validation/tabs-final-browser
```

Playwright is pinned to 1.58.0 and defaults to its installed Chromium 1208 executable. `--case touch` isolates the touch diagnostic; default execution includes the full suite. The browser fixture uses the same Shift-plus-vertical-wheel translation as the gallery; native SDL Shift-wheel parity remains outside this change.

The warning-enabled native build completed without warnings. Full CTest passed 119/120; only `distribution` failed because generated distribution sources are integrator-owned and stale after this source edit. Focused `test_choice` passed with AddressSanitizer, UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer and leak detection. Logs are `tabs-native-build.log`, `tabs-native-ctest.log`, and `tabs-asan.log` in the validation directory. No physical OS touch, native window-leave or full Tabs/scrollbar parity certification is inferred from these tests.

# Segmented Tabs: opt-in source shadow branches

This bounded appearance slice uses gpui-kit 0.7.1 commit `87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`: [TabBar indicator](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-kit/blob/87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34/crates/component/src/tab/tab_bar.rs#L195), [Tab branches](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-kit/blob/87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34/crates/component/src/tab/tab.rs#L650), and [private raised helper](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-kit/blob/87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34/crates/component/src/styled.rs#L114). It does not complete Tabs/TabBar or certify GPUI GPU AA/kernel/color identity. Prior actual CUI draw-list evidence in `docs/validation/shadow-consumers-next33.md` showed no DROP layers in measured/static segmented paths.

Append `shadow_policy` to `cui_tabs_options`:

| Policy | Segmented behavior |
| --- | --- |
| LEGACY=0 | Existing paint, no added shadows; zero initialization remains compatible. |
| SOURCE_TAB=1 | Standalone-like selected enabled inner cell uses public XS; no shared indicator, even if animation supplied. |
| SOURCE_BAR=2 | Requires caller-owned animation and horizontal orientation. Before measurement, selected enabled inner cell uses public SM. Once measured, the shared indicator uses the private raised pair. |

SOURCE_TAB is a styling mode on the existing CUI tab-list API, not a new claim that the standalone GPUI Tab composition/semantics are fully implemented. SOURCE_BAR explicitly requires the existing retained state instead of hiding an allocation; source retains its indicator through window-keyed state automatically. Other variants ignore valid policies and retain their paint/animation behavior. Invalid policy or unsupported SOURCE_BAR configuration returns false before Base reduction or content/render callbacks; `cui_tabs_shadow_policy_valid` offers an explicit check because the existing widget return is a changed flag.

Ordered tuples are `(x,y,sigma,spread,black alpha)` in logical pixels:

* Standalone XS: `(0,1,2,0,13)`.
* First-measure SM: `(0,1,3,0,26)`, then `(0,1,2,-1,26)`.
* Measured private raised: `(0,1,1.5,0,26)`, then `(0,1,1,-1,26)`.

Public SM/XS are used only where source calls those presets. The measured pair is not substituted with either public preset. Its caster is the spring-resolved inner indicator, never the text label or entire trough. Background is theme background; inner height and radius follow the applicable tab metrics. Source four-size radius selection follows the size enum independently of density. CUI's expanded design sizes use the existing inner-height radius mapping as an explicit extension. Core applies inherited opacity once (half opacity gives alpha6 for XS and13 for SM/private). The inner surface follows the shadows.

Disabled standalone/first-measure tabs have no shadow, matching source `TabStyle.shadow=false`. Source TabBar's shared indicator admission does not reject a disabled selected index: CUI preserves the externally controlled disabled selection and emits the measured indicator, while keeping disabled tab appearance, inert interaction and absence of its panel. The disabled outer background can cover parts of the indicator; tests must compose that background rather than compare shadows alone to white. No disabled activation or implicit selection repair is introduced.

The initial measurement requests a follow-up frame. Existing caller spring/transition behavior remains in use. Keep `cui_tab_animation` alive through `cui_end_frame`, since existing bounds tracking writes there; give each retained tab-list owner its own state and reset it on rebinding as before. The new prepaint payload contains only copied geometry/radius/color, never a pointer into that state. It emits two DROP commands plus the surface, with an explicit five-command budget including Core's two clip commands. Layout masks/modal/opacity and bounded frame storage follow Core's existing contract. Invalid policy is a pre-reduction failure; a later global Core frame/resource failure is not a rollback promise for already accepted widget events or callback side effects. Renderers still prepare their resources before clearing targets.

Existing CUI scrolling clips both axes, whereas the pinned source wrapper specifically hides horizontal overflow. This slice preserves the scrolling API and documents possible vertical-tail clipping. Vertical SOURCE_BAR is unsupported atomically; SOURCE_TAB can style CUI's vertical extension. Generic Source StyleRefinement, standalone composition API, all TabBar lifecycle/animation/scroll differences and full family parity remain outside this appearance slice.

## Review and registration receipt

Root registers new tests and regenerates distribution; this worker changes no global configuration/gallery/backend files.

* `tests/unit/test_tabs_source_shadows.c`: actual composed Core commands for all four source sizes, both themes, exact tuples/order/caster/radius/opacity, genuine first measure, measured disabled selection, real pointer enable/disable behavior, controlled selection changes, scroll caster translation/stability, immutable paint-copy lifetime, unchanged nonsegmented/legacy paint, invalid policy/missing state/vertical failure before callbacks or retained-state changes.
* `tests/integration/tabs_source_shadows_fixture.h` and `test_tabs_source_shadows_native.c`: copy actual component draw payloads then destroy the originating context; omit TEXT identically in each consumer for geometry/alpha proof without a hardcoded font. Software, SDL Renderer, SDL GPU and Sokol agree at straight interior/outside samples within three byte levels for40 frames: five branches × light/dark × opaque/translucent × DPR1/2. Uses real DISPLAY=:0 and constrained utility GPU window; plain Xvfb is not Vulkan evidence. Link cui_software/cui_sdl3/cui_sdl_gpu/cui_sokol and their native dependencies; define GL_GLEXT_PROTOTYPES. No wrapper symbols needed.
* `uv run tests/web/test_tabs_source_shadows.py --output OUTPUT --chromium PATH`: pinned Playwright1.58, Zig0.16 WASI reactor and actual composed Core/Components fixture. Chromium1208 passes40 frames, exact branch tuples plus Canvas/WASM pixels against ordered surface/clip/shadow compositing. Initial oracle omitted the retained disabled outer background and failed; corrected reference preserves the exact byte-tolerance assertion. This is standalone proof, not Gallery wiring.

Strict native warning build passes. Full CTest166/167 fails only stale generated `distribution`; Root regenerates. Scoped ASan/UBSan/leak checking passes. Actual Wasmtime49 WASI headless tests pass. Native proof `/tmp/cui-tabs-source-native.log`; browser proof `/tmp/cui-tabs-source-browser-corrected.log`; CTest `/tmp/cui-tabs-source-final-ctest.log`; sanitizer `/tmp/cui-tabs-source-asan-final.log`; WASI `/tmp/cui-tabs-source-wasi-final.log`. New tests are not yet part of the isolated baseline CTest count. No native font pixel or physical screen-reader claim is made.

# Ordered focus traversal

Reference: gpui-component commit `87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`.
Its Cargo.lock pins registry `gpui-pre` 0.3.8, checksum
`d7f0bc3ebba070f8981b3f8e905a12f47d27794a30d029e59cdb9edf7a4b3360`.
Source evidence: `crates/base/src/button.rs` defaults index 0 / stop true and
passes both independently; `crates/component/src/button/button.rs` does likewise.
Pinned GPUI `src/tab_stop.rs` defines a signed path of group indices plus leaf
index, lexicographic comparison, then insertion order. Prefixes precede longer
paths. Negative indices are ordered values, not automatic exclusion. Nonstop
handles remain traversal anchors. `src/window.rs` focus_next/focus_prev use the
rendered frame map and wrap at either end. These files were inspected locally
in `/tmp/cui-gpui-reference` and `/tmp/gpui-pre-0.3.8`.

Use `cui_set_tab_index` after registering behavior to opt into signed ordering.
Use `cui_set_tab_stop` independently to enable or disable traversal eligibility.
Use `cui_begin_tab_group` / `cui_end_tab_group` around child submissions for
hierarchical prefixes. Equal complete paths retain semantic submission order.
Groups are independent of focus scopes: scopes constrain eligibility, while
ordered groups constrain ordering. Tab uses the previous published snapshot;
`cui_focus_step_within` uses the current submitted controls within its scope.
Disabled and no-focus controls remain ineligible. Programmatic focus on an
eligible non-stop control anchors the next/previous search at that control's path.

Zero-initialized legacy semantics retain submission order. Legacy set_tab_stop
continues exposing index 0/-1, and legacy negative tab_index remains excluded.
Calling set_tab_index explicitly allows every signed int, including -1, as an
ordered stop. Index and stop setters do not overwrite each other's choice once
signed ordering is enabled.

Storage is bounded to 32 group levels, captured by value in each semantic
snapshot. An overflow begin fails atomically; callers must end only successful
begins. Index range is portable C int (GPUI uses platform isize). This is source
ordering parity, not all GPUI focus-handle lifecycle, retained paint replay,
or accessibility platform parity. Component option mapping is separate work.

# Styled text and font faces

`cui_text_ex` and `cui_measure_text_ex` take `cui_text_style`: Normal, Medium, Semibold or Bold weight, plus independent italic and monospace flags and an application-defined `uint32_t family` ID. Family zero selects the default; nonzero IDs identify separately registered families. `cui_text_ex` also accepts an optional logical line height. The older `cui_text`, `cui_text_with_line_height` and `cui_measure_text` APIs use regular text. The style travels through Clay measurement and the draw list to the software, SDL3, SDL_GPU and Sokol renderers.

Set `cui_config.measure_styled = cui_font_measure_styled` and `measure_user = font` when creating a context with a native `cui_font`. These native callbacks take `void *` and match the Core callback signatures directly; do not cast function pointers. If `measure_user` points to an application host struct, extract its font inside correctly typed wrappers; see the complete [typography example](TYPOGRAPHY.md). The renderer must use the same font object. The legacy `measure` callback remains available; if `measure_styled` is absent, layout uses that callback for every style. Native selection uses the exact family/style registration first, then that named family's registered regular face, then the default family's matching style, then the opened regular face. Measurement, font metrics, and drawing use the same selection. CUI does not synthesize bold, italic or monospace glyphs from a regular face.

Use `cui_font_register_style(font, style, path)` to open an actual family or variant face owned by the regular font. Registrations are keyed by family, weight, italic, and monospace. A nonzero family can register its regular style; the default family's regular face remains the one opened by `cui_font_open`. A failed path leaves the previous registration intact; replacing a variant or closing the regular font releases the owned face. `cui_font_set_style(font, style, variant)` borrows a face opened by the caller. Keep borrowed faces alive through every frame that uses them, then close them separately. Call `cui_text_metrics_changed(ui)` between frames after changing registrations so Clay remeasures cached text.

The gallery registers Noto Sans Medium, Semibold, Bold and Italic plus Noto Sans Mono only when the selected regular font is the known Noto Sans path. A custom `--font` or `CUI_FONT_PATH` retains its chosen family and uses regular fallback until the application registers matching variants. The renderer swap demos configure styled measurement with their selected font; they do not assume matching variant paths for custom fonts.

`cui_measure_font_metrics(ui, size, style, &metrics)` queries the actual selected face's ascent, nonnegative descent and renderer line height in logical pixels. Set `cui_config.font_metrics = cui_font_get_metrics` with the same `measure_user = font` for the FreeType adapter. Custom hosts supply the optional `cui_font_metrics_fn` callback; it shares the measurement user pointer and receives the complete text style. A missing provider, invalid input or malformed callback result returns false and preserves the output. This API deliberately supplies no guessed baseline from string height. Line spacing can be smaller than ascent plus descent, and callers must account for leading when positioning inline content.

The native gallery and renderer swap examples register the provider. Core tests cover unavailable providers, style and fractional-size forwarding, live metric changes, invalid results and output preservation; native tests compare selected variants to their underlying faces and check metric scaling against measured line height. This is infrastructure for inline-object layout; it does not by itself implement TextView's mixed text/image flow or complete shaping-aware selection.


For example, choose a stable application ID such as `7`, register its regular
face with `(cui_text_style){.family = 7}`, and register its bold face with
`(cui_text_style){.family = 7, .weight = CUI_TEXT_WEIGHT_BOLD}`. Pass those styles
to both measurement and drawing. Missing variants remain in the named family
when a regular face is registered; CUI does not synthesize variants. Family IDs
are opaque keys, not operating-system font names or automatic font discovery.
The native registry allocates sparse entries for registered IDs and supports the
full nonzero `uint32_t` range. Removing a family's regular registration leaves
its separately registered variants intact. Removing an absent style succeeds.

One caller-opened face can be borrowed by several registrations. Replacing or
removing a borrowed registration does not close that face, and closing the
registration owner leaves borrowed faces alive. Path registration opens an
independent owned face; replacement, removal, and owner close release it. Keep
borrowed faces alive while any measurement or draw can use them, and close them
once separately. Face operations remain confined to the UI thread. Never retain
an owned face pointer beyond its registration lifetime.

Core style interning includes family alongside size, line height, weight, italic,
and monospace, so equal text at equal size in different families has distinct
layout cache keys. After changing any registration, call
`cui_text_metrics_changed(ui)` between frames for every context using the font.
A custom styled measurement provider receives the family unchanged; a legacy
measurement provider may use one fallback face for all families. A custom
renderer or browser host must apply the same family mapping used for measurement.
Zero-initialized styles keep default-family behavior; rebuild consumers after
changing public headers because the style structure has gained a member.

`tests/integration/test_text.c` compares actual proportional and monospace faces
across measurement, font metrics, glyph raster coverage, core layout, fallback,
registration failure, replacement, aliases, and owned/borrowed close lifetimes.
Set `CUI_TEST_FONT` and `CUI_TEST_FAMILY_FONT` to distinct font files when system
fixtures are unavailable. The test returns 77 when no fixture pair is found.


The native integration test also configures Core through wrappers whose shared
user pointer is a host struct containing the font. It checks styled family
forwarding against actual layout/raster output and routes the Core font-metrics
query through that same host. A wrapper's first parameter must remain `void *`;
a function taking `cui_font *` directly is a different C function-pointer type,
even though object pointers can be converted inside the wrapper.

`cui_text`, `cui_text_with_line_height`, and `cui_text_ex` all word-wrap to the
available width of their layout parent. Give the parent a constrained width
(for example, `(cui_box){.width = 240, .fixed_width = true}`) to lay out a
paragraph; a content-sized parent has no narrower width to wrap against. Explicit
line height and font style do not change wrapping. `cui_text_line` preserves a
caller-laid-out line and may overflow its parent, so use a clipping ancestor
when overflow must remain hidden. For strict UTF-8 paragraphs with explicit hard
breaks and optional color spans, `cui_text_paragraph_colored` selects word wrapping
with its `wrap` argument.

## Embed fonts in a native executable

`cui_font_open_memory(const void *data, size_t size)` opens the first face in
an in-memory font using the native `cui_text` adapter. It performs no font file
I/O and does not copy the bytes. This supports fonts compiled directly into
an executable, with no font files to install beside it.

For example, generate a C header from a font you have permission to redistribute:

```sh
python3 - <<'PYFONT'
from pathlib import Path
font = Path("assets/App-Regular.ttf").read_bytes()
with Path("app_font.h").open("w") as out:
    out.write("static const unsigned char app_font[] = {\n")
    for start in range(0, len(font), 16):
        out.write(",".join(str(b) for b in font[start:start + 16]) + ",\n")
    out.write("};\n")
PYFONT
```

Include the generated header in one C source file:

```c
#include "cui/cui_text.h"
#include "app_font.h"

/* During application initialization: */
cui_font *font = cui_font_open_memory(app_font, sizeof app_font);
if (!font) {
    /* Report initialization failure. */
    return 1;
}
/* Use font for native measurement and rendering as with cui_font_open(). */
/* After destroying the UI and any retained text layouts: */
cui_font_close(font);
```

The buffer is borrowed and must stay immutable and valid until the actual face
is released. A layout can retain a face after `cui_font_close`, so a dynamically
allocated buffer must also outlive those layouts. A `static const` array stays
valid for the entire process and needs no separate cleanup. NULL, zero-length,
oversized, or invalid font data returns NULL.

Embed bold, italic, and fallback fonts as separate arrays, open each with
`cui_font_open_memory`, and register their handles with `cui_font_set_style` or
`cui_font_set_fallbacks`. These registrations borrow handles; keep the faces
alive while registered and close them separately after use. File-based and
memory-based faces can be mixed.

Embedding increases executable size; large multilingual fallback sets may be
better shipped separately. Check each font's redistribution and embedding
license. Embedding assets is independent of static linking: link CUI and its
native dependencies statically as well if your distribution requires that.
This API concerns native fonts; browser font loading continues to use the web host.

## Native letter spacing

See [Letter spacing](LETTER_SPACING.md) for the opt-in cluster tracking API,
provider capability checks, ABI rebuild requirement, negative-spacing policy,
and renderer/binding limitations. Canvas and GPU tracking are not implemented.

# Contextual paragraph text alignment

`cui_text_paragraph_colored_aligned` adds physical left, center and right alignment
without changing existing function signatures. It accepts the same text, style,
wrapping and full-text color spans as `cui_text_paragraph_colored`, followed by a
`cui_text_align`. It reserves an available-width paragraph box and positions every
final visual row independently within that box. The width comes from this frame's
layout, including the parent's padding; it does not read previous-frame bounds.

Center uses half the remaining row width; right uses all of it. An overflowing row
receives a negative center/right offset, as in the pinned source. Empty and trailing
lines retain their normal height without producing a text command. These are
physical directions: RTL text does not turn LEFT into logical start. Original
paragraph bytes, bidi context, selected byte ranges and intersected color spans
are unchanged. The resulting draw command bounds carry the final aligned origin,
so existing renderer, clip and copied-snapshot consumers receive that position.
No geometry session is retained or newly acquired for alignment itself.

`cui_label_options.alignment` forwards the same choice. Zero initialization keeps
the existing left/default path, including the legacy paragraph box sizing. Center
and right also expand the optional semantic wrapper to available width, so adding
a semantic ID does not change the text's alignment. Masked labels continue to
submit only bullet bytes, without highlight spans or original semantic names.

The old paragraph API, ordinary `cui_text`, contextual line APIs and legacy Label
wrapper keep their existing behavior. Applications can still align whole boxes
through `cui_box`; text alignment is distinct because rows may have unequal widths.
Scrolling/clipping owners retain Core's existing sizing conventions; applications
that permit oversized scroll content should supply its intended inner width.

The source requirement is frozen GPUI Kit commit
`87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`, `crates/component/src/label.rs:192-215`:
Label forwards its inherited Styled refinement to its containing div. The frozen
website documents `.text_center()` and `.text_right()` at
`website/component/label.md:36-49`; the actual story exercises both at
`crates/story/src/stories/label_story.rs:193-195`. Its pinned gpui-pre 0.3.8
StyledText renderer forwards `text_style.text_align` to wrapped line painting;
`src/text_system/line.rs:954-976,1000-1005` defines the signed row-width offset.
This API covers those three alignment choices, not arbitrary GPUI StyleRefinement,
justification, logical start/end, or platform pixel parity.

`test_text_alignment_source` checks all three choices at changing current-frame
widths, wrapped and unwrapped unequal rows, hard breaks, blank/trailing lines,
padding, original RTL paragraphs and intersected spans, copied command lifetimes,
invalid alignment/UTF-8 rejection, capacity failure and next-frame recovery,
legacy origin preservation, secondary/highlight colors, and masked semantic Label
alignment. It is portable C11 and runs headlessly with strict compiler warnings
and ASAN/UBSAN. Integrators register this new test and regenerate distribution.
documents.docs/TEXT_GRADIENT.md:
# Gradient text

`cui_text_paragraph_painted` paints real glyph coverage with a continuous linear
color field. One glyph can contain many colors. Wrapping, shaping, fallback,
contextual line sources, alignment, carets and selection retain their existing
geometry. The paint does not insert extra text runs or split shaping clusters.

```c
cui_text_gradient_stop stops[] = {
    {0, {236, 72, 153, 255}},
    {1, {59, 130, 246, 255}},
};
cui_text_paint paint = {
    .kind = CUI_TEXT_PAINT_LINEAR,
    .x0 = 0, .y0 = 0, .x1 = 1, .y1 = 0,
    .anchor = CUI_TEXT_ANCHOR_BLOCK,
    .stops = stops, .stop_count = 2,
};
bool ok = cui_text_paragraph_painted(ui, cui_string("A colorful heading"),
    36, 44, (cui_text_style){0}, true, CUI_TEXT_ALIGN_LEFT, paint);
```

Call inside an active frame. Check the returned boolean and frame error. Core
copies the 2–8 stops into frame storage; the caller may reuse its array after the
call. The emitted stop pointers and text remain borrowed until frame invalidation.
A retained draw-list snapshot must deep-copy both. `cui_typography_text_painted`
provides the same operation using a typography token. A zero-initialized solid
paint uses `paint.color` through the existing solid paragraph path.

## Coordinates and interpolation

Input endpoints are finite normalized coordinates in [0, 1], and must differ.
Use (0,0) to (1,0) for rightward paint, (0,0) to (0,1) for downward paint, or
(0,0) to (1,1) for a diagonal. Reversing endpoints reverses the direction.
`CUI_TEXT_ANCHOR_BLOCK` uses the complete paragraph layout container, including
hard breaks and empty rows. Every visual row receives the same resolved axis.
`CUI_TEXT_ANCHOR_LINE` restarts the axis in each visual row's advance box, after
alignment. Ink overhang can extend beyond that box. Anchors use layout line boxes,
not glyph ink bounds. Draw commands contain resolved global logical coordinates.
A resolved axis collapsed by an empty layout dimension samples its final stop.

Stop positions are finite, nondecreasing values in [0, 1]. Outside the first or
last stop, extend that stop's color. Equal positions make a hard edge: the last
stop at the exact position wins. Project each pixel center onto the axis.
Interpolate **premultiplied, encoded sRGB byte channels**, including alpha, then
unpremultiply and round to RGBA8. This is neither linear-light nor Oklab
interpolation. Transparent red to opaque blue therefore has a blue midpoint with
half opacity. Multiply the sampled alpha by glyph coverage. Ancestor opacity is
applied once to copied stop alpha in Core. Existing surface compositing follows.
This explicit contract does not promise CSS gradient color-space equivalence.

## Renderer support

Software and SDL advertise `CUI_RENDER_TEXT_LINEAR_GRADIENT` when a native font is
available. They sample actual glyph masks. SDL samples in logical coordinates at
the current raster density, preserving Retina positioning and existing solid
text cache behavior. Its temporary colored glyph surface is bounded to 4 MiB;
allocation or renderer errors return failure. Painted glyph results are not
cached by paint identity.

The Canvas module `web/modules/cui_text_paint.js` paints one complete shaped
visual row into a coverage mask, then samples the same field per physical pixel.
It preserves contextual shaping and italic ink overhang. Existing clipping,
alpha and compositing apply when the mask is drawn. Its temporary mask is bounded
to 4 MiB per row. Positive axis-aligned scale and translation are supported;
rotation, shear, invalid paint and oversized masks throw explicit errors.

Sokol and SDL_GPU reject gradient draw lists before clearing or submitting any
commands. They do not advertise the capability. GPU implementation and hardware
acceptance remain future work. Custom renderers must inspect the capability and
paint kind, and implement the documented sampling or reject the list. Ignoring
paint and drawing a solid substitute is unsupported.

Gradient paragraphs currently do not combine with byte color spans. Prepaint
writers reject gradient commands explicitly. There are no radial gradients,
textures, animated stop ownership, automatic selection colors or binding APIs in
this change. Selection highlighting remains a separate draw operation.

## Validation and integration

`tests/integration/test_text_gradient.c` checks copied stops, opacity, block and
line anchors, wrapping and identical bounds/caret/selection queries, hard edges,
transparent interpolation and two colors inside one actual native glyph.
`test_text_gradient_sdl.c` checks real captured glyph pixels and clips at densities
1, 1.5 and 2 under private Xvfb. `tests/web/test_text_gradient.py` runs headless
Chromium pixel checks at the same densities and compares contextual italic mask
coverage with a direct full-line Canvas fill. These checks do not constitute
macOS hardware or GPU renderer acceptance.

For integration, register the native tests with an explicit font fixture, copy
the new browser module with the gallery, and inline the private paint helper when
generating the Core amalgamation. Regenerate distribution/SDK artifacts together
with the public draw-command layout change. Test native builds through
`python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir <build>`; browser tests stay headless.

## Public gallery example

Open **Theme** in the public gallery, then change **Typography paint** from
**Solid text** to **Linear gradient text**. The typography sample uses the real
Core painted-paragraph API with copied pink-to-blue stops; the browser receives
the resolved axis and stops from WASM. The font family, size, weight and italic
controls continue to apply. The gradient's paragraph wraps within the sample
container. The solid sample keeps its existing single-line presentation.

The component's copy button supplies the painted-paragraph C example while the
gradient is selected. Its **Gradient text** guide link opens this guide. This
uses the existing Theme entry and preserves all 78 catalog families. It does not
reuse byte color spans as a gradient substitute.

`tests/web/test_gradient_gallery.py --directory <built-gallery>` loads the real
compiled gallery, changes the public paint control, checks serialized paint
stops and resolved coordinates, and reads actual glyph interiors. It exercises
desktop and 390px viewports at device pixel ratios 1 and 2, copyable code, the
return to solid paint and guide navigation. The guide must be included in the
public documentation generator before this integration test runs.

# Base Input change and submit notifications

Include `cui/cui_text_input_events.h` for two additive Base-only APIs:
`cui_base_input_events` submits the ordinary Input reducer and observes each event;
`cui_base_input_reduce_event_events` observes one event for composite controls that
already register their textbox and reduce events in queue order. Existing Input
signatures, options/results, validation, presentation and mutation policy remain
unchanged. A [Styled Input facade](TEXT_INPUT_STYLED_EVENTS.md) adds the same
observer at its existing reduction seam. [Textarea and Editor](MULTILINE_EVENTS.md)
have separately documented aggregate observers. Foreign bindings do not expose
these synchronous C observers.

```c
static void input_event(void *user, const cui_component_text_event *event) {
    unsigned *changes = user;
    if (event->event.kind == CUI_COMPONENT_EVENT_CHANGE)
        ++*changes; /* Update independent application state. */
    /* Inspect text only in this callback; copy with a bounded helper if needed. */
}
/* During submission, inside the textbox's same-ID layout box: */
cui_input_event_result result = cui_base_input_events(
    ui, input_id, cui_string("Name"), edit, &behavior,
    (cui_base_input_options){0},
    (cui_component_text_handler){input_event, &change_counter});
/* Reading result counts must not repeat the callback's side effects. */
```

This is drawing-free Base behavior. Painting, measured hit testing and styled
password mask resources must still use the appropriate existing composition.
Do not call an old reducer/Styled Input and this facade for the same events:
that would edit the model twice. The single-event API requires prior textbox
registration with `cui_interact`, increasing indices and the existing semantic/
paint completion responsibilities. It does not replay the rest of the queue.

## Meaning and ordering

CHANGE is a post-mutation notification when the existing single-event reducer
reports changed and the committed document revision actually differs. It is not
a rejectable proposed value and cannot veto or undo the edit. Selection-only
motion, preedit-only updates and rejected/no-op edits do not report CHANGE.
A missing observer does not make the control readonly: ordinary editing continues.
Use existing `validate`, normalization/format/matcher and readonly options for
their documented policies; no new REQUEST or COMMIT is invented here.

SUBMIT reports the existing single-line eligible nonrepeated Enter result.
It is an intent, not proof of accepted form data or successful validation. Existing
modifier, readonly, disabled, composition/preferred-character and consumption
behavior is preserved. In particular readonly Input can still report Enter under
its legacy policy; disabled Input does not. A rejected text edit followed by an
eligible Enter can produce SUBMIT without CHANGE. Multiline editing has no new
submit facade in this slice.

For each event: existing checked operation and presentation completion, final
revision comparison, CHANGE if changed, SUBMIT if eligible, then the next queue
event. TEXT/Enter/TEXT/Enter therefore exposes both intermediate committed values,
not just the final frame buffer. The whole-frame `control` field is the unchanged
legacy aggregate result; `change_count` and `submit_count` count actual observer
calls only, saturating at SIZE_MAX with `count_overflow`. No observer means zero
counts even when `control.changed` is true. Result reads/copies never dispatch.

IME START/UPDATE/CANCEL normally only affect provisional state. A successful
COMPOSITION_COMMIT that changes the committed revision reports CHANGE, not a
new COMMIT event. Rejected host COMMIT still ends its session using the existing
cleanup before observation; rejection does not become a document change.
Undo/Redo and synchronous clipboard edits report their actual committed revision
changes, retaining existing history/validation exceptions and clipboard errors.
No programmatic model edits outside these reducers are retrospectively replayed.

## Evidence, privacy and lifetime

`event` carries exact context-local frame/index identity. Known KEY_DOWN/UP
origins are KEYBOARD; actual pointer types are POINTER. TEXT and composition
origin remain UNKNOWN: a host-delivered text event does not prove a physical
keyboard. Presence flags establish evidence. No `HAS_ACTIVATION` or synthesized
activation snapshot is attached to text, movement, submit or IME operations.
No raw input/clipboard/preedit text is copied into metadata.

`before/after` are scalar `cui_edit_state` snapshots with UTF-8 byte offsets,
revision and history availability. They are not old text, a diff or a complete
multicursor selection set. `text` borrows the **current committed** model buffer
only through the callback. Copying the event struct alone does not retain text.
Use `cui_component_event_copy_utf8` with caller storage and an explicit byte limit;
check its status before retaining the returned owned-buffer span. No implicit
per-event document-sized allocation is introduced.

For masked Input or any password content purpose, `has_text=false` and `text` is
empty/NULL, including SUBMIT. Scalar length/selection/revision metadata remains
available; this API does not promise to hide those fields or make logging them
appropriate. A nonsecret empty value has `has_text=true` with an empty span.

Handler/user are borrowed synchronously. Observers may change unrelated app
state and record future edits, omission or teardown. They must not mutate,
rebind or destroy the active model/context/state/workspaces/caller buffers,
free userdata/resources or recursively submit. Apply such deferred changes only
after frame completion and renderer consumption. These are **preconditions**,
not runtime guards: the engine acceptance callback's mutation guard does not
extend automatically to a post-reducer observer. Existing presentation callbacks
retain their previous timing/side-effect contract. Never implement rejection by
calling Undo from an observer.

## Verification scope

`tests/unit/test_text_input_events.c` exercises ordered TEXT/Enter multiplicity,
intermediate values, exact indices/sources, passive counts, missing-observer edits,
selection/no-op behavior, Undo/Redo, accepted/rejected IME commits and preedit,
secure redaction, synchronous paste, presentation completion before observation,
bounded owned copies, invalid single-event indices and explicit composite
single-event reduction. Legacy Input/acceptance/password/Questionnaire tests
remain the behavioral regressions; native tests use
`python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir <build>`.

This establishes Base Input notification behavior, not browser/OS IME acceptance,
foreign request rejection, full event-family uniformity or general callback
reentrancy. Styled and multiline observer guarantees have their own guides. Integrators register the new test and
refresh source metadata/generated distributions/SDKs with normal tooling.
