# Styled Input observers

`cui_input_events` accepts the same arguments as `cui_input_ex`, followed by a
`cui_component_text_handler`, and returns `cui_input_event_result`. For example:

```c
cui_input_event_result result = cui_input_events(
    ui, id, &theme, cui_string("Name"), edit, &state, options,
    (cui_component_text_handler){on_text_event, app});
```

The handler receives committed CHANGE and eligible Enter SUBMIT events in input
order. A batch can deliver several of each; `result.control` preserves the legacy
aggregate result and the counts describe actual callback invocations. A null
handler still edits and produces zero callback counts. SUBMIT does not certify
form validity. Validation remains in the existing options.

Payloads and exact frame/index evidence follow [Base Input](TEXT_INPUT_EVENTS.md).
Text is borrowed only during the callback; use `cui_component_event_copy_utf8` to
retain a bounded copy. Masked and password-purpose inputs redact committed text
on both event kinds. IME preedit is not a committed CHANGE.

The observer runs after each event's presentation completion, before Styled Input
finalizes its mask cache and paints. Existing formatting, secure staging and
allocation failure behavior remain in the same submission. Failed mask preparation
does not notify or apply queued edits.

Keep context, edit, state, theme, buffers, workspace and resource descriptors alive
and unchanged throughout submission. Observers may update unrelated application
state, including a flag to omit the control next frame. They must not edit, rebind,
free or destroy these objects, recursively submit UI, or paint. This is a caller
precondition, not a runtime guard. Defer removal/destruction until after the frame
and renderer have consumed its borrowed resources.

The additive facade does not change `cui_input`, `cui_input_ex`, their options or
results. [Editor and Textarea observers](MULTILINE_EVENTS.md) have separate
aggregation and timing contracts. Language bindings do not expose these C observers.

`tests/unit/test_text_input_styled_events.c` compares legacy and facade results,
selection/revision and draw commands, ordered intermediate copies, masked IME,
password redaction, missing observers, deferred omission and mask allocation
failure. Existing Input acceptance and password tests remain required.
documents.docs/TEXT_VIEW.md: # TextView This module implements a bounded document model and selectable styled presentation against the frozen GPUI 0.7.1 TextView contract. It is a substantive first slice; the remaining source features below are not implemented. The application supplies `cui_text_view_workspace`: separate source and rendered UTF-8 buffers, byte mappings, spans, blocks, glyph geometry, and optional highlight storage. Keep this storage and state alive while the view is submitted. The parser allocates no memory. Source and rendered buffers include a terminating zero byte; capacities therefore include that byte. Documents are limited to 65,536 bytes and 8,192 nodes. Glyph capacity must cover rendered byte length. Insufficient parser capacity and malformed UTF-8 leave the previous document intact. Initialize with `cui_text_view_init`, update with `cui_text_view_set_text`, and render with `cui_text_view(ui, id, theme, &state, cui_text_view_default())`. The defaults select text, fit content without a scrollbar, use theme text/link/selection/code colors, and leave streaming fades disabled. Set a positive width for deterministic first-frame wrapping. Grow dimensions use retained bounds and a first-frame estimate (320 by 240); bounds changes schedule a follow-up measurement frame. Markdown handles headings, emphasis, strikethrough, inline/fenced code, links, entities, escaped punctuation, bounded nested lists and passive task checkboxes with source starting numbers and consecutive numbering, rules, pipe tables and block images. Soft paragraph breaks join with spaces; two-space hard breaks retain line breaks. HTML handles the corresponding safe presentation tags and strips script/style bodies; it never executes markup or loads resources itself. Each rendered scalar maps to its original source bytes, including entity atoms, while block separators have no source mapping. Markdown range highlights accept rendered byte ranges; source range conversion excludes syntax. HTML source mapping/highlights return unsupported, matching the frozen source restriction. Selection endpoints must be UTF-8 boundaries. `cui_text_view_select` reports whether selection changed. Selection supports separate-frame pointer dragging, Shift plus arrow/Home/End, select all, Escape clearing and copy through the optional portable clipboard interface. It is read-only. Links remain independently focusable; primary and secondary activation forward the original event to `on_link`. A selection drag suppresses link activation. An installed callback consumes activation; otherwise an explicit host `open_url` callback handles primary activation. URLs are decoded temporary slices valid during the callback and must be copied for deferred use. Image loaders return borrowed straight RGBA bitmaps; pixels must survive renderer completion. Image callbacks run during submission and may report not ready until a later frame. The application schedules invalidation when asynchronous work completes. Actual bitmap drawing uses Core clipping and the renderer adapters. Code and table action callbacks receive a unique action container ID and compose real controls. Code actions overlay the top right with 8px insets and a fitting opaque background, after document text paints. They do not enlarge code blocks. Table actions occupy a full-width footer separated by 4px. Callback heights are explicit; callbacks must not end the owning container. Interactive action controls keep their own pointer gestures and do not start document selection. The optional code highlighter supplies foreground colors per code byte. Scrollable views compose the real Scroll component, including scrollbars and consumed-event handling. Reveal requests retain only the latest range, expire after one second, follow unchanged source edits, and reveal the nearest line in the view's own scroll area. Fit views report window line bounds through an explicit host callback. Max-lines fit mode clips oversized content and drops ordinary lines that straddle the cap. Streaming append fades last 350 ms; replacement is immediate and reduced motion disables animation. Ordered highlights paint in request order, then selection above them. Unchanged source prefixes/suffixes retain highlights through edits. A replacement inside a table drops highlights from the edited row and subsequent rows because their cell positions may change; earlier unchanged rows and tables shifted as an unchanged suffix retain highlights. Nested HTML emphasis preserves outer styles after an inner close. `src/base/cui_text_view.c` links with the C math library only. Styled presentation requires Core, Theme and Scroll (base and components), the components checkmark drawing helper, plus portable platform clipboard declarations. Styled text uses real weight/italic/monospace measurement and drawing; register matching native faces for the desired typography. The regular face remains the renderer fallback. No Content rich-text parser existed to reuse. Remaining frozen-source gaps are tracked explicitly: complete CommonMark/HTML5 and complete nested-list/quote structure, MDX/plugins/YAML front matter, image error UI, complete shared-window selection identity, touch selection menus and handles, grapheme/BiDi shaping, inherited parent foreground palettes, fully configurable table/action refinements, automatic enclosing-list reveal, background syntax styles, cached/asynchronous parsing and layout. Default wrap tables use capped text-length column proportions (5 to 150 characters) and 64px minimum columns. Narrow wrap tables clip at the document edge; opt-in adaptive horizontal table scrolling is available through `table_mode`. These limitations must not be presented as full source parity. Headless tests cover transactional bounded parsing and randomized syntax, Unicode mapping/selection, edit tracking, entities, safe HTML, tables, clipping, fade state, composed action geometry and clicks, fence lengths and code content, real styled draw commands, separate-frame selection and focus, primary/secondary link callbacks, drag suppression, bitmap drawing and invalid geometry. Source-format copy uses `cui_text_view_copy_selection` with a separate caller-owned output buffer. It reconstructs partial inline emphasis, links, code, headings, quotes, lists, aligned table rows and fenced code. Table selections preserve all table rows, emit blank unselected cells and retain the delimiter alignment row. Select-all returns the original Markdown verbatim; HTML and plain documents use rendered text. Capacity queries report required bytes without writing output, and insufficient capacity preserves existing output. For Ctrl+C, provide `options.copy_buffer/copy_capacity` and set `copy_format` to Source. Scrollable views copy plain text, matching the frozen source's effective format. Insufficient output capacity leaves the clipboard unchanged. Default table cells use 8px horizontal and 4px vertical padding, normal inherited text weight, clipped content, and one border at each shared edge. Header backgrounds use the code background, body cells use the theme surface. TextView links follow the frozen text style's primary color mapping rather than the general link token. The pure layout API additionally exposes `table_mode` (`WRAP` by default, `ADAPTIVE`, or `NOWRAP`). Adaptive columns measure each trimmed cell line using its styled spans, retain a 48px minimum, and shrink to content-dependent floors between 160px and 480px (never above the measured content). Nowrap columns keep single-line content widths. Both account for 16px horizontal padding, shared 1px column borders, and the 2px outer frame. Extra viewport space grows columns in proportion to measured widths. The styled component uses the same mode and composes actual axis-locked horizontal Scroll owners with hidden bars. Borders stay fixed while cell content moves; links and selection use translated coordinates. Each first table cell owns its scroll state, retained across append/edit parsing when its block ordinal and source start remain stable. Reveal requests bring the target cell text into the horizontal viewport. Changing a table's source start or block ordinal resets its scroll state. Window-shared selection, touch and horizontal selection edge autoscroll remain separate limitations. Task list markers (`[ ]`, `[x]`, `[X]`) are source metadata rather than selectable text. Partial Source copy reconstructs them after the list marker. Presentation uses a 14px foreground border box, a foreground fill when checked, and the shared 10px checkmark drawing helper; the indicator has no interactive semantics. The checkmark chooses black or white contrast against the supplied foreground, which preserves the source defaults while also supporting custom palettes. Continuations after nested child blocks and nested non-list blocks remain parser limitations. `cui_text_view_decode_resource` decodes the bounded parser entity subset and Markdown ASCII punctuation escapes into a separate caller buffer. HTML attribute backslashes and Plain format bytes remain literal. Link, opener and image callbacks receive decoded, zero-terminated URI bytes borrowed only for the callback; asynchronous loaders must copy them. No URL fetching or URI policy is implicit. Source copy retains original source spelling. Complete HTML5 named entity and URI normalization behavior remains part of the full parser gap. Resource callbacks use at most 64KiB of temporary stack storage, reused across images; entity lookup scans no more than 17 bytes per candidate. List prefix spacing follows measured text, including the trailing space from the source prefix helper. Ordinary markers reserve their full measured prefix width; they do not impose a synthetic minimum or extra gap. Task indicators retain their separate 14px box plus 6px gap. Prefix bytes live in the caller block workspace so draw-command text remains valid through renderer completion. Horizontal table routing consumes horizontal wheel input at an edge or without overflow. Native precise gestures retain their initial axis until an end phase, a 28ms quiet interval, or a strong axis change. The frozen source disables this persistent gesture locking on WASM; ordinary vertical chaining is preserved. Host adapters must provide precise gesture phase metadata explicitly. Markdown list item nesting is tracked with parent block indices, source starts, and independent per-level ordered counters. Nested ordered markers use uppercase letters at depth one and lowercase at deeper levels; zero-start lists retain numeric prefixes. Bullet shapes vary across five depths. Each rendered nesting level adds 16px, while partial Source copy uses parent marker widths to indent children and includes empty ancestor markers for a selection confined to children. The parser supports at most 32 list levels and rejects deeper input transactionally. Nested-child continuations reconnect to their enclosing list item. The first paragraph after a nested list repeats the parent marker or passive task indicator; later paragraphs use the continuation indent. Source copy groups an item's selected paragraphs before its nested lists, while plain copy and selection retain paint order. The bounded serialization order uses at most 8192 16-bit block indices and may take quadratic time in that fixed node bound. Fenced code following an existing list paragraph retains parent membership and removes the opening indentation from content while keeping original byte mappings. It renders in the list continuation column with working code action callbacks. Fences written directly after a list marker are real code blocks with independent list-item metadata: the marker or passive task indicator occupies a separate column, outside the code background. Such code blocks own nested-list ancestry and keep exact source mappings for literal backslashes and subsequent lines. Loose-list spacing and multi-paragraph quote containers are not yet a complete list AST. First-child headings and single-paragraph quotes use real block styles with a separate normal-size list marker column. Following indented headings and quotes remain children of the enclosing item. List ordering is independent of heading level, preserving bullet versus decimal prefixes and subsequent counters. Ordinary list paragraphs join lazy continuation lines with spaces and preserve two-space hard breaks. A following indented paragraph stays attached to its list item, paints at a 16px continuation indent, and does not repeat a task indicator or marker. Partial Source copy prefixes the first selected item paragraph and indents subsequent paragraphs and hard-break lines under its marker. Continuations after nested child lists follow the separate row and copy rules above. Setext headings recognize one or more equals signs or hyphens after a paragraph, including joined paragraph lines. Leading indentation is limited to three spaces. Without an opt-in frontmatter parser, a leading horizontal rule followed by a Setext heading retains Markdown meaning; YAML frontmatter plugins remain absent. Prepared glyph lines use core's explicit no-wrap text leaf so Clay cannot wrap a measured line a second time because of fractional font measurements. Consecutive explicitly prefixed quote lines form one paragraph, with soft lines joined and two-space hard breaks preserved. This works for root quotes, first list-item quotes and indented list continuation quotes. Partial Source copy repeats the quote prefix after a hard break and keeps any surrounding list indent. Blank quote paragraphs, lazy unprefixed quote continuation, and nested quote containers remain outside this bounded paragraph representation. Markdown images in list items retain parent ancestry, ordered counters and Source copy grouping. Standalone Markdown images now use the same one-byte paragraph object flow as mixed images, including default inline sizing, loaded/unloaded slots and list continuation marker rules. Their ranges cover complete image syntax, rather than the former alt-text ranges. Bare root HTML images also use a separate paragraph with an atomic image slot. Exact source inline image flow requires styled font ascent, descent and baseline metrics. In frozen `inline_flow.rs`, each line starts with the body's baseline and descent. An image baseline is clamped to its height from `height / 2 + body_baseline - line_height / 2`; line ascent and descent expand with that baseline, and the image paints at `line_y + line_ascent - baseline`. The optional core font metrics provider now supplies actual body ascent and descent. The body baseline is `(line_height - ascent - descent) / 2 + ascent`. Ready standalone images use this formula and retain a separate logical row extent for list prefixes and following blocks. Pure layout accepts validated optional body metrics. Without a valid provider, images retain top alignment; no size-derived baseline is synthesized. Mixed Markdown images now occupy atomic one-byte span slots. Their host bitmaps reserve horizontal space among text runs and wrap at object boundaries. Default inline height is 75% of the logical line height, with loaded aspect ratio or a square unloaded slot, matching the frozen source. Selection maps each slot to the entire image source syntax, and Source copy preserves that syntax. Title tooltips, standalone-image dimensions and custom object renderers remain unimplemented. Bare root HTML image blocks still retain their earlier alt-text ranges. Tables following existing list content retain parent membership and paint in the 16px continuation column. Column sizing, horizontal viewport clipping and footer action widths use the remaining column width. Source copy emits the table among the parent item's own blocks, indents every table row beneath its marker, and keeps nested child lists after that content. Tables within a list omit inter-block paragraph space; the list still separates from following root content. A final root table also omits trailing paragraph space, matching the document's last-block rule. First-child tables introduced directly by a list marker preserve list-item metadata on the first cell. Other cells and nested children retain that item as their parent. The separate marker column stays outside the horizontal mask and does not move when the table scrolls; table-body snapshots preserve its scroll offset when appending rows. Inline image slots use a single space byte in the rendered selection coordinate space; Plain copy omits that slot, while Source copy writes the original image syntax. No unloaded bitmap is fabricated. Removing the host loader restores a compact square slot without discarding surrounding text or retaining stale pixels. Layout may provide a font-metrics callback keyed by each block's actual font size and style flags. The styled component uses the core provider, so a semibold heading image uses heading metrics rather than regular body metrics. The callback supersedes fixed body metrics and may decline measurement; unavailable or invalid callback metrics use top alignment. Host bitmap validity follows the shared core contract, and invalid loader output becomes an unloaded slot instead of a malformed draw. Each mixed image line expands its logical ascent and descent from the actual body baseline and image baseline. Wrapped following lines begin after that complete logical extent, including fonts whose ascent or descent exceeds the requested line height. Text-only lines retain their requested logical height. Bounded balanced brackets and parentheses recognize linked Markdown images and parenthesized destinations. Quoted titles and angle-delimited destinations no longer become part of the host image URI. A linked image uses its alt source as its link label, activates the host link callback through ordinary capture, and Source copy preserves its enclosing link. The frozen renderer itself ignores the image title (`image_element` takes `_title`), so no image-title tooltip is required. This delimiter parser is not a complete CommonMark grammar. Images inside HTML paragraph, heading and table-cell containers now share the atomic inline flow with neighboring styled text. Linked HTML images also use the ordinary link callback. Missing `src` images inside these containers are skipped. Bare root HTML images use the same sizing rules in their own paragraph. HTML source-range/copy support remains unfinished. HTML container tracking is bounded and does not replace a repairing HTML5 tree parser. Inline HTML image dimensions support finite nonnegative numbers, `px`, and `%`, with width/height attributes taking precedence over matching CSS declarations. Percentages use the logical line height as their base, matching frozen `inline_flow.rs`, rather than viewport width. A single loaded dimension preserves intrinsic aspect ratio; an unloaded width-only image uses the line height, and an unloaded height-only image uses a square. Both dimensions are independent when specified. Invalid declarations fall back to valid CSS or default dimensions. Numeric tokens are bounded to 64 bytes, exponents to ±38, and dimensions to 10,000,000 logical pixels. Zero-sized images retain their selection slot and paint no bitmap. Caller-provided NaN/negative/nonfinite dimensions are rejected before layout mutation. Tall image rows retain their logical origin separately from shifted text bounds, so aligned table cells move all runs together. Both Markdown and HTML standalone images now use one-byte image slots and source default sizing rather than alt-text ranges or unscaled intrinsic pixels. Bare root HTML images retain separate paragraph boundaries and accept the same explicit dimensions as paragraph images. Missing root `src` images are skipped. HTML tag boundaries respect quoted `>` characters and HTML attribute whitespace. HTML `` tags embedded in Markdown use the same atomic run model, decoded URI, explicit dimensions, baseline and enclosing Markdown link behavior. This includes the frozen linked HTML image after a soft newline regression. Missing `src` tags are skipped. Other embedded HTML tags and multiline HTML grammar remain outside this targeted inline-image handling. Plain copy and Ctrl+C omit image slots, matching source paragraph text output. Copying only an image in Plain mode produces no text and leaves the clipboard unchanged. The raw `selected_text` accessor remains a borrowed coordinate slice of `workspace.rendered`, including object slots, valid until the next text mutation; use `copy_document_selection(PLAIN)` for styled presentation or clipboard text. Default Plain clipboard output uses bounded temporary storage when no caller buffer is supplied. Ordinary Source-format Ctrl+C continues to require caller output storage. The frozen implementation selects shared text runs around images and includes images in Source copy when selection spans the adjacent run boundaries. CUI still retains atomic image slots in its low-level coordinate API. Styled pointer selection projects text glyphs instead of independently selecting those slots; full shared-window selection identity remains tracked. Markdown Source copy and selected source ranges include consecutive images at a paragraph boundary when selection begins at the first text byte after leading images or ends at the last text byte before trailing images. Selecting only a middle portion of that text does not include the boundary images. This follows the frozen paragraph's pending-image rule while leaving Plain output and raw selection coordinates unchanged. Optional shared selection uses an application-owned `cui_text_view_selection` and a fixed `cui_text_view_selection_member` array. Initialize the manager, then register each live state with its unique view ID, nonzero scope, stable logical `document_order`, table mode and enabled flag. Registration order does not control copy order. Duplicate state ownership and replacement of a live ID with a different state are rejected. Remove a member **before** destroying its state or workspace; removal clears its selection and removes the retained pointer. The array and manager must also outlive all uses. Re-registering the same ID/state updates its options; disabling the owner clears the active shared selection. For each frame, open the application's nonmodal focus scope matching the member scope, call `cui_text_view_selection_update` once before painting any members, then submit those views with `options.shared_selection` set to the manager and close the application scope. This preserves one event reduction and lets every member paint the same projection. Initial hit testing uses the previous clipped semantic ownership; member geometry becomes available after its first submitted frame. Do not update a scope before its modal/ancestor guards have been submitted. Registration does not create UI or make a disabled member selectable. A cross-view drag retains window anchor/cursor points and projects their row band through each member's retained viewport, vertical scroll and horizontal table scroll. Glyph midpoints follow the frozen window selection band rule. Image slots are not independently selected by this shared projection; text on both sides can still select their Source syntax. Other scopes are not projected. Ctrl+C joins nonempty selected participants with a newline in document order; Source copy uses each document's existing reconstruction. Caller copy storage is recommended for large multi-view selections; capacity failure leaves the clipboard unchanged. Standalone views retain their existing behavior when the manager is absent. Remaining shared-selection gaps include touch handles, comprehensive multi-click coverage across every block kind, content-key resolution across dynamic renderers, cross-view automatic scrolling, and individual image-separated text-run ranges within a paragraph. Projection retains a range for each block/table cell and clips to its viewport, rather than maintaining the source window manager's full inline-run state. Applications must refresh registration enabled flags and call the update before painting; there is no implicit window registry or stale-participant eviction. Styled Ctrl+C and shared copy use `cui_text_view_copy_document_selection`, which serializes selected blocks. Partial Plain Paragraph, Heading and Code selections include the source block's trailing newline. Table cells join with spaces, rows with newlines, and the table adds a final newline. Shared selection joins these participant strings with another newline in document order, preserving the frozen output (two selected one-line paragraphs copy as `first\n\nsecond\n`). Source mode retains Markdown reconstruction without those Plain terminators. `copy_selection(PLAIN)` remains a low-level coordinate slice copy with image slots omitted; it does not serialize document structure. `selected_text` is a borrowed bounding coordinate view and may include unselected gaps in a shared projection. Use document selection copy for source-equivalent styled text output. Shared projection stores separate ranges for wrapped table cells. Selection of one visual row therefore does not pull later wrapped text from a different cell into its copy or highlight. Within one paragraph, separate image-delimited text runs still share one block range; exact per-inline-run state remains tracked. Re-registering an existing member under a different scope or table mode clears its old projection; if it owns the active drag, the manager clears that drag. Changing text discards glyph geometry and projected ranges. Such a member cannot start a shared gesture until it has submitted fresh geometry; retained viewport coordinates alone are insufficient. Ordinary pointer drags now use the same window-point projection as shared selection. Dragging within an image selects no text and copies no Source syntax; a tap on a linked image still activates its link, while a drag cancels that release activation. Reverse text-image-text drags retain their direction and include image syntax in Source copy when adjacent text boundaries are selected. Programmatic `cui_text_view_select` remains the explicit low-level coordinate API and can select an image slot by itself; that does not describe the styled pointer behavior. HTML Source fallback to Plain and unavailable HTML source offsets match the frozen implementation's `effective_format` contract and html5ever's absent source spans; they are not missing HTML reconstruction features promised by that source. Mouse multi-click selection now uses the pinned source character classes and 128-scalar word boundary limit. Double-click selects a word without splitting UTF-8 or crossing image runs; triple-click selects an ordinary paragraph or the visual row in an image-flow paragraph. Higher counts use logical-line boundaries. Plain multi-click copy preserves the chosen text override while Source copy retains Markdown markup. Shared selection clears other members, retains focus ownership and preserves the selection after release. Headless tests cover bounded long words, UTF-8 offsets, whitespace/punctuation, image boundaries, paragraph/row copy, text mutation and shared view ownership. Touch gesture selection and complete coverage of every block/run kind remain unfinished. The website's Markdown example starts with a visible fenced C code block, then shows emphasis, a link, lists, a quote and a table. Select **Scrollable** to constrain the document viewport, or switch **TextView format** to HTML or plain text. Fenced code is parsed and rendered in monospace with the theme's code background; it is separate from the website's copyable C usage excerpt. ## Stream motion policy The frozen `crates/base/src/text/stream_fade.rs` at commit `87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34` defines words with their trailing whitespace as reveal units, or individual Chinese/Japanese/Korean scalars. CUI now exposes this timing through `cui_text_view_motion`, `cui_text_view_set_motion`, and styled `options.custom_motion/options.motion`. The default remains 350 ms, no stagger, ease-out cubic. Linear and ease-in-out cubic are also supported; arbitrary user-defined easing functions are not. Configure state **before** applying an appended document update. Initial document loading normally precedes enabling streaming so existing text appears immediately: This complete headless C11 program needs Core and the TextView components, with no browser or native font adapter. Its assertions verify stagger timing and reduced motion; a real host adds event delivery and draw-list painting: ```c #include "cui/cui_text_view.h" /* Keep this executable verification example active in release builds too. */ #ifdef NDEBUG #undef NDEBUG #endif #include #include int main(void) { static char source[1024], rendered[1024]; static cui_text_view_mapping mapping[1024]; static cui_text_view_span spans[256]; static cui_text_view_block blocks[128]; static cui_text_view_glyph glyphs[1024]; cui_text_view_workspace workspace = { .source = source, .source_capacity = sizeof source, .rendered = rendered, .rendered_capacity = sizeof rendered, .mapping = mapping, .mapping_capacity = 1024, .spans = spans, .span_capacity = 256, .blocks = blocks, .block_capacity = 128, .glyphs = glyphs, .glyph_capacity = 1024 }; cui_text_view_state state; assert(cui_text_view_init(&state, workspace, CUI_TEXT_VIEW_MARKDOWN)); assert(cui_text_view_set_text(&state, cui_string("Before")) == CUI_TEXT_VIEW_OK); cui_context *ui = cui_create((cui_config){0}); assert(ui); cui_text_view_motion motion = { .duration = 1, .stagger = .2f, .easing = CUI_TEXT_VIEW_FADE_LINEAR }; assert(cui_text_view_set_motion(&state, motion)); state.stream_fade = true; /* A real host sets the context preference from its platform settings. */ state.reduced_motion = cui_reduced_motion(ui); assert(cui_text_view_set_text(&state, cui_string("Before one two")) == CUI_TEXT_VIEW_OK); assert(cui_text_view_stream_opacity(&state, 7) == 0); assert(cui_text_view_stream_opacity(&state, 11) == 0); cui_text_view_options options = cui_text_view_default(); options.width = 300; options.stream_fade = true; options.custom_motion = true; options.motion = motion; options.reduced_motion = state.reduced_motion; options.dt = .3f; cui_theme theme = cui_theme_light(); assert(cui_begin_frame(ui, 400, 240, .3f)); assert(cui_text_view(ui, 77, &theme, &state, options)); cui_draw_list draws = cui_end_frame(ui); assert(draws.count && cui_last_error(ui) == CUI_OK); /* The component paints first, then advances its clock for the next frame. */ assert(fabsf(cui_text_view_stream_opacity(&state, 7) - .3f) < .00001f); assert(fabsf(cui_text_view_stream_opacity(&state, 11) - .1f) < .00001f); cui_set_reduced_motion(ui, true); state.reduced_motion = cui_reduced_motion(ui); /* Before the next text update. */ options.reduced_motion = state.reduced_motion; /* Also forward every frame. */ assert(cui_text_view_set_text(&state, cui_string("Before one two three")) == CUI_TEXT_VIEW_OK); assert(cui_text_view_stream_opacity(&state, 7) == 1); assert(cui_text_view_stream_opacity(&state, 15) == 1); assert(!cui_text_view_advance(&state, 0)); assert(cui_begin_frame(ui, 400, 240, .3f)); assert(cui_text_view(ui, 77, &theme, &state, options)); cui_end_frame(ui); cui_destroy(ui); return 0; } ``` Save the complete program as `textview_motion.c`, build the library, then run: ```sh cc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -Iinclude textview_motion.c build/libcui.a -lm -o textview_motion ./textview_motion ``` Each changed contiguous run within a paragraph/code/table-cell leaf starts its own word timing. Unicode whitespace follows the preceding word; leading whitespace joins the first word. CJK ranges match the pinned source: Hiragana/Katakana, CJK Extension A/unified/compatibility ideographs, Hangul syllables, and ideograph extensions U+20000–U+2FA1F. Every byte of a UTF-8 scalar receives the same birth time. Staggering spans inline formatting within a leaf; it restarts at block and table-cell boundaries. If the last unit would start later than the fade duration, the entire changed run fades as one chunk. CUI uses its existing rendered-byte/format comparison, rather than introducing a full source leaf-identity tracker; more complex reparses can have different chunk boundaries from the frozen implementation. `cui_text_view_stream_opacity` samples the current alpha multiplier without painting. `cui_text_view_advance` continues to request frames until the last delayed unit reaches full opacity. A disabled fade, zero duration, replacement, or reduced motion paints immediately. Replacing text clears unfinished fades in unchanged prefixes too. Invalid negative/nonfinite durations or stagger and unknown easing values fail without changing the state. A zero duration clears pending fades; other policy changes update durations/easing of active fades but do not reschedule already recorded stagger birth times. Set a policy before `set_text` for deterministic new-chunk timing. TextView's state clock is advanced by `options.dt` at the end of component submission, after painting. Supply the elapsed interval once per frame; do not also call `cui_text_view_advance` for that same interval. The pure model API may instead advance explicitly when used without the styled component. `cui_begin_frame`'s dt alone does not advance this model clock. TextView does not implicitly copy `cui_reduced_motion(ui)` into its state/options. Forward the host preference to `state.reduced_motion` before a text update and to `options.reduced_motion` on each submission. This prevents new fade birth times while reduced motion is active and immediately suppresses existing fades. A zero-duration motion clears pending birth times; merely suppressing a fade does not clear them, so unfinished text may resume fading if the preference is turned off before its stored deadline. The styled custom policy is validated before image, link, or composition callbacks run. Headless tests exercise overlapping word timing, delayed animation completion, Latin/CJK/Unicode-whitespace scalar boundaries, oversized chunks, easing values, zero/invalid policies, replacement and reduced motion, Markdown completion, independent table-cell timings, transactional failed parses, and actual text command alpha. Complete parser/plugins, touch selection, shaping and other gaps listed above remain outside this change. ## Callback ownership and timing `on_link(url, event, link_user)` runs synchronously while the matching link is painted. It overrides `open_url`; it does not run in addition to the opener. The event is consumed after callback return. The fallback opener's boolean is currently ignored: returning false still consumes the invocation and does not produce a confirmed navigation result. Primary activation and secondary release are distinct supported paths; selection dragging suppresses link activation. No callback return cancels a transaction or proves an external URL was opened. Decoded URI bytes and the event pointer are borrowed only during the callback. Copy URI bytes into bounded application storage before returning, checking `url.length` against capacity before copying and adding a terminator if needed. Do not retain `url.data`; copying `cui_event` alone does not own optional text data. For example, with a caller-owned `char saved[256]`, accept only `url.length < sizeof saved`, then `memcpy(saved, url.data, url.length)` and `saved[url.length] = 0`. Handle oversize input explicitly; never silently truncate an actionable URI. Copies survive later frames/document replacement independently of the borrowed workspace. `cui_text_view_reveal` queues a programmatic range. In scrollable mode submission adjusts internal scroll and clears the pending request without calling `on_reveal`. In non-scrollable mode a located range calls `on_reveal(window_line, reveal_user)` after layout/reduction and before viewport paint, then clears `reveal_pending`. The callback sees pending=true. Its rectangle uses the retained viewport origin plus the located current line bounds; it is a host scrolling request, not evidence that a parent scrolled. Disabled views and inert/layout parent scopes do not cancel this programmatic service callback. Do not set a replacement reveal from inside that callback: the outer operation clears pending after return. Callbacks may copy payloads and set unrelated application flags. Keep the active view, workspace, shared-selection registrations and context alive; do not reparse, rebind, destroy or recursively submit them during a callback. Apply document replacement or omission only after the outer call and renderer consumption. The view's boolean reports submission success, not link dispatch or selection change. Selection is already applied to caller-owned offsets; no rejectable selection event is implied. Bridge factories do not currently wire these C link/reveal callback hooks. `test_callback_contracts` in `tests/unit/test_text_view.c` covers reveal timing and coordinates, internal-scroll silence, disabled/programmatic parent scopes, link-over-opener precedence, false opener consumption, bounded decoded URI copy surviving reparse, and deferred omission. This is headless source/command coverage; it does not prove native URL opening or completion of host scrolling.

# Themes

A `cui_theme` C struct carries surface/background, text/muted, primary/on-primary, border/focus/destructive colors and typography/spacing/radius/control height. `cui_theme_light`, `dark`, `high_contrast`, and `terminal` return runtime values. Pass the theme to every styled call; copying and adjusting a token is an explicit per-component override.

Prefer component option overrides for local changes: Button has `custom_colors`
and Avatar has explicit fallback colors. A theme copy remains useful when a whole
subtree shares an override. The public struct stays flat for compatibility;
grouping its fields would break existing designated initializers and bindings.
Button variant names describe presentation, while `CUI_THEME_BUTTON_*` names
describe shared palettes; see [the mapping](BUTTON.md). In particular, Ghost has
no dedicated theme palette enum.

The website follows your system light/dark preference by default. Its header palette button selects Follow System, a built-in theme, or one of the pinned named GPUI palette adaptations; an explicit choice persists across visits. The Theme preview shows six actual semantic color tokens alongside typography and controls. It is a design-system demonstration, rather than a separate input widget. Native applications choose a `cui_theme` and pass it into styled component calls; system appearance is supplied by the host. High contrast and the terminal theme demonstrate alternative presentation over the same base behavior.

Motion uses host frame time and component state; Switch, Shimmer, disclosure, loading indicators and indeterminate Progress expose reduced-motion handling. A comprehensive typography/shadow/motion token system, native theme-file loader and automatic global density provider remain pending. The gallery density selector adjusts its example theme.

Intent tokens `warning`, `success`, `info`, and `danger` can be used as filled
surfaces or as text/borders on the theme surface. `on_warning`, `on_success`,
`on_info`, and `on_danger` supply their filled-surface text colors. All four built-in
themes test at least 4.5:1 contrast for each pair and each intent color against its
surface. Applications extending a custom theme must set these new fields; the
fields append to the prior public structure rather than reordering existing ones.

Each theme has `buttons[CUI_THEME_BUTTON_*]` palettes with independent filled
normal/hover/active colors, foreground, outlined normal/hover/active colors,
outlined foreground and borders. Default, primary, secondary and the four intent
palettes can be overridden independently. Link normal/hover/active foregrounds,
input background/border, secondary foreground and accent colors are separate.
Built-in constructors derive these initial values from CUI's own palette; custom
themes must initialize the extended fields. These are solid-color tokens; gradient
backgrounds and shadows remain separate rendering capabilities.

`spring_control` provides response seconds, damping ratio, epsilon and travel
permission (defaults: 0.18 seconds, 1, 0.001, true) for component motion. A theme's
motion settings are configuration; components still own their retained motion
state and the host supplies time/redraw scheduling.

`popover` and `radius_lg` independently style notification surfaces. Built-in themes initialize popover to surface and the large radius to radius+2 (zero remains square); applications can override both without changing ordinary controls.

The independent `secondary` background and `secondary_foreground` tokens style semantic secondary content such as Tag. Button palettes remain separately overridable.

Tabs have independent `tab_foreground`, `tab_active_foreground`, `tab_active`, `tab_bar`, `tab_bar_segmented`, and `secondary_hover` colors. These do not follow later edits to Button palettes automatically. `spring_move` configures positional motion separately from `spring_control`, defaulting to response0.28seconds, damping0.85, epsilon0.1 and enabled travel.

## Override a token

```c
cui_theme theme = cui_theme_light();
theme.radius = 8;
theme.font_size = 16;
theme.gap = 12;
cui_button(ui, id, &theme, cui_string("Save changes"), false);
```

Retain the chosen theme in application state. Change it in response to your host's appearance notification or theme menu callback and invalidate the context. Component values and models remain intact when the theme changes. `cui_theme_preset_get` loads a named palette by index without exposing platform types; see the Theme Presets guide for the pinned collection.

# Portable theme registry and host seam

This optional module adds bounded named themes and source semantic configuration.
Existing `cui_theme` color/button fields, constructors, all 38 preset names and
preset colors remain unchanged. It does not automatically change component
motion, Core preferences, native fonts, or host theme selection.

The reference is GPUI Kit 0.7.1 commit
`87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`, specifically
`crates/component/src/theme/{schema,registry,motion,mod,color}.rs` and Base
`theme_tokens.rs`. GPUI's serialized shadow layout comes from pinned
`gpui-pre=0.3.8`, `src/style.rs` and `src/color.rs`.

## Semantic configuration

`cui_theme_semantic_import` accepts the actual standalone source wrapper:

```json
{"tokens":{"colors":{"primary":"blue-600/80","foreground":"#1234"},
 "radius":{"md":6,"full":9999},"spacing":{"xxl":32},
 "typography":{"sans":"My embedded font","md":{"size":18,"line_height":26,"weight":500}},
 "shadow":{"sm":[{"color":{"h":0,"s":0,"l":0,"a":0.18},
 "offset":{"x":0,"y":1},"blur_radius":2,"spread_radius":0,"inset":false}]}}}
```

This is separate from the legacy ThemeSet schema. Groups are `colors`, `radius`,
`spacing`, `typography`, and `shadow`; motion is **not** in this JSON schema.
All source semantic groups are represented. There are 17 configurable color
roles; snapshot `selection` is an eighteenth role that source configuration does
not override. Radius has none/sm/md/lg/xl/full; spacing has xxs/xs/sm/md/lg/xl/xxl.
Typography includes sans/mono and xs/sm/md/lg/xl/mono_md, each with size,
line_height and numeric weight. Shadow arrays are sm/md/lg with the exact
serialized BoxShadow fields above; colors inside shadows use normalized HSLA,
not string color names. Optional field `null` preserves an inherited value;
non-optional groups/text-style objects require objects.

String colors support source hex #rgb/#rgba/#rrggbb/#rrggbbaa and 22 named palette
families at scales 50,100,...,900,950; a missing scale uses 500. Black/white and
`/opacity` percentages are supported. Hex is RGBA, not ARGB. Arbitrary CSS
rgb()/hsl() strings and semantic gradients are not accepted by the pinned source
parser. CUI rejects invalid scale/opacity/color values; the source sometimes
falls back or silently ignores invalid overrides. CUI also rejects unknown keys,
duplicate keys (including escaped duplicates), invalid Unicode/NUL, nonfinite
numbers and unsupported fields instead of silently losing data. Decimal parsing
is independent of the host numeric locale.

Snapshots own font strings and shadows. Defaults project generic colors/radii
from the supplied CUI theme, use the source spacing/text scales and source
sm/md/lg elevation metadata. Font defaults are logical `.SystemUIFont` and
`monospace`: this module performs no platform font discovery. Source shadow
metadata has no corresponding legacy CUI shadow-enabled field. Imported
families, weights, line heights, scale-only spacing/radius and elevation remain
available in the returned snapshot for application-owned UI.

Applying tokens updates only generic legacy fields and font_size/radius/radius_lg.
Surface maps to popover; muted background and foreground remain distinct.
Specialized button, sidebar, tab, chart and other component skins stay unchanged,
as in the source's generic projection policy. Selection is not rewritten by
this projection. Hosts must explicitly map the returned typography to their
font factory/style state; storing a family does not make it render automatically.

## Registry ownership and transactions

Allocate a `cui_theme_registry_entry` array, then initialize a registry with it.
No registry API allocates or reads files/network. Capacity is 1..256; seeded
initialization/reset requires room for exactly 38 frozen presets, including
Default Light and Default Dark. Unseeded reset produces an empty registry.
Every entry owns its UTF-8 name, semantic font strings and shadow data. Existing
`cui_theme` icon loader callbacks/userdata remain borrowed; their host lifetime
must cover any use of copied themes. The caller array must outlive the registry
and must not be mutated directly while registered. Reset invalidates all prior
borrowed query pointers; unused array slots are not a second registry.

`put` matches names case-sensitively. Existing names are skipped unless replacement
is explicit; skip does not change revision. Sorted queries put defaults first,
light before dark, then names using ASCII folding with deterministic UTF-8 byte
ordering/ties. This differs from source Unicode lowercasing. No Unicode-insensitive
sorting parity is claimed.

Legacy `cui_theme_registry_import` accepts source ThemeSet shape:
`{name,author,url,themes:[{name,mode,is_default,font.size,font.family,
mono_font.size,mono_font.family,radius,radius.lg,shadow,colors:{dotted keys},highlight}]}`.
The concrete representable color map is `src/theme/cui_theme_legacy_fields.inc`.
It includes 85 source keys; it does not implement every source role, highlight
syntax themes, gradient backgrounds or all derived fallback policies. The
existing preset adaptations remain the authoritative frozen built-ins.
Unsupported legacy fields reject the whole import by default. Explicit
`allow_unsupported` permits the mapped subset and returns `partial=true` plus
`unsupported_fields`; this is never a claim of full legacy import parity.
`is_default` affects ordering, while host selection names remain explicit.

Provide a disjoint caller scratch entry array large enough for the complete
resulting registry, not merely the new entries. Scratch, live entry storage and JSON source bytes must be mutually disjoint.
The optional report must not alias these regions or registry metadata. Scratch contents are temporary and may change on
failure; live registry entries/count/revision do not. All new entries are validated
before a single commit. Source skip-existing is the default batch policy; explicit
replacement is available. Conflicting names within a batch follow the same policy.
Imported source strings may be released immediately after the call. Mutation
increments revision once per successful batch; skipped-only batches leave it
unchanged. Revision overflow rejects. These are UI-thread APIs, not a concurrent
registry: transaction atomicity does not imply cross-thread synchronization.

Limits are explicit: 64 KiB JSON, 4096 parser nodes, depth 16, 127 UTF-8 bytes per
owned name/font, eight shadows per elevation. Parsing uses one shared 64 KiB decode workspace and bounded node storage,
with small recursive frames. An unoptimized GCC 64-bit build measures about
232 KiB for the importer plus at most 17 parser frames; the full registry test
passes with a 512 KiB stack. ABI/compiler overhead varies; avoid invoking imports
from a tiny host thread stack. Windows default-stack Debug testing is required.
Use caller heap/long-lived storage for large entry arrays and scratch. Geometry
values are bounded to 1e6, text size/line height to 4096 and weight to 1..1000.
These stricter CUI bounds reject atomically instead of truncating. The new module
has no destruction function because its registry/snapshots own no allocations.

## Motion and appearance

`cui_theme_motion_default` represents every pinned MotionTokens field: durations
instant/fast/normal/slow = 0/.12/.18/.28 seconds; enter/exit/move cubic Bézier curves
(.16,1,.3,1),(.4,0,1,1),(.2,0,0,1); control/move springs .18/1/.001 and
.28/.85/.1 with travel enabled; short/medium distances .25/.5 rem.
`cui_theme_bezier_sample` solves x before sampling y. Custom finite Bézier y may
overshoot; x stays in [0,1]. This exposes the semantic policy's Bézier curves,
not every Base Easing enum (steps, piecewise/custom closures).

`cui_theme_motion_project` copies the full policy and converts distances using an
explicit rem pixel size. Reduced projection sets durations, distances, spring
response and travel to zero; it keeps easing/damping/tolerances. Durations/response
are bounded to 60 seconds, damping/epsilon and Bézier y to 1000, rem size to 4096,
rem distances to 4096 and projected distances to 1e6 pixels. Invalid input leaves
output unchanged. Existing component-specific curves (for example Plot's quartic
appear curve) are distinct; no implicit adoption changes those defaults.

`cui_theme_host_update` accepts caller preferences and selection names. It selects
registered light/dark themes in follow-system or forced mode, explicitly projects
motion, and maps reduced motion/auto-hide into the copied scrollbar style.
High contrast chooses CUI's existing high-contrast palette as a local policy
extension; this is not a claim of source/platform high-contrast detection.
Host revision must not rewind. The output owns its snapshots and reports visual
`changed`, typography `metrics_changed` and separate `motion_changed` flags;
repeated identical preferences do not replay changes. The host performs rendering
invalidation, font/style rebinding and Core preference calls as needed.

No OS observer, portal query, filesystem watcher, async callback or global
appearance mutation is installed. A host can read/watch its own appearance and
file events, call a transactional import, and then resolve again using registry
revision. Registry queries borrow until the next mutation; resolved host snapshots
remain owned and valid after registry reset/destruction of caller storage.

## Tests and integration

The dedicated portable unit test covers schema/Unicode/colors, ownership, strict
capacity failures, structured malformed input, rollback, source skip/replace and
case sensitivity, sorting/reset, all 38 preset/button compatibility, full motion
projection, host revisions and no replay. An optional primary-source fixture test reads the pinned Ayu/Aurora JSON,
verifies strict rejection and observable partial imports, then overwrites source
and scratch to check owned entries. Missing reference fixtures return 77.
The native test paints imported and
high-contrast themes with an actual Noto Sans font/software renderer; missing
font fixtures return 77 rather than passing an empty glyph raster.

`tests/web/test_theme_registry.py` builds a standalone pinned Zig 0.16.0 WASM
probe and runs Playwright 1.58.0/Chromium 1208. Real matchMedia preference events
feed the host seam and change actual canvas pixels/typography/motion snapshots.
This validates the explicit host contract, not an SDK-installed browser observer.
`--chromium` can select revision 1228.

Integrator registration: add `src/theme/cui_theme_registry.c` and
`cui_theme_motion.c`, package `cui_theme_registry.h`, embed the private JSON,
equality, palette and legacy map files in amalgamation, register
`tests/unit/test_theme_registry.c` (cui) and
`tests/integration/test_theme_registry_native.c` (cui+cui_text+cui_software,
skip 77). Default builds stay Rust-free. Root owns CMake/distribution/notice
updates. Stale distribution verification is expected before that regeneration.

Programmatic `put` treats `.theme` as authoritative for the seventeen shared generic
color roles, md/lg radius, and md font size. Conflicting `.semantic` values in
those fields are normalized. Selection, other scales/text styles, font families,
spacing, shadows, and motion remain intact. Use semantic JSON/the projector or
update both snapshots when editing shared semantic values.

# TimeField applied change observers

Include `cui/cui_picker_events.h`. Use `cui_base_time_field_events` for semantics
without Styled paint, or `cui_time_field_events` for the complete Styled control.
Both preserve the old operation and return `cui_picker_event_result`:
`changed` is its exact legacy bool; `change_count` counts actual callbacks (0 or 1).
The existing entrypoints and options/state layouts are unchanged.

```c
static void time_changed(void *user, const cui_time_change *change) {
    bool *save_needed = user; /* Unrelated host state, not the active time owner. */
    *save_needed = true;
    /* Copy *change to retain previous/value and metadata beyond this callback. */
}
/* During UI submission, using existing caller-owned time/state/theme: */
/* cui_picker_event_result result = cui_time_field_events(
       ui, id, theme, cui_string("Appointment"), &state, &time,
       (cui_time_options){.seconds = true},
       (cui_time_handler){.on_change = time_changed, .user = &save_needed}); */
```

The callback reports `cui_time previous, value`, with hour 0–23 and minute/second
0–59. Twelve-hour display still reports the original 24-hour model; hidden seconds
are retained and participate in validity. An invalid time, even an invalid hidden
second, preserves legacy rejection without repair or notification. Required
pointers and a nonzero compound ID are checked before legacy work. Styled also
requires a theme. Invalid admission returns a zero result.

Each facade calls its complete old operation once, then compares all three time
fields. Base notifies after final semantics/invalidation. Styled notifies after
its existing paint. Missing callback still permits editing and ignores user.
Multiple inputs or digit writes yielding one final difference produce one callback;
net-zero changes produce none. Focus, digit draft, invalid-digit rejection and
segment repair alone are silent. Assigning a new owner value before the call sets
its baseline; it is not a programmatic notification.

Metadata kind is CHANGE, target is the TimeField compound ID. A proven active frame
is present; source is UNKNOWN, without input index or activation. An aggregate
can combine multiple routed segment inputs, so it does not promise a unique
pointer/key cause. Flags alone establish evidence. There is no request/rejection,
COMMIT, SUBMIT, draft lifecycle, IME composition, undo or new text-input support.

Disabled/readonly controls preserve old segment/draft repair, focus policy and
semantics, with no observation. Actual inert/layout-only scopes likewise suppress
new observations while retaining the legacy work; the facade does not override
Core routing. The old per-frame bool is preserved independently of notification.

Payload is pointer-free and copyable. Callback/user/payload pointer are borrowed
synchronously. Do not mutate/rebind/free active time/state/context, input, theme,
labels or other active resources, or recursively submit UI from the observer.
Unrelated flags and copying are allowed. Defer omission/destruction until outer
return and renderer consumption; keep caller resources live through that boundary.
These are notifications of already applied edits, not owner-rejectable requests.

`tests/unit/test_time_field_events.c` compares legacy/facade Base and Styled state,
results, focus/redraw, semantics/tab policy and paint. It covers routed pointer
selection plus editing, rollover, digit multiplicity/net-zero edits, 12-hour model,
hidden seconds, invalid input, missing observer, actual passive/inert scopes,
readonly/disabled maintenance, copied payload and deferred omission. Existing
`picker`, `picker_base_only` and `picker_events` remain regression gates. Tests run
through the private local wrapper; no browser/native-display parity is implied.

C bridge and Python/Node/TypeScript/Go/Rust retain their existing time values and
generic CHANGE events. This C facade adds no foreign typed previous/value payload
or synchronous callback timing contract. Full TimeField/binding parity is not
claimed.

# Toolbar and ToolbarGroup

Toolbar is a transparent horizontal command container. It exposes Toolbar
semantics, preserves ordinary Tab traversal through its controls, and handles
unconsumed Left/Right keys after its children render. Focus wraps among enabled
Tab stops in the scope, including nested groups. Nested toolbars handle their
own keys first. Hosted inputs retain caret navigation when their input behavior
consumes those events. The toolbar itself is passive. `disabled` suppresses only
its navigation; applications disable hosted controls individually.

This implementation follows the frozen GPUI Kit 0.7.1 `base/src/toolbar.rs` and
`component/src/toolbar.rs`. The website mentions vertical navigation, but the
actual source fixes orientation to horizontal and handles Left/Right only; CUI
follows that implementation.

`cui_toolbar_default()` selects Small. XSmall uses height 28, padding4, gap4,
font12, and sized wrapper 20. Small uses 32/4/4/14/24. Medium uses 48/8/8/14/32.
Large resolves to Medium. Custom preserves its numeric size for control
callbacks while using Medium bar geometry and a 24px sized wrapper, matching the
source's wildcard cases. Invalid enum/nonfinite/negative custom values fail
before submitting the container. Arrays are bounded at 1024 items and borrowed
for the call; no persistent allocations are required.

Each item has a render callback. Sized items receive `prepared=true`, final
metrics, and a centered fixed-height wrapper with a distinct nonzero ID. Their
callback implements the control-specific `prepare_for_toolbar` hook before
applying the final size; arbitrary C callbacks cannot be mutated automatically.
Unsized content gets `prepared=false` and no wrapper. Items render in source
order. A nested group callback forwards the presentation metrics into group
options to inherit the enclosing size. Group carries passive Group semantics
and an optional accessible label, lays out children horizontally and centered,
and adds no padding or gap. Its owner supplies spacing and disables controls.

`cui_toolbar_command_render` is the supplied sized-command callback: it renders
an actual compact ghost button, uses controlled selected/disabled state,
separate visible and accessible names, an optional icon callback, and validated
pointer/keyboard activation. A label-less command requires an accessible name.
Host tooltip display remains an application integration; the renderer does not
invent a tooltip from invisible text. Icon rendering and callbacks are borrowed
for the render call. Custom label commands retain natural content height and
20%-of-size horizontal padding; custom icon commands are square, as in source.

`custom_box=true` supplies a complete container layout/style replacement, rather
than guessing which zero fields in a C aggregate mean a style refinement. It can
add a background/border or override dimensions, but its owner must preserve the
source's intended horizontal layout when desired. Default containers have no
background/border and never shrink their fixed height. The surrounding header or
pane owns the surface.

The base begin/end API accepts application-owned layout and supports arbitrary
children without the styled layer. Pair end only after a successful begin. A
base toolbar opens a nonmodal focus scope; a base group adds semantics without
owning navigation. All pointer, focus, modal, clipping and inert rules come from
core. Arrays/callbacks/state belong to the application; no platform or Clay types
appear in the public API.

# Toolbar command activation

Include `cui/cui_toolbar_events.h` and call `cui_toolbar_command_events` in a
custom Toolbar item renderer. Existing container and command entrypoints remain
unchanged. For example, an application-owned adapter can hold its command,
handler and last result:

```c
typedef struct {
    cui_toolbar_command command;
    cui_component_activation_handler handler;
    cui_toolbar_command_event_result result;
} command_item;
static void render_command(cui_context *ui, const cui_theme *theme,
                           const cui_toolbar_presentation *p, void *user) {
    command_item *item = user;
    item->result = cui_toolbar_command_events(ui, theme, p, &item->command,
                                               item->handler);
}
```

Use `render_command` as a `cui_toolbar_item.render`, with the adapter as its user.
The handler uses the shared user-first signature
`void callback(void *user, const cui_component_event_metadata *event)`.

`valid` means legacy command/presentation/name validation passed. `submitted`
means the command ran during ordinary active submission with a nonzero frame
sequence; it does not promise allocation success or paint delivery. Measurement,
inert/layout-only and out-of-frame work does not emit an observer callback.
`activation_count` counts actual observer calls, zero or one. A missing callback
ignores its user and leaves interaction/legacy callbacks intact.

The command still interacts once, submits its icon/label/box, calls legacy
`on_activate(activate_user)`, then calls the new observer. Repeated accepted inputs
coalesce exactly as before; this API does not provide per-input callbacks. Choose
one callback/result path for each application side effect to avoid doing it twice.
Selected state is caller-owned presentation, not a Toggle CHANGE. Disabled
commands do not activate; a disabled Toolbar container suppresses navigation only
and may still host enabled commands.

ACTIVATE metadata targets the command ID. Evidence freezes immediately after
interaction, before icon or legacy callbacks can consume events/change focus.
Exactly one accepted activation carries its genuine snapshot/index/source. If
multiple activations coalesce, or genuine evidence is absent, only the proven
frame is supplied: source UNKNOWN, no invented index or activation snapshot.
No REQUEST, rejection, commit, container event, dispatch or binding API is added.

Handler/user borrow through the synchronous call. Metadata is pointer-free and
copyable beyond frame/context lifetime. Command/presentation/theme/strings/icon
resources and context must remain live through outer return and renderer
consumption. New observers may copy payloads and set unrelated flags; they must
not mutate/free/rebind active resources, recurse, destroy context or unwind across
C. Legacy hooks retain their timing and mutations but must leave resources needed
by remaining rendering/observation live. Record deferred omission/teardown and
perform it after submission and renderer consumption. Omitting a command emits
nothing; there is no retained registration or replay.

# Gallery touch coverage

Audit baseline: release `65da7b2`. The final run passed 41 of 42 assertions across 36 families; Carousel failed its swipe assertion. All 78 stories rendered without page errors. This inventory covers all 78 manifest families. Rendering a story is an inventory check, not touch verification. “Verified” means only the named representative assertions passed using actual Chromium CDP `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` contacts. It does not mean every variant, platform or interaction in that family passed.

The next16 integration fixes Carousel contact lifetime/cancellation ordering and text-area caret reveal overriding a pan. Its local Chromium rerun passes all 42 representative assertions; the historical baseline failure above remains recorded. Additional control and clipboard coverage is recorded in [the follow-up audit](TOUCH_FOLLOWUP.md). These checks do not establish physical-device or complete per-family acceptance.

Run from the repository root after building the WASI gallery:

```sh
python scripts/build_web.py --zig /path/to/pinned/zig
uv run tests/web/test_touch_components.py --chromium /path/to/chromium
```

The default command fails on a failed interaction. `--allow-defects` continues and returns success for evidence collection; inspect the JSON report and printed failures before assessing readiness. `--report PATH` saves semantic inventory and assertion results. `--inventory-only` only renders the 78 stories. Dependencies are pinned in the test script.

Configuration inputs create fixtures but do not perform the asserted component gestures. Textarea uses one row to produce overflow. Editor receives keyboard Enter events to create overflow before its touch pan assertion; this does not verify touch typing or IME. Component taps, drags, pans and pinch use CDP contacts, never mouse emulation or direct Core event injection. Disabled Button, List option and Resizable assertions verify unchanged state. Button backtracking drag and nested Dialog checkbox drag verify ghost-tap suppression. Dock moves a real tab between workspace regions. VirtualList asserts a changed bounded row window; DataTable tests both pixel scrolling and visible grid-cell selection.

## Matrix

Applicability describes the default gallery fixture. “Conditional” means a display or container family can have interactive options or children; those paths still need coverage. “Not applicable” means no intrinsic touch action is exposed in this fixture, not that the family was verified to pan its ancestors. | TextView | Applicable | Unverified | Text selection, links and enabled scrolling unverified. |

## Confirmed defect

**Carousel slow swipe fails to advance.** On the default horizontal `Workflow carousel`, the viewport is 716 logical pixels wide. Start in its content center, send four touch moves totaling 65% of its width to the left, with 50ms between moves, then release. `gallery_carousel_stats(0)` remains at page 0 instead of advancing. This happens with actual PointerEvents generated from CDP contacts. The test preserves this failed assertion rather than changing the source under audit.

The root is a horizontal scroll owner. Core translates touch pan into precise scroll events. Carousel currently treats a gap of 28ms as a wheel-burst end and snaps a partial move before the next touch move. This is a source-based explanation to investigate, not a verified fix. Relevant owners should preserve the continuous contact lifecycle or grant explicit drag ownership; normal slow finger movement must not require sub-28ms events.

## Remaining coverage

Nested **modal** ownership is verified: dragging in the child modal neither scrolls the obscured parent nor toggles its checkbox; a later tap toggles the child checkbox. Nested **scroll boundary chaining** is unverified in this gallery audit: no default fixture has two simultaneously overflowing scroll owners. Core headless nested-chain tests are separate evidence and do not establish gallery/component coverage. Add an actual nested overflow fixture before marking this behavior verified here.

These assertions run in headless Chromium with emulated touchscreen contacts. Physical Android/iOS hardware, Safari, Firefox, native SDL, multiwindow routing, pen contacts, custom cursors, every disabled variant, cancellation during unmount and all 78 family variants remain unverified by this suite. Public shared cursor/state hooks and prior Core/SDL tests are documented in [INTERACTION.md](INTERACTION.md); they are not a substitute for this component inventory. Input focus assertions do not establish soft-keyboard, composition, text-selection or IME behavior. A display family marked not applicable still depends on its containing scroll/viewport owner for gestures.

Validation for this audit branch: warning-enabled CMake/Ninja build passed; local CTest passed 88/88. No source behavior or existing test files were changed.

# Touch follow-up audit

Baseline: `fda9f70` on `integration/next16`, following the original 78-family
[coverage inventory](TOUCH_COMPONENT_COVERAGE.md). This follow-up adds actual
Chromium CDP touch contacts for ten interactive families. It changes no component,
gallery, Core or adapter source. It does not establish complete family parity.

Build the gallery with the pinned Zig toolchain, then run:

```sh
uv run tests/web/test_touch_more.py --chromium /path/to/chromium
```

The test imports the existing `Audit` helper from `test_touch_components.py`.
Both scripts must remain adjacent. Its Playwright dependency is pinned. The
default command returns failure when an assertion fails. `--allow-defects` is an
evidence-collection mode that returns success despite failed assertions; inspect
the printed results and JSON report. `--report PATH` overrides the default
`/tmp/cui-touch-followup-report.json`. `--inventory-only` records semantics without
running gestures and must not be interpreted as interaction verification.

All asserted component actions use `Input.dispatchTouchEvent`, producing browser
PointerEvents with actual contact identities. No component action substitutes a
mouse click, accessibility DOM click or direct `gallery_event` call. DOM options
only configure fixtures. Combobox receives ordinary keyboard text to prepare its
query; focusing, suggestion selection and outside dismissal use touch. Clipboard
permissions are granted to the browser context, and the test reads the real
`navigator.clipboard` contents after a touch copy action. It never stubs the host
clipboard provider.

## Results

The follow-up passed 15 of 16 cases. One controlled ToggleGroup semantic assertion
failed. These results cover representative gallery behaviors only.

| Family | Status | Assertions and limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DropdownButton | Verified | Touch primary action increments invocation count; split menu selects a real item and closes; outside touch dismisses; disabled primary and menu triggers do neither. Submenus remain unverified. |
| Combobox | Verified | Touch focuses the query, selects the matching Banana option, closes the popup, and exposes Banana as selected when the query reopens it. Outside dismissal and disabled touch are asserted. Query setup uses keyboard text. Multi-selection/chip removal and touch text entry remain unverified. |
| Command | Verified | Enabled row confirms and invokes its callback; disabled row does not confirm. A backtracking row drag causes no ghost confirmation. Touch opens the modal palette, confirms a row, and dismisses outside. Filtering and touch text entry remain unverified. |
| Calendar | Verified | Touch selects a date; disabled touch on another date preserves the first selection. Month/year navigation, ranges and disabled-date constraints remain unverified. |
| DatePicker | Verified | Touch opens the calendar, selects a date and closes with updated trigger text; outside touch dismisses; disabled trigger stays closed. Range mode remains unverified. |
| ColorPicker | Verified | Touch Red-channel drag changes RGBA; disabled drag preserves RGBA. Palette touch selects exact `0x5865F2FF`; a two-dimensional saturation/value drag changes color. Screen EyeDropper and other color models remain unverified. |
| Clipboard | Verified | Trusted touch copy writes `Hello from CUI` into the actual clipboard; touch read displays that content. Disabled copy preserves a distinct sentinel. Platform permission-denial paths remain unverified. |
| Toggle / ToggleGroup | Partial; defect | Standalone toggles twice and ignores disabled tap. Multiple selection retains Bold and Italic; disabled group preserves selection. Single selection updates the model correctly but leaves incorrect checked semantics, as detailed below. |
| Tree | Verified | Touch expands docs and exposes children, selects core.c, ignores a disabled base.c selection, and collapses src to remove its children. Overflow scrolling and custom row slots remain unverified. |
| Focus Trap | Verified | Touch opens the scope, focuses its first child, closes it, and restores opener focus. Keyboard containment is outside this touch assertion; nested traps remain unverified. |

Combobox query text and selected option are independent in the current API. The
test checks the selected option rather than requiring the query to be replaced
with its label. Likewise, the Command gallery's confirmation callback deliberately
keeps its surface open; the test checks confirmation and a separate outside
dismissal rather than inventing automatic close behavior.

## Confirmed defect

With the Toggle gallery in single-selection mode, Bold initially selected, touch
Italic and then idle for 150ms after the normal post-release wait. The controlled
model reports `[Bold=0, Italic=1, Underline=0]`, while checked semantics report
`[1, 1, 0]`. The selected values are therefore correct but their exposed state is
wrong. The failing case is retained in the default test command.

The gallery callback replaces sibling values while the group is being rendered.
An earlier sibling may already have been painted or registered before that
callback changes it. This is a source-review hypothesis for the component/gallery
owner; this audit does not claim a fix or claim that all controlled groups behave
this way. A fix must make rendered and semantic states agree after the callback
without requiring a later unrelated input event.

## Integrated correction

The integrator fixes controlled sibling semantics and requests repaint without replaying callbacks (`2ad721c`). The integrated Chromium follow-up passes all 16 assertions at source `57f8066`; the original baseline defect above remains historical evidence.

## IME scope and remaining work

The separate [IME documentation](IME.md) and `test_ime.py` explicitly cover four
consumers: Input, Textarea, Editor and Questionnaire input controls. This follow-up
does not run composition assertions. Ordinary keyboard preparation of a Combobox
query is not IME verification. NumberInput, OtpInput and Combobox composition,
preedit rendering, commit/cancel and undo remain unverified here; this audit makes
no claim that every textbox has those capabilities.

All gestures in this follow-up run in headless Chromium. Physical touchscreen
hardware, Safari/Firefox, native SDL, all variants, focus transfer during active
composition, permission-denied clipboard access and every remaining interactive
family are still outside its verified scope. Nested overflowing scroll boundary
chaining remains the gallery coverage gap described in the original inventory.

Validation: warning-enabled CMake/Ninja build (`-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror`)
passed; local CTest passed 90/90. The new CDP suite reports its known failing
ToggleGroup assertion independently of those existing native tests.
