# Mobile page touch navigation

The browser host now lets a single vertical contact navigate the document when
Core and its component reducers leave the movement unconsumed. This follows the
`3c8879ef` read-only audit (based on `3c992ec`), which passed only 3 of 10 navigation assertions. The implementation
branch starts at `d56820e`; its strict mobile suite passes 19/19 assertions.

This is headless Chromium with a 390 × 844 mobile viewport and actual
`Input.dispatchTouchEvent` contacts. It does not establish physical Android/iOS,
Safari or Firefox coverage. All 78 manifest families remain present.

After building the gallery with the pinned Zig toolchain, run:

```sh
uv run tests/web/test_touch_page_navigation.py --chromium /path/to/chromium
```

The script imports the adjacent `test_touch_components.py` helper and pins
Playwright. The default command fails on any assertion failure. `--allow-defects`
is evidence-collection mode and must not be treated as a passing result. The JSON
report defaults to `/tmp/cui-touch-page-navigation-report.json`; override it with
`--report PATH`.

## Ownership and lifecycle

Canvas retains `touch-action:none` so the browser cannot steal intrinsic control
drags, internal scrolling or opted-in viewport gestures. The private bounded
[host policy helper](../web/touch_page_host.h) examines actual Core dispatch after
component reducers. It uses Core targets, consumption, clipped hover/scope queries,
and completed semantic parents; JavaScript does not repeat hit testing.

The host gives Core first refusal. Consumed moves stay entirely with Core. A
single contact can claim page navigation only after eight pixels of dominant
vertical movement and an unconsumed move. Modal scopes deny fallback, including
hits on disabled modal content. Slider, Scrollbar, Separator, explicit drag
priority and opted-in gesture owners reserve their streams. Protected ownership
is retained from the initial down event. Completed semantic parents protect
custom drag ancestors as well as the direct target.

An unconsumed scroll can retain a nonzero Core target at a boundary: persistent
ownership and failed ancestor deferral do not necessarily clear it. The helper
therefore uses the reducers' final consumption rather than requiring target zero.
If a movement is partially consumed at a boundary, its entire delta stays with
Core; page handoff waits for a later unconsumed move. No residual delta is guessed.

On page claim the browser queues exactly one Core touch cancellation, clearing
pressed/captured component state. It retains browser pointer capture until the
contact ends and applies later page movement from client coordinates. It does
not feed the ended Core contact further moves or releases. A second contact
blocks page movement until the stream ends; a new finger arriving after page
claim is also kept out of Core to avoid becoming a fresh primary tap. A later
single-contact gesture starts normally. Cancellation, window blur and navigation
clear browser host contacts. Both C and JavaScript retain at most 16 contacts.

The helper retires raw pointer releases and Core-converted `SCROLL/ENDED` and
`GESTURE/ENDED` releases. Missing those converted endings would falsely mark
later gestures as multiple contacts. Synthetic capture-handoff cancellation is
kept separate from physical contact termination.

## Wrapper padding

The audit separately reproduced a trap in canvas wrapper padding. Changing only
`.canvas-wrap` from `overflow:auto` to `overflow:clip` restored native vertical
page scrolling there. Canvas remains responsive at 100% width; horizontal
Scrollable/VirtualList behavior remains inside Core. Code blocks retain their
separate `overflow:auto` behavior. The full browser suite, including 390px layout,
passed with this narrow change. Preview-card styling is unchanged.

## Verified assertions

| Beginning or owner of gesture | Verified result |
| --- | --- |
| Body margin and canvas wrapper padding | Native vertical document pan works. |
| Passive Avatar, Image and Label canvas | Vertical document pan works. Label is the typography-content representative; no manifest family was added. |
| Button drag without internal owner | Navigates page without activating the button. |
| Button backtracking drag, then actual tap | Drag produces no ghost activation; the next tap activates exactly once. |
| Scrollable with remaining range | Consumes exactly 110 logical pixels while the page stays fixed. |
| Scrollable bottom and top boundaries | Internal offset stays at 458 or zero; unconsumed vertical pan navigates the page. |
| Slider and Resizable | Relevant control values change while page position stays fixed. |
| ColorPicker saturation/value plane | Two-dimensional drag changes RGBA without moving the page. |
| Plot | Opted-in pan and actual two-contact pinch remain with the viewport; pinch changes its domain. |
| Dialog with disabled opener | Touch on modal content cannot navigate the document; close still works. |
| Multiple contacts | Do not navigate the page; a later single contact can navigate. |
| Second finger after page claim | Cannot ghost-activate a button; a later ordinary tap works. |
| Physical cancellation after page claim | Stops movement; Core cancellation count increases exactly once and later taps work. |

The new [headless C test](../tests/unit/test_touch_page_host.c) uses real Core
scenes to exercise passive eligibility, direct/ancestor drag protection, viewport
protection, modal denial including disabled content, consumed-move refusal,
boundary routing, converted terminal-event retirement, multitouch recovery,
cancellation and bounded contact capacity. The integrator registers it in the
native and WASI suites.

## Validation and limits

Warning-enabled native CMake/Ninja build passed. The new C test separately
compiled with `-std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror` and passed. Existing full
CTest ran 90/91: only the generated-distribution check failed because root-owned
distributions await regeneration; the earlier RTL render regression is absent
at this implementation baseline.

Real CDP suites passed: page navigation 19/19, original touch smoke, component
coverage 42/42, follow-up coverage 16/16, and full browser coverage of all 78
stories, mobile 390px layout and `/cui/` hosting. These are representative tested
behaviors, not complete family or device parity.

Canvas page fallback follows finger movement and does not synthesize fling
inertia. Physical mobile browsers, soft-keyboard/IME navigation, browser zoom,
all custom gesture combinations and every component variant remain unverified.
The partial-boundary-consumption limitation above is deliberate.

Unexpected browser pointer capture loss clears the host contact and cancels Core
once. A real CDP contact with `releasePointerCapture` verifies ghost suppression
and a usable subsequent tap. Normal release after pointer-up finds no contact.

# Tree

`cui_tree.h` adds a retained bounded hierarchy, independent headless behavior and an ordinary styled Tree. Nodes are a preorder array of nonzero stable keys, borrowed labels, depths and disabled flags. The first depth is zero, depth increases by at most one and the maximum is 63. Application-owned expansion flags and selected key remain controlled. Nodes/labels must remain immutable and alive until a successful rebuild; changing expansion flags externally requires rebuilding the visible projection.

Create a model with capacity up to 100,000 nodes. Two preallocated banks hold hierarchy, visible projection and key lookup. Rebuild validates depth/keys and swaps banks only on success, preserving the preceding model on capacity, duplicate-key or invalid-input errors. There are no allocations after create. Node lookup uses a bounded open-addressed key table; parent and branch lookups are constant time. Rebuild and expansion changes flatten the hierarchy in linear time. The memory-byte accessor reports model-owned allocations. The array representation also lets an application replace asynchronously loaded data without a platform-specific filesystem dependency.

Rows select and report activated keys through ordinary pointer or Enter/Space activation. Separate expand buttons toggle branches. Up/Down moves between enabled visible rows, Home/End selects endpoints, Left collapses or moves to an enabled parent, and Right expands or visits an enabled direct child. Consecutive events reduce in input order. Selection follows navigation unless manual selection is requested. Disabled rows cannot activate/navigate; enabled descendants of an externally expanded disabled parent remain independent. Collapse preserves a hidden selected key until the application or a later selection changes it. ASCII typeahead supports accumulating prefixes, a 750 ms timeout, wrapping and repeated-letter cycling; Unicode case folding is pending.

Semantic snapshots identify TREE and TREEITEM roles, stable parent relationships, expanded/selected/disabled details and a roving Tab stop. Expand controls are pointer/programmatic focus targets with no additional Tab stops. Native accessibility bridges and set-size/position metadata remain pending.

Fixed-height virtualization computes the visible/overscan range arithmetically and emits only that window. Scroll state accepts fractional logical pixels. The styled renderer uses clipped child translation, preserving both the tree clip and its ancestor clips. Overscan rows above/below the viewport cannot receive pointer activation. Keyboard navigation scrolls the active cursor into view; wheel events update controlled scroll state. Separate reduce/submit APIs let custom renderers apply the final scroll offset before registering semantics inside their clipping ancestor. The combined base function emits no draw commands. Variable row heights, automatic tree scrollbar chrome and retained scroll anchoring across arbitrary external reorders remain pending.

The styled Tree paints indented theme-colored rows, textual expand/collapse affordances, selected surfaces and focus borders. Its base model and public node accessors support application-specific row painting. Icons, custom row callback convenience, context menus and drag/drop are not implemented; none are claimed by the parity manifest.

Tests cover transactional rejection and preserved models, parent/subtree structure, expand/collapse, a 10,000-node viewport and 1,000 deterministic expansion rebuilds compared with an independent ancestor scan. Routed keyboard/pointer tests run all four themes and verify multiple navigation events, disabled skipping, direct-child/parent behavior, expansion controls, typeahead/repeated letters, activation, manual selection and semantic hierarchy. Fractional-scroll tests verify measured row positions and reject overscan pointer targets. The same event suite builds with `CUI_TREE_BASE_ONLY`, links only core/base Tree and emits no draw commands. Strict C11 warnings, fully instrumented ASan/UBSan and existing CTest pass before submission. Build/distribution registration belongs to the integrator.

The root exposes scroll offsets and extents for core wheel routing. Wheel events
apply only when routed to this Tree; ancestor boundary bubbling is handled by
core. Scrolling does not repeatedly reveal the focused row; keyboard navigation
reveals it again. Tree-item semantics include the one-based hierarchy level.

Items expose one-based hierarchy level, sibling position and sibling set size,
including disabled siblings and siblings outside the virtual window. Parents
remain logical keyed relations even when their row is unmounted by virtualization;
a DOM adapter cannot resolve an unmounted parent element directly. Sibling metadata
is computed during rebuild, without rescanning the hierarchy during rendering.

# Tree applied selection events

Include `cui/cui_tree_events.h`. `cui_tree_reduce_events`, `cui_base_tree_events`
and `cui_tree_events` add synchronous selection observers to the corresponding
legacy calls. They edit the same caller-owned selected key. A missing observer
still permits editing; its user pointer is ignored. No request/rejection API is
implied. Required pointers and nonzero compound ID are checked before admission;
invalid arguments return `result.error = CUI_TREE_INVALID` without legacy work.

```c
static void selection_changed(void *user, const cui_tree_selection_change *change) {
    bool *needs_save = user; /* unrelated application state */
    *needs_save = true;
    /* Copy *change here to retain it after this callback. */
}
/* During UI submission, with existing caller-owned model/state/selected: */
/* cui_tree_events(ui, id, theme, model, &state, &selected, options,
       (cui_tree_handler){.on_selection_change = selection_changed, .user = &needs_save}); */
```

Each different selected-key write emits one CHANGE immediately after the write.
A→B→A emits two callbacks even when legacy `result.selection_changed` is false.
`selection_count` counts actual observer calls, saturating at SIZE_MAX with
`count_overflow`; `result` preserves every legacy aggregate field. Already-selected
row invocation emits no selection CHANGE. Manual selection suppresses navigation
writes but retains existing row-invocation selection. Cursor repair, scrolling,
search timeout and programmatic model edits do not emit selection events.

Payload `previous`/`value` are stable keys; `node_index` is the current affected
model slot, not stable across reorder and not an input index. `event.target` is the
compound ID. Genuine accepted activation snapshots are copied when available and
retain their original row/toggle `activation.target`. Normal Tree reduction runs
before current-frame semantic submission, so snapshots need not be available:
fallback carries only proven active frame, actual event index and known event-type
source. Typeahead TEXT has UNKNOWN source; no keyboard device is inferred. Presence
flags are authoritative. No observer runs for disabled/passive/layout-only work.

Notifications precede existing later cursor/focus/scroll/semantic/paint work:
row selection notifies before cursor assignment; navigation notifies after cursor
assignment but before focus. Do not assume operation-final state or semantics in
an observer. Reducers, consume order, visible-row layout and paint run once.

Callbacks, user and payload pointer are borrowed during the call. Payload values
are pointer-free and copyable. Never mutate/rebuild/free active model/nodes/labels,
expanded array, selected key, state, input or context, or recursively submit UI
from an observer. Unrelated app flags may change. Defer structural changes,
omission and teardown until outer return plus renderer consumption. Nodes/expanded
arrays remain borrowed until next successful model rebuild; model must be explicitly
destroyed. Omission does not reset it. There is no new bridge/language binding API.

## Expansion

Set `handler.on_expansion_change` to receive `cui_tree_expansion_change` with key,
current model index and applied `previous`/`expanded` bools. `expansion_count` counts
actual calls. Repeated toggle or Left/Right input preserves each actual transition;
leaf/no-op requests are silent. Programmatic `cui_tree_set_expanded`, direct external
edits and rebuilds are outside these UI observers.

The callback follows the setter's rebuild attempt. On a valid unchanged borrowed
model, visible mappings already match the new bool; existing later cursor, focus,
consume and semantic submission have not moved. Capture key/index values rather
than pointers into the model's alternating mapping banks. The legacy setter writes
the bool before rebuilding and does not roll it back on rebuild failure: a real
bool difference is still notified while the old aggregate result remains unchanged.
Do not assume updated mappings on failure. Existing valid-data/lifetime preconditions
still apply; observer callbacks cannot edit the borrowed model or expanded array.
Toggle-origin activation evidence, when available, retains its toggle ID; Left/Right
navigation has actual keyboard/index evidence without manufactured activation.

## Row activation

Set `handler.on_activate` for `cui_tree_activation`. Each existing row-invocation
branch emits ACTIVATE after selected/cursor/legacy `activated` are assigned,
including an already-selected row. Any selection CHANGE precedes it and shares the
same frozen originating evidence. `activation_count` records actual callback count;
legacy `result.activated` still retains only the last key. A toggle expands without
invoking the row; navigation, search, repair and scrolling do not invent invocation.
Missing activation observer preserves the old action/result. All counts independently
saturate at SIZE_MAX and share `count_overflow`.

Current Core does not offer accessibility ACTIVATE for TREEITEM roles; querying
support returns false and queuing it is rejected. This facade does not change that.
Branch toggles have Button semantics and can support accessibility activation;
the submit-before-reduce-only composition can provide accepted copied evidence.
Normal Tree remains reduce-before-submit; this guide makes no new accessibility
routing guarantee for it. Existing focus/navigation semantics stay unchanged.

No move, rename, context-menu, async-load or rejectable expansion hook is added.
Those are separate owner operations. C bridge and Python/JS/TS/Go/Rust continue to
use their existing aggregate/net-change paths; they do not acquire per-transition
C callbacks or row-activation forwarding from this header.
documents.docs/TYPOGRAPHY_ROADMAP.md:
# Typography roadmap grounded in the current implementation

Audit baseline: `integration/density-reconcile`, commit `b96c6844`. This is a
proposal; the declarations below are illustrative and are not shipped APIs.
No font dependency, production code or renderer was changed for this audit.

Subsequent implementation added [body/heading/code tokens](TYPOGRAPHY_TOKENS.md)
and [linear gradient text](TEXT_GRADIENT.md) for software, SDL and Canvas, plus
[cluster letter spacing](LETTER_SPACING.md) for native Bidi/software/SDL. Those
guides and current public headers define the shipped APIs. The proposed broader
authoring declarations below remain design notes, especially browser tracking, numeric
weights/stretch and variable axes.

## What applications can use today

| Request | Current support and evidence | Remaining work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Body, heading, mono families | `cui_text_style.family` is an application `uint32_t` ID. `cui_font_register_style` opens/owns a face; `cui_font_set_style` borrows one. See `include/cui/cui_text.h`, `src/text/cui_text.c:family_find`, `docs/TYPOGRAPHY.md`. | Semantic roles and convenient theme defaults; automatic OS family lookup is absent. |
| Weight, italic, monospace | Four weights: normal, medium, semibold, bold; independent italic/mono flags. Exact face registrations are selected consistently for native measure, metrics and raster. | Arbitrary numeric weights, explicit stretch and variable-font axis authoring. No synthetic bold/italic guarantee. |
| Condensed type | A condensed font file can already be registered under a distinct family ID. | A same-family condensed variant cannot be selected independently of existing style keys; add an explicit stretch key before promising that API. |
| Size and line height | Float logical sizes; explicit line height or zero for natural measurement. Core interns family, size, style and line height. | Named reusable typography tokens and clear defaults across components. |
| Wrap and alignment | `cui_text_ex` wraps within a constrained parent; `cui_text_line` is unwrapped. Paragraph APIs preserve strict UTF-8, hard breaks, grapheme-safe wrapping and optional left/center/right alignment. | One convenient options API, logical start/end alignment and explicit overflow/ellipsis policy. |
| Letter spacing | `cui_text_style.letter_spacing` with explicit provider capability; native contextual measurement, geometry, wrapping, caret and software/SDL rendering share cluster tracking. See `LETTER_SPACING.md`. | Canvas, GPU and foreign style API remain unsupported. Broader authoring declarations below remain proposals. |
| Gradient text | Copied linear stops, block/line anchors and real per-pixel glyph masks in software, SDL and Canvas. See `TEXT_GRADIENT.md`. | GPU implementation, radial/conic paints, color-span combinations and broader native acceptance. |

Named-family fallback currently resolves exact family/style, named-family regular,
default-family style, then opened regular. This is variant fallback; missing glyph
fallback is separately configured through the ordered font fallback chain. Neither
mechanism discovers installed OS fonts. Style registration changes require
`cui_text_metrics_changed(ui)` between frames so existing layout caches remeasure.

Core accepts custom styled measurement and metrics callbacks with a shared user
pointer. If the host supplies only legacy measurement, every family can measure
as the same fallback. A convenient API must either require the complete provider
or expose capability failure rather than silently advertise full typography.

The native layout API already retains actual selected faces and exposes positioned
glyphs, visual runs and cluster advances. It accepts paragraph direction and
language at `cui_font_layout_line`; the convenient Core typography entry points do
not expose every one of those shaping inputs. Cluster edges intentionally do not
represent arbitrary caret positions inside ligatures or full editing navigation.
Native contextual behavior also requires the optional bidi build; disabled builds
report unavailable for that functionality. See `include/cui/cui_text.h` and
`tests/packaging/sdk_text_fixture.c` for the existing contract and checks.

Canvas is a separate host implementation: `web/gallery.js:canvasFont` maps IDs to
CSS font stacks and weights 400/500/600/700; measure uses `measureText`, draw uses
`fillText`. Browser system fonts and shaping are distinct from native
FreeType/HarfBuzz. The gallery now consumes the portable linear text paint using
a full contextual line mask; native software/SDL have separate pixel checks.
A browser demo alone cannot prove native text capability.

## Recommended authoring model

First ship semantic tokens on the existing primitives; this is useful without
redesigning native shaping. Keep font resources in the optional text/host layer,
layout contracts in Core, and theme conveniences in base/components. Core must
continue to have no FreeType, HarfBuzz, SDL, browser or Clay types in public APIs.

A proposed public convenience layer can look like this:

```c
/* Proposed API sketch; names and binary layout need review. */
typedef enum { CUI_FONT_BODY, CUI_FONT_HEADING, CUI_FONT_CODE } cui_font_role;
typedef struct {
    cui_text_style face;
    float size;                 /* logical px; finite, positive */
    float line_height;          /* logical px; 0 = selected face natural */
    float letter_spacing;       /* logical px; 0 preserves current shaping */
} cui_typography;
typedef struct {
    cui_typography body, heading, code;
} cui_typography_theme;
/* Resolve role and token first; submit a complete immutable style to Core. */
```

For today's equivalent, applications can keep these token structs locally,
register IDs for each family, and submit `cui_text_ex` with explicit size/height.
Use the landed `cui_text_style.letter_spacing` only after checking the provider
capability as described in `LETTER_SPACING.md`; it is unavailable on Canvas. A future `cui_text_options` submission
should contain resolved typography, wrap policy, alignment and paint, with a
bool/status result for unsupported combinations. Keep legacy APIs as wrappers
with zero tracking, current wrapping and solid paint. Decide token inheritance
explicitly: role defaults at the theme layer, caller overrides resolved once;
avoid changing every frozen component's metrics by implication.

Use an additive versioned descriptor/provider for extended font selection rather
than reinterpreting the four existing weight enum values as CSS numbers. Suggested
extended selection is numeric weight 1..1000, finite positive width percentage
(100 normal), italic flag and family ID, with documented exact/fallback policy.
A font registry can initially map those requests to explicit static files.
Variable axes and optical sizing should follow only after axis identity,
clamping, ownership and cache keys are specified. Registering a condensed static
face under another family is the reliable interim path.

## Tracking must change layout and paint together

The same resolved shape parameters must reach styled measurement, contextual
geometry, wrap candidate widths, selection/hit testing, retained layouts and draw.
The original audit found callbacks could not carry tracking or stretch. Native
tracking now uses the landed style field and explicit provider capability;
`LETTER_SPACING.md` supersedes the tracking proposal below. Numeric stretch
remains proposed.
Do not let Core compute `character_count * spacing` independently of the shaper.

Define tracking between eligible shaped clusters in visual advance order, with
no extra gap after the final eligible cluster. Combining marks must stay attached;
ligatures, Arabic joining, Indic shaping, default-ignorables, tabs and hard breaks
need explicit rules and fixtures. Retain natural shaping for zero tracking.
The landed policy preserves optional and required ligatures; splitting UTF-8 text into independent character draws destroys
contextual shaping. Negative tracking requires an explicit overlap policy and
must not invalidate finite geometry or hit-test ordering assumptions.

Line boxes, ink bounds and advance bounds are distinct. Explicit line height
sets baseline spacing and may be smaller than ink height; it must not stretch
raster glyphs. A gradient anchor must not be inferred from cropped glyph bitmaps.
Cache keys must include all shape parameters, selected face generation, direction,
language and relevant feature settings. Paint changes should reuse geometry.
Font-load/registration changes invalidate metrics; gradient-stop changes do not.

## Gradient glyph paint

Start with solid and linear gradients; defer radial/conic gradients and CSS string
parsing. A proposed portable `cui_text_paint` is a tagged value containing solid
color or finite start/end points, a bounded copied stop array and an explicit
coordinate space. Use resolved logical coordinates with a documented anchor:
whole paragraph block or each visual line. Make the default paragraph-wide so a
multiline heading has one continuous gradient. Resolve final box/alignment before
publishing commands, and preserve the same anchor on every emitted line.

Specify stop ordering, duplicate-stop hard edges, out-of-range rejection or clamp,
zero-length axis behavior and interpolation/color space. Reuse a documented CUI
color convention rather than claiming exact Tailwind/CSS fidelity by appearance.
Recommend premultiplied-alpha interpolation with explicit color-space selection;
CSS matching must name and test the matching space. Gradient alpha multiplies
coverage and cumulative ancestor opacity exactly once. Current draw colors and
bitmap opacity already absorb ancestor opacity in Core; extending paint requires
one consistent policy for stop alpha and span alpha, not a second backend factor.

Native software currently multiplies glyph coverage by `r->ink.a`; SDL3 caches
coverage textures and applies a single RGB/alpha modulation per glyph
(`backends/software/cui_software.c:glyph`, `backends/sdl3/cui_sdl3.c:glyph`). A
single modulation cannot express a continuous gradient across a glyph. Keep the
coverage cache independent of paint and sample the gradient at each output pixel
in software. For SDL, add a bounded temporary RGBA mask/composite path first or a
proper masked gradient rendering path; changing tint once per glyph is not
sufficient. Cache any painted result by paint, anchor, density and mask revision,
or do not cache it. SDL_GPU/Sokol need equivalent explicit support or observable
unsupported status; do not silently flatten to one color.

Canvas should render a full shaped line mask and apply a gradient in the same
resolved coordinate space using a bounded offscreen surface and compositing.
Preserve context state, clips, logical-to-device scale, baseline and opacity.
Avoid one `fillText` call per letter. If browser and native shaping differ, test
semantic anchor/alpha behavior independently and state the raster difference.
All paths must include italic overhang and fallback glyph ink beyond advance
bounds, respect ancestor clips, bound temporary allocations and handle empty
text/zero bounds without NaNs or accidental giant surfaces.

## Implementation sequence and acceptance evidence

1. Add a typography example using existing body/heading/mono IDs, registered
   static variants and size/line-height tokens. Cover missing variant/family
   fallback and dynamic registration invalidation. This can deliver immediate
   usability without waiting for tracking or gradients.
2. Add versioned extended shape/provider contracts and shared capability handling.
   Establish real static condensed-face selection before variable-font work.
   Extend cache keys and binding generators together.
3. Implement tracking in one retained native layout path and route measurement,
   geometry, wrapping and paint through it. Add RTL, combining, ligature, Arabic,
   fallback-face, negative/zero tracking and fractional-size tests. Assert caret,
   selection and measured/drawn advances agree.
4. Add paint descriptors and Core lifetime/opacity/anchor tests; implement software
   as the deterministic reference, then SDL3 and headless Canvas. Test a gradient
   inside a single wide glyph, transparent stops, multiline alignment, clipping,
   italic overhang, nested opacity and density 1/1.5/2. Unsupported adapters must
   report capability limitations until implemented.
5. Publish semantic theme roles and ergonomic overrides across components, then
   update generated SDKs/packages. Re-run actual installed library fixtures and
   compare wrappers as well as native text. Preserve all 78 manifest entries.

Native tests use `python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir build` on Linux;
browser tests remain headless. GPU hardware parity remains explicitly deferred
when unavailable under the virtual display. This audit ran no UI or native tests
because it changes proposal documents only.

# Reusable typography tokens

`cui_typography.h` is a header-only authoring convenience over existing Core text
APIs. It gives applications three semantic roles without owning fonts, modifying
the current theme or introducing new layout behavior.

```c
#include "cui/cui_typography.h"

const cui_typography_roles type = {
    .body = {.style = {.family = 11}, .size = 16.5f,
             .line_height = 26, .wrap = true},
    .heading = {.style = {.family = 12, .weight = CUI_TEXT_WEIGHT_BOLD},
                .size = 30, .line_height = 38, .wrap = true,
                .align = CUI_TEXT_ALIGN_CENTER},
    .code = {.style = {.family = 13, .monospace = true},
             .size = 14, .line_height = 23, .wrap = false}
};
cui_typography_token heading;
if (cui_typography_resolve(&type, CUI_TYPOGRAPHY_HEADING, &heading)) {
    /* In an open frame, inside a constrained layout parent. */
    bool submitted = cui_typography_text(ui, cui_string("A clear heading"), heading,
                                         (cui_color){24, 30, 40, 255});
    (void)submitted; /* Real applications handle submission/capacity errors. */
}
```

Roles are ordinary caller-owned values. Resolution copies the selected token;
change the copy to override one call without changing defaults. Only the selected
role must be valid. Invalid roles/tokens preserve the output. Valid sizes are
finite logical pixels in `(0, 65535]`; line height is finite in `[0, 65535]`, with
zero selecting natural metrics. Alignment is physical left/center/right. Weight
uses the existing normal/medium/semibold/bold enum. There is no implicit scaling,
inheritance, mutable current style or guessed font registration.

`cui_typography_text_colored` accepts existing paragraph-relative UTF-8 byte color
spans. Both submission helpers use `cui_text_paragraph_colored_aligned`, retaining
strict UTF-8 validation, grapheme-safe wrapping and contextual geometry when the
host supplies it. `wrap=false` retains hard breaks but may overflow; use a clipping
ancestor where needed. A constrained parent width is required to demonstrate
wrapping. Explicit line height sets spacing, not glyph stretching. Check the
helper result and the existing end-frame error contract for layout failures.

`cui_typography_text_painted(ui, text, token, paint)` uses the same token geometry
with a solid or copied linear text paint. See [gradient text](TEXT_GRADIENT.md)
for stops, directions, paragraph/line anchors, renderer capabilities and lifetime.
This helper does not combine gradient paint with byte color spans.

## Native font registration and composed example

`examples/typography/app.c` composes a centered heading, wrapped body, an italic
local override and clipped unwrapped code. All three families have distinct IDs.
Compile with `CUI_TYPOGRAPHY_NATIVE` to enable `typography_example_font`: it takes
five explicit file paths (body regular, heading regular, heading bold, body
italic, code regular), opens an owner and registers the exact styles used by the
example. Failure closes the partially built owner and returns NULL. There is no
OS name lookup or synthetic italic/bold claim. The returned owner must outlive
the renderer/context use and be closed by the host.

Configure the native context and renderer with the same font owner:

```c
cui_config config = {
    .width = 900, .height = 700,
    .measure_styled = cui_font_measure_styled, .measure_user = font,
    .font_metrics = cui_font_get_metrics,
    .text_geometry = cui_font_text_geometry,
    .text_geometry_line = cui_font_text_geometry_line
};
```

Then call `typography_example_frame` from the native host's frame loop and submit
its draw list to the existing renderer. The example itself creates no window.
After changing registrations, call `cui_text_metrics_changed` between frames.
Custom hosts and Canvas must apply the same family mapping in measurement and
paint; tokens do not make browser and native shaping identical.

`tests/unit/test_typography_tokens.c` checks validation, immutable resolution,
failed-input atomicity, styled/color-span forwarding and centered geometry.
`examples/typography/test_app.c` checks family/style/float-size commands, body
baseline spacing, wrapped line counts and stable roles across wide/narrow/wide
frames. Compiled with `CUI_TYPOGRAPHY_NATIVE`, it requires all five explicit path
environment variables `CUI_TYPOGRAPHY_BODY`, `CUI_TYPOGRAPHY_HEADING`,
`CUI_TYPOGRAPHY_HEADING_BOLD`, `CUI_TYPOGRAPHY_BODY_ITALIC`, `CUI_TYPOGRAPHY_CODE`;
without them it returns 77. It compares native measurement and raster output for
each used exact variant against the separately opened actual file. Use distinct
family files to exercise the intended body/heading/code configuration.

## Extending typography later

These tokens expose supported properties only. Tracking, numeric weight/stretch
and variable axes require complete provider, measurement, geometry and cache
contracts before authoring fields can be added. A future
extended layout/paint descriptor can have a new token type and helpers while
keeping these functions as wrappers for zero tracking and solid/span paint.
Current source callers need no migration to use this convenience header; font
registration, context callbacks and existing text entry points remain available.
documents.docs/UNICODE_WRAP.md:
# Source-compatible contextual wrapping

`cui_text_paragraph_colored(..., wrap=true, ...)` now computes visual rows at the
current frame's assigned width using the frozen runtime's actual candidate and
fallback policy. It retains all original UTF-8 bytes, including trailing spaces,
and intersects color spans with each final row. `wrap=false`, ordinary `cui_text`
and the existing unwrapped contextual APIs retain their previous behavior.

This policy comes from gpui-pre **0.3.8**, the exact dependency of frozen GPUI Kit
commit `87d10ae5e1299d1be18670a37570c5402f952e34`. StyledText calls
`LineLayout::compute_wrap_boundaries`; its classifier is
`LineWrapper::is_word_char`. This is not the Unicode default word algorithm,
UAX #14, CSS line breaking, or the separate editor-oriented `wrap_line` helper.

The source considers ASCII letters/digits, its explicit Latin/Cyrillic/Vietnamese/
combining-mark/Bengali ranges, selected punctuation and three glue characters to
be word characters. A word character following an ASCII space creates a candidate;
a non-word character other than ASCII space creates a candidate after the first
non-space character. On overflow it selects the last candidate, otherwise falls
back before the overflowing item. Only ASCII space has that special whitespace
role; tabs and Unicode spaces follow their explicit classifier result. State and
advance accounting follow the measured LineLayout implementation, including its
preservation of spaces in the previous row. Nonbreaking glue still participates in
fallback when an entire token cannot fit, as in the source.

CUI deliberately restricts candidates and fallback to extended grapheme boundaries
and, when available, shaped-cluster boundaries. Combining sequences, emoji ZWJ/
modifier sequences, regional-indicator pairs, Hangul clusters and Indic conjuncts
stay intact. A single indivisible cluster wider than the width occupies its own
overflowing row. The requirement to preserve complete graphemes takes precedence
over a source platform that happens to emit multiple glyph items for one grapheme.

Existing `cui_config.text_geometry_line` supplies a full contextual shaped session.
Core queries the whole selected line's selection rectangles once, sorts them by
original byte offset, and unions shaped-cluster boundaries with grapheme boundaries.
Advances are copied into bounded frame storage and the session is released before
layout publication. The current-frame layout callback performs no heap allocation
or host measurement. Native font callers can use `cui_font_text_geometry_line`.
If contextual geometry is unavailable, Core measures each grapheme once through
the existing styled measurement callback. That fallback preserves byte/cluster
safety but cannot reproduce shaping interactions such as kerning or ligatures
which a measurement-only host does not expose. RTL and mixed text retain their
complete original paragraph for contextual bidi shaping of every row; row ranges
remain contiguous logical original-byte ranges, not copied visual-order strings.
This is a source-policy port with these explicit adaptations, not a claim of
pixel parity across platform shapers or every GPUI style refinement.

The two opt-in hooks in the pinned Clay header allow custom intrinsic width/minimum
and final wrapping after width sizing and before height propagation. Hooks are
inactive for ordinary text and unwrapped text. Core's normal layout, clipping,
prepaint and bounds tracking continue to operate on the resulting visual rows.
Clipping/scroll container sizing retains the existing Core conventions; give text
an explicit inner width when a scroll owner intentionally allows wider content.

Strict UTF-8 validation, grapheme preparation, geometry extraction, and conservative
storage/element reservation finish before publication. Heap work and copied frame
metadata are bounded by configured frame storage. Invalid input or preflight
capacity failure publishes no layout. Exhausting final wrapped-row or clipped-span
capacity marks a Core capacity error and empties the draw list; the next frame
starts clean. Callbacks used for measurement/geometry cannot submit UI mutations.
Grapheme scans and measurement-only preparation are linear in text length; geometry
preparation uses one bulk query and an O(n log n) sort. Wrapping runs twice in linear
time to reserve all final rows before emitting any. No original masked input is
introduced: the Label component submits already-masked display bytes, so copied
cluster metadata also contains only those display scalars.

## Provenance and validation

- Runtime source: [gpui-pre 0.3.8 LineLayout](https://docs.rs/crate/gpui-pre/0.3.8/source/src/text_system/line_layout.rs)
  and [LineWrapper](https://docs.rs/crate/gpui-pre/0.3.8/source/src/text_system/line_wrapper.rs).
  Official crate archive: `https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/gpui-pre/0.3.8/download`.
  SHA256 `d7f0bc3ebba070f8981b3f8e905a12f47d27794a30d029e59cdb9edf7a4b3360`.
  The classifier/candidate policy was ported into C; the copyright/license notice
  for the Apache-2.0 runtime appears below.
- `src/core/cui_unicode_grapheme.h` copies the exact Unicode 17 generated grapheme
  ranges and UAX #29 scan from `src/base/cui_edit.c` at `74bdb58b`, with private names
  and a bounded forward helper. It adds no Core dependency on Base and downloads
  no new Unicode data. Official input URLs/hashes remain in
  `third_party/unicode/17.0.0/manifest.json`; the shared Unicode V3 notice is below.
- The Core private include `cui_unicode_grapheme.h` must be expanded by distribution
  generation. The patched Clay header and pin are described in its adjacent PIN.md;
  integrators update the dependency checksum and generated distribution together.

`test_unicode_wrap_source` runs all 766 vendored official grapheme conformance
fixtures and source-specific narrow-width cases covering punctuation, glue,
leading/trailing spaces, tabs, Unicode spaces, CJK, RTL, combining marks, emoji,
Indic and Hangul. It checks exact original row bytes/spans, oversized atomic
clusters, legacy/nowrap behavior, current-frame prepaint/bounds, shaped ligature
cluster preservation, capacity recovery and linear measurement-call growth.
`test_contextual_wrap_source` retains paragraph/Unicode-separator and copied software
snapshot coverage. Defining `CUI_TEST_WRAP_RENDERER` additionally enables real-font
raster tests; the Unicode test accepts a primary font path and optional owned RTL
fallback font path. Sanitizer and WASI builds exercise the same portable code.

# CUI v1.0 readiness

CUI is a working alpha. A live gallery and passing tests demonstrate useful functionality; they do not establish production readiness or complete component parity. This assessment is dated 17 October 2026.

The catalog contains all 78 families: 77 tested subsets, one implemented family and zero fully verified families. The feature ledger contains 360 entries: 315 tested, four implemented and 41 not started. Features differ greatly in complexity, so these counts are not a completion percentage or a release-date estimate. The machine-readable component manifest remains the acceptance ledger.

## Release gates

| Gate | Current evidence | Required before v1.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Component behavior | All 78 families have live examples and substantive APIs; tested subsets remain explicitly partial. | Close every feature gap, verify realistic usage, controlled state, keyboard, pointer, relevant touch, semantics and visual states for each family. |
| Touch and pointers | Shared controls expose hover, pressed, focus and activation. The published integration tests contact/device routing, precise touch scrolling, opt-in pan/pinch, cancellation, drag priority and broader cursor overrides. Physical-device/family coverage remains incomplete. | Test tap versus drag cancellation, nested scrolling, capture loss, overlays, multi-contact pan/pinch, disabled controls and device-specific cursor fallbacks. Zoom must require opt-in. |
| Text and editing | Unicode grapheme/word conformance, selection, multicursor edits, bounded grouped undo and cached large-document viewport work have tests. Single-selection composition across four text consumers plus Numeric, OTP and Combobox has integrated tests. Optional native bidi/hard-line shaping and explicit font fallback have tests. | Finish IME across remaining editable consumers, physical OS candidate windows/mobile keyboards, bidi caret/wrap integration and automatic font discovery, language-service integration and large-document end-to-end performance. |
| Rendering | Software, browser Canvas, Linux Sokol GL and SDL_GPU Vulkan have runtime evidence for supported capabilities. Native/software analytic path meshes have integrated runtime and pixel-test evidence for uniform paints; broader source paint parity remains unfinished. | Verify capability coverage, clipping, DPI, resource lifetime, recovery, visual consistency and native renderers on the advertised platforms. |
| Accessibility | Roles, state, names, actions and focus have headless semantic tests. The optional Linux AccessKit package passes native DBus and relocated CMake/pkg-config consumer tests; assistive-technology and broader platform acceptance remain open. | Implement and validate platform accessibility bridges with real assistive technologies; cover contrast, text scaling, reduced motion and touch targets. |
| Platforms | Portable library CI includes Linux, Windows and macOS; browser and Linux native runtime checks exist. | Native Windows/macOS, Linux display-server variants and Android/iOS runtime evidence. Compile-only evidence must remain labeled separately. |
| API and ownership | Portable C11 APIs, layered implementation, generated embedding headers and explicit memory contracts exist. | Review ABI/version policy, lifetimes, failure behavior, capacity limits and upgrade compatibility; finish the optional ecosystem promised by the scope. |
| Themes and motion | Bounded owned theme registry, transactional supported imports, semantic snapshots and explicit host preference/motion projection have native, header-only and browser tests. | Validate physical native preference changes, native contrast/motion observation and broader component integration of typography, spacing and shadows; close remaining source styling and current-frame chart/plot consumer geometry gaps. |
| Performance and safety | Warning builds, sanitizers, WASI and browser tests; selected measured workloads. | Reproducible startup, memory and frame-budget baselines, broad stress/fuzz coverage and regression thresholds on supported targets. |
| Documentation | Browsable guides, compiled C snippets, callback/state explanations and host-language examples. | Every shipped capability has accurate usage, ownership, limitations and reproduction instructions; examples must match released APIs. |

## How progress is reported

A tested feature is narrower than a verified family. A compile check is narrower than a native runtime check. A completed worker branch is narrower than an integrated and deployed release. Reports and the platform matrix preserve these distinctions.

The next milestones are consistent input across touch and pointer devices, complete heavyweight component behavior, international text and native accessibility, followed by platform acceptance and API stabilization. There is no defensible v1.0 date yet. Full catalog and ecosystem scope remains active rather than being reduced to reach a release label.

See [the component ledger](gpui-parity.json), [platform evidence](PLATFORM_MATRIX.md), [current report](NIGHTLY_REPORT.md) and [interaction feedback](website-feedback.md).

# Decoded video frames and a portable timeline

`cui/cui_video.h` supplies a decoder-neutral timeline model and a real CPU RGBA8
surface using the existing bitmap draw path. There is **no built-in codec**,
container reader, network transport, audio output, subtitle engine, recorder,
casting service or editor. The architecture roadmap remains [VIDEO_PLAN.md](VIDEO_PLAN.md).

The optional [offline audio host foundation](../examples/video_audio_host/README.md)
demonstrates bounded PCM buffering, worker cancellation, generation-safe seeks and
ordered output-consumption accounting with injected services. It is an
example-local C11 controller, not a CUI component API or device adapter. Its
deterministic tests require no network, microphone, speaker or window;
the guide includes build and invisible-display test commands. Browser video uses
the browser's existing audio decoder/output independently.

The separate [FFmpeg PCM decoder proof](../examples/video_audio_ffmpeg/README.md)
feeds that controller from real local media and converts audio to 48 kHz stereo
float. Offline tests check sample content, resampler draining, exact replay-based
seeks, a shared video/audio origin, cancellation and pending-worker shutdown.
This optional example currently admits only bounded PCM media and replays from
the beginning for seeks; it is not general compressed-media playback. Its pinned
FFmpeg package has GPLv3-or-later licensing, documented in the example. These
standalone proofs do not themselves connect a video UI to a device.

The optional [SDL output transport](../examples/video_audio_sdl/README.md) supplies
the controller's output interface. Its owner-thread pump submits bounded PCM
chunks and reconciles SDL's software queue drain without registering application
callbacks with the mixer. Headless tests use SDL's dummy driver and injected
failures. That evidence covers pause, resume, discard and ordered consumption;
it does not prove physical audibility or a DAC clock.

The separate [native video with PCM sound example](../examples/video_player_audio/README.md)
connects both workers and the SDL output to a real CUI VideoPlayer UI. Its initial
supported profile is immutable local Matroska with FFV1 video and PCM audio,
known zero container origin and duration at most 10 seconds. It offers play,
pause, seek, skip and replay, and selects decoded video frames against observed
SDL software-mixer consumption. It does not claim a physical DAC clock or
speaker-level synchronization. Native fullscreen, rate controls, general
MP4/AAC/Opus playback and actual device hotplug recovery remain unsupported in
this example. The existing silent video example remains available independently.

Build and test from the repository root with the pinned development dependencies
listed in that example's README:

```sh
cmake -S examples/video_player_audio -B build-video-sound -G Ninja -DVIDEO_SOUND_UI=ON
cmake --build build-video-sound --target video_player_audio test_sound test_sound_watch test_sound_output test_sound_legacy
python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir build-video-sound -- -R '^sound_'
```

Automated native checks use private Xvfb, forced SDL dummy audio and captured
actual decoded pixels. They do not open a desktop window or exercise speakers.
The README provides a separate explicit interactive launch command and explains
PCM conversion, package licensing, device invalidation, bounded buffering,
software-clock limitations and shutdown ownership.

## Initialize and advance

```c
#include "cui/cui_video.h"

cui_video player;
bool ready = cui_video_init(&player, (cui_video_config){
    .duration = 120, .duration_known = true, .seekable = true
});
if (ready) {
    ready = cui_video_set_playing(&player, true);
    /* Once per host tick, with elapsed monotonic seconds, excluding paused time. */
    ready = ready && cui_video_advance(&player, elapsed_seconds);
}
```

The caller owns the model and UI-thread synchronization. No wall clock is read
internally. Pause leaves position unchanged; rate is any positive finite value.
Known duration may be zero; unknown duration uses `duration_known=false` and
`duration=0`. Unknown playback advances until the host calls `cui_video_finish`.
No buffering/decode state or frame queue is implied.

Seeking requires `seekable`; known duration bounds the target. Successful seeks
increment `generation`, including a seek to the same time, invalidating previously
acquired frames. Seeking exactly to the known end stops playback. Starting an
ended seekable model restarts at zero with a new generation; restarting an ended
nonseekable source fails. A model with looping enabled wraps when advancing past
its known positive duration only when seekable. Each advance that wraps increments
generation once, even if several loops elapsed. `finish` is an explicit terminal
host acknowledgement and stops regardless of loop preference.

The timeline requests no decoder action itself: the host must translate seeks,
restart and loop generation changes into source commands and acknowledge actual
results in its own controller. Do not interpret an accepted model command as a
successful asynchronous decoder seek. Keep audio-synchronized time, error,
buffering and capability handling in that host/controller until an adapter
contract is implemented.

All model commands return false without changing the model for invalid inputs,
nonfinite values, overflow, unsupported seek/restart, or exhausted generation.
Initialization sets generation to one; do not reinitialize a player while old
frames can still be submitted. Replacing a source requires retiring its frames
and outstanding draw lists before reusing generation values.

## Submit an already-decoded frame

```c
cui_video_frame frame = {
    .bitmap = {.pixels = rgba, .width = frame_width, .height = frame_height,
               .stride = row_bytes, .revision = frame_revision},
    .generation = player.generation,
    .timestamp = presentation_seconds
};
/* Inside an active frame, after the host selects the due decoded frame. */
bool submitted = cui_video_surface(ui, video_id, &player, &frame,
    (cui_video_surface_options){
        .geometry = {.width = available_width, .height = 240, .fit = CUI_IMAGE_CONTAIN},
        .opacity = 1, .description = cui_string("Video preview")
    });
```

Pixels are borrowed straight-alpha RGBA8, including any row padding. Keep them
unchanged until **every renderer has finished consuming the draw list**;
`cui_end_frame` is not a release boundary. The helper retains no lease and invokes
no release callback. A host decoder's acquired-frame lease belongs to the host;
release it exactly once after consumption or after a rejected submission that
has no outstanding users. Never recycle a decoder buffer immediately after
surface submission. A paused preview still needs its frame's pixels alive.
Increment bitmap revision when pixels change in place; use distinct retained
storage when an older draw list is outstanding.

The surface checks model generation, timestamp, bitmap stride/dimensions,
geometry, opacity and description. A timestamp is metadata: the host selects due
frames, drops late ones and schedules redraws. No automatic PTS scheduling is
provided. Contain, cover, fill, scale-down and natural-size fit reuse the existing
image layout rules and a clipped parent. Native texture import, YUV/HDR conversion,
rotation and sample-aspect metadata are unsupported. Renderer support is that of
existing CPU bitmap draws; the new tests prove software output, not every backend.

## Optional controls

The surface submits no timeline/button hit targets. The controlled
Styled composition is documented in [VIDEO_PLAYER.md](VIDEO_PLAYER.md). It emits
requests against a read-only playback view, with optional controls and explicit
host capabilities. The timeline and surface remain usable independently.

## Headless evidence

`tests/unit/test_video.c` uses a deterministic synthetic clock and two borrowed
RGBA frames. It checks pause/resume, rates, seek/end/restart, looping/generations,
unknown duration, zero duration, invalid-input atomicity and overflow. Software
rendering checks contain letterboxing, cover crop, fill, opacity, changed frame
revision and stale-frame rejection. No codec or window is needed. The test must
link `cui` and `cui_software`; the timeline and surface implementation are included
in the portable `cui` target:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCUI_BUILD_NATIVE=OFF
cmake --build build --target test_video
python scripts/test_local.py --build-dir build -R '^video$'
```

The same model and software pixel assertions run under WASI with the pinned tools:

```sh
uv run scripts/test_wasi.py --suite video
```

The generated `dist/cui_video.h` module and Go/Rust source SDKs expose the same
API. These are C APIs; language-specific video builders are not yet provided.
documents.docs/VIDEO_PLAN.md:
# Video architecture proposal

Original architecture audit baseline: `b96c6844`, before selecting a decoder
dependency. The current portable surface and controls are implemented separately
from the optional FFmpeg example below. The remaining architecture proposals do
not establish shipped capabilities.

The portable timeline and borrowed CPU RGBA surface are now available in
`cui/cui_video.h`; [the implementation guide](VIDEO_GUIDE.md) describes their
actual behavior and tests. The [controlled player](VIDEO_PLAYER.md) and optional
[FFmpeg example](../examples/video_player/README.md) implement requests, a bounded
host-owned queue and actual silent local-file decoding. They do not change the
78-component baseline. Audio, browser playback, general decoder-adapter ABI and
production buffering/scheduling remain planned.

## Existing foundation and its limit

`include/cui/cui_media.h` already defines borrowed image frames (RGBA-sized
stride validation, revision, duration), an image loader, contain/cover/fill layout,
and image animation state with caller-provided time and next-wake scheduling.
`src/base/cui_media.c` validates frames and polls a host-side image cache. That
is useful precedent for ownership and frame presentation; it is not a streaming
video decoder, audio clock, seek engine, recorder or editor.

`cui_bitmap` in `include/cui/cui.h` is borrowed straight-alpha RGBA8 with stride
and revision. It remains valid through renderer completion. The current video
surface reuses `cui_paint_bitmap` and image-fit geometry with decoded RGBA frames. It
must not preload an entire movie into the animated-image frame array (currently
bounded at 4096 entries). Dynamic streaming requires bounded queues and explicit
frame release, buffering and end-of-stream behavior.

## Portable layers

1. **Decoded-frame surface:** accept frame identity/generation, dimensions,
   RGBA8 stride, pixel data and presentation timestamp. Retain/release a frame
   lease until the renderer finishes consuming it; never let the decoder recycle
   pixels at submission time. Draw using existing fit/crop rules. Start with CPU
   frames; zero-copy platform textures require separate optional adapters.
2. **Playback state/controller:** stopped/loading/playing/paused/buffering/ended/
   failed states; position, known/unknown duration, seekability, playback rate,
   mute/volume and error/capability values. Commands request state changes and
   asynchronous results acknowledge them. No codec handles or OS types in Core.
3. **Clock and scheduler:** host monotonic time for silent playback; optional
   audio master clock when audio is enabled. Compare timestamps, present due
   frames, drop late frames by documented policy and request the next wake.
   Pause/resume must rebase time; seek uses a new generation so stale frames and
   callbacks cannot reappear. Avoid busy polling and unbounded decode queues.
4. **Composed controls:** buttons, timeline slider, time display, loading/error
   overlay, volume, captions and fullscreen request. Keep these optional so the
   same surface supports thumbnails, backgrounds and applications with custom
   controls. Keyboard focus, accessible names/status, seek increments and reduced
   motion/autoplay policy belong in the UI/host contract.
5. **Optional adapters:** decoder/container/network input, audio output/clock,
   subtitle sources, platform fullscreen and GPU frame import. Adapter capability
   negotiation must expose unsupported seek/rate/audio/captions. Worker threads
   may decode; UI callbacks and font/UI state stay on their documented thread.

A proposed decoder-neutral interface should offer open/poll/command/close with
bounded events and explicit frame acquisition/release. Do not finalize ABI before
agreeing on time units, rational timestamp conversion, thread/cancellation rules,
seek completion, queue bounds, frame orientation, sample aspect ratio, color
metadata and source lifetime. Begin with RGBA8 SDR; document conversion/color
limitations. YUV planes, HDR, GPU surfaces and hardware decoding are later
capabilities, not implied by a CPU bitmap prototype.

## Different product scopes

| Scope | Required pipeline | Relationship to playback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local/streamed playback | Demux/decode, timestamp scheduling, optional audio output | Initial target; controls can be composed independently. |
| Recording | Capture source, timestamped audio/video, encoder, muxer, file lifecycle | Separate adapter pipeline; recording a CUI surface needs a defined readback boundary. |
| Casting | Device discovery/session/transport, remote control and remote playback state | Separate host/service integration with latency and permission requirements. |
| Editing | Source model, timeline, trims/tracks, preview, export/render/encode | Separate application model that may reuse the playback surface. |
| Screen/camera capture | Platform capture APIs, permissions, device lifecycle | Optional input adapter; not included in a decoded-frame widget. |

## Deliverable sequence and tests

First implement a renderer-independent playback state machine with a fake clock
and synthetic decoder frames. Prove pause/resume, buffering, cancellation,
end-of-stream, unknown duration, seek generations, rate changes and bounded
queues deterministically. Add a CPU RGBA surface and fit/clipping/opacity/revision
checks using software output; verify SDL under invisible Xvfb and Canvas headless.
Assert that frames remain leased until consumption and release exactly once.

Then compose accessible controls against the fake controller. Only after the
interfaces work should a separate decision compare decoder adapters against
supported platforms, license/distribution constraints, pinned versions, codec
availability, audio synchronization and package size. No dependency is necessary
to review or test the first two deliverables. The optional silent local-file
example proves decoded play/pause/seek and cleanup. Audio-capable playback still
requires audio synchronization acceptance.
Recording, casting and editing each need separate acceptance criteria and scope.

# Reusable VideoPlayer

Start with `cui_video_player_defaults()`: a 320×180 contained video surface,
compact playback/skip/timeline controls, short `m:ss / m:ss` time and fullscreen.
The seek row and icon buttons have 44-unit touch targets; artwork is 20 units.
The seek line is four units high. Narrow bars wrap buttons/time within the
configured width (minimum 160). Controls are below the surface, not overlays;
there is no auto-hide policy. Rate is available explicitly, not shown by default.
Set both `surface.geometry` and `controls_options.width` when resizing. The host
must supply capabilities and a request callback to enable actions. Fullscreen is
visible by default but disabled without `CUI_VIDEO_CAP_FULLSCREEN`; it never
silently changes a window or DOM element. No volume/audio state is invented.

`compact` is an appended field of `cui_video_controls_options`. Rebuild C
applications against matching headers and library; this prerelease does not
promise binary compatibility with an older struct layout. Legacy zero-initialized
options retain their existing full-size controls.

This complete portable C11 owner seam draws inside an existing CUI frame. The
host fills `confirmed`, optionally supplies an already-decoded RGBA frame, and
drains copied requests **after** submission/rendering. It must handle overflow
rather than assuming an unbounded queue. No codec/network API is required by CUI.

```c
#include "cui/cui_video_controls.h"

typedef struct {
    cui_video_controls_state controls;
    cui_video_view confirmed;
    cui_video_request pending[32];
    unsigned pending_count;
    bool overflow;
} player_owner;

static void player_request(void *user, const cui_video_request *request) {
    player_owner *owner = user;
    if (owner->pending_count < 32)
        owner->pending[owner->pending_count++] = *request;
    else
        owner->overflow = true;
}

bool player_owner_init(player_owner *owner, uint64_t source_id) {
    if (!owner || !source_id)
        return false;
    *owner = (player_owner){0};
    owner->confirmed.source_id = source_id;
    owner->confirmed.capabilities = CUI_VIDEO_CAP_PLAY | CUI_VIDEO_CAP_SEEK;
    return cui_video_init(&owner->confirmed.timeline,
        (cui_video_config){.duration = 120, .duration_known = true, .seekable = true});
}

bool player_owner_draw(cui_context *ui, const cui_theme *theme,
                       player_owner *owner, const cui_video_player_frame *decoded) {
    cui_video_player_options options = cui_video_player_defaults();
    options.controls_options.on_request = player_request;
    options.controls_options.user = owner;
    options.surface.description = cui_string("Video preview");
    return cui_video_player(ui, 700, theme, &owner->controls,
                            owner->confirmed, decoded, options);
}
```

The 120-second timeline is example host metadata, not media opened by CUI.
The host acquires sources, demuxes/decodes, schedules frames and audio, implements
seek/rate/fullscreen, and publishes confirmed state after success. Check request
source/generation before applying it; queueing is not acknowledgement. The null
frame draws an empty reserved surface. For actual decoding, the existing
[FFmpeg host example](../examples/video_player/README.md) is a separate adapter.
`cui_video_surface` remains the reusable Base surface for a controls-free view.
Keep captions, sample descriptions and diagnostic/debug text in host content
outside the player; the standard bar displays only media position and controls.

Legacy `cui_video_controls_defaults()` keeps its original layout and visible
parts. The additive `controls_options.compact=true` opts into the standard bar;
`cui_video_player_defaults()` selects it automatically. Existing manually built
player options are not forced into the new layout.

The pinned catalog already contained `skip-back`, `skip-forward` and `gauge`,
but they were excluded from the default embedded bundle. They now embed their
existing SVGs alongside play/pause/maximize/minimize, so standard controls need
no custom loader or all-assets build. All seven names are prepared and checked
for actual mask pixels by `test_video_player_defaults.c`; player seek icons are
also checked in actual software-rendered pixels. Catalog names/paths and
`theme.icon_loader` overrides are retained. The named Button icon cache accepts
catalog names/paths; arbitrary unknown names are not introduced by this API.

## Controlled video controls

`cui_video_controls.h` adds optional Styled controls above the portable video
surface. This extension is independent of the frozen 78-component baseline.
It does not decode, play audio, change native fullscreen, or acknowledge commands.

```c
#include "cui/cui_video_controls.h"

/* Retain one zero-initialized state per stable controls ID. */
cui_video_controls_options options = cui_video_controls_defaults();
options.on_request = request_playback;
options.user = application;
options.width = 320;
options.visible |= CUI_VIDEO_CONTROL_FULLSCREEN;
cui_video_controls(ui, controls_id, theme, &application->controls,
                   application->confirmed_view, options);
```

The view is copied by value. Its timeline is confirmed application state. Each
request contains `source_id`, observed timeline `generation`, and a monotonically
increasing `sequence`. The callback may accept or reject it without the controls
writing playback state. It must not destroy the context or controls state during
submission. A missing callback makes controls read-only. Sequence exhaustion
makes them read-only; retire outstanding work before replacing their state.
Source IDs must be nonzero and must not be reused while old frames or requests
can survive. Source or generation changes clear local scrub presentation.

`PLAYING` and `FULLSCREEN` carry the desired boolean; `SKIP` carries a signed
seconds delta; `RATE` carries the explicitly configured `requested_rate`.
`SEEK` carries absolute double-precision seconds and BEGIN/UPDATE/COMMIT/CANCEL.
BEGIN starts preview, UPDATE adjusts it, COMMIT requests the final decoder seek,
and CANCEL restores the gesture's starting preview. An application can implement
live seeking, but should bound outstanding seeks and ignore obsolete completions.
Keyboard changes emit all three accepted phases per key. Gesture preview is not
a second authoritative playback timeline. Removing a timeline/source invalidates
its local preview; it does not issue a stale cancellation request.

The slider uses normalized 0..1 Core numeric semantics because that ABI is float;
the accessible description gives position/duration in seconds. It retains double
seconds in requests. Space/Enter use existing Button behavior; focused timeline
arrows use `seek_step`, Home/End use bounds. Shortcuts never inspect global keys.
Buttons retain accessible labels when icon-only. Set labels to localize them.
Use each `*_icon` catalog name/path and `theme.icon_loader` for replacement SVGs.
No raw SVG parsing or codec types are added to the public player contract.

Visibility and capability are separate: absent `visible` flags submit no hit
regions or semantics; visible unsupported actions are disabled. Seek additionally
requires a known positive duration and a seekable timeline. Loading/buffering/error
views disable playback/seek/rate; fullscreen remains a separate host capability.
Fullscreen display follows only the confirmed `view.fullscreen` value.
Volume/mute/captions have no invented state; supply separate host-backed controls
when those features exist. This first bar has no auto-hide timer or overflow menu.
Buttons use 44-unit touch targets and flow into additional rows within the selected width (at least 160
logical units).

`cui_video_player` composes surface and optional controls. A null frame reserves
surface geometry for caller-supplied loading/error content. Its frame wrapper adds
source identity to the existing generation check. Mismatches fail before UI
submission. Pixels remain borrowed until every renderer has consumed the draw
list. No release callback or implicit decoder lease is provided.

## Extended Base slider

`cui_base_slider_controlled` is an additive unstyled double-precision API.
Legacy `cui_base_slider` retains its float pointer mutation and return semantics.
The new function accepts confirmed value by value, caller-owned `cui_slider_state`,
and `cui_slider_options`. It emits typed synchronous requests with copied source
events. Invalid arguments return false without changing state. Disabled/read-only
transitions cancel an active drag; no callback means no requests. State and user
callbacks must survive the call. Submit it inside a box with its own stable ID.

## Real optional decoder example

The [silent FFmpeg example](../examples/video_player/README.md) decodes on a worker,
retains bounded frame leases and demonstrates confirmed play/pause/seek/rate
requests. Its strict external harness runs portable controls, software decoded
pixels and private-Xvfb native decoded captures. It supplies no built-in codec or
universal format/browser/audio support; see its exact evidence and version/license
recording before using it as a host-adapter starting point.

## Browser gallery extension

The gallery provides **Video** (bare surface) and **VideoPlayer** (ready-made
controls) as extensions outside the frozen 78-family baseline. Build and exercise it locally (Chromium runs headless):

```sh
python scripts/build_web.py --output /tmp/cui-video-web
uv run tests/web/test_video_gallery.py --offline
uv run tests/web/test_video_gallery.py --directory /tmp/cui-video-web
python -m http.server --directory /tmp/cui-video-web
# Open http://localhost:8000/#Video
```

The browser decodes a checked-in original 12-second 320×180 sample using
`HTMLVideoElement`. The visible surface, buttons and timeline are CUI draw lists;
there are no HTML media controls. Play/pause, two-second skips, keyboard timeline
seeks and 1× / 1.5× rate requests are acknowledged from actual media state. The
sample includes a quiet generated tone and loops. VideoPlayer starts paused and
plays unmuted after the user presses Play; the bare Video surface autoplays muted
to respect browser autoplay policies. The browser routes decoded audio to its
normal output device and keeps audio/video synchronized. Fullscreen is a browser
capability and may reject a request; host errors are displayed explicitly.
Volume controls, audio-device selection and subtitles are not exposed by the CUI
controls yet. Native hosts must supply their own audio output; the FFmpeg example
remains silent. Universal codec/browser support and Safari are not validated.

The host chooses VP8 WebM or H.264 MP4 using `canPlayType`, with the alternate
encoding available if decoding fails. It fetches at most 512 KiB into a Blob so
this small sample can seek even when static hosting does not implement byte
ranges. Fetches are aborted and Blob URLs revoked on route exit. Larger streaming
applications need a separate buffering/range policy. Rebuild the original assets
with `python web/assets/video/generate.py`; its receipt records local FFmpeg
version, exact commands and output hashes. The generator requires local `libvpx`
and `libx264` encoders and uses bit-exact output settings; two consecutive local
runs produce identical files. FFmpeg is a fixture-generation tool,
not a browser runtime dependency; no media is downloaded during generation.

Decoded frames are copied into one fixed 230,400-byte WASM buffer. Session and
timeline generation checks reject stale submission. A separate decode ticket
retires pending frame callbacks during every seek; the timeline generation changes
on commit/cancel/skip so active scrubbing survives updates. Seek cancel restores
the position captured at begin; browser decoder completion remains asynchronous.
Pixels stay unchanged throughout synchronous Canvas consumption, and revisions
advance on each accepted frame. Host requests are copied into a 32-entry queue
and drained after rendering, never through CUI reentry. A batch exceeding 32 requests
is rejected in full with a visible limit message, resetting scrub presentation
and restoring an already-active scrub origin. This sample does not promise
unbounded gesture batching. Late operation promises are fenced by session,
operation sequence and decode ticket. No frame callback loop runs while paused;
leaving the route cancels scheduling, unloads media and exits only fullscreen
owned by this preview.

The focused Chromium test decodes both the actual WebM and MP4 assets, including
alternate-source recovery after a deliberately invalid preferred encoding. It
separates real encoded decoding/CUI interaction from
injected host-error protocol checks. It checks rendered pixel changes, confirmed
play/pause/seek/rate, keyboard routing, mobile DPR2 geometry, stale frame rejection,
route cleanup and the separate extension catalog. Other browser/platform codec
and fullscreen combinations remain unverified.
